in writing. the envisaged fiscal agreement (treaty) decided at the last council is a mix of proposals which seek to resolve a crisis generated by the non-existence of some of the proposed measures before it was triggered. unfortunately, the provisions on deficit reduction are not strong enough to solve the current crisis, which is manifested by a growing distrust of the bonds issued by eu member states. i believe that this impasse can only be overcome by measures to stimulate economic growth targeted at smes in the first place (for example, by partially subsidising the interest rate on bank loans). of course, excessive government deficits must be avoided, but a new skid is currently utopian, which makes me wonder what good these constraints are now. i believe that the member states must retain sovereignty over the tax rate and that competition between them in this respect cannot be harmful, just as competition between companies is beneficial for consumers. as for a financial transaction tax, the example of hungary is eloquent in terms of the effects: the decrease in capital exposure to that country and the reduction in credit is expected to happen at the eu level as well, even if perhaps more slowly than in the case of hungary.
in writing. − we all agree that urgent and courageous action is needed to counter the economic and sovereign debt crisis caused largely by structural weaknesses in the euro area. indeed, there is a need for sound governance of the euro area and a higher degree of budgetary discipline at member state level, but i do not know whether the intergovernmental agreement in its current form meets this imperative. i have a few reservations about this new treaty which risks creating a duplication of rules and creating a rift between the euro area and the rest of the member states without necessarily being necessary. the structural deficit criterion of 0.5% of gdp may well be included in the stability pact which is directly applicable in the member states. on the other hand, in order to ensure the democratic legitimacy of decisions implementing the provisions of the agreement, it would be ideal if they were taken by the community method and remained consistent with existing european law. last but not least, i believe that the provisions on fiscal union are currently vague, that is, that too much emphasis is placed on austerity without balancing it with some stimulus measures to revive the economy and return to the economic growth so necessary to alleviate social tensions.

at the durban conference, the union presented a clear agenda for reducing emissions, and this was on the table throughout the conference. no post-kyoto agreement was signed, the kyoto protocol was extended and a roadmap was set for 2015. the objectives of the 'durban platform', such as climate-friendly growth and poverty reduction, are however rather ambiguous. how will the industry be treated in the fight against climate change? an eco-efficient industrial policy creates jobs and economic growth. unfortunately, there is still no common analytical formula for determining emissions and the amount of emissions from air transport is not included. energy efficiency was also discussed in durban. in this context, the possibility of new opportunities and opportunities has been opened up. this allows us to make similar estimates for energy efficiency. by cop xviii, the itre and envi committees, together with the commission, must make concrete proposals for reducing emissions.
waste electrical and electronic equipment is one of the fastest growing sources of household waste and also one of the most hazardous. most of this waste is not properly managed and ends up in landfills, releasing toxic chemicals into the environment. the commission's proposal to improve and increase collection is therefore welcome. but as in other areas, the situation on the ground varies widely from one member state to another, and this reality must be taken into account if legislation is to be effective and easy to apply. in romania, the electrical products market is not yet saturated. in other words, we still do not throw away as much electrical and electronic products as other member states. it would therefore be important for us to have more time to adapt to the ambitious targets set by the new rules. the gradual increase in collection rates over the next seven years, which has been agreed as part of this package, provides us with some of the flexibility we need. as a general conclusion, the compromise reached provides a balance between the ambitious nature of the targets set and a realistic timeframe within which they can be achieved. i thank the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs for their work and their results in very difficult negotiations with the council.
waste electrical and electronic equipment is the waste with the fastest growing potential in the union, with estimates for 2020 reaching 12,3 million tonnes. i welcome the reform of the waste electrical and electronic equipment directive and stress the need for investment in the recycling of raw materials and rare earths, as mining, refining and recycling of rare earths have serious environmental consequences if not properly managed. the treatment of waste electrical and electronic equipment without proper procedures causes environmental damage, in particular by the release of heavy metals such as mercury from compact fluorescent lamps and flat screens and lead from televisions. according to the commission, only 33% of waste electrical and electronic equipment is officially separately collected, and it is possible that a large part of this waste, collected and undeclared, is treated in the union without adequate environmental protection or illegally shipped to developing countries, where certain valuable materials are recycled in a way that is hazardous to health and the environment or thrown away.

in writing. the new european rules on biocides aim to tighten controls on their impact on health and the environment, while simplifying the product authorisation procedure. 'biocides' are produced to combat harmful organisms and pathogens. they are used to protect human and animal health. they include disinfectants and insecticides and are used for preserving materials, embalming or painting vessels against the adherence of algae and micro-organisms. the eu has a longstanding legislation in this area, dating back to 1998. updating the legislation is a natural step so that only safe products reach the market. the new rules cover new areas such as furniture and textiles. the most dangerous substances - carcinogenic or toxic to reproduction - should be banned or used with more caution. the measures also facilitate the authorisation for placing products on the european market. as regards animal testing, in exchange for fair compensation, applicants should pool studies on vertebrate animals. a community-wide authorisation system should be introduced in the future to ensure a harmonised european market for biocidal products.

we've been talking about imbalances in the food chain for a long time. but the situation remains unchanged. farmers continue to be victims of abusive contracts and unfair competition. in my country, food manufacturers have to pay a fee to sell their products in supermarkets, but also a shelf fee, extra, to get visibility in the store. moreover, farmers receive only a tiny percentage of the profits that big-box stores make from selling their produce. in the vast majority of cases, the quality products of small and medium-sized farms have great difficulty reaching consumers because these producers cannot cope with the competition or the conditions imposed by supermarkets. in romania, farmers are forced to throw away a good part of their fruit or vegetable production because they cannot make use of it under current market conditions. i would like to take this opportunity to ask the commission and the member states to strengthen the bargaining position of farmers in the food chain, to ensure that competition rules are respected in agriculture and to encourage local markets.
agriculture is and will remain a strategic sector of the european union's economy and, in order to meet future challenges and ensure coherence of interventions within a given region, it is first and foremost necessary to establish close links between agricultural policy, rural development policy and regional policy. as regards the asymmetric reaction of food prices to commodity price fluctuations, i believe that this is mainly linked to the number of intermediaries operating along the supply chain. i therefore support the adoption of instruments to promote and support short supply chains and markets where farmers can unload their goods directly. this will create a direct link between consumers and farmers in a particular region, whereby the latter will get a larger share of the value of the final price, while the population will enjoy better prices.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the amendments to the visa code bring legal certainty for persons holding visas or residence permits for those eu member states which are outside the schengen area. it also clarifies the rules applicable at airports across the european union and eliminates the possibility of different standards being used by security authorities in schengen and non-schengen member states. beyond the technical changes proposed, it is also a symbolic message that member states must be treated equally and without discrimination, regardless of their membership of the schengen area. i think there is a lesson to be learned in the accession of romania and bulgaria to the schengen area or in the wider reform of schengen governance. following the adoption of that report, the commission should take the necessary measures to amend the visa application handbook accordingly to take account of the new provisions.
in writing. − in order to ensure legal certainty and greater transparency, it is necessary to amend the regulation on the community visa code in order to clarify all transit rules for international airport areas. the novelty introduced by this regulation concerns the exemption from the requirement to hold an airport transit visa for third-country nationals who are in possession of a valid residence permit or visa issued by one of the member states not fully applying the schengen acquis. the countries concerned are the united kingdom and ireland, which have decided not to apply the schengen acquis, and cyprus, bulgaria and romania, which are in the process of acceding to the schengen area. i think this amendment is normal, given that these people have already been checked by an eu authority and it is also a proposal that will reduce the bureaucratic obligations of the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the community code on visas because it clarifies some key technical aspects of the visa regime. following the adoption of this report, third-country nationals who already hold a visa issued by a member state are also entitled to exemption from the airport transit visa (atv) requirement by those member states which do not apply the schengen acquis. this is a logical step because once such a third-country national has passed all the required identification steps for securing the said visa, he/she should not require a second set of identification checks in order to obtain an atv.
in writing. − the eu-georgia agreement on protection of geographical indications of agricultural products and foodstuffs is an important step in bolstering trade between these two regions. upon the entry into force of the 1999 partnership and cooperation agreement, georgia acceded to the world trade organization in 2000 and has since then been party to the agreement on trade related aspects of intellectual property rights (trips). the purpose of this eu-georgia agreement is to safeguard the geographical indications, or place names used to identify origin and quality, reputation and other characteristics of agricultural products and foodstuffs. exports of georgia’s products to the eu in the last ten years have not only diversified, they have increased fourfold. while the agreement aims to streamline trade between the eu and georgia, it also allows georgia to strengthen its export economy to regions outside its traditional trade route. in the case of my home country romania, a tool such as this agreement can be quite instrumental for often overlooked countries to gain visibility and recognition in markets abroad.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, as the alde shadow rapporteur for georgia in the afet committee, i understand the significance of moving forward in pursuing closer trade relations with georgia. this is a positive step in eu-georgia relations because it will serve to enhance georgia’s access to a wider share of the eu market, which can only have positive effects on its economy. this agreement on protection of geographical indications ensures georgia’s capacity to assume key technical commitments and to implement them within a wider deep and comprehensive free trade agreement.
in writing. − i voted for the council decision on eu accession to unece regulation no 29 on uniform provisions for the approval of vehicles with regard to the protection of passengers in the cabin of a commercial vehicle. eu accession to this unece regulation makes it possible to apply the same standards in many countries, eliminating red tape, improving road safety, environmental protection and trade, and helping to maintain the international competitiveness of european industry. type approvals granted under unece regulations will be considered as ec type approvals, thus avoiding redundancies not only in technical requirements but also in certification procedures and administrative procedures, for the benefit of industry and national authorities. these technical requirements will apply in many countries located in particular in the eu, non-eu countries in western and eastern europe, south-eastern europe, the commonwealth of independent states, japan and north america, which are contracting parties to the 1958 unece agreement. type-approval, directly linked to internationally agreed standards and applied in so many countries, will be adopted by other third countries, further improving market access and strengthening the competitiveness of the eu industry.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the eu position on the draft regulation of the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) on pedestrian safety and the draft unece regulation on light sources with electroluminescent diodes (leds). the european commission, as the eu representative, considers that the two draft regulations, both on pedestrian safety and on light sources with light emitting diodes, should be included in the european union type-approval system for motor vehicles. the two draft unece regulations thus become part of the european type-approval system for motor vehicles. the standardised requirements of the draft unece regulation on provisions relating to the approval of vehicles with regard to pedestrian safety and provisions relating to the approval of vehicles with regard to light emitting diode (led) light sources aim to remove existing technical barriers to trade in motor vehicles between the contracting parties to the revised 1958 agreement (on technical requirements for wheeled vehicles) and to ensure that these vehicles provide a high level of safety and protection.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the government of the republic of indonesia on certain aspects of air services. the agreement signed on 29 june 2011 replaces certain provisions contained in the 19 existing bilateral air service agreements between eu member states and indonesia. certain provisions in the bilateral air services agreements between the eu member states and indonesia contained provisions that are contrary to the legislation of the european union and need to be brought into line with it in order to establish a sound legal basis for air services between the european union and indonesia and to preserve the continuity of those air services. the agreement aims to grant the right to non-discriminatory access to all eu air carriers on routes between the member states concerned and indonesia. the eu does not seek to increase the overall volume of air traffic between the union and indonesia through this agreement, nor does it seek to affect the balance between the air carriers of the european union and those of indonesia, or to negotiate changes to the traffic rights provisions in existing bilateral air services agreements. the agreement contains provisions on safety, aviation fuel taxation and the prohibition of anti-competitive practices.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because cooperation between the eu and the international civil aviation organisation needs to be strengthened. this memorandum supports the fundamental objectives of european external aviation policy. it is particularly important that the eu contributes to the decision-making process within icao, as the organisation currently has 190 member states. cooperation in areas such as aviation safety, aviation security, air traffic management and environmental protection should be further developed. the establishment of joint mechanisms will contribute to better coordination of programme planning and technical assistance. the promotion of new systems and technologies worldwide is necessary. it will enhance the competitiveness of the european civil aviation sector. i welcome the mutual commitment to achieving the highest levels of aviation safety in the world.
in writing. − this memorandum of cooperation aims to regulate and deepen relations and cooperation between the eu and the international civil aviation organisation (icao). i believe that the european union should attach greater importance to this cooperation because most of the matters covered by the chicago convention fall within the union's competence. the international civil aviation organization regulates policies in the areas of safety, security, environment and air traffic management. in addition, icao standards and requirements are the basis for community legislation and in conclusion i believe it is very important for the eu to be involved in the work and policy making of icao in order to contribute to the development of appropriate policies for the civil aviation sector. the mou also provides for the exchange of electronic information, data and official publications and the granting of access to databases, which will lead to a strengthening of relations between the two entities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the council decision on the conclusion of the memorandum of cooperation (mc) between the eu and icao, establishing a framework for enhanced cooperation and laying down related procedural steps. the general objective of the memorandum is to ensure harmonisation of standards, close coordination of civil aviation activities and to achieve efficient use of resources and avoid overlapping efforts. pursuant to the decision and in accordance with the provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the council shall decide on the eu position within the joint committee on the adoption and amendment of provisions. the union shall be represented within the joint committee by the commission, assisted by representatives of the member states. the commission sets the eu's position for cooperation on working conditions, financial and resource issues, consultation and exchange of information, interoperability of new technologies and coordination of inspection and audit programmes. in accordance with icao confidentiality rules, the parties shall exchange electronic information, official data and publications and grant each other access to databases. the memorandum provides for financial support of eur 500 000 per year, for an initial period of 3 years. subsequently, provisions in the field of aviation security, air traffic management and environmental protection previously adopted by the council will be included in the annexes to the memorandum.
in writing. − i voted for parliament's position on the waste electrical and electronic equipment directive (weee) as the directive supports the efficient use of resources and the recovery of valuable secondary raw materials. member states shall encourage cooperation between producers and recyclers and the adoption of measures to promote the design and production of eee (electrical and electronic equipment), in particular to facilitate the reuse, dismantling and recovery of weee and their components and materials. for weee from private households, member states shall ensure that systems are in place to allow for the free handing over of such waste. certain member states, including romania, may, due to the lack of the necessary infrastructure and the low level of consumption of eee, decide to achieve, within four years of the entry into force of the directive, a collection rate of between 40% and 45% of the average weight of eee placed on the market in the preceding three years and may postpone the achievement of the final collection rate referred to in article 7 (1) until a later date, but not later than nine years from the date of entry into force of the directive. the commission calls on the european standardisation bodies to develop european standards for the treatment, recovery, recycling and preparation for re-use of weee.
in writing. − i supported the agreement at second reading on the regulation setting the conditions under which biocidal products may be placed on the market because, despite rather difficult negotiations, a satisfactory result was reached in terms of both the competitiveness of the industry and the protection of the users of these products and the environment. i consider the introduction of a union-wide authorisation procedure to be one of the most important developments. even if i would have preferred a faster implementation than the agreed three-step approach, motivated by the need to ensure the optimal functioning of the european chemicals agency, i believe that this procedure, together with the simplified procedure for low-risk products, will considerably reduce the costs that the industry will have to bear in authorising new products. this will also encourage innovation in the field, encouraging the introduction of new products that are more efficient and less harmful to the environment and users. last but not least, i am pleased that the council members have accepted parliament's request to avoid duplicating animal testing when such testing has already been done.
in writing. − this own-initiative report identifies problems in the sectors overlapping agricultural production, highlights farmers' growing dependence on an increasingly concentrated manufacturing industry and proposes a series of measures to be adopted in the framework of the future cap reform. farmers need support to improve agronomic and environmental performance to meet new climate, ecological and economic challenges. i believe that the new cap policy should include specific support measures to encourage the streamlining of agronomic practices and the improved and sustainable management of agricultural resources in order to produce stable and productive agriculture, reduce production costs and nutrient losses and increase innovation, resource efficiency and efficiency and sustainability in agricultural production systems. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the agricultural factor supply chain, as the high level of volatility in prices of basic agricultural products and agricultural production costs has led to increased uncertainty in agricultural income and long-term investment by farmers. according to eurostat, over the last decade, total production costs of eu farmers have increased by an average of 40%, while farm gate prices have increased by an average of less than 25%. we call on national and european competition authorities to address the issue of abuses of dominant positions by agribusiness traders, food retailers and processing companies and to enforce eu antitrust law. member states need to improve their collection systems for agricultural products. we call on the commission and the member states to examine the role of producer organisations and cooperatives in organising collective purchases of agricultural inputs in order to strengthen the bargaining position of farmers. the commission should inform farmers and consumers of the need for more efficient management of energy, water and natural resources throughout the food chain in order to significantly reduce resource and food waste.
in writing. − i believe that food waste has become a widespread phenomenon in the eu, but has not received the attention it deserves. the current situation is unacceptable, as up to 50% of healthy food is wasted every year in supermarkets, restaurants and households in the eu, while 79 million european citizens live below the poverty line and 16 million receive their food from charities. we expect the european commission to come forward with a convincing strategy that will force eu member states to tackle this problem systematically. in the medium term, however, i believe that 2014 should be designated as the 'european year against food waste'.
in writing. - i voted in favour of paragraph 4 of the motion for a resolution as it was presented, because we must not reject legislation on relations between agricultural producers and large traders. the best evidence of the need for legislation is the failure of attempts to self-regulate in this area. producers need concrete and effective measures, and not least, they need them to be implemented as quickly as possible.
in writing. − i voted for the resolution on imbalances in the food supply chain, as the income problems of european farmers are increasing and the prices paid by consumers for products are not reflected in the prices paid to farmers for their products. this undermines the ability of farmers to invest and could lead to them going out of business. we call on the commission and the member states to urgently address the issue of unequal distribution of profits in the food chain, in particular to ensure adequate income for farmers. in order to stimulate sustainable production systems, farmers need to be compensated for the investments and commitments they make in these areas. i welcome the commission's proposals for cap reform, which aim to strengthen farmers' position in the food supply chain by supporting producer organisations and inter-branch organisations and promoting short chains between producers and consumers, such as markets for local products. considers it necessary to organise an information campaign at eu level to inform farmers about their contractual rights, the most common illegal, unfair and abusive contractual and commercial practices and the means at their disposal to report abuses.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is important that the eu has its own navigation system. i believe that european space competence needs to be developed. europe has a rich heritage in space. but it must be put to good use. the galileo global navigation satellite system will stimulate industries that need reliable and precise positioning services, such as transport, security and medical services. the economic impact for industry is estimated at around eur 90 billion over the next 20 years. i stress the importance of developing a strategy for research and innovation in the field of space policy. at the same time, technological progress should be ensured by stable funding in the long term. therefore, the promotion of public-private partnerships is of significant importance in this area. a competitive space industry would foster european access to space and orbital infrastructure.
in writing. − the european union must play an important role in the development of a space policy in order to promote scientific and technical progress. i support mr patriciello's report because it highlights this very point. at the same time, a legislative, administrative and financial framework is fundamental for industry's investment in research and innovation. it also believes that the eu must invest to ensure that european access to space and orbital infrastructure is guaranteed. the report also argues that although the strategy put forward by the commission identifies priority areas for action, these remain unclear. they need to be more explicit and present an assessment of the options, costs, benefits and risks
in writing. − the space sector plays a vital role in increasing competitiveness and innovation at union level. space infrastructure is a key framework serving the economic, social and strategic interests of eu citizens. the successful launch of the galileo project confirms to me that the eu needs an independent space policy integrated into the objectives of the different development sectors. i believe that the success of this policy lies in connecting the space infrastructure with the satellite service providers. unfortunately, european companies implementing satellite communication systems are reducing their activities in europe and reducing their staff by shifting production to other continents. the commission-funded sartre programme, which aims to implement technologies enabling satellite-guided vehicle transport in columns, brings considerable added value to research and innovation in the eu. the institutions and companies involved in the project benefit from the advantages of the european space infrastructure, contributing to increased safety and comfort in traffic with a reduced impact on the environment. romania has joined the european space agency (esa), becoming an institutional partner in a scientific space mission - euclid. romania is also on its first space experiment - the launch of the goliath satellite. esa's space systems enable the development of space applications for agriculture, the environment, transport, disaster measurement and telemedicine.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on an eu space strategy for citizens, as space policy is an essential element of the europe 2020 strategy and is an integral part of the flagship industrial policy initiative. the eu's space policy aims to improve the daily lives of european citizens by facilitating economic growth, encouraging the potential for innovation and supporting scientific progress. space solutions relying on cutting-edge technologies and a competitive european industrial base are indispensable for addressing current societal challenges such as natural disasters, monitoring of resources and climate, developing the telecommunications sector and promoting relevant applications in the fields of climate change policy, urban planning, environmental management, agriculture, maritime safety, fisheries and transport. we call on the commission to make concrete proposals in the strategic field of launchers, given the current critical economic situation of the launchers sector worldwide. the galileo and egnos programmes are essential for the creation of the single european sky and for the safe and cost-effective management of air traffic in europe. we call for a firm and ambitious timetable and stable funding for research and innovation, which will ensure technological progress and increase industrial capacity. as gmes is a key tool in combating climate change and environmental degradation, we recommend funding gmes under the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework.
in writing. − food waste has become so widespread in recent years that it can be considered a global problem, which unfortunately has serious repercussions on the food supply chain. the causes of food waste are diverse, ranging from losses during harvesting and storage, to unsafe transport, to labelling errors and poor habits of the final consumer when buying and using food. i believe it is essential to reduce food waste throughout the food chain by adopting a coordinated strategy followed by concrete actions. the exchange of good practices is also needed at both european and national level in order to improve coordination between member states to avoid food waste and to increase the efficiency of the food supply chain. combating food waste must become a priority on the european political agenda. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − with almost 80 million people in the eu living below the poverty line and more than half of the food waste in european households and along the food supply chain could be avoided, i believe that the adoption of this report is an important step towards increasing access to food for the poorest of europeans. at union level, we must already take all the necessary measures to cope with the future growth of the world population and, by implication, its food supply. i also supported this report because it addresses the environmental and ethical issues, but also the economic and social costs of food waste.
in writing. − i voted for the report on avoiding food waste: strategies to make the eu food chain more efficient, as each year in europe around 50% of the amount of healthy and edible food is lost along the food chain, becoming waste. we call on the council, the commission, the member states and the actors in the food supply chain to address food waste throughout the supply and consumption chain as soon as possible and to develop guidelines and support to increase the efficiency of the food supply chain in each sector. food waste has various causes: overproduction, misdirection of products (inappropriate size or shape), damage to products or packaging, marketing rules (looking problems or packaging defects) or improper stock management and marketing strategies. we invite the commission to assess the impact of a coercive food waste policy targeting all parties involved in the food chain, by applying the 'polluter pays' principle. we ask the commission to set specific food waste prevention targets for member states, as part of the waste prevention targets to be met by member states by 2014, as recommended by the 2008 waste framework directive.
given the alarming situation of youth unemployment, it was very beneficial to include on the council's agenda the debate on boosting employment for this category of the population. the future belongs to the young and they are the main beneficiaries of everything that is being built, for better or for worse, today. it is therefore essential that measures be taken to improve their situation, both at community level and at the level of each member state. i consider cohesion policy to be a basic instrument for achieving the objectives proposed in this respect. programming processes for european funds for the period 2014-2020 have now started at national level. i strongly recommend that the commission and the member states pay greater attention to youth and include well-funded and specifically targeted axes for youth employment in the structure of national programmes.
in writing. 25 member states have reached an agreement on stability, coordination and governance in emu, a key element in our efforts to maintain stability and an example of the solidarity and determination with which the union is prepared to deal with crisis situations. european leaders have had to take difficult measures to stabilize the eurozone. financial stability is an important but not unique element in the effort to ensure economic recovery. we need discipline, structural change, employment and sustainable growth. the use of european funds must be optimised. concrete proposals are needed to address youth unemployment and sme financing. we are entering a phase of economic governance based on the european semester, in which national governments recognise that areas of national competence must also be addressed at european level. the european economy needs to become much more competitive, and this is only possible by completing the internal market. the commission must therefore ensure that all internal market laws are applied in the member states and supervise their application. this agreement represents a major step forward towards fiscal and economic integration and better governance of the euro area.
at the european council on 30 january, 25 member states signed the treaty on stability, coordination and governance in the economic and monetary union. the new treaty obliges member states to have balanced or surplus national budgets, failing which an automatic correction mechanism is triggered. the treaty will be signed in march and will enter into force after it has been ratified by at least 12 euro-area member states. the treaty must be incorporated into eu law within five years of its entry into force. the treaty represents the firm commitment of the signatory states to strengthen fiscal discipline. austerity measures are not a guarantee of growth. austerity measures have created, in some member states, by deteriorating the quality of life of many european citizens and by increasing the proportion of the population at risk of poverty, genuine social crises and the deterioration of the european social model. we regret that at the european council on 30 january the member states did not commit themselves as firmly to boosting employment, especially among young people, to completing the single market, to increasing the eu's competitiveness and to stimulating financing for the economy, especially smes. they are essential for maintaining the european social model and for implementing the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. the political developments at the european council in december 2011 reconfirmed the priorities in the process of consolidating the eu, namely the resumption of sustainable economic growth and job creation. the demonstration of solidarity is the most important of these priorities. we must continue on the path of the euro plus pact and strengthen solidarity between the euro area and the member states outside it. the process of pooling the sovereignty of the member states must continue to ensure solidarity. we politicians, the members of the european parliament, must explain to our constituents why sharing sovereignty is not a concession and rebuild their confidence in the community's future. they will thus be more confident in the developments of the near future and in our efforts to build a new europe that is more united and coordinated under the democratic primacy of the european parliament, the only european institution whose members are directly elected by the citizens. i was of the opinion that the ep should have a bigger role in decision-making and that the president of the ep should attend all meetings of the leaders of the member states. and i also believe that the incorporation of the new stability pact into the european treaty must remain a major objective.
the epp group welcomes the council's decision of 23 january to extend the existing sanctions against iran. these are the toughest sanctions yet imposed on the regime in tehran. after the asset freeze of a long list of iranian companies and individuals, after the restriction of exports of sensitive products and investments in iran's hydrocarbons, the next logical step was to sanction the country's strategically important oil resources. the adoption of sanctions is never a superficial thing to do. in the case of iran, these measures are all the more necessary as the risk of nuclear proliferation linked to the iranian programme is of growing concern. i therefore think it is very important that the union has shown firmness in the absence of a clear response from iran to the proposal to resume negotiations. the tightening of sanctions and our firm tone sends a clear signal to the iranians that we will not accept the continuation of their nuclear program. finally, for those who argue that sanctions are ineffective and even counterproductive, i want to highlight two aspects that i think are important: sanctions so far have actually hampered iran's nuclear program, and have prevented iran from getting a nuclear bomb. on the other hand, iran has begun to show signs that these measures are having an effect on its economy. sanctions are therefore the key to resolving the nuclear crisis and can bring iran back to the negotiating table. (the president agreed to answer a question by way of a 'blue card' (rule 149 (8) of the rules of procedure))
answer to the blue card. i think if i understand the question correctly, we have the same point of view.
iran is in a very sensitive region. an iranian nuclear weapon would be practically an additional threat to the peace of this region and a method of exercising control over neighboring countries. i therefore agree that there is a need to clarify the intentions of this country. however, we have to ask ourselves whether a blanket sanction on iranian oil will have the desired effect. i believe that we cannot punish the whole of society for the mistakes made by the ruling class and therefore the sanctions must be directed at those who hold power, and i want to draw your attention, mrs. ashton, that there is a need for a permanent evaluation of the effects of these new sanctions. at the same time, the european union must constantly encourage dialogue with the iranian side, and, as you said, take advantage of the relationship it has with turkey. but the dialogue must not be limited to the nuclear issue, but must also include the human rights situation, as many of my colleagues have said. on this last point, the european union must obtain from its own companies the cessation of exports of products used precisely to oppress iranian citizens, such as, in particular, electronic products. finally, i would like to stress that the only solution to the tense situation in relations with iran is a peaceful one. military intervention would be a major mistake with disastrous consequences. the european union, through its high representative, must firmly declare that it is against military intervention and reiterate its openness to dialogue.
vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, this has been an important debate and i have listened with great care to all of the contributions that have been made. i will just try to bring together some of the themes that have been expressed in the house and to take them forward as part of our thinking about how to deal effectively with this extremely important issue of the nuclear aspirations of iran. a number of colleagues, beginning with mr salafranca in his first contribution, talked about the need to work with others to ensure that we are collaborating with our allies, who of course include those that we call the e3+3 – russia, china and the united states plus the uk, france and germany – the six countries which, when we do find ourselves in dialogue with iran, sit behind me as the e3+3 designated by the security council. of course, we are not only talking with those countries. i saw dai bingguo, the state councillor of china, when i was in india the week before last. we are constantly talking with russia – the political director is there currently – as well as with other countries like japan and korea, with the ambition of ensuring that the gap created by eu sanctions is not filled in ways that mean that there would not be an effect on the regime. a number of colleagues have mentioned the role of turkey. i keep in close contact with foreign minister davutoğlu on this issue. turkey has provided a conduit of information and dialogue to iran, being the reinforcer of messages, and also hosted the last round of talks. i pay tribute to the way in which that country has worked with us on this issue. i will be going to brazil this weekend for a number of discussions. one of these will be on what we are doing on iran and why. i take very much the points that have been made about strengthening and broadening the understanding of what the eu is doing, the reasons behind our actions and the need for the international community to stand together to seek a satisfactory resolution. so in all our discussions across the world we are keeping this on the agenda. we keep making the point that the sanctions are important and that their purpose is to try to persuade iran to come to negotiations. it is a twin-track approach, specifically designed to that effect. the second area i wanted to touch on is the effect on the people of iran. we are very clear that what we are seeking to do is to persuade the regime that it needs to come to the talks. i am very worried about iran’s economic capacity. it is a country that should have been able to grow economically. i keep watch over what we are doing, to try to ensure that the effects on the people of iran are minimal but that they also understand what it is that we are doing. as has been said, there are many people in iran who share the aspiration that we have to see iran turn away from its current path. it is also true that we are looking, with the member states, at the effect on the european union of all our work on sanctions. it is vital that we ensure that we understand what we are doing and that we look at the effect that it has. national legal systems are responsible for ensuring there is no circumvention, but the eu as a whole is working together in this direction. colleagues also mentioned the fact that camp ashraf has an iranian population. i have already mentioned a couple of times, in our question hour, the importance that we attach to trying to find a satisfactory solution for the people of camp ashraf. my concern is straightforward. it is to try to find a way in which we can keep them completely safe and give them a future. members of the un are in discussion with member states where there are issues of citizenship, and members of the high commission for refugees are engaged with this, as is martin kobler who, as i have indicated already, will be here tomorrow. we are working closely with the us and with the international community, and we will keep this on the agenda in our discussions with iraq. it is important that we move forward and that the people find a future, not that we simply keep them there because we do not have a plan. there does seem to be, if not a perfect plan, then a compromise solution under which, if we do things properly, there is potential for a future for these people that will keep them safe which, as i have said, is our final objective. my final point concerns something that mr tannock said about the glorious persian culture. absolutely. we are clear in this house, and right across the european union, that our quarrel on this issue is not with the people of iran. we wish them well. we wish to see this glorious persian history and culture rise and be part of the region and part of the international community, but we have obligations as countries and as the european union. those obligations are that, when people sign up to treaties and say they will not move toward nuclear proliferation, they are taking on obligations that they have to respect, and if they do not respect them then we have to do something about it. it is all done within the security council. these issues go back to the security council, and it is the security council which gives me my mandate and with whom the european union works. i do hope that we will have the support to make sure that these sanctions are seen as being an important contribution to getting the other track moving and through that medium, as i do in any other, i am asking the iranians to respond to my letter, to pick up what i left on the table or to come forward with their own ideas and come back to the talks.
in writing. – i strongly support the recent sanctions that the council has decided to impose on iran since its non-cooperative attitude generates serious concerns in europe and worldwide. there are serious doubts about the real objectives of the iranian nuclear programme, which has now become a global threat. given the authoritarian character of the iranian regime, i also believe that the eu should do more in supporting the iranian opposition in iraq. after the brutal attacks last year, iraq has imposed a deadline to close camp ashraf. yesterday the inhabitants were urged by the un’s envoy martin kobler to move to a new location near baghdad which, according to the council of europe statement last week, seems more like a prison, with a very limited living area and a heavy police presence. the hr’s special adviser has been refused a visa to enter iraq to take part in the negotiations. how come this diplomatic insult has been kept quiet by our services while we continue to pay a fortune to help iraq for development? should not our hr take a more active role by trying to organise even video-link interviews with the inhabitants in ashraf to help quickly bring out those with families in europe?
russia's accession to the wto, after 18 years of negotiations, opens up a new perspective on international trade relations. i think we should appreciate the russian side's willingness to modify almost 300 legal provisions to conform to international trade rules, and to agree to reduce its customs duties in numerous industrial sectors. the prospect of a doubling of eu-russia trade in the next 5-10 years is, however, conditional on the modernisation of the russian economy and the full adoption of a real democratic framework. the eu-russia partnership is conditional on respect for democratic values and rules. that's why we are concerned about the fairness of this year's presidential election, especially in the context of the protests that followed the parliamentary elections in december. sunday's appearance on state television of the opposition leader, the first after years of censorship, is an encouraging sign that all candidates will have unfettered access to the media. but this premiere also demonstrates the democratic deficit that russian society suffers from. that's why the electoral process is no guarantee of democracy, unless the elections are not rigged, including during the campaign phase. mr president, the report we are now debating is strategic, comprehensive and sophisticated, addressing europe’s challenge generated by the changing distribution of power within the international system: a process accelerated by the current world crisis. europe, which has created a modern international system, is now facing a double challenge. she has to keep her central place within it while having to fight a nasty internal crisis. in the past century, given europe’s centrality within the international system, war in europe has twice become world war. today, even if war in europe is unthinkable, our continent could still rock the world boat hard, both financially and economically. the west – the us and europe – now has to make room for the newcomers, either in existing bodies such as the un security council or by creating new ones for them such as the g20. brics is a nascent grouping which is relatively heterogeneous, while russia and china are well-established powers. there is a big question mark over the ambitions of brazil and south africa, with india apparently preoccupied primarily with china, which embodies this challenge. how can europe best engage these emerging power centres without destroying the current world international institutional architecture? to engage this power successfully, europe, which will have first to ensure coherence between the national and eu approaches towards them, will need to strike the right balance between change, namely permitting these emerging power centres to achieve their aims, and continuity, namely safeguarding her interests.

and protection of the most vulnerable – the most vulnerable in humanitarian catastrophes being children, women, the handicapped and the elderly – is often a key objective of what i do as commissioner for humanitarian aid. we support the protection of women, especially in conflict zones, through our humanitarian aid instrument, but we also support the empowerment of women through cash-for-work programmes that specifically target women in conflict zones. i will be in the democratic republic of the congo in three weeks’ time and my main objective will indeed be this issue: the issue that is the topic of this report, the protection of women, and specifically stopping the rape of women as an instrument of war. overall, the eu is active in more than 70 countries, and the eu institutions and member states have reported allocating a total of approximately eur 200 million in 2009 and early 2010. let me now turn to the eu common security and defence policy (csdp). most csdp missions and operations include a human rights and gender exercise. we now have a package of three fully fledged training modules on human rights, gender and child protection in the context of csdp, which are being finalised in 2012. we also work very closely with the eu military staff in order to have a good common understanding of all the humanitarian aspects in conflicts, but in particular of how conflicts affect the most vulnerable – among them, women. while we do a lot on the external side, it is also important to perform well internally by appointing women negotiators or mediators. by appointing more women in key positions in the european external action service, our member states are the most proactive in the un context. thirteen of the eu member states have adopted national action plans. others, like germany, have come up with special initiatives on women, peace and security. the first eu report on the indicators that measured the implementation of un security council resolution 1325 was finalised in may 2011. it shows that the eu has taken concrete steps to enhance protection of most vulnerable groups, including women. we can be proud of our efforts but we still need to be vigilant and go on working in all forums and in all countries to tackle sexual violence in conflicts and to ensure women’s meaningful participation in peace processes and public representation. to respond to the question on whether the eu is considering appointing a special representative, vice-president/high representative ashton announced in december that she is looking into the creation of the post of eu special representative for human rights, and is considering the definition of this function. let me finish by saying thank you very much for this discussion today.
in writing. – in order to encourage their participation in situations of war, women must be visible contributors to the prevention, mediation and resolution of conflicts. beyond engaging in behind-the-scenes roles, assuming leadership roles is key to building upon the foundation of gender equality. as women account for half of the eu population, it is logical that their participation in these three phases mirrors this statistic. aside from this simple democratic principle, what is perhaps the strongest argument for women’s participation is the unique perspective they bring to the table and the message their empowerment sends to the world. women need to be better represented in the military, for example, not just to fill a proportional requirement but also because they interact and communicate more effectively with local women. on the other spectrum, local women’s empowerment must be strengthened. education is a crucial means through which local women can gain integrity and be better equipped to engineer preventive measures against war and violence in their communities. in addition to the active participation of a proportional representation of women at the negotiation table, women’s knowledge is also critical in the peace-building process as women are more aware of the challenges faced by their communities.
the cross-border transfer of companies is one of the essential elements in the completion of the internal market and articles 49 and 54 of the treaty on the functioning of the union guarantee the freedom of establishment of european companies anywhere in the european union. however, the lack of uniformity in legislation on the transfer and modalities of the transfer of a company's registered office, as well as the employment risk, administrative difficulties, associated costs, social implications and lack of legal certainty, make the transfer difficult to achieve. we ask the commission to present a proposal for a directive on the crossborder transfer of head offices, so that the transfer only takes place after the management or board of directors of a company planning a transfer has drawn up a transfer plan for which the employees of that company have also been consulted. i believe that egovernment services and single points of contact, created under the services directive, can simplify the administrative burden in the event of a company transfer.
improving access to energy services contributes to the quality of life of the population. it is especially necessary for people living in poverty. in this regard, access to energy should become a priority in the debate on poverty eradication. i would point out that the difficult access to modern energy services puts women and children at a particular disadvantage. i support putting this issue on the agenda for the rio+20 summit in june. i support the idea of creating a specific programme on energy and development at european level. private investment should also be encouraged to increase the accessibility of these services to the population. i would stress the importance of financing projects in the field of renewable electricity sources. for example, in romania, green energy producers are set to receive €300 million in green certificates this year.
globally, some 1.3 billion people, 84% of whom live in rural areas, lack access to electricity, and 2.7 billion people lack current cooking facilities, leading to smoke in homes and over 1.4 million premature deaths each year. improving access to energy requires an estimated annual investment of usd 48 billion by 2030, equivalent to 3% of the global investment in energy infrastructure projected by 2030. i believe that access to modern and sustainable energy services for all is a prerequisite for achieving the millennium development goals, and i support the inclusion of universal access to energy in these goals from 2015. at the rio+20 summit, the union should propose concrete targets for the eradication of energy poverty and a roadmap for their achievement.
in writing. lack of access to electricity is a serious problem not only worldwide, affecting some 1.3 billion people, but even in some european union states. in romania, for example, many isolated rural areas are still without electricity, which has led to a worrying depopulation of the villages in these parts of the country. the same effect of rural neglect is also experienced by the lack of roads or sewerage. in these circumstances, it is important to maintain the second pillar of the future common agricultural policy, the one dedicated to rural development, and in particular to maintain the possibility of financing infrastructure investments, whether in electricity, gas or roads.
we can only have a fully functioning single market if the 500 million people of the european union enjoy all the rights of the community. unfortunately, reality has shown that our citizens face many obstacles to transnational activity, unacceptable obstacles that can undermine the very idea of the single market in the european union. at a time of high mobility of european citizens, i believe that special rules for crossborder and mobile workers should be adopted immediately, taking into account the interaction of tax and social security systems in different member states. i believe that better coordination and cooperation between the tax administrations of the member states will lead to the removal of transnational tax obstacles and to the harmonisation of national rules, which is so necessary for citizens and companies in the european union.
the main function of tax systems is to finance public services such as education, health services, public transport and infrastructure, protect public goods and reduce social inequalities through a more balanced distribution of income and wealth. fiscal policies should aim to encourage growth and job creation, enhance the union's competitiveness, reduce costs for businesses, especially smes. effective taxation helps public authorities to meet their obligations and citizens' expectations. the commission and the member states should continue to cooperate in combating double taxation, tax fraud and tax evasion, in order to increase transparency and to reduce shortcomings and uncertainties for businesses and citizens in tax collection. i would stress the importance of the initiative on the introduction of electronic invoices, equal treatment from 2013 onwards for vat on electronic and paper invoices, and e-government services for the efficiency and transparency of tax collection.
the lack of coordination of tax policies at eu level is an obstacle to cross-border activities and investments. it can also lead to evasion, abuse and fraud. europe needs a strategy of fiscal consolidation, the fiscal obstacles affecting transnational mobility must be removed. i support the commission's initiative to set up a working group on double taxation. i would stress that this mechanism increases the overall tax burden and has a negative effect on capital investment. in the medium and long term, it threatens the competitiveness of european societies. double taxation conventions can help to address these problems. according to a recent study, after the adoption of such a convention, bilateral portfolio investment can increase by up to 50%. romania has concluded double taxation agreements with 90 countries.
in view of the increasing number, frequency, scale and severity of humanitarian disasters affecting several areas of the world, i welcome the commission's initiative to increase the budget of the instrument for humanitarian aid in the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework to an annual average of around eur 915 million. another proposed measure is to increase the emergency aid reserve to €2.5 billion for the same period and to propose carrying over unused funds from the reserve to the following year. i believe that the union budget should support actions to anticipate, prevent and respond to disasters and to facilitate the launching of actions to overcome crisis situations. we demand special treatment for children as well as pregnant women and mothers with small children in terms of food, clothing, evacuation and transportation, and necessary medical services.
statistics from the past few decades show an increase in the frequency of natural disasters around the world. at the same time, the union's budget for humanitarian aid and civil protection is constantly growing. in this respect, sound financial management is essential, because the union needs a more realistic humanitarian fund. i stress the need to maintain a balance between the financing of disaster preparedness and emergency aid. europe needs to have formal mechanisms in place to prevent abuse. transparency of cooperation with international organisations is important. at the same time, the eu must ensure coherence between humanitarian and development assistance, otherwise it could have a negative effect on local markets. for example, surplus food aid can discourage local food production.
in the second part of paragraph 6 we would like to replace 'only' with 'mainly'. as i said yesterday, we need a firm union position on iran, the epp is not in favour of sanctions for sanctions' sake, the decision to adopt sanctions is not taken lightly, and unfortunately in the case of iran we have very serious grounds for concern. we have to be very firm and not dilute our message.
i voted for this resolution because i share the concerns about the iranian nuclear program. its military dimension can have major security implications with global, not just regional, effects. this is why efforts to find a solution must be stepped up, combining firm measures with proposals for dialogue. at the same time, the effects of sanctions must be assessed on a continuous basis in order to determine their effectiveness. in this context, i would like to remind you of the importance of coordinating with other international actors in order to achieve real results. turkey can play a positive role in efforts to resolve the iranian dossier. i hope that cooperation with ankara in this area will be intensified. i call on the authorities in tehran to respond to invitations to negotiate and avoid escalating the situation by blocking the strait of hormuz.
i welcome the report by my colleague on the european dimension of sport. i would particularly like to highlight the role of sport in strengthening european cohesion and in fostering an atmosphere free of intolerance. in connection with this report, let me draw your attention to a strange incident: recently, the national ice hockey teams of romania and hungary played in the hungarian-majority town of csixzereda in romania. as the romanian national ice hockey team includes only players from the hungarian minority community in romania, with the exception of two players, during the usual hymn singing before the match, these players also sang the hungarian national anthem. the case received special attention in the romanian mainstream press, with many accusing the hungarian national hockey team, which is almost entirely made up of romanian national teams, of treason. it is time for mutual respect and tolerance to define not only the atmosphere of sporting events but also public manifestations, because in this case it was not the gestures of the fans that fueled the intolerance, but the malicious manipulative activity of romanian politicians and representatives of the romanian press. by the way, the match was won by romans 4 to 1.
madam president, i welcomed the positive vote on the iturgaiz report. through it the parliament is adding its voice to the numerous petitions sent by citizens from all over europe to call on member states to properly transpose the waste framework directive. it has become clear that the management of waste disposal is posing a political and social problem in many member states and the european commission has a fundamental role in controlling and guiding them to ensure the proper enforcement of the eu waste acquis at national level and raise greater environmental awareness among citizens. this is the right time to stop saying waste is an issue and turn it into an opportunity for job and business creation because efficient waste management strategies can provide enormous opportunities for both employment creation and revenue enhancement while ensuring environmental sustainability.
i voted in favour of the report drawn up by mr iturgaiz in the context of the intensification of discussions on waste recycling. as a member of the committee on petitions, i have often taken part in debates on this subject. i would point out that the new member states are the last in recycling, although they produce less waste than the european average. romania is among the countries targeted by petitions in the field of waste management. to meet eu standards, my country is currently implementing the integrated waste management system. by 2015, it will lead to the closure of non-green waste dumps and the development of recyclable waste sorting stations. the current ramps pose a heightened risk to both the environment and the human communities in their vicinity.
in writing. − as the european union is one of the main actors interested in strengthening international institutions and building new international regimes addressing areas such as climate change or trade in goods, it is important that the union takes the first step towards building a new global system of governance by approaching relations with the rising powers in a constructive and pragmatic manner. the strategic partnerships concluded by the european union with these countries must be the starting point of this new foreign policy.
in writing. - the bric countries have experienced significant economic growth in recent years, which, in the context of the crisis, has produced shifts in the global balance of influence. but these countries, with the exception of russia, are still developing countries, with the highest concentration of poverty in the world. there is a risk that this accelerated economic growth will accentuate inequalities, despite significant progress, especially in the case of brazil. it is estimated that by 2020, china will become the world's largest economy, and by 2050, the economies of the seven major emerging economies will be stronger than those of the g7. with its growing political role commensurate with its economic weight, the bric core also has a growing responsibility in driving global social progress as well as international development policy. i hope that the common concern to complement aid effectiveness with development effectiveness will become a common platform for strengthening the involvement of emerging countries in development policies.
in writing. − i voted for the report on the eu's external policy towards the brics and other emerging powers, as the eu needs to work towards a better link between its foreign and security policy and eu sectoral policies such as development, energy security, trade, access to raw materials and rare earth elements, climate change and migration. the resolution highlights: the importance of brazil as the main power in the regional integration process represented by mercosur and the eu-brazil strategic partnership; the key role of the eu-russia strategic partnership in maintaining peace and security in europe, in enhancing trade and economic development, in maintaining energy security; the importance of the eu-india strategic partnership; the importance of china as a major economic power and its key role in the global economic recovery. relations with the brics countries should be developed on the basis of bilateral dialogues focusing on and stimulating democratisation and strengthening the rule of law, good governance, regulatory convergence, coordination of common positions in international fora and intensification of relations with the eu. the overall coordination of eu foreign policy towards brics and other emerging powers should be ensured by the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.
in writing. - we read in the press about the fabulous wealth of political leaders. for example, estimates of the personal wealth of hosni mubarak and his family range from $50 billion to $70 billion, with the bulk of that wealth invested in the eu and the us. kim jong-il also holds approximately $4 billion in european banks. and as a final example, omar al-bashir, the president of sudan, is suspected of embezzling $9 billion, which came from the oil boom that his country experienced, and which is largely deposited in british banks. this is why eu member states must strictly enforce travel bans against sanctioned persons for travel to eu territory for non-humanitarian purposes. it is equally important that eu member states investigate and, where appropriate, prosecute any natural or legal person in europe who has assisted sanctioned leaders and persons associated with them to evade or circumvent sanctions imposed by law against them.
in writing. − i voted for the recommendation to the council on a consistent policy towards regimes to which the eu applies restrictive measures concerning the personal and commercial interests of their leaders within the eu. according to article 21 of the eu treaty, 'the union's action on the international scene shall be guided by the principles which have inspired its creation, development and enlargement and which it intends to promote throughout the world: democracy, the rule of law, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, the principles of equality and solidarity, and respect for the principles of the united nations charter and international law'. regimes to which the eu applies restrictive measures with regard to the personal and commercial interests of their leaders within the eu are regimes that violate human rights, fundamental freedoms, the rule of law and the principles of good governance. these restrictive measures are intended to promote international peace and security and the principles of article 21 teu. the measures taken must also not have a negative impact on the civilian population, in particular its most vulnerable categories. i believe that in order to increase the effectiveness of these measures and the eu's credibility internationally, it is important for the union to act unitedly and coherently.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the union needs a harmonised regime for the regulation of crossborder transfer of companies: the freedom of a company to transfer its registered office is one of the essential elements in the completion of the internal market; it is important that the transfer does not affect the rights of the parties to the proceedings before the transfer; respect for the rights of workers and their protection against dismissal is essential; at the same time, adequate protection should be ensured for minority shareholders opposing the transfer; the transfer procedure needs to be transparent and to take place under fiscal neutrality conditions; maintaining the continuity of the company's legal personality is important. i would point out, however, that the transfer should not circumvent the legal, social and fiscal conditions of the company.
in writing. − at present, companies can only transfer their registered office either by their own dissolution and the creation of a new legal entity in the host member state, or by the creation of a new legal entity in the host member state and the subsequent merger of the two companies. administrative difficulties, which generate costs and social effects without providing legal certainty, should also not be forgotten. for these reasons, i consider the recommendations contained in this report to be relevant and i support them. the interdependence between the registered office and the place of business is not justified, since the transfer of the place of business cannot be made conditional upon the transfer of the registered office. finally, companies are free to establish their own separate business and social headquarters, depending on the level of taxation, labour costs, predictability of legislation, the degree of bureaucracy, the qualifications of the workforce, etc.
in writing. − the cross-border transfer of companies' headquarters to countries outside the european union is a problem that is felt in the labour market, especially as the union's concern in this period is to increase the employment rate of the labour force. the 23 million unemployed in the union, including 5 139 000 young people under the age of 24, are a cause for concern for all the countries of europe. to counteract the effects of this phenomenon on the labour market, i believe that effective public and private management is needed, a vibrant partnership between the two areas, so as to ensure a favourable environment for investment and a better use of the structural and cohesion funds. the freedom of cross-border migration of companies, as laid down in the treaty on european union, is a fundamental aspect of the functioning of the internal market. in this context, i believe that the free movement of workers within the european area plays a key role, making a significant contribution to reducing the existing gaps between regions. the ambitious targets for reducing youth unemployment and supporting growth, set by the commission at the informal council meeting earlier this month, can be achieved by increasing the mobility of companies and workers across the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution containing recommendations to the commission on a new company law directive on crossborder transfer of registered offices because i believe it is important to remove the barriers faced by companies when they want to transfer their registered office to another member state. the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) guarantees freedom of establishment for all european companies. parliament called on the commission to submit as a matter of urgency, pursuant to article 50 (1) and (2) (g) tfeu, a proposal for a directive on the crossborder transfer of registered offices. the directive should allow companies to exercise their right of establishment by migrating to a host member state without losing their legal personality, but by becoming a company governed by the law of the host member state without having to dissolve. the transfer should take effect on the date of registration in the host member state. in order to protect third parties, registration in the host member state and deletion from the register in the home member state should be published in an appropriate manner. the cross-border transfer of the registered office should be prohibited in the case of companies that are subject to winding-up, liquidation, insolvency, suspension of payments or other similar proceedings.
in writing. − it is well known that the european union is the world's largest donor of humanitarian aid. this humanitarian aid is provided in the form of financial aid, goods, services and technical assistance. the aim of this european policy is to respond to emergencies when non-eu countries are affected, whether by natural disasters or other crises. the total eu contribution in humanitarian aid in 2010, including that of the member states, was eur 2 957 million, with the share of member states at 64% and humanitarian aid channelled through the commission at 36%. the commission should ensure that weaknesses identified during regular audits of the partners' systems are promptly corrected by the partners. external auditors should continue to strive to improve the quality of the recommendations they make to partners, taking into account their specific structures, so as to ensure the acceptance and feasibility of those recommendations. in order to make resources and actions more efficient, i believe that the eu budget should also support disaster anticipation, preparedness and prevention.
