in writing. − the frequency and magnitude of humanitarian disasters have increased alarmingly in recent times. the earthquake in haiti, the one in japan, the cyclone thane in india, the floods in pakistan or the drought in somalia would be just a few of the worst examples of catastrophe, not to mention the humanitarian effects of the civil revolutions that have engulfed the world. a growing number of refugees are in need of food, shelter, and medical care. millions of children are malnourished, and sadly, many of them, after being treated, end up in the same situation because of lack of food. furthermore, the problems caused by natural disasters are compounded by violence that prevents relief organizations from reaching those in need. in these circumstances, i join my colleagues in sounding the alarm about the efficiency of these programmes and i ask the commission to improve the controls and monitoring of humanitarian aid funds, but also to impose bilateral auditing and measurable impact indicators in cooperation with its partners in the financing of humanitarian programmes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on budgetary control of eu humanitarian aid managed by the directorate-general for humanitarian aid and civil protection (dg echo). according to the european court of auditors, the overall ex ante control, monitoring and surveillance systems, the ex post audit work and the internal audit functions of dg echo are generally effective but can be improved. the resolution calls on the commission to further improve measures to improve the efficiency of cooperation with acp partners after 2012, to reduce excessive administrative burdens on acp partners and to ensure a higher level of accountability and transparency. the european union also needs to strengthen its capacity to respond to the multiplication of major natural disasters and to ensure an adequate humanitarian budget, in order to avoid chronically under-funding humanitarian aid budget lines. at the same time, financial leeway must be guaranteed throughout the budgetary year and a coherent balance must be maintained between the financing of actions aimed at preventing humanitarian disasters and those aimed at responding rapidly to emergencies, whether man-made or natural.
in writing. - i voted for the report drawn up by mr lehne because i believe that european citizens should be encouraged to exercise their rights in transnational situations. • as a recent legal instrument in europe, the collective action for damages is not known to consumers. • the benefits of exercise are undeniable. • thus, where individual financial claims do not give them access to a court, consumers can bring a class action. • this is also the way to share the costs of such a move. • collective action gives consumers an effective means of expression. • it also ensures the smooth functioning of the single market, where citizens can communicate directly with traders. • i would stress that this mechanism eliminates discrimination between citizens as regards the value of legal proceedings and their admissibility.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution because it opposes the adoption of the draft commission regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 as regards the list of nutrition claims. the resolution initiated by parliament is intended to force the commission to come up with a better legislative proposal. the main problem with the current proposal is the possibility of displaying a reduction of minus x% sugar on food packaging. or this wording is clearly misleading. reducing the sugar has no effect on the energy content of the product as the sugar will be replaced by other carbohydrates and therefore the calorie count will remain the same. in addition, the formulation 'x% less' would distort competition in the food industry market for products already low in sugar because such a formulation compares the product with itself and not with the whole category of similar food products.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because the wording 'now contains less than x%' risks misleading consumers who have no possibility of making a comparison with the relevant previous composition of the product. in these circumstances, the new terminology proposed by the european commission would represent a step backwards from the regulations currently in force.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution and against the commission’s proposed ‘x percent less’ claim. it is of course true that the food industry should be encouraged to reformulate foods to make them healthier, and that allowing the industry to demonstrate and ‘claim’ reformulation to their customers will drive this process. i do not think anybody really disputes that. the issue is precisely how the industry is allowed to communicate this information to consumers, or, in other words, the methodology behind the health claim. and the fact remains that, with this proposed health claim, a product claiming to have ‘x percent less’ fat could still have a very high fat content compared to similar products on the market. this is why a significant majority of us in this house believe that this claim is essentially misleading. i fully support the reformulation of foods as part of the eu’s strategy on nutrition, but the commission, in cooperation with efsa, must find a better way to drive reformulation through health claims.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on amending regulation (ec) no 1924/2006 as regards the list of nutrition claims, which opposes the proposal to amend the regulation. information relating to foodstuffs must not mislead the purchaser as to their nature, properties and characteristics. the use of nutrition and health claims should be easily understood by the average consumer. unfortunately, in its proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1924/2006, the commission proposes a new nutrition claim to appear on the food as follows: now contains x% less [name of nutrient: sugars/lipids, salt, etc.]. there are already mentions such as 'reduced [name of substance]' and 'dietetic'. the word 'dietetic' means a reduction of at least 10% (for micronutrients), 25% (for sodium), 30% (for sugars/lipids) compared to other similar products. the new proposed wording is ambiguous, misleading, confusing to the consumer and may discourage manufacturers from complying with the requirements for the words 'reduced by [name of substance]' and 'dietetic' as it is easier to reduce a nutrient by 15% than by 30%. we call on the commission to present a new proposal to amend the regulation, which contains clear provisions on nutritional value and does not generate confusion for the consumer.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i appreciate the improvements made to the draft treaty on stability, coordination and governance in the economic and monetary union by the european council on 30 january 2012. • i believe that commitments on budgetary discipline will bring the fiscal stability needed for a sustainable economic recovery. • limiting the public debt and budget deficits of the states parties to the treaty will create the conditions for genuine prosperity based on economic growth rather than loans. • i also welcome the commitments made by heads of state and government to stimulate economic growth by creating new jobs and reducing unemployment, especially among young people. • i think it is very appropriate to use european funds to support the creation of smes. • i also welcome the initiative to use european unemployment funds as a guarantee for young entrepreneurs to obtain bank loans. • for romania, which is lagging behind in absorbing european funds, these measures are all the more useful, because the unused funds allocated will be able to be used to create smes and generate new jobs. • i hope that the european council in march will adopt a consistent plan for implementing these decisions, including concrete programmes to boost employment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of parliament's resolution of 2 february on the european council of 30 january 2012, in which parliament takes note of the final text of the treaty on stability, coordination and governance in the economic and monetary union and insists on the need for concrete measures to restore the economy, boost sustainable growth and employment. the treaty incorporates changes previously requested by parliament, such as: a commitment to fully apply the community method and that stability, coordination and governance will be achieved through secondary legislation with full involvement of parliament; recognition of the rights of signatory parties whose currency is not the euro to participate in euro area meetings on competitiveness, the general structure of the euro area and the basic rules to be applied in the future; the addition of a reference to the objectives of sustainable growth, employment, competitiveness and social cohesion; a commitment to incorporate the content of the agreement into the eu legislative framework within five years. parliament stressed that measures to strengthen solidarity and stimulate sustainable growth and employment were necessary for economic recovery. we demand that the president of parliament be invited permanently and participate fully in the euro summits.
in writing. - iran's nuclear programme continues to hold the attention of the international community, and events over the past few days confirm that we are far from identifying solutions. the international atomic energy agency's mission to clarify the "grey areas" of iran's nuclear programme ended on tuesday with no apparent progress. although the iaea investigation has lasted for eight years, it has not been able to determine until now whether iran's nuclear program is purely peaceful, as iranian leaders have always claimed, or has a military purpose as well. the joint vote by the european union foreign ministers last week to impose an embargo on iranian crude oil is welcome, but it is only a first step. the reaction from officials in tehran was swift, with the iranian parliament wanting to pass a bill to completely suspend iran's oil exports to european union member states before the european embargo on iranian oil takes full effect. for these reasons, efforts to continue the dialogue must be supported and intensified in order to resolve these situations through diplomatic channels.
in writing. - iran's steps to obtain enriched uranium for military purposes are in flagrant contravention of un security council resolutions and are worryingly amplifying tensions in the middle east. international pressure has so far been unsuccessful, even though it has gone as far as the european embargo on iranian oil imports, the banning of contracts and the freezing of assets of the iranian central bank. these very harsh sanctions put the regime in tehran before a clear choice: either it gives in to the losses suffered by its second-largest customer, which absorbed a quarter of its oil exports, or it resorts to military confrontation to escape economic pressure, following the model of japan's relationship with the us in the second world war. the solution to this impasse must be exclusively diplomatic, which is why i insist that the eu continue its efforts to resume dialogue. i hope that the permission iran has granted to the iaea inspectors is a clue to this.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on iran because it underlines the need for a diplomatic solution to the nuclear problem, while expressing concern at the possible military dimension of iranian uranium enrichment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it represents a valuable contribution to defining new european competences in the field of sport. • i welcome the emphasis on the educational and cultural value of sport, alongside the promotion of a healthy lifestyle. • the more we are in an olympic year, the more i would stress that the spirit of fair play and the peaceful nature of competition are essential features of sport, which enable it to fulfil its social role. • i condemn violence, hooliganism and racism in sporting events. they must be fought, because they are contrary to the very spirit of the sport. i welcome the report's provisions in this area, including the proposal to ban violent supporters from all stadiums in europe. • i regret the violent incidents that have occurred in recent months at some football matches in romania. • i hope that the law on combating violence in sport, which was promulgated earlier this year, will help to eliminate such behaviour in the context of sporting competitions. • i would like to point out that the law includes measures such as tougher penalties and a significant increase in the amount of fines for acts of violence, as well as additional training programmes for security and guard personnel.
in writing. − the lisbon treaty has brought a new eu competence in the field of sport. however, it does not create a specific article, but integrates a legal basis on sport in the section of the treaties devoted to education, vocational training and youth. thus, article 165 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union states that the objective of the eu is to promote the european dimension of sport. sport itself is an important social phenomenon and a public good. for many, it is one of the most important forms of recreation, whether they are participants or spectators. one of the great benefits of sports is that it brings people together, regardless of their background, training, religious beliefs or economic status. sport promotes the active contribution of european citizens to society and helps to stimulate a sense of social inclusion. a major threat to sport remains doping. the prevention of doping in sport must be based on a clear understanding of the complex nature of the problem and on a comprehensive combination of strategies by all authorities involved in sport to succeed in eradicating doping in sport, recognised as a serious problem that undermines the fundamental principles of sport. i therefore believe that the eu should be more actively involved in the fight against doping.
in writing. − as sport contributes to the achievement of the union's strategic objectives and is a factor of integration, insofar as it is addressed to all citizens, irrespective of sex, ethnic origin, religion, age, nationality, social status or sexual orientation, i believe that access to sport must be ensured for all citizens in many and different circumstances, such as at school, at work, as a recreational activity or within clubs and associations.
in writing. − the commission's communication is the first policy paper on sport presented since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, which gives the eu a mandate to support, coordinate and complement sport policy measures taken by the member states. sport itself is an important social phenomenon and a public good. for many, it is one of the most important forms of recreation, whether they are participants or spectators. one of the great benefits of sports is that it brings people together, regardless of their background, training, religious beliefs, gender or economic status. doping, spectator violence and disorder unfortunately remain widespread across europe and a european approach is needed that includes measures to reduce the associated risks. sport promotes the active contribution of european citizens to society and helps to stimulate a sense of social inclusion, being an important and growing economic sector that contributes significantly to growth and employment, exceeding average growth rates in value added and employment. however, sustainable sport funding is an issue that needs to be examined in more detail.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the european dimension of sport because, under article 165 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the union aims to develop the european dimension of sport by promoting the spirit of fairness and openness in sporting competitions and cooperation between organisations with responsibilities in the field of sport, and by protecting the physical and moral integrity of athletes, especially the youngest athletes. sport is important for the european economy as it directly or indirectly provides jobs for some 15 million people (5.4% of the active population) and contributes 3.65% of european gdp annually. sport contributes to the health of the population and the promotion of physical and sporting activities can contribute to significant savings in public health expenditure. we call on the member states to integrate physical education into the curriculum of all types of schools, and we stress the importance of sporting activities at all levels of education, as well as within local communities, which should be encouraged to have sports facilities with appropriate equipment. i welcome the organisation of a 'european day of sport' this year to promote the social and cultural role of amateur and professional sport and the public health benefits of sport.
in writing. − the eu's waste policy has evolved over the last 30 years through a series of environmental action plans and a legislative framework that aims to reduce negative environmental and health impacts and create a resource and energy efficient economy. in some member states, recycling and recovery are the main waste management options, with landfilling being reduced to negligible amounts, while other member states still use landfills for the majority of their waste. this is also an economic opportunity. in 2008, the €145 billion turnover of the sector accounted for around 1% of eu gdp and 2 million jobs. compliance with eu policy would help create a sector with 2.4 million jobs and a total annual turnover of 187 billion. if member states recycled 70% of their waste, they could create at least half a million new jobs across europe.
in writing. − as the european parliament has received numerous petitions concerning possible violations of the european waste management directive, i voted in favour of this resolution calling for the implementation of waste management strategies in each member state and for the european commission to monitor compliance with the provisions on sorting and recycling. i also believe that the benefits of proper waste management for both the environment and public health should be promoted among the population.
in writing. − an unsatisfactory level of waste recycling affects the health of european citizens, the health of the environment, but also has negative effects on the economies of the member states. at union level, improving waste recovery and recycling could bring savings of €72 billion per year, increase the turnover of the european waste management and recycling sector by €42 billion per year and, not least, create over 400 000 jobs by 2020. this last point is in line with the eu's 2020 strategy objectives of creating new jobs at member state level. i therefore believe that member states should make efforts to accelerate the introduction of waste management strategies in line with the cdd.
in writing. − the numerous petitions sent to the european parliament recently indicate that more and more local communities are concerned that waste management is becoming a major political and social issue. the credibility of eu legislation itself is at stake. the waste industry in the european union is a public burden, often taken over by private interests and multinational companies, which treat 60% of household waste and 75% of waste produced by companies, with an annual turnover of eur 75 billion. this is why the european commission must propose clearer and more specific criteria for the location of ecological landfills and their proximity to homes, schools or hospitals. i supported the rapporteur's position precisely because of the measures to combat the infiltration of the waste management system by organised crime and to prevent any links between organised crime organisations and the waste industry or public authorities. another important proposal in the report is that after the waste processing funds have been allocated to companies, local and/or national authorities should put in place effective financial monitoring of the use of these funds.
in writing. − i urge the commission and the member states to promote greater public awareness of the environmental benefits of efficient waste management, in particular by providing information on the importance of separate collection, the real cost of household waste collection and, in parallel, the financial return on the recovery of this household waste, while at the same time achieving the objectives of the roadmap for a resource efficient europe and the greenhouse gas reduction targets. i believe that close cooperation between member state authorities and the ep technical committees (petitions, environment) in addressing citizens' direct concerns at local level would provide an excellent opportunity to facilitate dialogue between the responsible authorities and local communities on the priorities for implementing waste management strategies and could, where it proves useful, be an effective way of resolving local disputes and taking effective action to combat any infiltration of organised crime into waste management and any links of organised crime with this sector or with public authorities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the issues raised by the petitioners in relation to the implementation of the waste management directive and related directives in the member states of the european union. between 2004 and 2010, 114 petitions were sent to parliament, pointing to possible breaches of the waste management regulatory framework, from the following member states: the commission has also adopted a number of proposals for the future of the european union, including a number of proposals for the future of the european union. according to a study carried out for the commission, about 2.6 billion tonnes of waste are generated each year in the eu, or about 6 tonnes of waste per capita, and about 90 million tonnes of waste are classified as hazardous. the same study highlights that many member states do not have sufficient capacity to prepare waste management plans, nor to carry out the inspections, controls and other actions necessary for the proper implementation of waste legislation. the resolution calls on the commission and the member states to ensure both the design and implementation of comprehensive waste management plans, including the adoption of all the objectives set by specific european legislation, and solutions for the necessary funding.
in writing. − the previous success of the daphne programme in supporting violence prevention initiatives, campaigns and policies, together with studies showing that inadequate funding of previous versions of the initiative had significantly limited its otherwise notable success, justifies the continuation of this programme. violence against children, young people and women remains one of the major challenges facing european society. 98% of european citizens are aware of the prevalence of this phenomenon, while over two thirds of european citizens (68%) believe that the european union needs to be actively involved in preventing and combating violence against these vulnerable groups. the proliferation of new forms of violence against vulnerable groups, due to the expansion of access to new communication technologies, also calls for a firm response from the european union. the continuation of the programme is a useful tool for achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy in terms of combating social exclusion and the european commission's strategy on equality between women and men 2010-2015.
in writing. - i voted for the report because violence against children, young people and women is a scourge of our society. according to several gender-based violence studies, approximately 20-25% of women in europe have been physically abused at least once, and 26% of children and adolescents reported being physically abused as children. however, victims of physical or verbal abuse often do not have the courage to speak up, making it difficult to compile relevant statistics. i therefore believe it is essential to provide adequate funding for the daphne programme, which aims to prevent and combat violence against women and children and young people.
in writing. − as daphne is the only programme of its kind aimed at combating violence against women, children and adolescents at eu level, i believe that the continuity of funding for the daphne programme is essential to maintain the measures in place and to adopt new viable measures to combat all types of violence against children, young people and women.
in writing. − since the launch of the daphne programme, over 500 ngos, public authorities or institutions have successfully implemented projects funded by the programme. the projects aimed to protect children, young people and women against all forms of violence and to achieve a high level of health protection, well-being and social cohesion. although daphné will be included in the 'rights and citizenship' programme from 2014, i believe it is essential to keep the original objectives of the programme, alongside the objectives of the new 'rights and citizenship' programme. at the same time, to achieve its objectives, we need to maintain its funding at a level comparable to previous programmes or even higher. a balanced annual distribution would ensure continuity of objectives and actions pursued to date. it is also necessary to maintain the visibility of the programme in the new generation of programmes, given its success, effectiveness and popularity at the moment.
in writing. − the daphne programme was set up in 1997 with the aim of combating violence against women, young people and children. the initiative was taken up by ngos, parliament, the european commission and experts in the field. the aim was to strengthen cooperation at european level. all member states may participate in the daphne initiative. in 2000, the daphne initiative was transformed into a multiannual funding programme, covering the years 2000-03. the programme has attracted interest from both the european union and numerous international bodies, and the funds allocated have been used to stop the commercial exploitation of children. in 2004 and 2007, the daphne ii and daphne iii programmes were launched, with an annual budget of eur 10 million. i voted for this report because i support the need to introduce the 2014 daphne programme into the rights and citizenship programme and to maintain its objectives in support of combating violence against women for the period 2014-2020, alongside the objectives of the new programme, where gender equality and the fight against violence against women are not clearly expressed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the daphne programme as it is the only programme aimed at combating violence against women, children and adolescents at eu level. according to gender-based violence studies, approximately 20-25 per cent of women in europe have been victims of physical violence at least once in their lives, and 26 per cent of children and adolescents have been victims of physical violence in childhood. the daphne programme is a key instrument to combat violence against women and to give women's organisations and other stakeholders the opportunity to take concrete action in this area. since 1997, more than 500 projects have been implemented under the daphne programme, which has attracted a great deal of interest from ngos, who have sent a large number of proposals to the commission for funding from the programme budget. continued funding of the daphne programme is essential to maintain the measures in place and to adopt new measures to combat violence against children, young people and women. we call for a reduction in administrative burden, simplification of grant application procedures and a reduction in the period between publication of the project application and conclusion of contracts, to allow as many ngos as possible to propose and implement projects through the daphne programme.
in writing. − the impact of conflict on the civilian population remains disproportionate when gender and age are considered. conflict over the past decade has affected and continues to affect predominantly children, women and the elderly. famine, epidemics, and violence against civilians continue to claim more lives than military confrontations themselves. at the same time, it is worrying that violence and abuse against these groups are still considered in some regions as legitimate tools of military confrontation. the overall picture is even more worrying when we consider that only 10% of peacekeeping personnel are women. supporting the gender dimension by conditioning union financial and institutional support to the inclusion of representatives of women's organisations in the negotiation process, together with the inclusion of a more substantial female staff in the negotiating body, may constitute appropriate strategies for achieving the objectives of the european union action plan on gender equality.
in writing. - i voted for the report by my colleague nicolai because violence against women has increased in today's conflicts. i stress the importance of the consecration of female role models in peacekeeping to highlight their contribution to the success of the mission. with their courage on the front line, they are an important element in the army's structures. at the same time, we need to raise awareness among the public and policy makers about sexual abuse in war zones. • i also support the initiative to set up specialised clinics to provide the necessary medical and psychological assistance to victims. women also need to be involved in the reconstruction of conflict zones. through their active presence on the ground, they can ensure that gender balance is maintained within institutions.
in writing. − the need to involve women in all phases of conflict prevention, crisis management and post-conflict rehabilitation has been increasingly highlighted in discussions at the highest levels. the involvement of women in the security sector and in peacebuilding is crucial to the success of these efforts, and the exclusion of women from these processes leads to the inability to respond adequately to the concerns of the entire population. in peace negotiations, women represent less than 8% of participants and less than 3% of signatories to agreements. the eu's support for peace processes must be conditional on the participation of women in the international teams leading the peace negotiations. in contemporary armed conflict, about 90 percent of the victims are civilians, and women are often the victims of rape, used as a weapon of war, and sexual exploitation, as an extreme means of survival. therefore, i have called for special attention to be paid to pregnant women and mothers with young children in the provision of food, clothing, medical services, transport and evacuation to avoid unwanted pregnancies and sexually transmitted diseases as priority areas under the 2014-2020 development financing instruments.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the situation of women in war because it calls for the prevention of abuses against women during conflicts and their involvement in peace processes. in a context where women continue to be among the main victims of armed conflict, and gender-based violence is often used systematically as a tactic of war, strategies are needed to prevent such violence, to protect and assist victims, and to prosecute perpetrators.
in writing. − as history has shown that war seems to be a largely male-dominated activity and that there is therefore reason to expect that women's special skills for dialogue and non-violence could contribute very effectively to the prevention and peaceful management of conflicts, i believe that the european union's support for peace processes should also be conditional on the participation of women in international teams leading peace negotiations.
in writing. − i voted for this report because it touches upon a serious problem, sexual violence against women and children in situations of armed conflict. i want to underline three important points. first, it strongly condemns the continued use of sexual violence against women as a weapon of war equal to a war crime, recognising the deep physical and psychological wounds that such abuses leave on the victims. second, the rapporteur calls for the inclusion of more women in the military, both in leadership positions and at ground level. third, the report stresses that education plays a key role not only in empowering women and young girls but also in combating discrimination.
in writing. − the report refers to un resolution 1325 and aims to combat sexual violence against women and children in armed conflict. i voted for this report because women need to be increasingly involved in peacekeeping operations, both in the prevention and the mediation of conflicts, especially in leadership positions, both in national governments and at the political level. at the same time, they must be included in civilian operations, because they communicate much better than men on the ground. it is also necessary for women to be present in the peacebuilding phase, because as pillars on which communities rely, they are much more aware of the practical needs that peacebuilding projects should address. although the number of women in representative institutions has increased, women's participation in peace negotiations remains low; less than 10% of those formally involved in peace negotiations. the report strongly condemns the use of sexual violence against women as a weapon of war and therefore one of the main calls made by the rapporteur is the creation of the post of eu special representative for women, peace and security.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the situation of women in war because i believe that the human rights of women and girls are an inalienable, integral and indivisible part of universal human rights. sexual violence in the form of mass rape, human trafficking and other sexual abuse of women and children continues to be unacceptably used as a tactic of war in conflict regions around the world. the effects of violence, both physical and psychological, are devastating for victims, as they are often stigmatised, rejected, mistreated and considered dishonored and, in many cases, excluded from their communities and sometimes even killed. we call on the authorities to identify and punish those who are guilty of atrocious violence against women (rape, murder, infanticide) and children in conflict zones. closer cooperation with local women's organisations is needed to establish an early warning system and possibly enable them to prevent or reduce the number of abuses themselves. we call on the eu budgetary authority to increase the financial resources allocated to promoting gender equality and women's rights in future development finance instruments for the period 2014-2020.
in writing. − i voted for the report because i believe that access to energy for all must be a central point in the global discussion and action to eradicate poverty. i find it worrying that 1.3 billion people lack access to electricity, and 2.7 billion lack clean cooking facilities. in sub-saharan africa alone, about 70% of the population is faced with a lack of access to electricity. if we want to make real progress on this, we need to have 3% of global investment in energy infrastructure by 2030. on the other hand, we have to make sure that the people really benefit from the subsidies that are being offered, like fossil fuel subsidies.
in writing. − access to modern energy services for the population is a basic condition for poverty reduction and sustainable development. yet, according to the 2011 world statistics, published by the international energy agency, some 1.3 billion people do not have access to electricity. given that energy services have a direct impact on all aspects of people's lives and livelihoods, i believe that the importance of access to energy requires much greater attention from the international community and that policies for development need to be aligned with this objective. at the same time, the european union should create within the framework of eu development cooperation a specific programme on 'energy and development' with the main objective of facilitating universal access to energy. this will make a major contribution to raising the living standards of those affected today and to eradicating poverty worldwide.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on eu development cooperation in support of the goal of universal access to energy by 2030 because i believe that lack of access to energy services does not provide conditions for a decent life and particularly affects women and children. in the least developed countries, only a minority of the population has access to the electricity grid, and small-scale, decentralized energy solutions are the only viable way to ensure universal access to energy in the years ahead. renewable energy sources, and in particular small-scale decentralised solutions, have huge potential for providing reliable, sustainable and affordable energy services to the poor, especially in rural areas of developing countries. the resolution urges the commission and the member states to endorse and commit to support the international (un) target of universal access to energy by 2030 and to align their policies and development cooperation with this target. it also encourages the commission and the member states to support, through development cooperation and appropriate financial instruments, the transfer of technologies, including technical knowledge, information and good practices, appropriate for the provision of modern energy services to the poor.
in writing. - i voted for this report because i believe that we need improved taxation at european level. the cross-border activity of european citizens and businesses alike continues to be hampered by barriers to growth and employment. we cannot talk about integrated taxation if there is no real coordination of tax policies in the eu. i also share the rapporteur's view that the main function of tax systems is to finance services of public interest: education, health services, public transport and infrastructure, and to reduce social inequalities through a fairer distribution of income and wealth.
in writing. − i voted for the report on the annual report on taxation because i believe we must ensure that our citizens have a competitive europe that creates growth and jobs. taxation remains a matter of national sovereignty and, in some cases, local government. i would stress that the increased scrutiny of budgetary procedures by the commission must be matched by better democratic scrutiny by parliament. we call on the member states to apply a growth-friendly tax approach, improving taxation arrangements and moving towards less distortive taxes without compromising the social market objective. low taxation is essential not only for the social well-being of families and households, but also for competitiveness and job creation. optimising the single market and some tax harmonisation actions could be key factors in encouraging growth and job creation. in this respect, we look forward to the commission's proposals on removing transnational tax obstacles from the path of union citizens. we welcome the commission's intention to step up its efforts to ensure that all eu citizens have access to the necessary information and advice on tax regulations within the eu.
in writing. − improving business practices at european level will also have a positive impact on the functioning of the food supply chain. increased transparency on quality is essential to stimulate competition in the single market, to increase consumer awareness and to give consumers the opportunity to make a real choice. i believe that we need active monitoring of developments in consumer products markets and ambitious legislative proposals in the revision of the framework of the markets in financial instruments directive and the market abuse directive in order to combat speculative practices that are negatively affecting european industry and distorting the single market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the schwab report because i believe that the progressive removal of barriers to trade within the eu should be further supported. • maintaining a level playing field in financial and industrial markets is essential. • an effective policy in this area will enable the union to become more competitive on the world stage. • it is necessary to correct distortions created during the crisis. state aid must not distort competition. • i would stress that their over-allocation has contributed to imbalances in public finances. • at the same time, illicit practices and abuse of a dominant position in the credit rating agency sector need to be eliminated. • i encourage the commission to actively monitor competition in the energy sector. • i would point out that the three largest players in this field account for about 75% of the electricity market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the annual report on the european union's competition policy, as i felt that stricter rules were needed in this area, especially in times of crisis. competition should be encouraged in particular in the energy, credit rating agencies and banking sectors. the problem of 'too big to fail' banks, which received state aid during the crisis, needs to be addressed. it is surprising that these institutions can benefit from unlimited access to liquidity, while the european central bank has consistently expressed its reluctance to become the lender of last resort for the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the annual report on eu competition policy because i believe that the following measures are needed at european level: completion of the internal market for all modes of transport; achievement of an open and competitive single energy market; improvement of price transparency and increased competition in the roaming market; increased consumer information and protection. we ask the commission to monitor the level of competition in the energy sector and to provide guidance to improve access to the energy grid for energy from renewable sources. we stress the need for competition in the roaming market and improved price transparency, together with the elimination of differences between roaming and national tariffs by 2015. in order to ensure a level playing field at european level, we call on the commission and the member states to ensure the implementation of the services directive and egovernment systems, thus removing barriers to cross-border service provision. we call on the commission to actively monitor developments in the markets for consumer products and to come forward with ambitious legislative proposals to combat speculative practices that are harming european industry and distorting the single market. last but not least, an interconnected, interoperable and efficient transport network is indispensable for fair competition in the context of the completion of the internal market.
a harmonised and progressive approach to intellectual property rights is essential for achieving the ambitious objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, including the digital agenda for europe. the office shall provide a forum bringing together public authorities and representatives of the private sector, ensuring the collection, analysis and dissemination of objective, comparable and reliable data on the value of intellectual property rights and infringements of those rights, identifying and promoting best practices and strategies for the enforcement of intellectual property rights and contributing to public awareness of the effects of infringement. for the european parliament, respect for the fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens is fundamental. measures aimed at protecting intellectual property must not infringe the fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens. european law, through the telecoms package, prohibits service providers from filtering content on the internet without a warrant issued by a judge. the observer should only support and limit itself to the implementation of specific european legislation.
intellectual property in any form is an important subject at union level. studies show that piracy reduces the motivation for innovation in businesses, affects jobs and poses a threat to the health of our citizens. counterfeiting affects not only luxury goods but also everyday items, including medicines and food. the scale of the phenomenon thus requires a coordinated policy approach at eu level. in addition, cooperation with third countries and the development of technical assistance programmes targeting new means of counterfeiting are required. i want to draw attention to the mandatory distinction between piracy and private use, while also informing citizens about the multiple impact of intellectual property rights infringement. transparency of decisions taken within the office for... (the president interrupts the speaker)
i believe that the proposed amendment is optimal in the context of the budgetary constraints of the european institutional system. the merger of the office's remit with that of the observer means more visibility for external decision-makers. i support the proposal to ensure transparency in the operation of this mechanism in all its procedures. they also support the exchange of good practice in the field of intellectual property rights management by smes. amendment 6 of the report is relevant - the structure thus created can support the development of new business models. the diversification of the object of the activity must be accompanied by adequate protection of the intellectual property rights used. therefore, there is a need for constant communication between the member states, the commission and the office. at the same time, european citizens must be informed and actively involved in the office's work.
with the ease of the single market, many european companies are also doing business in other eu countries. for legal and commercial reasons, information on companies needs to be accessible in real time throughout europe. the creation of the european central platform will make this possible by connecting the trade registers in the member states. it will also increase transparency by using a unique identifier for companies and their branches in other countries. this will eliminate legal uncertainties, especially in the case of the dissolution of companies with subsidiaries in several countries. the new provisions will also facilitate the necessary cooperation between national registers in the event of mergers of companies located in different states. i consider that, at the same time, adequate protection of personal data must be ensured. in this context, i welcome amendment no 21 proposed by the european parliament. i also welcome the other improvements made to the draft directive at the suggestion of parliament. i am thinking in particular of the areas regulated by means of delegated acts. clarifications on how the new european connecting system will be financed are also appropriate. i would like to point out that the national trade register office in romania has recently launched a new it platform. it offers concrete benefits for the business environment and creates the conditions for connecting with other eu countries. moreover, since the first day of operation of the new online platform, a higher number of requests than the daily average has been recorded, which highlights the advantages for users.
the purpose of the directive is a purely technical interconnection of existing national registers, and not a harmonisation of their legal requirements. part of e-government services, the interconnection of national registers concerns only the exchange of information contained in registers, and not the establishment of a trade register containing its own data. only by interconnecting will the potential of computerized record keeping be fully exploited. the commission shall, by means of implementing acts, adopt the technical specifications, which shall define: the methods of communication by electronic means for the system of interconnection of registers, the communication protocols, the technical measures to ensure minimum security standards for the communication and distribution of information within the system of interconnection of registers, the detailed list of data transmitted for the purpose of exchanging information between registers, the data set necessary for the platform to perform its functions, as well as the method of storage, use and protection of such data, the structure and use of the unique identifier for communication between registers.
mr president, the proposed directive contributes, firstly, to the integration of the single market. secondly, it contributes to a more efficient use of the resources of the member states’ judicial systems thirdly, it contributes to increased market transparency by easy access to relevant information. eu economic actors will benefit from updated and reliable information on potential business partners and on foreign legal systems. they need this information. this makes them able to assess to a larger extent the risks and benefits of starting a business or doing business in a particular country. fourthly, it contributes to stronger, longer-term and more secure cross-border business. fifthly, all of this will improve legal certainty and reduce the incidence of legal actions in commercial matters throughout the eu. those are some benefits of this directive. using the e-justice portal as an electronic access point to legal provisions, information about registers and european and national databases is an inspired choice. initially designed to support judicial and police cooperation, this tool is now being extended to administrative cooperation in relation to the functioning of the single market. this will consolidate the utility and reliability of the platform and will provide additional incentives for enhanced mutual trust between member states’ administrations. the concrete procedures and technical specifications are being left for subsequent commission implementing acts. this is why the commission needs to foresee efficient means to ensure that data protection requirements will be observed and enforced effectively by all member states. particular attention should be paid to such procedures as effective automatic data transfers between registers, as provided for in the amended recital 15. overall, the new directive has the potential to enhance competition, in parallel with trust, by building confidence in the business environment of the internal market.
i support the proposal to create an internal market for payment services in euro, which will in practice considerably facilitate the system available to european consumers, who will be able to use a single payment method and a single type of account for transferring money within the european union. this initiative will increase the efficiency of cross-border payments, transforming a segmented european market into a single one and bringing economic benefits. as you know and as has been said, the european commission estimates that these benefits could amount to billions of euros within six years, through cost reductions. i also welcome the establishment of deadlines for the transition from the current national systems to the generalised one, so that the transition process is not unduly prolonged. we have seen how the original strategy adopted by the european executive for the transfer of credit, which was that the transition should be done by the private sector at a flexible pace, has not worked. from the figures i have, in february 2011, two and a half years after the launch of the initiative, only 15.7% of the total credit transfer in the euro area was through the european payment system. last but not least, i believe that consumer protection must be ensured throughout the transition to the new system and that is why, commissioner, i suggest that information programmes be set up to which the banking sector is practically obliged to contribute actively.
the single euro payments area is essential for the completion of the internal market. the close link between invoices and payments provides the single euro payments area with a platform for the creation of an interoperable european electronic invoicing system. in turn, the widespread adoption of electronic invoicing will stimulate the migration of financial instruments to the single euro payments area. for these mutual benefits to be realised, the e-invoicing standard needs to be consistent with the iso 20022 standard for financial services messages, which is used by the single euro payments area both electronic invoicing and the single euro payments area should also be integrated into the electronic public payment systems operated by public authorities in the member states and by the institutions of the european union. i would ask the commissioner for more details on the developments mentioned above.
for the single market to work properly, europe needs safe and efficient payment systems. national plans cannot provide sufficient impetus for a rapid and comprehensive migration to the single euro payments area. sepa is the basic building block in the creation of an internal payments market. it will help to reduce costs and allow substantial savings to be made. for example, the potential benefits of sepa could amount to eur 300 billion over a six-year period. it is important to set a common deadline for the migration of direct debits and credit transfers into euro. at the same time, it is essential to regulate multilateral interchange fees for direct debits. i believe, however, that more efforts need to be made to actively promote sepa products.
member of the commission. - madam president, i thank marielle gallo, on behalf of the committee of which she is a member, and many of you for asking me about this aspect of the future legislative proposal on collective management of copyright. what's the problem? putting collective management at the service of the single market in the age of the internet, bringing this copyright to life - as i said earlier in a more general way on intellectual property - in the present day, in the present day, mrs gallo, which, as you know, is the age of the internet and the age of europe. collective management of copyright is a complex issue. it affects the management of online rights but also offline rights, not only for authors but also for performers, actors, producers, publishers and even broadcasters. we immediately think of the large management companies, such as those responsible for the rights of authors themselves, but, ladies and gentlemen, we must not forget the companies that receive the remuneration linked to reprography or the right of sequence. if we look exclusively at the collective management of copyright as such, this is a sector - mrs gallo recalled - worth €7.5 billion worldwide, and €4.6 billion in europe alone, for nearly a hundred management companies. collective copyright management is complex, because these management companies - there are about a hundred of them in our country - while being strongly rooted in the various member states and actively participating in the cultural diversity in each of our states, must also adapt - as i mentioned earlier - to the internet and to a multi-territorial demand that is developing rapidly. this collective management must be at the service of the rightholders as much as it is at the service of the users. but now it is time for this collective management to be more at the service of the single market. the use of collective management is primarily voluntary and is the choice most often made by authors. it allows the licensing of the largest possible number of users and the widest possible coverage of rights. it must protect the interests of those entitled and ensure the remuneration, not only, as you said, mrs gallo, of those who are the most famous, the stars, but also of those who are less well known and who are entitled to the same protection. these are balances which are difficult to strike and the question of collective management divides many stakeholders. opinions and positions are very often divergent. at the same time, the market is changing very rapidly. yesterday's needs are no longer today's needs. ladies and gentlemen, having recalled the complexity and differences of approach which partly explain, madam gallo, the time i have taken to work seriously and conscientiously on this proposal, i should like to say a few words about this future proposal for a directive. in its communication of 20 may 2011, to which you referred, the commission announced its intention not only to cover the management of copyright related to online music but also to establish a common set of rules for all collective management organisations, whatever their activity. this decision was welcomed, particularly in the member states. we are therefore working towards this objective by broadening the scope of our future proposal. all interested parties were consulted. this consultation phase is now over. i did it - i did it a second time - without improvising, seriously, and listening to everyone. that is why i will be able, on behalf of the commission, to present - you have asked me to set a deadline - this proposal for a directive next spring. i think that the commission's proposal is a good one. i've asked my staff to work on two fronts. the first pillar concerns horizontal rules on transparency and governance. these are harmonised rules on transparency and governance which will apply, if you will, to all collective management companies in europe. these rules should create a level playing field for all companies and improve their functioning for the benefit of all rightholders, including nationals of other member states. it cannot be overlooked that each collective management company manages on its territory the rights (for example, broadcasting rights) not only of its own members but also of the members of foreign management companies. that is the first horizontal part of this future and next proposal. the second part concerns specific rules for online music. it's connected to the companies that manage copyright for online music. while ensuring a high level of transparency and a better quality of services to authors and users, we want to propose a clear legal framework, ladies and gentlemen, to facilitate the granting of multi-territorial licences by management companies for online music. these licences should also encourage the grouping of directories, the sharing of directories, in order to reduce the number of licences needed. in this approach, the commission will take into account, as far as possible, the position expressed by the european parliament in several resolutions and working papers. i just wanted to let you know that i'm personally working with all my teams on this case. we shall be ready in the next few months, and the time that has passed, which may have seemed long to you, is a useful time to propose a good, solid and balanced text. i am convinced that our proposal will help to accelerate the creation of this digital single market. collective management companies will benefit from a much clearer legislative framework, which will harmonise and define the basic principles governing their operation. in the online music sector, authors will benefit from the benefits of a much wider exploitation of their works. finally, citizens, and especially young people, will benefit from a wider range of innovative services. that is the direction in which we are working on these two aspects and that is the timeframe within which i think i will be able - subject to the approval of the european commission and the college - to present this text to you in the very next few weeks.

in writing. − the european union's economic prosperity is based on a process sustained by creativity, cultural diversity and innovation, the driving forces of a rapidly evolving knowledge society. protection of intellectual property rights (ipr) is therefore beneficial for the business environment, innovators and consumers, and those involved in cultural creations. in order to encourage greater cooperation between member states on ipr protection, the commission has set up the european monitoring centre for counterfeiting and piracy. the observatory and its increasingly numerous activities and tasks need to be embedded in a functional and cost-effective institutional structure, which enables it to carry out its tasks effectively and to support the fight against ipr infringements. i also believe that it would be beneficial for european citizens, business and public administration if the observatory developed a public platform accessible online, providing information and examples of best practices, awareness-raising methods that can be downloaded free of charge, and capacity-building initiatives on the many legislative and non-legislative means of combating ipr infringements.

in writing. − the european commission wants to replace the national euro payments system with a european one. the single euro payments area (also known as sepa) is based on the development of common payment services at european union level, which are to replace the current national payment services. this means, in short, that national and cross-border payments, bank transfers and direct debits are subject to the same legal regime. there are many problems with pay differentials in the european union. i support this initiative and would like to see consumer rights protected. this initiative should simplify the whole process and lead to increased competition which would normally lead to lower prices for services.
in writing. − in the context of the creation of a single euro payments area (sepa), real competition will be achieved and the differences in treatment between cross-border and national payments will be eliminated. this will bring significant benefits to the european economy and provide european individuals and legal entities with cost-effective, user-friendly and reliable euro payment services. i consider the proposal for a regulation to be beneficial as it seeks to simplify the legislation on accessibility for direct debit and credit transfer into one provision. simplifying payment processing will have direct beneficial effects for stakeholders, including public administrations, legal entities and natural persons. for consumers, who are increasingly mobile, the changes to standardised cross-border payments will eliminate the need to maintain several payment accounts in different countries. this will automatically lead to lower costs for them and increased operability.
in writing. − i voted in favour of parliament's legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation laying down technical requirements for credit transfers and direct debits in euro, as the creation of an integrated market for electronic payments in euro, without distinguishing between national and cross-border payments, is necessary for the proper functioning of the internal market. the single euro payments area (sepa) aims at the development of common payment services at union level, which are to replace the current national payment services. as a result of the introduction of common and open payment standards, rules and practices and through integrated payment processing, sepa is to offer secure, cost-effective, reliable and user-friendly euro payment services to natural and legal persons in the union. they should apply to sepa payments at national and international level, under the same basic conditions and with the same rights and obligations, regardless of their location within the union. it is of the utmost importance that all stakeholders, in particular union citizens, are adequately and timely informed in order to be fully prepared for the changes brought about by sepa.
in writing. - there is a consensus that the possibilities of the european single market are not being used to their full potential. i welcome the fact that this consensus is being translated into concrete decisions. the full use of the single market requires instruments and sepa is one such instrument. the free movement of labour and capital and the need to help european smes in practice to enjoy the benefits of the single market will only become a reality if the european banking system, today fragmented by the borders of the member states, becomes a system that operates under harmonised rules. the possibility of using one bank account and one banking service provider in the eu is an advantage for the average citizen, for companies, but especially for smes. the new sepa rules are all the more important as they will lead to the strengthening of the internal market in many areas, such as financial services and e-commerce. today's overwhelming vote in the ep plenary is more than a vote in favour of sepa, it is a vote of confidence in the euro.
first of all, i'd like to thank everyone involved for their efforts to find a compromise on this program. in the european union, poverty is deepening, and millions of people cannot afford a hot meal for more than a few days at a time. over 18 million european citizens have benefited from food through this programme. therefore, reducing its allocation or funding from national budgets, especially in a time of economic crisis, would have been a catastrophic decision. i would like to stress the need to keep this programme with cap funding beyond 2013 and i would like to express my concern at the statements by the german and french governments about its elimination. i want to convey to them that the right to food is a fundamental one. moreover, in a difficult time of deep economic crisis, we have a huge debt to the most vulnerable categories of citizens. just as states have a duty to help those who cannot help themselves, so the european union must show that solidarity is not just a principle on paper.
i don't think i need to make any more arguments in favor of the food distribution program for the most disadvantaged. even if it comes at the last minute, the approval of its funding is a hand out to our fellow citizens who face special problems. this programme, which has been proving its effectiveness for 25 years, is a sign of a europe of solidarity and unity. more than one in 30 europeans have received food aid in recent years, and i want to remind you that of the 40 countries in the world that are most food-vulnerable, four are members of the european union. i congratulate the commission on its efforts to break the deadlock, i congratulate the council on its wisdom and compassion, and i congratulate the rapporteur on all his work. at the same time, i believe that the european parliament should already be thinking about the future of this programme after 2013. finding the appropriate legal basis, together with the council and the commission, is the first step we have to take. are the costs of the program high? no, it's one euro a year from each of the 500 million europeans. the united states spent $85 billion on food assistance last year, 15 percent more than in 2010. over 43 million people, more than one in every eight americans, have benefited from this aid. in this period, we talk a lot about productivity, about growth, about innovation. i am convinced beyond a shadow of a doubt that these are the right solutions for resuming economic growth, but we have no moral right to ignore the poor of europe. the food aid program has worked for a quarter of a century and must remain a safety net for those in need.
the rise in the prices of basic foodstuffs in recent years has severely eroded the purchasing power of european citizens. the economic and financial crisis in the european union has had a significant impact, systematically increasing the social vulnerability of the union's most disadvantaged citizens. continuing the food distribution program is a vital measure in the current economic and political context. it could provide strong support for 18 million europeans without imposing additional burdens on national budgets. we need a transitional solution very urgently for the remaining years of the current multiannual financial framework. the proposal has been stalled in the council for two years and we are pleased to finally have a compromise. i would like to thank the commission and commissioner ciolos for their efforts. i therefore support the adoption of measures to resume the granting of this aid as soon as possible by the union, and the proposal by the epp group to extend the programme into the next multiannual financial perspective.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, this is quite an experience: 22 people are on the list to speak and there are only 5 in the chamber. i am saying this by way of response to the remark of honourable member werner langen, who mentioned that 18 reactions to olli rehn’s speech was quite a low number. i could not agree more, but his reaction and his conclusion on that number was that the commission did not do the job properly. i do not accept that conclusion. olli rehn is doing a great job. he could not be here today, but i can assure you he has to be active in the solution for greece. having said that i think that it is quite remarkable that as i began my speech mr bloom was saying ‘i have to go’, ‘i am hungry’. this type of reaction is not in keeping with the importance of the issue we are dealing with. i am more than willing to do the job and to give the answers that i have available on this subject. the subject is too important not to reply in full. i completely agree and, therefore, arguments in favour of pursuing eurobonds are clear. stability bonds would provide all participating member states with more secure access to refinancing, and reduce or eliminate the need for costly support and rescue measures for member states temporarily excluded from market financing. stability bonds would enhance financial stability and they would provide the source of more robust collateral for all banks in the euro area. this would reduce banks’ vulnerability to any deterioration in the credit ratings of individual member states, and other institutional investors would benefit from a more homogeneous and robust safe asset. but stability bonds are not a measure to address the current crisis. they are the next step in eu integration and a tool to limit the risk of future crises. stability bonds can make the euro-area financial system more resilient to future adverse shocks and so reinforce financial stability. we also need to be clear about legal, technical and political challenges. for example, the issuance of stability bonds under joint and several guarantees would, a priori, lead to a situation where the article 125 ban on bail-outs would be breached. in this case, an amendment to the treaty would be necessary. i do not need to explain to you the likelihood of success of such changes in the current circumstances. in so far as the introduction of stability bonds will increase the pooling of risk between participating countries, this might have the effect of weakening market discipline. this means that it is of crucial importance that all participating member states have confidence in other participants’ economic and budgetary policies, and thus a higher degree of control over each other’s policies. therefore, an increase in surveillance and in intrusiveness in the design and implementation of national fiscal policies would be warranted beyond the recent initiatives, and by that i am talking about the six-pack, the fiscal compact treaty and article 136 regulations proposed by the commission. the very existence of stability bonds could fundamentally alter budgetary processes, notably via the allocation mechanisms. the participating member states would collectively decide and approve individual budgetary plans through the allocation of bonds. all these issues require careful further reflection. the commission will therefore continue seeking the views of key stakeholders in this respect and will therefore consult, in particular, member states, financial market operators, financial market industry associations and academics within the eu and beyond. once sufficient clarity has been established on all those issues, the commission will give its views on the appropriate way forward. i sincerely hope that those who remain in the chamber and who are interested in the debate can accept this response in the name of olli rehn.
in writing. i consider it necessary to pool the risks faced by member states on financial markets. in the context of the threat of a downgrade of france by the credit rating agencies and the increasing difficulties faced by germany in financing itself a few months ago, it is clear that the refusal to implement eurobonds will only worsen the current situation for all the member states of the union. the creation of a single european bond market, alongside the setting of debt reduction targets for member states under the supervision of the european executive, would allow the euro to stabilise, increase liquidity and achieve significantly lower interest rates. a single currency cannot function without a common bond market and a common fiscal policy, and the euro has the potential to become a global reserve currency. in this context, i welcome the european commission's initial proposal on the stability bonds. as a result of the consultations, it should rapidly present a roadmap for the launch of this instrument.
the commission proposal for a decision of september 2010 establishing the first radio spectrum policy programme sets out policy guidelines and objectives for the strategic planning and harmonisation of the use of radio spectrum by 2015. the radio spectrum policy programme reflects the importance of the availability and efficient use of spectrum for the internal market for electronic communications and for other eu policy areas such as transport, research, earth observation, satellite navigation systems, environmental protection and combating global warming. i welcome the fact that the amendments which i proposed and which were adopted by parliament were also included in the agreement reached by the council and parliament. they shall aim at including in the policy objectives the following objectives: 1. in article 3 (c), to close the digital divide and achieve the objectives of the digital agenda by ensuring that all union citizens have access to broadband at a rate of at least 30 mbps by 2020 and by enabling the union to have the highest possible speed and capacity for broadband services; 2. in article 3 (l), to stimulate the accessibility of new products and technologies to consumers so that the switch to digital technology and the efficient use of the digital dividend are supported by consumers. i also welcome the inclusion in article 4 (3) of the need to pay special attention to standards for equipment to be used by disabled people. the decision provides for an inventory of the current use of radio spectrum for commercial and public purposes. the inventory will be managed by the commission, which will adopt implementing acts by july 2013 to define the modalities and formats for the collection and transmission of data by member states. the commission shall submit a report to the council and parliament on the implementation of this decision no later than two years after its entry into force and shall carry out a review of its implementation by 31 december 2015.
europe needs a flexible and coordinated radio spectrum policy. it will contribute to the creation of a pan-european telecommunications market. radio spectrum is essential for the digital society. it is important that the eu takes the lead in the world in terms of broadband speeds, mobility, coverage and capacity. the digital gap must be eliminated. the feasibility of extending unlicensed frequency allocations for wireless access systems shall be assessed. this technology needs to be accessible in rural areas, not just urban areas. i also draw attention to the protection measures against electromagnetic fields. the use of radio spectrum must not, however, endanger the health of citizens and it is therefore essential to ensure continuous monitoring of the effects of spectrum use.
as a limited resource, the use we make of the radio spectrum is of particular importance if we are to maximise the benefits for end-users and private operators. the agreement recently reached by the european parliament and the council demonstrates the european institutions' determination to take the lead globally in this technology. providing eu-wide internet access, high-speed connections and the standardisation of the 800 mhz frequency for electronic communications can help to bridge the digital divide, as studies show that data traffic is continuing to increase worldwide. in view of this, it is necessary to consider the usefulness of standardising other frequency bands. european regulation and harmonisation of spectrum allocation rules will provide the basis for innovation and increased competitiveness, helping us to meet the europe 2020 objectives.
in writing. we have been talking more and more about the development of the digital single market lately, given the trend towards digitisation and the evolution of the consumer habits of europeans. the demand for mobile data services has doubled in recent times and the trend is still rising. as the commissioner pointed out, european consumers are increasingly using audiovisual content on mobile devices, and this requires better mobile broadband services and, of course, sufficient radio spectrum. the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu concerning the definition of the concept of 'originating products' and the definition of the concept of 'originating products' and the definition of the concept of 'originating products' in accordance with article 3 of directive 2014/25/eu. the release of the 800 mhz band and its availability for electronic communications services will remove technical constraints for the development of new mobile data services. the allocation of at least 1200 mhz for mobile data services by 2015 is another positive measure in this respect. i believe that the agreement we are voting on tomorrow is one that will bring us closer to the goals of the digital agenda and contribute to the eu's competitiveness, and i will support it wholeheartedly.
