in writing. − the participation of iceland, the principality of liechtenstein, norway and switzerland in the committees which assist the european commission in implementing and developing the schengen acquis gives these associated states the opportunity to express any objections related to the application of the provisions in question. the countries concerned are thus involved in the legislative process in this area but not in decision-making. it is therefore necessary to formalise their association with the schengen comitology in accordance with an appropriate procedure. the proposal for a decision in this regard is welcomed to ensure equal treatment of associated states as observers through a single agreement and on the basis of clearly defined rights and obligations. the final decision on the application of the measures adopted in the committees is taken by each country individually, as stipulated in the initial clauses of the association agreements. as a romanian mep, i express the hope that the principle of equal treatment will be respected in all aspects of the schengen process, including in the acceptance of accession of countries that have already fulfilled all the formal criteria.

in writing. − member states' employment policies and especially job creation are one of the most important issues at the moment, as rising unemployment has generated numerous protests in several eu member states last year and this year. i am aware of the labour market problems in all eu countries at the moment, problems accelerated by the financial crisis, which is why i believe that the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy are very relevant. the eu must encourage member states in their efforts to develop their economies on the basis of an inclusive, highly skilled and, not least, demand-driven labour market. however, the role of the member states in this area should not be overlooked either, as they can find significant support from the european social fund, which makes considerable sums available to them in order to create an increasingly competitive labour market. i therefore support this report and consider these guidelines to be fully justified and absolutely necessary for the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and, in particular, the employment objectives.
in writing. − the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that the member states and the union are to develop a coordinated employment strategy and promote a trained, skilled and adaptable workforce and labour markets that are able to react rapidly to economic developments. the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth proposed by the commission sets five main objectives to guide the action of member states, including the european employment strategy. but in the context of the economic crisis, we risk that all this will remain a dead letter on paper. agree that the employment guidelines adopted in 2010 should remain stable until 2014 so that efforts are focused on their implementation and that member states should consider using the european social fund to implement the employment guidelines. unfortunately, i cannot share the commission's optimism in this respect, since most of the measures adopted, and even those envisaged, are necessary but not sufficient, as the rising rate of unemployment at european level shows.
in writing. − the european union has, and always has had, a highly regarded social model. however, there has been a recent decline in the member states' labour law, social rights and employment policies. i believe it is essential that member states take action in the current economic crisis to deliver on their commitments to increase employment levels, improve individual skills and create employment opportunities to reduce poverty and increase social inclusion. i believe that at union level, a policy of european solidarity and cohesion is needed, with concrete legislative, fiscal and financial measures. it is vital that member states respect those commitments in order to achieve more effective exchanges of best practices and experience in the field of combating social exclusion and poverty reduction, in close alignment with the poverty eradication objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the employment policies guidelines for the member states, because it represents an important step in maintaining the continuity of the european union’s strategy for growth and employment, europe 2020. i am very much looking forward to the member states following these guidelines while adopting employment policies, in particular because of the stress on a skilled, trained and adaptable workforce – a real engine for the future growth of europe. in these days of economic and financial problems for the european union, employment and growth become probably the most sensitive issues for the whole political debate. i believe that europe should recognise job creation as a central goal for the revitalisation of our economy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the employment guidelines and policies of the member states, taking into account the following considerations. in view of the economic and social difficulties faced by the member states, coordination of economic and employment policies is absolutely necessary. it is important that member states, through their national reform programmes, give priority to developing the labour market, reducing unemployment, especially among young people, and creating new jobs. now more than ever, we need integrated policies that address both economic and social issues. we cannot talk about sustainable economic growth without also considering sustainable job creation. member states must implement appropriate fiscal policies to support investment and encourage smes to create new jobs, and to make efficient use of the structural funds. thus, by supporting smes and using the structural funds, new jobs will be created and youth unemployment can be tackled.
in writing. − i voted for the resolution on the proposal for a council decision on guidelines for the employment policies of the member states because, due to the economic and financial crisis, the unemployment rate has risen alarmingly in the eu. according to eurostat, over 23 million people in europe are unemployed. the guidelines set out in decision 2010/707/eu will continue to be applied by the member states in 2012. employment policies should be geared towards: increasing labour market participation, reducing structural unemployment and promoting quality jobs, developing a skilled workforce that meets labour market needs and promoting lifelong learning, improving the quality and performance of education and training systems at all levels and increasing participation in tertiary or equivalent education, and promoting social inclusion and combating poverty. these guidelines aim to achieve the eu's key 2020 targets, such as raising the employment rate to 75%, reducing the school drop-out rate to below 10%, having at least 40% of young people in higher education and lifting at least 20 million people out of the risk of poverty and exclusion.
in writing. − although the eu enjoys, on average, one of the highest standards of living in the world, some people are unable to meet their food needs. it is estimated that there are 43 million people at risk of food poverty in the eu, that is, people who cannot afford to eat a full meal every two days. the programme for the most deprived persons supports the provision of food to these particularly vulnerable persons or families who are in a difficult situation. charitable organisations and ngos rely on the eu's contribution to supporting these people in need. for example, 51% of the products distributed in 2010 by the european federation of food banks came from this programme. each year, more than 18 million people in 20 eu member states benefit from food aid distributed under this programme. in romania, in 2010, over 2.8 million people - pensioners, people with no or very low income, people with disabilities - benefited from this programme. i therefore believe it is essential to find a solution quickly that overcomes the current problems and can make use of the funds available.
in writing. − the programme for the distribution of free food to the most deprived citizens of the european union, launched in 1987 under the common agricultural policy (cap), currently provides aid for 18 million people living in poverty in 20 eu member states. in the eu, 43 million people are at risk of food poverty, a figure that will increase as a result of the economic and financial crisis and rising food prices. if no action is taken, the funds for this programme will have to be reduced in 2012 to eur 133 million, compared to eur 500 million in 2011. the suspension of this aid programme without any prior warning or preparation will have serious repercussions for the most vulnerable eu citizens. a way must be found to continue the food distribution system for the needy in 2012 and 2013 (the remaining years of the current funding period) and also in the 2014-2020 funding period.
in writing. − i believe it is vital that this support continues into the future and i believe that european support for the disadvantaged should be at a level comparable to this year, knowing that the common agricultural policy has social components and that the needy must continue to be assisted. on the basis of the principle of european solidarity, member states which oppose the programme must demonstrate their understanding of the situation of the poor and accept the continuation of the programme within the parameters required, which is also a sign of solidarity at union level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the council position at first reading because the distribution of food products to the most deprived persons is too urgent an issue to be delayed any further. a second reading procedure would only have meant more suffering for the people in need, a scenario which is simply unacceptable. therefore, i think that the position voted for, by overcoming the stalled situation in the council, has to be considered as a valid transitional solution for the remaining years of the current mff. i would also like to express my desire for such a crucial programme to be maintained, or even enhanced, after 2013. too many people still depend on food distribution in europe and we – as representatives of the european people – must undertake this as a personal commitment.
in writing. − over time, the intervention stocks made available by the community have proved to be a safe and stable source of food supplies for the most deprived. the need to supply food has increased as a result of the substantial increase in the needy population and food prices affecting their food security. i believe that both appropriate national policies and the mobilisation of civil society are needed to provide food security for all. in addition, the modification of the community programme will generate a strong cohesion element and serve as a model for the distribution of food to the most deprived. this proposal seeks to maintain full union funding for the programme. the maximum level of community financing will be maintained in the future, but in order to ensure budgetary stability, an annual ceiling of eur 500 million is provided for the eu financial contribution.
in writing. − the need to distribute food aid across the eu is driven by the increase in the number of people in need as new countries have joined, but also by the rise in food prices. every citizen of the union has the right to be guaranteed access to food. funds should therefore be allocated to adequately cover the cost of purchases on the market for intervention stock. it is the eu's responsibility to secure food resources and reduce insecurity among its citizens. investing in people's well-being is an essential component of the healthy development of each individual, contributing to the prosperity of the union. the cold wave that has hit central and south-eastern europe, including my country, romania, during this period, attests to the importance of implementing a rigorous food distribution plan. preventive measures such as the one we are discussing today can reduce the suffering of the disadvantaged and, in the long term, remove barriers to the eu's development to its full capacity. these are some of the reasons why i am in favour of the report on the distribution of food to people in need.

in writing. − i welcome the decision, following negotiations with the council, to continue the distribution of food to the most deprived persons for the period 2012-13. i would like to stress, however, that this positive vote on the compromise text does not at all support the member states which envisage the complete elimination of this aid by the end of 2013. on the contrary, i believe that the current economic situation shows us more than ever how important it is to continue this programme for the next period, 2014-2020.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft recommendation for the second reading on the council's first reading position with a view to adopting a regulation for the continuation of food distribution to the most deprived persons in the union. given the urgency of the situation created by the two-year deadlock in the council, we believe that any delay in the adoption of this regulation would only prolong the suffering of the most disadvantaged eu citizens who could benefit from the food distribution programme. the amended commission proposal of 3 october 2011 and the council position under examination incorporated all the substantive amendments of parliament at first reading on the maintenance of full union funding for the programme. the current level of eu funding of 100% is maintained and, in order to ensure budgetary stability, an annual ceiling of eur 500 million is foreseen. the idea of eu food was also taken up. we stress the need to continue this programme of food distribution to the most deprived persons beyond 2013 and call on the commission to come forward swiftly with a legislative proposal to this effect. in 2010, over 18 million people benefited from this programme.
in writing. − access to the radio spectrum is essential for a very wide range of activities, from telephony and broadcasting to transport and space applications. in order for european citizens, both in urban and rural areas, to benefit from all the benefits of digital technology, it is of the utmost importance to ensure broad and equitable access to the radio spectrum. better use of spectrum can also provide a boost to the european economy, as high-speed wireless services will foster competitiveness and economic development. following today's report, the 800 mhz band will be made available for electronic communications services in all eu member states by 1 january 2013 and an appropriate spectrum allocation for wireless services will be made, totalling at least 1200 mhz by 2015, thus providing the best capacity for european industries. the digital economy is the key to the future, and the lines drawn in this report will ensure economic success in the future.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the council's first reading position with a view to adopting a decision on the establishment of a multiannual programme for radio spectrum policy. the union needs a programme covering the internal market in all union policy areas involving the use of radio spectrum, such as policies on electronic communications, research, technological development, space, transport, energy and audiovisual. the policy objectives to be implemented by the member states and the commission include: ensuring sufficient availability of spectrum, maximising spectrum flexibility, increasing efficiency of spectrum use through general authorisations and spectrum flexibility, avoiding distortion of competition, avoiding harmful interference and disturbance, harmonising technical conditions, ensuring the protection of public health. this programme shall ensure the creation of a very broad-based inventory of current use of the spectrum between 400 mhz and 6 ghz in order to create a flexible and coordinated european spectrum policy. the commission shall also, in cooperation with member states, assess the appropriateness and feasibility of extending unlicensed frequency allocations for wireless access systems, including local radio networks, to allow, for example, increased use of, for example, wifi technology.
in writing. − the european dairy market has been and is characterised by a pronounced imbalance and low predictability, due primarily to unfair trading practices in the production, processing and distribution process. the main actors who suffer from this phenomenon are, on the one hand, farmers, who, as we have seen, often happen not to know the price they will receive for their milk, but also the final consumers, who do not pay the price that starts from the producer but the amount imposed by all the other factors involved in the process of processing and distribution. i believe that there is a need for the accountability of operators in the dairy chain and this can be achieved through the use of formal written contracts. i also believe in strengthening the bargaining power of producers with processing plants. last but not least, another reason why i am voting for this report is its purpose: to promote good practice and to make the market more transparent in general. because, in my view, this is the only way we can talk about the dairy sector in the eu in the future. i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the abolition of quotas for dairy products in the eu in 2015 requires an increase in the bargaining power of producers, by concluding firm written contracts to strengthen the responsibility of operators in the dairy chain, and by encouraging producers to organise. the example of switzerland, which gave up its quotas in 2009, is useful to understand the impact of the new system and to anticipate its negative effects. the decline in demand and the maintenance of stable production have led to a collapse in prices on the european milk market in recent years. the increase in the price of raw materials in recent years has led to higher feed costs and production costs, including energy. i therefore believe that, in these circumstances, there is a need to increase the bargaining power of producers with processing units, in order to distribute added value more equitably along the supply chain. this would ensure a rational development of production and help to maintain fair living conditions for farmers in the dairy sector.
in writing. − with the report voted by parliament today, milk producers will have more bargaining power to get fair prices for raw milk, which will help them prepare for milk quotas in 2015. the current provisions will allow farmers' organisations to negotiate raw milk prices themselves without breaching competition law. i supported this report because, through its amendments, the european parliament requested the commission to prepare two reports assessing the situation of milk producers in less-favoured areas, one by july 2014 and the other by the end of 2018.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report. the measures proposed are certainly useful, but we must admit that they are not sufficient. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe, in particular the countries of the former soviet union, the former soviet union and the former soviet union. at the same time, the eu must continue and implement parliament's efforts to ensure a balance along the entire food supply chain, i.e. between producers, distributors, processors and traders, for the benefit of european consumers.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 on contractual relations in the milk and milk products sector. between 2007 and 2009 there were significant developments in the milk and milk products sector. a series of extreme weather conditions caused a significant decrease in supply, which led to a rapid and considerable increase in prices. subsequently, the financial and economic crisis adversely affected eu dairy producers and accentuated price volatility. i believe that the use of written contracts which comply with certain formal conditions, contain basic elements and are concluded before delivery could increase awareness and strengthen the responsibility of operators in the dairy chain to take better account of market signals, improve the allocation of prices, adapt supply to demand and help to avoid unfair trading practices. in order to ensure a stable future for the dairy sector after the abolition of quotas in 2015, the bargaining power of producers with processing units should be increased, which would lead to a more equitable distribution of added value along the supply chain.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it amends appropriately the rules of procedure of the european parliament on own-initiative reports. • without prejudice to the relevance of such reports and the useful debate on them, article 48 (2) in its amended form will allow for a greater concentration of the european parliament's work on the legislative process. • this is necessary, also in view of the new tasks and powers conferred on parliament by the treaty of lisbon. • at the same time, a clearer definition of the character of each own-initiative report from the authorisation stage will generate greater efficiency in the process of drafting, amending and adopting the text. the role of the specialised committees as the central framework for negotiations with a view to finding a compromise will thus be reaffirmed. • last but not least, i would stress the usefulness of clarifying the criteria for determining the strategic nature of an own-initiative report. they are designed to ensure the positive effects of this amendment to the regulation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of rule 48 (2) of parliament's rules of procedure on own-initiative reports, as i believe that the system applicable to this type of report needs to be improved, particularly at the plenary stage. motions for resolutions contained in own-initiative reports shall be dealt with by parliament in accordance with the procedure for the presentation of a summary. amendments to them shall be admissible for consideration in the plenary only if they have been tabled by the rapporteur to take account of new information or have been tabled by at least one tenth of the members. at the same time, political groups may table motions for resolutions to replace them, in accordance with rule 157 (4) on the admissibility of amendments. a political group or at least 40 members may table a motion for a resolution to replace a non-legislative motion for a resolution contained in a committee report, but without exceeding the length of the resolution of the committee responsible. the proposal shall be submitted without amendments for approval by parliament by a single vote. these provisions shall not apply where the subject of the report requires a priority debate in plenary, where the report is drawn up on the basis of the right of initiative or where the report has been designated as a strategic report.
in writing. − i support this report because stability bonds can be an additional means of stimulating compliance with the stability and growth pact, especially in the context of the new rules on the effective application of budgetary surveillance in the euro area. as the issuer of the second international currency, the euro area has a key role to play in maintaining the stability of the international monetary system, as well as a strategic interest in realising its full potential so that the euro can become a global reserve currency. but stability bonds can play an important role in the internal implementation and overall assertiveness of the euro area's monetary policy only if there is a sustainable fiscal framework based on growth, and not in the fragile context of the past two years, marked by speculative attacks, instability and poor economic governance.

in writing. − social policy and employment are the basic responsibility of the member states. in line with the principle of subsidiarity, the european institutions deal with those areas where eu solutions ensure policy harmonisation. thus, issues relating to financing, unemployment and social issues are of common interest to all member states. so far, the eu has only set minimum standards and rights, on the basis of which member states adopt laws and regulations that go beyond european social policy. the crisis has had dramatic consequences, especially for young people looking for stable employment. they face an unemployment rate of over 20% and, in some member states, even over 40%. between 2008 and 2010, the number of young unemployed in the eu increased by one million. the rate of young people aged 15-24 who are not in employment and who are not in any education or training programme increased by 2 per cent during the same period. for these reasons, i believe that finding solutions must be a priority for the european union, otherwise this generation of young people will be a lost generation.
in writing. - the economic and financial crisis that has been affecting europe for some time, and in particular the austerity measures taken in some member states, must not lead to a decline in social protection standards and health and safety standards. these measures do not in any way justify the existence of precarious forms of work among young people, such as temporary or part-time work and unpaid traineeships. i believe that such practices should be reduced, because young people, especially those who have not completed a full cycle of vocational training, should be encouraged to participate in training programmes appropriate to their individual abilities, programmes that promote entrepreneurship, which can ensure the transition from education to working life. by taking such measures, europe can avoid the loss of potential of the young generation and reduce the skills gap in the labour market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is essential, now more than ever, that the european parliament gives itself an instrument to make its voice heard on the issue of europe 2020 strategy implementation, in particular given the imminent spring european council on 1-2 march. despite the fact that the economic and sovereign debt crisis has clearly showed that austerity measures are not sufficient to overcome such a dramatic situation – even creating the conditions for a recession of the weaker euro area countries (the greek case is more than emblematic) – the commission’s approach, as expressed in the annual growth survey, again identifies priorities that are not contributing to achieving the eu2020 goals in a balanced way. the motion we have adopted is a comprehensive and well-elaborated document that will clearly define the role of parliament in the future negotiations with the council and the commission. i think the time has come to break down the dogmatic approach, defining job-creation and social inclusion policies as opposed to fiscal stability. the economic crisis will lead to a deeper and more dangerous social crisis if europe does not take action in the fields of growth, job creation and social inclusion.
in writing. − as unemployment has now reached alarming levels at eu level, a european-wide approach is needed to define an employment strategy. i voted for a package of three reports which help to define a coherent position of the parliament on this structural problem facing the member states. the emphasis was on fiscal consolidation, based on social non-discrimination and poverty reduction. job creation was another point in our calls, a move that can only be achieved if investment and tax reform are tackled in a committed and responsible way. concrete solutions and implementation will be the responsibility of the european commission and the member states, which are forced by current conditions to act in a coordinated manner.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the employment and social issues report in the annual growth survey 2012, which shows us how strong the impact of the economic crisis is at eu level and in terms of employment. the economic crisis has exacerbated social problems and had dramatic consequences, especially among young people, who are the most affected by unemployment. in order to reduce economic imbalances and achieve sustainable economic growth, it is vital that member states encourage investment for job creation. member states should therefore direct their policies towards the implementation of appropriate fiscal measures to support smes as growth generators. as regards the structural funds, it is useful and necessary to use them to support smes and combat unemployment effectively. member states should therefore step up their efforts to use the structural funds, with priority for combating poverty and unemployment. austerity measures are necessary, but they must be backed up by compensatory measures, stimulating investment and job creation.

in writing. − unfortunately, the annual growth analysis does not provide the solutions needed to restore confidence in european economies and financial markets. we need to take urgent action to support employment and to achieve the eu 2020 targets. we also need to take into account the interdependence of member states' economies and budgetary policies and the domino effects that may occur in some cases. the growth prospects of the member states are highly dependent on measures to combat the crisis. i therefore believe that all eu countries must take urgent action to correct excessive deficits and reduce sovereign debt to an acceptable level. to restore investor confidence, we need a reform of the financial sector's regulatory and supervisory framework. banks should not unduly restrict lending to the real economy and regulatory actions should lay the foundations for increasing their lending capacity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the contribution to the 2012 annual growth analysis. the commission's annual growth analysis for 2012 is a good basis for this year's european semester, but as the resolution underlines, solutions specifically addressing the current sovereign debt and financial crisis must be accompanied by medium- and long-term measures to boost growth and a reshaping of the overall economic framework in order to improve the competitiveness of the european economy. uncertainty about the outlook for the european economy and concerns about the euro area debt crisis have weakened confidence among european households and businesses, as well as in financial markets. high energy prices and persistent difficulties in accessing finance are also adversely affecting the recovery process. member states' and the eu's efforts need to focus on the following priorities: pursuing growth-friendly differentiated fiscal consolidation while ensuring economic recovery and job creation, securing the long-term financing of the real economy, promoting sustainable growth through increased competitiveness and investment, addressing unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis, and modernising european public administration and services of general interest.

mr president, in syria civilians continue to die. this monday the un high commissioner for human rights said that the situation in homs was deplorable. more than 300 people are estimated to have lost their lives since the beginning of february. the un human rights council cannot keep track of their numbers. children are being kidnapped, tortured and killed. these are the actions of a government which has lost its legitimacy in front of its own people and in front of the international community. the eu has imposed an asset freeze and visa ban on 108 individuals and an asset freeze on 38 entities. this stance must be intensified. we should cut the money supply through further sanctions on the sales of gold and precious gems. at the same time we must reach out to the syrian people and work with humanitarian organisations to develop humanitarian corridors to help the people. we must increase this momentum and put more pressure on the assad regime to stop the violence, step down and ensure a peaceful transition to democracy.
mr president, the arab spring generally – and syria in particular – has caused splits in the security council. the arab league, the eu and the us oppose the current regime, which is killing its own people, while others support it for – in my opinion – different reasons. some of its supporters are concerned by the legitimacy of regime change through foreign intervention, while in russia’s case there are also crucial strategic motivations. if the current syrian regime falls, russia will not only lose a strategic partner which allows it to continue to be part of the middle east equation, but also a naval bridgehead in the region and an important customer for its arms exports, possibly even a component in its complex relations with iran. however, with the syrian people, the arab league and most of the international community absolutely opposed to the current syrian regime, those who continue to support it will find themselves beyond the tipping point at which the losses outweigh the gains.

president of the council. - mr president, i have to say something. first of all, thank you again for an interesting debate. in the european union we believe that all that concerns human rights is of vital importance in moving the world forward and also in ensuring that these are not rights that are formed in individual situations but rights that are universal and that all countries commit themselves to and respect. we're not there yet, but that's what we're pushing for. i would like to stress that we in the council are also very concerned about this. we have an informal meeting of foreign ministers in march, a gymnich meeting, where one of the two subjects we will discuss is human rights, with a view to taking a decision on behalf of the european union again in june. when we have such a high profile as we have on human rights, it is also important that we, so to speak, sweep the floor before the sheep die. i mean, we keep our own path clean. this also means that we must, of course, constantly bring up these issues at bilateral meetings with third countries. and it is important, as several speakers have also pointed out, that we see progress in terms of concrete results as the world moves forward. i should now like to make a few comments on some of the countries mentioned. it is true - member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thank you, mrs mazzoni, for giving me the opportunity to raise the question of the copyright exception for the benefit of the visually impaired and the international discussions currently taking place. as you know, the european union is committed to advancing the rights of disabled people, and i have personally discussed this with all the organizations concerned with the blind, mrs mazzoni. the full participation of disabled people in social, cultural and economic life must be a real reality in our modern democratic societies. the european commission has committed itself to this, in particular - as you recalled - with the 2010-2020 strategy for people with disabilities. we support the full, complete and effective recognition of the rights of these disabled persons, as recognised in particular by the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and the charter of fundamental rights. this is the view which we also defend in the discussions currently taking place in the world intellectual property organization on the rights of the visually impaired to which your question refers. i would like to clarify and clarify things, ladies and gentlemen. part of the debate concerns the need and usefulness of a binding international legal instrument on exceptions to copyright for the benefit of visually impaired persons. in other words, does the objective which you and i are pursuing require, does it require, yes or no, an international treaty? regardless of the course of this debate, we must also be pragmatic, focusing on a more concrete and urgent issue. is the text currently on the table, in its economy and in its content, able to provide a practical, credible and effective solution to the difficulties faced by the visually impaired? as far as the european union and the law currently in force are concerned, all member states have introduced exceptions for the benefit of visually impaired persons, in accordance with the charter of fundamental rights and in accordance with the directive on copyright in the information society. in addition, concrete measures are being taken to encourage cooperation at eu level between the beneficiaries and organisations representing visually impaired people. beyond an exception, of course, there is also a need for effective cooperation between creators and organizations of visually impaired people to make books accessible as quickly as possible in formats best suited to those who need them. the need for books in accessible formats for the visually impaired is real and urgent. we must therefore ensure that the main focus of the discussions is on identifying the best response in terms of concrete, practical, effective and rapid response. ladies and gentlemen, these substantive discussions must be a prerequisite and enable us, once a solid common position has emerged among the parties concerned, to determine the legal nature of the instrument to be put in place. is that a treaty? is that a recommendation? i am personally open to either of these two positions. the commission and the european union are engaged in constructive discussions. we have helped to move the debate forward by proposing, with the support of other states, a single text to replace the four previous texts. this text was hailed as a major breakthrough, including by the world blind union. but i think we need to go further into its material content. at the last wipo meeting, the european union and its member states called for open discussions on the substance of the text, which needs to be improved rapidly. our position on the improvements to be made has been communicated in writing and orally to our partners and interested parties in a transparent manner. we are therefore encouraging our partners and all parties to the debate to get to the heart of the matter as quickly as possible. as this is a subject which interests me, mrs mazzoni, ladies and gentlemen, and on which i have personally engaged with the associations of the visually impaired, i intend to contact and dialogue very quickly with all the governments of the european union in order to move more quickly and more precisely towards a concrete solution and to resolve this problem in the sense in which your question calls it.
on behalf of the epp group. i would like to start by welcoming the initiative of my colleague, erminia mazzoni, to put this oral question. it is estimated that there are some 30 million visually impaired people in europe. additional measures are needed to ensure that they do not suffer from additional deprivation, such as access to books. they lead to reduced opportunities for education, training and subsequent integration into the labour market. for example, statistics show that today less than 25 percent of blind people are employed. technological developments provide new opportunities to increase the number of books accessible to the visually impaired. an important element is the diversification of formats: audio or electronic books are now available in addition to braille publications. what we lack is a european legislative framework to facilitate their emergence and dissemination. i call on the commission and the council to redouble their efforts to this end, including by supporting a specific exception to copyright. i also appreciate the need to encourage the exchange of experience and good practice between member states. in this context, i would mention that in romania public libraries have a legal obligation to set up book sections in accessible formats for the blind. finally, i would like to commend the generosity of authors and publishers who are willing to offer the rights to publish in a medium adapted to these people.
at eu-27 level, less than 5% of published books are accessible to blind and visually impaired people. such persons shall have access to published books or printed materials in braille, audio or electronic formats. blind people do not have proper access to braille books, bookstores, or libraries. libraries must be equipped with terminals for blind persons, enabling them to have appropriate access to literary works in electronic format. most of these people are unemployed and therefore do not have adequate income. therefore, the affordability of literary works in braille, electronic or audio formats is of utmost importance. i support the creation of an online european catalogue of works available in accessible formats. i support a binding copyright treaty for books and printed materials in electronic format for the visually impaired.
deposit insurance is an indispensable element of the system of supervision of credit institutions. the system will allow for the compensation of depositors up to a certain ceiling, which is fixed at eur 100 000. depositors are exempted from participation in long insolvency proceedings. today, the systems in the union provide different levels of protection for deposits and impose unequal financial obligations on banks. it is important that the deposit guarantee scheme ensures financial stability for customers. therefore, there is a need for depositors to be informed about both secured and unsecured financial products. i support ex-ante funding of deposit guarantee schemes and differentiated contributions. i stress that these systems must be monitored at all times. it is essential to carry out stress simulations for the systems used.
the approximately 40 deposit guarantee schemes in the union provide different levels of deposit protection for different groups of depositors, impose different financial obligations on banks, and limit the benefits of the internal market. the harmonised minimum level of collateral of eur 100000 provided for in this directive provides protection for a large proportion of deposits, both in the interests of consumer protection and the stability of the financial system. it is important that all depositors benefit from the same level of protection, regardless of whether the member state's currency is the euro or not. in the event of the closure of an insolvent credit institution, depositors at any branch located in a member state other than that in which the credit institution has its head office should be protected by the same guarantee scheme as other depositors at that institution.

commitment. the communication to the european parliament and the council, adopted in november 2011, therefore seemed the most appropriate way to open a debate with the other institutions on how to ensure the long-term success of gmes. the annex to this communication contains the elements that may be included in an international agreement between member states to replace the regulation which expires at the end of 2013. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. the commission considered that the costs of gmes could not be borne by the union budget alone, given the limits imposed on it. this is a way of ensuring the continuity of the programme while allowing the union to continue to fully meet its international commitments. it must be acknowledged that the structure of the union budget makes it difficult to finance large-scale programmes such as gmes, whose duration of implementation is much longer than that of the financial framework. as the commission reiterated in its communication of 30 november, it considers that it is particularly committed to the success of gmes. if, as proposed, a gmes fund is established by the member states, then the commission will present, in legal form, a proposal for its implementation. the timetable therefore depends on the establishment of the financing fund by the member states in the council. discussions on gmes are also taking place in the council at this very moment and in this context there is an exchange of views on this subject at the competitiveness council on 21 february. gmes will provide information that will help to manage issues ranging from climate change to border surveillance, as i have just mentioned. that is why i think it is an important programme which we must, in one way or another, continue to support together with the member states.

in writing. − regardless of whether a bank's financial situation is sound or precarious, it is impossible for it to have sufficient liquidity to repay all or part of its loans to the public in the event of massive withdrawals. for this reason, banking institutions risk facing the phenomenon of bank run, where depositors consider that their deposits are not safe and attempt to withdraw them at the same time. national deposit guarantee schemes in the eu are particularly important for our citizens and provide added confidence for bank deposit-taking. european guarantee schemes compensate depositors in the event of default up to a certain guarantee ceiling. the amount of the ceiling was first raised from eur 20 000 to eur 50 000 and from 2011 to eur 100 0000 per depositor. this directive applies to all credit institutions and membership of a deposit guarantee scheme becomes compulsory. in this way, we will have the certainty that depositors can redeem their claims at any time and that all systems are sufficiently funded. a high level of protection enhances the confidence of depositors and thus avoids the simultaneous withdrawal of funds by many depositors for fear of losing their money.
in writing. − i voted in favour of parliament's legislative resolution of 16 february 2012 on the proposal for a directive on deposit-guarantee schemes (reform), as the directive is an essential instrument for the completion of the internal market from the point of view of the freedom of establishment and the freedom to provide financial services in the field of credit institutions, while enhancing the stability of the banking system and the protection of depositors. national deposit guarantee schemes in the eu compensate depositors in the event of a credit institution's failure to meet its obligations up to the coverage ceiling which, as from 1 january 2011, is eur 100 0000 per depositor. in order for deposit guarantee schemes to have a stabilising effect in times of financial crisis, it is necessary to ensure sufficient ex ante funding of deposit guarantee schemes throughout europe. depositors must be better informed than they are at present about the operation of deposit guarantee schemes and, in the event of a credit institution's failure to meet its payment obligations, they must be compensated swiftly. the formulation of common requirements for deposit guarantee schemes allows member states maximum flexibility in the configuration of such schemes.

in writing. − globally, nearly 350 million people are affected by various forms of visual impairment. at the same time, as indicated in several european union documents, increasing the social inclusion of blind people is one of the objectives assumed in view of achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the creation of a european society in which equal opportunities are institutionalised and the support of political authorities to remedy or ameliorate the problems faced by a whole category of european citizens is a fundamental objective of european leaders and politicians. the proposal to amend the legislation to ensure greater access to written materials for visually impaired persons is therefore legitimate. it is important, however, that this measure is complemented by other policy decisions to help increase social inclusion and equal opportunities.
in writing. − access to written culture for the blind is still very limited, with only 5% of european publications available in accessible formats. their educational opportunities, especially in the sciences, are extremely limited because of the lack of textbooks and courses designed specifically for them. to meet this challenge, the council and the commission must support a world intellectual property organisation treaty on copyright for books and printed materials for the blind and visually impaired.
in writing. - i voted for the parliament's resolution on access for blind people to books and other printed products. article 26 of the charter of fundamental rights of the eu lays down the principle that the union recognises and respects the right of persons with disabilities to benefit from measures ensuring their autonomy, social and occupational integration and participation in the life of the community. according to european statistics, blind and visually impaired people in the eu have limited access to books and other printed materials because 95% of published works are not converted into formats accessible to them, such as braille, audio or electronic formats. i would point out that there are barriers to access for visually impaired and partially blind persons to copyrighted works. we therefore call for the creation of an online e-book service accessible throughout the eu. at present, there is no international legal norm providing for an exception to copyright for the cross-border distribution of formats adapted for visually impaired persons. we call on the council and the commission to support a binding wipo copyright treaty for books and printed materials for the blind and visually impaired.
in writing. − the social, commercial and economic integration of the mediterranean region among the countries belonging to this area has become a major objective of european policy on the mediterranean basin with the establishment of the euromed union. the conclusion of this convention is one of the instruments that can make a significant contribution to trade relations between the eu and its partners and to the continued development of investment in the region.
in writing. − i voted in favour because i believe that the conclusion of the regional convention on pan-mediterranean preferential rules of origin will bring timely simplifications for trade actors throughout this area, facilitating economic exchanges and thus contributing to the emergence of the euro-mediterranean free trade area. i believe that the new instrument will have important benefits, by increasing the geographical coverage of the cumulation of origin. it is relevant that the new convention will provide a single framework for the european union's trade relations with countries previously covered by various cooperation frameworks. the rules of origin in the trade agreements with the states participating in the barcelona process, respectively in the stabilisation and association process and the efta states will thus be unified. trade facilitation is likely to generate economic growth, with effects both for the balkan countries and for those in the southern neighbourhood. this single and simplified framework will support the work of enterprises, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises. it will also create the conditions for increased trade between the countries of the south. at the same time, to ensure the success of the new instrument, prompt and effective action by the commission in response to any possible malfunctions is necessary.
in writing. − the conclusion of the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin is an important step in the effective continuation of the process initiated in barcelona. it is an intermediate step in the creation of a euro-mediterranean free trade area, and the ultimate goal is the creation of a single convention to replace the current network of over a hundred bilateral protocols on rules of origin. we voted the draft resolution to create an instrument with a key role in reducing the complexity of current trade relations. strategies for the regions of the eu's southern neighbourhood must have a macro-regional approach. this will foster cooperation between regions to achieve common goals such as sustainable growth, encouraging investment through job creation and strengthening democracy. the development of effective cooperation between the european union and the mediterranean area requires the stimulation of access to funds through the european neighbourhood and partnership instrument (enpi). the simplification of the procedures for granting assistance to the mediterranean countries is also important. the european union must have flexible borders, not rigid ones, especially in economic relations!
in writing. − monitoring climate change and its impact on european countries, rapidly preventing security threats by collecting relevant information, providing data to underpin many economic and social policies of the european union and its member states are just some of the benefits of this important european programme. the initiative is also important because it is able to boost space research and exploration by bringing together resources that are not available to individual eu member states. the development of the programme is also important for the success of the europe 2020 strategy of the european union for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, significantly supporting the industrial component of this policy paper. i support the adoption of this programme which brings not only economic benefits (projected to be four times its costs by 2030), but also contributes to the development of better european governance.
in writing. − the global monitoring for environment and security (gmes) programme provides information to help us better understand how our planet can be changed and the means by which this is done. mitigating climate change, addressing emergencies, ensuring better border control, improving security and alerting citizens if air quality deteriorates are activities that depend on accurate and timely information about our planet. according to a cost-benefit analysis, the gmes programme is expected to generate benefits at least twice the cost of investment by 2020 and four times the cost by 2030. this represents a huge potential for growth and job creation through the development of innovative services and commercial applications in the downstream sector. the european dimension of gmes generates economies of scale, facilitates joint investments in large-scale infrastructure, promotes coordination of efforts and observation networks, enables data harmonisation and intercalibration, and provides the necessary impetus for the emergence of world-class centres of excellence in europe.
in writing. − i voted for the resolution on the future of the european earth monitoring programme (gmes) because this programme is a flagship eu space initiative and plays a key role in earth observation, being an essential tool for combating climate change and environmental degradation, for civil protection and security, sustainable development, mobility and crisis management. gmes offers important economic opportunities by stimulating innovation and job creation across the eu. gmes was established as an eu programme, funded from the union budget, worth approximately eur 3,2 billion until 2013, under the management and responsibility of the eu. we consider that the commission's current proposal to finance gmes outside the multiannual financial framework (mff) is not a viable solution, as the uncertainty surrounding gmes funding seriously affects the development and commercialisation of gmes services and applications, which are expected to generate economic growth and welfare for european citizens. in this regard, we call on the commission to present a legislative proposal for the long-term management, financing and operation of the gmes programme, funded under the mff, with a view to ensuring the proper implementation and functioning of the programme and achieving its objective of being fully operational from 2014.

the functioning of the internal market should be facilitated by removing obstacles to the free movement of persons who currently face difficulties in exercising their rights in the context of a succession with cross-border implications. the scope of the regulation covers all civil law aspects of succession, namely all forms of transfer of property, rights and obligations by reason of death. this regulation should allow citizens to organise their succession in advance by choosing the applicable law. that law applicable to their succession should determine who the beneficiaries are in any case of succession and should govern the succession from its opening until the transfer of ownership of the assets forming part of the succession to the beneficiaries. the documents issued by notaries in matters of succession in the member states should circulate under this regulation. the european certificate of succession issued under this regulation should be a valid document for the registration of the estate in a register of a member state. the authorities involved in the registration operation may require the person requesting registration to provide additional information and documents required under the law of the member state in which the register is kept, for example information or documents relating to the payment of tax documents. it would have been important for the completion of the internal market and the removal of barriers to the free movement of persons that this regulation applied to all member states. we therefore hope that the current situation in which the united kingdom, ireland and denmark are not bound by this regulation and are not subject to its application will be resolved.
the report makes clarifications that will facilitate the mobility of european citizens. i welcome the establishment of jurisdiction by centre of interest of the succession, as proposed in amendment no 6 to the commission's text. moreover, mutual recognition of succession rights will eliminate the current red tape through the use of the european certificate of succession. in this way, long-term cross-border mobility of persons is encouraged. it also ensures a predictable legal regime of succession for the whole european area by eliminating conflicts of jurisdiction. i would point out in this context the clarifications provided by the new romanian civil code on this matter. the institution of succession law is fundamental in the civil system of my country and its adaptation to today's realities guarantees the optimal functioning of the legal circuit of property.
in writing. the importance of crossborder successions within the european union has been repeatedly highlighted. the diversity of substantive law, rules of international jurisdiction or applicable law, the multiplicity of authorities that may be seised in an international succession, and the fragmentation of successions that may result from those divergent rules constitute an obstacle to the free movement of persons within the union. they currently face significant difficulties in exercising their rights in the context of an international succession. those different rules impede the full exercise of the right to private property, which, according to the settled case-law of the court of justice, is an integral part of fundamental rights, the observance of which is ensured by the court. in my view, it is necessary to make clear the situations in which the issuing of a european certificate of succession is necessary. the procedure will remain national when there is no foreign element. since the european certificate of succession replaces the national certificate and since the legislation of a member state contains different provisions concerning the national certificate of succession, i consider it necessary that the european certificate of succession contains both the european elements considered to be minimum and mandatory and any additional elements provided for by the national legislation.
