i have participated with great interest in this morning's debate on the council conclusions and i want to say to you that yes, it is clear, we need fiscal stability, but we also need growth. but for growth we need a concrete investment plan, to find the sources, to identify them, and the sectors that have growth and employment potential. because a lot of citizens, especially young people and women, need jobs and we have to create those jobs. and i ask myself why, if there are sources through that savings directive that mr barroso has spoken of, why is that directive still blocked within the council and why, when we talk about growth, employment and social policies, is the directive on maternity leave still blocked within the council? and i would also like to stress that i hope that in september romania and bulgaria will join schengen.
as regards the schengen issue, i believe that the continuing opposition of the netherlands to the accession of romania and bulgaria to the schengen area is an abuse that is contrary to the long-term principles and objectives of the european union. the netherlands' position has delayed the decision on romania and bulgaria's access to the schengen area and has shown, once again, that while all member states have equal responsibilities, not all enjoy the same benefits. ladies and gentlemen, the populist ambitions of some leaders and parties on the european political scene only weaken the union's power and reduce the credibility of politicians at european level. given that all the conditions for accession have been fulfilled, i hereby call on all the institutions responsible to identify and implement all the necessary measures to contribute to the enlargement of the schengen area.
in writing. it is welcome that the council conclusions mentioned the request that the september jha council take the decision on the accession of romania and bulgaria to the schengen area. it's more than nothing. the normal course would have been to ask for a decision at the next jai council, to stop an unjustified delay and without legal arguments. i think the schengen issue has become a concern for the union in general, not just for romania and bulgaria. the introduction of temporary border controls by denmark and france, the intention of the netherlands to install cameras at the dutch borders, the discussions on the legal basis for the schengen evaluation regulation, the recent statements by france are putting undue pressure on one of the union's most positive achievements: the free movement of persons. i therefore call on the council to pay very close attention to this subject in the very near future.
in writing. – it seems that both the council and the commission are taking the fact that for the first time this council was not held in response to a crisis as a sign that the crisis had started to be tamed; we only need more time ... . that time, however, might instead bring more xenophobia and more protectionism, as the electoral campaign in france is clearly demonstrating. my colleague hannes swoboda has asked a rhetorical question: what if we all had to show our passport once again to enter france? well, as a romanian mep, i have to do this every time i come to strasbourg, and not just to board a plane, as my colleague mr gollnisch pointed out, but to be allowed to enter the country which is making me attend the part-sessions here, in strasbourg, instead of brussels. and, on top of that, sometimes i have to subject myself to a search without a warrant instead of a normal airport check, and this only because my country is kept out of schengen arbitrarily. yes, we need tough measures to get out of the crisis, but not at the expense of what we have achieved with such effort until now.
in writing. the european council has again blocked romania and bulgaria's access to the schengen area. apparently, the blockade is a follow-up to the dutch veto. in reality, behind this opposition are other states whose leaders are trapped in national-populist discourse. against the backdrop of the global economic crisis, the renationalisation of europe is becoming threatening. the sacrifice of the freedom of movement of persons under the pretext that the security and cultural purity of european nations would thus be saved is the expression of the eurosceptic current that now marks the election campaign in france. if the french rejected the constitutional treaty in a referendum focused on debating national issues, the current presidential elections are bringing european issues into dispute. it would be salutary if the tone were not anti-european. mr hollande is speaking out against the european economic governance initiated by the fiscal compact. mr sarkozy calls for a 'political governance' of the schengen area. a 'strong france' would define the principles of this governance, allowing 'legitimate' governments, unlike the european commission, to sanction states that do not sufficiently combat illegal immigration. the real problem is not the defence of the eu's external borders, but the inconsistency of eu migration policy. a community solution is also needed to guarantee the application of the principle of solidarity and sincere cooperation between eu member states, enshrined in the treaties but now a dead letter.
in writing. the european council of 1-2 march 2012 was marked mainly by the signing of the treaty on stability, coordination and governance in the framework of economic and monetary union. implementing the eu's economic strategy, however, requires decisive action to stimulate growth and job creation. the european council endorsed the five priorities for 2012 identified in the commission's annual growth survey: continuing growth-friendly differentiated fiscal consolidation, resuming the normal lending activity of the economy, promoting growth and competitiveness, addressing unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis, and modernising public administration. however, i believe that further efforts are needed at eu level to achieve the single market and in particular to complete the digital single market by 2015. i emphasise the important role of industry in growth, competitiveness, exports and job creation in europe, as a driver of productivity and innovation. i welcome the decision of the european council to grant serbia the status of candidate country. given that the european commission has repeatedly recognised that romania and bulgaria fulfil the technical criteria for accession to the schengen area, i ask the council to adopt a decision to this effect as soon as possible.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, let me start by saying that i have been impressed by the commitment of members to debate this issue. as i started out by saying, the danish presidency would certainly have liked it if a solution on the egf could have been found in the council. that was not possible, and now we will be working on the future of the egf. i will be looking forward to constructive cooperation with this house. i would also like to make it very clear that the danish presidency, and the council, are firmly committed to combating the crisis as we know it because, as many members in this chamber have made clear, the crisis is not over yet. therefore it is important that we continue to reform the single market and that we use the euros in the mff as wisely as possible to make sure that growth and job creation will be on the agenda, especially for young people. that will be the aim of the danish presidency and of the commission. i will also be looking forward to working closely with parliament on achieving this.
in writing. i consider that the extension of the derogation concerning the european globalisation adjustment fund is necessary in the current context. to date, this instrument has proved useful in mitigating the effects of the economic crisis and preventing other social disasters. in order to continue in the same direction and to steer the economy towards sustainable growth, i consider it important to adapt the fund. this mechanism is particularly necessary for workers, the victims of the crisis, who need to find an answer to their problems. we need to support displaced workers in their search for a new job, and eu assistance in this regard needs to be more dynamic to meet their needs. in december, romania requested the european commission for financial assistance through the european globalisation adjustment fund for nokia employees, who decided to move their business to asia. i recall that in september last year nokia announced the closure of the jucu factory and the transfer of business to china, despite the fact that in 2010 the cluj factory recorded a turnover increase of more than 55% compared to the previous year. my country's position is in favour of maintaining the instrument with a european co-financing rate of 65%.
in writing. the economic crisis has led to a decline in economic activity and has led to an increase in unemployment amid a steep decline in productivity and a deterioration in the public finance system. the adaptation of the egf has become necessary in order to mitigate the effects of the current crisis. recent forecasts indicate that structural changes in economic sectors will continue to involve job losses due to the closure of some enterprises or the relocation of others. i would like to stress that many member states have not benefited from egf benefits to date, due to the fact that they have not faced massive closures or relocations. due to recent restructuring at company level, there is a risk that redundancies will become a frequent phenomenon in the immediate future. i therefore consider it absolutely necessary to extend the derogation in the light of the crisis. the importance of financing with egf support lies in its flexibility. by targeting aid to affected workers over a limited period of time, the egf contributes to reducing unemployment, enabling member states to emerge from the economic crisis and steering their economies towards smart, sustainable and inclusive growth.
in writing. the extension of the crisis derogation should be maintained, at least temporarily. it is clear that offshoring is, at least for now, vital for european capital looking for areas with lower wages. to respond to the effects of globalisation, the union has created this fund. to what extent it's functional, that's another discussion altogether. but at the moment we have no tools to mitigate the effects of bankruptcies or job cuts due not to globalization but simply to the economic crisis. initiatives related to research and innovation, to increasing competitiveness - these are economically sound, but they only have long-term effects. until then, europe must overcome the crisis. either a new, dedicated instrument or the extension of the derogation is necessary in this respect.
i voted for mr giegold's report because european cooperatives contribute to economic growth, the strengthening of the internal market and job creation. they also participate in the implementation of cohesion policy, by working at global and regional level. at present, this important sector is not managed in a uniform manner. i welcome the initiative to revise the european cooperative societies directive under article 17 to take into account the specific needs of workers. their participation in cooperatives is essential and must take place under the most favourable conditions. at the same time, the statute of the european cooperative society should be amended in order to simplify access for users. this will establish a uniform legal framework to enable cooperative societies in the member states to plan and carry out their activities at community level.
i voted in favour of this report because the union needs quality education that encourages research and innovation. young people need to be able to develop a wide range of skills in order to integrate and adapt quickly to the labour market. given the difficulties encountered in the first employment, i stress the importance of internships and professional integration programmes. recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications is essential to encourage student mobility, but also for the single market and the free movement of workers. i hope that the ministerial meeting in bucharest in april will produce positive results, contributing to the creation of the european higher education area. i mention that romania has launched a complex program of education reform, as part of the state reform. ensuring quality education remains one of the priorities of the romanian government.
in writing. − i welcome the objective of the agreement to improve judicial cooperation between the member states of the european union and norway and iceland by applying all the provisions of the 2000 convention on mutual legal assistance between member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament’s consent to the agreement between the european union and the republic of iceland and the kingdom of norway on the application of certain provisions of the convention of 29 may 2000 on mutual assistance in criminal matters, because it is an important step forward in the direction of a stronger mechanism for combating trans-border crime. both iceland and norway are already part of the schengen area: this agreement, by strengthening mutual legal assistance and by including provisions on hearing of witnesses, experts and accused persons by telephone or video conference, controlled deliveries, covert investigations and joint investigation teams and requests for information on banking transactions, bank accounts and their monitoring to combat crime in general and organised crime in particular, makes the partnership on criminal issues with the two northern european countries stronger and more effective. the european parliament, by giving its consent to this agreement, is providing democratic validation for its implementation within the eu as prescribed by the lisbon treaty.
in writing. − i supported this agreement at first reading because i believe that eu citizens who choose to settle in another member state were in great need of clearer rules on jurisdiction, conflict of laws and enforcement in relation to crossborder inheritances. the single market is not just about businesses doing business across national borders, but also about people setting up in other member states who need to feel as protected as in their home country. at present, if someone lives in a member state other than their home member state and owns property in that member state which they wish to leave as a legacy, there is a risk of conflict between the courts of the member states concerned claiming jurisdiction. this may lead to burdensome administrative formalities for heirs or even litigation in court. i consider that the european certificate of succession and the clarification that the competent court and the applicable law is that of the last member state in which the person was resident, unless the will specifies that the law of the state of origin applies, will simplify matters significantly while maintaining the necessary flexibility.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for the regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions and authentic instruments in matters of succession and the creation of a european certificate of succession, because it makes clearer the eu rules as regards to succession. a european certificate of succession represents a step forward in the direction of a more homogeneous legal framework in the member states, simplifying the adoption of the internal market rules in matters of succession. whereas cross-borders relations are growing within the eu, transnational and more harmonised tools are necessary to properly tackle the challenges and to take advantage of the benefits which come along with the single market. with this regulation, handling cross-border successions would be considerably easier. besides, the proposal stresses the ‘right to choose the law applicable’, a principle able to introduce a positive significant innovation for many citizens and for the member states as well: a significant european added value.
in writing. − i voted for the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of judgments and authentic instruments in matters of succession and the creation of a european certificate of succession. an increasing number of european citizens move from one country to another within the eu to live, study, work or retire. the number of eu-27 citizens residing in a member state other than their home member state reached approximately 12,3 million in 2010, an increase of 3 million compared to 2005. in order to settle a succession with elements of alienability in the union in a rapid, simple and effective manner, heirs, legatees, executors of wills or administrators of the estate should be able to easily prove their status and/or their rights and powers in another member state, for example in a member state where the estate is situated. the regulation thus provides for the creation of a uniform certificate, the european certificate of succession, to be issued for use in another member state. in order to respect the principle of subsidiarity, the certificate should not replace internal documents that may exist for similar purposes in the member states.
in writing. − the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives of building an open and inclusive society, capable of providing significant resources for the sustainable development of the european union in the medium and long term, cannot be achieved without addressing in a transversal way several gender equality issues facing societies in the member states. it is important, in these circumstances, that member states take legislative measures to ensure equal and effective economic independence for men and women in european societies. directly linked to this objective is the issue of equal pay for men and women without sustained efforts, the 17.5% gap between men's and women's earnings cannot be reduced. equally important to the success of the european union's medium and long-term objectives is addressing the gender gap in decision-making: with 60% of higher education graduates being women, the fact that only 12% of the executive board members of large listed companies and only 3% of the ceos of large european companies are women is further evidence of the systemic problems we face. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − despite a comprehensive theoretical framework of directional manifestations for the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, inequalities persist in all fields of activity. in the current financial and economic context, strengthening the position of women in the labour market is not only a moral evolutionary argument but also an economic necessity. the risk of poverty and social exclusion continues to increase and the austerity measures taken by some member states in recent years have overlapped with the harsh reality of the lack of support mechanisms for women, in the context of discrimination in the labour market and in society. family and child support measures were eliminated or reduced in the context of many difficulties in the health and pre-school education system, lack of utilities and medical care in rural areas, which led to a sharp deterioration in the living standards of families with children. also, wage cuts were made in budgetary sectors dominated by women, such as education and health, which led to a considerable decline in incomes. in this context, we call on member states to implement urgent support measures, through the creation of effective poverty reduction and family support mechanisms, for the achievement of gender equality.
in writing. − as violence against women, including psychological violence, is a major obstacle to equality between women and men and a violation of their fundamental rights, and remains one of the most widespread human rights violations in the eu, i believe that member states and the european commission must move towards individualised social security systems to improve women's autonomy and position in society.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this motion for a european parliament resolution on equality between women and men in the european union, because it represents a key priority of the eu for the coming years. the motion explains the crucial importance of overcoming gender disparities and any form of gender and sexual discrimination, also by explaining in clear and unequivocal terms the economic importance of gender equality for growth and in the fight against poverty. europe 2020 contains in its priorities the goal of a 75% employment rate for women by 2020. improvements have been achieved; however, because of the economic crisis, it is important to accelerate in this direction. this document tackles the problem through a pragmatic approach, underlines the current situation and calls the european union and its member states to enhance their efforts not only by providing sufficient funds to build a due balance between men and women in our societies but also by being the promoters of a change in people’s mindset and traditions.
in writing. − equality between women and men is a fundamental principle of the eu and, despite the progress made, many inequalities between women and men still persist. i call on the european institutions and the member states to develop a clear strategy to address the gender pay gap - a european target of reducing the gap by 10% in each member state - by ensuring equal pay for women and men doing the same work and with the same qualifications. member states should in particular include women workers in the training and education programmes for 'green jobs', considered by the commission to be the 'key growth segment' of the european labour market. the representation of women in political decision-making has not improved, the representation of women and men in national parliaments has remained unchanged, 24% women and 76% men, and in some member states the number of women in national parliaments does not exceed 15%, with women overall representing 23% of all ministers. the commission shall propose in 2012 legislative acts, including quotas, to increase the representation of women in company management structures to 30% by 2015 and 40% by 2020, taking into account economic, legal and regional specificities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on equality between women and men in the eu because equality between women and men is a fundamental principle of the union and because, despite progress in this area, many inequalities between women and men still persist. i voted for amendment no 28 because i believe that the definition of 'family' is a matter of subsidiarity. i voted for the request that member states use the 2007-2013 structural funds to develop childcare services to enable both women and men to combine work and private life. given that women in the eu earn on average 17.5% less than men, i called on member states to redouble their efforts to implement european measures to reduce this gap. i voted in favour of calling on the european institutions, the member states and the social partners to develop a strategy to address the persistent gender pay gap. i voted in favour of introducing statutory parity systems and gender quotas, both for parliamentary assemblies and for senior positions in companies, public administration and political bodies, given good practices in countries such as france and spain.
in writing. − a series of data published by eurostat in the context of international women's day indicates that in the european union, women are much more at risk of poverty and social exclusion than men, with the most dramatic situations in this regard in romania and bulgaria. mothers, especially single mothers, elderly women and women in rural areas are the main victims of the effects of the economic and financial crisis. the representation of women in political decision-making has not shown any linear improvement in recent years, and in some member states the number of women in national parliaments does not exceed 15%. across the european union, there is a clear under-representation of women in political office and a lack of parity is prevalent across all fields of activity. the active participation of women is an economic necessity in the current context and therefore the creation of mechanisms for the implementation of gender policies aimed at achieving parity in participation in the political decision-making process, ensuring the effectiveness of these measures, is indispensable.
in writing. − as women's participation and representation at the highest levels of political decision-making is still hampered by various issues, such as the lack of an encouraging atmosphere in political institutions and societal support structures, the persistence of gender stereotypes, and the consequences of the recent economic crisis and its negative impact on gender equality issues, i believe that member states and the commission should encourage women's networks and promote mentoring, necessary training and the exchange of good practices and programmes in this field, with a special focus on women in political decision-making at the beginning of their careers.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament resolution on women in political decision-making – quality and equality – because it addresses a clear and fundamental problem in our political practices. women, despite the broad and shared acknowledgement of the need for equality in gender balance – in particular in power and decision-making – still face strong differences and barriers in their access to politics and public administration positions. it is worrying that during the last years no real and consistent improvements have been achieved as regards this crucial issue. the motion calls on the commission and the member states to elaborate clear measures to be implemented, such as a system of quotas to be applied by the member states at all levels of policy-making, including the areas of macro-economic policy, trade, labour, budgets, defence and foreign affairs.
in writing. − gender equality in decision-making is a matter of quality and equality. more gender-balanced participation contributes to more diverse and thus better decision-making. in order to strengthen women's political participation, the structural barriers that prevent women from participating in political life must be addressed. another action needed is the creation of an enabling environment for women to participate in political life at all levels. reconciling work and private life is recognised at eu level as an important priority for achieving gender equality and facilitating women's participation in political life. the commission and the member states should design and implement effective gender policies and strategies aimed at achieving parity in participation in political decision-making and political leadership at all levels, in particular in the areas of macroeconomic, trade, labour, budgetary, defence and external affairs policies, through impact assessment and the provision to the public of appropriate gender equality indices and indicators, ensuring quantified targets, clear action plans and regular monitoring mechanisms, followed by binding corrective actions and monitoring if targets are not met by deadlines.
in writing. − unfortunately, in the european union, although women represent 60% of higher education graduates, they are still underrepresented in positions of responsibility in the economy. i believe that more support is needed for initiatives and campaigns that challenge stereotypes about women's inefficiency in the workplace and their lack of leadership skills. on the other hand, i stress the importance of programmes for the vocational training of women in leadership positions. in conclusion, i would like to ask the member states to adopt measures setting binding targets to ensure the balanced presence of women and men in management positions in enterprises, in public administration and in the political sphere.
in writing. − i voted for the report on women in political decision-making quality and equality, because equal representation of women and men in political decision-making is an aspect of human rights, social justice, sustainable development and an essential requirement for the functioning of a democratic society. gender balance is guaranteed in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the objective of gender equality implies better political representation of women. the representation of women in political decision-making has stagnated in recent years, with the gender imbalance at the level of national parliaments in the eu remaining unchanged (24% women and 76% men), with women occupying only 23% of ministerial posts. the nordic countries have the highest level of women's representation in national parliaments, at 42.3%. in the european parliament, 35% of the members are women and 65% are men. i ask the commission to present to the european parliament an annual report on the progress of gender equality in political decision-making in the european union. it also calls on the commission and the council to commit themselves to achieving parity in all decision-making bodies by establishing and implementing quota systems when recruiting officials for senior levels.
in writing. − as only 12 member states had transposed the directive by the deadline set in the directive (18 august 2006), with the last implementing provisions being adopted only in march 2009, the commission launched infringement actions against 16 member states, followed by three referrals to the european court of justice. in almost all member states, transposition was achieved through the adoption of legislative provisions preceded by consultation of the social partners, through procedures that reflected the specific traditions of each country. the cooperative movement has been associated with this procedure in most member states. the main way of achieving this objective is through an agreement negotiated between the management of the legal persons concerned and the workers' representatives. in the absence of agreement after a period of six months (which may be extended by common agreement to 12 months), the directive lays down a number of reference provisions. in addition, the employees' representatives may decide not to open or terminate the negotiations and to rely on the rules on information and consultation of employees in force in the member states where the sce has employees.
in writing. − as the economic and financial crisis has shown that the issue of the attractiveness of a legal form cannot be seen only from the point of view of the shareholders; i believe that an enterprise as a social organisation has responsibilities towards shareholders, workers, creditors and society, and this must be taken into account in such an assessment, and i believe that there is a need to ensure a contribution of cooperatives to the social dialogue at european union level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament resolution on the statute for a european cooperative society with regard to the involvement of employees because it brings to the attention an issue which, in my opinion, deserves a much higher position in the european agenda. the model of cooperative societies, especially in a period of economic crisis, represents a virtuous example for sustainable development, social and financial responsibility, a catalyst for workers’ rights and a very useful tool for tackling local and regional development. this document urgently calls the commission for greater concern as regards to the sces, by asking measures to have the implementation of the directive 2003/72/ec supplementing the statute for a cooperative society with regard to the involvement of employees respected by the member states, and by stressing the disappointing scarcity of funds that are minimizing the impact of sces. i strongly believe that the european social model is not dead. cooperatives enhance the work sector and embody the virtues of fair and responsible workfare. they deserve much more.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, given that european cooperative societies (ecs) can be a means of developing the economic power of smes on the market. however, as of 8 may 2010 there were only 17 european cooperative societies registered in 9 member states, none with a significantly large number of employees. while the eu's 21 million smes are a major asset for sustainable growth and job creation, the difficulty of accessing finance is a major obstacle preventing smes from launching new products, strengthening their infrastructure and hiring more workers. it is therefore necessary for member states to promote more favourable conditions for access to credit and tax incentives. access to finance for smes is also a key objective proposed by the commission in the 12 'together for a new growth' levers for stimulating growth and building citizens' confidence in the single market act, and the key action proposed by the commission is to implement legislation to make it easier for venture capital funds established in one member state to invest in any other member state without any additional obstacles or conditions.
in writing. − cooperative societies and other social economy enterprises are part of the european social model and the single market and should be given a high level of recognition and support. cooperative societies could be another step towards completing the eu's internal market and they aim to reduce existing cross-border barriers and strengthen the eu's competitiveness. thus, the specificities of social enterprises must be recognised and taken into account in european policies; measures must be taken to ensure that the european sme observatory includes social enterprises in its surveys; dialogue with social enterprises must be intensified and the legal framework for social enterprises in the member states must be improved. member states should promote more favourable conditions for cooperatives, such as access to credit and tax incentives. the commission should provide an open method of coordination for the social economy, including cooperative societies, involving member states and stakeholders to encourage exchanges of best practices and to ensure a gradual improvement in the way member states take into account the nature of cooperatives, in particular as regards taxation, credit, administrative burdens and measures to support enterprises.
in writing. − i voted for the resolution on the european cooperative society's status in relation to worker participation, because the more than 160 000 cooperative societies across europe provide jobs for some 5.4 million people. cooperative societies create high-quality, locally-based, inclusive and crisis-resilient jobs that cannot, in principle, be relocated. we invite the commission and the member states to encourage cooperatives to step up their efforts to implement policies that promote diversity and ensure equality between men and women in the workplace and, in particular, to increase women's access to senior management positions. in this context, we urge the commission to include european cooperative societies in any european regulation to ensure better representation of women in management positions and on the boards of public and listed companies, should the companies fail to reach, on a voluntary basis, the 30% target by 2015 and the 40% target by 2020. member states should also promote measures to support enterprises, in particular advice on commercial matters, training of workers and access to finance.
in writing. − the development of the european union and the overcoming of the effects of the global economic and financial crisis require the continuation of european integration through the bologna process. support for education and training by national and european institutions is also an integral part of the europe 2020 strategy for a more open society and actively promotes social inclusion. continued european or national support for ensuring easy and equitable access to education and for increasing the representation of disadvantaged social groups is essential for the success of the strategy in this regard. i support the decision of the european authorities to promote policies at the level of the education systems of the member states to link the content of educational programmes with developments on the european labour market. equally important is the process of developing the research sector, which i consider essential for building an economy capable of sustaining development based on innovation and competition. with more and more young europeans choosing to study in a country other than their own, building a european society united in its diversity cannot take place without increasing the compatibility of national education systems.
in writing. − the bologna process has meant profound reforms of higher education for all participating states, marked by changes in legislation and a reconsideration of the basic principles of the educational process for a knowledge-based society. european universities have not only thoroughly revised and reorganised their educational activities in the context of the three-cycle framework envisaged by the bologna process, but have also strengthened their social role by carrying out activities more suited to the so-called 'third mission' of the university system. it is worth noting that there has not always been a good correlation between this system and the labour market. consequently, the statement in the lisbon document that 'despite providing education of a reasonable quality, european universities are not able to realise their full potential to promote economic growth, social cohesion and more and better jobs' remains valid. in the light of the above, i consider that the strengthening of the entire bologna process is essential for the growth targets set out in the europe 2020 strategy to be achieved.
in writing. − i would like to congratulate mr berlinguer on the clarity and conciseness he has shown in drawing up this report. education plays a key role in ensuring that european citizens have access to an internal market without barriers. there are generally recognised advantages of the bologna process, such as the introduction of ects credits, the facilitation of the recognition of diplomas in all eu countries, and consequently the recognition of professional qualifications within the eu. i am pleased to see the achievements of this process, which has given many young people the chance to study in different eu countries, and i believe that the reforms aimed at implementing it must be continued. i agree with the ideas put forward by the rapporteur and support increasing the number of beneficiaries of study grants abroad, facilitating the recognition of qualifications obtained and extending these programmes also within the post-graduate system. i am aware of the importance of education and the effects that gaps in the system could create - youth unemployment is the clearest indicator of this - which is why i support the eu's strongest contribution and involvement to ensure that our children's academic future is the best possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament resolution on the contribution of the european institutions to the consolidation and progress of the bologna process, because i strongly believe that, in order to reach the goal of becoming ‘the most competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy in the world’, the eu must give itself a common framework for the higher education area and, more importantly, a truly european system for mutual recognition of diplomas. i want to underline how this issue closely intertwines these two fields of action. in fact, not only would a more integrated european university system provide evident benefits for research and industry in europe, but it is only possible if the eu is able to strengthen the mobility of its citizens within the union and if it enables the goal of social cohesion in europe. the targets of the bologna process are able to trigger this virtuous circle. this document delivers a clear message from parliament to the member states involved in the bologna process: we need more.
in writing. −the new eu 2020 strategy supports skills development through increased cooperation between education, business and governments. strategies developed by the european institutions have stimulated a major structural reform of the european university system. we need a harmonisation of academic standards at european level. but there are many problems in the eu's university systems, the most important being the link between universities and the labour market. we need to follow these issues closely. the report underlines that european universities have not only thoroughly revised and reorganised their educational activities in the context of the three-cycle framework envisaged by the bologna process, but have also strengthened their social role. i support this report and i advocate for more transparency of universities towards students.
in writing. − the bologna process has brought about fundamental changes in higher education in europe. remarkable progress has been made in many areas, but more efforts are needed to ensure full achievement of all the bologna objectives in the next decade. institutions should be supported to improve recognition and credit transfer by implementing ects, academic results, the diploma supplement and the lisbon convention on the recognition of qualifications in a comparable and fair manner across europe (for example, through a european recognition user guide and european training seminars funded by the commission). signatory countries should ensure the full and comparable introduction of national qualifications frameworks, in line with the urgently needed european higher education area qualifications framework, in order to facilitate mobility, recognition and lifelong learning. in order to promote europe as an attractive study destination for students from all over the world, the european commission could promote european higher education activities globally.
in writing. − by initiating the bologna process, we have achieved an important objective for the union and the partner countries: the creation of a common framework for higher education in europe. the principles on which this commitment is based have been largely implemented, whether it is the two-tier university structure, the system of transferable credits or the mobility of students and teaching staff. to further improve the global competitiveness of european higher education, and the integration of european citizens into the labour market, we need to make further efforts. the number of master's places needs to be adapted to the existing demand, given that in some countries the bachelor's degree offers low employment prospects. at the same time, it is necessary to regulate the status of pre-bologna students in those countries where they are disadvantaged in entering master programmes. on the other hand, universities in the signatory states must recognise traineeships completed under mobility programmes supported by the european commission, while creating a sufficient number of traineeships to facilitate their subsequent integration into the labour market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr berlinguer's report because it stresses the need to adapt education systems to the current market requirements. in the current socio-economic conditions, it is very important to strengthen the entire bologna process in order to achieve the growth targets set out in the europe 2020 strategy. on the other hand, such consolidation is one of the requirements for the full integration of the eu's internal market and an indispensable tool to meet the challenges posed by the economic and financial crisis.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the contribution of the european institutions to the strengthening and progress of the bologna process, as there is a need to strengthen support in terms of mutual recognition of university qualifications, harmonisation of academic standards, promotion of mobility, social dimension and employment prospects, active democratic participation and removal of administrative obstacles in the application of the principles of the bologna process. i voted for member states to reiterate their commitment to the bologna process by strengthening the financing system to achieve the growth targets set by the europe 2020 strategy. i voted for paragraph 26, which stresses that measures to facilitate occupational integration (e.g. lifelong learning and the development of a broader range of labour market-friendly skills) must be top priorities in order to achieve sustainable growth and prosperity objectives. in this context, we support university exchanges of teachers and students, university-business dialogue, apprenticeships and the skills passport. we stress the need for specific action and more effective cooperation between universities and the labour market, with a view to developing more relevant university programmes, harmonising educational activity and improving employment prospects by establishing similar criteria for access to different professions.
in writing. − statistical information is the result of statistical production processes carried out throughout the european statistical system (ess). users of european statistics should be able to use this information with confidence for decision-making purposes. to this end, those statistics shall be appropriate for use. it is essential that users consider statistics to be relevant, timely, accurate and in line with the principles of official statistics, such as professional independence, impartiality and objectivity. this is true for the whole of the european statistical system, including eurostat. the overall quality of statistical information at european level depends to a large extent on the adequacy of the entire production process used to obtain these statistics. if the data provided by the member states are of unsatisfactory quality, this has a negative impact on the quality of european statistics. to prevent such situations, comprehensive and reliable sse quality management is needed. this systemic approach to quality will benefit from the results of the reform of the method of production of european statistics, as it is expected to streamline the entire chain of statistics production.
in writing. − as eurostat provides the economic indicators needed for the surveillance of fiscal policies and the scoreboard of macroeconomic imbalances, alongside new enforcement mechanisms, i believe that the quality management of government financial statistics and other national statistical data, as well as the accuracy and timely reporting of data, is a prerequisite for the proper functioning of the european statistical system.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament resolution on quality management for european statistics, because i firmly believe that improvements in the quality of statistics delivery, and in their driving mechanisms, have an evident impact on the policy-making – and therefore on the economic credibility, stability and growth – of the european union and its member states. i greatly welcome this document, aimed at asking the commission for legislative proposals to introduce elements of the revised european statistics code of practice into eu law, because it calls for the independence and transparency of the statistical authorities to be strengthened, nationally and at european level, and asks eurostat to simplify its reports and publications in order to become more user-friendly and accessible to all eu citizens. i believe that clear, independent and transparent data gathering and publication provide a solid basis – and the most important starting point – for fair and balanced law-making.
in writing. − the provision of accurate and relevant statistics is essential for sustainable and balanced regional development. such details in areas such as demography, economy and environment play a key role in the decision-making process on regional development, in particular in the context of the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. it is therefore necessary to develop a coherent system of research on socio-economic processes in cross-border areas (including those in regions situated at the external borders of the european union), together with statistics for macro-regions, in order to obtain a complete and accurate picture of the economy in terms of regional and macro-regional development, covering both urban and rural areas. in the future, eurostat should find a way to make its analyses, especially online ones, easier for non-professionals to use and to include comparative charts to provide more added value to citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european statistics report because, in my view, the provision of accurate and truly relevant statistics is essential both for sustainable and balanced regional development and for the development of european policies capable of responding effectively to economic, social and territorial realities at all levels: local, regional, national and european. we need to take the necessary steps to ensure that users of statistics have access to quality information, provided in a timely manner, both at member state and european union level. in the context of the economic crisis in the euro area, which has very clearly highlighted the risks associated with statistical inattention and statistical fraud, i consider it particularly important that statistical bodies have mechanisms and protective systems in place to avoid being politically influenced. this way we can be sure that they are independent, which is very important for maintaining the credibility of statistical data. and last but not least, i would like to welcome the binding nature of the rules on the production and verification of the accuracy of european statistics, because in this way member states will have to ensure that statistics are accurate at all levels of governance.
in writing. − the crisis of statelessness currently affecting europe, the achievement of the 2020 objectives and the need for sustained economic growth and development at both micro- and macro-regional levels require a coordinated, well-considered and evidence-based economic policy on the part of the european union (eu). clearly, only precise, objective figures, unaffected by political entities, can underpin the measures that will underpin the eu's sustainable economic development. to this end, it is important that both member states and eurostat make accurate and reliable data available to policy-makers and citizens. this is a prerequisite for monitoring economic and demographic developments and for allowing any erroneous measures to be corrected in a timely manner. it is essential that the court of auditors review the statistics submitted by eurostat and the member states, carry out regular financial audits and provide expert assistance, where necessary, by means of expertise. in light of all this, i can only support the motion.
in writing. − i voted for the report on quality management for european statistics because independent and high quality statistics are needed to guarantee growth and employment. users of statistics should have access to relevant, accurate and timely data, which should be collected and compiled by national agencies in accordance with the principles of impartiality, objectivity and professional independence. precise data are a basis for detailed information and analysis in areas such as demography, economics and the environment and therefore play a key role in regional development decision-making. eurostat publications, in particular online publications, should be easier to use for the average citizen and non-professionals. the eurostat website should allow easier access to complete data and include intuitive and comparative charts, in order to provide more added value and clarity for citizens. member states should ensure that statistics are accurate at all levels of governance. we encourage eurostat to inform the public if it has any doubts about the accuracy of all types of statistics. we invite the commission and the member states to take the necessary measures to strengthen the independence of eurostat, including through changes to its institutional status.

according to unicef, an estimated 158 million children between the ages of 5 and 14 are working, or one in six children worldwide. millions of children are working in conditions that endanger their health, practically exposing them to various harmful chemicals. in west africa alone, more than 100,000 children are working in the most difficult conditions in the cocoa fields, and 10,000 children are victims of human trafficking. low marketing prices for cocoa push farmers to use child labour, with profound consequences for children's health and school performance. i believe that access to education is a fundamental condition for reducing poverty and ending the exploitation of children. the union has at its disposal several instruments to put an end to these practices and i would remind you here of the possibility of suspending trade preference agreements under the gsp and of the need for all trade agreements with third countries to contain provisions on the elimination of child labour.
if we look closely at the figures on the prevalence of diabetes in the population of the european union, whether we're talking about type 1 or type 2 diabetes, it's clear that serious efforts are needed to combat diabetes. i want to emphasize prevention, both because prevention is the best in terms of cost-effectiveness, and because, unfortunately, in diabetes and other chronic diseases, right now we're focusing more on treatment and less on prevention. promoting a healthy lifestyle and tackling risk factors are key to tackling this disease. the fact that we are now discussing the horizon 2020 research programme is also a great opportunity to improve the system, to better coordinate the diabetes research effort and to ensure the necessary funding and infrastructure. we need a european strategy that focuses on prevention, early and effective diagnosis, management of this disease, public information and research.

in writing. – although there is no cure for diabetes, it can often be prevented. in 2007, the commission published its strategy on nutrition and obesity, which emphasised how clear and accurate information about food can help prevent diseases such as diabetes. so, five years on, what has the strategy achieved? it has promoted voluntary codes and a self-regulatory approach to the advertising of foodstuffs to children. however, according to the commission’s own progress report, some member states have not yet adopted a voluntary code, whilst others have no mechanism in place to check whether their code is being implemented. unhealthy foods which increase the risk of obesity and diabetes are still being aggressively marketed to children. the strategy on nutrition also highlighted the role of the health claims regulation in ensuring that consumers are not misled by inaccurate or confusing claims. but this regulation cannot function properly because the commission has not yet proposed key elements of it. so the health claims legislation is not yet in operation and, in the meantime, junk food continues to be advertised to children. the commission and the member states must re-think their approach to information and education about food if they are serious about tackling diabetes.
in writing. i believe that since approximately 10% of the total population of the union suffers from diabetes, we must take a global leadership role in finding the most appropriate solutions to reduce the incidence of diabetes. among the things we need to do is allocate additional funds to diabetes prevention measures in the population and identify the most appropriate measures to improve healthy consumer behaviour. the first steps in this direction are already being taken, and i am referring in particular to the regulation on nutrition and health claims on foodstuffs, but also to the reform of the common agricultural policy, which represents an opportunity to increase the population's access to healthier food. in addition to prevention measures, we must consider early detection of the disease and, by implication, the development of appropriate tools to address social inequalities among populations at risk. to do this, we need to have access to data on chronic diseases in the member states and we need to work together because only together can we overcome the scientific challenges. in addition, we need to pay more attention to education and its role in choosing the healthiest consumption patterns.
the lack of co-financing capacity is undoubtedly one of the most important obstacles to the effective use of european funds, including the european fisheries fund, at the moment. the financial crisis, through the budgetary constraints it has caused, has brought additional difficulties to the situation of european states below the overall eu average. the commission's proposals for all categories of funds are therefore good news for the member states concerned. i must stress that another difficult problem remains unresolved, however, namely the lack of resources for private co-financing of investments. this is true for all categories of european funds, and especially for those for small businesses and agriculture. in this regard, we need credit facilities and public guarantees in support of potential beneficiaries. simplification of procedures is also essential.

in writing. trade policy is an important area for the european union and the member states, which is why any regulation that improves its implementation, either at national and european level or in relation to third countries, is beneficial for all partners. this report builds on the changes brought about by the treaty of lisbon to the legal and institutional framework and allows for the systematic transposition of those changes into secondary legislation in the field of the common commercial policy. i believe that the entry into force of its provisions will enable the commission to exercise its implementing powers more effectively, which will lead to a more effective common commercial policy. in addition, both the partners involved and citizens will be able to understand the procedures applicable in the framework of trade policy more quickly, and the application of the horizontal regulation will increase the overall level of transparency in the application of trade policy.

economy. the recovery from the economic and financial collapse in 2008 and 2009 is well under way. this is not least due to responsible macroeconomic policies and tough decisions on structural and welfare reforms. also due to this, iceland successfully completed its imf programme in august 2011 and has just recently seen itself upgraded by the rating agency fitch. iceland still faces challenges. but with the current economic outlook, we are convinced that iceland will be able to cope with competitive pressures and market forces within the union over the medium term. let me move on received and dealt with all screening reports except those from the fishery chapters. we expect to receive that report around easter. as for the negotiations of the 35 negotiation chapters, 11 chapters have now been opened and eight have been provisionally closed, thanks to the efforts of previous presidencies. this is a remarkable result, which underlines iceland’s very high level of preparedness for membership. it also represents momentum to be upheld, which we will do everything possible to achieve. the next accession conference with iceland at deputy level is planned for 30 competition policy, energy, and foreign security and defence policy, and also to provisionally close some of those chapters. the accession conference at ministerial level planned for june will confirm the results of the accession conference in march and sustain the momentum in the negotiations by opening and provisionally closing a further number of chapters. all in all, we expect negotiations to continue at very good speed this semester. some more challenging negotiations, such as those on fisheries, lie ahead of us. however, given the commitment and focus from the icelandic side, we are very confident that, with the right amount of goodwill and political determination, substantial progress can be achieved in these areas as well. i am convinced of the commitment of all parties to bring the negotiations forward. in conclusion, the aim of the presidency is to sustain momentum in the negotiations and bring them forward as much as possible. this is a task that we can only achieve with the support and cooperation of the member states, the commission and, not least, this parliament, as this debate will show. let me also, on behalf of the danish presidency and the member states, thank this parliament and in particular your rapporteur, mr preda, for the work done on this issue. your continued commitment to enlargement is vital to its success – as is, of course, your particular role in promoting popular support in the eu for this cause. the resolution on iceland and its endorsement in plenary is indeed a forceful political and strategic message. i also believe that, through contacts with fellow parliamentarians from the althingi in iceland, this house will be able to make an important and much-needed contribution to enhancing understanding of the eu, the values that we in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of this report on the regulation of imports of high-quality beef. the dispute over hormone-treated beef has had a negative impact on transatlantic trade in agricultural products for more than two decades. in 1988, the european union banned imports of beef and beef products treated with certain growth stimulating hormones for consumer protection and food safety reasons. in 1996, the united states and canada challenged this ban under the wto dispute settlement system and were subsequently authorised to impose trade sanctions against agricultural products imported from the european union. since 1999, the us and canada have imposed retaliatory tariffs on a wide range of european products. the proposal contains protocols which i consider crucial and which will be implemented in several phases, in accordance with american and canadian criteria. the impact on the european market is still limited, but failure to adopt the regulation could lead to further trade sanctions against the union.

in writing. − trade policy is one of the main pillars of the european union's relations with third countries. the achievement of a common trade policy was part of the original plan for european economic integration, so that the eu's (initially the eec's) trade policy has been broadly common to the rest of the world since 1968, with the achievement of the customs union. this proposal for a commission regulation aims to replace the decision-making procedures on implementing measures under 26 delegated and implementing regulations. as regards those regulations, these are mainly provisions allowing the use of trade defence measures. the commission proposal provides for adjustments only where specifically regulated council decisions were previously applicable. the commission does not propose to amend the references in the regulations to the old comitology procedure based on council decision 1999/468/ec. in this regard, the commission has indicated on several occasions that these adaptations should be made in a second proposal for a regulation, namely the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending certain regulations relating to the common commercial policy as regards the delegation of power to adopt certain measures (omnibus ii).
in writing. − the vote in favour of the report on the common commercial policy was necessary to bring european trade policies into line. with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon on 1 december 2009, trade policy became an area of exclusive responsibility of the european union. through the report, 26 regulations are brought into line with the treaty, by delegating powers to the european commission and by establishing control procedures by eu member states. these include, for example, the regulation on the trade arrangements applicable to certain goods resulting from the processing of agricultural products or the regulation on trade in certain goods which could be used for capital punishment, torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.
in writing. − the commission proposal for a regulation aims to replace the decision-making procedures on implementing measures under 26 regulations with delegated and implementing acts. until now, thanks to these special decision-making mechanisms, european trade policy has been broadly and explicitly exempted from the existing comitology procedure. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon brought an end to this special regime and the commission will thus become responsible for all executive decisions in the field of trade policy. the aim of this proposal is to integrate the commission's responsibilities into all regulations in the field of the common commercial policy. i consider this report to be a balanced, well-conceived document which respects the economic and legislative interests of all parties involved and the institutional interests of the three european institutions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation amending certain regulations on the common commercial policy in relation to the procedures for adopting certain measures. the regulation aims to replace the decision-making procedures on implementing measures under 26 delegated and implementing acts. as regards those regulations, these are mainly provisions allowing the use of trade defence measures. the report recommends the use of delegated acts under those regulations in the following cases: - for amending or adapting one or more annexes to the regulation concerned and - for adopting detailed provisions on the specific transposition of individual articles. in all cases, these are non-legislative delegated acts of general scope which supplement or amend certain non-essential elements of the legislative act, in accordance with article 290 (1) tfeu. only the instrument of delegation ensures the control of the commission by parliament and the council. the report calls on the commission to submit biannual reports to parliament on the application and implementation of the agreements, including information on the activities of the various bodies responsible for monitoring the implementation of the agreements and the fulfilment of the obligations arising from them, including the obligations relating to trade barriers.
