in writing. − the proposal for a regulation to strengthen the fight against organised crime is of particular importance for the safety and security of european citizens and supports one of the main objectives of the european union, namely to create an area of freedom, security and justice without internal borders, in which crime is prevented and combated. that is why i believe that the establishment of a special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering will help the european union to anticipate and counter these threats at national and international level. the tasks of this committee will include analysing and evaluating the implementation of union legislation in this area to ensure that union law and policies are based on data and real threat assessments. it will also be responsible for monitoring and reviewing the activities of eu agencies in the field of home affairs dealing with organised crime, corruption and money laundering, as well as related security policies.
in writing. − i voted for the establishment of a special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. its establishment also responds to the calls of the resolution on eu anti-corruption efforts, which i initiated and which was adopted by the european parliament on 15 september 2011. organized crime and financial fraud cannot exist without corruption. organized crime structures use corruption as a tool to gain access to improper resources and information and to ensure that criminal acts cannot be traced and proven. money laundering provides the 'fuel' that organised crime structures use to perpetuate corruption. it is clear that these three types of criminal offences can only be tackled simultaneously. european citizens want to see concrete measures to combat crime at european level. the commission will examine the extent and impact of organised crime, corruption and money laundering on the union, the effectiveness of the european agencies in the field of internal affairs (europol, cosi, eurojust) in achieving their objectives and will propose measures to combat these acts simultaneously. i hope that the commission's work will have a tangible and visible impact on citizens, by reducing the number of criminal offences and effectively sanctioning them.
in writing. − i voted for the mandate of the special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the tasks of the special committee will include: analysing and assessing the extent of organised crime, corruption and money laundering and their impact on the union and its member states; proposing appropriate measures to enable the union to anticipate and counter these threats at international, european and national level; analysing and assessing the implementation of union law on organised crime, corruption and money laundering and related policies; examining and monitoring the implementation of the role and activities of union agencies in the field of internal affairs (such as europol, cosi and euro) dealing with organised crime, corruption and money laundering and related security policies. the commission will have 45 members and a 12-month mandate, starting on 1 april 2012, with the possibility of its extension. the commission will present to parliament an interim report and an end-of-term report containing recommendations on actions or initiatives to be taken.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the continuing professional training of judicial staff is essential for the functioning of the institutional system in the member states. the pilot project launched by the european parliament aims to strengthen the network of trainers and training institutes in the field. the stockholm programme aims to create a judiciary that is fully independent and impartial. the separation of powers in the state - particularly in the judiciary - is one of its aims. the public trust in judges and the public prosecutor's office and the free access to justice must also be strengthened. here i would like to mention the training programmes carried out by the national union of notaries public in romania in collaboration with the european council of the liberal professions, of which he is a co-founder member. only in this way can he ensure the fair administration of justice and his role as moderator of society. the national judiciary is the guarantor of fundamental rights closest to the beneficiaries of those rights. the project will also support the development of a european network of experts in the field of crime prevention and investigation, as well as the development of a european network of experts in the field of crime prevention and investigation.
in writing. − continuing legal training is a particularly important element for a successful national, but also european, legal system. the benefits that european cooperation in this field could bring are not negligible. the exchange of experience between legal practitioners plays a very important role, as it is open to interpretation and the views of legal practitioners may differ even if the subject is the same. in addition, legal doctrine is dynamic and the knowledge of legal practitioners must be constantly updated. the establishment of a 'european legal culture' through the organisation of traineeships at european level, the use of new 'apps' (applications for legal training) and the moderation of annual forums where judges and prosecutors can exchange experience would facilitate the dissemination of information at european level. this helps to remove barriers in the internal market in this area, which will facilitate access for lawyers/judges to eu legal posts, while also helping them to improve at national level. we deserve the best lawyers, the best judges, and for that we must give them the opportunity to excel at european level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on judicial training because i believe that the european judicial area must be based on a shared european judicial culture of practitioners, judges and prosecutors, based not only on union law but developed through mutual knowledge and understanding of national judicial systems, through in-depth review of university programmes, through exchanges, study visits and joint training courses. the active support of the academy of european law, the european judicial training network and the institute of european law is essential in this regard. the comparative study on judicial training in the member states, commissioned by the parliament and carried out by the european law academy in collaboration with the european judicial training network, highlighted the existence of language barriers, the lack of (timely) information on existing programmes and the fact that programmes are not always adapted to the needs of judges. i believe that the use of ict technologies, videoconferencing, online courses, webstreaming, as well as the organisation of exchanges of experience, facilitation and promotion of dialogue and professional contacts can contribute to improving the judicial training process.
in writing. - as the european union is both the world's leading producer of chocolate and the world's leading importer of cocoa, i believe that the european authorities cannot shirk their responsibility for working conditions in this sector. it is up to the european institutions to step in and send a clear message that trafficking in live meat and the exploitation of children in this sector are not tolerated or encouraged by the european authorities and consumers. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. − as in recent years programmes and initiatives to combat the worst forms of child labour on cocoa farms in west africa have made significant progress and as the re-emerging conflict situations in the region, especially in côte d'ivoire, have further aggravated the situation of children, i believe that the use of forced child labour on cocoa farms is a very serious matter and that the use of child labour on cocoa farms should no longer be used.
in writing. - i voted for the report on child labour in the cocoa production sector. according to estimates by the international labour organization, over 215 million children worldwide are exploited in child labor. 70% of the world's cocoa production is in west africa, and about 7.5 million people are employed in cocoa production in this region. the cultivation of cocoa beans is labour intensive during harvesting seasons and producers face strong pressures to keep labour costs low. during peak production periods, all family members, including children, are involved in this process. studies in ghana and côte d'ivoire highlight the diverse range of hazards faced by children working on cocoa farms. i call on the commission to ensure that all trade agreements contain effective provisions aimed at poverty reduction and the promotion of decent work, safe working conditions and include binding clauses on human rights and internationally recognised social standards, as well as clauses ensuring compliance with these standards and measures applicable in the event of their breach.
in writing. − i welcome the conclusion of the new trade agreement on the marketing of cocoa, which replaces the previous legislative framework dating back to 2001. the new agreement meets the imperatives of transparency in trade deals, creating the conditions for sustainable development and a fairer distribution of financial resources generated by transactions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament consent to the international cocoa agreement 2010, because it defines improvements to the social and market sustainability of the cocoa production industry, establishing a fair balance between prices for consumers and producers. the european union is one of the main importers of cocoa beans: therefore we both have the need and the responsibility to get involved in the multilateral process of international market regulation. i very positively welcomed the decision to link the adoption of the agreement to a resolution and a commission statement on child labour in the cocoa sector: the issue certainly merits a separate treatment given its crucial relevance in the field of children rights. we urgently must take the direction of the total ban of child labour in trade.
in writing. − as the cocoa trade is vulnerable to exploitation in various forms, having a framework in place that protects both producers and consumers is important. therefore, i am in favour of the renewal of the international cocoa agreement. cocoa consumption in developed countries, especially in europe, is higher than in the developing countries where it is grown. in return for the privilege of reaping the economic benefits of selling this commodity, europe must be prepared to abide by certain standards. in order for this market to sustain itself, efforts dedicated to environmental protection need to be maintained. responsible growing and harvesting practices must be respected. in addition, cocoa producers need to be adequately remunerated. it is much too easy in a system like this to ensure that the majority of the profits wind up in the hands of the people who simply market the product, not in the hands of those who actually produce it. certainly in order for these and other standards not mentioned here to be met, transparency is key. consumers are more than ever concerned with the weight of their spending power. this agreement has the potential to respond to the needs of the globalised world.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the 2010 international cocoa agreement. as the largest importer and consumer of cocoa, the union has an important share of responsibility for enhancing the sustainability of the cocoa-producing sector. the 2010 agreement aims to create the conditions for a more economically, socially and environmentally sustainable and fairer global cocoa trade. the objectives of the new agreement are to promote international cooperation in the global cocoa production sector, to provide an appropriate framework for discussions between governments and with the private sector on all aspects of cocoa production, to strengthen the national cocoa production sectors of the member states, and to work towards fair prices that generate fair revenues for both producers and consumers. the agreement aims to bring more transparency and sustainability to a sector that provides livelihoods for 50 million people worldwide. i believe that the agreement will have a positive impact on all participants in the cocoa production sector and will translate into tangible long-term benefits for both small farmers and their communities.
in writing. − diabetes is one of the most prevalent chronic diseases affecting european citizens, putting a serious strain on the healthcare and health insurance systems of the eu countries. according to the world health organization, the number of people with diabetes in europe has already exceeded the 35 million mark and is set to approach the critical level of 50 million by 2030. the sustained efforts of national health authorities and the improvement of the european cooperation framework are essential to reverse these trends of great concern to public health. since more than a third of newly diagnosed cases of diabetes could have been prevented by regular medical checks, coupled with the practice of a healthy lifestyle and diet, i believe that special emphasis should be placed on organising european campaigns to raise awareness of the factors that favour or cause the development of diabetes. that's why i voted for the resolution.
in writing. − the disordered lifestyle has caused a real 'diabetes epidemic' in recent years, with new cases increasing month by month. globally, the number of patients is estimated to increase from 194 million today to 333 million in 2025. in the european union, 31 million people, or 8.6% of the population aged 20-79, suffer from diabetes. in romania there are 370 000 registered diabetics, and their number is increasing by 50 000 every year. diabetologists, however, claim that the real number of diabetics in romania is double that. diabetes is the leading cause of death in europe, with 80% of people with diabetes dying from cardiovascular complications. in the light of the above, i believe that an eu diabetes strategy with clear objectives on diabetes prevention, diagnosis, management, education and research is needed.
in writing. − according to statistics, almost 285 million people worldwide are diagnosed with the disease, of which about 55.2 million in europe. the estimates for 2030 worldwide are 438 million patients. but the cost of treatment is high -- in the united states alone, it's $210 billion a year, and that's going to be over $300 billion by 2025, because there's no medical solution to diabetes, there's a social solution. diet and lifestyle play a key role in avoiding chronic degenerative diseases such as type 2 diabetes. prevention of this devious disease must begin very soon. we have clear studies that prove that it's enough to lose three to four pounds, by walking for 30 minutes a day at a brisk pace, to reduce the incidence of diabetes by almost two-thirds. taking all this into account, member states should promote the prevention of type 2 diabetes through education in schools on healthy eating habits and physical activity. harmonisation of food policies is also needed to promote a healthy diet and to enable consumers to choose healthy products.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution and would like to recall the five priority actions identified by the un special rapporteur on the right to food to put nutrition at the heart of food systems in the developed and developing world: taxing products harmful to health; regulating foods high in saturated fat, salt and sugar; curbing advertising for junk food; and reviewing unwise agricultural subsidies that make some ingredients cheaper than others; and support local food production so that consumers have access to healthy, fresh and nutritious food.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on tackling the diabetes epidemic in the eu, diabetes being one of the most widespread non-communicable diseases, estimated to affect over 32 million eu citizens, which is almost 10% of the union's population. according to statistics, the number of people with diabetes in europe will increase by 16.6% by 2030 as a result of the obesity epidemic and the ageing population. calls on the member states to promote the prevention of type 2 diabetes and obesity through healthy lifestyle strategies, including diet and exercise, and education in schools on healthy eating habits and physical activity. only 16 of the 27 member states have a national framework or specific programme to tackle diabetes. given that there are considerable differences and inequalities in the quality of diabetes treatments across the eu, i call on member states to ensure that patients have permanent access to diabetes treatments and technologies, including e-health technologies. i call on the commission to develop and implement an eu diabetes strategy with clear objectives on diabetes prevention, diagnosis, treatment, education and research.
in writing. − the western balkans are an area of great interest to the european union and, as promised to the states in this area, sooner or later they will be able to become members of the european union. although the council did not take a decision to open accession negotiations with that country at its meeting on 9 december 2011, recent progress by the former yugoslav republic of macedonia is encouraging. the enlargement process in this region must be based on intensive regional cooperation and good neighbourly relations. that is why it is very important to find a compromise on the issues that are the subject of dispute in this region. i believe that the accession process will contribute to greater regional stability and to the improvement of the economic performance of the balkan region.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that macedonia must go forward on its way to the european union and therefore it is essential to send a positive signal regarding its future with us. on 5 december 2011, the international court of justice decided that greece, by objecting to the admission of macedonia to nato, had breached its obligation under the interim accord of 13 september 1995. i welcome this decision. now, the council should reflect the court’s decision and immediately follow the recommendation of the european commission by giving macedonia a start date for its accession negotiations. the name issue between macedonia and greece is exclusively a bilateral issue and, as such, it should not interfere with the opening of accession negotiations. progress has been made in the judiciary and the fight against corruption. i encourage the authorities to continue improving the independence, efficiency and resources of the judiciary and would stress that the unification of jurisprudence and publishing all court decisions are vital for the predictability of the judiciary and public trust in the system. high-level corruption cases must be a priority, along with transparency of public expenditure and the funding of political parties.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the enlargement of the former yugoslav republic of macedonia. regional cooperation and good neighbourly relations remain key components of the enlargement process. i welcome the progress made in modernising transport, energy and telecommunications networks. given the importance of rail links as an alternative to road transport, i welcome the government's intention to modernise or build rail links from skopje to the capitals of neighbouring countries. i encourage continued efforts to implement the bologna process in higher education and cooperation with other countries in this region to increase the quality of universities in the region. i call on the government to do more to tackle structural unemployment and protect vulnerable groups, in particular through sustainable economic growth and the creation of a favourable business environment. to this end, i call on the government to support small and medium-sized enterprises by facilitating their access to finance. i am concerned about the modest progress on workers' and trade union rights. i call on the authorities to further strengthen labour law and trade union rights and to make more efforts to align national legislation with the eu acquis in this area.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the 2011 country report on iceland. i support iceland's accession process as iceland contributes to european cohesion and solidarity. i encourage the icelandic authorities to continue their efforts to reduce the level of unemployment and in particular youth unemployment. i call on the government to stimulate small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) by facilitating their presence in the international market and ensuring adequate access to financial resources. iceland, whose energy production is mostly from renewable sources, can make a valuable contribution to eu policies in this area, due to its experience in the field of renewable energy. the icelandic authorities have also provided information on the implementation of the new rules on the protection of personal data. i believe that iceland's accession to the eu would significantly strengthen the union's prospects of playing a more active and constructive role in northern europe and the arctic, contributing to multilateral governance and sustainable policy solutions in the region.
in writing. − unfortunately, the report the commission has submitted to the european parliament finds too little progress, both politically and in the other areas addressed in the accession process. political and legal reforms have stagnated. the constitution has not been harmonized with the provisions of the european convention on human rights, there are problems between the country's parliament and the parliaments of the three entities, reforms have produced too little progress in increasing the administrative capacity of the state and its various institutions. the report shows that justice remains a major issue. so is freedom of the press and freedom of speech. the eu has a strong interest in the stabilisation of the western balkans and has done everything in its power to deliver on its commitments. it seems that our partners lack the political will to take the decisions needed to be able to achieve the expected progress together. i understand the problems of bosnia and herzegovina, that many of the wounds of the past have not closed or the healing is superficial. but it is precisely to avoid a repeat of the past that these changes are needed, progress in the political and judicial spheres first and foremost. these are some of the reasons why i support the resolution.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the 2011 progress report on bosnia and herzegovina. the prospect of eu membership is one of the most unifying factors for the population of this country. i stress the vital role of education in creating a multi-ethnic society and promoting an inclusive and non-discriminatory education system. i believe that the quality of education, adapted to the demands of the labour market, needs to be improved. in this regard, i call on the authorities of bosnia and herzegovina to address the shortcomings in vocational training, to attract foreign direct investment and to ensure the start of accreditation of educational institutions and the full functioning of the agencies responsible for the recognition of diplomas. in bosnia and herzegovina, workers' rights and trade union rights are still limited. i call on the government to further strengthen these rights and to work towards harmonising the legal framework for them across the country. welcomes the implementation of the small business act and the efforts to ensure measures to provide financial support to small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). i stress the importance of creating a register for the production of economic statistics, as well as a single system of registration of smes for the whole country, which will facilitate the increase in the number of smes and the creation of a specific status for them.
a first conclusion of the demonstrations and elections in russia is that russian civil society has become stronger and may be able to generate an alternative to the current power. i believe that in its relations with the kremlin administration the european union must promote pragmatism, without this being a compromise with our political and moral values. russia must know that our position on respect for human rights and democratic and transparent governance is non-negotiable. the european union must also make it clear to moscow that its position on regimes such as syria is not in favour of the people suffering under totalitarian governments. i think it's important that the new administration condemns what's happening in syria, especially in the united nations. on the other hand, it would be desirable for the european union and the member states to speak the same language when it comes to key dimensions of relations with the russian federation, such as energy policies.
for many of us who have lived under the shadow of russia under communist regimes, the outcome of this election is simply the election of vladimir putin as president. i would not want us to delude ourselves and look at things from only one perspective. russia will be, for a very long time from now, between asian-style modernization and european-style democracy. what is certain is that the 30% of russian citizens who are motivated to choose the european model are worth our investment. i stress that our partnership with russia must focus on strengthening civil society and strengthening an opposition that hopefully will no longer be divided. on elections: they certainly were neither free nor transparent, according to our standards. we shouldn't judge elections by the day of the vote, but by the context. but i think if our partnership is to remain a privileged policy, we'll have to continue with realism.
on behalf of the alde group. i want to welcome, first of all, the realistic way in which the statement made on behalf of mrs ashton addresses the situation in kazakhstan. and i think that not only kazakhstan, but the whole of central asia should be a strategic partnership for the european union, because we can't just talk about human rights, but also about social rights, and this is something we should be particularly concerned about. i want to welcome the start of negotiations for this partnership and cooperation agreement, because we have never had the cynicism to just criticize, but we have understood, as politicians, to get involved to change things. this seems to me to be the way forward in an active foreign policy action of the european union. within this agreement, human rights issues must be given priority. at the same time, however, we cannot afford to ignore the major democratic lapses we are facing in kazakhstan. i also welcome the release of natalia sokolovska, but i particularly demand the release of the opposition leader, mr kozlov, and the leader of one of the most important press authorities, mr igor viniavski, the editor. these are not the only leaders who today face unfair and unfair trials based on a law that targets national security in kazakhstan. i think the main signal that the leaders of kazakhstan want to democratize their country, want to ensure a future that is meant for its citizens, is the way they approach fundamental rights and freedoms. it is vital that that national security law be re-discussed, because it is the source of these oppressions and this cannot be tolerated. we can't consider free speech a violation of a law that concerns national security. no concept of national security in the world can violate the fundamental rights and freedoms of the individual.
the european union and kazakhstan can develop a genuine partnership based on political and economic cooperation to the benefit of both parties. this is evidenced by the increased frequency of meetings over the past year and the launch of negotiations for a new partnership and cooperation agreement. but for these relations to develop further, the kazakh authorities need to respect their commitments on democratic reforms and fundamental human rights. a number of measures are essential in this respect. first, the irregularities reported by the osce/odihr in the january elections should be investigated. at the same time, further efforts are needed to ensure the rights of the opposition and freedom of the press. in this context, i would also like to welcome the recent release of natalia sokolova and hope that other similar gestures will follow. in addition, the janaozen incident in december 2011 resulted in the deaths of at least 10 civilians and the detention of at least 10 civilians. the authorities have, however, stated their determination to investigate the facts in a transparent and comprehensive manner, within the framework of a committee of inquiry. we must encourage them to make every effort to do so. i would like to ask the high representative, if she were present, how she would assess kazakhstan's role at regional level in relation to the other central asian countries.
what is happening in nigeria, the instability, the violence, the extremism, and now the killing of two western citizens, is a strong warning signal on two levels: on the communication between the countries of the european union and on the spread of sectarian violence on the african continent. i think we need to become much more aware of this region where terrorist groups coordinated by al qaeda are active. there is also a need for greater concern for nigeria as a whole. in africa's most populous country, 80 percent of its 170 million people are living in squalor and poverty, even though the country itself is not poor. nigeria is the ninth largest oil exporter in the world, but at the same time, it's one of the most corrupt and lowest ranked countries in the un's human development index. that's why i think we need to move beyond the minimal stage of election monitoring in african states, otherwise bad governance, poverty and corruption will continue to fuel instability and violence.
for several months now, news from nigeria has been troubling. the actions of the terrorist group boko haram have become increasingly violent. in november 2011, 65 people were killed in a series of bombings in damaturu; on christmas day, 44 people were killed in an attack outside the sainte-thérèse church in abuja. the friday night attacks in kano, in the north of the country, which led to the deaths of at least 185 people, are among the most barbaric acts yet claimed by boko haram. nigeria, on the other hand, has been, as we know, for decades, the scene of clashes between christians and muslims. the deterioration of the security situation is, however, at this moment evident and i do not think it can be ignored any longer. the actions of boko haram threaten the balance of the entire country and there are many voices who wonder even if, at this moment, nigeria is not on the verge of disappearing. our support is therefore needed more than ever to establish a climate of tolerance and respect for religious freedom in nigeria. finally, i would like to draw attention to paragraph 7 of our joint resolution: boko haram threatens not only nigeria, but the entire region, because of potential connections with aqim. we must therefore encourage regional efforts aimed at preventing synergies between boko haram and aqim.
the news about nigeria in recent times has been almost entirely about violent incidents. this is a worrying fact, especially given the rise of religious extremism, which is fuelling a very significant number of attacks. the question is what can be done now to avoid making this situation worse. the consequences would be disastrous in a country with over 170 million inhabitants, 250 ethnic groups and a population that is 50% muslim and 40% christian. tensions between different communities overlap with a very difficult economic context: 85% of the population lives on less than two dollars a day, even though nigeria has significant oil reserves. i would have liked the high representative to present proposals for a more active contribution by the union to promoting a peaceful and stable climate in nigeria, had she been present.
the escalation of tension between the european union and belarus has reached an unprecedented point, culminating in the withdrawals of ambassadors from each other. i believe that belarus' neighbourhood and its importance in the eastern partnership are arguments for finding a solution to this situation and i believe that we must persuade the minsk regime to respect the fundamental rights of citizens and allow democracy to be established in the country. this should include concrete progress such as an end to the persecution of the opposition, the release of political prisoners, the holding of free elections and the opening of belarus to european values. last but not least, we must bear in mind that, isolated internationally, the citizens of belarus suffer once again, struggling to cope with economic hardship, poverty, record inflation and huge trade deficit.
the deterioration of relations with belarus puts the union in the paradoxical and undesirable situation of having diplomatic tensions with a neighbouring state, a member of the eastern partnership. however, this will only change when the lukashenka regime stops its policy of repressing the opposition and civil society. the authorities' attitude is only isolating the country internationally. for example, in the latest reporters without borders report, belarus is listed as an internet enemy state for restrictions on online expression, and the imf recently announced its refusal to negotiate a loan with the country. however, the economic consequences are felt first and foremost by the population. i would have liked to ask the high representative how we can limit the effects on citizens while maintaining a firm line towards the authorities.
although this country committed itself to respect human rights at the eastern partnership summit in prague, it is becoming increasingly unreachable. i think it's the closest country to the european union and the furthest from european values. i would like to point out that sanctions must also be taken within the framework of the eastern partnership. we need to talk to the members of this partnership, especially the neighboring countries, to put pressure on the regime in minsk to change its attitude, to the extent that an individual like lukashenko is able to do so. i, however, have serious doubts about lukashenko's willingness to change his behavior. why can't we work with russia on this? because russia would have an opportunity to prove its commitment to values that are human, perennial and not only specific to the european union, russia also adhering to international documents and i am referring in particular to un documents.
in recent years, several romanian sailors have been kidnapped by somali pirates. last october, three of them were fortunately released after eight months in captivity. the eu must address piracy both from the perspective of its causes and its impact on security in the region. europe must change its strategy for the political and economic reconstruction of somalia, through cooperation with the african union. efforts must also be accompanied by an efficient distribution of humanitarian aid. in parallel, efforts to combat attacks at sea must be centralised. the eu, china and the us are now conducting parallel missions in the coastal area. the military protection of the international transit corridor in the gulf of aden must also be a priority in such a structure.
i thank you for your proposals, and i thank my fellow rapporteurs as well. of course, the european union must continue to lead the fight against climate change, and europe needs investment and job creation now more than ever. citizens need jobs and therefore investments in environmental protection can be seen as a driver of development, and the roadmap you have proposed and which we support is an answer to this. however, it must be borne in mind that member states' efforts to transition to a low-carbon economy are not similar, as the starting points are different and, by implication, the implementation efforts are different. i welcome the budgetary planning of european funds to ensure that projects that lead to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions are financed, but at the same time allow the infrastructure gap between member states to be reduced. the commission also needs to review the allowance trading scheme, as the evolution of the carbon market is uncertain and influenced by a multitude of factors, and a balanced balance between set aside and the number of allowances for the post-2012 ets needs to be considered.
without a doubt, both member states and regions must contribute to the achievement of the low-carbon targets by 2050. however, we must be aware of the difficulty of achieving these objectives. the report brought to our attention, in the transport section, the need for a cultural shift towards new and more sustainable modes of transport. encouraging new forms of investment to facilitate the modal shift to greener modes of transport and reduce transport demand, as proposed in the report, will address specific regional situations. the lack of adequate infrastructure, especially in poor regions where it use is low, will generate a number of accessibility problems. cultural change needs to be supported by measures that do not affect the daily lives of citizens and, in particular, their jobs. i believe that to meet this challenge, there is a need for a full alignment of sectoral policies at european union level and involvement of all institutional levels.
the european parliament's motion for a resolution sends a clear message to the world water forum: water is a resource that is shared and should not be treated as a commodity to be used for profit by a minority. access to safe drinking water and water for sanitation is a human right. this is the main political message i want the european union to send to marseille. the motion for a resolution also deals with other essential issues, and one of the most important, in my view, is the use of water in agriculture. seventy percent of the water we use from nature is used in agricultural activities, and in some countries, that percentage rises to 80 percent or even 90 percent. ensuring access to water can only be achieved through the wider use of technology and methods that produce more food using less water, such as efficient irrigation systems. to achieve this, it is necessary to stimulate the use of these techniques. we must support the farmers in the european union who use them and we must try to remove the barriers to farmers in third countries. let's not forget that while 70 percent of the water we take from nature goes to agriculture, at the same time, we waste 30 percent of our food. we're pouring, in other words, a lot of water at every point in the food chain, from extraction to consumption. ensuring access to water is also closely linked to other global issues, such as food security. as with the related topics of biodiversity and climate change, we need an international forum to address this global issue. i hope that the european union's negotiators will convey these messages in marseille as well as at the rio conference.
the world's population has already passed the seven billion mark, and food needs are set to increase by 70 percent by 2050. this increase in food demand would mean a 19% increase in water used in the agricultural sector, which already accounts for 70% of global water consumption. the motion for a resolution under debate rightly points out that new technological advances would make it possible to increase water efficiency and encourage the use of new technologies, equipment and machinery in agriculture related to water use. i would like to draw attention in this connection to the benefits that would be gained from the wider use of gm plants which are also more cost-effective and can help farmers to take care of the environment, including by saving water.
in writing. nearly half of the developing world's population lacks sanitation, over 800 million people still use unsafe sources of drinking water, and inadequate access to sanitation and poor hygiene practices are the cause of more than 2.5 million child deaths per year. deforestation, urbanisation, population growth and climate change are adding new, greater pressure on the availability and quality of safe and healthy water resources and generating higher risks of water-related extreme events, with poor populations being the most vulnerable and least able to adapt to these trends. i believe that public health and environmental protection are priorities for any water management policy and that the protection of drinking water resources is fundamental to human health. i support the development of integrated global river basin management plans and stress the need to achieve a thematic concentration of available funding for water-related actions and to mainstream water issues in all policy areas, including all eu financial and legal instruments, as addressing water-related challenges is an integral part of a functioning 'green economy'.

schmallenberg issue very closely from the start, and we continue to coordinate the eu response. i would like to say to ms reimers, who asked how we get a standard procedure for new diseases in place, that we think that we already have good mechanisms to ensure an appropriate response to emerging diseases. these mechanisms allowed us to detect the virus and prepare coordinated actions. recent experience, like the response to the h5n1 and the pandemic h1n1 influenza virus, demonstrates that the eu level of preparedness is satisfactory and the application of the one health concept leads to successful reaction. the current event is thus an opportunity to fine-tune those existing mechanisms. under the new animal health strategy, the commission is, however, taking further actions to ensure that the eu level of preparedness further improves. in this case also a guidance document addressing the main priority actions to be undertaken in the eu has already been prepared by the commission and endorsed by member states’ experts and stakeholders. as regards prevention of further spread of the virus, while this virus has already circulated in the animal population of eight member states now, it is unlikely that there is any virus circulation during the winter season. in view of this, the most appropriate control measure to be applied, for now, is surveillance, which is already in place. i should make clear that the movement and export of diseased animals is not permitted in the eu. any veterinary measure we might take would need to be proportionate and sustainable. it would need to take into account that the available information suggests that the impact of this virus on animal health and production is limited, and that there is no evidence that it can cause illness in humans. however, the commission has asked the european food safety authority (efsa) to collect epidemiological data from member states to further assess the impact of the schmallenberg virus (sbv) infection on animal health, animal production and animal welfare. the commission and the efsa are liaising with member states to facilitate and standardise data gathering and transmission of data. there is a knowledge gap as regards this virus due to its novelty. to address this gap, the commission is co-ordinating – and plans to financially support – scientific studies to gather further information aimed at developing a sound veterinary policy for this infection, which is essential for possible future control measures to be adopted either at member state level or eu level. as with any other viral disease, there is no specific treatment to cure animals infected with the schmallenberg virus. at this stage, we cannot predict when an effective vaccine might become available. with respect to any possible public health risk related to this virus, the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) stated in december of last year that it is unlikely that this new virus could cause disease in humans. current data supports this assessment. however, it cannot be excluded at this stage. if new evidence arises on the public health impact of sbv, the commission would, of course, ask the ecdc to provide an update of its risk assessment to take such developments into consideration. the coordination of any public health response would be ensured through the eu early warning and response system. regrettably, despite this rigorous approach, more than ten third countries have applied, or are preparing to apply, trade restrictive measures related to the schmallenberg virus. the commission agrees very much with what mr nicholson was saying when he urged a proportionate response. we consider restrictive measures against eu exports of ruminants and their products to be disproportionate and unjustified on the basis of the currently available scientific evidence. thus the commission is working in close contact with third countries to prevent and reduce their trade restrictions. to conclude, a measured response at eu level is necessary to avoid provoking unjustified market disturbances within the internal market and in trade with our international partners. it is imperative that we continue to keep matters in proper perspective.
in my view, the whole debate has two aspects. first, how serious this crisis is. the outbreak started five months ago, the virus is already present in over 1200 farms, there is no known treatment, the information from the commission has been mixed so far, and the approach of the warm season raises new problems. secondly, what are the consequences for european producers, apart from the decline in livestock numbers, especially in view of the export restrictions imposed by our partners? in response to a question in january, the commission indicated that the adoption of trade restrictions for union exports is not justified and is not in line with the international standards of the world organisation for animal health. however, the russian federation announced that it would ban imports of live animals from all member states as from 20 march. the russian authorities have cited the failure of the union veterinary agencies to provide the russian side with information on the outbreak and the measures taken to combat it. the commission should specify whether it considers the russian side's complaints against the european veterinary agencies to be well founded and, in view of the previous statement on the incompatibility of such a measure with international standards, what steps it intends to take in the dialogue with the russian federation.
this new phytosanitary alert is another reason for the eu to develop its animal health standards. unfortunately, the vaccine to combat the virus is still in the works and it is estimated that the epidemic will have its greatest impact in april. the union should therefore make every effort to ensure that farmers in the member states are informed in real time. continuous surveillance of areas not yet affected by the virus is needed to determine the routes of contamination. furthermore, correct diagnosis and reporting of cases to national authorities is essential to isolate outbreaks. commissioner, the virus has already been included in the rapid alert system for food and feed. how do you see the dissemination of the necessary information directly to farmers in the affected areas?

in writing. − the eu published in march the roadmap for moving to a competitive low-carbon economy, applicable to all economic sectors. detailed plans for each sector are currently being developed, the most recent being the energy outlook 2050. given that the evolution of demand and supply is difficult to estimate, the plan presents several scenarios, analysing the possible effects, challenges and opportunities generated by the modernisation of the energy system. the commission notes that the aid is granted to the beneficiaries of the aid, and that the aid is not granted to the beneficiaries of the aid. the price of electricity is expected to increase by 2030. that is why we need to invest in 'smart' electricity grids and improved technologies for energy generation, transmission and storage. combined with the completion of the common energy market, these measures should ensure a decrease in prices in the long term. the sustainability of the investments, the jobs generated and the reduction of the import dependency will offset the costs.

in writing. − achieving the union's carbon reduction targets of 80%-95% by 2050 can only be achieved through effectively coordinated community action with practical application at local level. the conclusions of the durban climate change meeting and the position of third countries on the air carbon tax show little interest in rapid action and political commitment to reduce carbon emissions. the development of low-carbon economies at local and regional level and investment in these areas contribute significantly to the creation of new jobs and to the competitiveness of regions. waste management, energy efficiency of buildings and the creation of standardised infrastructure for electric and low-emission vehicles are priorities that can deliver immediate results at local level. the future of sustainable investment will look at reducing dependence on external energy suppliers outside the eu. the development of an integrated system of cross-border energy markets contributes to the energy balance between member states and strengthens domestic generation capacity.
in writing. − approximately 90 parties to the united nations framework convention on climate change, including emerging economies, which together are responsible for more than 80% (eu-11%) of global emissions, have made unilateral declarations on quantified economy-wide emission reduction targets, even though they are not legally binding. if these objectives become binding targets, it is essential to take account of national circumstances and the pressures on the budget that may arise. i call on the european commission to carry out a thorough assessment at member state level of the impact of the new emission reduction targets on the european economy, competitiveness and labour market, as well as an assessment of the equivalence of measures taken by other developed countries in the context of international negotiations.
in writing. − we voted on the roadmap for moving to a competitive low-carbon economy by 2050. i voted in favour of setting interim greenhouse gas emission reduction targets for 2030 and 2040, but i voted against requiring them to follow a linear trajectory, as these reductions involve medium- and long-term investment and the effect is not linear. i voted for the introduction of a long-term target to reduce the energy consumption of the eu's building stock by 2050 and for continued support for investment in other forms of low-carbon energy production. i voted against paragraph 24 (b) which calls for changing the annual linear reduction rate of 1.74%, set by the ets directive, to meet the requirements of the co2 reduction target by 2050. i voted for amendment no 10 which calls for assurances that none of the proposed measures will reduce the level of allowances for sectors that may be exposed to carbon leakage, as set out in decision 2011/278/eu. i voted against amendment no 24, which eliminates the recognition of the contribution of nuclear energy to the current target of a 20% reduction in co2 emissions by 2020.

in writing. − on 28 july 2010, the united nations general assembly adopted the resolution on the fundamental right of every human being to safe drinking water. international access to drinking water is limited. according to data presented by the united nations environment programme, 884 million people lack access to clean water, and some 2.3 billion people lack even basic sanitation. the decline in freshwater resources and the expansion of deserts - a problem that in the past was more likely to affect africa and asia - are knocking on europe's door. in southern spain, the desert is expanding by one kilometre a year, romanian oltenia is exposed to a slower but similar process, and in other regions of the world drinking water resources have become a cause of interstate conflict. last but not least, yemen's official announcement that by 2017 it will become the first country in the world without any natural water source is well known. in view of the above, i believe that sustainable water use is not only an environmental but also an economic necessity and that greater transparency in water charging systems would be necessary.

the countries of the western balkans have all chosen the path of european integration. the region's inhabitants hope that this will improve their living conditions, boost the economy and resolve tensions between ethnic groups. the people of serbia hope the same, serbs and hungarians, roma and romanians, albanians and croats all. however, if the union does not pay sufficient attention to tackling minority issues, future eu citizens will be disappointed in us. the best way to deal with inter-ethnic tensions is to provide political autonomy. in the province of vojvodina in serbia, this is the way of the future. for a long time, this was the solution for kosovo, but time has passed for an intra-state settlement. i ask the commission and the member states not to allow the accession countries of the region to lose their european perspective. to do so, we must be attentive to their problems, even if that means taking part in the settlement of interethnic relations.
the european commission's october assessment of the republic of serbia's progress on the european path must be based on the fulfilment of the copenhagen criteria, of which the protection of the rights of persons belonging to national minorities is an important part. as regards the situation of romanian minorities throughout serbia, i do not think we are dealing with a bilateral situation, but one that depends on the fulfilment of political criteria. on the basis of the principle of self-identification, serbia must implement minority legislation in a coherent manner, i.e. throughout its territory, and consistently, i.e. for all minorities. ensuring access to education, religious service, media and public administration in the romanian language for all who identify as romanian is a necessity. the implementation of the recommendations agreed by romania and the republic of serbia in the protocol of 1 march this year on national minorities should be an evaluation criterion in the european commission's report in october.
in writing. i support the enlargement of the european union, through the accession of the western balkan countries and, by implication, serbia, to the extent that they apply the copenhagen criteria in practice. just as romania had to adhere to strict principles on minority rights, and is today a model in this regard, serbia will have to align itself with the european model in this area if it wants to join the eu. i am referring to the situation of national minorities in general and of the romanian minority in particular, regardless of the various names under which we find the latter or the number of citizens more or less formally recognized. ethnic romanians demand, above all, education, religious service and the press in their mother tongue, that is, normal rights in a democratic state. unfortunately, these requests are consistently denied and the problems have been going on for years, with the serbian authorities still not aligning themselves with eu practice in the treatment of national minorities. in these circumstances, until the issue is satisfactorily resolved, i consider it useful for the european commission to monitor the implementation of european standards on minority rights in serbia.

rapporteur. − mr president, this report, a non-legislative one, contains questions of crucial importance on how the future of corporations will look. having said that, such measures should not be applicable to non-public corporations. corporate governance rules are naturally necessary to regulate the relationship between shareholders, directors and managers. if the number of shareholders is not large, irrespective of their size or business, there is no need for corporate governance. moreover, such rules are not appropriate for smes where flexibility is of the essence. so, the key points of this report, as well as of the future corporate governance legislation, should strengthen the ties between a company and both its non-executive directors and its shareholders. in this respect a clear demarcation line should be drawn between the attributions of the chairman of the board and the chief executive officer. furthermore, non-executive directors should have a professional background, an expertise, for instance former executives from other companies in the same or another industry or in the same or another market. such qualifications are necessary because it is the board that selects the officers and furthermore watches over their activity in order to report to shareholders and supervisors. to perform this properly they should be trained and skilled. moreover, the number of seats that one director can hold should be limited, except in the situation where the companies on whose board the director sits are members of the same group or where the director is performing this role as a representative of an institutional investor where he holds his main job. the composition of the board should also be more diverse and the role of non-residents – for multinational companies – and of women should be increased. shareholders should be more involved, to stimulate their appetite to participate in decision-making within the company, even if their investment is just for a short period of time. electronic voting could be a solution and the commission should evaluate this possibility based on a cost-benefit ratio. shareholders should receive the same amount of information from the company, irrespective of their stake. cooperation between shareholders should also be allowed. in some member states this is forbidden when it comes to voting. a conflict of interests between shareholders and the company, for instance transactions with related parties, should lead to the shareholders concerned, irrespective of the size of their stake, refraining from voting. minority shareholders should be protected against the abusive decisions of the dominant one, but without giving the opportunity to allow harassing behaviour by the former. risk behaviour should be approved by the board and publicly disclosed, and the bonuses of officers should be linked more to long-term results in order to discourage risky behaviour that endangers the company in the long run. furthermore, the remuneration policy of both directors and officers should be approved by the general meeting of shareholders. the report aims also to strengthen the role of the audit, nomination and remuneration committees. the key issue of this report will be mandatory norms versus compliance with plain principle and i am glad that the ppe point of view in favour of the latter prevailed after the vote in the committee on legal affairs. last, but not least, all such measures to be introduced should be considered based on the cost of each measure, for instance periodic mandatory appraisal. the commission should then come up with a set of tools contained in a european code of conduct which will leave the main corporate governance instruments to be applied by public corporations, customised in certain matters in accordance with the policy of each member state. the final goal of the future legislative report that is yet to come, later this year, is to preserve the strength of our corporations and make them important global actors, protecting their competitiveness and, as a consequence, securing jobs and profits.
first of all, i want to congratulate sebastian bodu on this report. the construction of a single market at european union level was not and is not possible without the existence of strong trading companies and their appropriate development in the light of the economic environment, which is very dynamic at european and international level. to keep pace with these dynamic developments, europe needs to adapt its legislative framework to the needs of companies, to provide adequate protection at european level for shareholders, creditors and all partners who are influenced by the activities of companies. in a europe without internal borders, proper harmonisation of national laws and company structures in the member states is essential to ensure that european citizens can benefit from all the services and products offered by them, especially in terms of cross-border trade, but also from the point of view of corporate social responsibility and their role in innovation and economic growth.
corporate governance is defined as the system by which enterprises are run and controlled and as a set of relationships between the management of an enterprise, its board of directors, its shareholders and other stakeholders. the corporate governance framework for listed companies in the european union is a combination of legislation and non-binding legal instruments, including corporate governance recommendations and codes. directive 2006/46/ec promotes the application of corporate governance codes and requires listed companies to refer to a code in their corporate statement and to report on its application. the commission finds that the proportion of women on the boards of listed companies in the european union is currently on average 12%. we call on the commission to submit a legislative proposal by the end of 2012 if companies do not meet the objective of 30% of women on boards by 2015 and 40% by 2020 through voluntary measures.

in writing. the programme for the provision of food to the most deprived persons was established by regulation 3730/1987. over more than two decades, the programme has contributed not only to poverty reduction and the implementation of eu social policy, but also to the achievement of common agricultural policy (cap) objectives such as stabilising markets and ensuring reasonable prices for products delivered to consumers. unfortunately, some member states have called for the cap funding for this programme to be phased out. however, the commission has proposed and the european parliament and the council of the eu have approved the continuation of the programme in 2012-13 through the cap, at a value of eur 500 million/year. the programme has contributed to the distribution of some 440 000 tonnes of food to 18 million disadvantaged people in 19 member states each year. we call for the programme to continue beyond 2013 and we call on the commission to integrate it correctly into the future multiannual financial framework so that it continues to contribute to both the eu's social and cap objectives. i consider that the funding of the programme from the european social fund alone is not appropriate as it would mean a decrease in the funds allocated to other social measures to combat poverty and increase social inclusion.

rapporteur. − mr president, i would like to start by saluting the efforts of the european commission to reinforce eu citizenship by giving real substance to citizens’ rights. this was done by introducing the report on citizenship in october 2010. this is indeed what we need in the eu: to take steps forward by engaging member states, institutions and citizens to fully respect eu law and lift obstacles to the free movement of our citizens. so far the eu has been less successful and has not given enough priority to ensuring the legal framework is applied in practice. as a result, the free movement of persons has developed less than the other three freedoms. over the last years an increasing number of petitions have been registered with respect to problems encountered by eu citizens who exercise their right to free movement, accounting for approximately 25% of the total number of petitions received. also some progress has been achieved following the adoption of the parliament report on application of the free movement directive in 2008, of which i was the rapporteur, and also the publication of the commission’s guidelines for implementation of the free movement directive. numerous petitions bear witness to the fact that there are still many problems related to the implementation of the directive: unjustified administrative burdens, particularly for third-country-national family members, including entry requirements and lengthy procedural delays; a lack of recognition of free movement rights for certain registered partners, including those in a same-sex relationship; public policy exceptions to serve economic or security aims which have ignored the principle of proportionality, especially in abuses of expulsion orders; discrimination towards certain nationals and ethnic communities. these are just a few examples of such breaches of european citizens’ fundamental rights. there is a large gap between the expectation of citizens, who increasingly take free movement for granted and expect the spirit of the treaty and the legislation to be respected, and the practice of national authorities who insist more on the conditions and exceptions. to achieve real free movement as well as eu citizenship, member states need to be pushed to do it, to change their laws and administrative practices. the only institution that can do it is the one that is charged with the task of being the guardian of the treaties, the european commission. an important number of petitions highlighted the problems encountered by citizens on the mutual recognition and free circulation of civil status documents and their effects. procedures for the recognition of documents can be extremely time-consuming and involve many costs, especially with regard to translation and authentication. there are even member states which refuse to issue certificates of civil status to persons who intend to engage in a partnership or marriage in another member state. since free movement rights are guaranteed by a mix of european laws and national implementing measures, citizens often find themselves caught up in red tape, being asked to produce an excessive number of documents in original form or authenticated copies and translations. the problem with the recognition of professional qualifications brings delays in job applications that can take months, even years, preventing even the attempt to access the labour market. this hampers labour mobility, which has a positive impact on economic growth. so on and so forth. we have been discussing in the committee on petitions all these obstacles which citizens encounter in exercising their rights as european citizens. let me conclude by saying that this citizenship report is based on the petitions received from the citizens who address us with their concerns and worries, expecting the european parliament to protect their rights guaranteed by the treaty. the signal we are going to give today by voting on this report is an important one. the rights achieved by our citizens should be respected by all, no matter the political family we belong to or the country we come from.
the report shows that although the right to free movement and residence is the most widely recognised among citizens, it is the right to which the most complaints are made, based on the number of petitions submitted. this means that the eu is most associated by eu citizens with the right to free movement, and the disappearance of physical and virtual borders between member states is arguably the most popular achievement of integration. at the same time, citizens are the most sensitive to the violations of rights related to this. the petitions submitted do indeed point to a number of irregularities, but we must not forget that citizens of two member states still cannot feel equal to other eu citizens. and they get no sound answer to their question as to why. the inexplicable delay in the accession of bulgaria and romania to schengen is a violation of the rights of citizens of both member states related to citizenship of the union. would it take 27 million petitions to change that?
i believe that designating 2013 as the 'european year of citizens' will increase awareness of citizens' electoral rights in the 2014 european parliament elections, remove obstacles to citizens' rights. there is currently a severe lack of trust in the political class and citizens want better representation and more effective involvement in european decision-making. in 2013, we can regain citizens' trust through a series of measures such as uniform access to treatment in all eu member states, removing the obstacles faced by people with disabilities when exercising their right to free movement, achieving genuine economic and territorial cohesion for all european citizens, better promoting the european citizens' initiative, which will come into force on 1 april 2012, and, last but not least, accepting romania and bulgaria into the schengen area.
in accordance with article 45 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the guarantee of freedom of movement for workers entails the elimination of all forms of discrimination based on nationality between workers of the member states as regards employment, remuneration and other conditions of work and employment. we demand the removal of the existing barriers to the free movement of romanian and bulgarian workers. those barriers affect migrant workers and nationals of the member state of destination equally, since they favour social dumping. as 2013 is the 'european year of citizenship', i welcome the launch of the ocs online collection application, which was developed by the commission through the isa programme and will allow signatories of a petition and a citizens' initiative to use the same standard online forms in a secure manner from 1 april 2012. i congratulate the rapporteur, mrs adina vallelean, on her report.

rapporteur. − mr president, the 2010 eurobarometer survey shows that only 42% of europeans know their rights, while the special eurobarometer from 2011 reveals that 85% of europeans lack sufficient information about the charter of fundamental rights. a citizens’ europe for and by the people will only be successful when we ensure that people can exercise their rights in full knowledge of what those rights are and how to benefit from them. in this context, i welcome the commission’s proposal to declare 2013 as the european year of citizens, aiming to enhance awareness of their rights and the advantages attached to european citizenship. however, looking at the budget allocated for the preparation and implementation of this european year – eur 1 million, the smallest ever budget envisaged for such a year – i can only imagine that it will allow for top-down communication measures and not for the tangible actions boosted so often by the commission. i also want to draw attention once again to the request made by the committee on culture and education for a comprehensive communication policy on citizens’ rights. let me conclude by saying that, for this report today, i have tabled, thanks to the support of 120 colleagues from different political families, an amendment with a paragraph which was unfortunately voted down in the committee on petitions. the paragraph called on the member states to ensure freedom of movement for all eu citizens and their families without discrimination on grounds of their sexual orientation or nationality. i expect all the democratic and pro-european groups in this house to support the report in the vote today in plenary and not act as if on a battlefield, as they normally do in the petitions committee, because the report is based on what citizens are requesting and their problems; in writing. in order for european citizenship not to remain a mere concept and to bring concrete opportunities for citizens, i believe that there are some legislative, implementation and, above all, information gaps that need to be closed. european citizenship will be a reality when settling in another member state does not bring additional difficulties to the situation in the country of origin. at the legislative level, improving the system for the recognition of professional qualifications, facilitating the portability of pensions and other social rights, broader access to banking services or facilitating the re-registration of motor vehicles when they are moved from one state to another are just a few examples of the reforms needed. european citizens are not just consumers. these are people who get married, divorced, inherited, and so on. when the partners are of different nationalities or have lived in several member states, these circumstances need not complicate matters. we recently passed the succession regulations. we need such initiatives, which set clear rules and simplify people's lives in cross-border situations. last but not least, information plays a crucial role. the 'your europe' portal has been transformed, it provides ample information on different initiatives and i believe it needs to be further promoted and developed.
