in writing. − i believe that in recent years significant price increases and their increased volatility have had an impact on certain raw materials, including natural rubber. therefore, the analysis of this phenomenon showed that the origin of these developments is the increasing demand, in particular from china. i believe that the restrictions affecting the short-term supply, the low number of rubber trees planted, the abundant rainfall in the main producing countries have put pressure on the global rubber supply.
in writing. - welcomes the commission's decision to amend the rules on air passenger transport, which is designed to strengthen one of the most important services that gives substance to the freedom of movement of citizens of the member states in the european area; the amendments covered by this legislative proposal outline a clear and coherent framework for protecting the interests and rights of passengers, without however neglecting their responsibilities as beneficiaries of transport services. it is important that european passengers have access to timely services and to ways of challenging and redressing any damage caused by their interaction with airlines.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that adequate protection of the rights of air passengers must be ensured. i would stress the importance of making all information on travel conditions available to passengers from the moment they purchase their ticket, in the language in which the booking is made and in a format that is as easy to understand as possible. i also intend to ensure transparency as regards the final price of the ticket and any additional fees and charges that may apply. it is of the utmost importance that passengers can receive information and assistance quickly in the event of unforeseen flight events, such as cancellations or very long delays. in this context, i support the proposals for the presence of contact persons or services at airports and the establishment by airlines of accessible and efficient call centres. i would point out that simplified procedures are needed for submitting possible complaints and claims for compensation or reimbursement. i welcome the idea of establishing a european award for the most accessible airline to consumers. i believe that this will stimulate competition and promote best practice.
in writing. − knowing your rights is essential for all people travelling by air. for this reason, i believe that information on passenger rights should be provided in a simple, appropriate and easy-to-understand form at all essential stages of the journey, starting from the moment when the passenger is thinking about buying a ticket. in the event of disruption to the journey, passengers should be informed in good time of the reasons for the delay or cancellation, the estimated duration of the delay and alternative travel options, including by other means of transport, where appropriate. i also think that the three options that the passenger can choose from, namely reimbursement, redirection or a new booking, should be emphasised as an elementary right. last but not least, passengers whose baggage is lost or arrives late should enjoy equivalent rights to those of passengers who have themselves been delayed.
in writing. − i believe that the european commission should look at measures to ensure the protection of passengers arriving and departing, ensuring that passengers are adequately compensated in the event of loss or excessive delay of luggage.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the functioning and application of established rights of people travelling by air, because it represents a very positive step forward in terms of protecting passengers’ rights, in particular paying due attention to people with reduced mobility. this document contains significant improvements on the previous eu regulation no 261/2004 in terms of consumer-rights’ safeguards, security, transparency and privacy of the passengers, and pays attention to flight safety conditions and to complaint handling – introducing standards that companies will therefore have to comply with. in addition, further cooperation, collaboration, exchanges of practice, and a more uniform application of the eu rules by the member states’ enforcement bodies will be called for. this will surely provide stronger guarantees not only in terms of compliance with rules but also in terms of delivering higher levels of protection for passengers – whose rights are often not respected and who have lacked information.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on air passenger rights because i believe it is important not only to guarantee passenger rights through legislation, but also to ensure that they are functional and, above all, that they are properly applied. the role of enforcement bodies has been strengthened and the provision to bring them together in a european network will help to improve their cooperation and thus the results achieved. we voted for more transparency and accountability, for better complaint handling and for the introduction of a single european complaint form. we've asked operators and airlines for regular reports to increase efficiency of enforcement agencies and competition. clarifying and strengthening existing rights and explaining them to consumers was the reason for parliament's request to continue the passenger information campaign launched by the commission in 2010. i also voted for the clear interpretation and uniform application of the regulations on passenger rights in the european union.
in writing. - i welcome the adoption of this resolution and in particular some of the requirements expressed, such as the harmonisation of rules on hand luggage or the prohibition on the display of unclear prices or additional charges at the time of booking. it is also important to establish rules against unilateral rescheduling of flights and to discourage price discrimination against passengers on the basis of country of residence. i believe that such measures are in the interests of the citizens who travel, who are increasing in number every year.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the functioning and enforcement of the rights of persons travelling by air as it is essential that passengers are provided with complete, easily understandable, accurate and timely information by both air carriers and tour operators. we ask air carriers to ensure that there are contact persons or a service at each airport from which they operate who can take immediate decisions, in particular on assistance, reimbursement, redirection, lost or delayed baggage, rebooking and complaints. we call on the commission to ensure the effective application and enforcement of existing legislation on price transparency, to ensure that the price displayed correctly reflects the final price. we call for the protection of passengers against abusive contractual clauses such as contractual issues related to damaged/ delayed/ mishandled baggage, ticket transferability, force majeure circumstances, unilateral rescheduling of flights, prohibition of use of return ticket if the departure ticket has not been used, excessive restrictions on hand baggage. we support the elimination of the abusive practice of requiring persons with reduced mobility (prm) to sign a document exonerating the airline from liability in the event of damage to prm mobility equipment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this draft legislative resolution because i firmly believe there is an urgent need for a europe-wide system based on enhanced solidarity, which also has to be extended to third- country nationals as well as citizens of europe. a crucial point, in my opinion, must be highlighted: the european union should help those member states willing to undertake reform of refugees’ resettlement by providing them with sufficient funds. eu policy in this regard should also follow a more efficient and rationalised pathway, in particular by pursuing a set of key priorities. i strongly believe that the first of these priorities should be to provide help and assistance to the most vulnerable people, who face traumatic and precarious living and social conditions. in conclusion, i positively welcome this document which constitutes an important step towards greater solidarity in the management of migration flows.
in writing. - i voted in favour of parliament's legislative resolution amending decision no 573/2007/ec establishing the european refugee fund for the period 2008 to 2013. this regulation establishes the asylum and migration fund, developed with the assistance of the european refugee fund, the european fund for the integration of third-country nationals and the european return fund. the regulation extends this process to cover more comprehensively different aspects of the union's common asylum and immigration policy, including actions in third countries. the commission proposal provides for the allocation of eur 3,869 million to the asylum and migration fund for the period 2014-2020. more than 80% of this amount should be used for member states' national programmes, while eur 637 million should be managed by the commission to finance union actions, emergency assistance, the european migration network, technical assistance and the implementation of specific operational tasks by union agencies. i believe that a well-organised policy on legal immigration, in line with the stockholm programme and supported by the union's legal instruments, has a central role to play in ensuring the union's long-term competitiveness and its social model.
in writing. − this initiative is part of a wider series of actions at international level aimed at bringing more stability to the financial system in general and the otc derivatives market in particular. as regards non-financial (corporate) counterparties, they will in principle not be covered by this regulation unless their otc derivative positions reach a threshold considered to be systemically important. as it is assumed that, in general, their derivative transactions are directly related to trading activities rather than speculative ones, those positions will not be subject to this regulation. i consider that the national competent authorities should reserve the responsibility for authorisation (including withdrawal of authorisations granted) and supervision, as they are best placed to analyse the day-to-day operation of ccps, to carry out regular reviews and to take appropriate action whenever necessary. given the systemic importance of ccps and the cross-border nature of their activities, it is important that the european securities and markets authority plays a central role in the process of their authorisation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on otc derivatives, central counterparties (ccps) and central transaction logs. it lays down the conditions for the authorisation of ccps, the screening criteria to ensure the appropriate characteristics for central clearing and the registration of derivatives in central trade repositories where the aggregated information can be used, including for systemic risk analysis. ccps are regulated by the prudential regulators of banks in most member states and at european level, the eba has the most expertise, so close cooperation between esma and the eba is essential. the proposed amendments to the regulation clarify certain definitions, facilitate certain procedures, help to avoid 'clearing shocks' and other disproportionate burdens on businesses, propose to remove the information threshold, consider that the clearing threshold provides sufficient assurance, introduce consistent and transparent criteria for regulatory decisions, clarify the procedures for determining the eligibility for clearing of otc derivatives and counterparties. while promoting the resilience and transparency of derivatives markets, the regulation also aims to maintain the efficiency of those markets in covering both financial and non-financial end-users. maintaining the international character of this market promotes both objectives when supported by cooperation between supervisors and convergent international standards.
in writing. − this directive lays down minimum requirements, giving member states the possibility to maintain or adopt more favourable provisions for the protection of workers, in particular to set lower levels for the guide values and limit values for exposure to electromagnetic fields. a system of protection against electromagnetic fields must be limited to the definition of the objectives to be achieved, the principles to be observed and the fundamental values to be applied. the protection of workers exposed to electromagnetic fields requires an effective and efficient risk assessment. this obligation must be proportionate to the situation encountered at the workplace. it is therefore important to define a protection system that establishes a gradual scale of risks that is easy to understand. employers should adapt to technical progress and scientific knowledge of the risks associated with exposure to electromagnetic fields in order to improve the safety and health protection of workers. in view of scientific progress and the increasing use in various fields of equipment generating electromagnetic fields with a well-defined purpose and useful to society, i call on the member states to allocate the necessary funds to the field of research for the detection as fine as possible of the negative effects produced by exposure of the human body to electromagnetic fields.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of directive 2004/40/ec on the minimum safety and health requirements regarding the exposure of workers to the risks arising from physical agents (electromagnetic fields). in 2011, the commission adopted a proposal for a directive to replace directive 2004/40/ec. the aim of the new directive is to ensure a high level of protection of the health and safety of workers, while allowing the continuation and development of medical and industrial activities using electromagnetic fields. proposal com ((2011) 348 aims to update and improve a significant number of provisions of directive 2004/40/ec, including by introducing elements that make it easier for employers, in particular small enterprises, to implement the measures. the amendment proposed by the commission by com ((2012) 15) only affects the obligation of member states to transpose directive 2004/40/ec by 30 april 2012, the deadline being extended until 31 october 2013. the amendment does not affect the substance of the directive in question and therefore does not impose additional obligations on undertakings. the extension of the transposition deadline to 31 october 2013 will give parliament and the council sufficient time to debate and reach a compromise, on the basis of the commission proposal com ((2011) 348), for a new directive, which will update and improve the provisions of directive 2004/40/ec, while repealing and replacing the previous directive.
in writing. − in the eu, excise duties apply to three categories of products: alcohol and alcoholic beverages, processed tobacco and energy products. these excise duties play an important role in influencing public behaviour and contributing to the public budgets of the member states and the eu. the european union has progressively developed and put into practice a new and modern system for monitoring the movement of products under excise duty suspension in the internal market excise movement and control system (emcs). more importantly, the new system should allow the relevant authorities to track the movement of goods in 'real time' and to compare the information immediately, which will allow for a faster and more detailed analysis of the information. a large part of the proposal concerns the legal rules on how administrative cooperation should take place under the new system. i consider that the proposal is a balanced approach, which will allow member states to take advantage of the advantages inherent in the new system without increasing the administrative burden for them or for economic operators.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on administrative cooperation in the field of excise duties because the creation of a european tax union should include a comprehensive, rapid, efficient, accessible and, as far as possible, automatic exchange of information between member states, with a view to combating tax evasion more effectively. the provisions of regulation (ec) no 2073/2004 establish a legal framework for administrative cooperation in the field of excise duties. those provisions need to be revised to take account of the introduction of the computerised system for the movement and control of excise goods. other proposed changes to the regulation are to remove provisions that are no longer relevant, to structure the text in a more logical way, and to take account of new administrative cooperation procedures in the field of excise duties and other areas in order to provide a more efficient and less burdensome regulatory framework for both excise authorities and economic operators. i voted for the amendment which calls on the commission to set up a new vat and excise forum, modelled on the joint transfer pricing forum, in which companies can address issues relating to vat on companies and disputes between member states. the commission is to present to parliament and the council a report on excise fraud by 2013.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the estimate of parliament's revenue and expenditure for the financial year 2013. in paragraph 8, parliament defends the principle of multilingualism and stresses the uniqueness of the european parliament in terms of translation and interpretation needs. in paragraph 16 parliament insists that funding should be granted only to parties which strictly respect the founding principles of the eu and the charter of fundamental rights. paragraph 11 also underlines parliament's willingness to contribute to maintaining budgetary discipline by freezing all travel budget lines and suspending the indexation of all individual allowances of members until the end of the parliamentary term. i voted against paragraph 2 of the resolution which states that the places where parliament's work is carried out should be limited to a single seat for members and officials, as they cannot be limited without a corresponding amendment to the union treaties. i voted against amendment 2, which considers it unnecessary to conduct an information campaign on the 2014 elections, which the bureau includes in its estimate. i also voted against amendment no 8, which calls for the abolition of the european journalism prize, and against amendments nos 9 and 6, which call for the funding of the house of european history to be stopped and the project to be dissolved.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the request for mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) submitted by spain for the building sector in the valencia region. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the egf was extended to provide support to workers affected by the economic and financial crisis and to assist them in their reintegration into the labour market. the request concerns 1 138 redundancies in 513 construction companies in the region of valencia, spain, between july and november 2011. spain pointed out that unemployment in the region had increased in 2010 by 12,2% compared to 2009 and by 309% compared to 2007, the year before the crisis. in 2010, workers made redundant in the construction sector accounted for 28.18% of the total redundancies in the region, compared to only 6.3% in 2007. we call on the commission and the member states to ensure a swift and smooth procedure for the adoption of decisions to mobilise the egf, with the objective of helping workers made redundant as a result of globalisation and the financial and economic crisis. we call on the commission and the member states to monitor the integration into the labour market of the beneficiaries of this egf mobilisation request.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it appropriate, given that both parliament and the council have equal powers under the ordinary legislative and budgetary procedures. in view of the new institutional balance after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, there is no longer any reason to maintain the council's question time in its current form. the role of the european parliament has increased significantly, becoming a co-legislator within the european union. it also created new institutions, such as the european council and its permanent president, the high representative or the eurogroup. in view of the recent developments in interinstitutional relations, i believe that it is essential to revise the rules of procedure of the european parliament. however, i also support the rapporteur's view that the priority should be to change the time allocated to questions to the council. at the same time, i consider it useful to maintain the possibility of putting questions to the council, within a specified period of question time, on matters relating to the council's powers which are not related to the exercise of its legislative and budgetary functions.
in writing. − i believe that the conference of presidents, following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which made parliament a co-legislator within the european union and gave it powers equal to those of the council under the ordinary legislative procedure and the budgetary procedure, must highlight this new institutional balance. i agree that the conference of presidents considers that the possibility of allocating time for questions not only to the president of the commission but also to the vice-president/high representative and the president of the eurogroup should be maintained.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a parliament decision on amending the rules of procedure to take into account the changing relationships between parliament and the institutions representing the national governments, because it was fundamental to update the rules of procedure after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, since changes occurred thereafter to the attribution of responsibilities and competences in the eu institutional architecture as regards legislative, budgetary and political competences. besides, i strongly believe that the european union needs to strengthen the loyal cooperation between its institutions, in order to increase the effectiveness and the functionality of the eu policy and decision-making. with regard to this, i would like to draw attention to the example of the negative experience of the schengen evaluation reports that made it evident that existing limitations have to be overcome.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of the rules of procedure in the light of the evolution of the european parliament's relations with the institutions representing national governments since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament's role as co-legislator within the european union has been strengthened, with powers equal to those of the council under the ordinary legislative procedure and the budgetary procedure. given this new institutional balance, the conference of presidents considered that it was no longer justified to maintain the time allocated to questions to the council in its present form on the agenda for the plenary session. the elimination of the time allocated to questions to the council, in its present form, reflects the change in the institutional balance referred to by the conference of presidents. i believe that it would be useful to maintain the possibility of putting questions to the council, within a specific period of question time, on matters relating to those council competences which are not related to the exercise of its legislative and budgetary functions. the report also does not exclude the possibility of a further in-depth study of the evolution of relations with the institutions representing national governments and the possible changes to the regulation that would result from this.
in writing. − the current global economic and political context is one which is putting the issue of democratisation back on the agenda of international debates. the revolutions in the middle east or the globalisation of the mass media and international economic networks are processes which show how important it is for the european union to live up to its role as the world's leading provider of economic aid and benevolent civil power. the establishment of a european democracy fund is both a firm guarantee that the union remains committed to promoting democratic instruments and a useful complementary instrument for the development of the union's external policies, such as the eastern partnership or the neighbourhood policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the idea of a european fund to support the democratization processes in the union's neighbourhood. to achieve its objectives, however, it must provide real added value, complementing existing instruments in a coherent and effective way. to this end, it is appropriate to focus on strengthening the basis of society in the process of democratic construction. however, clear and transparent procedures are needed, including for the methodology for selecting beneficiaries. the simplification of the financing process and flexibility are also needed, especially as regards the possibilities for rapid rescheduling of funds. i would draw attention to the importance of the appropriate involvement of the european parliament in the operationalisation of the edf. i would stress that the edf results will need to be monitored and analysed carefully to ensure its maximum effectiveness. i would point out that the implementation of the edf must support in a balanced way the processes of democratisation in both the eastern partnership and the southern neighbourhood, while respecting the principle of 'more for more'.
in writing. - i voted in favour of parliament's recommendation to the council on the modalities for the creation of a european democracy fund (edf). the eu enshrines universal human rights and democracy as its founding values, strives to eliminate inequalities and promote equality between men and women. parliament called on the council to ensure that the edf would generate a strategic and political perspective on the eu's role in supporting democracy; to clarify the edf's mission and values in order to ensure clear criteria for the selection of beneficiaries, in particular on the methodology of selection processes; to ask the edf to guarantee the principle of national ownership of democratic processes; to ensure that the edf provides added value by complementing and not overlapping or limiting the activities of existing funding instruments and that, at the level of strategic planning, the edf cooperates with other eu instruments and structures active in the field of human rights and democracy. parliament asked the council to ensure that the edf pays particular attention to the participation of women in the process of democratic reform by supporting women's organisations and projects in areas such as combating violence, creating jobs and political participation, extending equal access to justice and education for women and girls, and preventing or stopping existing violations of women's rights.
in writing. - serbia's progress towards european integration is remarkable, considering the sacrifices of serbian citizens and the fact that the wounds of the past have not been healed. certainly, serbia is paying for the wrong decisions of the past, but it is commendable that it has taken up its responsibilities in the violent dismemberment of yugoslavia and is acting to right the wrongs done. i would like to focus on the progress serbia has made in the treatment of ethnic minorities. there is room for improvement, including with regard to the vlach minority, which has recently been the subject of a dispute between romania and serbia. i think belgrade needs to understand that one of its advantages comes from the existence of this ethnic diversity, which allows it a better relationship with its neighbors, if it uses it wisely. identity crises, inter-ethnic conflicts have done a lot of damage to the balkans in the past. serbia has a lot to do to meet european standards on the rule of law and civil rights and freedoms. the willingness of the serbian leaders to complete the necessary reforms is encouraging. the eu and its member states expect facts, fulfilment of commitments and real progress in the areas under monitoring.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution in order to acknowledge serbia’s progress towards european integration and highlight the remaining goals to be achieved for the benefit of its people. however, further efforts are needed in judiciary reform. the publication of all judgments and the unification of jurisprudence should be priorities in order to ensure public trust and a predictable and efficient judicial system. on the fight against corruption, serbian authorities must focus on high-level corruption cases. this is the test of the judiciary and of the political class. serbia needs to show a strong track-record of final convictions in high-level political cases. the efficiency of the eu funds spent on justice reform and combating corruption must also be assessed. the consistency of the rule of law throughout a nation is vital to its ability to progress politically and democratically.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on serbia's european integration as serbia can become an important actor in ensuring security and stability in the western balkans region and constructive strategies on regional cooperation and good neighbourly relations are key elements of the stabilisation and association process. we welcome the significant progress made by serbia in aligning with the acquis in the field of environmental protection and call for further sustained efforts in this area, with a particular focus on enforcement. we urge the authorities to step up their efforts, especially in water quality and waste disposal, and encourage serbia to adopt climate change targets that are in line with those of the eu. we call for further efforts to create a viable public transport network in serbia, in particular to improve the railway system and inland waterway transport (corridor vii) as well as road infrastructure, including the rapid completion of european corridor x. we welcome the active role serbia is already playing in implementing the eu strategy for the danube region by assuming the role of coordinating country for the priority actions: improving mobility and intermodality and developing the knowledge society research, education and ict.
in writing. − the european union's policy towards the western balkans has been clear, consistently applied and the recent accession of croatia proves that it is fair and productive. regardless of the fact that some member states have not recognised kosovo, the construction of its statehood must respect a number of principles and values. i am afraid that these principles are not always respected and that democratic reforms are long overdue, but there are encouraging signs about the dialogue with serbia, which the eu has done everything in its power to mediate and facilitate. the eulex presence in kosovo is a positive factor in resolving many problems between the kosovo majority and the serb minority. there is also progress in cooperation within regional mechanisms. i voted in favour of this resolution not least because of its non-ultimate nature on the question of the recognition of kosovo's independence. it is a step forward, including for the recognition of the right of each eu member state to decide in this respect.
in writing. - as regards the motion for a resolution on the process of european integration in kosovo, i voted against the first part of amendment no 2, which largely retains the original text of paragraph 1 of the resolution. parliament noted that 88 countries, including 22 eu member states, had recognised kosovo's declaration of independence and stressed that parliament would welcome both the recognition of this declaration by all eu member states and their more active participation in the process of mediation between serbia and kosovo. given that the recognition of such a declaration is a prerogative of the member states and given that romania has not recognised kosovo's declaration of independence, i considered that a vote against this text respects both the eu treaties and the subsidiarity of the member states. i also voted against the second part of amendment no 2, which refers to the diplomatic pressure exerted by serbia to prevent certain countries from recognising kosovo. finally, as these texts were adopted despite the constructive criticism and recommendations of the resolution on kosovo's european integration process, i did not support the final text of the resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because turkey is one of the european union's most important economic and geostrategic partners. with a spectacularly growing economy, which has tripled in size in the last decade, turkey is one of the most representative emerging powers, and its role in the middle east stability equation and in the eu's energy supply is becoming increasingly important. the eu is turkey's main economic partner, providing 80% of foreign investment in the country. unfortunately, economic growth has not been reflected in gdp per capita and in progress in the fight against poverty, especially among women. i believe that efforts to increase girls' schooling must be followed by progress in women's integration into the workforce and their representation in decision-making. but especially in combating violence against women, more concrete steps are needed to eradicate so-called honour killings and forced marriages, and to increase protection and shelter measures for women and minors who are victims of domestic violence.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution because there is a trade interdependence between the eu and turkey, the european union being turkey's most important trading partner. however, a lack of convergence persists in many areas. one example is visa policy, with turkey being the only candidate country not benefiting from visa liberalisation. one reason is the large number of illegal immigrants who, taking advantage of turkey's pivotal position, use its borders to enter the union. turkey is also not implementing the additional protocol to the association agreement and the customs union in their entirety.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution to wind up the debate on statements by the council and the commission pursuant to rule 110(2) of the rules of procedure on the 2011 progress report on turkey, because i firmly believe that procedures for accession by turkey should proceed faster and in a manner that unlocks the current stall. today, turkey represents a fundamental partner of the eu and the accession negotiations have not been dealt with in a consistent and balanced way. the copenhagen criteria have to be considered as the only valuable guidelines for any evaluation of progress made by turkey in complying with the eu acquis. parliament should firmly reject the attempt made by conservative and reactionary groups and parties throughout europe to create obstacles to any serious discussion regarding turkey’s accession on a merely political and populist base. the future of the european union depends on its capacity to be inclusive, open to intercultural dialogue and socially and economically sustainable. the accession of turkey, once the issues as already identified have been solved, opens the way for that future to happen.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the progress made by turkey, as turkey is the union's seventh largest trading partner and the union is turkey's most important trading partner. turkey's economy has tripled in size over the last decade and grew by about 10 percent last year, making it one of the world's fastest growing economies and one of the seven largest emerging economies in the world. i emphasise turkey's economic and development potential and its significant role in regional stability and energy security. turkey is a major eu energy corridor for oil and gas resources in the caucasus and caspian sea, and the nabucco pipeline remains one of the eu's top energy security priorities. turkey also has significant potential in renewable energy from solar, wind and geothermal sources. we welcome the progress made by turkey in the field of renewable energy sources and support future efforts to increase the use of renewable energy sources in all sectors. we underline turkey's role in developing and implementing a future eu black sea strategy, as called for by parliament in its resolution of 20 january 2011.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. i welcome the progress made by montenegro on its european path. the good neighbourly relations fostered by montenegro and its positive role in a still tense regional context, as well as the promotion of good inter-ethnic relations at home, are encouraging. evidence of this is the legislative framework for respecting minority rights, including the education law, as well as the way sensitive aspects of ethnicity were addressed in the population census. there is therefore a strong case for opening accession negotiations with montenegro in june, as promised by the european council.
in writing. − i voted for the 2011 report on montenegro's progress on enlargement. the eu and the member states aim to open accession negotiations with montenegro in june 2012. the eu is founded on the values of solidarity, tolerance and equal rights for all members of society. we draw attention to the under-representation of women in parliament, in high government positions and in decision-making positions in the public and private sectors. we welcome the significant progress made in the adoption of anti-corruption legislation, the new law on public procurement, the law on the financing of political parties and amendments to the law on conflicts of interest. we encourage montenegro to strengthen the legal framework for the rights of persons with disabilities and to improve their access to employment, including in public institutions. in view of the energy problems facing montenegro, we welcome the adoption of the government's energy policy plan until 2030. we call on the authorities to accelerate progress in the area of security of energy supply and energy efficiency and to continue their efforts to establish a regulatory framework that encourages the increasingly large-scale use of renewable energy sources in all sectors, in line with the relevant provisions of the eu renewable energy acquis.
in writing. − as a member of parliament from a country that joined the european union only five years ago, i know the importance of reports tracking the progress of countries that want to become members of the union. these reports provide incentives to continue the reforms already under way and, at the same time, provide important guidance for what the countries concerned need to do in other areas. the reports adopted today on serbia, turkey and montenegro are therefore, for better or for worse, an essential instrument for dialogue between these countries and the union.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is a good and necessary initiative for a more transparent, stable, secure and accountable corporate sector in the eu, with better corporate governance, taking into account the complexity and type of enterprise, so that the measures to be applied to enterprises are also adapted to the needs of small and medium-sized enterprises in supporting them to be competitive. the document covers a number of issues that were unfortunately not covered in the european commission's green paper of 5 april 2011, such as: decision-making by the board, the accountability and independence of the administrators, conflicts of interest or stakeholder involvement. i consider it extremely important that the boards of directors have independent and competent persons, recruited through transparent and merit-based methods. i also voted for equal opportunities for women and men. another aspect which i welcome is the decision by the member states to limit the number of boards of directors on which a person can sit, and the fact that directors must devote sufficient time to fulfilling their duties.
in writing. - as regards the report on a corporate governance framework for european enterprises, i voted against amendment 1, which calls for an increase in the number of women on boards of directors through a flexible quota system. i voted in favour of amendment no 3, which calls on the commission to present as soon as possible comprehensive, up-to-date data on the representation of women in all types of enterprises in the eu and on the mandatory and non-mandatory measures taken by the commercial sector, as well as on the measures recently taken by the member states to increase the representation of women. the report also calls on the commission, if the exercise concludes that measures taken by member states and enterprises are inadequate, to propose by 2012 legislative acts, including quotas, to increase the representation of women on the management bodies of enterprises to 30% by 2015 and to 40% by 2020, while taking into account the responsibilities of member states and their specific characteristics in economic, structural (especially in terms of enterprise size), legal and regional terms. i also voted in favour of amendment no 4, which made significant improvements to the report.
in writing. the european investment bank has recently become one of the most important financial institutions in the european union. the increase in lending to the member states to eur 52 billion and to non-eu countries to eur 6 billion in 2010 underlines the important role that the eib continues to play on the european continent. in a context where overcoming the effects of the global economic and financial crisis is one of the key priorities of the member states and the european union, strengthening the role and instruments of the eib is essential. i believe that the activities carried out by the eib to support european economies and stimulate growth and employment must be encouraged by the european institutions and the member states. the practice of presenting the eib's annual credit reports to the european parliament should also be institutionalised as an integral part of the european union's policies to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the 2010 annual report of the european investment bank because i believe that the eib is a very important player in a europe that is short of capital and that needs massive investment in development, infrastructure and research. i support the proposal to increase the bank's capital and i also believe that it should give priority to investment projects located in the regions and member states facing the greatest economic difficulties.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the 2010 annual report of the european investment bank (eib) because, as established by the treaty of rome, the eib's main objective is to contribute to the development of the single market and to narrow the development gap between the various regions. eib financing operations within the eu focus on six priorities: ensuring economic and social cohesion and convergence, implementing the knowledge-based economy, developing trans-european transport and access networks, supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), protecting and improving the environment, promoting sustainable communities and supporting sustainable, competitive and secure energy supply. we encourage the eib to continue its activities to support the development of the european economy and to foster growth, to stimulate employment and to promote social and territorial cohesion, with a particular focus on projects targeting less developed regions. we support the bank in its commitment to focus on the 'knowledge triangle' that brings together education, research and development and innovation. we urge the eib to increase its support for infrastructure networks in the new member states, whose level of support is still low compared to that of the eu-15 member states. we call for greater participation in the financing of infrastructure networks in the case of cross-border interconnections.
in writing. − there are still many obstacles to european citizenship, a citizenship which should give the right, among other things, to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states, to vote and stand as a candidate in elections to the european parliament and to municipal elections in the member state of residence, and to consular protection. unfortunately, seven years after the entry into force of the directive on free movement, for example, many people who should benefit from it still have difficulties entering or settling in another member state. the expulsion of the roma population in 2010 by the french authorities was a flagrant violation of fundamental rights. considering that it is urgent to remove all obstacles to the rights of eu citizens, i voted in favour of the eu citizenship report in 2010.
in writing. − i believe that all eu citizens brought before the courts of a member state have the right, in order to defend themselves, to access documents translated into their mother tongue, to prevent discrimination on the basis of language, and, in particular, i believe that all citizens must be informed of any legal action against them and that the whole process must take place within a timeframe acceptable from a judicial point of view.
in writing. − i voted for the report on eu citizenship in 2010: removing obstacles to eu citizens' rights. parliament called for the removal of barriers to the free movement of eu workers and for the guidance and counselling of mobile workers on employment opportunities and living and working conditions in the eu through eures. we call for better coordination between member states to tackle issues such as double taxation or the lack of harmonisation of pension taxation for eu citizens. in the area of health, we call on the commission and the member states to better inform eu citizens about their rights to cross-border healthcare and the means available to exercise them, such as reimbursement of costs on the basis of the european health insurance card. we draw attention to the fact that doctors, midwives and nurses who are nationals of the member states that have joined the eu since 2004 have encountered problems with the recognition of their qualifications or rights acquired in a member state other than their own. we welcome the role of the information and problem-solving networks created by the commission (such as the europe ta website, europe direct, solvit, european consumer centres) to inform citizens and resolve complaints about internal market failures or limitations on the rights of eu citizens.
vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, i would like to, if i might, make a statement on argentina and the situation there in response to mr salafranca’s request and to the concerns of this parliament. last night the argentinian government announced that it intends to expropriate the majority stake held by the spanish company repsol in the ypf energy company. this announcement gives cause for grave concern. ypf is an important european union investment in argentina. a takeover sends a very negative signal to international investors and could seriously harm the business environment in argentina. the measure creates legal insecurity for all european union and foreign firms in the country. i am also alarmed to note that the president referred in her speech to investments in other sectors, such as telecoms and banking. this announcement adds to a number of problematic decisions taken by argentina over the past few years in the areas of import restrictions and investment policy. the government of argentina must ensure compliance with its international commitments on the treatment and protection of investments originating from the european union. as a result of this announcement, we have decided to postpone the meeting of the eu-argentina joint cooperation committee which had been scheduled to take place on friday this week. this matter will also be discussed at next monday’s foreign affairs council in luxembourg. the spanish government has our full backing in this matter. the european union delegation in argentina has conveyed these concerns to the government of argentina. the announcement was only made last night, but the commission and the external action service are studying the argentinian draft measure so as to determine the next steps. all possible options are being analysed.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on development. - as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on development on this subject, i would like to congratulate mr howitt and welcome the integration of the totality of our suggestions into the final text. the importance of effectively integrating human rights into development cooperation is thus recognised, in line with the lisbon treaty logic of having a coherent foreign policy. in this respect, the new approach contained in the joint communication on human rights and democracy at the heart of the european union's external action is welcomed. this is an integrated human rights strategy covering the whole spectrum of union policies. but much remains to be done to make the strategy a reality. budget support should be more closely linked to the human rights and governance situation in the beneficiary countries, and the criteria for granting it should, i believe, be detailed. although difficult to bring up in times of economic crisis, another key point is the increase in funding for european mechanisms to support democracy and human rights. for the union, these are concrete means of promoting democracy and human rights in third countries.

member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, honourable members of the european parliament, i am pleased to have the opportunity today to discuss on behalf of high representative/vice-president ashton our regional cooperation efforts and perspectives in the black sea area. i welcome the attention that the european parliament is giving to black sea regional cooperation. the black sea region is a distinct geographical area rich in human and natural resources. it acts as a gateway between europe, asia and the middle east and therefore offers black sea stakeholders an opportunity to identify areas where our interests come together to further practical cooperation. since 2007, with the accession of bulgaria and romania, the european union has been directly involved in black sea affairs. there are significant opportunities and challenges in the region that require coordinated action. this is why we established the black sea synergy in 2008 as the european union’s contribution to regional cooperation. i am sometimes asked whether the black sea synergy duplicates the eastern partnership. my answer is no. the eastern partnership is about bringing our eastern neighbours closer to the european union through political association and economic integration. the black sea synergy is about bringing the european union closer to the black sea by contributing to regional cooperation. let me add a couple of personal comments here. there is, of course, interaction between the two – between the eastern partnership and the black sea synergy. we have developed the eastern partnership into a major instrument of our relationship with our eastern partners. i think it gives us an opportunity for the black sea synergy to become a real instrument providing us with synergies between our policies in our region as we put together our efforts to build more of the european union in our partner countries through our cross-border cooperation and our more active role in a regional framework of cooperation. while our interests in the black sea are broad, ranging from the environment, maritime affairs and fisheries to energy, transport, movement and security, we have focused our activities on the creation of the three sectoral partnerships in the fields of the environment, transport and energy. in march 2010 we launched the environment partnership. in addition, we have a substantial programme of cross-border cooperation in the region which i referred to a second ago. the budget for the 2007-2013 black sea basin programme under the cross-border element of the european neighbourhood and partnership instrument has increased from eur 17 million to almost eur 26 million. the 18 projects implemented after the first call for proposals cover the three priorities of the european union’s 2007-2013 black sea basin programme: supporting cross-border partnerships for economic and social development, sharing resources and competences for environmental protection and conservation, and supporting cultural and educational initiatives for the establishment of a common cultural environment in the basin. however, we have not progressed as much as we would have hoped in implementing the three partnerships. the time has thus come to reflect anew on how to take our cooperation in the black sea region forward. i therefore welcome the opportunity to discuss this with you. as for the future black sea strategy, we have to make sure it will be well received both within the european union and among the black sea states that are not part of our union. in the meantime, we are reflecting on how to revitalise the black sea synergy as a natural step towards the future strategy. in taking this forward, we will have three considerations uppermost in our minds. firstly, we must reinvigorate the european union’s approach to cooperation in the black sea region in a way which takes account of the variety of relations we have with the countries around the black sea. we have a candidate country (turkey) and a strategic partner (russia), plus our partners within the eastern partnership: ukraine, moldova, georgia, armenia and azerbaijan. we will also have to bear in mind the sometimes difficult relations these countries have with each other or with countries neighbouring the black sea region. secondly, we will need to take into account the other cooperation frameworks in the region. we do not need to reinvent the wheel. in the environmental field, the black sea commission is an important player, and the european union hopes to be accepted as a full member soon. we would also like to step up our engagement with the black sea economic cooperation organisation, especially in the context of its 20th anniversary summit due to take place in istanbul on 26 june. a reinvigorated black sea synergy initiative and engagement with the black sea economic cooperation organisation will provide great opportunities to develop practical cooperation and to foster dialogue between the european union and russia and between the european union and turkey, both being important stakeholders in the region. my third and last – and most important – point is this: we must play to the european union’s strengths and the opportunities offered by the lisbon treaty to bring together our internal and external policies and instruments. i will continue to value the exchanges with parliament on the black sea region as we take forward our process of reflection on how to enhance the european union’s policy approach towards this important region.
on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, as rapporteur on the black sea for this house i can confirm that 15 months have passed since this house called for the adoption of an eu strategy on the black sea which would upgrade the black sea synergy. when the black sea synergy was launched back in 2008, expectations were high. the launch of the black sea synergy had several important merits: firstly, shaping the black sea region as a separate unit of eu policy-making, and secondly, qualifying the region as strategically important for the eu. four years later the results are disappointing. in terms of eu policy, the black sea region looks very much like a black hole. no global reporting on the implementation of the synergy has taken place since 2008. no coherent policy document presents the current situation in the black sea region. secondly, the challenges in the black sea are not waiting peacefully for the commission to put pen to paper. the black sea is an unchecked collection of tensions and potential crises. despite some improvements in sectoral fields – environment, maritime and fisheries policy – one cannot speak of improvements in strategic fields such as security and energy. on two occasions – in 2008 and 2011 – the european parliament called for the upgrading of the black sea synergy to a black sea strategy, and the question still stands. is the commission planning to elaborate such a strategy?
the black sea region is of geostrategic importance, in particular for energy security and for the diversification of sources and routes of energy supply to the union, due to its proximity to the caspian sea, the middle east and central asia. following the accession of romania and bulgaria, the union should become an important player in the international relations of the region. as rapporteur for the itre commission opinion on a european union strategy for the black sea, i emphasised the european added value and the importance of the southern gas corridor as a means of improving the security of supply of the union. i believe that projects such as the nabucco gas pipeline, together with the trans adriatic gas pipeline, the pan-european peop oil pipeline, the turkey-greece-italy interconnection or the azerbaijan-georgia-romania interconnection highlight both the particular importance of the union's commitments in the black sea region and the subsequent need to intensify cooperation between the countries around the black sea. we call on the commission to give greater priority to the black sea region and to develop a european union strategy for the black sea, accompanied by an action plan.
the strategic importance of the black sea region is undeniable in political, economic, energy, commercial, ecological, cultural, transport security, neighbourhood policy and external relations. i therefore believe that the development of a union strategy for this region is not an option but a necessity. it must aim first and foremost at increasing stability and security, with a focus on resolving frozen conflicts, but also at exploiting the economic potential of the area, in particular by encouraging major energy projects. romania supports an active and comprehensive black sea policy, complementing the eu strategy for the danube region. the latter, now in the implementation phase, successfully demonstrates the importance of a concrete framework for cooperation. that is why, commissioner füle, i am asking the commission to present the draft black sea strategy as soon as possible.
the black sea region has a recognised strategic importance given its very rich natural resources and a potential market of over 350 million consumers. however, enhanced regional cooperation between the countries bordering the black sea and those in the wider black sea area is needed. a realistic solution for regional cooperation is to promote more strongly the bridge dimension of the european neighbourhood policy. the wider black sea region is part of the european union's eastern neighbourhood, but black sea cooperation has a rather modest place in the european union's current plans for the renewal of its neighbourhood policy. moreover, the european union can play a significant role in stimulating this regional cooperation by creating a european black sea strategy, building on the black sea synergy and complementary to the strategy for the danube region.
commissioner, i'd like to ask you a question. for the development of the black sea maritime corridors, there is currently no financing line open in this multiannual financial framework, although for all other seas of the european union there is one. we call on the black sea littoral states to conclude a memorandum of understanding for the development of the black sea sea corridors and we call on the commission to open a tnt budget line to finance the black sea sea corridors, similar to those financing the baltic, north sea and mediterranean sea corridors. also, with the exception of bilateral agreements, there is no global agreement on the regional management of fish stocks in the black sea. the commission's support is needed to develop the regional dialogue with a view to developing a common marine strategy in the black sea area involving the other black sea littoral states.
in writing. the eu's involvement in black sea policy must become increasingly consistent and substantial in line with the development potential offered by the region. at eu level we have an integrated policy for the socioeconomic development of maritime regions, but the black sea dimension is still limited. i would like to mention that the black sea is an important axis for energy and transport as half of the oil and gas imports of european countries will transit through this region. it is important, in my view, that the european black sea strategy is without doubt and perhaps an important objective of eu foreign policy, especially given the geostrategic importance of this area in the context of the 'arab spring' and the economic crisis.
in writing. there are many initiatives and opportunities in the black sea region, but the eu presence is not sufficiently visible. we can even talk about a timid policy in the black sea, the best example being fishing. bulgaria and romania have european quotas for cod, while turkey does not respect european policy in this area and does not apply any restrictions. turkish vessels fish 80% of the black sea cod, with the remaining 20% going to bulgaria and romania. in this context, dialogue with the black sea neighbours must be an integral part of this 'in-the-box' european policy.
in writing. – although the eu has been a black sea actor since 2007, its hesitancy to approach the area is still visible. the black sea synergy of 2008 has not been the precursor of a more elaborate approach, as we, the members who are located in that area, hoped for, but rather a time-buying mechanism to avoid just that: a more substantive approach towards that particularly important area of our continent. primarily, the motivation is related, on the one hand, to the inherent complexities of the area and, on the other, to the care the eu is demonstrating not to upset important countries in the region, particularly russia. probably, the eu considers that the instrument of eastern partnership is already a sufficient annoyance to russia – our main strategic partner in the east of the continent – to add to that a well defined strategy to deal with the area. even the black sea synergy was not conceived to be an efficient instrument, the proof of it being its minuscule ‘success’. under the circumstances, i am afraid that it will take more time for the area to get a proper strategy, which other similar regions – see the baltic sea, (russia included) – already enjoy.
member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, i would like to thank you for this opportunity to report on the progress made in the negotiations on the association agreements between the european union and armenia and azerbaijan respectively. i welcome the interest and engagement demonstrated by the european parliament in this regard. we have had an intensive and regular exchange with the two rapporteurs to prepare the two well-structured and comprehensive reports, for which i would like to thank mrs jäätteenmäki and mr poreba. the adoption of these reports comes at a moment when the relations of the european union with the south caucasus, and in particular with armenia and azerbaijan, are under the spotlight. during the visit of the armenian president sargsyan to brussels in march, and when i visited baku to attend the euronest plenary session two weeks ago, i conveyed two key messages to our interlocutors: first, our readiness to strengthen our links and to provide support, and second, our wish to see tangible progress on a number of issues, including deepened democracy, respect for human rights and conflict resolution. before providing comments on the reports, let me briefly give an update on the negotiations. there has been considerable progress since they were launched in july 2010. we had eight plenary meetings with armenia, and five with azerbaijan. out of 28 chapters on sectoral and economic reform, we closed 24 chapters with armenia and 13 with azerbaijan. discussions on the political as well as the justice, freedom and security chapters are well advanced, in particular with armenia. let me also stress that we perceived a genuine commitment of our interlocutors to fruitful – although at times difficult – negotiations, and this is reflected in the number of chapters closed so far. as to the reports, i would like to say from the outset that we fully share the views of the rapporteurs that the association agreements currently under negotiation are fundamental and far-reaching tools for deepening our relations with the two countries. within the multilateral dimension of the eastern partnership, these agreements should also be instrumental in developing, in a regional context, a series of bilateral contacts between the two countries in a number of areas. at present, such contacts between armenia and azerbaijan are almost non-existent. let me also share with you my impressions on the two issues addressed in detail in the reports. first, on nagorno-karabakh, the european union has recently expressed its concern at the slow progress in the peace negotiations and it called on both armenia and azerbaijan to step up their efforts to reach agreement on the ‘madrid principles’ as a basis for peace. increased tensions along the front lines add further concerns. we therefore urge the leaders on both sides to fully implement all commitments made in the minsk group framework. the european union stands ready to continue to provide enhanced support for confidence-building measures and this will remain complementary to the minsk group framework. the european union has the capacities and experience to contribute to confidence-building measures on people-to-people contacts and on security. the european union could also contribute to a number of initiatives, such as the mechanism proposed by the osce to investigate incidents along the lines of contact. we have underlined the need for unconditional/unrestricted access for european union representatives to nagorno-karabakh and the surrounding regions. we continue to work on this with the armenian and azerbaijani leadership. the second aspect is the issue of democracy, respect for human rights and the rule of law. armenia and azerbaijan are committed to sharing values and principles with the european union in this field and we should make every effort to stress to them the need to ensure that their countries fully comply with these standards. an important test for armenia will be the upcoming parliamentary elections in may and the presidential election next year. in the case of azerbaijan, the european union has clearly expressed the need for progress in democratic reforms in a number of areas. we also called for an invitation to be extended to the rapporteur for political prisoners of the parliamentary on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, i would like to start from the core problem preventing fully-fledged development and stability in the south caucasus region: the nagorno-karabakh conflict. occupying territories and preventing refugees and internally displaced persons from returning to their homes is against european values. some believe that negotiations within the framework of the minsk basic principles would bring an agreement to resolve this problem. in my view the negotiations were not robust enough and did not bring the expected results. we will have to agree to disagree on the results of these negotiations. this is why i believe that the european union should take a more active role in the settlement of this conflict and call on armenia to withdraw its forces from the occupied territories in nagorno-karabakh, along with confidence-building measures and multinational peacekeeping operations. this is why i insist and reiterate that the union should be involved in the negotiations using the experience of its member states, and i also refer to the experience of the baltic countries in the 1990s when it comes to holding – or not – a possible referendum in future. on visa facilitation, i welcome the launch in march of the negotiations on the visa facilitation and readmission agreement, but our cooperation on mobility should go further. once all the conditions are met we should aim for visa liberalisation. people-to-people contact is crucial. azerbaijan still has many challenges ahead, especially with regard to the judiciary, to the fight against corruption and organised crime, and in particular to implementing international law on human rights. many things are to be done and i would recommend focusing on high-level corruption cases, which are the test for both judges and politicians, and on improving transparency of public income and expenditure.
i support the negotiation of the association agreement with azerbaijan, because it will allow the union to intensify its relations with this important partner. economic and trade exchanges are an essential element of the process as they contribute to the development of political cooperation. i am pointing out the need to promote energy partnerships even more. it responds to a mutual interest in ensuring energy security by diversifying sources and transport routes. in this context, i would like to recall the agri lng interconnector project launched by romania, azerbaijan and georgia. i also stress the need for the union to be more involved in efforts to resolve the nagorno karabakh conflict. the framework provided by the eastern partnership and euronest must be used more to increase trust and promote dialogue between the parties.
in my speech i shall refer to the report on the recommendations of parliament on the negotiations between the european union and the republic of azerbaijan for the conclusion of an association agreement. i stress the importance of cooperation between the european union and azerbaijan for the diversification of sources and routes of energy supply to the european union. i welcome the joint declaration on gas supply signed in january 2011 in baku by the president of the european commission and the president of azerbaijan as an important milestone in the realisation of the southern gas corridor. we call on azerbaijan to continue its efforts to promote projects such as the baku-tbilisi-ceyhan and baku-tbilisi-erzurum pipelines. we call on the union to provide technical assistance to azerbaijan for the use of renewable energy sources and the promotion of energy efficiency. finally, i welcome the progress made by azerbaijan in the field of communications and information technology, especially e-government, thus increasing the transparency of public administration and helping to fight corruption.
the issue of alleged cia flights and detention centres in europe has come back to the attention of the european parliament, which is a positive thing, as i believe it is very important that the truth comes out. the fight against terrorism can never be, and must never be, more important than the protection of human rights, and therefore any abuses must be condemned. on the other hand, however, we must bear in mind that repeatedly accusing states without any real evidence is also a form of abuse. romania, for example, has been repeatedly accused of hosting cia detention centers, and the only evidence for this is a few articles in the press. parliamentary and civil inquiries proved that there were no centres of any kind. therefore, i would like to draw attention to the fact that finding the truth in the case of cia prisoners does not mean launching repeated and unfounded accusations, but fair analysis of real and objective facts that, at least in the case of romania, have proven to not exist.
i too support the amendment of the regulations on the coordination and implementation of social security systems. this will improve legal certainty. i welcome the fact that the proposal takes account of changes in national legislation as well as the latest developments in cross-border mobility. it is more important than ever to ensure the free movement of labour for all union citizens. romanian and bulgarian workers are more affected than the rest of the population by the additional demands placed on them in an already overcompetitive labour market. simplification of regulations is necessary in particular with regard to applicable unemployment benefits in order to protect citizens' rights. in this connection, i would stress the importance of amending article 65. the proposed amendments will contribute to updating and improving existing rules in the context of changing social realities.
i particularly appreciate the simplification that this proposal for a regulation aims to achieve. as you know, i have been advocating since the beginning of my mandate for the most flexible, flexible and simple approach to all the issues at european level to make things work as well as possible in line with the needs of european citizens. i therefore believe that the achievement of coordination of social security systems can only be a step forward in the current context of the need for jobs and, by implication, for encouraging labour mobility. regulations (ec) no 883/2004 and (ec) no 987/2009 should be adapted to the new situation. in addition, these efforts must be accompanied by member states, governments, which must continue to ensure the proper functioning of social security systems and work together in support of those regulations at european level for those who work or stop working in different countries with different systems.

member of the commission. − perhaps the previous commissioner for enlargement will supplement what i am saying, but this is exactly the point: since the freedom of movement from new member states is regulated within the enlargement agreements, the same rules in fact apply to those countries that joined the union in 2004 and in 2007, and to croatia, which will join next year. there is no discrimination because these three stages have been defined in an identical way vis-à-vis these countries. nevertheless, we do emphasise the merits of free movement and we have been inviting the older member states to open their labour markets faster than has been laid down, and quite a few of them have actually done that. quite a few opened very early, and some –italy and the czech republic – abandoned the restrictions from 1 january. so they will not apply the restrictions vis-à-vis romania and bulgaria for the next two years. i have been calling on all others to reconsider their decisions. i sent a letter to these governments in order to encourage them to reconsider their decisions, and in the forthcoming employment package we also point to the importance of this.

in writing. - i voted for the report on the coordination of social security systems. the proposal aims at regularly updating regulations (ec) no 883/2004 and (ec) no 987/2009 with the aim of ensuring adequate coordination at eu level of national social security systems. since member states frequently amend their social security legislation, coordination measures in the field of social security are necessary for the full exercise of the right to freedom of movement enshrined in the tfeu. the diversity and evolution of the conditions in which professional activities are carried out make it necessary to take account of the situation of highly mobile workers. new labour supply patterns, such as those in the air transport sector, have become apparent. social security coordination addresses cross-border situations where no member state can act alone. i think it is important that this regulation facilitates the coordination of social security systems by the member states and that people moving within the eu are better protected, so as to eliminate the risk of losing social security rights already acquired in another member state. this is in line with article 48 tfeu, which requires the european parliament and the council to adopt the measures necessary to establish freedom of movement for workers.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the decision on eu accession to the treaty of friendship and cooperation in south-east asia. the treaty of friendship and cooperation in southeast asia (tpc), signed by the original members of asean in 1976, aims to promote peace, stability and cooperation in southeast asia. the treaty was originally designed to apply only to states in the region and was amended in 1987 to allow for accession by states outside the region. in addition to the asean member states, other countries party to the treaty include china, india, japan, russia, australia, france, and the united states. in july 2006, member states agreed to initiate the procedures for eu accession to the treaty of friendship and cooperation, and to this end the treaty was substantially amended to allow accession by non-state entities. the treaty supports the peaceful settlement of disputes, the maintenance of peace, the prevention of conflict and the strengthening of security in southeast asia. the rules and principles set out in the treaty shall correspond to the objectives of the union's common foreign and security policy. the contracting parties shall also endeavour to cooperate as closely as possible and to provide each other with mutual assistance in the form of training and research facilities in the social, cultural, scientific, technical and administrative fields.
