in writing. − although the human rights situation in the eu is good, i believe we cannot stop here. the european union supports efforts to combat racism, xenophobia and other forms of discrimination based on religion, sex, age, disability or sexual orientation, with particular attention to respect for human rights in the areas of asylum and immigration. to promote human rights in the world, the eu is funding the european initiative for democracy and human rights, which has a budget of €1.1 billion for the period 2007-13. the initiative finances projects on gender equality and child protection, but also supports joint actions between the eu and other organisations involved in the defence of human rights, such as the united nations, the international committee of the red cross, the council of europe and the organisation for security and cooperation in europe. in view of the above, i believe that the eu must remain a major player in this area.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document concerning the annual report on human rights in the world and the european union’s policy on the matter, including implications for the eu’s strategic human rights policy, because it presents a balanced opinion of the current state of play and the improvements to be implemented to the eu’s action as a global player and within its internal governance, with regard to the human rights discipline. in particular, i strongly support the need for the european parliament to be recognised, and to further enhance its role, as a key actor in the shaping of the implementation of the european union’s human rights strategy. for this reason, i strongly believe that the council and the commission should systematically take up the parliament’s resolutions and communications, by providing substantive responses to the impulse received from the democratically elected body of the eu. the report addresses the fundamental issues of the death penalty, arms control, torture and other cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment or punishment, women and human rights, freedom of religion, discrimination, children’s rights, freedom of expression. the guarantee of the highest standards of human rights must imperatively guide the eu’s action, in its external and internal policies.

tax evasion causes significant economic losses, affects the functioning of state institutions and thus endangers national security. romania has revenues of only 33% of gdp, below the european average of 40%. the government of my country has made the fight against tax evasion a priority by setting up an interministerial committee to combat tax evasion. it is well known that the netherlands opposes my country's accession to the schengen area on the grounds of corruption and fraud. ironically, a shipment of 40 million contraband cigarettes worth 15 million euros was stranded for four days undetected in the port of rotterdam in the netherlands, a schengen country. this would not have been possible in the port of constanta in romania. the credit for this impressive capture, which took place last week, goes to the irish authorities, whom i would like to congratulate.
i would like to thank my colleague, mrs thyssen, in particular, for her efforts in producing this very good report. although the development of economic integration requires a system for the creation of a common consolidated tax base for companies operating in several member states, although the draft directive provides for the optional nature of companies to join this system and although each member state has the right to apply the tax rate it wishes to the part of the consolidated tax base that falls to it by way of allocation, we are still in a situation where some national parliaments have sent objections claiming that the principle of subsidiarity is violated, including my country's parliament. some governments are also opposed to the draft directive. i ask the commission to treat the position of the national parliaments with the utmost care. i think it is useful to have a meeting with these national parliaments which have invoked the principle of subsidiarity, and we in the committee on economic and monetary affairs are ready to take part in this dialogue.
the report we are voting on tomorrow is a strong signal to the governments of the member states to introduce a european corporate taxation framework. it is a requirement which parliament has put forward on several occasions, and it constitutes a step towards the completion of the european internal market and the economic integration of the member states. it should be borne in mind that many companies are now active in more than one member state. by representing a common set of rules in this area, the common consolidated corporate tax base will significantly reduce the administrative costs of companies and increase transparency, making the union a more attractive place for investors in practice. the european commission estimates an annual reduction of €700 million in compliance costs and also a decrease in tax evasion. in this context, i support this proposal and consider it necessary in the future to apply the system to small and medium-sized enterprises and to introduce a minimum level of taxation at european level. i also hope that parliament's proposal will be fully taken into account by the council of ministers.
i believe that the commission's proposals and the amendments proposed in the report largely contribute to adapting this directive to the objectives which the union has set itself in the field of the environment and climate change, by means of taxation which favours energy products with the lowest possible impact on the environment. but like other colleagues, i have serious reservations about the principle of proportionality and the impact it might have on the price of petrol. with fuel prices already putting pressure on european consumers, i do not think this increase in the price of petrol would be the most appropriate measure. in addition, it would also limit the interest of consumers in vehicles that run on this type of fuel, so it will also have an impact on the car manufacturing industry in the european union. given that diesel engines are one of the strengths of european industry, i think we could lose this comparative advantage. and we're not going to have the environmental advantage, because there's an energy difference between gasoline and diesel.
in writing. the proposal for a directive on the taxation of energy products and electricity is undoubtedly ambitious from the point of view of environmental protection. i agree that we need a substantial reduction in co2 emissions not only for the sake of environmental sustainability, but also for the health of european citizens. however, the proposal comes at a difficult time for the european economy. increasing the levels of excise duties on energy products as well as on electricity could generate an increase in budget revenues. however, all eu citizens already affected by the application of tough austerity measures would be the ones who would be hit by such decisions, especially in relation to vulnerable households. in addition, the minimum level of excise duty on diesel is to be increased from 2013 onwards, as diesel is currently taxed less than petrol. this is not a realistic timeframe to put such a measure into practice without disrupting the market in member states where diesel is preferred by car owners precisely because of the lower price. i therefore oppose the commission's proposal because it does not fairly represent the interests of european consumers.
in writing. i think it would be a big mistake to impose extra burdens on citizens in this time of crisis. unfortunately, this directive could do just that, as it could lead to higher energy, electricity and fuel prices. the report adopted by the econ commission rejected itre's suggestion to reduce the high price of co2 emissions, and this will be felt in consumer prices. also, although there are some references to low-income categories, measures to protect them remain vague and ineffective. the social impact of this new directive could be very serious, especially in member states such as romania, where harsh measures have already been imposed on citizens, such as mass redundancies, wage cuts or tax increases. the directive would impose a double additional tax burden on these persons: they would pay both direct taxes on energy and the cost of the inflation that the taxes would generate. i think these concerns are legitimate and that is why i think we should reconsider our support for this directive.
in writing. the proposed amendment to the directive on the restructuring of the community framework for the taxation of energy products and electricity introduces two components for the taxation of energy: taxation in relation to carbon dioxide emissions and taxation of general energy consumption. the introduction of carbon taxation is the introduction of a carbon tax, which will affect both industry, households and european competitiveness. i believe that for households, the removal of the currently applicable shields and reductions is a difficult task to bear, especially in this period of economic crisis, when unemployment is alarming and the quality of life of many european households has decreased. the increase in diesel taxation will also have a negative impact on both car owners and the car industry, which, according to european regulations, has already invested in less polluting engines. i welcome the adoption of the amendments tabled, which call for electricity used for irrigation to be exempt from taxation and for electricity used to power electric and hybrid vehicles to be exempt from taxation by 1 january 2023. i consider that the setting of the carbon dioxide tax at eur 20/t is arbitrary. this value should be set by the market, and not arbitrarily modified by the commission, just to make investments in renewable energy profitable.
on behalf of the alde group. any change to the regulation to facilitate the rapid implementation of cohesion policy programmes will certainly have an immediate and real impact on the economies of the member states most affected by the crisis. it is therefore extremely important that we adopt tomorrow the report on risk-sharing instruments for member states facing serious difficulties with their financial stability, in order to provide them with the financial support they need to continue their projects and the process of economic recovery. it is also very important that the council adopts it as soon as possible. even though the report is very technical, the alde group supports the present compromise because, in our view, it is a balanced proposal which takes account of the problems that have been identified during the debates. in addition, it is very important that the european investment bank is in a very strong position in the use of this financial instrument, which countries under a financial assistance programme will be able to use in the next year and a half. the instrument itself enjoys our support, but we must ensure that projects which do not make economic sense are not financed. i think it is particularly important that the projects financed undergo a detailed cost-benefit analysis to ensure that they are geared to increasing the number of jobs and, by implication, the competitiveness of the member states.
the ongoing economic and financial crisis across the eu is affecting the macroeconomic stability of many countries and access to finance. the proposal for a risk-sharing instrument seeks to strengthen synergies between loan programmes and union funds in countries receiving assistance from the eu or the imf: the commission has also proposed that the member states should be given the possibility to apply the principle of proportionality. the aim is to find solutions for projects that generate viable income. examples would be the obtaining of private financing for infrastructure projects that generate net revenues, for example toll motorways, or productive investments for which state aid has a maximum allowable limit. the proposed solution is of course an exception, but it is a concrete measure, in the context of the crisis, of risk-sharing with the european investment bank and other financial institutions, in order to maintain the degree of involvement of private investors and to overcome the major obstacles to the implementation of cohesion policy programmes. the use of the mechanism is an additional solution for the use of the structural and cohesion funds, which could not be absorbed by the end of the current 2007-2013 programming period. the commission's proposal to limit the amount of the appropriations to 10% is a very good idea and should be adopted. i congratulate the rapporteur on the excellent way in which she has handled this report.
the mistrust and reluctance of private investors as well as the financial sector have meant that in some member states there is a high chance that a number of strategic projects will not be realised. the main projects affected are infrastructure projects and the analysis shows that the financial resources needed to develop the infrastructure of the european union for the period 2010-2030 are over eur 1 500 billion. this figure shows that an efficient transport network at european level requires substantial efforts and that this requires diversified sources of funding, both public and private. a risk-sharing instrument will be a real solution to these problems we are facing and will allow the continuation of the implementation of european programmes by injecting additional funds into the economy from the eib and other financial institutions. funds to co-finance projects implemented with the support of the structural and cohesion funds will have an immediate impact on the economy, contributing significantly to job growth.
i welcome the coordination between the loan programmes and the union funds for countries facing financial stability difficulties. it is important to ensure the continuation of programmes co-financed by the erdf and the cohesion fund in countries subject to budgetary constraints. i believe that this proposal will have a positive impact on the economies of the member states affected by the crisis. it will allow major infrastructure projects to be developed, thus contributing to economic recovery through investment. romania is among the countries receiving financial assistance from the imf. in my country, economic hardship has affected infrastructure projects. in these circumstances, the measures discussed today are welcome, especially since the imf and the european commission have recommended romania to use as much european funds as possible in the national infrastructure development programme.
on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, colleagues, this is a controversial agreement because, while its aim – fighting terrorists through preventive means – is welcome, it undeniably interferes with the protection of other equally important values such as privacy and data protection. i am not the only person saying that the agreement violates this right and eu legislation; the european data protection supervisor demonstrated it in a thorough analysis. what is more, the scope of the agreement goes far beyond combating terrorism. many say it is a better agreement than the previous one – which only means it is less bad than the previous one – but it remains an agreement with severe consequences for our fundamental rights. i respect the fact that the american authorities and lawmakers are interested in their citizens’ rights, but i believe that we are entitled to care above all about the protection of our own european citizens’ rights. it has been said that, without this agreement, our air carriers will violate eu legislation on data protection because if they want to land in the usa they will continue to transfer data. but you must remember that the agreement obliges the air carriers to implement the ‘push’ obligations in two years, which means investing a huge amount of money in equipment and software to transmit all data to the us authorities in real time. what if some of the air carriers are not able to implement this obligation? big companies will probably do it, but either smaller companies will be forced out of business by this expenditure or the current situation will continue. they will allow the extraction of data by the american authorities directly from their computers. i have never believed that a bad law is better than no law.
i hope that this parliament can give priority to the diversity of opinions and i am convinced that we all agree that the risks of transnational crime and the risks of terrorism are global risks that require global responses. the only way forward in this context is to have a legal framework, and that is how this treaty was adopted, which, from the point of view of european citizens, even the lame ones, as it is written, constitutes a rule of law that guarantees them respect for their rights. but unfortunately, we have to give priority to a number of fundamental rights. i agree and respect personal data, but we must agree that european citizens have the right to individual security as a fundamental right of the right to life. from this point of view, i believe that the improvements that have been made in this agreement, the fact that we can renegotiate, we can monitor and i have no reason not to trust the european commission and the american authorities, are arguments for voting in favour of this agreement.
madam president, today’s agreement is an expression of the new balance between an ever-inquisitive state and the ever-decreasing respect for the privacy of their citizens after 11 september 2001. i am not going to dwell on technicalities; i will rather try to make three points. first, before being concerned with the transfer of pnrs, we should be concerned primarily with their content upon collection. i do not see the relevance of, for instance, my trade union membership when booking a flight. second, the data does not become public through transfer but through collection here in europe. third, our american friends want the data mostly to compare it with their own data already collected through other means. in view of the above, i am afraid that we do not have an alternative to approving the agreement, which i personally intend to do.
in writing. – the eu-us pnr agreement should be favoured because it is an effective tool for the fight against terrorism and serious transnational crime. the us authorities have provided several concrete examples where the pnr data system had been crucial in disrupting major terrorist plots. the cases of david headley, faisal shahzad or najibullah zazi, arrested before they could accomplish planned terrorist crimes, are strong arguments in favour of the security benefits this agreement carries. the agreement also provides for judicial and extra-judicial means of redress for individuals who may feel that they or their data have been improperly handled. according to the us department of homeland security, however, no complaints of abuse of personal data have been recorded so far under the pnr agreement currently in effect. the conclusion of this agreement is a good opportunity for the eu to advance negotiations with the usa for the application of the reciprocity principle on the elimination of visas for all eu member states, including romania, bulgaria, cyprus and poland, in the framework of the visa waiver programme.
in writing. we live in a globalised society, where potential dangers are no longer confined to national borders. the fight against terrorism has exposed some states to serious threats. this is the case in several european countries, but also in the united states. the agreement with the us on the exchange of passenger data legislates a current practice, based on a provisional agreement of 2007. such data have been used for the last 60 years by customs authorities around the world, and new technologies have come to facilitate their transmission. according to the draft agreement, the information will be stored in a secure database and will be used mainly for the prevention and investigation of cross-border crime. it is important to note that eu citizens have the right to compensation if their personal data is used in an inappropriate manner. the conclusion of this eu-us agreement, modelled on other similar agreements (with australia, for example) is important for the strengthening of cooperation, as it is a guarantee for the continuation of the policy of eliminating travel visas for citizens and of free movement in safe conditions.
i voted for the conclusion of the agreement because it represents a step forward in eu-us cooperation in combating terrorism. the current document provides more safeguards for passengers than the 2007 text, ensuring enhanced protection of personal data. for example, those concerned have access to the information stored and can make changes if necessary. furthermore, it mentions the possibility of the deletion of part of the information by the passengers concerned. i would also stress that the principles of proportionality and reciprocity have been included. the us authorities are thus under an obligation to provide the relevant data to the european party. the right to privacy is ensured by clearly defining the conditions under which access to information is granted, and the establishment of differentiated penalty thresholds is a significant improvement over the previous text.
i abstained on this report because my country has a reserved position on this proposal for a directive. a single tax base is very important for the development of economic integration. only then can there be fair competition in the field of taxation. at the same time, harmonisation strengthens the eu's competitiveness and has beneficial effects on the economy and the labour market. the proposal for a directive initially provides for the application of the levy to be optional and each member state will be able to set its own tax rate. however, several national parliaments, including my own, have invoked the principle of subsidiarity. in addition, romania requested clarifications on the definition of the principles and concepts related to the tax base. i believe that we need fair tax competition to protect the national tax base.
this report is a testament to the positive role of parliament, because a number of amendments, which mainly concerned the principle of proportionality, were adopted by parliament and thus succeeded in mitigating a fundamentally wrong proposal that the european commission made at that time. i think that this automatic price indexation that has been avoided, the taxation based on co2 emissions and the energy content of the product was fundamentally wrong, introduced a certain bureaucracy, led to higher prices, which does not prove at all that there is a very clear vision of economic reform and economic revival in general. i think that once these amendments have been accepted mrs lulling's report can be regarded as acceptable.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion of the voluntary partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of liberia on forest law enforcement, governance and trade in timber products entering the european union. nearly 45 percent of liberia is forested, and the country has more than half of the remaining tropical rain forests in west africa. the timber regulation, which will enter into force in march 2013, aims to facilitate legitimate trade in timber products and ensure a level playing field for all market participants. it will ban the sale in the eu of illegally harvested timber and timber products manufactured in accordance with the rules of the country of origin. the regulation lays down the obligations of operators placing timber or related products on the eu market. it will aim to guarantee access to european markets for products from legal sources while halting deforestation in liberia. i ask the commission to report regularly to parliament on progress in implementing existing voluntary partnership agreements and the negotiation and implementation of new ones.
in writing. − the european union is currently facing a persistent economic and financial crisis, which is affecting not only the macroeconomic stability of many member states, but also access to finance throughout the european union. the aim of this measure is to find a solution to the serious problems faced by certain member states in obtaining the private financing needed to carry out infrastructure projects and productive investments which can only be partially financed by public funds. the commission proposal only concerns revenue-generating projects, as the investment costs covered by the revenue are not eligible for eu co-financing. in the member states most affected by the financial and economic crisis, there is a risk that a number of strategic projects that have been selected for co-financing by cohesion policy programmes will not be realised, as private sector investors and banks either lack the liquidity to provide loans for projects and project promoters, or are no longer willing to take on the risks of investments under current conditions.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the agreement between the united states of america (us) and the eu on the use and transfer of passenger name record (pnr) data as it replaces the 2007 agreement and provides more safeguards than the 2007 agreement. to date, several member states have concluded agreements or memoranda of understanding with the usa, including on the transfer of passenger data, a prerequisite imposed by the usa for the lifting of visas for nationals of member states wishing to travel to the usa. therefore, in the context of the approval of the agreement between the us and the eu on the use and transfer of passenger name record data, i am asking the united states of america to eliminate visas for romanian citizens traveling to the us. we welcome the adoption of the 'push' method as the standard method for data transmission as well as the provisions of article 5 concerning data security and integrity. we regret that the agreement does not provide for reciprocity between the parties and does not provide sufficient guarantees for the legal remedies of european citizens, the applicable law being us law. i would stress that the agreement must be interpreted in the context of a global approach to pnr, including negotiations with other third countries (australia and canada), as well as the proposal for an eu-wide pnr system.

in writing. − given that there are different tax bases in the eu countries which in practice act as trade barriers to growth and employment, i think this proposal is a good one, which can bring improvements for businesses that carry out cross-border activities to increase the competitiveness of eu businesses.
in writing. − the proposed directive will likely produce certain positive effects such a lower risk of double taxation and tax evasion and fraud as well as greater fiscal transparency and legal certitude for multinational corporations. on the other hand the proposal will be applied to a highly heterogeneous economical area, where any harmonising measure has to be thoroughly considered. apportionment formulas based on factors such as wage costs or assets are likely to harm the economic balance of the newer member states. such factors should only play a decisive role within a common corporate tax policy once their convergence in all member states is adequate. otherwise reduced enforcement costs and red tape in the eu will be achieved at the expense of the competitiveness of some of its member states. moreover, the proposal can be perceived as a first step in the creation of a common eu corporate tax policy, which has strong subsidiarity implications, and which should be considered by all eu and national stakeholders. therefore i voted for the legislative resolution but against the amended proposal in order to point out that while i agree with the general idea behind the commission’s proposal, i am not satisfied with the final result.
in writing. − i abstained on this report because romania has a reserved position on the current version of the proposal. this proposal promotes renewable energy sources, contributing to the european 20-20-20 strategy to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. providing the necessary framework for carbon taxation would also lead to an increase in energy efficiency. i also support the rapporteur's view that a positive signal should be sent. the proposal for a directive would also raise the minimum levels of excise duty on energy products and electricity. moreover, the price of diesel is already quite high, and a further increase would be to the detriment of consumers. i think it's important to have a constructive approach without making things more complicated.
in writing. − energy is a key element of any economy, with a major impact on all sectors. the specific policies promoted in this field must ensure the development of a climate favourable to the promotion and exploitation of all available sources of energy, so as to mitigate the negative effects on this market. the revised proposal for a directive adapts the structure of energy taxation to support the objective of a low-carbon and energy-efficient economy and to avoid problems in the internal market. by introducing a co2-related element in energy taxation, the proposal aims to bring energy into line with eu commitments to combat climate change. the european union's approach to the taxation of energy products and electricity is converging with a view to ensuring a tax framework that is as favourable as possible to achieving maximum efficiency in promoting the best possible use of energy products at the highest possible rates and, at the same time, reducing waste and unjustified consumption of these products.
in writing. − i consider this proposal to be an important contribution to the achievement of the europe 2020 strategy on greenhouse gas emission reductions.
in writing. − i voted against this report on the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2003/96/ec restructuring the community framework for the taxation of energy products and electricity, because i strongly believe that it will constitute a further and excessive burden on our citizens, who have already been heavily subjected to the dramatic effects of the economic and financial crisis. the main effect of this taxation will be an increase in energy and electricity bills in all eu member states due to the imposition of a flat rate of tax in addition to other national taxes. this is unacceptable, firstly because prices for energy and fuel have increased tremendously in recent years; secondly, because a flat rate of tax is discriminatory, since it does not take into account the socio-economic, structural and infrastructural differences between eu countries; lastly, because it greatly interferes with the domestic fiscal policies of the member states. i believe that if environment protection is the goal of the eu, this should be achieved by proposing investments in renewable energies and infrastructures, not through a tax which will have to be paid by our citizens, and them alone.
in writing. − this draft council directive on the restructuring of the community framework for the taxation of energy products and electricity proposes to review the old rules on the taxation of energy products and electricity in the european union. the new rules aim to restructure the way energy products are taxed, to eliminate current imbalances and to take into account both their co2 emissions and their energy content. by taxing polluting products and services differently, without taking account of environmental rules, producers are encouraged to invest in research to develop more energy-efficient products and services. in this way, the legislative changes proposed by this directive can contribute to the promotion of research and innovation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the amendments to the report and welcome the decision adopted by the european parliament on the system of taxation of energy products and electricity in the european union. the methodology proposed by the european commission would have led to a substantial increase in excise duties on petrol in most member states, which would have been detrimental to citizens who invested in diesel cars, especially given their competitive advantages. the methodology proposed by the commission also disadvantages farmers, who should have invested more in agricultural works or irrigation. however, i decided to abstain in the final vote, given a number of other provisions in the report which i do not consider to be entirely satisfactory.
in writing. - i voted against the amendment to the energy taxation directive because the proposal introduces two components for energy taxation: taxation in relation to carbon dioxide emissions and taxation of general energy consumption. i voted against amendments nos 21 and 44, which were adopted by the european parliament. amendment 21 removes the possibility of applying exemptions and reductions to households and charitable organisations as provided for in directive 2003/96/ec, and amendment 44 limits the granting of reductions for heating to households only until the beginning of 2025. i voted against amendments nos 23 and 40, which removed the existing exemptions for fuels used in shipping and aviation. shipping is a less polluting and cheaper transport and should therefore be encouraged. air transport is, as of 1 january 2012, included in the emissions trading scheme (ets) and the application of a new emission-based taxation would have been double taxation. i also think it is inappropriate to increase the tax rate on diesel fuel, because in 2009 a european regulation required car manufacturers to invest in less polluting engines. the increase in the level of diesel taxation will affect both car manufacturers and european citizens who have bought less polluting diesel-powered cars.
in writing. − according to some estimates, the annual loss of tax revenue for the 27 eu member states amounts to around eur 1 billion. i believe that there is a need for closer cooperation at european union level to combat tax fraud and evasion and i therefore voted in favour of the report on finding concrete solutions in this area. to achieve the goal of eradicating these harmful behaviours, a common european tax framework, reform of accounting rules and stricter regulation of company registers are needed. the revenues recovered from combating fraud and evasion would allow eu governments to pay their debts and make significant public investments.
in writing. − i believe that there is a need to continue to emphasise the key role that the common consolidated corporate tax base can play in combating tax fraud at union level.
in writing. − i am pleased to note that the danish presidency has tax cooperation among its priorities, as the subject is topical, especially in the current economic context. i hope that by june the european commission will have proposed concrete measures to combat tax evasion, thus complying with the decision taken by the council in march. i also hope that the european commission will come forward with a proposal to revise the interest and royalties directive as soon as possible, with a view to eliminating tax evasion through hybrid financial instruments in the eu.
in writing. − i fully support this resolution. tax fraud generates illicit funding which is invested in illicit activities and is often subject to money laundering. too light an approach can result in tax fraud and tax evasion generating – in time – complex mechanisms that secure virtually inexhaustible resources for organised crime networks and corruption. the resolution touches upon some of the more substantial problems that we witness today across europe, such as: secrecy within the banking sector, the resort to foreign non-cooperating jurisdictions (tax havens) in order to conceal both licit and illicit financial interests, corporate tax avoidance, inefficient collection of tax, the abundance of unjustified exemptions etc. expectedly, each of these forms of tax avoidance and evasion are more specific to some countries than others. within the eu these specificities should be accurately traced out and countered by region-specific measures.

blue-card answer. – madam president, i think that my colleague is actually making a mistake and confusing the european court of human rights in strasbourg with the national courts in russia, in ukraine and in the other countries. i think there is a huge difference between the two. if someone knows how the european court of human rights functions, they understand that there is always the possibility of having the right decision. so far the jurisprudence of the european court of human rights, which was literally applied also by the luxembourg court of justice, has proved that it was a very good court with very sound decisions.
in writing. i welcome the eu's accession to the european convention on human rights (echr), as the union needs to have a clear system for the protection of fundamental rights. i appreciate that it will make a major contribution to strengthening the human rights regime throughout europe, ensuring greater protection for citizens, including with regard to community legislation. the debate is not new, but the provisions of the lisbon treaty provide the legal instruments necessary to carry out this project. the union is founded on respect for human rights and already has a 'charter of fundamental rights', but to ensure their full promotion and protection, a specialised judicial mechanism is also needed. the european court of justice has no specific powers in this area, whereas the strasbourg court has a long and varied history in this area. while informal consultation has so far ensured consistency in the practice of the two courts, this accession will require technical harmonisation, both as regards the statute of the two courts and the details of judicial cooperation. it will also bring important benefits to the member states by bringing legal clarity, avoiding possible conflicts of jurisdiction or divergences of provisions between the echr and community law.
author. − the current problems with the high number of forged biometric passports are largely due to the fact that not enough attention is paid to the entire issuing cycle. as the european parliament's 2008 report rightly states, it is not enough to guarantee a high level of security of passports if the way they are obtained is not as secure. the main problems that persist, in my view, are related to the reliability of the data collected, especially on children and the elderly, but also to the number and security of origin documents accepted as proof of identity for the issuance of passports. in other words, there is no point in producing secure passports if they are issued on the basis of false documents. to counter these problems, the commission needs to present a clear assessment of the shortcomings throughout the passport issuance cycle. i think the most important element to consider is the origin documents. at present, there are dozens of different documents at union level on the basis of which a passport can be issued, and many of these documents have questionable security levels and can be easily forged. two things are therefore essential: on the one hand, limiting the number of origin documents accepted for the issuing of passports, and on the other hand, establishing minimum security standards for these origin documents. in the same vein, a possibility to be considered is the harmonisation of national identity card models at eu level. this is necessary as identity cards are most often used both as origin and travel documents within the eu. finally, i would also like to stress once again the need for a thorough study by the commission on the security of the entire biometric document issuance cycle, as this will be of particular relevance for future smart borders systems.
biometric passports have been and are still difficult to accept by the population. it does not readily accept new things, especially if they are not adequately explained. true, while it may seem to be a very secure system for identifying travelers, fraud is possible because of the various technologies and devices that hackers use to steal data from the chips. people fear that just as bank card data is stolen, so too is the data on the biometric passport chip. i think the public should be better informed about what a biometric passport is and the security measures it provides. it is necessary to consider the possibility of creating a system in the future whereby the radio frequency identification device contained in the passport chip can only be detected by the competent authorities.
a few remarks very close to those made by my colleagues so far: firstly, the new common agricultural policy will not be able to enter into force without the new regulations on less-favoured areas, which is impossible as long as parliament has no access to the simulations carried out. parliament cannot turn its back on something that is not known, because it is ultimately parliament's role to explain to the citizens the decisions it has taken. any decision taken away from public opinion will be a contested decision and will lack legitimacy. secondly, without waiting for the results of the simulations, the commission should proceed to draft another proposal reflecting the european parliament's observations. farmers expect all factors that limit production to be taken into account, including geographical factors such as isolation or socio-economic criteria.
in the debate on the quality package, i tabled a number of amendments relating to the issue under discussion today. the aim was to introduce a new european label called 'product on my farm', applicable to products sold directly on or near the farm, including in the market, or sold by direct delivery to consumers. i think this would be the best guideline to follow in establishing a definition of local products. as regards criteria such as the distance from the farm to the consumer or the mode of production, i consider that they are not relevant, only the direct link between producer and consumer matters. local sales systems bring advantages to producers, who can benefit from a higher percentage of the final price, and to consumers, who can benefit from fresh produce at affordable prices. the issue of potential food nationalism raised by the questioners is a false issue. if anything, it's price and quality, and if local products meet those criteria, consumers will buy them.
today's debate takes place one year after the launch of the european quality policy in agriculture. as part of the cap reform, this initiative promotes the preservation of europe's local culinary heritage. the regional specific has a crucial role in maintaining cultural diversity as a whole. local recipes and products express the traditions of the different areas of the union and support organic farming. to preserve this cultural resource, the definition of locally produced food needs to be clarified. this discussion is all the more relevant in the case of foodstuffs that have a cross-border production process. the situation of recipes and products common to the border regions is also unclear. i would like to ask commissioner ciolos if the geographical criterion will be the predominant element in this classification and in relation to which benchmark the distance used in the granting of the local product status will be determined.
according to statistics from the authorities in athens, 90% of illegal immigrants in 2011 entered the union through greece. any member state would have great difficulty in coping with such a situation. it is once again proving that a coherent approach is needed at european level to deal with such cases. it is necessary for all neighbouring countries to cooperate in order to regulate migration flows and secure borders. the role of frontex is crucial in this process, which is why the agency must become even more involved in the efforts of the authorities. there is also the question of speeding up administrative procedures for granting legal status to immigrants. i point to the voluntary repatriation plan announced just yesterday by the greek government. it is a step forward in resolving the situation, especially as it involves ngos.

the great challenge facing humanity today, climate change, is closely tied to equality. in the event of natural disasters or their aftermath, women are 14 times more likely to die than men. one explanation is statistics that show that 70 percent of the world's poorest people are women, because they work primarily in agriculture, 85 percent of those who die from climate-related disasters are women, 75 percent of environmental refugees are women. women are still the most likely unseen victims of resource wars and climate change violence. on the other hand, women are discriminated against in terms of access to resources and technologies, to services of all kinds, including medicines. for the most part, women do not own land, cannot get credit, and, above all, do not have decision-making power. these are some of the reasons why women are less able to adapt to climate change. i believe that by addressing this issue, we are not launching a competition between gender equality and climate policies, but we need to find the most appropriate solutions to advance these areas simultaneously. i welcome the rapporteur's proposal to establish gender databases at the evaluation or launch stages of projects. a better understanding of the gender dimension of climate change is essential to finding the best policy solutions to combat it.

rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on agriculture and rural development. − the european natural heritage is an important ecological capital that contributes to the well-being of all citizens, which is why all eu countries must cooperate and coordinate their efforts to make better use of natural resources and limit the degradation of biodiversity. when we talk about biodiversity, we must refer to both the extraordinary biodiversity, included in the parks and nature reserves, which are already protected or are in the process of being included in this list, and the ordinary biodiversity, also known as functional biodiversity. it plays a major role in maintaining the habitat of small fauna and insects, especially those that help to pollinate plants. on the other hand, conservation of basic natural resources, animal and plant genetic resources, the environment and the steering of agrotechnological processes are necessary to ensure that the requirements of future generations are met. i believe that a balance between the european biodiversity strategy and the member states' rural development plans is essential to ensure the conservation of biodiversity.
agriculture is now faced with the challenge of producing more with less and less damage to the environment. the biodiversity strategy report rightly notes the importance of this dual challenge. however, a number of observations need to be made on the elements relating to the future common agricultural policy. the so-called greening of the cap is undoubtedly necessary and welcome, but the formula in which it has been proposed will lead to a reduction in the capacity of the agri-food sector to be more competitive and to enter a path of sustainable growth. the 30% set aside for greening is disproportionate in the context of budgetary austerity. giving up seven percent of the land is not the right decision, given the growing demand for food. diversification of crops is virtually impossible for smallholders. last but not least, the system involves too much bureaucracy and enormous costs. agriculture can make an important contribution to biodiversity conservation, but policies in this area must be chosen with particular regard to long-term food security.
biodiversity is in crisis in europe, with species disappearing at an unprecedented rate, leading to the degradation of ecosystems. the annual costs of biodiversity loss run into billions for the global economy, undermining economies, business prospects and opportunities to fight poverty. i encourage the commission and the member states to further promote a common approach to nature conservation throughout the european union, including in the outermost regions and in the overseas territories of the member states. i stress the importance of integrating the protection and conservation of biodiversity into the development, implementation and financing of all other european policies, including those on agriculture, forestry, fisheries, development, regional cohesion, energy, industry, transport, tourism, development cooperation, research and innovation. to make the union's sectoral and budgetary policies more coherent, ensure that they honour its binding commitments on the protection of biodiversity.

in writing. − the public sector and its relations with society have generated a great deal of analysis and discussion in recent years. increasing demand for public services, budgetary constraints, personnel costs and the new facilities offered by information technology have been challenges generating new concepts: 'online government', 'e-government', 'e-government'. the key element of the concept of 'e-government' is to improve the relationship and smooth the exchange of information between the public sector on the one hand and citizens and business on the other. e-government means providing public services in electronic format to citizens and businesses, a more efficient and cheaper alternative that would allow the government to be closer to citizens and to tailor its services to their requirements. i consider e-government to be one of the important manifestations of the information society, because it involves state institutions, public and private organisations and, above all, the citizen, whom it transforms into an e-citizen, directly, concretely and constructively involved in all areas of political, social, cultural, civic and moral life.

in writing. today, 9 may, in the ep plenary we are talking about the future of europe. in the elections that have taken place in the eu member states over the last year, citizens have voted for change. if we analyze the ideological meaning of this change, we see how in france the right was replaced by the left, and in spain it was the other way around. what do winners have in common? the more or less populist promises to end austerity policies and to meet the expectations of those who want to maintain the european welfare state that takes care of everyone. the question now is whether, after the crisis, we can return to the european welfare state of the late 20th century. the eu can no longer exist as just an economic union and a single market as albion wants, it can no longer stand as just a 20th century intergovernmental union of nation states. it's going to fall apart. the eu must become a federal europe, a europe of regions and communities, with clear powers for its institutions in brussels, balanced by clear accountability for the eurocrats to the 500 million european citizens. and the undisputed democratic deficit of today's european construction can only be addressed by strengthening the role of the ep.
i congratulate mrs niebler and the shadow rapporteurs on the report they have worked on and on the negotiations with the council on the basis of the mandate given by the itre commission. the regulations of 2007 and 2009 and, in particular, this regulation, aim at consumer protection and flexibility for roaming providers by introducing euro-tariffs for voice, sms and data roaming. however, today there is no internal telecommunications market as long as there are significant differences between national prices and roaming prices. the digital agenda's objective 101 is to achieve convergence between domestic and roaming charges by 2015. the ultimate objective should therefore be to eliminate the difference between national and roaming tariffs, thereby establishing an internal market for mobile communications services. i have argued in my amendments that users living in border regions should not be charged excessively high prices for accidental roaming. roaming providers should take reasonable measures to protect customers against the charging of roaming charges when they are in the territory of their member state. national regulatory authorities should also take appropriate measures to mitigate those problems. the sale of regulated roaming services separately from domestic mobile communications services is an intermediate measure necessary to increase competition and to lower roaming charges for customers, with a view to achieving an internal market for mobile communications services in which there is ultimately no difference between domestic and roaming charges. we call for the regulation to be revised in 2016 to ensure adequate consumer protection if convergence between domestic and roaming charges is not achieved by then.
madam president, the common market and freedom of movement are some of the cornerstones of the construction of europe and yet the citizens of europe have to pay an extra fee for communicating with each other when travelling within the eu, which i believe is unacceptable. the roaming regulation in this negotiated form achieves some quite positive results in terms of reduced price caps for voice calls, data services and sms. however, the way to a european single market for mobile communication, which has to be our ultimate goal, is still far from being reached. in my view the extra costs for roaming are not justified by any technical reasons. they create fake and unjust commercial borders; they represent an actual impediment to the free competition among network operators that would lead to better services, lower prices, more consumption and more growth in the european union. the biggest improvement that this new regulation will bring in terms of benefits for the european citizen is the significant cut in the price of data services. this was a top priority for the s&d group and i am pleased that such an important point has been agreed upon. however, i am quite disappointed that not enough attention has been given to the net neutrality issue as i believe that customers should be allowed to access any internet services from their phones without discrimination. the overall outcome of the negotiations with the council is satisfactory. however, i would like to remind you that this parliament should push for the creation of a single market for telecommunications and that the eu must become a roaming free area.
first, let me give my colleague niebler a little credit. indeed, this conversation should have been had much earlier. but it's good that we're doing it now. the last price cap for roaming services was in july 2009 and since then, technological developments have been significant. and roaming has gone unnoticed and we're still paying the same prices in 2012. it's often, frankly, much cheaper to take a taxi and get to a destination than to look on the internet, on a normal map, for the destination, whether it's a hotel or other destinations. data transfer is playing an increasingly important role in communication, whether we're talking about business or private. that is why i think that this price limitation should have come earlier, it is good that it is coming now and i think that through these measures taken at european level, we can bring about a standardization in terms of communication systems at european level in the 27 states.
in writing. the regulation of roaming charges is one of the essential elements of the completion of the single market for electronic communications. this proposal for a regulation will help to improve the welfare of mobile users in terms of price, choice, quality and safety. at present, excessive roaming prices and reduced use of roaming services within the eu due to high levels of tariffs are not serving either the european consumer or the european economy. for these reasons, i welcome the introduction of a retail price cap for mobile data services for the first time. the new regulation will also extend the obligation for mobile telecommunications companies to notify their own users when their roaming bill exceeds eur 50 and also to inform users about the price of the roaming services offered.
in writing. i consider the agreement on the reduction of roaming charges within the eu to be optimal in the context of the structural problems generated by roaming services. thus, as from 1 july 2012, the charges for calls made in a member state other than the country of origin may not exceed 29 cents per minute and those for incoming calls may not exceed 8 cents per minute. limiting the impact of high roaming charges requires a shift from a monopoly held by mobile operators to sustainable competition designed to encourage investment and job creation. this will enable users to choose their mobile operator for the period of their stay abroad. i would like to draw attention to the situation of customers living in border regions who pay excessively high bills due to accidental roaming. to this end, it is necessary for roaming and mobile providers to warn users immediately of the roaming of their phone. freedom of movement within the european union must be coupled with the freedom to communicate at affordable rates throughout europe.

the reporter. − i am the rapporteur for the decentralised agencies of the european union for 2010 and for the public-private partnership enterprises. 24 centralised agencies and 7 public-private partnership enterprises are subject to the discharge procedure. for three agencies, i propose to postpone discharge, mainly for reasons related to conflicts of interest and public procurement. a few words about the importance of conflicts of interest: conflicts between public tasks and the private interests of those in public office have increased through the collapse of the barriers between the public and private sectors, through public-private partnerships, through the exchange of personnel between the two sectors. this has created grey areas and potential conflicts of interest for those in public office. a conflict of interest arises when a public official has to make decisions that may affect his private interests. if not identified and managed properly, conflicts of interest can distort the allocation of public resources, human resources policy, lead to waste of public money and to a decline in citizens' trust in european public institutions. conflicts of interest should therefore be analysed and sanctioned in the course of the discharge procedure. it is our role to look at conflicts of interest when we review and decide on the discharge of all the european institutions. i recommend that you postpone the discharge to the european food safety authority. it's an agency involved in the licensing of the food and drink that we consume every day. our health also depends on the decisions of this authority. that's why the conflicts of interest in this agency, mainly in the board, in the board, are worrying. there are many examples that have been made public. i'll give you just one very recent one: diana banati, who on may 8th, two days ago, joined an institute funded by the food industry and, at the request of the authority, resigned as director and board member. there are other cases on the board of the food safety authority, for example, like the ones in the expert groups. in addition, the costs of board member meetings in 2010 were over eur 6 000 per person per meeting, the highest cost among all agencies. the fda is the second agency i'm proposing to delay discharge. and there are conflicts of interest issues, and this agency is extremely important in the application process, in the approval process, in the authorization process for the drugs that we use, that come into the market. the agency has drawn up a plan to avoid, to prevent conflicts of interest, but what i propose to parliament is to see how this plan is applied, because application, implementation is the key issue. if it's applied correctly, of course, in the
