in writing. - i voted in favour of amending the regulation on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community, given the incompatibility of article 9.5 of the basic anti-dumping regulation with articles 6.10, 9.2 and 18.4 of the wto anti-dumping agreement and article xvi:4 of the wto agreement. given that the proposal is in line with the treaty on the functioning of the european union and respects the principle of proportionality, i consider the amendment to be welcome. the wto agreements contain no legal basis to support the provisions of article 9.5. exporting producers with activities in non-market economy countries should not be required to demonstrate that they meet certain criteria in order to be granted it. however, certain special situations must be taken into account when determining the degree of compatibility of the articles for the imposition of a dumping margin and a single anti-dumping duty. thus, although exporters are legally distinct entities, they sometimes need to be treated as a single entity.
in writing. - dumping must be limited to simple selling practices at low prices as a result of reduced costs or higher productivity. in this respect, the key criterion is not in fact the relationship between the exported product price and its price on the importing country's market, but the relationship between the exported product price and its normal value. thus, a product is considered to be dumped if its export price to the european union is lower than the comparable price, in the ordinary course of trade, for the like product in the exporting country. the application of any anti-dumping duty also requires the presence of a second key element: the material injury suffered by the community industry, whether caused to an industry present in the eu, the threat of injury or the substantial delay in the creation of such an industry. i consider that anti-dumping measures cannot be applied if it is found that it is not in the eu interest to impose them. to this end, all interests at community level as a whole, including those of the community industry, users and consumers, must be taken into account. all interested parties shall be given the opportunity to make their views known.
in writing. − i voted in favour of repealing the regulation on the application of restrictions on imports of certain steel products from the russian federation, as maintaining quantitative limits on these imports is in breach of wto rules, taking into account that the russian federation became a wto member in 2011. i believe that with russia's accession to the wto, trade between russia and the european union will improve significantly and develop in accordance with the existing provisions in the bilateral agreements. the eu will thus benefit from greater access to the russian market, leading to an increase in the number and value of exports. moreover, as a result of the export tax reduction, competitiveness will improve and consumers will benefit. i support the need for closer surveillance and the removal of the other existing barriers to trade between russia and the eu.
in writing. − the bilateral relationship between the european union and the russian federation is based on the fundamental values and principles of democracy, human rights, the rule of law and the market economy, and its legal basis is the partnership and cooperation agreement (pca). the agreement entered into force in 1997 for an initial period of 10 years, automatically renewed annually after 2007. it sets out the main common objectives, the institutional framework for bilateral contracts and calls for activities and dialogue in a number of areas. in addition to the pca provisions, there are a number of sectoral and international agreements and other mechanisms for cooperation. steelmaking and textiles are the main sectors covered by bilateral trade agreements. the latest steel agreement stipulated that it would end if russia became a member of the world trade organisation, which it did on 16 december 2011. in view of the above, i support the rapporteur's position on this draft resolution.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because widening access to eu legislation is an important element in ensuring transparency and communication with citizens. the electronic edition of the official journal of the european union (oj) being considered as the official, authentic, up-to-date and complete version will also result in increased legal certainty. at the same time, this measure will avoid the considerable costs associated with the publication of the printed version of the oj, representing a welcome saving for the community budget. in the current economic context and in the light of the difficulties faced by a number of member states and citizens, it is important that the european institutions eliminate unnecessary or avoidable expenditure by identifying practical ways to save money. the electronic publication of the european union oj is an example that should be followed by other similar measures and initiatives.
in writing. − the official journal of the european union is a daily periodical in all the official eu languages and publishes all eu decisions and legislative proposals, in print and electronic form. the 2007 judgment of the court of justice, which held that legal rights cannot be invoked and obligations cannot be applied on the basis of the electronic version of the oj, leads to suspicions as to the precise content of eu legal acts currently available in the eur-lex database. consulting the printed editions of the official journal is a time-consuming, costly and, not least, rarely used process. i welcome all reforms aimed at increasing legal certainty and reducing the cost of access for citizens and businesses, especially in this period of economic crisis affecting the eu.
in writing. − it can be seen from the events i have attended that i fully encourage the use of modern technologies, especially in view of the rapid pace at which society is developing and the need for eu citizens to be constantly informed about the decisions taken within these institutions. the publication of the official journal in electronic form is a timely proposal that meets the demands of the population, and the delay in such a decision can only be a mistake. i would stress that not only is immediate access to documents important, but also the absence of uncertainty about their content. all those who consult the electronic edition should be assured of the authenticity and veracity of the information. the most important aspect of this proposal, in my view, is to give the same official status to texts published in electronic form as to those which have appeared in print.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the draft council regulation on the electronic publication of the official journal of the european union. the proposal for a regulation provides that electronic publication will be equivalent to the legally required publication of the official journal of the european union (oj). in 2011, the commission adopted the proposal for a regulation to increase legal certainty by broadening access to eu law and allowing everyone to rely on the electronic edition of the oj as the official, authentic, up-to-date and complete version. the proposal also addresses the technical requirements that electronic publishing must meet to be equivalent to compliant publishing and sets out the competences of the publications office of the european union (ojeu) in this area. however, in exceptional and temporary cases of unforeseen interruption of electronic publication, the printed edition will have legal value. i believe that legal certainty should be increased and citizens' access to european union legal acts improved. today, almost everyone only consult the electronic form of eu legislation. consulting the printed editions of the official journal is a time-consuming, costly and rarely used process.
in writing. − regional airports are vital for the eu's territorial cohesion and social and economic development. i believe that they have the potential to attract new business and also offer many opportunities for regional tourism as well as specialised freight transport. an integration of regional airports into the ten-t will create opportunities for private financing in airport infrastructure and encourage member states to invest in integrated land connections with major airports. in order to improve the overall quality of service, certain practices of low-cost airlines such as certain unavoidable charges on the main price of their airline tickets or the imposition of extremely strict rules on the number and size of hand luggage should be regulated.
in writing. − regional air transport plays an important role in the development of eu regions because of its many economic and social benefits, through economic and tourism development, increased mobility of citizens and job creation. regional airports are open gates to regions both within the eu and externally. they improve connectivity and access to eu regions, helping to increase their attractiveness. at the same time, regional airports can help to relieve congestion at busy airports. intermodal transport solutions help to develop transit between airports. the commission and the competent authorities should give priority to existing regional airports. their efficiency and development by improving the necessary infrastructure would also bring short-term benefits in terms of investment costs. the importance of diversifying regional airports lies in increasing passenger safety. the availability of alternative airports in the event of deteriorating weather conditions or in terms of the safety of take-offs and landings must be a priority for airport authorities in the eu.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the bradbourn report, in particular because of the commission's request to simplify the way in which airports with less than 500000 passengers per year can access state aid. they also support the inclusion of a larger number of regional airports in the ten-t network. such a measure can stimulate economic growth in european regions. at the same time, i consider the provision in recital (a) which excludes the application of the proposed measures to regional airports serving mainly a capital city to be at least questionable. these airports must be granted similar conditions, any other situation being discriminatory.
in writing. − i voted for the report on the future of airports and regional air services in the eu, as regional airports contribute to economic development, industrial revitalisation and employment in their regions. regional airports with extensive connectivity to third countries and intra-european traffic and contributing to the multimodal nature of transport in their region, as well as regional airports that can serve to decongest traffic, should be included in the ten-t network planning. we are concerned about the single baggage rule and other restrictions on carry-on baggage imposed by certain airlines. such practices lead to a poor quality of service for passengers, constitute a breach of competition law and a breach of the obligation of transparency regarding the charges applicable to a ticket. we call on the commission to adopt a balanced approach when reviewing the aviation guidelines in order to create the conditions for a socially and economically viable development of regional air services, with a view to developing the infrastructure necessary to ensure intermodality, while ensuring the accessibility of these services to union citizens and taking into account the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on discharge 2010: general budget of the eu, european ombudsman. i welcome the fact that the ombudsman has set out key performance indicators in the 2010 action plan, as well as a central scoreboard which allows, on the basis of a system of benchmarks, to measure the ombudsman's work. the annual report on the ombudsman's activities in 2011 should contain a chapter on the measures taken on the basis of the european parliament's discharge resolution and a comprehensive table of all the human resources available to the european ombudsman, broken down by category, grade, sex, participation in training courses and nationality. i stress the importance of further increasing the number and proportion of inquiries completed in less than one year, and increasing the number and proportion of cases for which a decision on admissibility is to be taken within one month. these measures will help to increase the trust of european citizens in the european ombudsman. welcomes the audit carried out by the internal audit service in 2010, which took into account the comments made in 2009 and concluded that the management and control system is effective, subject to the implementation of the agreed measures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the discharge for the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2010, section ix european data protection supervisor. i welcome the fact that, on the basis of its audit work, the court of auditors estimates that, overall, the payments for administrative and other expenditure of the institutions and bodies for 2010 were free from material error, the error rate in the 'administrative expenditure' sector being estimated at 0,4%. i also welcome the fact that the european data protection supervisor corrected in 2010 and 2011 the errors mentioned in the 2009 insurance declaration and implemented the tools that contribute to improving the management of compensation. due to the profound changes in the way staff are organised in 2010, we request information on the results of the new organisation chart. in this respect, the european data protection supervisor should report in its annual activity report on the implementation of parliament's recommendations. we request that the 2011 annual activity report also contains a comprehensive table of all human resources available to the european data protection supervisor, broken down by category, grade, gender, participation in training courses and nationality.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report ‘2010 discharge: performance, financial management and control of eu agencies’, despite amendments which partially watered down the criticism in my report, in particular the one referring to the way the european court of auditors fulfilled its duties as external auditing body for the agencies. in my view, agencies need to reduce their running costs and follow a zero-based budgeting approach when drawing up their budgets: each agency budget must be based on its real current needs and not on its needs established years ago. it is also time for the commission to carry out an evaluation in order to detect occurrences of unnecessary or overlapping activities and to analyse the merger of some of the agencies. eu agencies should publish on their websites the lists of all contracts awarded over the last three years as well as the list of the management board members together with their declaration of interests and curriculum vitae. the same should be done for all persons in management positions in the agencies and for all experts and scientific guests. conflicts of interest have proved to be a serious concern in several agencies.
in writing. − i voted to grant discharge to the european aviation safety agency (easa) for the financial year 2010 as the agency plays an important role in establishing and maintaining a high and uniform level of civil aviation safety in europe. in 2010, the agency had eur 34 200 000 from the european union budget. the agency's budget was increased by 61% between 2007 and 2010, from eur 85 200 000 to eur 137 200 000, and its staff increased from 333 to 524. we regret that the court of auditors found irregularities in the recruitment and procurement procedures. we call on the commission to ensure that the agency properly applies union regulations and stress the importance of transparency in procurement and recruitment procedures. the court of auditors also stated that it had obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the annual accounts of the european aviation safety agency for the financial year 2010, and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions.
in writing. − the report on the 2010 discharge for the european environment agency provided for postponement of the discharge. i certainly voted for the postponement of the discharge, which i proposed as rapporteur. i have serious concerns towards this agency with regards to conflict of interest, public procurement, transparency and the way it spends the eu taxpayers' money. in 2010, the agency built a green façade that lasted only 5 months but cost more than 294 000 euro and yet no public tender was made. the agency will also spend 250 000 eur for media monitoring in the next 4 years. this is excessive, unjustified and disregards the taxpayers' money. conflicts of interest are a major problem in the agency. in 2010, while the eea executive director was a member of the international board of directors of earthwatch, 29 staff members of the agency, including the executive director, went for up to 10 days of research on different biodiversity projects in the caribbean or mediterranean managed by earthwatch to whom the agency paid a total of eur 33 791,28. moreover, worldwatch institute europe used the eea premises for its own activities without paying any rent.
in writing. − the report on the 2010 discharge for the european food safety authority provided for postponement of the discharge. i certainly voted in favour of this report, as rapporteur and the one who proposed the postponement of the discharge. the costs of the agency's management board are excessive although it is composed of only 15 members. in 2010, each meeting cost on average 92 630 euro, which represents an amount of 6 175 euro per member. the decisions of the agency are repeatedly challenged over cases of conflict of interest involving members of the management board and members of the experts' panels which come from or go to the food industry, or even are in both places at the same time. for instance, in september 2010 the chair of the management board was reported to be a member of the board of directors of the international life science institute (ilsi) - europe, a food lobby group, from where she stepped down in october 2010, only to accept a professional position at ilsi on 8 may 2012. a thorough screening of the declarations of interest submitted by the agency's staff, experts and members of the management board must be undertaken.
in writing. - i voted to postpone the discharge for the european environment agency, the european medicines agency and the european food safety authority, following the alarm signals regarding possible conflicts of interest and, in particular, the excessive expenditure attributed to them. the delay in the discharge is not a solution to these problems, but i believe it can be the starting point for a rigorous analysis of the way these agencies, and the other agencies, which are very numerous at european union level, operate, their costs and their usefulness.
in writing. − the report on the 2010 discharge for the european medicines agency provided for postponement of the discharge. i certainly voted in favour of this report as rapporteur and the one who proposed the postponement of the discharge. during the 2009 discharge procedure, the european parliament requested a multi-annual procurement plan from ema, which has not yet been adopted. moreover, the management board refused a new payment system for the agency, hence the management board accepts and takes direct responsibility for very important risks, such as non-compliance with legislative requirements, the potential financial impact of the current remuneration system as well as reputation. serious weaknesses in terms of conflict of interests also remain. its approach on the scrutiny of declarations of interest is based on trust rather than on verification of the experts' declaration of interest published by the relevant national agencies. a genuine mechanism enabling proper scrutiny of the declarations of interest recently adopted by the agency must be implemented and show concrete results. the cv of its experts should be made available on its website. consumers and at the same time taxpayers should be aware of who, how and why drugs are recommended and used by citizens.
in writing. − the european maritime safety agency (emsa) provides technical assistance and support to the european union and its member states in the development and implementation of eu legislation on maritime safety, pollution from shipping and maritime security. its responsibilities also include oil spill prevention and response, vessel monitoring, and long-range vessel identification and tracking. in view of the new tasks conferred on the agency by the amendment of regulation (ec) no 1406/2002 establishing the agency, we ask the commission to increase the resources allocated to it. we call on the agency to ensure sound management of resources for the proper fulfilment of its new tasks under that regulation. we draw the agency's attention to the european parliament's resolution of may 2011 on the 2009 discharge for the performance, financial management and control of eu agencies and ask the agency to comply with the recommendations of this resolution. in the resolution, parliament called on the agency to: draw up a gantt chart as part of the programming for each of its operational activities; compare operations carried out in the year under discharge with those carried out in the previous year; improve planning and monitoring with a view to reducing the number of budgetary transfers; and apply public procurement procedures correctly.
in writing. - i voted for the discharge for the european agency for network and information security (enisa). the agency's mission is to ensure a high level of information and data security in the eu by supporting national authorities and eu institutions as an expert on information and data security. the agency also acts as a forum for the exchange of good practice, facilitating contacts between the eu institutions, national authorities and european ict businesses. the court of auditors stated that it had obtained reasonable assurances as to the reliability of the agency's annual accounts for the financial year 2010 and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. we welcome the fact that the agency has improved its transparency both in budget estimates and in the allocation of project responsibilities and has strengthened its procurement authorisation procedure at the level of financing decisions and the work programme. given the importance of the agency, the proposed amendment to the regulation establishing enisa, which gives new tasks to the agency, and the opinions of the court of auditors in previous years, we ask the agency to allocate the main share of both staff and expenditure to actions specific to information and data security.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the european railway agency for the financial year 2010. the agency contributes to the integration of european rail systems by enhancing rail transport safety and ensuring the possibility of non-stop crossing of eu member states' borders. in collaboration with the railway sector, national authorities, eu institutions and other bodies, the agency works to develop common and economically viable technical standards and safety measures and objectives. the agency also issues reports on railway safety in the eu and coordinates efforts to develop uniform signalling rules across europe. in the context of the financial crisis, optimising the use of budgetary resources is very important. we urge the commission and the agency to analyse and establish the actual budgetary needs for the fulfilment of all the agency's tasks. it is recalled that the agency has already carried over substantial funds from the financial years 2008 and 2009 to the following year. we consider that these serious breaches of the budgetary principle of annuality cannot be accepted in the future and that, in the event of a further breach of that budgetary principle, the next time discharge should be refused. in this regard, we request the agency to take the necessary corrective measures without delay.
in writing. − the financial crisis facing the european union requires special measures to ensure adequate protection of the financial interests of the union. i believe that a more rigorous implementation of fiscal policy has the potential to bring europe out of the crisis, in particular by reducing the size of the eu's underground economy, estimated at around one fifth of official gdp. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report to acknowledge the need to consolidate the fight against fraud, corruption, and economic crime. in april, the european parliament's special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering held its constitutive meeting; this is a good step forward, but its results will depend on finding concrete examples to argue for changes in law and practice. many challenges remain. member states should be made more accountable for the amount in irregularities that remain to be recovered; the commission and the member states should apply uniform systems of procurement, define and implement clear conditions for participation in public procurement, as well as transparency in criteria and decision-making on public procurement. we also need one-stop transparency: we need a single website that publishes all the beneficiaries of eu funds on the basis of standard categories of information to be supplied by all the member states in at least one working language of the union. otherwise we will be lost in a lot of diverse information in diverse languages that fails to provide an overall picture and cannot offer real transparency.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the protection of the european union's financial interests combating fraud annual report for 2010. in 2010, the financial impact of irregularities in the spending of european funds increased to eur 1.8 billion, compared with eur 1.4 billion in 2009. the financial impact on revenue is also higher: €393 million, compared to €357 million in 2009. according to statistics for 2010, about 70% of all irregularity reports were related to cohesion policy. we call on the commission and the member states to design, implement and periodically evaluate uniform procurement systems to combat fraud and corruption, to define and implement clear conditions for participation in public procurement. it is necessary to implement systems for reviewing public procurement decisions at national level, to ensure transparency and accountability in public finances and to adopt and implement risk management and internal control systems. we ask the commission for reliable statistical data on the extent of fraud and corruption, in particular tax and customs fraud, as well as on organised crime activities related to the misuse of eu funds.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on ‘roaming on public mobile communications networks within the union’ because the text makes for better discipline in the mobile communication market in the eu. it was necessary to find an agreement at first reading as the previous regulation was about to expire and that would have left europe’s mobile communication market without this discipline for the whole summer period. in particular, the regulation provides for cuts in the price caps for roaming on voice calls and text messages. but the most significant improvement achieved concerns data services. thanks to the fundamental contribution of the s&d group, citizens will enjoy significant price reductions when using internet services from abroad. i would reiterate, however, that our final goal must be the creation of a roaming-free europe, in which no artificial borders will prevent citizens from communicating with one another freely and cheaply, even when they travel or live in other european states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it brings additional legal clarity on chemicals, while ensuring greater involvement of the european chemicals agency in the application of the regulation on the export and import of dangerous chemicals. i appreciate that a good balance has been struck with regard to the prior informed consent procedure. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road, rail and inland waterway. at the same time, it will ensure that the eu's high standards in public health and the environment are further promoted, avoiding the substitution of products that meet lower standards in these areas. i also stress the importance of applying the measures on the classification, packaging and labelling of chemicals, in accordance with amendment no 14 to the european parliament's proposal.
in writing. - chemicals play a vital role in our society today. we use them every day, from medicine to cars and construction materials to toys. the eu's chemical industry is the third largest in the world, generating direct waste of hazardous chemicals. the regulation on the export and import of dangerous chemicals aims to promote joint responsibilities and cooperative efforts in the field of international transport of chemicals that present a risk in order to protect human health and the environment from potential harm. the regulation applies to all chemicals exported to other parties to the convention or other countries, unless these provisions conflict with any specific requirement of the parties or countries concerned, subject to the provisions of the classification, packaging and labelling of hazardous chemicals regulation. the eu is a world leader in environmental legislation and i believe it is our duty to maintain this position.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation concerning the export and import of dangerous chemicals. i did so because i believe that this report contains a balanced analysis of the role that the eu has to play in protecting human health and the environment, both within and outside europe. the eu, deeming health and environmental protection to be of fundamental importance for its citizens, has decided to extend the list of prohibited chemicals established by the international rotterdam convention. i welcome the rapporteur’s suggestion to oppose allowing exporters to trade the listed products when they have not received a response within 60 days from the importing countries, because this would create an exception that would be potentially harmful to the health and to the environment of those countries with weaker administrations. this goes against the purposes of the eu, and the rotterdam convention as well. it is important that that the eu carefully limits its derogations regarding the export of dangerous chemicals, since i believe it is our responsibility to ensure that the products we export do not have negative effects in other countries.
in writing. − a note of caution is required in the case of commercial transfer of chemicals between countries, as they involve risks to the environment and the population. but the commission's proposal to amend the pic (prior informed consent) regulation will only give manufacturers of substances banned or restricted by the eu the opportunity to sell their goods in countries with clear legislation on these transactions. we cannot allow, and i do not agree, that the ignorance of the governments of all the countries facing this situation endangers the health of their citizens. the only point in this proposal which i welcome is the clarification of the definitions in the regulation and the involvement of echa (european chemicals agency) in its application, but i consider it absolutely necessary to limit the derogations from the pic procedure allowed by the commission, in order to be consistent with the european union's duty to contribute to the creation of fair and beneficial partnership relations for all the parties, the participating states.
in writing. − i would like to thank our colleagues for their hard work on this dossier and to congratulate them on their successful negotiations with the member states. as well as transposing the rotterdam convention into eu law, this agreement reflects parliament’s additional concerns about the trade in dangerous chemicals. we are determined that the eu does not become complicit in the export of dangerous chemicals to countries which have not fully considered their impact and which may lack the capacity to use, store and dispose of them safely. i welcome the guarantees that this agreement provides, particularly with regard to those chemicals which are carcinogenic, mutagenic, or toxic for reproduction.
in writing. - i voted in favour of amending rules 87a and 88 of the rules of procedure of the european parliament, as this will clarify the modalities for the rapid adoption of delegated acts as well as implementing acts. the two new articles are important because they lay down the procedure to be followed in the case of a committee responsible. given that the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has substantially transformed the comitology procedure, i welcome the new article 87a, which provides for the procedure to be followed when the commission transmits a delegated act to parliament, and the new article 88, which provides for the modalities for the exercise of implementing powers. i also consider that the introduction of a new article 88a, which provides for specific provisions on procedures with associated committees or joint meetings, is necessary, as it complements the provisions laid down in the two preceding articles.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation to the commission amending regulation (ec) no 864/2007 on the law applicable to non-contractual obligations (rome ii). i believe that there should be legal remedies when people's freedom is violated, especially when their privacy and reputation are harmed. each member state must ensure that such remedies exist and are effective in the event of a breach of these rights. the rome ii regulation does not provide for the determination of the law applicable to infringements of the right to privacy and of rights relating to personality. we therefore ask the commission to submit a proposal to add to the rome ii regulation a provision determining the law applicable to non-contractual obligations arising from the infringement of the right to privacy and rights relating to personality, including defamation. in order to promote the public benefits of reducing litigation, improving access to justice, ensuring the proper functioning of the internal market and guaranteeing an appropriate balance between freedom of expression and the right to privacy, the commission should propose the establishment of a centre for the amicable settlement of cross-border disputes arising from infringements of privacy and personality rights, including slander, through an alternative dispute resolution mechanism.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the european union's trade and investment strategy in the southern mediterranean following the arab revolutions. through this report, the european union is sending a strong signal of support for the democratic aspirations expressed by the peoples of the southern mediterranean. i would also like to draw attention to the fact that some eu member states have not yet ratified their amendments to the agreement on the european bank for reconstruction and development. in view of the experience the bank has gained in eastern and southern europe and the potential usefulness it could have in the southern mediterranean, i believe that the decision to extend the mandate of the ebrd to the southern mediterranean basin needs to be ratified urgently by all eu member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the eu trade and investment strategy for the southern mediterranean following the arab spring revolutions, because i believe that a determined eu strategy for the development of economic and trade relations with these neighbouring countries is fundamental. since international trade is one of the exclusive competencies of the eu, given the importance of the euro-mediterranean strategy resulting from the barcelona process and in view of article 8 of the treaty on european union which states that the eu must develop a special relationship with neighbouring countries with the aim of establishing an area of prosperity and good neighbourliness, i believe that the european union has both the legal competence and the political responsibility to trigger a serious engagement in the area. i very much welcome the introduction of the ‘more-for-more’ principle, since it can represent a very effective tool to enable tailor-made and bottom-up strategies, which are fundamental for tackling the different economic and societal demands of the different southern mediterranean countries (smcs), while also ensuring that funding schemes, shaped according to the political and economic ambitions of smcs, are sufficiently effective.
in writing. − the arab spring was a landmark event and was driven by both people's aspirations for freedom and their desire to improve their living standards. at present, unrest in this region persists and is clearly linked to weaknesses in local economies. they are characterised by an unequal distribution of wealth, insufficient economic reforms, low capacity for job creation and a low level of regional trade integration. i believe that these countries need to reinvigorate their economies to achieve sustainable and inclusive economic growth, and that this requires much more consistent and fairer support from the eu for real economic development for the benefit of all. these countries should also be encouraged to create a strong legislative framework that is business and entrepreneurship friendly, giving a strong role to small and medium-sized enterprises, which play a key role in job creation.
in writing. − the european union has a duty to support the continuation and deepening of the reforms initiated in the arab states following the 'spring' of 2011. this support should include measures associated with the union's trade policy. however, i insist on the need to impose on farmers in these countries who wish to export to eu countries the same standards of food safety, the environment and animal welfare as are imposed on european farmers. any product that reaches european consumers' tables must meet these standards, which are the highest in the world, and at the same time extremely expensive.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the eu's trade and investment strategy in the southern mediterranean following the arab revolutions. a successful trade strategy for the region must strengthen the role of smes, which account for up to 30% of employment in some countries. more efforts are needed to reduce the high number of unregistered smes operating on the 'black market'. studies show that the proportion of illegal work (excluding agriculture) in some southern mediterranean countries is as high as 70%. i regret that smes and cooperatives have limited access to investment and insist on the need to provide them with adequate access to finance through the provision of reliable, accessible and easy-to-use microcredit and through the european investment bank (eib) counter-guarantee programmes. in this respect, i welcome the recent extension of the mandate of the ebrd. visa facilitation remains an issue for many representatives of smes from the southern mediterranean countries who intend to undertake visits to the eu institutions to attend meetings or training sessions, or for other business reasons. the eu has a responsibility to take the lead in facilitating the region's transition to democracy and economic integration, based on a free and fair market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft resolution, as it was indispensable to help clarify a dangerous situation of legal uncertainty, with a potential impact on farmers' activities and also of a nature to cause concern amongst public opinion. the complexity of the problem calls for a wide-ranging debate to follow, because the solutions called for in the resolution are necessary but not sufficient. parliament must send a strong signal in this respect, because no one can hold a patent on nature. however, neither the current debate nor any future one should turn into a battle against companies involved in research, and intellectual property rights based on sound arguments should not be called into question.
in writing. - today, 80 to 90% of world trade is carried by sea. the annual cost of piracy to the global economy ranges from 7 to 12 billion dollars, and the earnings of pirates in 2011 were estimated at 238 million dollars. pirate attacks in the arabian sea, the gulf of aden and the indian ocean have increased from 20 in 2006 to 219 in 2011, and the pirate area has now expanded to 1,300 nautical miles off the somali coast. the gulf of aden is one of the world's most important shipping routes, carrying about 12 percent of the world's oil. somali territorial waters and adjacent shores are largely ungoverned, allowing piracy to flourish and affect the international maritime domain. this combination of illegal activity and lawlessness is a breeding ground for high levels of instability, organised crime and other transnational threats.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on maritime piracy. maritime transport has been one of the cornerstones of economic development and prosperity in europe throughout its history, and over 80% of world trade is carried by sea. unfortunately, piracy is a threat to international security and regional stability and therefore the eu has a real interest in contributing to international maritime security and in combating piracy and its root causes. with 10 000 european ships crossing dangerous sea areas every year, piracy is both a matter of life and safety for people and an economic problem, as it endangers international maritime trade routes, with a significant negative impact on international trade. we demand immediate and effective measures to bring to justice and punish those suspected of acts of piracy. we urge third countries and eu member states that have not yet done so to transpose into their national legislation all the provisions laid down by the un convention on the law of the sea and the un convention for the suppression of unlawful acts against the safety of maritime navigation.
i would also like to congratulate my colleague, mr busuttil, on this report of his own initiative. the single market is an area on which all member states, without exception, agree that it is an asset of the european union to return to economic growth, to create jobs. however, the first condition for the proper functioning of the single market is that all member states transpose european rules into national legislation; and here, unfortunately, although progress has been made, we still have member states which are lagging behind in this transposition. the second condition is to have a good quality of transposition of european rules into national legislation - and here i must stress that we are hitting the first hurdle in the process of drawing up european legislation itself. every time we enter into a tripartite negotiation between the european parliament, the council and the european commission, we encounter the resistance of some member states to agree to the drawing up of tables of correspondence between the provisions of european rules and the provisions of national legislation in which these rules are transposed. these tables of correspondence are the first step to ensure competent monitoring of the quality of the transposition process. that is why i think we must have as a rule that any european legislation must be accompanied in the member states by the drawing up of these tables of correspondence.
the single market plays a crucial role in helping europe to emerge from economic stagnation. in this context, i would like to stress the importance of the timely transposition and correct implementation of european directives. i therefore consider that constant monitoring of member states is essential. this will create a framework for stronger regulation of the internal market. both businesses and citizens will be able to benefit from an improved single market. the latest internal market scoreboard shows that only a small number of member states have met their transposition targets. romania has unfortunately failed to meet its 1% target despite good results in march. our country must step up its efforts to transpose the union's rules.
member of the commission. − madam president, the issue of visa non-reciprocity continues to be a significant irritant in eu-canada relations. canada continues, as you know, to maintain the visa requirement for the citizens of bulgaria and romania, and also reintroduced it for czech citizens over two years ago. this is an issue we have raised numerous times in the course of the contacts we have with canada, on every relevant occasion and at all levels, in order to try to find a solution in partnership with the member states affected. the eu is the number one source region for asylum applications in canada. this is of course a serious concern, and we know it could have potential negative effects on the successful conclusion and ratification of several important agreements with canada, such as the comprehensive economic and trade agreement (ceta) and the strategic partnership agreement. visa-free travel between the eu and canada does not fall within the scope of the ceta negotiations, and ceta has not been directly used as a way of putting pressure on canada. however, the eu negotiators have repeatedly, in the margins of the negotiations, made it clear to their canadian counterparts that this issue is important for the eu, and decisive for the member states concerned. it has been pointed out to the canadian negotiators that such measures are in contradiction with the spirit of an agreement like the ceta, which tries to bring the eu and canada more closely together. the commission welcomes the draft asylum reform proposed in canada. once this is adopted and in force, it should act as a deterrent to unfounded applications and lead canada to lift the visa requirement for czech citizens. we are ready to explore with canada, in close cooperation with the member states concerned, possible additional measures to help reduce unfounded asylum applications, and we plan to set up a joint working group on this issue. in the case of romania and bulgaria, full accession to the schengen area will be an important factor with regard to canada’s position on visas. the commission will shortly present its seventh visa reciprocity report. this will include the canadian issue and will set out the future approach. our previous report, in 2010, concluded that the eu was ‘confronted with the limits’ of the existing reciprocity mechanism. in the ongoing negotiations on the amendment of regulation no 539/2001, the commission fully supports improvements to the reciprocity mechanism to ensure solidarity among the member states, provided that these are legally and institutionally sound and do not conflict with the commission’s right of initiative. a better reciprocity mechanism should enable the eu to exert quicker and more sustained influence over relevant third countries. all existing countries would be re-examined by the commission under this new, more efficient mechanism. the commission hopes that the legislative negotiations on all aspects of the proposal will proceed quickly, allowing agreement to be reached in the course of the danish presidency.
on behalf of the epp group. the european union and canada have special status relations. however, citizens of three member states need a visa to enter canada. this undermines the common european visa policy, which is based on reciprocity and is designed to ensure equal treatment for all union citizens. member states shall participate on an equal footing in the comprehensive economic and trade agreement with canada. this agreement is decisive for the future of economic relations between the european union and canada and will establish the future legal framework for the development of these relations. under this agreement, canada treats all member states equally. but when it comes to granting visas to enter canada or equal treatment when it comes to visa elimination, canada is not as consistent. a double standard is applied and criteria are not sufficiently clear and transparent. new legislation on the canadian asylum system discourages asylum seekers from union countries. it is an additional argument that the maintenance of visas for the three member states is unjustified. the commission will soon, later this year, seek parliament's assent to the comprehensive economic and trade agreement with canada. the lack of equal treatment for all union citizens with regard to visa-free travel to canada creates clear reservations about voting and it is not impossible that the the ceta agreement currently under negotiation is a step forward in the trade and economic relations between the european union and canada. however, it is also a symbol of a great paradox and a serious inconsistency on the part of the european union. under this agreement, goods and services produced in romania, bulgaria, and the czech republic will move freely in canada, but without the citizens of these countries having the same right. in other words, goods produced in romania, bulgaria or the czech republic are unfortunately more important than the citizens of these member states themselves. it is an abnormal and discriminatory situation which cannot be accepted and which also demonstrates the inability of the european commission to ensure equal rights for european citizens. also speak of a lack of good cooperation on the part of canada. while in the case of the czech republic the reason invoked has discriminatory tendencies towards an ethnic group, in the case of romania canada artificially maintains a high refusal rate to justify non-inclusion in the visa waiver programme. numerous romanian citizens, and i will mention here only those who agreed to have their names made public: maria dalcu, cosmin dragoi or nicolae ion, have complained to us about the unjustified way in which canadian consulates have refused their visa applications. the cases are far more numerous and even make me question the good faith of the canadian authorities involved. of course, there are also positive signs from the canadian authorities, whom i have had the opportunity to meet in several official delegations. during my most recent visit to ottawa earlier this month, i received assurances from both the federal minister of immigration and members of the federal parliament that the visa problem would be resolved once the new immigration law was passed in june. however, real progress is very slow, and even if the new law does come into force it is unclear when and if visas will be eliminated for romania, bulgaria and the czech republic, as other conditionalities could be used to further block visa-free access to canada for citizens of the three countries. i would like to stress once again that the issue of visas must not be left on the back burner by either canada or the european commission, but must be a priority on the agenda of bilateral relations. as i said, goods and services can't be more important than our own citizens. it is our role as representatives of these european citizens to ensure that their rights take precedence over any other economic considerations. that is why i want to end by saying very clearly that the ratification of the ceta agreement may also depend on progress in lifting visas for romanian, bulgarian and czech citizens.

crucial, and we fully share the view of the rapporteur that any legislation at eu level must fully respect the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. we know – and it has been clear from the debate here – that criminal law is a sensitive area, with quite substantial differences between the different member states. this has to be taken into account. because of that, it is crucial that we ensure full respect of the rights guaranteed by the charter of fundamental rights and the european convention on human rights for all eu criminal law legislation. we need to understand each other’s systems better in order to be able to assess how we can bring them closer together where this is necessary, while respecting the different legal systems and traditions in all member states. eu criminal law to strengthen the enforcement of eu policies is only needed in selected areas, but it can provide significant added value. we have seen this for example in the context of environmental crime, where two important directives were adopted in 2008 and 2009. these were the first instruments adopted on criminal law in the ordinary legislative proposal. the fruitful cooperation between the commission and parliament on these files has set an example for future work. we also see the importance of common eu rules when it comes to discussing proposals for criminal law measures to fight insider dealing and market manipulation. it is clear that the eu financial markets can only have investors’ confidence and trust if we send a strong signal in the form of common rules. in addition to to legislate common minimum rules on definitions of offences and sanctions. much has been achieved in relation to the latter in the post-lisbon period, specifically with the adoption of directives on the fight against trafficking in human beings as well as the fight against sexual exploitation of children. negotiations are being finalised regarding the cybercrime directive, and the newly-adopted proposal on the harmonisation of confiscation laws is about to be negotiated. all these initiatives have so far contributed to the development of treaty provisions contributing, inter alia, to a pragmatic interpretation of the concept of common minimum rules in both areas, and they are important frames of reference for further development of criminal law at eu level. putting in place a coherent eu criminal policy requires further reflection and discussion on many legal issues. the european commission has just set up an expert group which will meet for the first time in june, and we will be happy to report once they have met. it will be composed of experienced academics and practitioners in the field. this expert group will be a forum to discuss the challenging and difficult questions which arise when the eu considers criminal law measures and advises on the best way forward. we fully share the approach set out in the resolution. for instance, our criminal law communication also supports the idea of simpler language to guide eu legislators when they draft criminal law provisions. so the commission’s communication last year, and this report – which has received considerable support here – are the starting point for the shaping of a common eu criminal policy, and i look forward to working with parliament and moving further towards a common goal: a true area of freedom, security and justice.

mr president, i voted in favour of the report on the eu approach to criminal law. i support the application of the principle of mutual recognition in practice – not so much to extend the scope of eu harmonised law but rather to promote cooperation between judiciaries which must be equally reliable and share the same level of quality and integrity. i would like to make a comment following what i heard from my british colleagues in particular. as an mep from a new member state, i want to change my domestic judicial system for the better, and it is in my interest to look at judicial systems which work better and are long-established and proven over hundreds of years, so that is why i am voting for eu-level cooperation, through which best practices can be imported into the new member states.

in writing. − the strategy highlights all threats to the union, from terrorism and organised crime to cybercrime and drug, arms and human trafficking. in addition, natural as well as man-made disasters such as forest fires are taken into account, and there is also an emphasis on coordination in the face of a challenge to citizens across the union. an important objective is to prevent terrorism and to combat radicalisation and recruitment of islamist militants. this would be achieved by developing a policy for the extraction and analysis of financial messaging data within the eu, the eu terrorist finance tracking programme (tftp) (2011), establishing a common european network to increase public awareness of radicalisation and adopting measures to counter violent extremist propaganda (2011), strengthening the eu transport security policy (2011). the strategy focuses on preventing these phenomena, both through an efficient exchange of information between the union's member states and through actions to identify their causes.
in writing. − i voted for the european union internal security strategy because the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon further strengthened the area of freedom, security and justice (afsj) with regard to fundamental rights and the different legal systems and traditions of the member states, and because policies in this area are a shared competence between the union and the member states, in accordance with the treaty provisions, and the treaty of lisbon has firmly anchored eu security policy in a specific eu rule of law, laying the foundations for the development of a security agenda, deeply shared by the eu and the member states and subject to democratic control at european and national level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the european union’s internal security strategy because i strongly believe that the ever more globalised criminal activities have to be combated as a matter of urgency with a joint effort by all the european member states. this report, by clearly addressing the logic of subsidiarity driving the eu treaty regarding criminal matters, calls for an improved synergy between the internal and external aspects of security and highlights the importance of ensuring that measures implementing the iss are in compliance with union’s rights obligations. i also very positively welcome the capacity of the report to clearly explain how border management and human mobility are not just security issues, but key features of a wider political strategy, that have to involve the security dimension as well as immigration, asylum and development policies. in this sense, free movement and fundamental rights maintain their central importance for the application iss dispositions: the eu, as an area of freedom and justice, must keep these as leading principles.
in writing. − to counter major threats to internal security, the european union needs a unified, integrated approach. a strategy is therefore needed to provide a climate of increased security for every european citizen, but this security requires respect for common values and priorities, respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, the rule of law and democracy. the key elements of ensuring a secure environment for european citizens must be the involvement of the european institutions and political, economic and social actors in security strategies, the strengthening of mechanisms to prevent crime, terrorism and criminality, and cooperation and solidarity between member states. concurrently, concrete action is needed to promote democracy, peace and stability in the european union's neighbourhood, thus facilitating the creation of a common space of stability, security and progress. i would point out that all measures to improve security must focus on the main beneficiary: the european citizen!
in writing. − the report proposes a harmonisation of criminal law in the member states with a view to achieving a common legal culture in the fight against crime. criminal law differs from other legal fields in that, by definition, it restricts certain human rights concerning the fundamental freedoms of accused and/or convicted persons. often, even if a person is not convicted, the criminal investigation itself can have a stigmatizing effect, so many people will tend to believe that there are no rumors without a real cause. to facilitate future cooperation it is essential that the institutions agree on a certain type of common framework. such a framework could include a set of principles governing any criminal law instrument. i also believe that such a framework should contain precise guidelines on the internal procedures within each institution in order to ensure a coherent approach.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the eu's approach to criminal law. in order to facilitate cooperation in the future, it is essential that the institutions agree on a certain type of common framework. such a framework could usefully include a set of principles governing any criminal law instrument. in addition, model provisions may be added, as included, for example, in the council conclusions of november 2009. such a framework could serve as a basis for the preparation of impact assessments by the european commission and could contribute to the development of appropriate legal analyses for the council and parliament. in addition, it could contain precise guidelines on internal procedures within each institution, with a view to ensuring a coherent approach.
in writing. − the current rules on consumer rights are insufficient and a better strategy for strengthening the rights of vulnerable people is needed. the report suggests solutions for troubled sectors such as finance, transportation and the internet. in the transport sector, despite existing legislation, travellers still frequently encounter difficulties when their journey is cancelled or delayed, particularly for disabled people. i believe that the situation of vulnerable consumers, in particular those with reduced mobility and disabilities, should be taken into account in the planned review of eu legislation on travellers' rights. my view is that the development of such a strategy not only contributes to the social inclusion of these consumers, but also to the advancement towards a more just and tolerant society.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because consumer protection is always an important topic of debate and for this, certain measures and regulations must be taken by the eu. in this regard, it is imperative that product safety standards exist and that measures are introduced to protect the rights and interests of the consumer, in particular against misleading advertising that gives the consumer an image of the product that is not in line with reality. i consider it appropriate to examine the sectors which present a higher degree of consumer vulnerability and which require a higher degree of protection. these include financial (the price and quality of the product must be presented in a fair and sufficiently clear way), food (controlling advertising so that it truly reflects the product and its benefits), transport or the internet. the consumer must also be given the means to enjoy fully the benefits of a liberalised market, allowing him to make an informed choice of the most attractive offers. lastly, in order to increase consumer confidence in the internal market, it is essential to ensure that there is adequate access to judicial and alternative remedies, the development of which is indispensable.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report concerning a strategy for strengthening the rights of vulnerable consumers, because i believe it is essential to provide an adequate, and therefore updated, approach to consumer protection. this report does precisely this: it calls for an adaptation of the definition of vulnerable consumers which is synchronised with the changing nature of consumption in europe, not only regarding the goods that are consumed but also the evolving categories of consumers. given the extraordinary importance of the internal market for the european union’s economy and growth, a solid and trustworthy legal basis for consumer protection must imperatively be established. europe should provide itself with effective legislative means to avoid any form of abuse towards its citizens, in particular the most vulnerable ones. however, it is also fundamental that a right balance between individual freedom and consumer choices is struck. the sectors identified by the report, namely finance, food, transport, internet, free markets and access to justice, will have to be carefully regulated according to the driving principle of this dossier: consumers are susceptible to becoming vulnerable consumers over the course of their lives.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on a strategy to strengthen the rights of vulnerable consumers and i appreciate that the observations in this report are essential and must be taken into account in future regulations as soon as possible. the fact that less than 50% of consumers feel informed and protected, according to the results of the latest eurobarometer, is particularly worrying. another figure mentioned in the report is also quite alarming - 70% of the websites of financial institutions and companies make fundamental errors about the products offered and the costs are presented in a misleading way. in these circumstances, the problems of vulnerable consumers must be subject to strict regulation and dissuasive penalties.
in writing. − i voted for the report on strengthening the rights of vulnerable consumers. market liberalisation has increased competition, which can be to the advantage of consumers if they are properly informed and can compare prices and choose their suppliers. the lack of transparency in key markets, including in the energy and transport sectors, can lead to increased difficulties for consumers, in particular in identifying the right tariff for their needs, switching suppliers and understanding the elements invoiced. i call on the commission and the member states to take appropriate measures to ensure that all consumers have access to clear, easy to understand and comparable information on tariffs, conditions and remedies and that they can easily switch suppliers. despite existing legislation, vulnerable consumers continue to face difficulties when travelling. we call on the commission and the member states to take the necessary measures to ensure a good supply of information and quick access to both complaint procedures and complaint-resolution mechanisms on travellers' rights. we ask that in these procedures the situation of vulnerable consumers, in particular persons with reduced mobility, be taken into account.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that binding rules on the issuance of euro coins are needed to guarantee greater transparency. as euro coins circulate throughout the euro area, their characteristics are a matter of common interest to the member states. i would point out that too many notes and coins in circulation could lead to inflation. and the ecb's role is to ensure stability. in this context, the european central bank must control the issuance of euro coins. i would stress that reducing the number of commemorative coins will increase their value, while simplifying administrative formalities. i also believe that member states should be able to issue collector coins, which are different from circulation coins.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the issue of euro coins. although the issuance of 1 and 2 euro banknotes would reduce the number of 1 and 2 euro coins in circulation, the use of such banknotes would also bring benefits to member states. the issue of 1 and 2 euro banknotes would increase the currency's maneuverability and acceptance and have a positive influence on european tourism without reducing the value of the other euro coins in circulation. the issuance of 1 and 2 euro banknotes would also increase the value of euro collector coins. the reduction in the number of commemorative coins in circulation simplifies administration and, in addition, increases the value of those commemorative coins by making them rarer.
in writing. − given the degree of circulation and use of the euro in the eu member states, and the clear definitions of the legal framework in which this process will take place, i support the issuance of commemorative and collector coins of 1 and 2 euros. i also believe that one way of optimising the currency is to print banknotes of the same value. the most important aspect that this change would serve is in relation to the maneuverability of these banknotes. often, tourists in a country that uses the euro find it difficult to automatically distinguish between the two because of the similarities in shape and color. we could help tourists in a practical way by this amendment, thus bringing an advantage to the member states.
in writing. − in this time of crisis, the role of the single market is crucial to europe's exit from economic stagnation. but whenever one or more member states fail to transpose eu rules into national law within the timeframe, a vacuum is created in the eu legal framework, leading to fragmentation. the economic interests of all member states may therefore be affected if a member state fails to fulfil its obligations. today, the internal market scoreboard shows that there is an urgent need for member states to step up their efforts to transpose eu rules. in the last reference period, 16 of the 27 member states failed to meet the target of a transposition deficit of no more than 1% set by eu heads of state or government in 2007. this means that, on average, 1.2% of the internal market directives whose transposition deadline has expired are currently not transposed into national law.
in writing. − i supported this report because it is a comprehensive and high-quality report, offering a number of useful recommendations for improving the governance of the single market and for improving the performance of single market support services. i firmly believe, as i have said on other occasions, that the relaunch of the single market is one of the solutions to overcoming the crisis and returning to growth. i would stress once again that the member states must take more seriously the transposition of legislation on the single market, legislation to which they have directly contributed. without proper implementation, even the most effective legislation will not produce the expected results. for this reason, i think we need an even more ambitious target than the 1% for the compliance deficit, 0.5%. it is simply a matter of political responsibility on the part of the member states and of respecting the word given in the council. finally, i fully support the report's recommendations on internal market support services. i believe that they need to be further developed and promoted more vigorously so that citizens and businesses are aware of their existence and use them more widely.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the scoreboard for the internal market. several instruments have been created to further encourage the completion of the single market and to measure the contributions of each member state to this objective. the single market scoreboard is one such tool that encourages member states to improve the quality and timeliness of transposition of single market directives. in its latest internal market scoreboard, the european commission highlights that malta has the best record on the timely transposition of single market directives, while the czech republic is at the bottom of the list, although making steady progress.
in writing. − the financial and economic crisis has affected all sectors of our economy, destabilising businesses and the workforce and reducing the purchasing power of millions of european consumers. by allowing the negative effects to be absorbed, the single market is one of the eu's main assets in the face of this crisis and will help us to get out of the situation we are in. this is why constant and frequent monitoring of member states' progress through the scoreboard is one of the key factors in encouraging them to step up their efforts. i also believe that the scoreboard will speed up the transposition of the single market directives, both in terms of quality and timeliness, and we will thus benefit from all the benefits of the single market, including more growth and more jobs.
in writing. − i voted for the report on the internal market scoreboard because it is a tool that encourages member states to improve the transposition of single market directives in terms of quality and timeliness. the publication of the scoreboard contributes to strengthening the transposition of union legislation by providing objective and substantive data on the transposition and implementation of those rules by the member states. more precise information on the quality of transposition is needed to identify the causes of the lack of transposition of the legislation. 85 directives remain untransposed in at least one member state. two directives exceeded the transposition deadline by more than two years, thus directly breaching the 'zero tolerance' target set in 2007, and the number of incorrectly transposed directives remains at an average of 0.8%, despite the fact that in the single market act the commission stressed the need for a clear and well-established non-compliance policy. we call on the commission to support member states in the transposition of eu legislation by developing new tools such as transposition guidelines and a transposition assistance centre. completing the internal market by effectively transposing existing and new legislation can effectively combat the economic, financial and social crisis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on women in turkey in 2020. violence against women is one of turkey's most acute problems. every day, two or three women are killed by their husbands, friends, families or ex-husbands. the current legislation, law 4320, has shortcomings such as the lack of a mechanism to immediately remove domestic violence offenders from the vicinity of the woman who has been subjected to this violence. in addition, there is not always a consensus among police, prosecutors and judges as to the scope of the law and the punishment to be applied to the one who has resorted to violence. it is essential, in addition to amending the law to implement more effective and immediate remedies in cases involving domestic violence, to ensure a uniform interpretation and application of this law across all authorities involved in its implementation.
