in writing. − i voted for the amendment of the rules of procedure of the european parliament as regards the implementation of the european citizens' initiative. the citizens' initiative is a powerful tool available to citizens, which aims to give them the same rights of political initiative as those already enjoyed by the council of the european union and the european parliament. the aim of the initiative is to provide citizens with a means of bringing to the attention of the european institutions concrete issues that they consider important and that they consider to be lacking in attention or support. the european parliament will be able to contribute to these objectives by using all the means at its disposal to support the citizens' initiatives considered eligible, in particular by organising public hearings. to this end, it is necessary to amend the rules of procedure of the european parliament, in particular the article on public hearings on citizens' initiatives and the article on the citizens' initiative, we also consider it necessary to establish a single contact point at the european parliament with which citizens, representative associations and civil society can get in touch on issues relating to european citizens' initiatives. we call for appropriate measures at parliament level to ensure the visibility of public hearings on citizens' initiatives.
mr president, dear commissioners, let me remind you that we asked for discipline and for rules to be respected, and we ended up with a marathon for austerity. now we fear that no competitor will be crossing the finishing line, and the european supporters are steadily decreasing. meanwhile, the rest of the world never shared our solutions. preaching that growth is a direct consequence of restorative measures appears ridiculous and only creates more uncertainty amongst citizens and on the market. growth should have always been at the core of each and every eu policy, or was this not the case? this informal summit should dig through this growth mantra and focus on jobs to get the economy moving. however, simply declaring that we need jobs and investment is so obvious that it has become a cliché. the question is: do we want to invest our own profit or do we want europe to be attractive to outside players? because if we decide later, we need to establish and guarantee a stable and harmonised regulatory framework across member states and put a stop to the uneven competition between public and private financing.
the european union was founded on the stability and growth pact. both of the issues discussed today are mentioned, fiscal stability and economic growth. unfortunately, this pact was not respected and budgetary imbalances led to austerity measures. so clearly, there is no sustainable economic growth without financial stability. at the same time, austerity measures must be accompanied by measures to boost economic growth. the previous economic recovery programmes must be followed up with concrete measures. the commission should propose programmes to support smes, including loan guarantees or 'venture capital' funds. the necessary amounts may be secured by redirecting funds not allocated or not distributed to date. funds not absorbed for various reasons should not be collected and returned to the member states but redistributed for programmes to support the economy. the union budget is 95% directed towards investment and is a generator of growth and jobs. it is clear that european policies and the european budget are the instruments through which the union can intervene to support the economy. common policies 2014-2020 regulations should contain as many measures for growth and jobs as possible. the 2014-2020 budget must be approved as soon as possible so that member states can design their national policies. a good idea would be to approve, as a first step, chapter 1 of the mff which deals with cohesion, transport, education, research and innovation, ict, jobs. we need to promote new financial instruments such as, for example, project bonds. i think it would be a great step forward if we could reach an agreement on own resources, an agreement which would reduce the pressure on national contributions.
in writing. the eu is at a crossroads and needs bold decisions. austerity, as the only solution to the crisis, has proved a failure. states that have relied solely on austerity have made their situation worse, and the suffering of their citizens is even greater. we need to get back to growth together. this is no time to flaunt our differences and to confine ourselves to national egoism. it takes solidarity and vision. reducing development disparities between european countries can be an important driver of future economic growth. failure to act in this direction will have higher costs than a return to growth. european citizens cannot be blamed for their lack of desire to work, given that bad policy decisions have destroyed jobs. we have to relearn how to produce the goods and services we need.
in writing. the informal eu summit on 23 may is devoted to investment, growth and job creation. at this meeting, heads of state or government should identify and mobilise new policies to support economic growth in the eu. the summit should pay particular attention to measures to create new jobs, especially for young people, whose unemployment rate has exceeded 20%. as regards the structural funds, they should focus on increasing the competitiveness of the member states and increasing economic and social cohesion. member states with an unsatisfactory absorption rate should be supported to accelerate the use of the structural funds in areas and projects that contribute to job creation. given that industrial production has declined in many member states in recent years, with dramatic effects on jobs across europe, i believe that the eu should make better use of strategic partnerships with third countries to secure its raw materials and to support industrial production in the eu, exports and the eu's economic interests. we ask that the eib focus on supporting smes and infrastructure projects, particularly in the transport and energy sectors.
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, on behalf of my colleague ms damanaki, i would like to thank mr romeva for the work he has done on this report, and i am also very pleased to see the strong support from the fisheries committee on the substance of this important proposal. the rapporteur is absolutely right: the recovery of bluefin tuna is a very important issue because this is the most important species covered by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) and currently the only one subject to a multi-annual recovery plan. the eu has been a leading force behind this multi-annual recovery plan, and the aim of the commission’s proposal is to transpose into eu law a recommendation adopted in the iccat framework. the recommendation sets out a number of management measures to support the recovery of bluefin tuna. these measures were adopted by iccat as early as november 2010, and have been in force since june 2011. a week ago, and for the second time, we entered a fishing season without such management measures being transposed into eu law. this could jeopardise the uniform application of the measures within the eu and make them more difficult to enforce vis-à-vis individuals. it is therefore vital that we transpose iccat measures into eu law without delay. not doing so would certainly set us back from a conservation standpoint, and it would also seriously undermine the credibility of the eu in iccat and internationally. i therefore warmly welcome both co-legislators’ efforts to conclude this matter rapidly. the commission can accept the compromise text agreed in the last trialogue but it will make a declaration that this is without prejudice to its future position as regards recourse to implementing acts for the effective transposition of international conservation and management measures adopted by regional fisheries management organisations. i would like, once again, to thank the rapporteur and the fisheries committee for their work, and i am looking forward to the debate.
reporting for the opinion of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety. − today we have the opportunity to discuss one of the most concrete risks to food security: the major threats to global fish stocks. fish is essential to a healthy diet, being one of the most recommended sources of animal protein. this vital resource is being decimated by unsustainable exploitation through fishing practices that do not take into account long-term food security, but also by abuses linked to illegal fishing. i would like to thank the rapporteur for his efforts to strengthen the rules on bluefin tuna fishing. at the same time, i am disappointed that his amendments and our similar amendments in the committee on the environment, public health and food safety have not received sufficient support. the measures provided for in the new international agreement will ensure better implementation and enforcement of existing rules. it's a very important step. i would like to thank those who made it possible for these improvements to come into effect before the start of the new season, but reality clearly shows that these measures will not be enough. future agreements will have to be much more ambitious if we are really to protect the marine environment and the healthy food source it provides.
in writing. i welcome the fact that the recommendation of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) has already been adopted at international level. i believe that iccat could do more to adapt to the current situation in fisheries. true, we can already see some improvements in the bluefin tuna situation in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean, but important steps must be taken now. i very much appreciate the rapporteur's position that the union should not wait for iccat initiatives but should take firm precautionary measures on its own, in line with the united nations fish stocks agreement. the idea of declaring the main spawning grounds for bluefin tuna in the mediterranean sea, which are under eu jurisdiction, as closed zones or reserves - thus prohibiting fishermen from entering these areas during the breeding season - is welcome. i am aware that the eu not only sets very strict regulations in this area, but also spends impressive sums of money to comply with these rules. i am glad that we have made a significant contribution to the conservation of the bluefin tuna, but i believe that we can do even more than that!
on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, let me start with congratulations and thanks to the rapporteur. her job was not easy because a wide range of views were incorporated into amendments and compromise amendments, but ultimately – and i speak on behalf of the ppe – we find most of our ideas in this report. the word ‘reciprocity’ was the key word used by everybody, and there is only one possible sense of that word: it refers to the fact that the european union is open, and that china should be open and should reciprocate the openness of the european union. that much is clear. several controversial issues for us are addressed in the report, notably the questions of the public procurement market, joint ventures and the possibility for foreign companies to have a presence on the chinese market. of course, the matter of intellectual property rights is one of the hot potatoes of the moment, but that is an evergreen in eu-china relations. i welcome the crystal clear statement made here a few minutes ago by commissioner reding, who stated that eu recognition of market economy status depends on china itself. i think that is, or should be, the position of this house too, and the commission should ensure that it is translated into reality. the institutional framework for eu-china relations requires attention. we have a multiplicity of redundant institutional frameworks, so let us take care of that. let us speak with one european union voice in our relations with china, and also with the other brics. in conclusion, i think that the principle of reciprocity will bring balance to our relations.
in paragraph 7 of the report under debate there is a reference to agriculture, which i would describe as at least superficial. the text of the report includes china's criticism of agricultural subsidies for european farmers and the complex system of agricultural customs duties. i think the report should also have noted that the european agricultural policy has been fully subject to the rules of the world trade organisation since 1995, and that by decoupling and focusing on rural development measures, the european union has managed to transfer 88% of the aid granted to the wto's green box. eu producers are obliged to respect the highest standards of quality, product hygiene and the environment. this must be taken into account whenever parliament refers to our agricultural subsidies and the positions of our trading partners on them. finally, i believe that the opinion of the committee on agriculture on the subject of this report would have been useful and would have brought important elements into the debate.
the european union suffers from a huge trade deficit with china, which has deepened over time, reaching eur 169 billion in 2010. to reduce this deficit drastically and to restore the eu-china trade relationship to a level playing field, the chinese partner needs to solve a number of problems. these include: 1. transparency, to know exactly how much china has been involved in the economies of the member states; 2. fair market access for european firms; 3. a change in chinese policy on goods and the yuan which is undervalued and non-convertible and also 4. respect for intellectual property rights. i also call on the chinese authorities to respect in good faith and in practice the civil, political and labour rights of its citizens.
the economic and trade partnership with china is very important, but it needs to be balanced to bring full benefits to both sides. i therefore support the report's emphasis on increasing reciprocity as the main solution to economic imbalances. i also appreciate that we need to support european companies even more to have fair access to the chinese market. i would point out that romania pays particular attention to intensifying economic cooperation with china, especially in areas such as cross-border infrastructure, energy, agriculture or tourism. in 2011, bilateral trade reached a total value of usd 4.2 billion, and the volume of romanian exports to china was 36% higher than in 2010, the growth rate exceeding that of imports.
in writing. the european union is the main market for exports from china. between 2009 and 2010 alone, they increased by 39.5%. on the other hand, china is the eu's second largest trading partner. in addition, in the current context of the sovereign debt crisis, china has played an important role through its investments in infrastructure programmes in greece and its willingness to provide financial support to spain and portugal. so we can no longer speak of an emerging economy, but of a global economic actor. i therefore believe that the european strategy on china needs to be re-examined in order to synthesise both the opportunities offered by china's rapid rise internationally and the economic challenges it entails. it is time to consolidate a partnership based on mutual benefits and, by implication, to abandon the logic of competition. at the same time, the chinese economy does not yet meet the criteria of a market economy, which makes it difficult for european operators to operate on the chinese market. i therefore consider that the world trade organisation is the institutional forum through which this situation can be remedied.
trade agreements concluded by the eu with other countries are an important tool for strengthening economic relations. they must also support democratic developments, sustainable development and respect for human rights. european citizens have expectations in this area. they are becoming more and more careful about the source of the products they use and how they are made. as regards colombia and peru, the trade agreement must be able to produce a qualitative change in areas such as economic growth and social cohesion. i also invite the commission to present the measures envisaged to ensure the positive and lasting impact of union action in the partner countries. i would particularly like to know whether specific action has been taken to protect the rights of women and children.
the questions put by the authors are very timely and relevant, but i would add one more question: how does the commission intend to encourage the reduction of child labour in agriculture in the two countries? according to the latest statistics available, more than two million children between the ages of 6 and 14 are used for various kinds of labor in peru, or 29 percent of the total number of children in this age group. 70% of these, 1.4 million children, work in agriculture. colombia has also seen a sharp increase in the amount of child labor, with at least one million children employed in 2009, most of them in agriculture. this issue should therefore be on the agenda of official talks with the two states alongside, of course, the other issues raised here.
i will support the introduction of this financial transaction tax, even though, as my colleagues have pointed out, there are still issues to be clarified and it would be good if it were introduced in a global way, all member states accepting this and also not being pushed on customers by the financial sector. what has happened in the last few days, when we learned that one of the largest investment banks in the world has again told us, frankly, that it has billions of dollars in losses from the very same financial transactions that caused this crisis that we're in, makes us think that some of the major players in the financial sector have actually learned nothing from this crisis and want to continue to do business as usual. that's why i think a tax like this, especially on speculative financial transactions, is welcome.

in writing. − since intensive bluefin tuna fishing has led to massive declines in fish stocks, as evidenced by several independent assessments, it is imperative that the european authorities adopt meaningful conservation policies and implement effective control procedures. fisheries remains one of the areas on which the european economy and a significant number of workers in the member states depend, and ensuring the premises of sustainable development requires the adoption of measures that offer prospects for growth and long-term stability. at the same time, it is important that the european institutions clearly and consistently undertake the imperatives of biodiversity conservation, as reflected in union policy documents such as the europe 2020 strategy. i support the adoption of the report as a strong signal from the european union and its institutions to the imperatives of protecting the environment and restoring stocks.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it requires rapid and concrete measures, as well as a comprehensive multiannual strategy, to ensure the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. this species is currently threatened, both by overfishing and by the fishing methods and practices used. in this context, the existing regulations need to be complemented by detailed provisions addressing the legislative gaps on concrete issues such as caging. the european union has an important role to play in this process, but measures taken at european level alone will have only a limited impact if they are not followed by similar measures at international level. i therefore encourage european states to support stricter regulations within iccat. i also believe that the eu must be involved in promoting sound and sustainable management of bluefin tuna stocks, upholding these principles in relation to other important players in this sector, in particular japan. they also stress the importance of control activities to ensure compliance with existing legislation and to combat illegal fishing.
in writing. − the tuna stock has been declining for over ten years and is likely to disappear completely unless action is taken to restore the stock. to manage this decline, 64 measures have been adopted over the last 20 years, 13 of which are still in force. the recovery plan was first adopted in 2006 and subsequently amended in 2008, 2009 and 2010. the eastern bluefin tuna fishery is currently the most heavily regulated fishery in the eu and probably among the most heavily regulated fisheries in the world. the dramatic decline in tuna is mainly attributed to huge demand from the fish market, illegal fishing and fishing out of season.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 302/2009 on a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean. the eu must declare those regions as closed zones or bluefin tuna reserves and prohibit access to fishermen during the breeding season. such a measure would also be in line with eu environmental legislation (emcdda, natura 2000, etc.). the eu could make an important contribution to the conservation of bluefin tuna, which would significantly increase the likelihood of recovery of the stock. a unilateral eu declaration of closure of areas during spawning could apply to vessels flying an eu flag in all six areas and to vessels flying the flag of a third country only in waters under eu jurisdiction (in zones 1, 2 and 3). the fact that the eu has 56% of the tac for bluefin tuna means that the temptation to leave the eu register to fish in these waters would be minimal.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation concerning a multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean, because i truly believe that the european union needed to urgently comply with the most recent international standards in tuna catching. the report, by adopting the necessary amendments to the iccat recovery plan, improves the tuna fishing practice in europe, by increasing the protection of bluefin tuna, which risks disappearing from our seas. fish is a fundamental resource for our economy and the biodiversity of our seas is of undisputable value. a careful and well-tuned regulation of fishing practices and environmental protection is therefore essential. i believe this report will have a very positive impact in the fishery sector, by forbidding malpractices, overfishing and illegal catches.
in writing. − the recommendation of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas is binding on the union and must therefore be transposed into european union law. it provides for a further reduction in the total allowable catch, the strengthening of measures to reduce fishing capacity and the intensification of control measures, in particular as regards transfer and caging operations. the objective of the measures to reduce fishing capacity is to ensure the effectiveness of the bluefin tuna recovery plan with a view to achieving a biomass corresponding to maximum sustainable yield of at least 60% by 2022. i believe that for the next period a timetable is needed for adjusting the capacity of each member state so that all member states eliminate entirely the difference between their fishing capacity and their own fishing capacity in proportion to the quota allocated, applicable both to fishing vessels and to traps.
in writing. − the transposition into eu law of the 2010 recommendation of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas, to which the eu is a contracting party, is necessary and urgent, given the need to supplement measures to protect bluefin tuna. we also have to take into account that not only bluefin tuna is endangered, but five of the eight sub-species of bluefin tuna, such as southern bluefin tuna or whitefin tuna.
in writing. − i voted for this report, although not without some reservations. it is regrettable that the text does not represent a significant improvement on the commission’s proposal, and i am not convinced that it is consistent with the eu’s obligation, as laid down in the marine framework strategy directive, to achieve good environmental status by 2020. on the plus side, the new rules will come into effect before the next fishing season. for the long term, however, a much greater level of ambition is needed if we are to save our fish stocks.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the consequences of major ecological disasters demonstrate the need to accelerate the introduction of double hull requirements or equivalent design standards for single hull tankers. i believe that adequate protection must be ensured in the event of accidents, avoiding the disastrous effects of oil spills on water, soil, flora and marine fauna. at the same time, it is important to respect the specific competences of each european institution when defining regulations in this area. i support the position of the rapporteur, who has amended the commission proposal to reflect the position of the european parliament on delegated acts. in this context, i draw attention to amendment no 1, which mentions the importance of the commission organising appropriate consultations, including at expert level, during its preparatory work, but also recommends that all relevant documents be sent to the european parliament and the council.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the acceleration of the introduction of double hull requirements or equivalent design standards for single hull tankers. i consider this subject to be particularly important in view of the erika cases of 1999 and the le prestige case of 2002, and in view of the fact that oil tanker oil spills are major ecological disasters for both marine fauna and flora and for tourism in coastal areas. the objective of this regulation is to reduce the risks of accidental pollution of european waters through the accelerated introduction of double hulls. in single-hull vessels, the oil in the loading tanks is separated from the seawater only by a metal plate that forms the bottom and walls of the tanks. if this metal plate is damaged by collision or failure, the contents of the cargo tanks risk spilling into the sea and causing major pollution. an effective means of avoiding this risk is to cover the loading tanks with another inner metal plate, at a sufficient distance from the outer plate. such a 'double hull' design protects the loading tanks against damage and thus reduces the risk of pollution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because the provisions of the new protocol with mozambique will allow for improved management of fisheries in the region and the continued presence of the european fleet in the waters of the indian ocean. i believe that the partnership agreement will provide the appropriate framework for increasing the sustainability and good governance of the fisheries sector by mozambique. i would, however, ask the commission to monitor closely the way in which these provisions are implemented, to ensure responsible and rational fishing practices, as well as the other concrete aspects of the conditionality clauses for the annual payments, including respect for human rights. i welcome the inclusion in the agreement of specific measures for the employment of mozambican seamen. this will have a positive impact on the local economy. i also point out that the new partnership framework will allow cooperation to be intensified not only in the economic field but also in the scientific and technical field, thus enabling the fisheries sector to develop to the benefit of both parties.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has affected the member states of the european union and reduced the living standards of a significant number of eu citizens. it can also be seen that several features of international markets, such as the increase in the volume of financial transactions, the preference for short-term and high-risk operations, together with the development of high-frequency automated transactions, are relevant to the transformation of the financial system into a highly volatile sector prone to periodic crises. the report also calls for the introduction of a european tax on financial transactions, which would generate new revenue sources of around eur 57 billion, and systematically discourage high-risk and speculative transactions, which played a major role in triggering the current financial crisis. the introduction of the tax, together with the implementation of an effective supervisory system, may lead, in the medium and long term, to a reorientation of the trading system towards productive and sustainable investments for european economies.
in writing. − i voted against this report because i do not believe that a financial transaction tax would be effective unless it was applied at eu level. such a fee, applied correctly at global level, could represent an important source of revenue, allowing the financial sector to contribute equitably to the costs of the crisis. otherwise, however, it would affect competitiveness and have negative consequences, which would be felt first and foremost by citizens. we need to take action to remedy the effects of the economic downturn and to finance sustainable growth and development. but i don't think that a financial transaction tax would have the desired effect. i stress that the tax should not have any negative consequences on the banking system. i also draw attention to the fact that the risk of relocating investments to less transparent areas should be considered.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a council directive on the common system of financial transaction tax and amending directive 2008/7/ec. this tax could generate significant new revenue sources - according to recent estimates, up to €57 billion if implemented at eu level. it can shift the burden to activities with negative externalities, such as high-frequency financial transactions and highly speculative financial transactions, thus ensuring a fairer distribution of the tax burden. it can also become a deterrent to speculative transactions involving very high and damaging borrowing rates, thus contributing, together with appropriate regulation and supervision, to stabilising markets and reorienting the sector towards productive long-term investment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the financial transaction tax because i believe that this initiative is of particular importance in the context of the financial crisis the european union is going through. the introduction of the tax proposed by the american economist james tobin will stabilize the financial sector and channel it into long-term financing of the real economy, reducing the incidence of speculation. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the financial sector would have been able to recover the aid from the beneficiaries. i do not share the concerns that some governments have expressed regarding the alleged negative impact of the tax on the business of companies. the european union is too important a market for the financial sector to be able to afford to significantly reduce its activity here. i would also like to stress that if the amounts generated by this levy were administered at european union level, they could be used to finance european public policies and goods.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council directive on a common system of financial transaction tax (ftt) because i believe it could represent an important tool for the european union in tackling the economic crisis which has been heavily affecting the eu. the ftt may improve the level of security for financial activities, stop the deviations resulting from financial speculation and, at the same time, increase the financial sector’s contribution to the economic recovery of the union, which has so far only been loaded onto people’s backs through austerity measures and excessive taxation. i also positively welcome the derogation granted by the proposal to pension funds which would see the tax waived on their transactions. pension funds constitute, in fact, a very delicate field, differing by their very nature from the financial sector’s other activities: they deserved to have special treatment. i believe that the ftt will be able to grant the eu the necessary stability and resilience in financial activities, producing more certainty for investors, protecting the system from speculators and granting the eu new resources to be redirected to the real economy of our countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on the common system of financial transaction tax (ftt) and amending directive 2008/7/ec. in order to prevent distortions that may be generated by measures adopted unilaterally by member states, taking into account the very high mobility of most of the relevant financial transactions, and to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market, it is important that the fundamental elements of the ftt applied in the member states be harmonised and that the directive be applied at union level. the directive does not address the issue of the management of ftt revenues. i consider that part of the revenue from the ftt could be administered at union level, either as part of its own resources or in direct connection with specific union policies and public goods. the use of part of the revenue from the ftt as union own resources would reduce national contributions to the union budget and therefore free up funds from national budgets for other uses. i voted against amendment no 15, which exempts from the application of the directive investment managers of pension funds or institutions for occupational retirement provision, and entities set up to make investments for such funds or institutions.
in writing. − with developed markets on the verge of recession, china has become the outlet for many european exporters. in 2010, they exported goods and services worth around eur 113,1 billion to china. europe mainly exports transport machinery and equipment (more than 60% of eu exports, according to 2010 data), chemicals and raw materials. at the same time, imports from china are consumer goods, including clothing, office equipment and telecommunications. i believe that access for european companies to the chinese market must be under the same conditions as access for chinese companies to the european market. for good cooperation, the safeguards against access to the chinese market by european companies should be removed, including the authorisation system, direct aid and, last but not least, the barriers to public procurement.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report concerning the trade relations between the european union and china because i truly believe that, given the rising role of china in international trade relations, measures are urgently needed in order to guarantee an equal legal ground and mutual respect for international trading rules. china joined the wto in 2001 and is the world’s leading exporter of goods. however, china keeps on operating not in full compliance to international standards. therefore, given its role and its significant global impact, such practices create serious imbalances in the economic system, and for this reason have to be taken into consideration and dealt with carefully. this report, by calling on the commission to negotiate an ambitious and balanced eu-china investment agreement, able to create a better environment for eu investors in china, and to improve the transparency regarding governance of chinese companies which invest within the eu, will represent an important starting point for an improved and more trustful trade relation with china, which most certainly is a crucial partner for the european union and its member states.
in writing. − from the data provided by the rapporteur, the undeniable conclusion is that there is an imbalance in trade between china and the eu. the main question that needs our attention is: 'is china proving to be an unfair competitor to the eu?' the social and economic growth that this country has enjoyed in recent years is linked to business and especially to exports to member countries. given the percentages of this increase, it is vital that europe maintains an open dialogue with china and raises the issue of restrictions on entry to the chinese market again, because the need to work together is very important for both partners, and china must not ignore this truth. one problem that has not diminished is that of all counterfeit goods entering the eu. the quality of these products is poor, they are counterfeits of reputable brands, and consumers can be easily deceived. in order not to mislead citizens, i believe that we must encourage the purchase of products manufactured in the territory of the member states, thus ensuring that consumers comply with the rules on their manufacture and encouraging reindustrialisation and research policies in the union.
in writing. − trade between the eu and china is at an impressive level - one billion euro a day. the eu is china's main trading partner and china is the eu's main supplier of manufactured goods. in these circumstances, as president barroso has said, the eu-china partnership is one of the most important in the world. the report voted today is relevant to the problems in trade relations between the two partners. i voted in favour of this report; however, i regret that it does not focus on the problems of agricultural trade and does not take into account the special situation of european farmers, who are obliged to respect the highest quality standards in the world.
in writing. - i voted for the european parliament resolution on eu-china trade relations because i believe that a balanced agreement between the eu and china on trade relations is needed. i regret the insufficient protection of intellectual property rights in china, as well as the lack of concrete means available to european businesses, especially smes, to effectively combat infringements of intellectual property rights. the commission and the member states are invited to defend intellectual property rights more firmly in all multilateral organisations to which china belongs (wto, world health organisation and world intellectual property organisation). i also urge the commission and the member states to step up customs cooperation between the eu and china on the seizure of counterfeit goods and to simplify customs procedures. we call on the commission and the member states to cooperate more closely with third countries on copyright and licensing issues. i urge the commission to negotiate an ambitious and balanced eu-china agreement aimed at creating a better environment for european investors in china and guaranteeing transparency in the governance of chinese companies investing in the eu, while increasing the level of mutual capital flows.
in writing. − i support the proposal for a regulation on the detailed arrangements for the exercise of the european parliament's right of inquiry. this new legal framework aims to improve the functioning and effectiveness of committees of inquiry by providing them with the means to carry out their task of examining alleged breaches of union law and cases of maladministration. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal for a european parliament regulation on the detailed arrangements for the exercise of the european parliament's right of inquiry and repealing decision 95/167/ec, euratom, ecsc of the european parliament, the council and the commission. the treaty of lisbon created the conditions for a renewed and stronger institutional balance within the union, allowing its institutions to function more efficiently, more openly and in a more democratic way; in this context, the european parliament's powers of political control have been strengthened and extended. therefore, in accordance with national parliamentary practice and the requirements of the treaty on european union, the treaty on the functioning of the european union and the treaty establishing the european atomic energy community, the committees of inquiry of the european parliament should be strengthened by conferring on them specific, real and clearly delimited powers which are more in line with its powers and political status, while respecting the principle of proportionality as set out in article 5 of the treaty on european union. the powers of committees of inquiry, which are exceptional instruments of political control, should not prejudice the responsibilities of other institutions.
in writing. − believing that this proposal for a regulation respects the doctrine of the separation of powers in the state, i support the reform of the european parliament's right of inquiry. we need these changes in the regulation because experience has shown us that, although parliament can set up committees of inquiry, they can face many restrictions in the course of an inquiry. the increased power of these committees does not pose a risk to the institutions or the persons under investigation, the code of procedure being also clarified by the rapporteur. although parliament has the power to impose sanctions, it must be made clear that its main purpose is to investigate any type of situation that would prove to be detrimental to the eu and its citizens. by taking a broad view of any irregularities that may arise, we will have the chance to improve the current regulation with the desire to move towards an optimal functioning of the eu legal systems.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the detailed arrangements for the exercise of parliament's right of inquiry. the treaty of lisbon has created the conditions for a renewed and stronger institutional balance within the union, allowing its institutions to function more efficiently, more openly and in a more democratic way. in this context, the european parliament's powers of political control have been strengthened and extended. in accordance with national parliamentary practice and the requirements of the treaties (teu, tfeu and euratom), the committees of inquiry of the european parliament should be strengthened by conferring on them specific, real and clearly defined powers, which are more in line with its powers and political status, while respecting the principle of proportionality. the regulation lays down detailed rules for the exercise of the right of the european parliament to investigate, in the context of its tasks, without prejudice to the powers conferred by the treaties on other institutions or bodies, alleged contraventions of the rule of law or maladministration in the application of union law by a union institution or body, by a public administrative body of a member state or by any person empowered by the union to implement union law.
i begin by condemning the bombing of the northern part of south sudan, bombing conducted on monday and tuesday by sudan. for a moment i thought that the information that came in on monday would not be confirmed, but i saw that the information was confirmed and i think that in this case, we can talk about a new challenge from sudan. it's a shocking gesture, i think, which comes just days after thabo mbeki announced that the leaders of the two countries had expressed their desire to return to the negotiating table. the recent attacks confirm, i think, that sudan's strategy is to stall. i also think that president al-bashir is probably not willing to negotiate a road map to end the conflict at this point. that is why i encourage the african union negotiator and the panel he leads to accelerate the negotiations with sudan and work to prevent the escalation of a new war in the sudanese zone. i would like to end by paying tribute to the united nations interim force in abyei for its efforts to keep the peace in the area. i hope that the mandate of this force which expired yesterday will be extended, considering the deteriorating situation in the area. i'm calling on the united nations to increase the number of troops and police in the force to be able to respond to a crisis that seems to me imminent.
a conflict between sudan and south sudan would affect regional stability as well as the international economy. the union must continue to engage in efforts to de-escalate the situation in accordance with the un roadmap. additional measures are also needed to help the population. hundreds of thousands of people are already suffering the consequences of the crisis between the two countries. for example, the number of refugees in the yida camp has doubled in the last two months. i would like to draw particular attention to the situation in the nuba mountains, where the sudanese regime does not allow access even for the delivery of humanitarian aid. un agencies warn that the area is on the brink of catastrophe due to a lack of food and vaccine doses for children. i stress the need to negotiate humanitarian corridors to provide assistance to the population.
guinea-bissau has been affected by many years of instability in a context of corruption, drug trafficking and violence, and the military coup that disrupted the electoral process has aggravated the situation. for the moment, avoiding violence is a priority, which is why it is positive that a national agreement has been signed to exit the political crisis, as well as the transfer of power to civilians. but the ultimate goal must remain the restoration of constitutional rule and the beginning of a genuine democratic transition. the solidarity of the international community is essential to this end. i welcome the unanimous adoption of resolution 2048 by the un security council. i also appreciate the constructive role played by ecowas, which condemned the coup and sent a peacekeeping force last week. i call on the high representative to continue to work closely with the west african regional organisation.
over the past 12 years, we have seen both a significant increase in global commodity prices and worrying volatility. in the second half of 2010, 44 million people were pushed into poverty by rising food prices. these phenomena are caused not only by the scarcity of resources but also by their inefficient allocation or by speculation in commodity markets. in this context, the european union must work towards the development of a global system for the use and allocation of world resources and i therefore ask the european executive to seek to include environmental standards and the principle of fair trade on the agenda of the world trade organisation. continuing efforts to reduce and eliminate tariff and non-tariff barriers to trade in green goods and services is also an important step towards more efficient use of resources. last but not least, i would like to remind you that speculation in raw materials directly affects the lives of millions of people, causing poverty and hunger. i therefore consider it imperative that this practice be prohibited as a matter of urgency.
the answer to the resource efficiency challenges facing our society cannot be too simple or too easy to identify. i would therefore like to congratulate the rapporteur, the shadow rapporteur and all those who have contributed to the completion of this report. what is important now is that we know exactly what we have to do, we know where we want to go, it remains to mobilize to achieve our proposed objectives in a timely manner. there's a lot more to be done at the national and local levels. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the waste is not disposed of in a manner that would be contrary to the principle of subsidiarity. there are member states that have completely eliminated landfilling of municipal waste, such as germany and the netherlands, countries where the recycling rate of municipal waste is very high, such as belgium or sweden, or countries where the recycling rate is quite low, such as romania. in this context, i would like to add that the adoption of a national waste management strategy and plan is one of the priorities of the new romanian government. it is clear how important the role of national and local administrations is in accepting the new directions of the european agenda, but also in developing methodologies and processes to implement the necessary changes as quickly as possible. it's essential that we have the citizens on our side, that more and more people are proactive, believe in sustainable consumption, in the importance of recycling and minimizing waste. this is the right direction we should be heading.
to overcome the current economic crisis we must look for new ways to guarantee development and progress. we need an ambitious agenda for future growth, which ensures a higher quality of life; but boosting economic performance must be based on a rational and efficient use of resources because they are not unlimited. we already know that mineral resources are not renewable, but neither are water, soil or air. already, worldwide, we are consuming more than the earth can produce, and the industrialized countries, including european nations, have the highest per capita consumption of resources. in this context, i stress the importance of recycling and recovery, but also of information programmes to change individual behaviour.
the efficient use of energy resources is a key element of energy policy, which aims to achieve the sustainability objective of the eu 2020 strategy. i am convinced that in the next decade renewable energy, which today is still a luxury, will overtake the role of alternative sources and become the main source of energy in the eu. however, the energy potential of the member states differs. they must focus on the internal energy potential. natural gas will play an important role in the union's energy mix, given the new extraction procedures. however, energy efficiency is dependent on the union's ability to connect these markets. we need considerable investment in energy infrastructure, which could ensure easy transport between member states. the financing of these investments could be achieved by attracting private investors or investment funds.
a resource-efficient europe will require not only innovation and technology, but also new patterns of behaviour in production and consumption and new models of governance. this is why the european commission should initiate the transformation of europe's energy production by organising, for example, a forum with local and regional authorities and relevant stakeholders from both the private and public sectors as a starting point. the european commission should also set binding green procurement targets for national governments and include them as a separate element of the future public procurement directive to increase legal clarity in this area.

century, that century actually represents the resource-intensive model. the population increased fourfold, economic output increased many, many more times, and the use of any resource you could pick up increased by approximately the same factor. so, in fact, resource prices at that time, if measured by the composite index and with the exception of world wars and the oil crisis, were constantly falling. the recognition that resources are finite was absolutely not present in that model, in which, to some extent, we are still living. this situation is, in many ways, changing. the population is growing. not only will we reach nine billion in 2050 but, more importantly, as the mckinsey report says, in 2030 we can expect three billion more citizens to be raised from poverty to middle-class consumption. they will have every right to that, but they will not be able to get there if we continue with the model developed in the 20th century. what does that mean for europe? europe is extremely import-dependent. over the past decade and more, the prices of many resources have been going up. that trend is expected by a majority of companies to continue in the next five years – at 85% – and the volatility of those prices is huge. so today the european business sector is refocusing from labour productivity to resource productivity because that is the area in which businesses see the real opportunities. in many cases it is already recognised that energy and raw materials are critical. as for other resources – apart from water and land perhaps – it is not yet recognised in many cases that they are finite. these resources will be the focus of attention for our societies and businesses in the future. nature is not yet so much in the picture, but it will come. that is the change which we are facing. how is this connected to the story which we are all living through – the story of crisis and of the absolute need for growth and new jobs? as olli rehn said in his speech a day ago, if we had a silver bullet we would already have fired it, but we do not have it so we have to work consistently and patiently. there are some areas in which europe is strong and in which it could become even stronger. one such area is talent: the knowledge economy, research and innovation. the other major area is resource efficiency. why? because using less water, less energy and less raw materials, and producing products which can be reused and recycled makes economic sense. that is the trend which is currently very much present in the economy and in business. so ultimately we are talking about economic resilience and environmental resilience at the same time. i also really appreciate your highlighting the question of urgency and the need for implementation. these are matters to which we also try to draw attention when we talk about economic governance – the so-called semester story. here too, we emphasise those issues that point in the direction of resource efficiency. as was rightly mentioned by one of your colleagues, taxes are not to be feared. we are proposing no more and no less than the shift of taxation away from labour – and in europe we have high labour costs – in the direction of, for example, landfill taxation, which makes more sense. the removal of environmentally harmful taxes makes all the more sense at a time when we are trying to tap all the reserves in our public finances. this is not something which we can afford to ignore today. in our discussions with member states, we know that we bear a responsibility and we are advising them. and, by the way, in the council conclusions of march 2011 they supported our ideas. for the rest, we are working hard on the implementation of the roadmap. this year we will focus heavily on water. we will launch the resource efficiency transition platform within a few days – some of you will be participating in this – and it will bring real political impetus and direction. it will rightly be an important part of the seventh environmental action programme and, of course, the urgency of implementation is the core consideration. we will be discussing these issues at the rio+20 conference in just a few days’ time. the conference will not, of course, be about resource efficiency, but rather about the green economy. however, it is the same story. it will not be about europe, but about global commitments and the world as a whole, because we all understand that these things are necessary. to conclude, if everything was all right with brown growth, we would not be discussing green growth today, but brown growth has inherent limits which are recognised today by the business sector. we, as politicians, should recognise them too. when we talk about green growth, we are actually talking about how to design future growth capable of bringing greater well-being and more benefits to society than brown growth is bringing today. i am not trying to paint a catastrophe scenario because that will not happen: we are intelligent societies and an intelligent species. but a sustainable future, my friends, is simply not a choice. it is inevitable. finally i would like to thank all of you – the many of you – who have stayed to the end of the debate.
in writing. the initiative to promote resource efficiency is part of the europe 2020 strategy and is one of the principles on which eu action on climate change, energy, transport, raw materials, agriculture, fisheries, biodiversity and regional development will be based. i mention that the growing demand for natural resources and their overexploitation are leading to environmental degradation, accelerating climate change and destroying the planet's finite natural capital, including the decline of biodiversity. i stress the importance of research, development and innovation to accelerate the transformation to a resource-efficient europe. i believe that putting the economy on a resource-efficient and resource-efficient path will bring increased competitiveness and productivity and new sources of growth and jobs.
in writing. – the need for action on resource efficiency is becoming increasingly urgent as the global population grows and our resources are depleted. one aspect which is particularly important and which deserves special attention is the relationship between water use, food production and food waste. up to 80% of the water we take from the ground is for agriculture, yet we throw away up to one third of our food. the amount of water and energy which fuels this level of waste is shocking. we know that food waste is produced throughout the supply chain, at producer and retail level, as well as at consumer level. we need urgent action to tackle food waste at all levels. we can invest in all the irrigation technology and green energy we want, but there seems little point if it just produces food which rots on the supermarket shelf or ends up in the kitchen bin.
i am glad that romania was not targeted by mr barroso's letter, so it is not among the top eight countries in the union in terms of high youth unemployment, but my country is also very much affected by this phenomenon. i insist on three measures which i have outlined on several occasions to remedy this situation: re-establishing vocational and technical schools, stimulating young entrepreneurs and reducing school dropout, especially among the roma. i also stress the importance of apprenticeship programmes and traineeships. to increase the chances of young people in romania getting a job, the apprenticeship law was amended in 2011. procedures have been simplified and benefits for employees and employers have been increased. companies that employ young people also benefit from some facilities. thanks to them, over 10,000 young people entered the job market last year.
the number of young people who have difficulties entering the labour market and developing a career is increasing in almost all eu countries, and this is mainly due to declining opportunities for economic development. the fact that in the countries hardest hit by the crisis the youth unemployment rate is approaching dramatically the 50% mark calls for urgent action by the authorities. it is of the utmost importance that the efforts of national actors, intensified by the support of the commission, focus on directing european funds towards improving this situation. the long-term sustainable development of europe depends on how we harness the economic potential generated by young talent. i think our approach has to focus on the link between educational needs, the expectations of young people, and especially the needs of the labour market. we need to focus on preventing early school leaving and developing the school curriculum in line with the specific needs of the labour market. the lack of synchronisation of education systems with employers' needs and expectations in terms of candidates' skills is one of the biggest problems.
in the current context we cannot ignore the fact that the youth unemployment rate is approaching 50%. the support we want to offer from the european institutions must not be delayed. the requirements that employers today are almost unfulfilled in terms of the skills of candidates and the conditions that they have to meet, i mean some of the employers expect graduates to have maybe 25 years and 10 years of work experience. this is not possible, which is why there is a need for regulation at european level. even those without a college degree can benefit from tailor-made programs for youths. the problem is not their ability to learn and understand, but is found in employers. that's why i'm asking for special programs for young people so that they can enter the workforce and the problem of unemployment can be solved.
one of the goals we set for ourselves is to have a higher percentage of graduates in higher education. sadly, the present situation shows that young people are not even able to put their education to use, having to accept jobs far below their qualifications. this is a waste of money that member states have invested in education and it is a wake-up call that we urgently need to adapt the school curriculum to the needs of the labour market. in order to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, we need to allocate substantial funds to pragmatic training of young people and lifelong learning programmes. i believe that we can counter the problem of youth unemployment by increasing the co-financing for the structural funds. another important point we need to focus on is engaging young people in research and innovation for technological development so that we become more economically competitive globally.

the gender pay gap has its origins in school years, when girls are more likely to be directed towards humanities subjects, as opposed to boys, who focus on science subjects. in this way, not only do women end up being paid less in the profession they choose to practice but they also choose specific jobs that are traditionally less well paid. it's an outrageous inequality in our century when we talk about the integration of minorities of all kinds, but we don't give equal treatment to the 50 percent of the population, let alone discriminate based on the argument of motherhood. some employers still make the granting of a job conditional on a commitment not to procreate for a certain number of years after the employment. what we should be concerned about is the danger of poverty that comes from these practices, which can stigmatize entire generations of children.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the general arrangements for the granting of macro-financial assistance to third countries. the framework regulation aims to clarify the rules and to increase the efficiency, transparency and effectiveness of union assistance. macro-financial assistance is an instrument of the union's external policy and should serve to enhance the union's visibility and influence beyond its borders and should be used to provide exceptional financial assistance to third countries experiencing temporary balance of payments difficulties. unlike other instruments providing direct support for the union's external policies (the instrument for pre-accession assistance, the european neighbourhood instrument, the development cooperation instrument, etc.), macro-financial assistance should not be used to provide regular financial support, nor should its main purpose be to support the economic and social development of the beneficiary countries. macro-financial assistance should include measures to enhance the commitment of beneficiary countries to the common values shared with the union, including democracy, the rule of law, good governance, respect for human rights, combating forced child labour, support for sustainable development and poverty reduction, and other principles of free, fair and rules-based trade. the achievement of these objectives should be monitored regularly by the commission.

the prolonged impasse facing europe has one major cause: lack of concerted action. the place left by the great absence of the european project, solidarity, is unfortunately being successfully replaced by national interests. the most telling example is germany, which opposes the issuance of bonds. to survive, the european union needs urgent and convincing measures, the main aim of which is to reduce social inequalities and restore the european citizen's confidence in the benefits of european integration. austerity measures promoted by certain national governments have only deepened social inequalities. but as stiglitz notes in a recent article, inequality leads to a profound neglect of human potential, inhibiting consumption and amplifying social tensions. the great recession of the last century, with its massive cuts to basic services and unprecedented rise in unemployment, did just that: it exacerbated inequalities. it's time to take this historical lesson and adopt bold stimulus measures, such as a financial transaction tax and bond issues.

in writing. the decision of the justice and home affairs council on the right of schengen member states to temporarily reintroduce checks at national borders is a major and regrettable step backwards in the process of european integration. it is also a flagrant breach of the provisions of the lisbon treaty, which establishes the council-european parliament codecision procedure. it is a revolting shift from the council's previously constantly restrictive attitude to the question of freedom of movement to the exclusion of the european parliament from the decision-making process on the schengen area. this abuse risks undermining both the community spirit and the institutional and regulatory framework on which the european union is founded. the tendency to renationalize the schengen area, on its 27th anniversary, under the pressure of populist-nationalist tendencies opposed to the free movement of citizens is unacceptable. and changing the legal basis of the mechanism for assessing the implementation of the schengen rules would mean that the european parliament would be demoted from the position of co-decision-maker, as provided for in article 77 of the lisbon treaty, to a strictly consultative position. it is a double attack, against open borders - one of the major symbols of the european union - and the only european forum directly representative of the will of the citizens.
in writing. the council's decision to change the legal basis of the schengen evaluation mechanism is unacceptable for at least two reasons. first, it constitutes a serious breach of the treaties and of the principle of loyal cooperation between the institutions, thus contributing to the creation of a spirit of mistrust between the european institutions. secondly, beyond legal and interinstitutional considerations, the council's approach endangers the very integrity of the schengen area. the evaluation mechanism proposed by the council is no improvement on the current system and is the opposite of what the european parliament wants, namely a european evaluation system in which the commission plays the central role. in practice, member states want to continue the practice of covering up problems at schengen borders instead of promoting an effective evaluation mechanism that involves both assistance in cases of disability and sanctions when they are necessary. the european parliament cannot accept such an approach to the schengen area and is prepared to refer the matter to the european court of justice if the council does not reconsider its position.
in writing. – the members of the council insist that the schengen legal basis is in need of change merely because they want powers to reintroduce the internal borders within the eu. this is utter populism, since internal borders do not improve the life and security of the citizens, but put limits on their freedom. it is clear that the council intends to renationalise the schengen project, and to go back to an outdated intergovernmental approach. more than seeking to satisfy the ego of one of the european institutions, this reflects the demagogic approach of the dialogue with the national societies, rather than the concern for the security of the citizens. the change in the legal basis of the schengen evaluation mechanism should be considered only in terms of finding the correct paths for the implementation and putting into effect the schengen acquis. the member states gathered in the council want to control and change the schengen mechanism as they please, not for improving it, but for hiding their incapacity to improve the life of the citizens by presenting the freedom of movement as the source of all evils.
