in writing. - latin america will continue to be a priority for the european union, and this is evidenced, in particular, by the considerable progress made in bi-regional relations in recent years. as a member of the european parliament's delegation for relations with mercosur, i believe that the european union must continue to give strong support to the development and stabilisation process in the region and develop, in close consultation with the latin american countries, a policy for the development of the region which is sustainable, equitable and balanced. to this end, i recommend intensifying bilateral dialogue and cooperation in key areas of common interest such as energy, transport, research, science and technology, and good governance in fiscal matters. this involves adjusting the relationship on a case-by-case basis to achieve the greatest mutual benefit. this approach will also complement and support efforts to achieve greater regional integration.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the definition of a new development cooperation policy in relations with latin america, as, according to the lisbon treaty, the overall objective of development cooperation is to eradicate poverty and promote sustainable economic and social development, and to achieve the millennium development goals (mdgs) by 2015. latin america and the eu form a bi-regional strategic partnership based on shared values and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, with brazil and mexico being two of the eu's nine strategic partners in the world. the eu is also the main investor and second largest trading partner, as well as the main provider of development aid in the region. the eu's priorities in development cooperation and implicitly with latin america include energy efficiency, renewable energy, transport, biodiversity protection and support for smes. in this context, the conclusion of an eu-mercosur association agreement will stimulate cooperation and development between latin america and the union, provided that it is based on the principle of fair trade and on respect for labour, environmental, public procurement and intellectual property rights standards. trade between latin america and the eu is a crucial factor in reducing poverty and ensuring prosperity on both continents.
in writing. − volunteering benefits both personal development and civil society as a whole. by engaging in cross-border volunteering activities, european citizens have the opportunity to develop new skills necessary for good job placement and to benefit from the experience of cultural and linguistic diversity. i believe that member states need to promote involvement in cross-border volunteering, establish a legal framework favourable to the performance of volunteering activities and recognise the rights of volunteers. i believe it is essential that the skills and competences acquired through volunteering activities are recognised as professional experience and informal and non-formal learning. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it presents useful proposals which will support volunteering at european level. as we live in a digital age, i particularly support the suggestion in article 20 to create a centralised union portal. it will allow citizens in any member state of the union to have rapid access to all the necessary information, including in the field of cross-border volunteering. i also support the idea of a 'european skills passport'. i believe that it will not only make it possible to put to good use the experience gained in volunteering activities, but will also be a timely complement to the measures for the recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications at european level. i draw attention to the role that volunteering can play in the transition from first job to working life and retirement. i would like to point out that the eleventh edition of the national volunteering week took place in romania from 14 to 20 may. more than 10,000 people from 111 localities were involved in the activities.
in writing. - i wanted to explain my vote in favour, because i'm really an active citizen, i believe in volunteering, i believe in patronage, i believe that to be strong is to do good. although there is increasing progress in volunteering (the year 2011 was the european year of voluntary activities), the rapporteur believes that there must be a clear distinction between the value of voluntary activities, which have no financial counterpart, and gainful activities. volunteering needs to be further supported and the creation of a centralised eu portal on volunteering, the establishment of a 'european voluntary humanitarian aid corps' and the creation of a 'european skills passport' would bring a considerable improvement to the notion of volunteering and to volunteering processes in general. this skills passport will allow volunteering to be publicly recognised (even in cvs, for example) and the skills acquired will be used later by young people in education and work.
in writing. − volunteering activities directly contribute to the eu's fundamental policy objectives, such as social inclusion, employment, education, skills development and the promotion of citizenship. however, there is no clear legal framework for volunteering activities and the skills acquired by volunteers are often insufficiently recognised. i welcome the decision to develop a 'european skills passport' as it will ensure the recognition of professional qualifications across borders and give citizens the opportunity to keep a record of the skills and competences acquired through volunteering.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because i believe that we need a clear and appropriate legal framework for volunteering activities at the level of each member state. the potential of volunteering activities in developing socioeconomic cohesion should not be overlooked. i therefore believe that member states must protect the rights of volunteers and ensure non-discriminatory access to healthcare as well as social protection services. as regards cross-border volunteering, it is important that older people who choose to engage in volunteering activities in another member state have unconditional access to information and receive funding and support appropriate to their situation.
in writing. − volunteering activities attract more and more young people every year, which is beneficial for both local development and cross-border cooperation. such cooperation projects play a significant role in promoting solidarity, active citizenship and intercultural learning, as young volunteers have the opportunity to study the language and culture of the country in which they work. i believe that the member states of the union must recognise the benefits of all citizens participating in cross-border volunteering activities, activities through which they have the opportunity to develop new skills that can contribute to better integration into the labour market, but also to their mobility.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament resolution on recognising and promoting cross-border voluntary activities in the eu because of the great contribution that voluntary work organisations make to the eu, the member states and all the regions of europe. this report, in particular by urging national, regional and local authorities to ensure stable funding and provide tax incentives, aims at a strengthened recognition of the organisations involved in volunteering activities. it also stresses the importance of ensuring that skills and knowledge gained by volunteers during their work should help them find jobs and receive due recognition as part of their working experience. moreover, the transnational nature that characterises voluntary work should receive special treatment from the european union, since it represents one of those issues that actively trigger a dynamic definition of european citizenship. voluntary work puts transnational european solidarity into motion.
in writing. − the 2011 year of volunteering initiative report, adopted in the cult committee and in the ep plenary, is an assessment of the eu's actions during the past year, a year dedicated to the idea of volunteering. in addition to its evaluation function, the cult committee has also made recommendations for promoting and facilitating volunteering activities, especially in transnational situations. i supported this report both in committee and in plenary, because i consider it to be a report with significant added value, even if it remains an own-initiative report. the elements they incorporate are fundamental to the effective functioning of eu programmes in the field of volunteering. it insisted on funding, both through its own programmes and through the cohesion fund, and on visa liberalisation for non-eu citizens interested in volunteering in the eu.
in writing. − i welcome the fact that the european parliament has given a new signal by affirming the special role of crossborder volunteering activities at eu level. beyond being a catalyst for creating a shared civic spirit, the report's data shows that volunteering can contribute up to 5% of gdp growth. given that around 100 million europeans are involved in this type of activity, a more effective regulatory framework in the union is required. among the excellent measures in this report, i find the creation of an eu portal with a section dedicated to cross-border volunteering, as well as the establishment of a european volunteers humanitarian corps to select and train people to respond to natural disasters, extremely useful. last but not least, the introduction of a european skills passport, valid in all member states, will provide for the proper recognition of professional qualifications and skills acquired through volunteering. in addition to the concrete benefits of volunteering, expressed in social cohesion, as a factor of integration and a source of human resources, this activity also has a symbolic role for the union: it contributes to the development of citizenship and the common european identity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the recognition and promotion of crossborder volunteering in the eu. volunteering is an informal learning experience suitable for people of all ages and provides benefits in terms of personal development, civic values, social solidarity and participation in democratic life. we call on member states that do not have a clear and appropriate legal framework for volunteers to create one and to develop national strategies for promoting volunteering activities, including the recognition of volunteer rights, and to pay attention to this sector in the development of future policies, programmes and funding. national, regional, local authorities and the eu must pay particular attention to disadvantaged young people, especially those with disabilities, so that they can volunteer and receive appropriate educational and financial support. we propose the creation of a centralised eu portal, in cooperation with organisations and associations active in the sector, comprising a database of good volunteering practices and a section dedicated to cross-border volunteering. the portal should provide information on available programmes, their cost and conditions of participation, information on administrative formalities, legal and fiscal aspects of volunteering, obstacles to accessing programmes and the best ways to overcome them.
in writing. − the development of digital services and infrastructure at european level is not only a consequence of the qualitative and quantitative increase in the importance of these communication and working environments for european citizens, but also an essential element of european policies to stimulate economic growth and competitiveness. the security of information infrastructures is a key element for achieving the objectives of the digital agenda of the european union and the europe 2020 strategy. without a more secure digital environment, both european economies and citizens suffer. i welcome the conclusions of the report and support the directions of development and action it describes. increasing the security of the information infrastructure and, by implication, the security of the european citizen cannot be achieved without flexible strategies to promote cooperation between the public and private sectors. only through this cooperative process, bringing together governments, economic actors and citizens, can vital areas such as financial services, health, food security and water supply be effectively defended against new threats. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted for this report because security and confidence are key conditions for achieving the europe 2020 smart growth objectives. and the digital agenda aims to increase the eu's competitiveness by strengthening information and communication technology. today, in the context of increased internet use, the development of a high level of security is becoming increasingly important. the disruption of the internet entails major risks as it can affect a large number of european citizens and businesses. improving the assessment and management of cyber risks is therefore essential. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's cybersecurity legislation and will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's cybersecurity legislation. given their complexity and the fact that they are becoming increasingly sophisticated, coordination of measures is essential. the eu must take a coherent approach to tackling security issues.
in writing. − the rapporteur is of the opinion that the issue of internet security is a pertinent one and he is right. it therefore proposes that measures already taken, such as directive 2008/114 on the identification and designation of european critical infrastructures and the assessment of the need to improve their protection, or the commission's 2009 communication on 'protecting europe from cyber-attacks and widespread disruption: improving preparedness, security and resilience', be maintained and even developed in line with technological progress. the rapporteur believes that this requires a responsive, flexible, innovative and long-term framework, as this will enable effective interaction between governments, businesses and all other stakeholders. i voted for all of these ideas.
in writing. − in recent years, the internet has become an increasingly common tool in everyday life, both professionally and personally, with the entire european and global infrastructure expanding rapidly. a disruption of this network could cause significant losses to the administration, the business community or ordinary citizens. as such, i believe that a common policy is needed to protect these infrastructures, as well as the establishment of joint cyber emergency response teams (cert), leading to the development and implementation of national cyber security strategies. last but not least, it would be beneficial to include health, food and water supply, nuclear research and the nuclear industry among the sectors targeted for cooperation between eu states and third countries, for the development of warning systems and the exchange of good practices.
in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament resolution on critical information infrastructure protection achievements and next steps: towards global cyber-security, because i truly believe that it would be impossible to achieve the ambitious goals of the digital agenda for europe without a resilient and secure internet system. the eu must imperatively have a comprehensive internet security strategy and this report, in particular by calling on the commission, in cooperation with the member states, to assess the implementation of the ciip action plan and urging the member states to establish well-functioning national/governmental certs and national internet security strategies, properly addresses this fundamental need. in addition, the focus on the role of international cooperation for the development of a shared approach for tackling cybersecurity issues with all like-minded countries assumes a central relevance in the adopted report, which also maintains that internet security issues should be included in the scope of the future eu's external relations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 12 june 2012 on the protection of critical information infrastructures - achievements and next steps: towards a global cybersecurity context. we call on the commission, in cooperation with the member states, to assess the implementation of the ciip action plan and urge the member states to organise national cyber emergency response teams (cert), develop national cyber security strategies, organise regular national and pan-european cyber incident exercises, develop national cyber incident response plans and contribute to the development of a european cyber incident response plan by the end of 2012. we welcome the current proposal to revise enisa's mandate and to extend the agency's tasks. calls on the commission to propose, by the end of 2012, a comprehensive strategy on internet security, setting out the principles, objectives, methods, tools and policies (both internal and external) needed to streamline national and eu efforts and to establish minimum resilience standards between member states to ensure a secure, continuous, robust and resilient service, whether for critical infrastructure or for general internet use;
in writing. − strengthening the external dimension of the eu's energy policy will ensure that the union has secure, sustainable and affordable energy. i believe that there is a need for better coordination of member states' policies in this area and for closer cooperation between the council, the commission and the european external action service on matters relating to the common external energy policy, so that the european union can have an improved negotiating position vis-à-vis third countries. i voted in favor of this resolution.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the european union must succeed in diversifying its sources and transport routes to ensure the security of its energy supply. to this end, coordination and coherence between external, energy and trade policies are needed. romania considers that the black sea has a major potential in achieving european energy security, representing a gateway to central asia and the caspian area. a concrete example is the agri interconnector project for the transport of liquefied natural gas, as well as the energy cooperation initiated with turkmenistan. at the same time, my country supports major projects such as the nabucco pipeline and the southern corridor, because their completion will allow energy diversification on the european market, but also reduce the current degree of dependence on certain energy sources or routes. at the same time, romania attaches particular importance to the interconnection of energy networks with neighbouring states. and the gas fields discovered in the black sea will allow romania, according to estimates, to be energy independent within three to four years.
in writing. - i agree with the rapporteur that europe is a major buyer of energy on world markets. this is an advantage because if there is a firm and common position at eu level in negotiations with third countries, then we could be a strong market player. i think that there needs to be a greater focus on research, development and innovation. a common approach to research is needed within the eu, as results can be more efficient, cost-effective and dynamic than if they were achieved by each member state individually.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe that we need improved security of energy supply. on the one hand, the european commission needs to provide a clearer definition of 'energy solidarity' between eu member states, and on the other, there needs to be real diversification of suppliers, routes and sources of external energy supply. it is estimated that by 2030, global energy demand will increase by 40%. in addition, the eu's dependence on energy imports could also increase, despite efforts to improve energy efficiency and use renewable energy sources. the nabucco project could have contributed to a necessary diversification of energy supply sources. unfortunately, there is no visible progress towards the realisation of this ambitious european project.
in writing. − europe has set itself ambitious targets through the 20-20-20 package and a long-term commitment to decarbonise the european economy by 2050. research, development and innovation play a key role in achieving these objectives. i therefore believe that the european union and the member states must step up their efforts in this area in order to achieve an efficient and dynamic level of research activity. such cooperation could allow for better results than those achieved by each member state individually. last but not least, it is beneficial to continue cooperation in research, development and innovation with third countries, which will allow the european union to remain a major player globally, including in partnerships in international fora: the eu-russia dialogue, the eu-us, the energy charter, the energy community process and relations with other international bodies concerned with energy and climate.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament resolution on engaging in energy policy cooperation with partners beyond our borders: a strategic approach to secure, sustainable and competitive energy supply, because it addresses the crucial challenges of the union’s energy policy in its foreign relations, carefully taking into account the main aspect of security of energy supply. europe plays a key role in the global energy market, especially in terms of consumption. energy policy, therefore, must align the geopolitical and strategic role of the european union with its energy needs. this report, by creating a more coherent and coordinated approach by the member states, the council and the commission in shaping and achieving the union’s goal in this field, strengthens the position of the eu in negotiations with third countries. in addition, the report stresses the importance of parliament being appropriately involved in the consultation processes relating to energy policy, in line with the article 194 of the tfeu. this is of paramount importance for enabling democratic involvement when defining such crucial policies of the union, which will surely have a major impact on the quality of our citizens’ lives.
in writing. − energy policies are a priority for the european union and efforts to extend cooperation to as many of the community's neighbouring countries as possible should be encouraged and addressed with great seriousness. i regret, however, that the process of negotiations with a view to the enlargement of the energy community with countries such as turkey and the southern mediterranean countries is slow and difficult, although rapid measures are needed to enlarge the european energy system, based on strategic cooperation. i also believe that we must now focus our attention on urgent cooperation initiatives in the field of clean, renewable energy, in the context of the expected increase in the global population, which will lead to a significant increase in energy consumption over the next 20 years.
in writing. − i voted for the report on engaging in energy policy cooperation with partners beyond our borders: a strategic approach to secure, sustainable and competitive energy supply. i voted for the amendment which calls on the commission to draw up common energy roadmaps with all the main energy suppliers and with strategically important transit countries. we also called for partnerships with countries facing similar energy challenges to promote cooperation in technology, research and industry and to create common standards on renewable energy technologies, energy efficiency, electric vehicles, new and unconventional energy technologies, offshore drilling safety, and nuclear safety and non-proliferation. i would like to stress the geostrategic position of the black sea region in terms of diversifying energy sources and routes and renewable energy potential. in this context, i would like to stress the importance of the southern corridor, the nabucco project and the transcaspian pipeline, as well as other smaller projects. we call for the application of existing mechanisms and the creation of new ones within the european neighbourhood policy and the black sea synergy, in order to strengthen cooperation and the stability of the eu's energy supply.
vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − madam president, first of all can i say that i agree with mr salafranca that this is in our dna, and i am really pleased to have the opportunity to speak again in this house on the subject of human rights. as honourable members know, this is one of my top priorities, and i really value the opportunities to continue our discussions. may i also formally thank mr salafranca for the work he has done on his report. the recommendation that is before this house today is a welcome contribution to the preparations for the appointment of a special representative on human rights. i give absolute credit to parliament for championing this idea since its report in 2010. we have now reached the point where it commands a broad consensus across the political spectrum. i congratulate mr salafranca for delivering such an overwhelming vote in the committee on foreign affairs (afet). the broad consensus is the result of broad consultation. over the past few months my services have been canvassing opinions from this house, from member states, commission services and from ngos, and that has helped to ensure that the thinking of this house is reflected in the draft mandate which i presented to the council. honourable members, the mandate will be broad and flexible. i want the new special representative to work with me to set priorities, to be able to develop the themes that mr salafranca has so ably put before us: abolition of the death penalty, combating the use of torture, women’s rights, children’s rights, and to ensure that they are able to do that in the context of working collaboratively with the institutions of the european union and, of course, to work closely with the european external action service. the mandate will be longer than usual: two years instead of one. it is the first time ever that the european union will have appointed a thematic eu special representative so i believe it is important that the mandate should be long enough to start delivering on issues that are inherently long-term issues. i believe that the special representative will have significant experience and expertise. i am looking for somebody with an established track record, real experience in human rights and a strong understanding of european union policy. member states have put forward some excellent candidates, and i look forward to making a swift appointment. i do want to be clear that the special representative will be an important interlocutor for this parliament. you have my full commitment that he or she will be able to brief parliament regularly, fitting in line with existing arrangements. the special representative will also add considerable value to our existing work, and that may take the form of leading our human rights dialogues and consultations, where it is obvious that the special representative should be a natural interlocutor for our partners. communications and public diplomacy will be key. they need to help us to be more visible and to promote human rights across the whole range of the european union’s external policies. but just to be absolutely clear, i will remain personally as involved as ever, but with now, in the future, additional, high-level, expert support to work with me and with the team based in brussels – some of whom are with us today, and to whom i pay tribute for the extraordinary work done over these last few years. the special representative is part of the bigger package because, as you know, the council is due to adopt a strategic framework and an action plan on human rights and democracy too. preparation for this has taken account of input from members of this house in line with my undertaking to engage this house throughout the process. the latest of these exchanges took place today, just before this debate began, when my deputy secretary-general, maciej popowski, met with the contact group in parliament, under the chairmanship of mrs lochbihler. i hope that these contacts will continue and become a regular feature of our inter-institutional discussions on a more effective and comprehensive approach to human rights and democracy. i have always intended this process to be inclusive and to give the opportunity for all stakeholders in eu policy to contribute to defining our future priorities. madam president, i end as i began, with a thank you to mr salafranca for his report.
on behalf of the epp group. the treaty is clear: human rights are values on which the union is founded, but so are the union's relations with third countries. in this perspective, i remember lady ashton starting her term by declaring that human rights would be the guiding principle of foreign policy. but for the moment, the union's actions to promote human rights abroad are rather disparate, and the lack of coherence in this area has been criticised many times in this parliament. the appointment of a union special representative for human rights is intended to strengthen the coherence of european action in this area and, of course, we must welcome such an innovation. on the other hand, as long as we treat human rights as a separate field, covered by so-called human rights dialogues and not in high-level meetings between political leaders, i fear that our credibility will continue to suffer. the arab spring reminded us that human rights are universal, demonstrating that every individual wants his or her fundamental rights and freedoms to be respected. i therefore believe that the success of the mandate of the union special representative for human rights requires, beyond the institutional architecture, a political will on the part of the main european and national actors to guide their actions in accordance with the solemn proclamations of the treaties.
never have human rights been more important and brought about so many changes of government as they are in our time. events in the middle east and north africa have demonstrated the strong link between human rights and democracy. it is clear that the european union must change its reactions, since the states of the middle east and north africa are interested in seeing what solutions they can apply to the transition to a democratic state, to a state-building that includes the protection of human rights, which had been affected in the regimes prior to the arab revolutions. that is why the future human rights representative will need to have a strong mandate, be a key interlocutor for ngos, minorities, work with the united nations and lead consultations with third countries on human rights.
guns play an important role in ensuring security and the defence sector, but at the same time they can fuel conflict, violence and instability. that is why i argue that there is a need for clear regulations on the international arms trade. i also tabled an amendment in which i stressed the usefulness of specific provisions on the marking of weapons. at the same time, we highlighted the need for additional measures to ensure traceability from the producer to the end user. it is found in paragraph 9 of the resolution. the adoption of a multilateral legal instrument will allow for higher standards and more transparency in this area. however, for the new treaty to achieve its objectives, it must include concrete provisions on accountability mechanisms. in this context, i stress the need to pay greater attention to preventing and combating illicit arms trafficking. in 2011, global arms spending was €1.398 trillion, according to sipri data, representing 2.5% of global gdp. and a recent report by oxfam shows that in the past 12 years, embargoed countries have managed to purchase $2.2 billion worth of arms.
there are several areas of crisis in the middle east lately, but we must not neglect the israeli-palestinian relations, because they influence the stability of the entire region. i would like to stress once again that the union's policy in this area must be constructive and must avoid, first and foremost, the aggravation of tensions. it must show balance and reaffirm its support for the two-state solution, coexisting in peace and security. i would like to ask you, madam high representative, if there has been any dialogue with israel following the critical conclusions of the last middle east council. at the same time, i'd like to know your opinion on the peaceful reforms that jordan has initiated. do you think they can have a positive influence on other countries in the region?
in writing. – when king abdullah ii of jordan visited strasbourg about two month ago, the situation in syria looked somehow ‘stabilised’, with the regime still in control. the kofi annan mission looked poised to bring relief to the embattled people of syria and both russia and china seemed inclined to contemplate the cost of sustaining the assad regime to the end. two months later, all that is gone. the bloodshed continues at even higher levels, the regime is holding fiercely onto power, kofi annan’s plan has become questionable and russia in particular has toughened its stance to the point of preventing any potential external intervention to relieve the syrians of this nightmare. after all, the international community was able to unite and act – see bosnia and kosovo – in situations that were not apparently as bad as that existing in syria today. still, with all those shortcomings, the annan’s plan seems to be all that we have got, because, in lady ashton’s words–‘no other option has been able to gather any kind of international support’. sad, but true, this is how international politics works. the question is, how will we look into the eyes of the ordinary syrians when all this is over?
mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate my colleague mrs nedelcheva on her report and her commitment to the drc issue. this debate is an opportunity to reflect on a very interesting problem: the link between elections and democracy on african soil. there are indeed quite different cases. on the one hand, first of all, there are countries where the electoral process is taking place. the most recent example is senegal, where, despite some emotions before the elections, everything went well and a certain democratic stability is established. on the other hand, there are cases, like the most recent one in mali, where the military takes control and an electoral process is effectively blocked. in between these two limits are the more complicated cases, notably the drc - this is also the case in guinea - where electoral processes are organized and then, all of a sudden, there are postponements, post-electoral violence, a much more difficult and, in a way, unpredictable journey of democracy. what can we do? i believe it is our responsibility to support, on the one hand, the monitoring of the electoral process with our missions. on the other hand, as my colleague mr striffler has just mentioned, electoral support must of course be linked to development support.
on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, i am happy with mrs ashton’s discourse. i am not happy with afghanistan’s future. according to the lisbon summit, the isaf mission will be finished in 2014. we are now analysing 10 years of partnership between the international community and afghanistan. what has happened in these ten years? we can all report some achievement in economics, in freedom, in human rights, in women’s rights, in healthcare, but are these achievements enough to consider afghanistan a stable and democratic country? is afghanistan today a country which certainly has a democratic future? if i look to the nato summit i see a lot of optimism. i believe that we must look behind this optimistic approach, and behind this optimistic approach we will see still increased drug production in afghanistan, increased corruption and widespread unemployment in that country. i am really sure that women can play an active role in democratisation, but for how long will women be allowed to play this role after the withdrawal of the isaf mission? i am afraid that our strategy for a future afghanistan is not a realistic one and it is going to be really difficult to implement. certainly, we need a strong partnership, not only between the european union and afghanistan, but i believe also between the united states and afghanistan. unfortunately, coming back to the nato summit, i can see one chair left empty. it is putin’s. maybe russia can start to play an active role in the area.

especially to support the building of a civilian police force, so essential to the state’s future, when justice and the rule of law can be not only talked about but can be seen to be effective across in writing. nato confirmed in chicago that isaf military operations in afghanistan will end in 2014, following a gradual transfer of responsibility to the afghan authorities. i stress again, as in my previous speeches on this subject, that the full participation of the afghan government is needed to ensure long-term stability. at the same time, international support must continue beyond 2014, in particular through training and assistance programmes. i believe that the eu can also make a valuable contribution to this process. i therefore welcome the council's decisions in may to support the stabilisation efforts in afghanistan and hope that they will be put into practice as soon as possible. to this end, i suggest that the possibility of structured cooperation between eupol and other training missions be explored. i also ask that special attention be paid to programmes to improve the situation of women in development assistance. i note that my country has already confirmed that it will maintain its commitment in afghanistan until the end of the isaf mission, aiming to ensure security in the zabul region. last but not least, i salute the courage and dedication of the romanian military, which contributes, sometimes at the cost of their lives, to the establishment of security, stability and democracy in afghanistan.
in writing. after eleven years of efforts by the international community, the current situation in afghanistan still requires significant improvements. violent extremism both inside and outside the region, the problem of drugs grown and produced in afghanistan, and socioeconomic indicators all highlight the need for a much more active eu role in the reconstruction and development of the region. the union's efforts should focus on improving the functioning of afghan government structures. the afghanistan strategy must focus on a strong engagement of afghan institutions and citizens in the development of their country with a view to achieving a stable government, supported by the international community, that focuses all its efforts on socio-economic development. the european union is one of the most important partners in afghanistan's reconstruction, through the logistical and material assistance it provides. i want to draw attention to the need for a reorientation of how aid is delivered to afghanistan and how it is distributed. i believe that more aid should be channelled directly through afghan institutions, rather than through international development and cooperation bodies. the legitimacy of the afghan government will be gained if it is responsible for implementing the aid.

in writing. the negotiation of the future multiannual financial framework is a complex and sensitive process which will lay the foundations for the union's economic and political action for the next seven years. seven years that we hope will be seven years of growth and economic recovery. that is why we need a strong investment budget, one that is as united as possible for all the member states. regional policy, the common agricultural policy, research policy, erasmus, support for smes - these policies have become the basic pillars of the european economy today and are in fact the real engines of the single market. but to achieve them, we need a budget that can meet the challenges ahead: globalisation, climate and demographic change, the transformation of the economy to one based on new technologies. negotiation is the art of compromise, but when it comes to the future financial framework, the european parliament has defined a set of minimum criteria to which we will not yield: • keeping the budget at least at 2013 levels • a higher share of own resources • and for the european parliament to be recognised as a true negotiating partner. we all know we need this budget, and i'm confident that eventually we'll find a middle ground.
in writing. as representatives of european citizens, we have a duty to ensure a well-funded, transparent and fair budget that is focused on results. that is why i believe that the european union needs investment in its priority areas more than ever. i believe that directing expenditure towards policies that have proven to be a real success, such as cohesion policy, can continue to provide real added value, boosting economic growth and the european union's global competitiveness.
in writing. the european council on 28-29 june will address issues of economic policy, the multiannual financial framework, as well as the governance of the schengen system and asylum. in defining and implementing its policies and actions, the union shall take into account requirements relating to the promotion of a high level of employment, the guarantee of adequate social protection, the fight against social exclusion, as well as requirements relating to a high level of education, vocational training and the protection of human health. i believe that the union needs a common agenda for growth and job creation, with a particular focus on youth employment. we call on the heads of state and government to define and adopt this agenda. in this context, the multiannual financial framework is an effective instrument to help achieve economic growth in the eu. as regards the governance of the schengen system, we call for the use of the co-decision process and the involvement of the european parliament in all decisions concerning the free movement of persons, one of the eu's greatest achievements. we also support the accession of romania and bulgaria to the schengen area, as both the commission and the european parliament have repeatedly recognised that the two countries meet the necessary technical criteria.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the ep recommendation to the council on the 67th session of the un general assembly. the eu needs to increase its level of cohesion to remain a major player in an increasingly multipolar world, which requires concerted global action. i believe that maximum coordination is needed, common positions should be put forward and the eu's coherence and visibility as a global actor in the un should be improved. the eu and its member states are among the largest financial contributors to the un system. the eu-27 finances 39% of the un's normal budget and over 40% of un peacekeeping operations. i think it is important to ensure that the proportion of overall european aid channelled through the eu budget is not reduced and that it maintains its poverty and hunger dimension. given the eu's support for the 'education for all' initiative and its commitment to play a role in global health, 20% of all eu assistance should be allocated to basic social services, with a particular focus on free and universal access to basic health and primary education services.
in writing. − the eu's generalised system of preferences was introduced in the 1970s and the preferences granted are intended to complement the common commercial policy with the policy of development cooperation in favour of developing countries, representing a system of tariff preferences granted unilaterally by the eu to products originating in these countries. the gsp is based on three fundamental rules: preferences are general, non-reciprocal and non-discriminatory. the eu offers low customs duties or tax exemptions for 178 countries and territories, while granting special benefits to the 50 least developed countries and to those that apply labour and environmental protection standards. the gsp scheme can have a longer-term effect in that it improves the attractiveness of preference countries as inward processing locations, stimulating fis who subsequently wish to export to the eu market. in general, trade experts have had difficulty in identifying another positive effect of trade preferences on gsp exports, apart from the transfer of the rent associated with duty-free entry of goods.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the application of a system of tariff preferences, considering that a revision of this framework was a necessity. by removing high-income, upper-middle-income and those already in a preferential bilateral agreement with the union from the list of beneficiary countries, we ensure that countries that have achieved a high level of development are not unfairly favoured.
in writing. − i believe that the purpose of this key trade instrument - the gsp - is to enable developing countries to participate more intensively in international trade and thus generate additional export revenues, to support income growth and the implementation of their own sustainable development and poverty reduction policies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council applying a scheme of generalised tariff preferences, because it improves the coherence and coordination of the union’s aid for the development of the poorer countries in the world. i positively welcome the interconnection made between the concessions granted to those countries and the need for improvements, on their side, concerning human rights, labour rights and sustainability. this represents, in my view, the best way to guarantee the delivery of help to the people, by building up, at the same time, more trustworthy governance systems in their countries, which will result in a better future and more reliable partnership. unfortunately, the suggestion made by the s&d group to include more low-income countries in the generalised scheme of preferences (gsp) did not get enough support from other political groups. this report, nevertheless, is the result of a good compromise, which i am confident will manage to deliver a significant contribution to the development of those countries more in need.
in writing. − as recent developments in the euro area have shown, the increasing interdependence between european states in the context of the widening effects of the recession is the main challenge facing the european union in the short term. the possibility that economic and fiscal problems in one state can have effects of extreme gravity at union level is a major vulnerability that needs to be addressed through a set of pragmatic and effective public policies. the priority at this stage is to restore the credibility of monetary union, and several of the solutions proposed in these reports can make a decisive contribution towards achieving this objective. as the experience of recent years has shown the great importance of decisive action taken in good time, the adoption of procedures for supervising the financial stability of states facing economic problems is one of the solutions expected by markets and international investors from the european authorities. the legislative package needs to be strengthened by the procedures proposed by the european parliamentarians, in order to ensure the stability and credibility that european states need, and to prevent the spread of the difficulties to other economies in time. i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − the establishment of economic and budgetary monitoring measures for euro area countries experiencing financial disturbances is undoubtedly an important step in preventing situations of serious long-term financial destabilisation that automatically have a negative 'domino' effect on other member states, whether inside or outside the euro area. what i regret, however, is that these measures should have been taken much earlier and could have avoided or ameliorated financial imbalances in some member states, as is the case in greece today, which is going through a critical period of serious economic and budgetary difficulties which will be difficult to resolve without greatly affecting other countries. at the same time, i believe that strict legislation to this end encourages dialogue between the various european institutions, in order to decide in a responsible and coherent way on the most appropriate means of financial assistance to be provided to states in difficulty.
in writing. − this regulation comes in the context of the financial and sovereign debt crisis currently facing the union. several member states (portugal, ireland, greece and this week spain) have requested financial assistance. i support the commission's proposal that a member state whose currency is the euro should be subject to increased surveillance when it is experiencing or is likely to experience serious financial disturbances. it is necessary to return quickly to a normal situation and to protect the other euro area member states against possible negative spill-over effects. my country, romania, is not yet part of the euro area, but its economy is deeply linked to that of the countries that have adopted the single currency, and so any imbalance in the euro area is immediately felt in romanian markets. i therefore believe that countries that are not part of the euro area or are in the process of joining (romania wants to join the single currency) must also be co-decision-makers.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, as i too support extending the geographical scope of the ebrd operations to the south and east of the mediterranean. the main objective of the european bank for reconstruction and development is to contribute to economic progress and reconstruction. the report thus aims to support the transition to a market economy and to promote entrepreneurship and private initiative in the countries concerned. the political and economic situation in the countries of the southern and eastern mediterranean has led to the development of an ebrd strategy, which aims at a multi-stage approach tailored to the specific requirements of these countries. i draw attention to the fact that the bank should contribute to the transition towards energy efficiency and an open and inclusive market economy, while taking into account the social, civic and human rights context. i also believe that the principles of banking prudence, transparency and anti-fraud should be taken into account in the ebrd's activities.

in writing. − the european union wishes to support the efforts of the countries of the southern mediterranean to transition the region towards a market economy and a pluralist democratic society, and the extension of the european bank for reconstruction and development's area of activity in the area is the implementation of this support of the union and the international community for the hopes generated by the 'arab spring'. i welcome the support of the ebrd for projects aimed at, inter alia, promoting sustainable development, poverty eradication, environmental protection and human rights protection, as well as encouraging the private sector, with a focus on developing entrepreneurship among young people.
in writing. - the events that gave rise to the 'arab spring' have not only resulted in the democratisation of the states of the southern and eastern mediterranean, but also in the opening of a dialogue and long-term cooperation with the structures of the european union, which can only be of benefit to the states concerned, with a view to their rapid and sustainable reconstruction. therefore, the inclusion of these countries in the scope of the ebrd will certainly facilitate the transition to an open market economy, but will also encourage cooperation with the eu countries in various sectors of the economy, one of which is the energy sector itself, which is of priority importance in the current global context. on the other hand, i am concerned about the possible consequences of this geographical expansion of the ebrd's operations, namely disruptions caused by various fraudulent or non-transparent actions by these states, since the transition from a closed communist regime to a democratic, open society is not an easy or risk-free process.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the decision on the amendments to the agreement establishing the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) to extend the geographical scope of the ebrd's operations to the south and east of the mediterranean. since its inception in 1991, the ebrd has supported the countries of central and eastern europe in their transition to an open market economy and in promoting private initiative and entrepreneurship. in response to the economic and political situation in the countries of the southern and eastern mediterranean, the ebrd has developed a gradual approach to its business start-up, which will take into account the specificities of the region. the geographical scope of the ebrd should therefore also include the countries of the southern and eastern mediterranean in order to promote similar objectives. the representatives of the union on the governing bodies of the ebrd should encourage the ebrd to expand its work on private sector development in order to contribute, also through its financing, to the achievement of a socially and environmentally sustainable society. the contribution of the ebrd to the transition to an open, energy-efficient and socially inclusive market economy should be encouraged, while taking into account the social context, civil and human rights.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the multiannual financial framework and own resources. i voted for paragraph 3, where parliament insists that the eu budget should present an appropriate balance between own resources and expenditure, as required by the treaty. the next multiannual financial framework (mff) cannot be adopted without a political agreement on reforming the own resources system, ending current cuts and other corrective mechanisms and leading to more transparency, fairness and sustainability. we welcome the legislative proposals made by the commission on 29 june 2011 on reforming the own resources system, including the proposal for a financial transaction tax (ftt) and a new vat as own resources. these measures aim to reduce the gdp-based share of member states' contributions to the eu budget by up to 40% by 2020, thus supporting member states' consolidation efforts. i voted against amendment no 4, which deletes from the text the part insisting on the principle of unity in the eu budget and stressing that all eu policies and programmes should be included in the mff together with the corresponding funding, thus helping to ensure transparency, predictability and accountability.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the eu-colombia-peru trade agreement, as this agreement aims to open up markets for goods, services, public procurement and investment and to promote global economic development. the aim of the agreement is to reduce poverty and create new employment opportunities, improve working conditions and raise living standards by liberalizing and expanding trade and investment between the territories of the countries party to the agreement. the union is the second most important trading partner for colombia and peru. the planned trade agreement provides for the full liberalisation of trade in industrial products and fisheries, which could lead to a long-term increase of up to 1.3% of colombian gdp and up to 0.7% of peruvian gdp. an important part of the agreement is devoted to respect for human rights and democratic principles. failure to comply with them would also lead to the possibility of denouncing or suspending the agreement in part or in full. in this regard, we call on both andean countries to ensure the establishment of a transparent and binding roadmap on human rights and labour rights.
in writing. − the appointment of a european union special representative for human rights reflects the strong commitment of the member states and the european institutions to the regional and international protection of the human rights regime and democratic values. in order for the special representative's actions to be able to fully exploit the potential of this function, active and effective cooperation between the special representative and the european legislator is necessary. although the appointment of the representative remains the prerogative of the council, i consider that the presentation of an annual report of his work to all the union authorities, as well as the hearing/exchange of views with the ep's committee responsible, is an essential condition for the transparency and legitimacy of the eu's actions to protect human rights internationally. they also support the need to establish effective cooperative relations between the special representative and international institutions or non-governmental organisations with a long tradition in the protection of human rights, and to provide substantial institutional and financial support from the european authorities for the fulfilment of the mandate of the future representative.
in writing. − recent events in syria, where the assad regime's abuses have turned to carnage, and in libya after the removal of gaddafi, as well as the deteriorating human rights situation in many other countries, make the need for the appointment of an eu special representative for human rights more urgent than ever. in the eu treaties, there is this firm commitment to promote human rights and democracy in all its external actions. the eusr shall be given a strong, independent and flexible mandate. it must be given the freedom to act quickly and effectively in the face of events that require an urgent response. i hope that we will have close cooperation with the council in this respect, given parliament's constant and substantial concern for the defence of human rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a european parliament recommendation to the council on the eu special representative for human rights, because i believe that, given the central importance of the human rights doctrine in the eu and for its external relations, the appointment of the eu special representative (eusr) for human rights constitutes a matter of coherence and effectiveness of eu action. the adopted report contains a list of recommendations to the council, some of the more important being, in my view, those stressing the importance of transparency of the eusr selection procedures, the crucial need to provide him/her with a strong, independent and flexible mandate and the need for cooperation with representatives of local, regional and national civil society, ngos, experts, and regional and international organisations acting in this field. it is also important that the representative for human rights be supported in his/her work by sufficient human and financial resources: this is not only a matter of effectiveness of his/her action, but also a crucial requirement for granting the eusr the sufficient visibility of its position, crucial for the achievement and diffusion of the eu’s goals in the field of hr protection.
in writing. − the appointment of the eu special representative (eusr) for human rights would strengthen the visibility and coherence of the union’s human rights policy and its commitment to human rights around the world. although it is formally a council decision, the special representative should work together with the council working group on human rights and its political and security committee. the parliament should play its part by keeping the special representative under regular review during his/her mandate and making annual progress reports. the mandate should be flexible, strong and ensure independence in order to act swiftly and decisively to promote democracy, the rule of law, international justice and international humanitarian law worldwide.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the eu special representative for human rights. the treaty on european union reaffirms the eu's commitment to promoting human rights and democracy in all its external action, while ensuring coherence and consistency between the different areas of its external action and between these and its other policies. the eusr for human rights should act and speak on behalf of the union, reflecting the common and indivisible responsibility of all eu institutions and member states for the protection and promotion of human rights worldwide. the appointment of an eu special representative for human rights should increase the visibility and coherence of the eu's human rights policy as a fundamental component of the eu's common foreign and security policy (cfsp) and contribute to promoting the eu's human rights profile globally. i believe that, in the implementation of his mandate, the special representative for human rights should cooperate with representatives of local, regional and national civil society, ngos, experts, as well as regional and international organisations working in the field of human rights and democracy.
in writing. - unfortunately, a series of outbreaks of violence, fuelled by arms trafficking, often illegal, persists. there is an international legal framework, verification mechanisms, but also plenty of loopholes and a lot of hypocrisy in the criteria for transferring weapons to sensitive areas. often, profit-making criteria take precedence over the dramas fueled by the arms trade. that is why i believe that a redefinition of these criteria would be welcome, to include aspects such as good governance, strict respect for human rights and the fight against corruption that accompanies the arms trade. the eu must play a greater role in this monitoring mechanism, in defining the criteria and in negotiating their acceptance by all signatories to the arms trade treaty. if this arms trade cannot be excluded from the life of nations, we must ensure that they are used only for self-defense and under strict rules.
in writing. − the deterioration of the situation in the democratic republic of congo, in particular the continuing atrocities in kivu province, is of grave concern. the number of casualties has increased at a shocking rate, with civilians, especially children, women and the elderly, being the most affected. thousands of women have been raped, mutilated, and killed, and many of the survivors are infected with hiv. the perpetrators of these crimes must be punished. the fight against impunity and the strengthening of the judicial system are therefore needed. we should insist more on the creation of a special tribunal to try cases of genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity. in a country where three quarters of the population live in poverty and which is facing a serious refugee crisis, the lack of democratic elections and human rights violations are locking congolese society into a vicious cycle of instability, violence and underdevelopment. i therefore call on the commission to act to ensure that the congolese authorities implement the recommendations of the report of the eu eom.
i am convinced that of all the instruments and institutions created by the crisis, the european semester is, in my view, perhaps the most important and can become the most effective instrument for preventing and correcting financial, budgetary and economic imbalances and for preventing a new crisis in the future. i hope that the european commission will be equally firm on how the member states will implement the recommendations, because what we call the european semester is basically a continuous process, which lasts for a year and will be repeated every year. but i would also like to stress a very important aspect, which concerns the national parliaments: the role of national parliaments in the european semester. i would like to tell you that, at the initiative of the danish presidency, a meeting of the national parliaments took place this spring, which also discussed their role in the european semester. i noted then the desire of these national parliaments to be part of this process. national parliaments now have a direct say in how governments take the necessary steps to implement the recommendations made in the european semester. and i think it is important to continue this exchange of experience between national parliaments, at the initiative of the european parliament, so that they really feel that they are a direct, responsible part of this process which is the european semester.
corporate law is particularly important and, together with corporate governance, can, if well written, provide an impetus for foreign investment. whether company law and corporate governance are to be dealt with together or separately, i believe it is essential for european companies to benefit from a flexible regulatory framework, and this can only be done within a code of conduct. the 'apply or explain' principle must therefore be the solution, with strict application of sanctions, where exceptions to the rules are not explained in a transparent and comprehensive manner. the code of conduct must also be a single, community code, otherwise we cannot speak of european legislation. the code of conduct in this case must apply to listed companies because only the number of shareholders is important in this process; other indicators, such as turnover or the number of employees, are socially irrelevant. of course, there are also situations where rules can go beyond the flexible framework of a code of conduct. and i want to give you an example of conflicts of interest: they need to be sanctioned and discouraged, to protect investors and employees. i hope commissioner barnier agrees that we need investment and jobs created through market instruments and not through strict rules which are seen by investors as obstacles in their way.

in writing. – with eu unemployment hitting record levels and forecasts of a dramatic economic outlook for the months ahead we, as socialists, should come up with a set of concrete measures to boost jobs for the citizens of europe. the eu needs a dynamic and inclusive european labour market and we need investments for job creation, mainstreaming of the ilo’s decent work agenda, protection of labour law in smes, combating of illegal work and forced self-employment, and minimum wages to fight in-work poverty and social dumping. moreover, we should continue to fight to obtain some other important aspects which are essential for the wealth of the citizens like: solidarity in taxation systems, coordinated collective bargaining as a factor for social cohesion and the fight against in-work poverty through living wages. to accelerate job creation, we need proposals towards a european investment plan, a coherent european industrial strategy and investment in public services, based on new sources of revenue, including a financial transactions tax and eurobonds, giving priority to investments that promote a sustainable economy, quality jobs and social justice. finally, i appreciate that the ec sent a strong message to governments to lift restrictions on labour market access for workers from bulgaria and romania.
in writing. in its communication on employment of 19 april, the european commission refers to the importance of a minimum wage and decent working conditions, and thus distances itself from the strategy of austerity and labour market liberalisation that some european countries continue to pursue. the austerity administered to workers, as we have seen with regret in greece and spain, has had nothing but disastrous results, causing unemployment and poverty. the european commission's proposal can also be improved by introducing more concrete aspects of political direction. the european union urgently needs a common investment plan that prioritises investments that create quality jobs, such as in education, health or research. to support these investments, member states have no alternative but to show solidarity. the financial transaction tax and the pooling of part of the public debt are a necessity if the tragic history of a divided europe is not to be repeated.
in writing. history provides too many examples of devastating industrial accidents involving dangerous chemicals that take lives and destroy the environment. although community legislation has evolved to reduce the frequency and impact of these accidents, since the accident in hungary in 2010, we have all understood that further improvements and revisions of community rules are needed to strengthen the protection of communities and the environment against these potential catastrophes. for several years i have opposed a mining project in romania which, in the event of an accident, would damage a vast region, valuable both from the point of view of the environment and biodiversity, and from the cultural and historical point of view, by pollution with cyanide. the public is rightly concerned that the initiators of such projects deny transparency and public access to objective and balanced information. they should be legally obliged to provide accurate and complete information, guaranteeing transparency. i appreciate the fact that this report focuses on public information and the rights of citizens to know about the potential dangers that lie around them. i will continue to promote transparency and public debate on other projects, such as shale gas and mining projects.
in writing. i would like to welcome the results of the negotiations with the council and the compromise package reached. this update of the legislation brings the added security that eu citizens needed. the legislation in question strengthens the policy of preventing chemical accidents and of responding to them by operators and authorities responsible in the event of accidents, in order to ensure a high level of protection of human health and the environment. in addition to requiring operators to implement a series of measures to continuously improve major accident prevention, stricter standards for industrial plant inspections are also introduced. it is of the utmost importance for the public to be able to access information on their legitimate concerns regarding the safety of the environment in which they live, as well as to have access to information on how to react in the event of accidents involving dangerous substances. in this respect, i welcome the fact that the compromise package includes these rights mentioned above, as well as provisions on public participation in decision-making.
on behalf of the s&d group. first of all, i would like to thank the rapporteur for taking into account the recommendations of her colleagues, both during the preparation of this report and with regard to the amendments. in my view, the purpose of these regulations is to ensure that people have access to accurate and relevant information about the food they eat. in recent years, european union legislation has made great progress on food labelling, and as a result, transparency and consumer protection have increased. but the old dietary laws are a hindrance to this development. that is why i welcomed the commission's proposal and the improvements made to it in the committee on the environment, public health and food safety. one of my main concerns in this case was the issue of labelling and advertising of infant formula and infant formula. as we know, in many cases, even in spite of advice or regulation, breast-milk substitutes are aggressively promoted. meanwhile, statistics confirm that the percentage of mothers who breastfeed remains low throughout the european union. legislative loopholes are exploited which either allow the rules on advertising to be circumvented or make their enforcement more difficult. i opposed the inclusion in these regulations of so-called 'growth milk', the product intended for young children. we had a good reason: there is no evidence to support that this product offers any nutritional benefits compared to a normal, balanced diet. this product is not a food for special medical purposes; it is just a costly substitute for regular milk and a balanced diet. because it is still in stores, advertising claims made by manufacturers about the quality of the product must be very strictly justified. the purpose of these regulations is clear: to help people make informed food choices and to opt for a healthy and balanced diet. in writing. after more than 30 years, the rules on food for special nutritional purposes as laid down in framework directive 2009/39/ec no longer meet consumer needs and the latest market developments. we need a legislative framework that will provide citizens with a high level of food safety, especially when food is intended for vulnerable groups such as infants, young children and people with special illnesses. european citizens must be properly informed when choosing what to eat and not be misled when they opt for a healthy and balanced diet.
in writing. the european union has always had a model legislative framework for foodstuffs with a special nutritional purpose which is highly appreciated. however, recent developments in the food market and food law have shown that major changes are needed. i consider that the application of the concept of 'food with a special nutritional purpose' on which this framework directive is based, in the light of the evolution of the market situation, has led to considerable problems for the parties concerned and for the supervisory authorities. food safety, especially for food intended for vulnerable groups such as infants, young children and people with special diseases, is an essential condition for its free movement and for the proper functioning of the internal market within the european union. i therefore believe that a european solidarity policy is needed at union level, with legislative measures to eliminate these differences between national legislation on foodstuffs for special nutritional uses, thus allowing their free movement and creating a level playing field for competition.
if nothing is done before the quota system expires in 2015, the high quota values will prevent the most productive farmers from benefiting from new opportunities, while the least productive farmers in disadvantaged areas, especially mountain areas, would face great difficulties due to a significant drop in prices following the drastic elimination of the quota system. in this context, the question naturally arises as to whether and what kind of measures should be taken to ensure a slow transition to a market policy in the dairy sector before the expiry of the milk quota system on 31 march 2015. does the commission have the dairy policy instruments in place to facilitate this transition? because it's clear that before making certain decisions, we need to assess their impact on this sector.
after the abolition of quotas in 2015, a major change will take place in the dairy sector. the new legislation aims to increase the bargaining power of milk producers to get the best price. in this regard, their involvement in producer organisations should be further encouraged. the dairy sector is the only sector in agriculture where producers can collectively negotiate their price. this ensures fair living conditions for farmers and a rational development of production. despite the fact that in romania there are not many large farms involved in milk processing, my country is in the middle of the ranking of the largest milk producers in the european union. they must be supported and protected in the post-quota period to ensure a stable future for the sector.
member of the commission. − mr president, i will try. i would like to thank members for their contributions to this debate. i have listened carefully and i assure you that i will pass your varied comments to my colleague, dacian cioloş, who by the way is not here because he is on official business in china. it is clear that the milk sector is a very important part of our agricultural policy. that is why the commission pays close attention to developments in this sector. concerning the quota, some of you want a ‘softer landing’. let me add a few words to what i have already said. i am aware that in 2008 parliament asked for a more flexible approach by ‘setting of quota’ at eu level. this was not adopted because it would have had an uncontrollable and unforeseeable impact on dairy production. instead, a 1 % annual quota increase over the period 2009-2013 was retained. some others want to keep the quota system beyond 2015. i want to make three remarks concerning this point. firstly, we have recently put in place the milk package, which is our first response to the concerns about the quota system being phased out. secondly, the phasing out of quota will end a rigid milk production system which has hampered farmers from gaining experience in adjusting supply to demand. thirdly, the commission will come up with a report by the end of 2012 with an assessment of the market situation and the conditions for phasing out the quota. as to the market situation, i would like to remind you that dairy product prices have been particularly high over the past two years. over the past months, the trend has changed. this coincides with the seasonal pattern of milk production and prices and is reinforced by milk production in the union and in the other main milk-producing regions. prices seem to have reached bottom and some are even trending higher already. in any case, safety-net mechanisms are available for operators who so far have only proposed butter for private storage. this is a good sign of confidence in a positive evolution of the market.
