in writing. − the introduction of a single legislative instrument on companies in the eu countries encourages the expansion of business cooperation between them and provides a clearer framework for the creation of new companies. as regards the question of the operation of companies, i believe that we must now concentrate on the development of european accounting and auditing standards, which will simplify the procedures for the establishment and operation of companies, especially smes, uniformly applicable throughout the european union. it is well known that in some countries the procedure for setting up a company is time-consuming and expensive, while in other countries it can take only one day at a much lower cost. such discrepancies are unacceptable in the context of the desire for economic unity at the level of the european community. simplification of procedures would also reduce the costs incurred by smes in drawing up complex financial statements, which would thus be easier to understand and interpret by interested parties.

in writing. − the european union cannot achieve the objectives set by the europe 2020 strategy without supporting investment projects necessary for the creation of new jobs in a variety of areas, from vocational training and retraining for people interested in changing jobs to investments in the green economy, health, social services, information technology and new technologies. it is essential that all member states develop national employment plans as part of their 2012 national reform programmes and then implement them on the basis of a well-defined timetable, precisely in order to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the european union needs a growth and recovery strategy that is much more focused on creating new jobs and encouraging mobility in the european labour market, in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. unemployment in the eu member states is currently very high, especially among young people, which is affecting the potential for economic growth. the european union and the member states must therefore focus their efforts on stimulating job creation and vocational retraining programmes. at the same time, it is important that the eu makes full use of the right to free movement of workers and encourages their mobility in order to increase the growth potential at european level. in this respect, it is essential that all restrictions on the european labour market for romanian and bulgarian citizens be removed as soon as possible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the commission communication entitled 'towards a job-creating recovery'. the unemployment rate increased from 9,5% in 2010 to 10,2% in 2012, and the total number of jobs lost from 2008 to the present has reached six million. austerity measures aimed at fiscal consolidation applied by several member states have contributed to a significant increase in the unemployment rate, and the commission's estimates indicate a stagnation of eu gdp in 2012 and a recession in several member states. we believe that the development of entrepreneurship and business creation should be promoted as a means of creating more jobs and we call on the commission and the member states to invest more in these areas, in particular through public procurement and access to finance. we also ask the commission to support the member states in their fight against unemployment and, in particular, youth unemployment, using the unused resources of the structural funds. i believe it is important that member states make better use of eures, as eures plays a key role in the functioning of the internal market by advising workers and jobseekers on their rights in other member states.
in writing. − it is important that the european commission ensures that specific attention is paid to female genital mutilation as part of the programme to combat violence against women, and at the same time that member states take firm action to combat these illegal practices. in this context, i believe that it is necessary to finance information and education programmes to make women themselves aware that genital mutilation is not a traditional practice that gives ethnic and historical specificity to the populations to which they belong, but forms of violence against women. many women in these regions consider it an honor and a duty to submit unquestioningly to such practices, which are often performed by women who are skilled healers or midwives and who are valued and respected within the group. at the same time, it is important to fund and organise programmes for the education of girls and boys on equality from an early age, in order to avoid segregation of society on the basis of sex and gender discrimination which is manifested by these acts of violence against women, which are these genital mutilations.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the ep's motion for a resolution on ending female genital mutilation, as it is a serious abuse affecting 140 million women and girls today. according to the world health organization, at least 500,000 women and girls in europe have been affected by female genital mutilation, and an estimated 180,000 girls are at risk. according to experts, these figures are underestimates and do not take into account second-generation migrants and undocumented migrants. any form of female genital mutilation is an act of violence against women and girls, constituting a violation of their fundamental rights, in particular the right to privacy and security of the person and the right to physical and mental health. calls on the member states to continue to ratify international instruments and implement them through comprehensive legislation prohibiting all forms of female genital mutilation and providing for effective sanctions against perpetrators of such practices. i call on the commission to give priority to ending violence against women and girls and, by allocating adequate financial resources, to actively support specific and innovative programmes both in the eu and in third countries.
in writing. − according to the findings of the french health authorities, a french manufacturer (poly implant prothèse) is under investigation for the fraudulent use of low-quality material (industrial silicone) different from the material indicated in the documents submitted for conformity assessment. a lack of both clinical and epidemiological data on the potential risks of pip breast implants was noticed. i voted in favour of: strengthening the controls on medical devices already on the market, including those using samples; improving supervision by national authorities of notified bodies and ensuring consistency across member states; and improving the functioning of the vigilance system for medical devices, for example by facilitating and actively encouraging patients, patients’ associations, patient groups and healthcare professionals to report all adverse events and harmful effects to the competent authorities and by setting up a centralised procedure for gathering and treating notifications on adverse effects and on the withdrawal of devices from the market. the medical devices directive needs to be revised, with the aim of introducing a capacity to detect and minimise the risk of fraud, and focusing on provisions on market surveillance, vigilance, and the functioning and tasks of notified bodies, so as to avoid a repetition of the pip case.
in writing. − i consider that a single european data base for the breast implants should be established to bring together information about medical devices on the market, the registration of economic operations, vigilance and market surveillance, clinical investigations, notified bodies (which check compliance with eu rules) and ec certificates issued.
in writing. − although the pip scandal was a clear case of fraudulent and criminal activity, it has highlighted a number of other practices with regards to the promotion and sale of implants which need to be addressed. there are serious concerns about advertising of breast implants for cosmetic surgery. advertising typically does not inform the consumer properly, and many women are not even aware that implants need replacing every ten years or so which means many operations over the course of a woman's lifetime. the s&d group was right to table an amendment calling for a ban on the advertising of breast implants for cosmetic purposes, and i regret that it was not adopted. in cases where the implants are needed following surgery, for example because of breast cancer, these adverts are not necessary. in all other cases, we should not be encouraging women to commit to a series of unnecessary operations over their lifetime for cosmetic purposes, with all the associated risk and cost.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on defective silicone gel breast implants produced by the french company pip (poly implant prothèse). tests carried out by the french authorities on the physical integrity of a sample of silicone pip breast implant revealed defects in the pip breast implant coating which were not detected in other implants available on the market. because of the lack of registration of breast implants at european level, the total number of women who have received implants is not known. based on data provided by the european commission, it is estimated that around 400 000 pip silicone breast implants have been sold worldwide. the highest number of pip silicone breast implants were sold in the united kingdom (40 000), france (30 000), spain (10 000), germany (7 500) and portugal (2 000). the case of pip implants demonstrated the non-compliance of the current certification system with the essential health and safety requirements, the existence of deficiencies in the controls of notified bodies and the lack of oversight of notified bodies by the competent national authorities in accordance with the medical devices directive (2007/47/ec). i recommend that the medical devices directive be revised to introduce fraud detection and risk reduction capability, in particular on the provisions on market surveillance, to avoid a repeat of the case.

the reporter. i would like to begin by thanking colleagues from all the political groups for the good cooperation we have had in drafting this report. the tachograph plays a crucial role in checking compliance with the rules on driving time and rest periods by professional road transport drivers, contributing to improving road safety, working conditions for drivers and fair competition between road transport undertakings. the new proposal for a regulation sets out a number of technical measures, such as: improving the functions of the tachograph, wireless communications to reduce traffic controls, introducing a harmonised interface with other applications of intelligent transport systems, but also non-technical measures, such as: improving the credibility of workshops, increasing the protection of the driver's card against fraudulent manipulation, improving the training of control agents, a minimum level of harmonisation of penalties, modernising the rules of use. the commission is also proposing that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment and the protection of the health of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the public authorities, including the provision of services, and to extend the scope of the directive to include the provision of services to the public authorities. we ask the commission to analyse existing technical solutions, compatibility issues and data protection issues before proposing the merging of the functionalities of these cards. the tran committee stresses that in the interests of a clear, efficient, proportionate and uniform process for the implementation of social security rules in road transport, it is essential that the member states' authorities apply the rules in a uniform manner. the manual setting of the driver's activity is essential for compliance with social legislation and the correct use of the tachograph. by amendment 21, the tran committee proposes to use the definition of daily working time for the purposes of this regulation provided by the court of justice of the european union in case c-394 of 1992. in order to improve road safety and social conditions for professional drivers, the tran committee proposes that by 2020 all vehicles not exempted from the application of this regulation should be equipped with a smart tachograph. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services by rail, road and inland waterway. in no case shall remote communication for control purposes lead to the automatic application of fines or penalties to the driver or the transport undertaking. as regards workshops, member states shall take measures to prevent conflicts of interest between installers or workshops and road transport undertakings. the tran committee requires that the audits of the unintended technique cover, per year, at least 20 per cent of the authorised workshops. also, in order to reduce red tape, the driver card is issued, upon request, by the competent authority within 15 days of receipt of the application. i would like to stress, commissioner, that this regulation is considered a unique opportunity to amend regulation 561 on social legislation, which is why we have many amendments tabled in this respect. i personally do not support them, because i do not think that the digital tachograph regulation is the right time to change regulation 561, but we also have some amendments on certain exceptions which can introduce some flexibility. i look forward to hearing from my colleagues.
social legislation in the field of road transport improves safety and working conditions for drivers and ensures fair competition between businesses. violation of social norms on minimum rest periods can lead to accumulated fatigue for drivers, thus affecting road safety. companies may also be tempted to break the law in order to gain significant competitive advantages. in these circumstances, the regulation needs to be revised to reduce the possibility of fraud. road transport needs to become safer and more efficient, and this can be achieved by increasing the reliability of recording equipment and reducing the administrative burden. the tachograph must provide reliable data to allow an effective control.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, thank you very much for your remarks on this important issue. the tachograph has proven to be a useful instrument to increase road safety, and it has really worked well. now we need to adapt the rules in line with new technology and obtained experience. harmonised enforcement is extremely important; but i think that there is increasing cooperation between member states. also we, the commission, try to follow and push these practices in the right direction to have more harmonised enforcement. this is in the hands of the member states, but this is an important issue on which i share the concerns expressed about harmonised enforcement. as regards costs: our impact assessment shows that there will be practically no additional costs, and it is hoped that there will be no additional burden for businesses. it is just a development of new technology which is in many cases more convenient and can be better used. i would also like to emphasise that this proposal already extends the exemption for the use of tachographs from 50 km to 100 km. that is quite an extension. it also reduces the costs and the administrative burden for the business as a whole. if we go further and extend this extension to 150 km it can pose some serious problems concerning the overall social acquis in road transport and also have other potentially important consequences. extensions have already increased from 50 km to 100 km. this increase was not emphasised today, but i think it is quite a reasonable proposal.

member of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, i think i should start with something which many of you mentioned: water as a public good, water as a human right. i would like to be clear on the commission’s position about this because we have just finished those discussions also in rio. there we have just agreed to reaffirm our commitments regarding the human right to safe drinking water and sanitation, to be progressively carried out for our populations with full respect for national sovereignty. the commission was one of the most active supporters of this and of the two other related millennium development goals on access to drinking water and sanitation, and this was reaffirmed in rio. so i would like it to be clear what the commission’s position is on this. however, it should not be confused with the question of whether water should be free for all. because if we go that way i can guarantee that we will not reach exactly the goal which we would all like to reach. so we have pricing of water as one of the tools in our water framework directive, and when we are implementing the water framework directive we are also looking at that, so i think it is important that this distinction is made. it is also important because we all understand that water today is one of the fundamental finite resources – and i stress ‘finite’. that is why we have also pushed so much for it to be included on the agenda in rio as one of the goals and targets which we would like to see in the rio document. so yes, we should fight for that globally and also at european union level, and the blueprint should absolutely be one of the important parts of that fight. if we continue with the use of water resources as we are currently doing, estimates are that we will have an approximate 40% shortage of water globally by 2030. so it is absolutely an issue which we need to address in a proper way. it is truly a complex issue. as you all know there is a quantity and vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i must admit that this topic is very close to my heart because in my former political life, when we regained independence in our country, this was a major element in our economic policy – to attract foreign direct investments. and we were quite successful in this. the commission welcomes the report on the attractiveness of investing in europe and thanks ms kratsa-tsagaropoulou for her work. in the current economic climate we need to create the necessary conditions to offer our companies and citizens the best possible business environment to produce and to compete in europe. it is true that the rise of emerging economies has intensified competition, but it has also created new opportunities for the eu through trade and investment in international value chains. foreign direct investment is an important part of this. the eu is the world’s leading host of foreign direct investment, attracting investments worth eur 225 billion from the rest of the world in 2011 alone. however, the eu’s share of the world’s inward foreign direct investment has declined substantially – from 45% in 2001 to 23% in 2010. a detailed breakdown by country reveals that the decline in foreign direct investment has been highly uneven across member states. this means that we cannot relax, but we should rather continue to improve our framework conditions in order to keep our good international position. it also suggests that we can learn from each other in europe as regards best practice if we wish to attract foreign investments. and basically we know what attracts foreign direct investment. the main reasons the eu is still an attractive location for foreign direct investment is our highly-educated workforce, low foreign direct investment regulations, declining regulatory burdens for starting and elaborating a business, extensive investor protection laws, high quality investment promotion agencies and various support measures often linked to regional policy measures. other important factors include a high level of productivity and technological infrastructure such as research and development and ict endowment. i am pleased to see that these issues are all addressed in parliament’s report. as a continuation along these lines, the commission is now preparing a communication on industrial policy. the long-term goals of our flagship product, europe 2020, remain fully valid. we have made very good progress in the deployment of industrial policy agreed in 2010. we will continue to push harder to establish the appropriate framework conditions to release the creative capacity of european industry. the main areas currently considered for further action are: access to finance, improvement of the single market, industrial innovation and globalisation challenges for eu industry and small- and medium-sized enterprises. the commission’s policy approach takes the same starting point as parliament’s report and we also identify the same areas where action is needed. as regards some of the concrete proposals in parliament’s report, i note in particular the call for a european observatory for foreign direct investment and the urge for improved international regulatory cooperation. these are areas where work is already being done. over the past years the european commission has developed several regulatory dialogues with our major trading partners and we have projects for the exchange of good practice among member states as concerns foreign direct investment promotion. i cannot go through all the details of this detailed parliament report here, but i welcome the broad approach of the report and the many areas for constructive cooperation ahead. we started today’s sitting with a discussion on the development of a single european railway area; this is one thing that shows that when we develop good infrastructure we attract investments. you have on various occasions discussed the single market act and will continue to discuss the next proposal. one of the most important aspects of this is to attract foreign direct investment. therefore, everything is in our hands.
in writing. to attract investors, member states and regions need to offer local specific advantages. i believe that, alongside the fiscal and legislative advantages, the eu's cohesion policy has been a real driver of change, making a major contribution to convergence and growth within the union. the existence of competitive infrastructure is also a basic condition for attracting investors in the context of the new challenges we are facing. in addition, the main prerequisites for the competitiveness and attractiveness of the regions are the promotion of research, innovation and technological development and the availability of appropriate high-quality vocational training programmes for people in the european regions. in order to strengthen knowledge and innovation as engines of future economic growth and economic competitiveness, i believe that it is necessary to: improve the quality of education, to apply research results in the economy and to promote innovation and knowledge transfer across the union.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, it is a pleasure to discuss with you the eu’s trade policy towards our eastern neighbours. i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr ransdorf, for having taken the initiative of this report, as well as all the honourable members who have participated in the constructive discussions on the text. it covers not only trade in goods but also cooperation in other related fields, for example investment protection, streamlining customs and border procedures, reducing technical and other non-tariff barriers to trade, strengthening sanitary and phytosanitary rules and other measures. as you know, the last months have been particularly important for our trade relations with most of our eastern partners. the negotiations on a deep and comprehensive free trade area (in short a dcfta) with ukraine were completed in december and the two parties intend to proceed to the initialling of the dcfta text on 16 july, once the current legal review of the text is finalised. it is now up to ukraine to create the overall political conditions which will allow its signature and ratification. in any case, i want to stress that there cannot be provisional application of the association agreement, and for that matter of the dcfta provisions, before the decision concerning the signature of the association agreement and before parliament has given its view. the first part of this year has also seen important progress of our bilateral relations with moldova, georgia and armenia; three partners with whom dcfta negotiations have been launched. the negotiations advanced well, thanks to the thorough preparatory process carried out over the past years. it is now key that throughout the negotiations the pace of reform started during the preparation phase is maintained. indeed the negotiations of a dcfta are still only the beginning of a long process of reform. with belarus and azerbaijan, the commission is committed to pursuing a similar agenda as with the other eastern partners. however, the commission considers that wto membership and basic reforms in the trade and trade-related part of the economies of the partner countries are the prerequisite for an enhanced trade agenda. the decision to enter into trade negotiations should depend on the real capacity of the trade partner to effectively implement dcfta conditions. unfortunately azerbaijan and belarus do not currently comply with these conditions and do not currently dispose of such a capacity. let me however stress that our bilateral trade relations with the eastern partners cannot be separated from the broader political context in which they operate. this message applies across the board to all our neighbours. i wish to recall that this is also in line with the basic principles of the eastern partnership, according to which dcftas are an integral part of the broader association agreements and therefore cannot be envisaged in isolation. given the human rights situation, belarus only participates in the multilateral track of the eastern partnership. i believe that overall the report prepared by the rapporteur mr ransdorf reflects well the fact that parliament and the commission share the same views on trade relations with our eastern partners. i take the numerous amendments proposed, as well as the large support in favour of the report, as proof of parliament’s commitment to promoting stronger bilateral trade ties with our eastern neighbours. i welcome very much the role played by the euronest parliamentary assembly, which is very supportive in this respect. i can assure you that the commission fully agrees on the need to promote an ambitious trade agenda as a vector of reform for our eastern partners and shares the willingness to drive such an agenda forward. we all know that this will not be an easy task. therefore, it will be essential that parliament and the commission continue working in very close cooperation.
in writing. the 2011 revolutionary movements in north africa shifted the focus to the southern dimension of the neighbourhood policy, to the detriment of the eastern partnership. i believe that we need to revitalize the union's relations with its eastern partners, in particular through association agreements. they can be an effective tool to persuade participating states to adopt important reforms for the democratisation of their political regimes. at the same time, efforts to democratise are directly conditioned on improving the living conditions of citizens, creating a strong civil society, as well as ensuring freedom of the press and strengthening democratic institutions. in this respect, i welcome the creation in 2008 of a civil society institution under the umbrella of the eastern partnership, which fosters dialogue between governments participating in the programme and civil society. however, some non-compliance with respect to workers' rights persists in states such as georgia, where child labour exploitation is still a reality. ukraine is another example of a partner state with a deficient judicial system, which prevents the completion of the association agreement with it. that is why i am calling for our eastern partners to undertake internal reforms that will give them more credibility externally.
in writing. the relationship with the eu's eastern partners is of particular importance, both economically and socially. beyond the human rights and rule of law aspects, we must give due weight to the pragmatic dimension of these relations. by creating deep and comprehensive free trade areas, we can stimulate partner countries to continue the reforms they have started, so as to achieve a stable and predictable economic environment, in which the democratic principles on which the union is founded are respected. moreover, we can facilitate alignment with eu rules by gradually removing trade barriers as russia and china become more present in the region. in areas such as research, development and innovation, ict and tourism, cooperation between the eu and the eastern partners needs to be strengthened. the commission proposal on the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, which envisages a 40% increase in the funding available for the neighbourhood policy, is therefore welcomed. i also hope that the eu black sea strategy will be developed, given its importance in the eu's external energy strategy, with concrete perspectives for strengthening energy security and diversifying supply.
i stress the importance of macro-regional strategies and that they must be based on multi-level governance, ensuring the involvement of local and regional authorities, as well as representatives of civil society, universities and research centres, both in the process of developing and implementing macro-regional strategies. in order to ensure the proper implementation of macro-regional strategies, we ask that the operational programmes of the member states also focus on the priorities of these strategies. we call on the commission and the council to give their full support to the approach taken for the danube basin, which should be subject to regular assessment and monitoring. in order to facilitate the implementation of the european union strategy for the danube region, parliament has since 2010 requested the allocation of eur 1,5 million for the preparatory action aimed at creating the governance model for the implementation of the european union strategy for the danube region.
macro-regional strategies are beneficial as they offer new perspectives for territorial cooperation projects. they can also ensure better coordination between regional programmes and the europe 2020 objectives. in this context, i would like to underline the particularly important role played by the baltic sea strategy. it has provided a framework for cohesion policy. i would also like to draw attention to the opportunities in southern europe. they should be exploited through enhanced cooperation in the region. the development of a macro-regional strategy in the mediterranean would be a step forward. this area has a similar culture and history, as well as significant potential. the area offers optimal conditions for development, both in terms of maritime traffic and renewable energy.

in writing. the heads of state or government have agreed on a pact for growth and jobs, which sets out the actions to be taken by the member states and the european union to boost growth, investment and employment and to increase europe's competitiveness. country-specific recommendations have been approved to guide member states' policies and budgets. particular attention should be paid to investments in areas that are future-oriented and to ensuring the sustainability of pension systems. a clear priority is to boost employment, both among women and men, and especially among young people and the long-term unemployed. it is important to promote the reactivation of older workers. the council will examine and decide on the proposals contained in the 'employment package', with a focus on quality job creation, structural labour market reform and investment in human capital. it is essential to address youth unemployment, in particular through the commission's initiatives on youth guarantees and the quality framework for traineeships.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of directive 2009/138/ec on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of insurance and reinsurance (solvency ii) as regards its date of transposition and date of application and the date of repeal of certain directives. directive 2009/138/ec (solvency ii) provides for a modern, risk-based system for the regulation and supervision of european insurance and reinsurance undertakings. the deadline for transposition of this directive is 31 october 2012 while the existing insurance and reinsurance directives, which are known as the solvency i package, will be repealed as of 1 november 2012. the deadline for transposition of directive 2009/138/ec is amended from 31 october 2012 to 30 june 2013 and the date of repeal of solvency package i from 1 november 2012 to 1 january 2014 as proposed and approved. those changes were necessary to take account of the new insurance supervisory architecture, namely the creation of the european insurance and occupational pensions authority (eiopa), in order to make solvency ii fully operational, to ensure a smooth transition to the new system and to prevent a legislative vacuum from arising after 31 october 2012.

in writing. - i voted in favour because, outside the eu, the people living in the mediterranean region have extremely low living standards in all respects: economically, socially, ecologically and politically. for these societies, their development is a key requirement, and for europe it is an opportunity, because it could translate into greater security, more 'sustainable' control of immigration flows and direct participation in this area of growth. all of this would have a positive impact on the performance of its own economy. the events of last spring on the southern shore of the mediterranean thus provide a powerful stimulus for the development of new active neighbourhood policies. by incorporating them, at least in part, into a macro-regional strategy, they could acquire a concrete territorial dimension, guaranteeing increased effectiveness. the member states and eu regions in the mediterranean area must engage in enhanced cooperation, which must be open to all partners in this area, which is essential for the future of europe. the macro-regional strategy is the best way to achieve this.
in writing. − the importance of the strategies already developed, such as the baltic sea and the danube, was that they provided both an integrated framework for addressing the challenges and opportunities in this region and pilot projects for future macro-regional strategies. given their success, i believe that the european union can use these models in the development of future strategies. in addition to the mediterranean region mentioned in this report, i would also like to give the example of the black sea region, which is of recognised strategic importance, given its very rich natural resources and a potential market of over 350 million consumers. unfortunately, cooperation in the black sea has a rather modest place in the current plans of the european union, but i believe that the eu should play a significant role in this region by creating a european black sea strategy. a possible strategy will bring significant benefits not only to the black sea basin states but also to the union as a whole, thus creating a real bridge between europe and asia.
in writing. − macro-regional strategies are new bridges of territorial cooperation supported by eu cohesion policy. although there is currently no standard for defining macro-regions, they include territories in several countries or administrative regions that share one or more common characteristics. the macro-regional strategies started three years ago with the baltic macro-region strategy, which set the objective of concentrating cooperation between the regions of the states around the baltic sea in the areas of environment, prosperity, accessibility and security. the danube macro-region strategy was followed, covering the regions of the danube basin with a population of over 100 million inhabitants, covering one fifth of the union's area. initially, the commission was reluctant to support these initiatives on the grounds that they would burden the administrative architecture, increase costs and be ineffective. however, i believe that macro-regions represent european added value and can contribute to the implementation of trans-european energy and transport projects. i supported this report because territorial cooperation at macro-regional level can bring benefits to initiatives of territorial cooperation groups (tegs) by ensuring the involvement of local and regional authorities, together with representatives of civil society, in decision-making with a view to the effective use of their common potential.
in writing. − i voted for the report on the evolution of eu macro-regional strategies: current practice and prospects, especially in the mediterranean region, because i believe that macro-regions are a favourable framework for creating synergies between existing initiatives and optimising the use of resources. the european parliament's own-initiative report refers to the status of current macro-regional strategies such as the eu strategy for the baltic sea and the danube region, identifies priority areas for future macro-regional strategies and makes recommendations for an eu macro-regional strategy for the mediterranean. we stress that the major areas of intervention for a mediterranean macro-region should target the appropriate sub-regional levels for cooperation under specific projects. major areas of intervention should include energy networks, scientific cooperation and innovation, cultural networks, education and training, tourism, trade, environmental protection, sustainable shipping, maritime safety and security and protection of the marine environment against pollution, overfishing and illegal fishing, strengthening good governance and effective public administration to promote job creation. i believe that a macro-regional strategy in the mediterranean should coordinate existing european funding, in particular from neighbourhood policy, cohesion policy and territorial cooperation policy, to implement projects that respond to common challenges.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the regulatory framework for the rail sector in europe needs to be amended to make it simpler and clearer. this will increase competitiveness, improve investment conditions and strengthen market surveillance. i would stress that greater transparency of market access conditions will lead to fair competition for railway undertakings. cooperation between national regulatory authorities will also help to remove remaining barriers to access to rail services and thus ensure a better functioning market where passengers and goods can cross borders with ease. we must continue to look at the development of the sector in order to establish the single european railway area. rail transport retains its potential for development, but i believe that the rules should be strengthened and harmonised to make it even more attractive.
in writing. − a single european railway area should remain our objective, as the more than 20 national signalling and speed control systems, which are not mutually compatible, severely limit the development of the sector and the competitiveness of rail transport in relation to other modes of transport. in order to create this unique space, i think two elements are essential, and i am referring to the regulatory body and, respectively, to the essential functions of the infrastructure manager. in the long term, i believe that a european regulatory body should be set up to oversee cross-border transport. the basis for such a body should be a network of national regulatory bodies, which should become trusted entities capable of taking swift and effective decisions. as regards the infrastructure manager, network development should be one of its core tasks, as it is better aware of the needs of the whole sector.
in writing. − i supported the adoption of the new single european railway area directive because technical incompatibilities between states are a major obstacle to the fast-growing rail freight market, where cross-border traffic has the greatest potential. they also represent obstacles to the development of a wider european transport network. increased interoperability will mean that trains must be able to run on the entire trans-european network and will contribute significantly to lower operating costs. i strongly support the vision of this directive for a european transport research and innovation policy based on joint efforts towards a competitive and resource-efficient transport system.
in writing. − in a europe where citizens travel more and more often, both for personal reasons - on holiday or to visit family or friends - and for professional reasons, the provision of rail transport services through european infrastructure should enable railway undertakings to provide better services to all users, whether they are freight or passengers. as such, non-discriminatory access to the infrastructure of the sector for all partners is essential, as is a tariff regime that is as homogeneous as possible. i believe that the european executive should carry out a study on the methodology for calculating the tariffs applied in the member states, with a view to establishing a uniform method of calculation, in order to determine a tariff system accessible at european level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on the establishment of the single european railway area. given the international dimension of european rail transport, it is important to establish at union level general principles for the licensing of railway undertakings and the coordination of member states' systems governing the allocation of railway infrastructure capacity and the charging of infrastructure charges. the new directive requires member states to adopt and publish an indicative strategy covering a period of at least five years, renewable, on the development of railway infrastructure to meet mobility needs, on the maintenance, renewal and development of infrastructure, based on sustainable financing of the railway system. transparent rules on access to related rail services and service infrastructure (freight terminals, maintenance infrastructure, train training stations, etc.) are crucial for the competitiveness of the sector. in order to ensure the development and efficient operation of the rail system, the activity of providing transport services and the operation of infrastructure will be managed separately and must have separate accounts. member states may also provide that such separation requires the organisation of separate departments within the same undertaking or that infrastructure and transport services are managed by separate entities.
in writing. − the tachograph plays a crucial role in checking compliance with the rules on driving time and rest periods by professional road transport drivers, helping to improve road safety, drivers' working conditions and fair competition between road transport undertakings. making the use of tachographs cost-effective is one of the key elements of the commission's strategy to better integrate the road freight market and to make road transport safer, more efficient and more competitive, as outlined in the white paper on transport of 28 march 2011. in view of the current situation regarding road safety in the field of freight transport, the tachograph must be able to provide reliable and credible data, allowing effective control of driving time and rest periods of drivers. the security of the tachograph system is essential to prevent fraud and illegal manipulation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eec) no 3821/85 on recording equipment in road transport and amending regulation (ec) no 561/2006 of the european parliament and of the council. the measures will significantly extend the functions of the digital tachograph, leading to a new type of digital tachograph (smart tachograph) that will facilitate distance communication based on the tachograph for control purposes, automatically recording the exact location and integrating the digital tachograph into other applications of intelligent transport systems.
in writing. − i welcome the establishment of a website and a free eu-wide telephone helpline which can be contacted free of charge and anonymously by all drivers or other interested parties wishing to report fraud falling within the scope of this regulation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (eec) no 3821/85 on recording equipment in road transport, because it contains fundamental provisions concerning the transport sector in the eu, which will significantly improve the safety of our roads and will provide stronger protection against fraud in the area of transport legislation. i truly believe that more efficient and innovative tools have to be put in place for guaranteeing the highest standards of social rules, such as drivers’ working conditions, minimum number of breaks and maximum driving times; this is very much a matter of public safety, and the report efficiently addresses this problem. i welcome the fact that the report underlines the importance of improving the use of advanced digital tachographs, which will not only reduce administrative burdens, but will also greatly enhance the possibility of monitoring compliance with rules in the european transport sector.
in writing. − the tachograph plays a crucial role in checking compliance with the rules on driving time and rest periods by professional road transport drivers, helping to improve road safety, drivers' working conditions and fair competition between road transport undertakings. all vehicles put into service for the first time 24 months after the entry into force of the technical specifications shall be equipped with a smart tachograph capable of communicating data to those authorities while the vehicle is in motion. i voted in favour of regulation 561/2006 applying to all vehicles, including towed and semi-towed vehicles, intended for the carriage of goods by road with a maximum authorised mass exceeding 2,8 tonnes (which are not subject to any exceptions which may be granted by the member states). i believe that these improvements to the regulation will help to increase road safety and to ensure better working conditions for professional drivers. i believe that the regulation on the social conditions for professional drivers should contain as few exceptions as possible. that is why i did not support amendment no 129 which extended certain exceptions to a radius of 150 km from the premises of the undertaking, nor amendment no 120 which introduces an exception for the construction sector.
in writing. − the eu's economic prosperity is based on a process underpinned by creativity, cultural diversity and innovation, the driving forces of an evolving knowledge society. protection of intellectual property rights (ipr) is therefore beneficial, both for the business environment, for innovators and consumers, and for those involved in cultural creations. customs authorities have an important role to play in ensuring effective compliance with idps at the external borders of the union because, once goods move across the territory of the member states, it is much more difficult and costly for them to be located and the necessary procedures initiated.
in writing. − given that the phenomenon of the marketing of goods infringing intellectual property rights causes significant harm to right holders, law-abiding producers and traders, i voted in favour of adopting this regulation. counterfeit products are also misleading to consumers and can endanger their health and safety. the entry into the customs territory and the placing on the market of such goods should therefore be prevented as far as possible. i consider that customs authorities should be able to control goods that are or should have been subject to customs supervision in the customs territory of the union, including goods under a suspensive procedure, in order to ensure the enforcement of intellectual property rights. last but not least, i believe that member states should allocate sufficient resources to enable customs authorities to fulfil their extended responsibilities and provide customs officials with adequate professional training. the commission and the member states should adopt guidelines to ensure the correct and uniform application of customs controls for the different types of infringements of the rights covered by this regulation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council concerning customs enforcement of intellectual property rights, because it is a fundamental step for the implementation of the eu strategy on ipr. beyond a doubt, the construction of a knowledge-based economy is of paramount importance for the european union’s growth and innovation strategy. an adequate and fair level of ipr enforcement constitutes the prerequisite and the necessary environment for its realisation. i welcome in particular the adequate stress on the need for ipr infringements to be exclusively based on the eu substantive ip legislation or the national laws of the eu member states. this constitutes, in my view, a balanced approach to ipr enforcement legislation, one of the most criticized aspects of the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement, as demonstrated by the positions of all the parliament’s committees which have been called for their opinion on that international agreement. the eu possesses all the instruments to elaborate valuable tools for the protection of iprs, whilst keeping in mind the crucial importance of a coordinated approach, at the global level, on this field.
in writing. − in the context of the increasing volume of counterfeit and pirated goods transiting through the eu, a unified regulation on the enforcement of intellectual property rights by customs authorities is absolutely necessary, all the more so as these goods can also affect the health of final consumers. given that decisions to suspend the release of goods or to detain goods liable to infringe an intellectual property right must be taken by specialised staff, references to the continuous training of customs workers in relation to pirated or counterfeit goods, which must be easily identified, have been omitted. i therefore propose that the member states should focus on the continuous specialisation of customs workers, so that they are as efficient as possible in correctly and quickly detecting goods in transit suspected of being imitations or copies of products protected in the eu.
in writing. − the proposal for a regulation on the enforcement of intellectual property rights by customs authorities concerns the commercial aspects of intellectual property rights, insofar as it envisages measures to enable customs authorities to enforce intellectual property rights at the border for goods in international trade. this regulation will replace regulation (ec) no 1383/2003. article 3 (1) provides for the exclusive competence of the european union in the field of the common commercial policy. i voted for amendment no 5, which says that member states should allocate sufficient resources to enable customs authorities to fulfil their extended responsibilities and provide customs officials with adequate training. the commission and the member states should adopt guidelines to ensure the correct and uniform application of customs controls for the different types of infringements of the rights covered by this regulation. i voted for amendment no 6 which states that, once its implementation is completed, this regulation must contribute more to the creation of a single market that ensures more effective protection of rights holders, stimulates creativity and innovation and offers consumers reliable and high quality products, all of which contribute to strengthening cross-border transactions between consumers, businesses and traders.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because water is essential for life and its efficient management is of particular importance for our health, our economy and the society in which we live. improving access to water is fundamental to improving the quality of life of the population. that is why i believe that resources must be protected as much as possible from the risks to which they are exposed, such as population growth, urbanization, pollution, overconsumption or climate change. at the same time, i would like to draw attention to the need for concrete action and a comprehensive approach to overcome the current challenges and achieve a more effective policy in this area. i therefore believe that the issue of water should be given greater consideration and should be integrated into all policy areas. water efficiency plays a key role in the europe 2020 strategy. in this context, reducing consumption should be a priority for all union citizens.
in writing. − the decline in freshwater resources and the expansion of deserts, which in the past were a problem mainly in africa and asia, are now also occurring in europe. in southern spain, the desert is expanding by one kilometre a year, romanian oltenia is exposed to a slower but similar process, and in other regions of the world drinking water resources have become a cause of interstate conflict. the protection of water resources, in particular drinking water, must be approached from a global perspective, taking into account all the ecosystem services provided by water. it is important that pollution be controlled at source to prevent the release of hazardous substances into the environment and to reduce the pressure on wastewater treatment. in view of the above, i believe that sustainable water use is not only an environmental but also an economic necessity and that greater transparency in water pricing systems would be necessary.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report and i consider that both the problems highlighted and the solutions proposed are consistent. but i cannot help but notice a paradox: in the text of the report, agriculture is mentioned in at least ten paragraphs, as a major water user, but also as a possible part of the solution, through the more efficient use of resources. however, the committee on agriculture and rural development of this parliament has not had the opportunity to express its views by way of an opinion. european farmers are open to discussing problems in this area and putting into practice the solutions needed for better water management, but their views must be heard and taken into account. agriculture is indeed a major user of water, but it uses it to provide consumers with sufficient and quality food.
in writing. − i voted for the report on the implementation of eu water legislation. i believe that water is a public good essential for life and that its proper management plays a major role in protecting the world's natural capital and ecosystems. europe currently draws up about 13% of the total available freshwater, which already indicates some water stress. in many places in europe, water abstraction is below sustainable levels, threatening wildlife, the security of society's water supply, and in some regions of southern europe, the water abstraction index has exceeded 40%. the future of industry in europe depends on finding effective responses to today's water challenges and on the responsible and efficient management of existing water resources, which directly affect human health, energy production, agriculture and food security. i'm highlighting the link between energy production, energy efficiency and water security. i stress that strategies need to be adopted at european level to ensure that the increasing demand for energy does not pose a threat to security and sustainable water availability.
in writing. − road safety is a major societal issue and an essential aspect of transport policy at union level. the harmonised implementation of a pan-european interoperable system for transmitting emergency calls from vehicles has been on the european commission's agenda since 2005 and has now become a priority. according to official ecall statistics, it is estimated that the full integration of the system into cars in eu member states will save approximately 2 500 lives annually, while reducing the severity of injuries by 10-15%. the ecall system will be of great help to road users who do not know their routes and exact location in the event of an accident and will allow emergency calls to be made without linguistic difficulties, based on the digital data included in the message format with the minimum set of data, which should reduce misunderstandings. i believe that every effort should be made to make ecall mandatory in all member states and to make it a reliable, high-quality, accessible and user-friendly service throughout the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the installation of an ecall service will improve road safety and bring significant benefits to society as a whole. its introduction is all the more important as the number of road casualties is continuously increasing. the emergency call within the system will provide increased assistance in the event of a major accident, while reducing the severity of the damage. it would also have a positive effect on incident management, helping to avoid secondary accidents or reduce traffic congestion. i draw attention to the fact that by fully integrating the system into automobiles approximately 2,500 lives will be saved annually. in this context, i stress the importance of developing a service that is reliable, accessible and easy to use for all road users. as its positive effects have already been proven by numerous studies, i consider that ecall should be made mandatory.
in writing. - the ecall system, which is triggered automatically as soon as sensors inside the vehicle detect a serious accident, is estimated to speed up the arrival of rescue teams by around 40% in urban areas and 50% in rural areas. the european commission has launched a new ecall service in the european union, which will help to reduce the number of accidents and injuries caused by cars and other vehicles. in view of the above, i support this report and believe that ecall should be a free public emergency call service for the benefit of every driver in europe, regardless of the make of their car.
in writing. - my vote in favour of the introduction of ecall is justified by the need to speed up the arrival of emergency services, save lives and reduce the damage caused by road accidents. it is estimated that ecall could save up to 2500 lives a year. the necessary technology is already available at eu level and the commission requires member states to modernise their response systems to handle ecalls by 2015. in my view, ecall should be a free public emergency call service for the benefit of every passenger in europe, regardless of the make of their car. the faster arrival of rescue teams, police and towing companies allows the accident site to be cleared faster, reducing external costs. for public authorities, the benefits of ecall are the reduction of the medical consequences of an accident, the risk of a subsequent accident at the same location and the impact of an accident on traffic. the introduction of ecall as a mandatory service for all newly approved vehicle types is also opening up new opportunities for the implementation of additional value-added services for the automotive industry.
in writing. − member states have set themselves the goal of reducing the number of fatal accidents, traffic congestion at such times and improving the way in which such events are managed. i believe that the ecall service can make an important contribution to this, particularly in terms of reducing the time needed for the arrival of the specialised emergency services. the trust of european citizens in these services is important when they travel to other member states, which is why it is beneficial to include the ecall service in all vehicles, regardless of the brand, country or current location of the vehicle, and to rapidly deploy ecall components on board vehicles without intermediate steps.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament resolution on ecall: a new 112 service for citizens, because it will greatly improve the effectiveness of emergency services on our roads. ecall represents an innovative and technologically advanced tool to promptly notify car accidents through satellite technology. this own initiative report, by stressing its countless benefits, clearly explains the european added value of the service, urging therefore the commission to submit a proposal within the framework of directive 2007/46/ec in order to ensure the deployment of a public, 112-based ecall system by 2015 in all new, type-approved cars and in all member states. i fully share the opinion that the service must be simple, affordable, operational and accessible to everybody throughout the eu, regardless of the vehicle and its location and, imperatively, free of charge and obligatory. the report also adequately stresses the need for data protection standards, in order to prevent the system to be used as a tool for tracing the journey of a vehicle.
in writing. − although the introduction of such a service has been discussed for a very long time, the fact that the decision has been delayed at eu level so far is a positive aspect because it gives member states time to update the necessary equipment in the emergency response centres (psap), which at the time of the start of the service must operate to the highest standards of technology in all member states. i would like to point out, however, that the report does not deal with the issue of personal data protection, which is rather vague and needs to be carefully reviewed and completed before the implementation of this public service, so as to avoid any interpretation in favour of interested parties using confidential information of citizens for other purposes, such as the initiation of commercial activities by car manufacturers.
in writing. − i voted for the report on ecall: a new 112 service for citizens, as it is estimated that the full integration of this system into eu cars will save around 2500 lives a year. the purpose of the ecall in-vehicle system is to ensure automatic notification of emergency services in the event of a serious accident, with the aim of reducing road fatalities and reducing the severity of injuries caused by road accidents through the rapid arrival of qualified and equipped assistance. the emergency call is generated automatically by activating sensors in the vehicle which, when activated, establish a direct voice and data connection with the emergency response centres. we draw attention to agricultural and industrial vehicles, especially agricultural tractors, which operate in remote and isolated areas and are therefore often unable to alert emergency services in the event of an accident. i voted for the paragraph asking the commission to consider whether ecall should be extended in the near future to other vehicles such as heavy goods vehicles, buses, coaches and two-wheel motor vehicles and to assess the need to introduce it also for agricultural tractors and industrial vehicles.
in writing. − as the economic and financial crisis has directly affected the living standards of many european citizens, strengthening the position of the european union as the main global destination for foreign investment is essential for the economic recovery of european states. it is imperative to adopt measures that help to increase the competitiveness of european workers and businesses, and to make member states' economies more attractive to foreign investors. adopting these policies is the only solution to create jobs and to revive economic growth. internationally, it is important that the european union remains an active promoter and participant in global economic governance processes. i support and encourage the european union's policy of continuing its efforts to conclude bilateral or multilateral agreements promoting free trade and the union's participation in such trade regimes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on increasing the attractiveness of investment. the eu must respond appropriately to the challenges of stabilising the international economy in order to fully exploit global opportunities. the eu must address weaknesses and strengthen the strengths of all countries and regions to attract local and international investment that contributes to balanced growth and cohesion. the eu is the world's largest trading bloc and foreign trade has so far played a dynamic role in promoting growth, particularly in the services sector. at the same time, attracting investment must be differentiated on two levels: making europe an attractive destination for foreign investors, making entrepreneurship attractive for local entrepreneurs. reforms, both at national and european level, are needed to improve the functioning of the single market and to make full use of the structural funds.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the attractiveness of investment in europe because it plays a vital role in strengthening competitiveness, productivity and the potential for economic growth. we need as much investment as possible, both in infrastructure and innovation, and in scientific and social initiatives. eu cohesion policy makes a significant contribution to the european economy and is one of the largest sources of community investment. the commission and the member states should propose specific measures to support all enterprises that provide jobs in line with the europe 2020 strategy and national and regional development strategies and ensure that funding decisions are based on the quality of the project and its value to national, regional, local and eu strategies. i would also like to stress that a discriminatory approach towards large companies could impede innovation and reduce the competitiveness of other eu companies, and i am referring here to smes in particular, by excluding them from key global partnerships in collective innovation and by reducing their access to advanced technology.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by my colleague rodi kratsa because i believe that in the context of the current economic and financial crisis it is essential to focus on attracting as much foreign as possible, as well as local investment in the european union. i believe that investing in human capital training, promoting the entrepreneurial spirit and stimulating a favourable environment for small businesses are vital elements in the eu's ability to attract foreign direct investment. i would like to draw attention to the need to reduce the administrative burden faced by small and medium-sized enterprises in accessing european funds. at the same time, the development and encouragement of public-private investment and the effective use of structural instruments for economic recovery are essential to attract and retain foreign and domestic capital in the european union. but we cannot talk about attracting investment to europe without having in mind the creation of a favourable investment climate through sustained economic growth. therefore, rules should be put in place to ensure both fair competition and a level playing field.
in writing. − i voted for the resolution on the attractiveness of investment in europe because the economic, financial and fiscal crisis in the eu has significantly accentuated economic and social disparities between member states and between regions, giving rise to an unequal distribution of internal and external investment within the european union. i support the union's innovation objectives and call on member states to set themselves the objective of increasing investment in education, research and innovation, given the positive medium- and long-term effects of these areas on growth and development. the eu should also promote trans-european networks, the mobility of workers, students and researchers, and strengthen cooperation and complementarities between eu economies. i called on the commission and the member states to implement the 'european egovernment action plan' which can deliver e-government services more efficiently and at lower cost, including for businesses, both locally and across borders. i believe that the eu and the member states should take action, in particular to strengthen the use of the structural funds and the cohesion fund as a catalyst for attracting additional funds from the eib, the ebrd, other international financial institutions and the private sector, while encouraging initiatives based on public-private partnerships.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament resolution on the trade aspects of the eastern partnership, because it highlights the importance of dcftas as a vital trade instrument for building up economic relationships with third countries. it also contains a very important analysis of the ongoing trade, economic and social situation of the ongoing negotiations on the eu-ukraine, eu-moldova, eu-georgia, eu-armenia and eu-azerbaijan association agreements. i particularly welcome the underlined dcftas potential for conflict prevention through economic and social cohesion, which relies on the ‘more for more’ principle as the appropriate instrument for acknowledging the efforts of those who make the most progress and motivating others to step up their efforts. the report expresses the need for the economic integration of the eastern partners with the eu to be carried out according to the necessary political and social reforms, and that institution building and proper implementation of commitments are prerequisites for the successful implementation of dcftas.
in writing. − trade is a very important component of the eu's relations with the eastern partnership countries. trade agreements are vital tools for building long-term economic relations with our eastern partners and lead to the promotion of economic reforms, the rule of law and social and environmental standards in our neighbourhood. i believe that the economic integration of the eastern partners with the eu cannot be effectively achieved without political and social reforms, without the participation of civil society in the decision-making process and the existence of economic integration among the eastern partners themselves, as the report also emphasises. the report also notes that the role of national parliaments is also important in the harmonisation of trade legislation with the eu acquis, which is a prerequisite for the conclusion and proper implementation of future agreements. there are eastern partnership countries that have made remarkable progress, such as the republic of moldova. the report welcomes the fact that moldova, despite having a fragile economy, has in recent years undergone a remarkable reform process and has greatly improved its economic performance; in this regard, it stresses the vital importance of the financial assistance provided by the international monetary fund and the macro-financial assistance provided by the eu. these are some of the reasons why i support this report.
in writing. − with regard to the trade aspects of the eastern partnership as a whole, the establishment of deep and comprehensive free trade areas (dcftas) with the eu will certainly bring real long-term benefits for all parties involved. i believe, however, that measures concerning certain key sectors of activity for the development of the economies of these countries need to be more comprehensively analysed and regulated from the perspective of eu policies, such as the sme sector, but also the research and innovation sector. what concerns me, however, is the political and economic instability in certain countries in the region, which must be closely monitored, and that is why i believe we must be cautious, but at the same time continue our efforts to provide economic facilities to the countries concerned, as well as institutional support.
in writing. − i vote in favour of this resolution because i believe that we must show our support to the countries of the eastern partnership. the creation of deep and comprehensive free trade areas is a key incentive for democratisation. people who can trade more freely will discover on their own the advantages of a political system based on respect for the rule of law and democratic values. i also welcome the commission’s proposal to increase by 40% the funding available for the eastern neighbourhood policy in the multiannual financial framework 2014-2021. we need to spend european taxpayers’ money in an effective way and reward high achievers. the republic of moldova has made considerable progress in the past year. this would not have been possible without the eu’s support. we need to continue our negotiations with the eastern partners and open up new economic possibilities for their citizens. financial support, free trade and strong conditionality are the tools the union should use in promoting our values in the neighbourhood.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report, particularly because it contains a number of very important references to trade relations with the eastern states in the agricultural sector. one of these references relates to the process of fulfilling eu sanitary and phytosanitary measures, which would guarantee the possibility for partner states to export agricultural products to the eu without putting european farmers at a disadvantage. only then will the eu's agricultural trade relationship with third countries be able to work, if the rules are the same for everyone.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the trade aspects of the eastern partnership. the conclusion and implementation of association agreements including deep and comprehensive free trade areas (dcftas) is a priority objective of the european neighbourhood policy on the eastern partners. i welcome the efforts to strengthen the eastern partnership, in particular the commission's initiatives on smes, including the facility for smes under the eastern partnership. i believe that the greatest benefits of the implementation of the gats for the eu will come from more stable and predictable trade. for example, ukraine is the eu's largest eastern partner and the ftaa opens up a new market of 46 million consumers for the eu. i stress the importance of moldova's continued alignment with the eu of its energy infrastructure and its systems of technical regulation, standardisation, conformity assessment, testing, and market surveillance. i welcome the commission's proposal for the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, which proposes a 40% increase in funding for the european neighbourhood policy. the eastern partners cannot bear the costs of legislative harmonisation and the necessary institutional and structural reforms on their own, and eu financial support should complement their reform efforts.
we support the fight against the sale of counterfeit products, but this must not be done at the risk of breaching the fundamental rights of european citizens. therefore, we cannot support the acta agreement in its current form. we are particularly concerned about the provisions of article 27, which, in paragraph 4, provides that the competent authorities of a signatory party have the authority to require an online service provider to promptly disclose to a right holder sufficient information to identify a subscriber whose account is allegedly - and here i emphasize: is allegedly - used for infringement. article 14 (2) also provides that a party may exclude from the application of the agreement small quantities of goods of a non-commercial nature contained in travellers' personal luggage, which means that it may also decide not to exclude quantities of such goods, raising serious concerns about possible breaches of the free movement of goods and persons within the european union.
in writing. i believe that intellectual property rights need to be better protected online too, but this should in no way be achieved by violating fundamental rights as is unfortunately the case with acta. the agreement flagrantly infringes at least three fundamental rights, namely the right to the protection of personal data, the right to privacy and confidentiality as also clearly demonstrated in the opinion of the european data protection supervisor. if acta were to enter into force, it would require internet providers not only to monitor all user activity on a large scale, but also to report any irregularities found to intellectual property rights holders. these measures are not only excessive and disproportionate, but they are also illegal because they create a private law enforcement system in which the providers and rights holders are the policemen and judges of the online space, to the detriment of the judicial authorities. for these reasons, i believe that, in this form, the acta agreement is unacceptable and must be rejected by the european parliament.
the budget must take account of long-term priorities and strategies. the objectives of growth, competitiveness and employment in the member states should therefore be strengthened. i am particularly in favour of concentrating an appropriate level of budgetary resources on supporting young people and smes. most companies active on the labour market fall into the sme category, but they attract only a small percentage of total investment. i therefore believe that increased support for smes could successfully help to overcome the current crisis. i would stress that fiscal responsibility is particularly important at this time of fiscal consolidation and that the union budget must be complemented by the recovery policies pursued by the member states if the impact on the economy is to be positive.
