view, but it is also a work which is of great political sensitivity and importance, particularly for the european parliament, but also for all the institutions involved in the decision-making and implementation of the common agricultural policy. i am fully aware of the political importance of this alignment debate for the european parliament. as mr de castro has mentioned, the discussions began under the hungarian presidency and continued for almost a year. we were very close to an agreement at one point, but we finally found ourselves in a deadlock after the last trilogue on 20 december 2011, under the polish presidency. the danish presidency then decided to include the alignment part of the four main regulations in the debate on the reform of the common agricultural policy and to continue negotiations on the other alignment dossiers separately. i wish to be clear. i have said this several times before the committee on agriculture, but i would like to repeat it: i have always been concerned to defend the prerogatives of the european parliament, as they derive from the treaty of lisbon, in all the alignment packages, in order to achieve a balanced distribution of powers between the council and parliament. for each grey area, and wherever legally possible - i want to emphasise this - i preferred an approach which allows both institutions to play their part. i have tried to go along with parliament in favouring delegated acts and in a strict reading of article 43 (3) of the lisbon treaty, which mr de castro mentioned. that is why, as an example, i have course, compromises have had to be found. but overall, on the basis i have just outlined, the overall compromise package in each of the alignment operations has strengthened the prerogatives of parliament. in any case, we must avoid that this alignment has an impact on the substantive discussions on the reform of the common agricultural policy, which are very important for all of us. i in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the conclusion of the eu-russia agreement on the maintenance of commitments on trade in services is part of the new legal framework generated by russia's accession to the wto, allowing for a greater opening of the russian market to services from the european union, as well as better conditions for european economic actors already present on the services market in russia, through provisions on non-discrimination and free competition. the benefits will be significant for european service providers, as exports in this area reached a turnover of eur 22.6 billion in 2010, representing 20% of total eu exports to russia. in addition, the bilateral agreement will allow european investors to continue to benefit from preferential treatment more favourable than that offered by the multilateral trading regime in two areas (maritime trade and temporary movement of employees for professional purposes) where current commitments towards the union under the 1994 partnership and cooperation agreement are stricter than those russia will take upon formal accession to the wto.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because the eu-russia agreement on trade in motor vehicle parts and components is linked to wto commitments. in addition, it provides a compensation mechanism for eu automotive component manufacturers, should their exports to russia decrease as a result of the russian investment programme in the field, until 2018. if this risk materializes, it is important that preferential conditions for european exporters can be maintained, especially as it is difficult to assess at the moment how trade in cars and car components between the eu and russia will develop in the coming years. in addition to the measures implemented under the investment programme, several factors may determine the increase or decrease in the volume of trade in this area, including the evolution of global demand for motor vehicles, but also the development of infrastructure in russia. i therefore support the approval of this compensation mechanism, which supports eu car and auto component manufacturers in the event of a significant drop in exports in this area.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of the eu-russia agreement on trade in motor vehicle parts and components. the union negotiated this bilateral agreement in order to have a compensation mechanism for manufacturers of automotive components in case eu exports of such products to russia decrease as a result of the implementation of the russian automotive investment programme until 2018. the triggering of the countervailing mechanism (article 5) provides that if exports of certain automotive parts and components from the eu to russia decrease by 3% over a 12-month period compared to a benchmark calculated on the basis of eu exports to russia in 2010, russia must allow the import of parts and components originating in the eu with reduced import duties in quantities equal to the decrease in eu exports. the compensation mechanism shall apply for a period of at least 12 months and shall be reviewed every 12 months thereafter. in exceptional economic circumstances, where the total number of new cars sold in russia in the year in which the mechanism is triggered is significantly lower than in the previous year, the compensation mechanism shall not apply under the agreement. russia will administer the compensation quotas through an import licensing system.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because the eu-russia agreement on the introduction or increase by the russian federation of export duties on raw materials is designed to protect the union from additional restrictions on export duties. since the russian federation considers that it can apply new or additional export duties to products not included in the wto commodity concessions and commitments list, it is important that the union obtain bilateral guarantees that increased duties will not be introduced on raw materials in which it has a major, existing or potential interest. the commission has also assessed the impact of the measures on the union industry, in particular the impact of the measures on the union industry's financial situation. although the rapporteur has noted a number of shortcomings in the commitments made by the russian federation through this agreement, it is useful as a temporary measure pending the conclusion of a more stringent raw material trade treaty with the russian federation.
in writing. − russia's accession to the world trade organisation brings numerous benefits to the european union, especially in terms of imports of raw materials into the member states. but the problem of russian export duties is an obstacle to better economic cooperation. the european union is also committed to the development of a common foreign and security policy, including the establishment of a common foreign and security policy. i therefore believe that the principle of reciprocity in eu-russia trade relations should be emphasised, by regulating and implementing concrete measures that benefit both sides, especially in critical sectors of activity such as energy or mineral resources.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the decision on the conclusion of the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the eu and the russian federation on the introduction or increase of export duties on raw materials. the bilateral agreement with the russian federation was negotiated in the context of the accession of the russian federation to the world trade organisation and can be formally concluded after the approval of the european parliament. in the context of its accession to the wto, the russian federation has committed to reduce or phase out export duties for a list of raw materials. these export duty rate commitments were included in the list of concessions and commitments on goods of the russian federation. the russian federation is a major supplier of arms to the russian federation. under the bilateral agreement, the russian federation undertakes to make efforts not to introduce or increase export duties on raw materials listed in the agreement. if the russian federation envisages the application of export duties on these products, it shall consult the european commission at least two months in advance 'in order to find a solution which takes account of the interests of both parties'.
in writing. − i voted in favour of parliament’s recommendation to reject acta, because i believe it is not a suitable tool for the european union in responding to the tasks for which it was called. despite the central need to protect our market and our customers from counterfeit goods from outside the union accessing the market, the need to defend the intellectual property rights regime, also in the digital environment, and the fundamental need for a global approach on this matter, acta unfortunately raised more perplexities than guarantees. the european union will have to find better instruments to address the surely basic issues touched upon by the agreement. not only did the european data protection supervisor publish a very negative opinion on the agreement but also, and more importantly, the opinions expressed by four parliamentary committees (itre, deve, libe, juri), state their evident concerns about acta. finally, i strongly believe that the unprecedented public campaign against the agreement, which ended up in a petition containing more than 2.4 million signatures, cannot be left unheard by the democratically elected body of the european union. the european parliament represents the interests of the citizens of europe.

in writing. − better protection of the intellectual property rights of european producers involved in world trade is of paramount importance. by eliminating counterfeiting in the commercial domain and online piracy we can help to increase economic activity. at the same time, the risks to the health of citizens, for example from the consumption of counterfeit medicines, are reduced. the way in which copyright protection is envisaged, however, through acta raises some questions, all the more so as the negotiations of the agreement in question have been conducted in a too opaque manner. the benefits of the text appear to be far outweighed by the possible dangers to civil liberties. the vagueness of certain aspects of the agreement and the uncertainty of its interpretation, which may lead to abuse by the authorities, should give us pause for thought. in these circumstances, as representatives of european citizens, we can no longer guarantee adequate protection of fundamental rights under acta and many of the terms of the agreement need to be clarified. the acta text can therefore be voted on by parliament once the uncertainties relating to the scope and protection of individual freedoms have been resolved in order to avoid undesirable interpretations.

in writing. − acta has rightly been the subject of a lengthy debate here in the european parliament. it is our duty, as the single directly elected european institution, to ensure that fundamental rights such as the right to privacy and the right to freedom of expression are safeguarded. in the course of our discussions we came to the conclusion that the concerns about acta, expressed in a series of protests and campaigns across the globe, were entirely justified. this is why my group voted to reject the agreement. we must find an alternative way to address the challenges of digital piracy and counterfeit products which does not infringe the fundamental rights of the individual and which follows an open, transparent public debate.
in writing. − i voted against the anti-counterfeiting trade agreement between the european union and its member states, australia, canada, japan, the republic of korea, the united mexican states, the kingdom of morocco, new zealand, the republic of singapore, the swiss confederation and the united states of america (acta). the eu is firmly committed to the fight against counterfeiting and has one of the most modern legislation, fully in line with specific international agreements, in the field of intellectual property and copyright protection in the information society. however, the acta text contains provisions that may lead to interpretations that may lead to the infringement of fundamental rights of european citizens. that is why we cannot vote in favour of the current form of the acta agreement. the rejection of acta does not weaken the eu's commitment to protecting intellectual property or to fighting counterfeiting. the european parliament's rejection of acta underlines that any future international anti-counterfeiting agreement signed by the eu must guarantee respect for the fundamental rights of european citizens. we hope that if the commission proposes in the future a new text for such an agreement, the european parliament will be consulted before the agreement is signed and that the final text will also include the amendments proposed by the european parliament.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i am a great animal lover and i believe that a legal framework at union level would contribute to better protection of pets and stray animals. as a member of the peti committee, i am aware of the concerns of european citizens about the poor treatment to which these animals are sometimes subjected in the european union. in most cases, there is adequate legislation at national level, but local authorities, which have the main responsibilities for managing these issues, face difficulties in implementing it, including due to a lack of the necessary resources. i therefore believe that a european legal framework would not only bring about harmonisation of measures and practices at member state level, but should also be a way of supporting the efforts of the authorities responsible at regional and local level.

in writing. - i voted for the report on the creation of an eu legal framework for the protection of pet animals and stray animals. there is currently no eu legislation on the protection of pets and stray animals, despite the estimated number of pets in the eu of over 100 million. some pets and stray animals are victims of attacks in many member states, and the signatories of the petitions mainly refer to member states in southern and eastern europe. it calls on the european union and the member states to ratify the european convention for the protection of pet animals and to transpose its provisions into national legal systems. we call on the commission to come forward with proposals for an eu legal framework for the protection of pet animals and stray animals, including: rules for the identification and registration of animals; strategies for the management of stray animals, including vaccination and sterilisation programmes; measures to promote owners' responsibility; a ban on unauthorised breeders and shelters; a ban on the killing of stray animals without any medical indication; information and education programmes in schools on animal welfare; sanctions for any member state that does not comply with the rules.

in writing. − access to a bank account has now become a precondition for full participation in economic and social life for every european citizen, and the use of cash is rapidly declining. today, lack of access to a basic bank account makes everyday life more difficult and expensive. thus, paying utility bills or collecting income can become a problem. i'm not talking about e-commerce that's becoming inaccessible. in view of the above, i strongly support the right of any european citizen, regardless of his or her financial situation, to open and use a basic payment account, including in a member state other than that in which he or she is habitually resident.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on recommendations to the commission on access to basic banking services. i voted for a basic payment account to be effective, easy to open and to provide a specific range of basic services. i voted for the existence of effective measures for effective supervision and dispute resolution, and for facilitating access to such an account for consumers without a fixed address. i believe that anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing legislation should be applied proportionately and should never be used as an unjustified pretext to reject less commercially attractive consumers. the commission should also examine the need for a link between consumers and the member state in order for them to be eligible for a basic payment account. we call on the commission to present a detailed analysis of the situation in all member states by september 2012 and to submit a proposal for a directive to the commission by january 2013 on the basis of article 114 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union on ensuring access to basic payment services for all consumers legally resident in the union.
mr president, i am glad that growth, one of the core concepts we have always defended, has reached the frontline of the debate. nevertheless, we must bear in mind that growth is created by markets – not by institutions or legislators – so, if we want growth, we should support the market. if we want to speed up the development of infrastructure in order to complete the internal market and boost competitiveness, we must use our shrunk budgets to attract private finance dedicated to long-term investments. the new mechanisms, like the connecting europe facility, should primarily rely on these financial instruments to develop energy and telecom infrastructure in a stable and transparent framework which will not distort markets and which will attract private investors, rather than crowding them out by creating an uneven competition between public and private money. yes, we need project bonds to work and, yes, we need them to be assessed and improved after their pilot phase. what we also need is for our institutions to support the real stakeholders: banks and institutional investors. we need to develop this new asset class which should bypass current uncertainty and debt driven constraints and that will help to complete and expand markets. being part of the solution requires leverage for each euro spent by the public sector. for this, the time is gone when we could rely on grants alone.
the pilot phase of the europe 2020 project bond initiative should be launched to prepare the connecting europe facility as we want it to be as soon as possible. the pilot phase should be financed in 2012 and 2013 through budgetary reallocations from the current transport, energy and telecommunications programmes. thus, up to eur 200 million from the ten-t budget, up to eur 20 million from the budget of the competitiveness and innovation framework programme and up to eur 10 million from the ten-e budget could be reallocated to this initiative. the european investment bank should request budgetary funds on the basis of a list of projects which the bank considers appropriate and feasible to implement. however, it is important that member states submit these applications by 31 december 2013 and, only in the case of very complex infrastructure projects, by 31 december 2014. so now is the time to prepare for a good absorption in the future multiannual financial framework.

on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, we have heard again and again from the council, from the member states, but also from you, commissioner, that the implementation of the schengen agreement has been very good, almost perfect. allow me please to at least partially disagree. it is true that for several years no one has challenged how member states implement the schengen rules. border controls have been reintroduced for limited periods of time, but no one complained. however, in the last 18 months there have been way too many attempts to apply schengen rules in a much more personalised and dangerous manner. the joy of the arab spring was over-shadowed by italy’s reaction and france’s decision to reintroduce border control. denmark considered that its domestic political problems could be solved by reintroducing border control as an alleged way of combating trans-border crime. for more than one year – one year – the netherlands has had an initiative which was considered by a dutch court as having the same effects as border controls. for several months another attempt to curtail free movement has taken place in germany, where on a systematic basis more than 55% of czech buses are checked. i cannot help wondering how long the commission will keep pretending that things are ok within the schengen governance. they are not. this is why the commission in fact came up with a legislative package to improve it. if the commission continues with only half-measures, never daring to start infringement procedures, i am afraid we will wake up one morning realising that free movement no longer exists. i am addressing you, commissioner, because i have full confidence in your commitment to the defence of free movement. i am not addressing the council at this stage, waiting for a better time to enlighten the member states and make them understand what the real interests of european citizens are.
the recent debates on the schengen agreement have focused too much on the interinstitutional war between the council and parliament and too little on the real substance of the problem. that is why i think this debate is a good opportunity to return to the arguments justifying a thorough reform of the schengen area. unfortunately, i have to say that there are important problems in the current schengen system, mainly because of a general tendency to re-nationalize the schengen area. this trend has been manifested in recent years by the already well-known cases of abusive reintroduction of internal border controls. but what is less well known and less publicised are the hidden internal border controls, which are present in no less than 11 member states, as the commission pointed out in its biannual report in may, and as confirmed by the commissioner responsible for the schengen area and by my colleague mr coelho here. the refusal to admit romania and bulgaria is another example of the misinterpretation of the schengen rules. i hope that the admission of romania and bulgaria this autumn will be the first step towards normalising the situation with regard to compliance with these rules. in romania, right now, the national parliament and the ponta government are making efforts to introduce the rule of law and eliminate the presidential dictatorship that has been imposed in recent years. romania is thus on the way to a return to normalcy after a long period of abuses and breaches of democracy, which will ensure that the administrative and judicial problems that have delayed romania's admission to the schengen area will disappear and never be repeated. the european union urgently needs to reform schengen governance, involve the european parliament and the commission must take on the role of an impartial arbiter, both in assessing the application of the schengen acquis and in taking measures to remedy any problems that may arise.
the council decision of 8 june to change the legal basis of the schengen evaluation regulation may have adverse consequences for the functioning of the schengen area. if we really want to have a higher degree of transparency and democratic and judicial accountability in the way the schengen rules are implemented and applied by the member states, then we must go back to the basic treaty and restart the discussion with the european parliament. moreover, it is hard to accept that member states with weaknesses at their external borders refuse a coordinated assessment of the schengen mechanism and at the same time block access to the schengen area to countries which, as a result of their efforts, have managed to achieve a very high level of security at their external borders. by refusing to co-decide on the schengen file, the council intends to maintain a schengen evaluation system which has proved to be currently ineffective in identifying non-compliance with the schengen rules. this means that the union prefers to tolerate situations of illegal checks at internal borders or irregularities at external borders. some member states consider that the introduction of internal borders will help to ensure the safety of citizens and to control migration flows. unfortunately, it is a false lead. the union should focus on strengthening schengen governance and harmonising the level of security at the external borders of all member states. the european parliament wants to avoid a reduction in the existing standards on external borders laid down in european legislation. a review of the current schengen rules, leading to a standardisation of the external borders, is needed and this must also be legislated by the european parliament as co-legislator.
i welcome this debate and consider it useful for two reasons: because it is a debate on the institutional relations between the three european institutions and because it is the first time that the council has allowed itself to ignore one of the institutions which has the necessary legitimacy to respond to the aspirations and checks of european citizens. the council must understand that the parliament is the only european institution with increased democratic legitimacy. we are elected here by popular vote and represent the interests of the european citizens. the interest of european citizens is more cohesion, more cohesion means more space and more freedom of movement. i do not think that if we have governments that are incapable of providing adequate solutions to the crisis and resort to populist measures, we should go back to feudalism, which, even in the feudal period, was not typical of europe, because freedom of movement is a given, it was not built by the european union. the european citizen has understood very clearly that this is what unites him culturally and civilisationally.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president, it is a difficult discussion. i hope that nobody really questions the intentions of the cyprus presidency. the council firmly believes that the new arrangements for schengen governance, which are already in place, provide a solid basis for ensuring greater oversight of developments in the schengen area, including by the european parliament. please allow me in this intervention to limit myself to the issue at hand and not comment on external borders, although we all know that the two questions are interlinked. the council very much wants the parliament to be involved in the ongoing process on the legislative aspects of the new schengen governance arrangements. that includes not only the proposal for amending the schengen borders code, which remains – as many of you very rightly mentioned – subject to the ordinary legislative procedure (codecision) but also the schengen evaluation mechanism proposal. and in saying this i really weigh my words. my plea to all of you is that we at least agree now to define, confine and circumscribe the disagreement that indeed exists between the european parliament and the council to one question, and that is the question of evaluation. the honourable rapporteur, mr coelho, will allow me to say and to insist that there is also a fundamentally legal question and, please do not get me wrong, i am not doing away with the political sensitivities and political aspects of this. but when it comes to evaluation there is an issue on whether, under the treaty, evaluation remains a peer review or whether it is a competence which has been transferred to the community level. and somewhere there is agreement there. we should not have a very passionate debate on this – let us talk and let us find a way forward! but please do not consider that it is about lowering existing standards and guarantees. the council is already publicly committed to ensuring that the view of the european parliament will, to the fullest extent possible, be taken into consideration in all its aspects before the adoption of the final text. we have, of course, also taken very good note of all the comments and, i assure you, all the criticisms you addressed to the council and be assured that we do not take it badly and we will convey the ‘heat’ we received to the council and to the member states. based on this, we will try our utmost to find a satisfactory way forward and we hope that we can come to a mutually satisfactory understanding as to how that can be given a practical expression, thus enabling work on these proposals to be brought to a successful conclusion in the very near future. let me conclude by saying that we remain as committed as all of you to preserving and strengthening the free movement of persons, as one of the most tangible and successful achievements of european integration. we firmly believe in a european union as a space of freedom, including the fundamental issue of freedom of movement, to which schengen makes an outstanding contribution. of course we will fully respect the treaty and the framework of the treaty, but we of course stand ready to discuss, and see what improvements we can bring.

line with the acquis. that would imply a change of the legal base, also involving the european parliament. we maintain that view from the commission side. schengen is a european achievement, and that in writing. for european citizens, freedom of movement is one of the main tangible benefits of european integration. at the same time, it consolidates the construction of a single area of freedom, security and justice. any decision to restrict this right must be well justified, carefully considered and strictly limited in time and exceptional in nature. clear criteria and conditions of application are needed for situations where internal border controls may be carried out, and parliament has the right to be closely involved in their development and monitoring. the unjustified delay in romania's accession to schengen already creates de facto discrimination for millions of european citizens. if, in addition, internal border controls are abused, one of the foundations of the european construction will be threatened. i call on all european leaders not to give in to populist temptations and to defend freedom of movement. i also ask the commission to monitor closely the member states' compliance with the schengen acquis and to take prompt action in the event of any abuse. last but not least, i ask that a clear decision be taken in september with a precise timetable for romania's accession to schengen.
in writing. the creation of the schengen area is an important part of the process of consolidating and strengthening the european union. this area has brought benefits to all member states, both economically, which have free movement of goods across internal borders, and to european citizens, who can travel freely without being checked every time they cross an internal border. thanks to the actions of opportunistic politicians, driven by their desire to attract populist votes, the schengen system has been repeatedly attacked, by using it as a sort of scapegoat for increasing electoral capital. the same can be seen in the case of bulgaria and romania where, although they have met all the necessary criteria to enter the schengen area, the final decision is still pending.

mr president, at rio+20 the world leaders focused on sustainable development. they recognised that we are confronting not only an economic crisis but also an environmental crisis. they also recognised that we need bolder action to stop the destruction of the environment. if we really want green growth, if we really want a green economy, then we have to pay much more attention to what economics teaches us. people respond to incentives. therefore, people who pollute and firms who pollute should pay the right price for destroying the environment. we in the european institutions should support technical innovation for a green economy; we should support action to preserve nature; and we should support taxes on energy based on carbon. we should also support the improvement of our accounting systems to reflect the impact of our way of life on the environment.
in writing. − the current structure and the rules of procedure of the full court of justice of the european union are the result of the changes introduced by the treaty of nice. the president of the court and the presidents of chambers of five judges are currently very busy. in response to these charges, the court amended its rules of procedure to allow, in cases concerning intellectual property, the abolition of the oral procedure and clarification of the status of interveners, so as to allow for a more rapid treatment. in those circumstances, i consider that an increase in the number of judges of the general court is necessary in order to make the court's work more efficient.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament legislative resolution on the draft regulation amending the protocol on the statute of the court of justice because, given the evident increase in the workload of the court in the last years, a revision of the rules concerning its activities and the composition of the court was fundamental. the document, containing proposals relating to the court of justice and to the general court, aims at strengthening the working capacity of the ecj, in line with the guidelines suggested by the european commission. the suggested reform, by amending articles 16 and 17 of the statute, wants to increase the participation of the judges in cases assigned to the grand chamber, allowing them to sit far more frequently than at present, thereby easing the activities of the president of the court and the presidents of the chambers of five judges, redistributing the workload in a more balanced way. i positively welcome this text amending the protocol on the court of justice because it responds to the urgent need for a necessary rationalisation of certain specific aspects of the working rules of the ecj, a crucial component of the european union institutional architecture.
in writing. − i support the proposal for broader participation of judges assigned in cases in the grand chamber. this would ensure that case law is consistent, as currently the court of justice judges have a very heavy workload while other judges sit in relatively few cases. i also support the establishment of a vice-president to assist the president in carrying out his ever increasing duties. as for the general court, the number of cases disposed of has been lower than the number of cases brought before the court for several years. despite the court’s substantial efforts and increased productivity, it cannot keep up with the resource-intensive job. the increase in workload comes from a variety of reasons, including the increase of litigation following 2004 and 2007 accessions, european integration, and the devolution of jurisdiction. the court has made several efforts to deal with cases more expeditiously but believes a structural solution is urgently required, such as increasing the number of judges. this must be done to increase the effectiveness, urgency and flexibility of the court. not only is effective judicial protection vital, but inefficient justice might be even more costly.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft regulation amending the protocol on the statute of the court of justice of the european union and annex i thereto. the court of justice of the eu has proposed several amendments to its statute, as well as the adoption of a regulation on the temporary judges of the civil service tribunal, which, following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, need to be adopted, for the first time, by the european parliament and the council, acting in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure. the proposed amendments affect the three courts currently constituting the court of justice of the eu differently and are necessary due to the increased workload of these courts. the proposed changes for the court of justice concern the increase of the quorum for deliberations in the grand chamber and the plenary, the creation of the office of vice-president and the definition of his duties. as regards the general court, in order to cope with the increase in its workload and the time taken to deal with cases, it is proposed to increase the number of judges to 39. as regards the civil service tribunal, the court requests that three temporary judges be assigned to it, to be able to call upon when a judge is unable to perform his duties for a long period.
in writing. − i support the regulation of the european parliament and the council to allow temporary judges to be appointed to the eu civil service tribunal. since the tribunal consists of just seven judges, its work can be severely affected if one member is unable to perform his or her duties. it is crucial that the tribunal carry out its judicial functions. the temporary judges would only be able to perform strictly judicial duties and would not participate in administration or elections. they would be selected according to capability and flexibility to immediately perform the duties of the tribunal. thus i find this proposal a realistic solution to ensure the tribunal’s work does not get disrupted or adversely affected.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the decision establishing a competitiveness and innovation framework programme (2007-2013) and laying down general rules for the granting of community financial aid in the field of the trans-european transport and energy networks, because i believe it may become an important tool in the achievement of the economic relaunch of the union. as unanimously agreed upon, investments in infrastructure will have to play a crucial role in this sense, not only as a means for growth and for the completion of the single market in transport and energy, but also as a necessary precondition for the convergence of the european regions. however, it is also evident that the eu budget alone cannot sufficiently tackle this challenge. one of the key actors in this field being the involvement of the private sector, i believe that the launch of a phase testing the financial markets’ reactions and the functioning and optimisation of project bonds can constitute an important tool to attract private investments, triggering a virtuous circle for the european economy as a whole.
in writing. − there are certain key areas of activity at the moment, as investment in development projects in these sectors will certainly lead to the relaunch of the community economy in the long term. i have noted, however, that the allocation of budgetary funds to the three critical areas (transport, energy and information technology) is disproportionate, in that the financial resources for the trans-european energy and information networks in the 2012-13 pilot phase will be limited to eur 10 billion and eur 20 billion respectively, compared to the amount of eur 230 billion allocated to the trans-european transport networks. the energy infrastructure sector, in particular the clean and resource-efficient energy sectors, is a top priority for the eu's policy on sustainable economic growth and therefore deserves a much larger share of the available funds, at least half of which is allocated to transport. an argument such as the obstacles to the authorization of these energy projects is unacceptable and our efforts must be directed towards reducing the bureaucratic procedures that impede economic development, and not towards reducing the allocation of funds for these reasons.
in writing. − the trans-european transport network plays a strategic role in economic, social and territorial cohesion, while ensuring the free movement of passengers and goods within the european union. however, europe is facing increasing investment needs in transport infrastructure. in this context, i welcome the europe 2020 project finance bond initiative. i believe this is a key stage in attracting private sector funding for transport, energy and telecommunications infrastructure, which has a significant potential to contribute to job creation and growth. the pilot project will allow investors to familiarise themselves with the new financing structures and at the same time support a resource-efficient economy in line with the europe 2020 strategy. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that innovative financial instruments have a particularly important role to play in attracting additional private sector funding to key infrastructure.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's report on the proposal to amend decision no 1639/2006/ec establishing a framework programme for innovation and competitiveness (2007-2013) and regulation (ec) no 680/2007 laying down general rules for the granting of community financial assistance in the field of trans-european transport and energy networks. difficulties in accessing long-term private or public sector financing for infrastructure projects should not lead to a deterioration in the performance of transport, energy and telecommunications infrastructures, nor to a delay in the penetration of broadband networks. the commission should involve the eib in the implementation of the pilot phase due to the fact that the eib is the main financer of infrastructure projects and the eu financial body designated by the treaty. the eib should apply for budgetary funds on the basis of a list of projects judged by the eib and the commission to be appropriate, consistent with the union's long-term objectives and achievable. those requests and the related budgetary commitments should be made by 31 december 2013. for major infrastructure projects, the eib's actual approval should be possible at a later date, but no later than 31 december 2014.
in writing. − i voted in favour of parliament's report on draft amending budget no 3/2012 of the european union for the financial year 2012, section iii commission. in 2011, for the second year in a row, the budgetary authority reduced the level of payment appropriations in the union budget for 2012 by more than eur 3 billion compared to the commission's initial estimate, including in the areas of research and cohesion policy. it should be noted that the underspending (eur 0,73 billion) is not due to absorption difficulties or mismanagement but is the result of the rules in force on adjusting the distribution of payments according to needs. the european parliament regrets that, despite the provisions of article 310 (5) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union on sound financial management and the joint declaration on payment credits agreed by all three institutions in the 2012 budgetary procedure, the council initially decided to reduce by two thirds the amount of eur 485 million for the transfer request of dec 9/2012 from energy projects with a low execution level to supporting economic recovery by strengthening the three budget lines for fp7 - cooperation.

member of the commission. − mr president, firstly i would like to express my appreciation to mrs yannakoudakis for the report on the voluntary and unpaid donation of tissues and cells. the commission welcomes this report. tissue and cell transplants are of immense value to many patients. such transplants represent a fast-evolving area of medicine and can make a real difference to people in terms of quality of life. the commission will analyse in detail parliament’s recommendations. in the meantime, let me assure you that the commission acknowledges, and indeed shares, many of the concerns raised. i believe we all support the fact that the donation of tissues and cells is voluntary and unpaid. the issue of an adequate supply of tissues and cells to meet eu citizens’ medical needs is, as we know, an area of concern for many member states. this is why i believe member states need to strike the right balance so as to help improve the availability of tissues and cells without in any way compromising voluntary and unpaid donation. the donation of tissues and cells depends on public trust in our transplant systems. your report highlights key elements to build and maintain that trust. a transparent and safe donation system is essential for public support. ensuring traceability of donated material between donors and recipients is essential in order to guarantee the safety and quality of the transplanted tissues and cells. ensuring adequate information for citizens looking for tissues and cells through banking services via the internet is important to guarantee citizens’ safety. in addition, the report rightly highlights the need for member states to share best practices so as to increase donations and foster international collaboration. european and international cooperation can bring much added value, in particular in medical fields like stem-cell transplantation, where finding the right match of cells for the right patient is difficult. regarding stem-cell transplantation, the commission would like to thank parliament for expressing its support for cord blood storage and use as an alternative source to bone marrow transplantation. it is important to ensure that good quality cord blood samples are available for patients. in order to support member states in their work, the commission has already started to address some of the key issues that parliament raises in this report. the commission is developing tools to support traceability and vigilance at eu level. an eu code will be applicable to all tissues and cells exchanged between member states as from 2014 and the communication platform for competent authorities’ rapid alerts for tissues and cells will be operational before the end of this year. discussions with member states are ongoing to define equivalent standards of safety and quality for tissues and cells imported from third countries. we plan to present a proposal on this issue by the end of next year. the commission has also supported several projects fostering the sharing of best practices and providing training for tissues and cells authorities under the health programme. however, despite such progress, much work still needs to be done. public awareness about cord blood donation and how to ensure availability and access to cord blood and bone marrow across the eu need careful consideration. another issue that requires thorough reflection by member states concerns the delicate balance between compensation and remuneration. the tissues and cells directive stipulates that compensation must be strictly limited to making good the expenses and inconveniences related to the donation. it is up to the member states to define such compensation, which may vary according to the specificities of the healthcare systems in the different member states. overall, the national application of the principle of voluntary and unpaid donation for tissues and cells therefore requires careful and judicious analysis within each and every member state. another area that requires our attention is scientific and technical progress. since the tissues and cells directive was adopted, new testing methods, new storage techniques and new therapies have emerged. such developments are being evaluated by the commission in collaboration with the member states. the commission is also currently finalising the transposition check of the tissue and cells legislation and preparing a survey on its implementation in the member states. the commission will be pleased to share the results of the survey with parliament by the end of next year. on the basis of the results of this survey, the commission will consider the possible review of the tissues and cells directive. your report is very timely and will be a valuable support for the commission in undertaking this task.
in writing. i would like to welcome the report, first of all because it brings considerable improvements to the eu's health system. this report encourages member states to pay due attention to the collection of umbilical cord blood stem cells at birth and promotes better and more extensive collaboration between family and public blood banks. in the context of the fact that, contrary to the current transplant legislation, there are still countries where the trade in tissues and organs is unfettered, it is very important to create the legal framework for the transparent and safe operation of tissue and cell banks for patients. the transformation of these banks into profitable businesses that exploit the economic situation of certain segments of the population must be avoided. as in most cases the number of donors is not large enough in a member state, health authorities need to introduce clear criteria for tissue and cell donations in order to protect the poor from abuse. in addition, let us not forget that it is very important that donors be fully informed about the procedures used in the process of donating tissues and cells, but also about the moral, psychological, medical and social consequences of their actions.

member of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, i would like to thank mrs garcía pérez for her report on the working conditions of female workers. this report offers a comprehensive but gloomy picture – an assessment that the commission shares. women are over-represented in low-quality, precarious positions and frequently have few opportunities for career advancement. lack of policies to reconcile work and family or private life, inappropriate incentives or rigid gender roles can contribute to this unfavourable situation. the presence of children, too, often dampens women’s employment prospects significantly. this is an issue that has to be dealt with urgently, as a woman’s decision to have a child should not imply her exclusion from the labour market. the persistence of the gender pay gap, women’s lower representation in decision-making positions and the barriers facing immigrant women are all further issues we have to fight against. overcoming these challenges features high on the commission’s political agenda. first, although there is no definite target for female employment rates in the europe 2020 strategy, it says that the 75 % employment rate in the 20-64 age group should be achieved through the greater involvement of women. the europe 2020 strategy also sets a target for reducing the number of europeans at risk of poverty by at least 20 million by 2020, which can hardly be achieved without better inclusion of women. second, gender issues were prominent during the european semester of enhanced policy coordination. the solid conclusion emerging from the first european semester was that the member states need to put in place a comprehensive policy mix to combat the gender employment gap and its main causes. fiscal disincentives for second earners from the tax benefit system, to provide flexible working arrangements and to combat the gender pay gap. the commission has monitored actions taken by the member states in this field and taken stock of progress made but has noted that additional efforts were necessary. the commission has instruments to help member states design and implement more efficient actions in this area. addressing equal treatment for women can be found in our few recent initiatives that underline the importance of a growing and inclusive workforce and a more equal society. directive on equal pay matters in 2013. the commission has recently launched an initiative which will help to raise the awareness of companies about the business and economic case for gender equality, labour market. the employment package also calls on the member states to establish national job plans within their national reform programmes and use them to focus on job creation and to fine-tune the the energy performance of buildings directive requires member states to achieve near-zero energy consumption for all new buildings from 2021 and for all new buildings occupied and owned by public authorities from 2019. however, so far the commission has not received any national plan on increasing the number of nearly zero-energy buildings. the directive discussed today introduces new obligations for member states, such as the annual renovation of 3% of the surface of buildings owned by public institutions, to increase energy efficiency. although less ambitious than the original itre commission position, the compromise presented gives flexibility to national, regional and local authorities. i would point out that we are imposing ambitious obligations on the member states, but without ensuring adequate funding. i call for energy efficiency measures to have adequate sources of funding in the future multiannual financial framework, in particular through the structural funds. tomorrow's vote should represent a firm commitment by parliament to this end.
in writing. the new energy efficiency directive is an important step towards achieving the europe 2020 targets in both energy and pollution reduction. the new directive could lead to a reduction in energy consumption, limit imports, create new jobs and social security. it should be borne in mind that energy efficiency does not only mean investing in renewable energy or new energy projects, but first and foremost improving existing ones and reducing energy waste, which is very high at the moment, generating unjustifiable costs for citizens and, in particular, for socially vulnerable people. it is essential that new investments in energy efficiency are economically sustainable and do not lead to unwanted side effects such as increased energy costs for end-users. i also believe it is vital that this investment should also cover the private housing sector, as in many member states, especially in central and eastern europe, this generates extremely high energy losses. the same applies to energy production and transmission infrastructure, which needs to be modernised to limit collateral losses.

member of the commission. - i believe that our task is to avoid increasing poverty and reducing the net disposable income of european citizens. i believe that our joint work in the coming years can lead to growth, to more employment and also to the competitiveness of the member states, their citizens, their businesses and their economies. in the field of energy: the commission is in the process of controlling the market, preventing or destroying monopolies, promoting competition and strengthening consumer rights. we have a big conference in london every year, where the only issue is consumer rights, i.e. the position of the small consumer of electricity or gas or heat vis-à-vis his contractual partner in an open market. in conclusion, the commission's budget proposal for the period 2014-2020 focuses on the energy sector. we will publicly fund energy research with european funds and thus relieve the burden on consumers. we want to co-finance infrastructure connecting europe facility with 19.1 billion from the european budget, thus relieving the burden on electricity and gas consumers, and we want to co-finance energy efficiency by focusing our structural programmes on the renovation of european buildings with the aim of achieving higher energy efficiency and thus lowering the long-term electricity bill, whether for schools, kindergartens or old people's homes, whether for private homes or for public infrastructure.

in writing. − continuing efforts at institutional cooperation in the field of standardisation is one of the instruments through which the european union can stimulate the increase in the economic competitiveness of actors on its territory, as well as technological progress and innovation capacities. the standardisation process also contributes to a high level of consumer satisfaction through its indirect positive influence on lowering prices and improving the quality of european products. supporting the standardisation process can make a positive contribution to the european union's efforts to combat the effects of climate change and to supporting the work of small and medium-sized enterprises in the member states, the largest group of economic actors on the continent. national and european authorities must not forget that, in promoting standards-setting efforts, the interests of building an inclusive society must also be taken into account. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
