in writing. − the eu's unity in diversity is a compromise that brings advantages, but also creates numerous obstacles. this is why the public and economic sectors, together with actors defending the interests of civil society, need to standardise services to operate more efficiently. european businesses need to improve their ability to adapt to changes in the global economy. standardisation can provide real support, especially for smes, and therefore it is necessary to take them into account when developing standardisation criteria. the low interest of public authorities in participating in the european standard-setting process creates delays and contributes to maintaining gaps between eu regions. in the field of public procurement, the harmonisation of procedures is a priority and digitalisation plays an important role in this respect. i consider it a priority to involve the social partners in the process of establishing standardisation criteria. the creation of a common framework on safety and rights for workers, people with disabilities and measures to increase sustainability contribute to improving social standards in the eu. i support this report because i believe that the process of standardisation is essential to attract investment from third countries. potential investors complain about the diversity of european markets and their lack of correlation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on european standardisation, as i believe that european standardisation can help to increase the competitiveness of businesses by facilitating the free movement of goods and services, the interoperability of networks, the means of communication, technological progress and innovation. the main objective of standardisation is to define voluntary technical or qualitative specifications that can be met by current or future products, production processes or services. standardisation may address different issues, such as standardisation of different classes or sizes of a particular product or technical specifications in product or service markets for which compatibility and interoperability with other products or systems are essential. the fundamental principles recognised by the world trade organisation (wto) in the field of standardisation, namely the principles of consistency, transparency, openness, consensus, voluntary application, independence from private interests and efficiency, should underpin european standardisation. in line with those fundamental principles, it is important that all relevant stakeholders, including public authorities and small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), are adequately involved in the standardisation process at national and european level. national standardisation bodies should encourage and facilitate the participation of interested parties.
in writing. − in these economically difficult times for the union's member states, it is not appropriate to burden farmers with additional administrative requirements. farmers have enough challenges to deal with to add to their burdens. at the same time, however, food security is one of the main concerns of european citizens. electronic identification of bovine animals allows for more reliable data and also strengthens the traceability system. member states will be able to decide whether the requirements will be mandatory in their territory. i think it is a very good solution and i support the rapporteur's approach and the solution proposed by the commission, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − food safety is one of the main concerns of european citizens. european legislation must ensure their optimum protection by means of updated and stricter provisions whenever this proves necessary. following the crisis of bovine spongiform encephalopathy, the european union introduced strict rules on the identification and traceability of bovine animals in 1997. electronic identification of bovine animals allows for more reliable data, strengthening the traceability system and, at the same time, food security. it also allows for faster registration of cattle, automation of certain tasks and more effective management of herds. i think it is necessary to debate whether this measure is mandatory or optional and to quantify the costs that farmers should bear.
in writing. − this proposal aims to address important challenges in the adoption of emerging electronic bovine identification technology, the simplification of beef and veal labelling provisions and the updating of the rules on the commission's powers. this is to ensure the clarity and applicability of legislation on the identification and traceability of bovine animals and to achieve an optimal level of food security. an adaptation of the current legislation is necessary, in particular to recognise electronic identification as an official means of identification of bovine animals. it is essential to ensure the harmonisation of technical rules in order to avoid a possible anarchic development of this method of identification and to achieve interoperability between national devices. i request that the information to the actors in the system for the identification and registration of animals be provided 'at no cost to the addressee' in order to protect small farmers and other actors in the identification system and that it be repeated 'as often as necessary' to take account of the adaptations to this regulation. in order not to create problems for trade within the internal market, it is necessary that member states are informed by the commission of devices accepted in the territory of member states that have opted for mandatory electronic identification.
in writing. - i voted against the amendments to remove the optional labelling of beef and poultrymeat, because european citizens have the right to have as much detailed information as possible about the products they buy. i am in favour of simplifying this system but not of eliminating it. optional labelling systems should be encouraged in all areas of food production, provided that they do not lead to excessive bureaucracy.
in writing. - i voted for the report on the electronic identification of bovine animals and the abolition of the provisions on the optional labelling of beef and poultrymeat. electronic identification of bovine animals allows for more reliable data, strengthening the traceability system and, at the same time, food security. an adaptation of the current legislation is necessary, in particular to recognise electronic identification as an official means of identification of bovine animals. tracing beef to its source by means of identification and registration is a mandatory condition for origin labelling throughout the food chain. those measures ensure consumer protection and public health and promote consumer confidence. the use of electronic identification systems could streamline traceability processes by automatically and more accurately reading and recording in the farm register. it would also allow for the automatic reporting of animal movements to the electronic database and thus improve the speed, reliability and accuracy of the system. the use of electronic identification systems would improve the management of direct payments to farmers per head by optimising controls and reducing the risk of payment errors.
in writing. − i support this first reading agreement which will enhance pharmacovigilance within the eu. i particularly favour the introduction of the activation of an automatic urgent procedure allowing the commission to withdraw from the market a pharmaceutical drug if risks for public safety are detected. i truly believe that more efficient and transparent procedures need to be put in place, especially since the mediator scandal in france has dramatically highlighted how the lack of uniform and rational rules on this issue can severely harm eu patients’ safety. i particularly commend the fact that the rapporteur has fully understood the importance of ensuring that the highest possible level of protection is equally granted to all eu citizens, also in line with the actual commission orientation. i also wish to express my full support to this agreement as far as the need for further clarification of transparency obligations on companies when they withdraw a drug is concerned: in the aforementioned mediator scandal, the french company servier withdrew mediator from spain, claiming it was for commercial reasons, thus severely delaying investigations that might have helped save a number of lives estimated between 500 and 2000.
in writing. − the european parliament and the council agreed to review the rules governing pharmacovigilance at eu level by adopting directive 2010/84/eu. a number of measures are needed to lead to greater safety of medicines at eu level by strengthening the role of the european medicines agency in data collection and taking action in the event of detection of signals, as well as a number of other measures, such as: - clarification of transparency obligations for companies when companies voluntarily withdraw a medicinal product or do not apply for the renewal of a marketing authorisation, they must specifically state whether this is due to safety concerns; - summary of the product a brief description of the essential characteristics and data of the product that the patient needs to understand the benefit and potential risks of the product and to use it safely and appropriately; - the publication by the agency, on an annual basis, of a list of medicinal products for which marketing authorisations have been refused, revoked or suspended, the supply of which has been prohibited or which have been withdrawn from the market, including the reasons for such measures.
in writing. − i voted for the resolution on the proposal to amend directive 2001/83/ec on pharmacovigilance, as recent pharmacovigilance events in the union have demonstrated the need for an automated procedure at union level in specific cases of safety concerns, to ensure that the issue is assessed and addressed in all member states where the medicinal product is authorised. the normal procedure should be initiated for the quality, safety or efficacy of medicinal products where the interests of the union are at stake. the union-wide emergency procedure should be initiated when a rapid assessment of concerns arising from the evaluation of data generated by pharmacovigilance activities is required. whether the union-wide emergency procedure or the normal procedure applies and regardless of the centralised or non-centralised procedure by which the medicinal product has been authorised, the pharmacovigilance risk assessment committee should always issue a recommendation where the reason for action is based on pharmacovigilance data. the measures adopted substantially strengthen the legal framework for pharmacovigilance, through provisions to strengthen the coordination role of the european medicines agency, detection flagging capabilities and the application of coordinated procedures at european level.
in writing. − the european parliament and the council agreed to review the rules governing pharmacovigilance at eu level by adopting regulation (eu) no 1235/2010. a number of measures have been identified as being necessary following the european commission's stress test of this legislation, namely: - an automated emergency procedure for example, where member states wish to withdraw a medicinal product, benefiting from a discretionary margin to do so, and the european commission proposes that the emergency procedure be automated; - a new element triggering the emergency procedure if companies decide not to apply for the renewal of the marketing authorisation for safety reasons, this should trigger the emergency procedure; - for medicinal products included in the list of medicinal products subject to additional monitoring, the summary of product characteristics and the package leaflet must state 'this medicinal product is subject to additional monitoring'. this shall be preceded by a black symbol selected by the commission on the recommendation of the pharmacovigilance risk assessment committee by 2 july 2013 and followed by an appropriate standard explanatory note.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 726/2004 as regards pharmacovigilance. in order to ensure transparency regarding the supervision of authorised medicinal products, the list of medicinal products subject to additional supervision introduced by regulation (ec) no 726/2004 should include all medicinal products subject to post-authorisation safety conditions. the european medicines agency, in collaboration with the member states, shall establish, manage and publish a list of medicinal products subject to additional monitoring. the list includes a link to the product information and the summary of the risk management plan. that list shall include the names and active substances of: (a) medicinal products authorised in the union containing a new active substance which was not part of any medicinal product authorised in the union on 1 january 2011; (b) any biological medicinal product not covered by point (a) which has been authorised after 1 january 2011; (c) medicinal products authorised under this regulation subject to the conditions referred to in article 9 (4) (c) or article 10a (1) (a), article 14 (7) or article 14 (8); (d) medicinal products authorised under directive 2001/83/ec subject to the conditions referred to in article 21a (b) and (c) or article 22 or article 22a (1) (a) of that directive.
in writing. − for the shipping industry, the traditional means of propulsion used by seagoing vessels is heavy fuel oil, a derivative of oil. heavy fish may have a sulphur content of up to 5%. for comparison, the sulphur content of fuels used by trucks or cars must not exceed 0,001%. sulphur dioxide emissions are known to cause acid rain and to generate suspended dust. these dusts are hazardous to human health, causing respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, and reducing life expectancy in the eu by up to two years. for these reasons, i support the commission's proposal, which is part of the efforts to tackle air quality problems and precedes a wider review of air policies to be carried out before 2013.
in writing. − the objective of the proposal is to implement the upper limits on sulphur content in marine fuels agreed in 2008 within the international maritime organisation (imo). the imo sulphur limits are 0,1% in the sulphur emission control areas (secas) from 2015 and 0,5% in the other maritime zones from 2020. the sulphur limit in the ceaz is currently set at 1%. by the end of 2011, fuels used at sea may contain up to 4,5% sulphur and thereafter, by 2019, up to 3,5%. the 0.1% sulphur limit proposed by the commission is to apply to all territorial waters of eu member states within 12 nautical miles of their coasts. by the end of 2013, the commission should explore the possibilities of establishing new emission control areas in european maritime zones and methods leading to further emission reductions, and subsequently report to the parliament and the council on this subject and present proposals for the establishment of possible new sulphur and nitrogen oxide emission control areas.
in writing. − air pollution from shipping is thought to be responsible for thousands of premature deaths each year in europe, as well as for causing significant long-term environmental damage. i fully support this agreement, especially the more ambitious deadline of 2020 by which the new limits must be in force. it strikes the right balance between environmental protection, legal certainty, and a realistic target for operators. regulating the maritime sector and creating a genuine level playing field for its operators is notoriously difficult. the international agreements made through the international maritime organisation are minimum standards, and we should strive to improve on them. as the commission’s analysis shows, the health and environmental benefits of a 2020 deadline will be significant, and the sector will be encouraged – and helped – to make the necessary investments, resulting in a cleaner atmosphere and a healthier environment.
in writing. - i voted for the report on the reduction of the sulphur content of certain marine fuels because the application of the new provisions will help to reduce environmental pollution caused by the burning of marine fuels with high sulphur content. the achievement of the objectives of directive 1999/32/ec on the reduction of sulphur content in certain marine fuels requires the appropriate application of the obligations on the sulphur content of marine fuels. i believe that a stronger system of monitoring and enforcement of sulphur obligations is needed to ensure the proper implementation of the directive. compliance with the low sulphur limits of marine fuels may result in a significant increase in prices. appropriate solutions are therefore needed to reduce the compliance costs borne by the affected industries, such as the authorisation of alternative and more cost-effective compliance methods. i believe that member states and the commission should promote the testing and development of new technologies, considering the possibility of creating a joint programme to reduce pollution from marine fuels, co-financed with industry and based on the principles of similar programmes such as the clean sky programme.
in writing. - i voted for this report because of the importance of the wine sector in romania. my country is a major wine producer and for that reason i think it is appropriate to amend the regulation on the single payment scheme and support for wine growers. in this way, we will ensure that this sector is appropriately financed in the future multiannual financial framework. romania attaches particular importance to the reform of the common agricultural policy, aiming for the period 2014-2020 at maintaining allocations at least at the current level. if we want romanian and european agriculture to progress, we must ensure that the money for the cap is used in the most efficient way possible. this is the main challenge for the common agricultural policy in the forthcoming multiannual financial perspective.
in writing. − as farmers face increasing risks and problems in increasing productivity, the latest cap reforms focus on strengthening support for rural development as an integrated policy in the development of rural areas across the eu. the new proposal on support for winegrowers recommends that the five-year period provided for in the current legislation be reduced to one year and apply only in 2014, with the possibility of an irrevocable transfer decision from 2015. i believe that the solution proposed by the commission is favourable to the wine system and will bring continuity to the strategies adopted by the member states in this sector of agriculture. this will enable winegrowers to manage risks much better and to react quickly to crisis situations. a strong agriculture is vital both for the european food industry and for global food security.
in writing. − the development of administrative cooperation between member states and the european institutions on the single market's information communication infrastructure is an implicit guarantee of increasing the european union's economic competitiveness. it is equally important, however, that the benefits and opportunities offered by the internal market information system are also shared with the european citizens directly affected or involved, in a manner that does not affect the security and functionality of the system or through an interface separate from the system itself. at the same time, the economic and political development of the european union depends on the expansion of its relations with external partners. it is appropriate for the european institutions to examine the possibility of extending the internal market information system or of interconnecting it with the specialised it infrastructure of partner countries. last but not least, a strong commitment to european legislation on the protection of personal data should play an important role in all these efforts. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the internal market information system (imi) has proven to be a fast and secure means of ensuring crossborder information exchange and administrative cooperation. there are currently over 6 000 authorities in all member states registered in the system. a smooth cross-border exchange of information between member states' authorities is essential for the deepening of the single market in the european union. i believe that the commission's proposal will establish a sound legal framework for the imi. it will also facilitate the possible future extension of imi to new areas of eu law and clarify the role of the different actors involved in imi. last but not least, a comprehensive data protection framework will be ensured by developing rules for the processing of personal data in imi.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the imi system is a proven instrument in the effort to complete the single market. the new formula will also ensure better data protection and faster exchange of information between competent authorities by creating a 'face-to-face' electronic network of european administrations. the establishment of this common, efficient and secure communication channel, which is available in several languages, will further foster cooperation between the administrative structures of a member state with their counterparts in any other member state. i also agree with the rapporteur that this proposal will ensure that the full potential of the imi is exploited, bringing net benefits to both the internal market and citizens.
in writing. − i consider it beneficial that the competent authorities of the member states can, through the application of this regulation, communicate more quickly in a wider range of policy areas and, in particular, it is important that there is the possibility of better cooperation between local authorities and their participation in the single market.
in writing. - i voted for the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on administrative cooperation through the internal market information system (imi regulation). the internal market information system (imi) is a software application accessible via the internet, developed by the commission in cooperation with the member states, by establishing a centralised communication mechanism to facilitate cross-border exchange of information and mutual assistance. the imi shall help competent authorities to identify counterparts in other member states, to manage the exchange of information, including personal data, on the basis of simple and uniform procedures and to overcome language barriers on the basis of predefined and pre-translated workflows. i consider that, in order to overcome language barriers, it is necessary for imi to be available in all the official languages of the union. this regulation lays down the rules for the use of imi for administrative cooperation, including for the processing of personal data, between the competent authorities of the member states and between the competent authorities of the member states and the commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that europe must be put back on the path of economic growth and development and that the crisis we are still facing must be overcome as soon as possible. in this context, i believe that a clear and comprehensive picture of member states' strategies is needed. it is essential to develop new common policies in order to avoid a similar crisis in the future. at the same time, existing policies need to be reviewed to ensure that they remain appropriate to the challenges facing member states. the common system of taxation applicable to interest and royalty payments made between associated companies in different member states is an appropriate one, but it must provide greater clarity. to this end, i consider the commission's proposal to be a positive and at the same time necessary step.
in writing. − i consider that cooperation between the tax systems of the member states is essential to avoid the reduction of revenue not collected, which is detrimental to the proper functioning of the internal market. it is also beneficial to avoid the possibility of tax evasion, tax substitution or any undue tax exemptions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the common system of taxation applicable to interest and royalty payments made between associated companies in different member states. the european parliament called for concrete ways to combat tax fraud and tax evasion, drawing attention to the possibility of tax evasion. we call on member states to ensure cooperation and functional coordination between their tax systems to avoid involuntary tax avoidance and tax evasion. the elimination of all taxation of interest and royalties in the member state from which the payments originate is the most appropriate solution to eliminate formalities and problems and to achieve equality of tax treatment between domestic and cross-border transactions. this directive shall not affect the application of national provisions or provisions based on a convention which go beyond the provisions of this directive and have as their objective the elimination or mitigation of double taxation and the double non-taxation of interest and royalties. in order to ensure a simplified and more transparent taxation system, it is therefore necessary to eliminate the taxation of such payments when they are made between associated companies in different member states or between the permanent establishments of such companies.
in writing. − europe must commit itself to the social market economy model, which leads to sustainable growth, jobs and a better quality of life for citizens. the union's main challenges are to maintain competitiveness, to grow the economy, to combat unemployment, to ensure a functioning labour market and good social conditions to improve employment performance, to promote decent work, to guarantee workers' rights and working conditions across europe and to reduce poverty. the european commission must present a european action plan to stimulate sustainable economic growth and decent jobs. it must also present an eu strategy for the homeless, addressing the growing problem of poverty among women and minimum pension schemes. slow progress was made on the presentation of a commission legislative proposal on improving gender balance in company management and the commission's lack of initiative in revising the directive on equal opportunities for women and men in matters of pay and employment. the commission should closely monitor the launch of the paternity leave initiative and present a legislative proposal on the eradication of violence against women.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the commission's work programme for 2013, calling on the commission to take action on simplifying eu programmes, in particular in the field of research and innovation, and to monitor closely the use of financial engineering instruments. we also call on the commission to present a detailed action plan with measures for a fully integrated and interconnected single energy market and to develop a strategy to address the impact of rising energy prices on the most vulnerable members of society. we support the need to modernise europe's multimodal transport network, which is fundamental to the success of the internal market. we voted for the paragraphs stressing the importance of youth employment and the need to expand the union's capacity to stimulate education and training and we expect concrete measures to reduce poverty and reform the labour market. we call for a strong cohesion policy at eu level after 2013, ensuring the integration of existing funds and programmes, ensuring adequate resources, building on multi-level governance and aligning with the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy.
in writing. − donations should be made voluntarily, without profit and in a transparent manner. it exclusively refers to tissues and cells that fall into one of these three categories, namely multiple tissues, reproductive cells and non-reproductive cells. in order to optimise the potential of cord blood, the competent authorities should develop awareness campaigns, targeting in particular future mothers. common rules should also be strengthened and implemented within both national and private banks, which should work together to increase the availability of national cord blood samples. compensation for donations should be carefully managed and presented by member states and should be limited to compensation for expenses incurred in the process of donation, such as travel expenses, loss of income or medical costs. member states should consider increasing the number of bone marrow and peripheral blood stem cell donors so that any patient requiring a stem cell transplant has the best chance of finding a compatible donor.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution and was pleased to reiterate my support not just for the principle of unpaid and voluntary donation but also for the related issue of cord blood research. i want to stress the importance of giving the right information to parents so they can make informed choices about the collection and in particular the storage of cord blood. whilst fully exploring the potential of this area of medicine and promoting the collection of cord blood for the mutual benefit of everyone, we must be sure that the information given about the potential uses of cord blood is consistent with scientific knowledge and not unproven speculation. i am grateful that parliament gave its support to my call for the european group on ethics to re-examine the ethical aspects of cord blood banking.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on voluntary and unpaid donation of tissues and cells. i think it is important that all member states clearly define the conditions under which fair and proportionate financial compensation can be granted, taking into account that it is strictly limited to covering the costs of donating tissues and cells. member states must adopt measures to protect living donors and ensure that donation is anonymous (except for collection from a living person for a close relative), voluntary, freely consented to, informed and unpaid. it is necessary for member states to step up their public information and awareness campaigns in favour of tissue and cell donation and to ensure the provision of clear, fair, scientifically sound and conclusive medical information and data enabling the public to make an informed choice. it considers it important to establish rules to ensure the traceability of tissues and cells of human origin from donor to patient and vice versa, and a system to regulate imports of human tissues and cells from third countries, ensuring that equivalent standards of quality and safety are applied.
in writing. − an ecological or sustainable economy is a system that conserves the productive capacity of ecosystems while creating a society in which the basic needs of all people are met. equal participation in ecological politics and economics is needed to ensure that women's interests are taken into account as well as men's. the current economic system ignores the limited nature of natural resources. production and consumption generate emissions and forms of pollution that sooner or later will end up in our ecosystem. the capacity of the ecosystem to absorb and manage emissions and to adapt to changing circumstances is finite. once the absolute limit is reached, important ecosystem services are at risk of disappearing. i think that to avoid such a scenario, we need to move to an economic system where the pace of natural resource extraction favors resource recovery as well as the production of new resources.
in writing. − the green economy is defined as a socially and ecologically sustainable economy, as social sustainability includes a social order based on gender equality and social justice, regardless of gender, ethnicity, colour, religion, sexual orientation, disability or political opinion. the role of women in the green economy in many member states continues to be underestimated and ignored, creating numerous discriminations in terms of lost benefits such as social protection, health insurance, adequate wage and pension rights. member states must recognise the importance of the essential role women play in raising and educating children and protecting the environment and adequately remunerate both informal and formal work. the european commission must support investments and programmes that promote green jobs for those who need them most: young people, women and the poor. member states must ensure appropriate working conditions and strengthened social dialogue to facilitate the transition to the new green jobs, also for women. they must also be proactive in granting women access to a decent standard of health care and education and housing.
in writing. − socially and ecologically, the green economy is a sustainable economy, which includes a social order based on both gender equality and social justice, regardless of gender, ethnicity, colour, religion or political opinion. in several member states, the role of women in the green economy continues to be ignored, creating numerous discriminations in terms of lost rights such as social protection, health insurance, wage and pension rights. in this context, i believe that, at european level, environmental policies at all levels must include a gender perspective in defining, implementing and monitoring the promotion of gender mainstreaming as an instrument of good governance in the context of the europe 2020 strategy, but also in strengthening gender equality and social justice. i also believe that member states should promote specific research and studies on women and gender equality in the green economy so that the gender perspective is included in environmental protection and environmental impact assessment studies.
in writing. − the transition to a green economy affects women and men equally in different sectors of activity both socially and professionally, but not to the same extent, with much greater discrepancies in some member states than in others. unfortunately, we still do not have concrete data, based on extensive eu-wide studies, to illustrate these differences as realistically as possible and to allow us to draw up clear policies in relation to gender perspectives. these policies are needed to be then specifically integrated into sustainable development programmes at regional, national and international level, thus eliminating the disparities existing in different areas of the eu.
in writing. − i voted for the resolution on the role of women in the green economy because i believe that a sustainable economy means an economy that creates decent jobs and sustainable communities and allows for a fairer distribution of resources. we voted for the provision of adequate working conditions and decent standards in health, education and housing for women, and for their strong participation in social dialogues to facilitate adaptation to the new green jobs. i support the need for more childcare centers, which is absolutely necessary to reconcile work and family life. we believe that european policies should provide support for social security, family planning and childcare, because only a society that provides these conditions can enable women to bring their experience to bear and contribute equally to the prosperity of green economies. we call on member states to ensure equal representation of women in political decision-making bodies, as well as in government-appointed bodies and institutions dealing with the definition, planning and implementation of environmental, energy and green jobs policies, so that a gender perspective is integrated into these policies.
in writing. − in the european union, in 2010, service jobs accounted for 69.4% of total jobs, of which 83.1% of the female labour force worked in the service sector, compared with 58.1% of the male labour force. in romania, according to a world bank report on equal opportunities for women and men, women are paid on average 10% less than men for similar jobs and the same level of education. this difference is, however, smaller than that in the region. equal pay for women and men is a 'smart economy', as countries that create opportunities and good working conditions for women can increase productivity. to achieve a good balance between gender representation and professional competence, companies should adopt a system of flexible quotas for women's representation on boards. flexible quotas mean that each company will set its own percentage, selection procedure and deadline for reaching the quota.
in writing. − in the eu, in 2010, service sector jobs accounted for 69.4% of total jobs, while industrial jobs accounted for 25.4% and agricultural jobs for 5.2%. the majority of the female labour force is employed in the service sector: 83.1% compared with 58.1% of the male labour force. member states should adopt policies to integrate vulnerable workers, in particular those with low skills, the unemployed, young and older workers, persons with disabilities, persons with mental disorders or belonging to minority groups, such as migrants and roma, into the labour market through well-targeted and tailored vocational guidance, training and traineeship programmes. the situation of migrant and undeclared workers in the service sector, in particular those employed in private households, the majority of whom work without a contract, in precarious work, in home services and in inappropriate working conditions, with lower wages than those of declared workers and without social rights, requires the adoption of appropriate policies to ensure that migrant workers enjoy fundamental human rights, including the right to healthcare, fair working conditions, education and training, physical and moral integrity and equality before the law.
in writing. − the increasing individualisation and flexibility of the labour market in many member states puts employees, and particularly women, who also have to fulfil family obligations, in a more vulnerable position, which can lead to precarious employment. the share of women in precarious employment in the labour market is high and certain forms of precarious work performed by women, such as paid domestic work and care work, are almost non-existent in the labour market. in the european union, there are wide disparities in employment opportunities, quality of work and equal pay for equal work or work of equal value, according to the current legislative framework. in these circumstances, i believe that both the ec and the member states must adopt clear guidelines and concrete measures to safeguard existing jobs but also to create employment opportunities, especially for women, within the europe 2020 strategy. a strategy on precarious work at european level is needed, with a focus on both decent and green jobs and gender mainstreaming.
in writing. − i voted for the resolution on working conditions for women in the service sector because 83.1% of the female labour force worked in these sectors in 2010. also, nine out of ten new jobs created are in the services sector and the future development of the single market for services will contribute to significant job growth in this sector. i support the need to strengthen policies aimed at reconciling family and working life and, in particular, to increase free and quality public social services and structures to provide childcare and other dependants in both rural and urban areas. i believe it is important to involve more women in research, as they can play a decisive role in the development of new and innovative systems and new products and services in the service sector. they argue that greater participation of women in innovation processes would open up new markets and increase european competitiveness. last but not least, the acquisition of ict skills will increase the employment opportunities of women, especially in the service sector.
in writing. − vocational education and training is one of the engines of economic growth, while also contributing to greater social inclusion and cohesion. it is therefore necessary that policies in this area are implemented in the europe 2020 strategy as effectively as possible. i believe that there is a need for further investment in education, lifelong learning, research and innovation. i believe that young people should benefit from increased measures to integrate into the labour market after leaving school, as they are a category that has been deeply affected by the current crisis. last but not least, i believe that older people should be encouraged to participate in education and training activities aimed at personal fulfilment and social contact. i voted in favour of this resolution, which can help to improve cooperation in the field of education and vocational training in the next stage of the 'education and training 2020' programme.

in writing. − the education sector must be seen as a priority in all member states, and how we regulate lifelong learning now will have a profound effect on the well-being of future generations of the european union. although there are efforts to implement and popularise adult continuing training programmes at a wide level, i believe that considerable efforts are needed in terms of vocational retraining. jobs come and go from decade to decade, and the number of people who are unable to work because they are not keeping up with the pace of science and technology is constantly increasing. moreover, i believe that the increase in the retirement age is an additional argument for starting solid investment in comprehensive vocational retraining and lifelong learning programmes across the union.
in writing. − our regular discussion of the general situation in education and training across the union helps us to assess progress towards the common goals. cooperation in education and training can undoubtedly support the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. we need to do more to reduce early school leaving and increase the proportion of higher education graduates, including by providing support for young people from financially disadvantaged families. early education is in turn an extremely valuable factor in the later development of the individual. we cannot afford to give up this component of training, which has a long-term positive impact on national budgets and on the health of citizens, which helps to reduce antisocial behaviour later on. lifelong learning must also be encouraged, as the retirement age is steadily rising in europe and the skills needed by employees are becoming more diverse. we fully recognise the importance of citizens' participation in crossborder mobility programmes, but we have not yet succeeded in removing the obstacles to labour mobility. it is time to expand the very small list of professions recognised at european level and to remove the barriers that exist in the member states.
in writing. − in the current situation in the context of the most severe and prolonged crisis in the history of the european union education and training and the prevention of early school leaving are investments that guarantee a successful resolution of the crisis. it is imperative that the demand for and supply of work be exactly in line with each other in order to avoid the creation of so-called lost generations. the lifelong learning programme can and should be the most helpful in this respect, because it can and should enable you to adapt to a changing labour market of opportunities. through better quality education and training, younger or less younger generations have a better chance of overcoming the crisis. the member states have a difficult task: it is difficult to create synergies between labour supply and labour market absorption capacity. higher education makes it easier to find a job, but we must beware of the 'dumping' of higher education, because society is in great need of craftsmen, skilled workers and the continuation of our traditional trades.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on education and training in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. if the eu is to emerge from the current economic and financial crisis, economic growth must be based primarily on education, knowledge, innovation and appropriate social policies. in order to successfully overcome this period, it is important that policies in this area are properly and fully implemented in the framework of the eu 2020 strategy. i call on member states to prioritise spending on education, lifelong learning, research, innovation and linguistic and cultural diversity as investments for future growth, while ensuring the added value of this investment. the unemployment rate in the eu has risen to over 20%, with levels above 50% in some member states and regions, and young people, especially the least qualified, are particularly affected by the current economic and financial crisis. i would stress that young people have a key role to play in achieving the main objectives of the europe 2020 strategy in terms of employment, research and innovation, climate and energy, education and poverty reduction. economic and social development and the competitiveness of the eu and its member states depend on investment in education and training and the quality of services in these sectors.
in writing. - i voted for this report because the european audiovisual market is very fragmented. greater predictability is needed for both copyright holders and consumers. the creation of a digital single market requires the removal of all barriers to the free movement of audiovisual products. this must be done in a way that respects copyright and ensures adequate remuneration for rightholders. i also consider it particularly important to respect the principle of net neutrality. we must allow consumers non-discriminatory access to audiovisual products distributed on the internet. the achievement of general interest objectives such as media pluralism and cultural diversity requires special measures. the commission and the member states should propose concrete measures to this end.
in writing. − digital technology and the internet are rapidly changing the way audiovisual material is produced, marketed and distributed. increasingly, consumers want to be able to watch anything, anywhere, anytime, on any device. business models need to evolve rapidly to keep pace with the ever-accelerating pace of technological change, which offers new opportunities for creators and distributors, while also creating new expectations among consumers and thus stimulating growth and job creation. the production, financing and distribution of audiovisual works in the eu is handled by a complex network of large, medium and small specialised enterprises, each with its own specific characteristics. the single market is working and offers new perspectives and opportunities for consumers, creators and service providers alike. i believe that the union's policy in this area must aim at creating an environment which favours the development of legal content accessible to all, innovation and creativity.
in writing. − in an increasingly dynamic information society, the cultural and creative industries must continue to provide a significant number of jobs in all member states. this will also make it possible to increase the economic contribution of these sectors to the gross domestic product of the countries of the union. last but not least, we must bear in mind that these sectors make a significant contribution to the education of young people, a priority area of european policies.
in writing. − the issue of intellectual property rights in audiovisual content, including in the digital sphere, has been discussed at eu level for a long time, with many attempts at harmonisation taking place to date. what i think we're missing, however, is a more cause-and-effect approach, in this case a matter of educating citizens about the importance of copyright protection and the proper use of online distribution channels. moreover, education systems in the member states need to focus on developing digital skills and integrating new technologies into curricula so that future generations are aware of the importance of adopting a civic attitude in the digital environment.
in writing. − given the specific nature of the audiovisual sector, but also the fragmentation of the european online market, a unified approach to several issues at community level is required. online use can be a real opportunity for better dissemination and distribution of european works, provided that the provision of audiovisual works is made legally, in compliance with the principle of copyright. looking at the figures available at european level, an interesting phenomenon emerges: the cultural and creative industries we are talking about contribute up to 2.5% of gdp, which is similar to the figures for the automotive industry. this makes it all the more important to organise public awareness campaigns on the importance of copyright, alongside programmes to promote digital and media literacy for all eu citizens, including those with disabilities. i also support facilitating online payment methods for audiovisual works, and rethinking the associated costs, as an accessible alternative to piracy. i also stress the importance of adapting european legislation to the realities of the internet and the digital age, and one of the biggest challenges is still preventing access to platforms offering illegal content.
in writing. - i voted for the report on the online distribution of audiovisual works in the european union. the fragmentation of the online market is characterised by technological barriers, the complexity of licensing procedures, differences in payment methods, lack of interoperability for essential elements and variations in certain taxes applicable to goods and services. i believe that a transparent, flexible and harmonised approach is needed at european level in order to progress towards a digital single market. i would stress that the digital divide between member states or regions of the eu is a serious barrier to the development of the digital single market. i recommend that broadband internet access be extended throughout the eu to stimulate access to online services and new technologies. online use can represent a real opportunity for better dissemination and distribution of european works, in particular audiovisual works, provided that their legal provision can develop in an environment of fair competition. calls on the member states and the commission to promote solutions to support the digitisation, preservation and educational availability of these works, including at cross-border level.
on behalf of the s&d group. – madam president, we are now debating again a traditional and important report on our cfsp. this year its author elmar brok has decided to break the pattern of this report and introduce a newer approach, less conventional and more strategic in nature, setting a relatively high level of ambition for our cfsp. a first hurdle to overcome has been that of the current situation which compels the eu to be more inward-looking and parsimonious with its means, in other words, while challenges are accumulating, our willingness and capacity to properly deal with them have objectively diminished. under the circumstances one wonders whether the level of ambition stated by the report is reflecting a normal situation unaffected by crisis or is attuned to our current difficulties. this is important because in the first case we might become unrealistic and in the second we might lack credibility. a second hurdle has been the rapid evolution of the international environment, including the one in our direct neighbourhood. the report is inevitably a snapshot of the situation at a certain moment in time, while the international environment is in a state of flux. therefore one needs to anticipate and be in front of developments if one wants to stay relevant. a third hurdle is our credibility. indeed we have to convince the rest of the world that we continue to be an attractive option, that we can both master our own problems and still pay considerable attention to what happens around us and in the rest of the world. inevitably, all these hurdles have influenced the outcome reflected in this report, thus time is continuously pressing and we have all had to accommodate ourselves to the new tempo and deal with its novelty. consequently there were numerous amendments, too short a time to debate them and reach the inevitable compromises, and last minute amendments which sometimes go beyond and outside the compromise amendments reached previously. however, paying proper attention to this very important report, for which i salute the rapporteur, is indicative of our mission to continue to address properly international, political, economic and military issues in parallel with the efforts to overcome our internal crisis.
madam president, ms ashton, the csdp’s military and civilian missions have always been part of a larger international commitment, and they have only rarely brought about a real improvement in the situation on the ground. their function was always more to indicate to nato and the united states that the eu is in a position to take on security policy missions. only in a few instances, such as somalia, georgia and macedonia, was efficient crisis management achieved. in the future, member states should discuss and reach a decision on the following key documents prepared by the european external action service. on the one hand, there is a new security strategy, and on the other hand, a european white paper on security and defence policy defining what military and civilian tasks the eu will take on, where it will intervene, how the necessary capabilities will be provided, and how member states’ resources can be committed to these purposes. in doing so, the csdp must become more efficient at offering clear added value. in writing. – we will never be able to be efficient or have a proper vision of our external action as long as we fail to understand the fact that our values cannot be promoted until we manage to resolve our geo-strategic problems. this is not about abandoning our values. it is about creating a framework for them to grow roots and flourish. the primacy we currently give to the values does not reflect our attachment to them, but our incapacity to define the geo-strategic interests of the eu. since we do not know our identity, we do not know our interests and we cannot define our long-term objectives. this is why we prefer to fight an illusory crusade that gives us the false impression of being capable of imposing our model around the world, believing that this solves all of our other problems. until we change this approach we cannot have a real common foreign and security policy. what is worse, since our foreign policy is not the goal but rather the means, through its lack we condemn ourselves to irrelevance within the international competition.

the problem of the sugar sector is much wider than the issues raised by the questions in the debate today and is not confined to sugar cane. romania, for example, only obtains 20% of its consumption from its own resources, i.e. from beet grown and processed in the country, production being limited by the quota system. the remaining 80% of consumption is provided by refining imported raw sugar or directly by importing white sugar. in recent years, romanian refineries, and others, have had major problems supplying the necessary raw materials and maintaining the market. imports of raw materials are strictly limited to certain sources and only a small quantity can be purchased from efficient sources that can ensure a continuous supply. the european commission has so far been unable to come up with consistent proposals that would ensure supply to refineries in the medium and long term and allow for minimal planning of activity. as a result, refineries are operating at only 60% capacity. under these conditions of underutilization, refineries are inevitably forced to close their doors. we expect measures to remove the limitations on the supply of raw materials through tariff and non-tariff barriers. these measures are necessary and urgent if the union is to continue to have its own refining industry. if not, we'll keep importing.
the reform of the sugar market carried out by the union in 2006-07 has shown its limits. production at european level has decreased considerably. many of the member states have become importers of sugar after being net exporters a few years ago. this is also the case in romania, which can no longer satisfy its domestic consumption from domestic production. the future common agricultural policy will have to take account of these aspects. the quota system will have to be adjusted to the actual production, processing and consumption capacities of each country. the commission will also have to ensure fair competition between the three sugar production models. i am referring to cane sugar refineries, which are facing major difficulties in supplying raw materials.
