in writing. the european countries are in a very serious situation, and i do not want to talk primarily about the current economic and financial crisis, but about the moral crisis and the crisis of confidence that are affecting our societies at least as much as the debt crisis. the european nations embarked on an unprecedented project to create a common europe after the second world war, and yet, unfortunately, we all experience that even today, trust is still not complete, not only between the member states and the eu, but also between the states and their citizens. some countries are devoting considerable resources to goals that are long overdue. for example, some member states do not value national minorities living on their territory, but hinder their legitimate aspirations and continue to seek their assimilation. they spend more on their outdated, centralized administration, intelligence, military than they do on education, infrastructure, social issues. in my opinion, particularly in the present circumstances, these practices do not help to overcome the dual crisis of morality and trust that is stamping our daily lives.
mr president, i voted in favour of this proposal because it will strengthen and give more substance to the rights of the victims in the european union and will improve their protection throughout the union. we have finally set minimum standards for handling the victims of crimes, irrespective of their nationality or the place where the crime was perpetrated. this directive provides for the first time a unified definition of a victim to be used in all eu countries. this definition was broadened to include people such as the victims’ close family. this directive will increase the confidence of eu citizens in the area of justice and they will feel they are equally protected in all member states. i call on the member states to develop greater cooperation and coordination to protect and provide support for the victims of crime.
the role and needs of victims in criminal proceedings are still generally not sufficiently taken into account in the legal systems of the member states. the current situation shows that in many cases victims are not treated with respect and dignity, are not sufficiently protected or supported, and do not have effective access to justice, compensation and reparation. it is not acceptable that the level of support provided to a victim differs depending on the member state in which the victim was injured. mutual recognition can only work effectively in a climate of trust, where not only judicial authorities but also all parties to criminal proceedings can have confidence in the adequacy of the rules in each member state and can be sure that they are correctly applied. i therefore support this report and express my conviction that, once this directive is adopted, the situation of victims will improve considerably throughout the european union and that victims of crime will benefit from the same basic rights and services in all member states.
i voted in favour of this report because the european union's efforts to achieve sustainable fishing activities are not enough, as long as they are individual. the union must also encourage third countries to follow its example and pursue sustainable fishing activities. overfishing of certain fish stocks, such as mackerel, can have global effects. these effects are felt beyond the borders of the exploiting state, with long-term consequences for marine biodiversity. the imposition of trade barriers on states that engage in unsustainable exploitation may be the union's response to encourage responsible behaviour on their part. the adoption of such measures should be preceded by an environmental, commercial, economic and social impact assessment.
i voted for this report because the commission's proposal must provide a high degree of predictability for producer organisations. the common organisation of the markets in fishery products is a basic component of the common fisheries policy. the choice of products in full knowledge of the facts is particularly important for the european consumer. the use of an eco-label for fishery products provides clear information on the environmental sustainability of these products. to this end, full coherence between the common fisheries policy and the common commercial policy is necessary. imported products entering the union market should meet the same marketing requirements and standards as european union producers.
i voted in favour of this report, which is an annual report, a position paper and, above all, a document which should have a vision. of course, he continues the classic line of approach to the european union - he does not bring much new in this approach - but it was important to me that, in the security component of european policy, the rapporteur addressed some subjects which are important not only for the future of a common policy, which is sensitive in this area, but also for the visibility and strength of the european union outside its borders. i am referring to the fact that the strengthening of the external action service's capacity to act in the field of conflict prevention was welcomed. i think that allocating a significant amount of money in the future budget is very important. secondly, the issue i would like to highlight is the arms trade. a common position on the negotiation of the future treaty is the key to success in this area.
i too supported mr brok's report because the solution to global challenges can only be found through integrated approaches. the lisbon treaty gave the union a number of instruments to enable it to speak with one voice. however, there are still a number of shortcomings in the common foreign and security policy. strengthening relations between the european external action service, the commission and the member states is essential. only in this way can we achieve synergy in the effective implementation of external action. i believe that, as regards the future of the cfsp, special attention should be paid to the european neighbourhood policy, with emphasis on its eastern dimension. the eastern partnership must be an essential means of promoting the union's values in eastern europe and of offering a real european perspective to countries such as the republic of moldova.
i voted for this report because the current system of fishing quotas has brought the short-term concerns of the states to the fore. the sustainability of the fisheries sector has thus been put on the back burner. the regionalisation of the common fisheries policy should be considered as a solution to address the current shortcomings. the commission must initiate long-term plans which take account of the needs of the member states on the one hand and the need to preserve fish stocks on the other. some 60% of european fish stocks are exploited beyond the maximum sustainable yield. this overexploitation also affects other species, such as the black sea dolphins. they are accidentally caught in fishing nets very often. in this connection, i have initiated a written declaration on the need to establish means of protecting the dolphins in the black sea.
i also voted in favour of this report because the reform of fisheries at european level must take account of the realities in each member state. the commission should therefore draw up a series of studies on the fish stocks available at union level. estimates are required on the sustainable exploitation of these stocks. these estimates should propose a timetable for the reduction of the exploitation leading to a recovery of stocks in a relatively short time. it is particularly important that the studies are adapted to each member state and take account of the actual exploitation capacities it has. the possibility of regionalising the common fisheries policy needs to be examined more closely, however. this would ensure a much more efficient use of funds for fisheries.
in writing. − i entirely support this directive with the changes proposed in this report, because it will strengthen the rights of victims all over europe. i also voted in favour of this report because of the attention given to vulnerable categories in society, like children and people with special needs. in the past, citizens of the eu residing or travelling in another eu member state faced serious difficulties in getting the same level of protection as the nationals of that member state. this directive will create a set of minimum common standards across the eu for victims of crime, creating a shorter and easier process for victims to receive the support they need. ultimately, this will ensure that each victim is treated with respect and dignity without any sort of discrimination anywhere in the eu.
in writing. − trust in justice is a priority for all citizens, especially for victims whose rights are ignored or not respected. a common and transparent judicial system, applicable in all eu member states, is a pressing need. the directive will not only defend the rights of victims by providing support and protection, but will also help european citizens to gain confidence in the judicial systems of their own country and those of their eu neighbours by harmonising minimum standards. in order to assess in detail the circumstances and characteristics of the victims, it is necessary to define 'gender-based violence' and 'intimate partner violence'. gender-based violence refers to violence directed against a person because of their gender. intimate partner violence includes acts of violence by partners or former partners or other family members, leading to discrimination and violations of the fundamental freedoms of victims. the special situation of victims with specific needs shall be taken into account when designing appropriate support services or training practitioners who will have direct contact with victims. the directive thus includes a number of rights guaranteed to victims, filling a significant gap in the protection of human rights for victims of crime.
in writing. − i support the report on strengthening the rights of victims of crime across the eu. since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty in 2009 and the guidelines for the european area of freedom, security and justice, the protection of victims of all types of crime has been, as envisaged in the stockholm programme, at the top of the eu agenda. a common and transparent justice system, applicable in all eu member states, must be based on the need to support victims, including those with special needs or, as they have been called, vulnerable, such as victims of gender-based violence, children and people with disabilities. in europe, more than one fifth of all women have experienced physical violence at least once in their adult lives, and more than one in ten have experienced sexual violence involving the use of force. in this context, i believe it is essential to criminalize all forms of gender-based violence and to take special measures to prevent, protect and redress victims of this type of violence.
in writing. - approximately 15% of the eu population, i.e. about 75 million citizens, are directly affected by the approximately 30 million crimes (excluding minor crimes) committed annually (eurostat statistics 2007). previous regulations for the protection of victims of crime and their enforcement have been deficient so far. at the same time, member states' laws are currently very different and social dynamics are creating new regulatory requirements. given the above, i support this report, as the proposed measures will: - guarantee the respectful treatment and full and accurate information of victims and their accompanying persons about their rights; - provide victims with legal, financial, psychological and practical assistance; - ensure communication in a language that the victims understand; - ensure effective access to compensation and redress. i also consider it useful to take into account in the establishment of support measures factors such as the age, intellectual capacity of the victim, personal characteristics or the type of crime, which would make persons outside the categories established as vulnerable in general vulnerable.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on the establishment of minimum standards on the rights, support and protection of victims of crime. victims of crime must be recognised and treated with respect, care and professionalism, without discrimination on any ground such as race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic features, language, religion or belief, political or other opinion, belonging to a national minority, possessions, birth, disability, age, gender, gender identity and gender expression, sexual orientation, residence status or health. information and advice provided by competent authorities, victim support services and redress services should, as far as possible, be provided through a range of means and in a manner that can be understood by the victim. the victim should have the right to challenge a decision finding that interpretation or translation services are not necessary, in accordance with the procedures under national law. victims should also be informed of any right to appeal against a decision to release the offender, if such a right exists under national law.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the amendment to this regulation is welcome and at the same time necessary for the management of certain community tariff quotas for certain types of meat and cereal products. the existing legislation and the powers conferred on the commission to adapt the implementing measures and to amend the regulation should be aligned to the treaty of lisbon as soon as possible. those powers should take into account both the delegated and implementing acts. they also believe that parliament should be more involved in the preparation and implementation of delegated acts. at the same time, the removal of references to the committee procedure is particularly important in order to reflect changes in the application of the procedure.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the alignment of the council regulations on imports of olive oil and other agricultural products from turkey with the regime of delegated and implementing acts. i also support the rapporteur's amendments concerning the introduction of new recitals on implementing and delegated acts and greater involvement of parliament in the preparation of delegated acts. i also consider it appropriate to extend the period for objecting to a delegated act and to extend the monitoring period. furthermore, limiting the delegation of powers to the commission is a positive step. i believe that the amendments in question will make it possible to apply and monitor the legislation in the field of the common commercial policy correctly.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, as i believe that the amendment to the mutual recognition agreement with australia is intended to simplify and improve its functioning. this type of agreement aims to remove technical barriers to trade while also protecting health, safety and the environment. i therefore believe that mutual recognition agreements are extremely important and that their amendment should aim at clarifying and facilitating their functioning. they must allow greater flexibility and, at the same time, remove unnecessary restrictions from the path of international trade, facilitating its development under the best conditions. i welcome the fact that the agreement will apply to all the products concerned, irrespective of their nature or origin. i also support the institutional and procedural changes that have been put in place.
in writing. - i voted for the report on the amendment of the agreement on mutual recognition in relation to conformity assessment, certification and marking between the european community and australia. mutual recognition agreements aim to remove technical barriers to trade while protecting each party's health, safety and environmental objectives. the mutual recognition agreements with australia provide for general rules on the establishment of conformity assessment bodies as well as specific rules applying to the various regulated sectors. i welcome the simplification of the operation of the mutual recognition agreement, which establishes a simpler procedure for mutual recognition in conformity assessment. i welcome the abolition of the rules on industrial products. i also welcome the revision of the sectoral annexes on medicinal products and medical devices to take account of technical developments and administrative practices.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i support improving and simplifying the functioning of mutual recognition agreements. i believe that all unnecessary barriers to international trade must be removed as soon as possible. i also believe that health, the environment and safety are particularly important in this context and must be taken into account and protected as much as possible. the amendment of the agreements will ensure greater flexibility and reduce the administrative burden in managing them. at the same time, this adaptation aims to facilitate and clarify the way in which the agreement operates. i would also like to stress that during this process account must be taken of technical developments and of updates or changes in legislation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and new zealand amending the agreement between the european community and new zealand on the mutual recognition in relation to conformity assessment. the draft amendment to the mutual recognition agreement (mra) with new zealand was negotiated by the commission with the objective of improving and simplifying the functioning of the mra. mutual recognition agreements aim to remove technical barriers to trade while protecting each party's health, safety and environmental objectives. the mutual recognition agreement with new zealand lays down, in its main part, the general rules for the establishment of conformity assessment bodies. the purpose of the amendments is to allow greater flexibility in the structure and to remove unnecessary restrictions on trade between the parties, to reduce the administrative burden and to facilitate and clarify the functioning of the agreement. it is necessary to establish a simplified procedure for the recognition, withdrawal of recognition and suspension of conformity assessment bodies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report, but i think that parliament should have been more insistent in calling for firm action. the eu has a special responsibility not only to ensure sustainable fishing but also to protect european fishermen, who are subject to strict and costly rules. european fishermen are seriously disadvantaged by unfair competition from fishermen from states that systematically refuse to comply with any rules.
in writing. - i voted for the report on measures applicable to countries allowing unsustainable fishing, with a view to conserving fish stocks. this regulation establishes a framework for the adoption of certain measures concerning the fisheries-related activities and policies of third countries in order to ensure the long-term conservation of stocks of common interest to the union and those third countries. measures applicable to countries allowing unsustainable fishing should be proportionate to the objectives pursued and compatible with the obligations imposed by international agreements to which the union is a party and any other relevant rules of international law. considers it necessary to impose quantitative restrictions on imports of fish of any associated species and fishery products derived from or containing such fish when caught in fisheries targeting the stock of common interest under the control of countries allowing unsustainable fishing. in order to ensure that the measures are environmentally sound and sustainable, effective, proportionate and compatible with international standards, the commission needs to assess the commercial, environmental, economic and social effects of these measures in both the short and long term, as well as the administrative burden associated with their implementation.
in writing. − the common organisation of the market in fishery and aquaculture products also requires the establishment of a guide price before each fishing season, based on the average of prices on the wholesale markets and representative ports over the last three seasons and oriented according to production and demand trends, as well as the needs of stabilising the market, supporting producers' incomes and protecting consumers' interests. a second community price, the withdrawal price for products which cannot be sold above or at least at the same level, is set according to the quality of the fish, but it must be between 90% and 70% of the guide price. within this band, producer organisations may themselves set withdrawal prices below which they will not sell the products supplied by their members, in which case surplus quantities will be withdrawn from the market and producers will be paid compensation from the intervention fund set up by them from the producer's contributions, determined on the basis of the quantities withdrawn by each producer for sale.
in writing. − in the development of the future common organisation of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products, i believe that the main role should be played by producer organisations, as they are the main responsible for the proper application of the common fisheries policy and the common organisation of the markets. i therefore recommend that the commission take steps to ensure that these organisations have well-defined objectives and only carry out sustainable fisheries and aquaculture activities. in addition, we must ensure that producer organisations take account of the conditions imposed by the eu in the fisheries and aquaculture sector, with particular attention to small-scale fisheries. this will help to contribute constructively to the dynamic development of the eu aquaculture sector and to meet the growing demand for fish against the backdrop of declining global fish stocks.
in writing. − the common organisation of the markets is the first component of the common fisheries policy, but also one of the most important. i welcome the adoption of this report, which is the first element of the wider package of reform of european fisheries. across the union, citizens who live off fishing and fish processing expect this reform to bring about substantial changes that will improve the quality of their lives and the quality of the products that reach the tables of european consumers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation on the common organisation of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products. the regulation aims at ensuring that the common organisation of the markets contributes to the objectives set out in the regulation on the common fisheries policy and in particular to providing market incentives in support of more sustainable production practices, to improving the market position of union products, to developing production strategies to adapt to structural changes and short-term fluctuations in markets, and to strengthening the commercial potential of union products. the common organisation of the markets shall be guided by the principles of good governance, based on a clear definition of responsibilities at union, national, regional and local level, a long-term perspective, broad participation of operators, flag state responsibility and consistency with the integrated maritime policy, the commercial policy and other union policies.
in writing. − terrorism, organised crime, the proliferation of regional conflicts, security of energy supply or climate change pose security threats. these threats are increasingly felt around the world, including in europe. to cope with these risks, the european union must take an integrated approach, through the joint and joint efforts of all states. partnerships with key players on the international stage are also essential to combat these scourges. the european union must further support the efforts of partner countries in the process of implementing obligations in the field of human rights, strengthening democracy, the rule of law and judicial independence. it is necessary to ensure coherence and consistency between the components of foreign policy. therefore, particular attention should be paid to strengthening the relations between the high representative of the european union, the european external action service and the member states. as regards the future of the common foreign and security policy, the strengthening of financial instruments promoting peace, security, democracy and the rule of law is of particular importance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the annual report from the council to the european parliament on the common foreign and security policy. the eu should further develop its foreign policy objectives and promote its values and interests throughout the world, with the overall aim of contributing to peace, human security, solidarity, the rule of law, conflict prevention and the promotion of democracy, the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms, sustainable development, transparent and accountable governance, free and fair trade and poverty eradication. under the lisbon treaty, the eu has all the means to adopt a comprehensive approach, using all the union's diplomatic and financial resources in support of common strategic guidelines to promote the security and economic prosperity of european citizens and their neighbours, and fundamental rights, with all its strength. we call for the further development, with the participation of the relevant commission services, of an appropriate mechanism within the european external action service (eeas) integrating geographical and thematic expertise and leading to a comprehensive approach to the planning, formulation and implementation of the common foreign and security policy.
in writing. − according to the latest commission report, the current common fisheries policy has not achieved its objectives in terms of conservation and sustainable exploitation of eu fisheries resources. moreover, fishing capacity has not been adapted to the available fisheries resources, as shown by the alarming figures: over 60% of fish stocks in european waters are fished above the maximum sustainable yield. i therefore believe that the development of long-term management plans for commercial fishing activities by the commission is a necessity. the regionalisation of the common fisheries policy should also be a priority, as the specificities of the different european seas and the situation of small-scale fishing in the different regions of the union must be taken into account. the creation of closed areas where fishing activities are prohibited is also important to achieve effective results in conserving biological aquatic resources and the marine ecosystem. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − for the conservation and good management of fisheries resources, technical conservation measures have been adopted applicable, inter alia, to the size of nets, the authorised size of fish that can be caught and restrictions on catches in certain areas, periods or by certain types of vessels. i believe that the best exploitation of resources also requires permanent monitoring of fisheries by means of surveillance vessels. in this situation, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, the community relies on the coercive means of the member states. the authorities of the member states are thus obliged to inspect fishing vessels in accordance with a common procedure, and their crews are obliged to keep a logbook indicating the quantities of each species caught and retained, and to submit to the authorities of the landing point, after each voyage, a declaration of the quantities landed.
in writing. − although the commission has established multiannual recovery plans, they have so far covered only a limited number of fish stocks in eu waters and thus have not sufficiently reduced overfishing. in addition, given the diversity of european seas, i believe that long-term management plans should be drawn up taking into account the needs of all geographical fishing regions in the eu. the european commission must ensure that plans are drawn up in a highly decentralised manner, with full involvement of all stakeholders. by regionalising the common fisheries policy, we will be able to align management measures with the real situation faced by the different fleets and thus reduce overfishing.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the reporting obligations under regulation (ec) no 2371/2002 on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources under the common fisheries policy. over the past decade, the european fisheries sector has lost a significant number of jobs due to the poor state of fish stocks, rising production costs, falling prices due to cheaper imports and technological advances. we call on the commission to ensure that long-term management plans are drawn up for all commercial fisheries in the union, under a decentralised management regime involving all stakeholders. scientific research in the fisheries sector is an essential tool for fisheries management, indispensable for identifying the factors influencing the development of fisheries resources, for carrying out a quantitative assessment and for developing models that make it possible to estimate the evolution of these resources, as well as for improving fishing equipment, vessels and the working and safety conditions of fishermen, complementing their knowledge and experience. we invite the commission to measure, before the end of 2013, the capacity of the european fleets, in order to determine where there is excess capacity in relation to available resources and what reductions/conversions are necessary.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report, which touches on a number of important issues of fisheries in the european union. i also appreciate that the report refers to the need for a new regional fisheries management organisation in the black sea, given that the current competent body, the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean, is not an appropriate framework. it is also necessary to intensify dialogue with the black sea coastal states, in particular on the exploitation and conservation of fisheries resources.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp). the fisheries sector is of strategic importance for the supply of fish to the population and for the food balance of the various member states and the union, making a considerable contribution to the socio-economic well-being of coastal communities, to local development, to employment, to the maintenance and creation of upstream and downstream economic activities and to the preservation of local cultural traditions. the eu is the fourth largest producer in the world; however, it imports over 60% of the fish it consumes. i believe that the cfp must apply the precautionary approach to fisheries management and ensure the sustainable exploitation of living marine biological resources, in order to restore and maintain populations of all harvested species at levels close to those capable of ensuring maximum sustainable yield. we call on the commission to take action to adopt long-term management plans for all eu fisheries and to use the ecosystem approach as the basis for all such plans, with well-defined harvesting control objectives and rules, which will play a fundamental role in each plan.

in writing. the hungarian community in romania, which, with its size of 1.5 million citizens, is the largest minority community in the eu, is firmly attached to european principles and values in the organisation and functioning of the rule of law. the udmr, the legitimate representative of this community, has been going through a difficult period in recent months, like the other political forces in romania. the split in society, the suspension of the romanian president, the institutional and political crisis have put us in front of difficult decisions. in addition to the general crisis, my community has also faced a blow to one of our specific desires, which results from our history and traditions: the restitution to the community of the property wrongfully confiscated by the communist regime. almost 30 000 people protested on 1 september in st. george against the abusive decision to renationalize the building of the székely mikó high school, legally returned in 2002 to the reformed church in ardeal. this decision completely ignored the principles of the rule of law and called into question the guarantee of the property rights of hungarian historical communities and churches. the lasting solution to the institutional conflicts in romania, which reached a peak this summer, and the guarantee of property rights can only be achieved through a genuine reform of the judiciary and a long-delayed constitutional reform.
i would also like to recall that the european parliament has stressed, since the summer of 2010 and on several occasions, the imperative of creating an integrated banking supervision mechanism. the regulations in this area are insufficient, and citizens have paid the excessive costs of rescuing institutions from bankruptcy, turning private debts into public debts. two years later, the council finally calls for a banking union. i believe that the european union is today paying the price of late decisions and insufficiently transparent procedures. in a union where anti-european sentiment is growing and where citizens want concrete solutions, i hope that we will finally learn our lesson and live up to the expectations of those we represent.
we are currently facing the need for better monitoring of european banks in the euro area, and the single supervisory mechanism could help to achieve this. however, the granting of greater power to the european central bank may create imbalances between banks in the euro area and those outside. at the same time, there are still some concerns about competition between large and local banks. i therefore believe that an appropriate balance needs to be found in order to reduce the vulnerability faced by this sector. in this context, commissioner, i believe that there is a need for clarification of the commission's intentions with regard to future legislative proposals. it is also important to know whether the treaties are to be amended to achieve the objectives in this area.
the commission, together with the member states, must ensure that the union has access to diverse energy sources so that european citizens can enjoy uninterrupted access to affordable energy. the proper functioning of the internal energy market contributes to the security of energy supply of the european union, which is essential for the economic and social development of the european union and for its competitiveness. in view of the need to optimise the functioning of the internal energy market, this decision establishes a mechanism for the exchange of information between member states and the commission on intergovernmental agreements in the field of energy. i believe that the commission should provide member states with a guide to the approach to the negotiations in order to ensure compliance with union law, solidarity between member states and the guarantee of energy supply. it is also important that, at the request of a member state, the commission provides support and technical assistance in the process of negotiating and concluding intergovernmental agreements with third countries in the field of energy.
europe is currently dependent on energy imports, for which it pays some eur 400 billion a year. to reduce vulnerabilities and increase energy security, greater diversity of sources and supply networks is needed. at the same time, improvements in energy security help to strengthen the union's role in foreign policy. as for romania, my country has an advantage both from its geographical and geopolitical position, because the black sea has a major potential in achieving european energy security, representing a gateway to the union's regional economic and political bloc. my country supports major projects, like the nabucco pipeline. at the same time, it attaches particular importance to the interconnection of the national electricity system with similar systems in neighbouring states.
the european union has competitive advantages over other global competitors in several areas. producing and marketing high-quality agricultural products is one of them. with the present proposal, i believe that european farmers will have additional means to communicate essential details of the products they buy to consumers. the proposal will also improve the functioning of national and private certification systems. for romanian farmers and producers, this will have a significant impact. the establishment of a system of traditional specialities guaranteed will stimulate traditional production methods and recipes. currently, many romanian producers do not have the opportunity to promote their recipes and products that offer added value. last but not least, i believe that simplifying marketing standards and mentioning the place of agricultural origin on labels will have a positive impact on european consumers.
i would like to welcome in particular two proposals, amendments nos 73 and 75, which i consider particularly important. the first amendment concerns the introduction of a new term, 'mountain product', for products whose raw materials come from mountain areas. the second amendment concerns the possibility of introducing a new labelling system for local farms and direct selling activities to help producers in the process of marketing products locally. the introduction of this label depends on a future study by the commission, which i hope we will have soon. i believe that the two new entries could bring important benefits to producers, who will find it easier to find their niche in the market in the face of competition from large producers. they will also benefit consumers who want to buy food produced in their region through the efforts of farmers in the vicinity of their cities. alongside the future support measures provided for by the reform of the european agricultural policy, the encouragement of the two labels would be an important support for small and medium-sized producers.
i welcome the commission's proposal to provide increased support for promoting access to finance. to this end, venture capital funds play a particularly important role in the economy, fostering growth and job creation. moreover, the funds stimulate the creation and expansion of innovative enterprises, thus supporting innovation and competitiveness. they address the challenges facing most member states today. in this context, i would like to stress the importance of creating a common regulatory framework as soon as possible. this will reduce obstacles to the functioning of the single market and eliminate distortions of competition. european venture capital funds make a considerable contribution to promoting access to finance for smes.
unfortunately, we are living in a time when the primary objective of companies that are going into business is to make immediate and substantial profits. the regulation of european social entrepreneurship funds is a tremendous opportunity for those entrepreneurs whose main objective is to generate social outcomes, which unfortunately have become less and less targeted in recent times. i am concerned, however, that there is a risk that the levers highlighted in the report, not sufficiently explained in detail, may be used for purposes not indicated. i therefore believe that we must now concentrate our efforts on achieving as complete a regulation as possible, providing specific protection and control rules, in order to eliminate completely the possibility of misuse of these funds with enormous potential for social progress.
despite the extraordinary wealth of europe's cultural heritage, some of the works are not used, being kept in archives and libraries due to their status as orphan works. through copyright, innovation, investment and production are stimulated, which is the foundation of the creative sector. thanks to the new legislation, digitisation could in future allow online access to these works throughout europe and even beyond. we are talking about books, newspapers, publications, films, musicals and tv productions whose authors cannot be identified and which will be legally accessible under the framework created by the current proposal for a directive. personally, i support allowing cultural and educational institutions to use orphan works for their own purposes. in the future, it is important to reduce the number of orphan works by establishing clear criteria for identifying and locating the authors of these works, so that they can enjoy the rights to which they are entitled.
copyright is the economic foundation of the creative industries, as it stimulates innovation, creative activity, investment and production. the digitisation and dissemination of works therefore constitute a method of protecting europe's cultural heritage. copyright is an important means of ensuring that activities in the creative sector are rewarded. copyright holders should be entitled to cancel the orphan work status of a work when they claim rights in the work or other subject matter. copyright holders who revoke the orphan work status of a work should be granted appropriate compensation for the use of their works or other subject matter protected under this directive, to be determined by the member state in which the body using the orphan work is established. member states should be free to determine the circumstances in which such compensation is granted, including the time at which the payment is made.
in writing. the problem with orphan works is that any lawful use of the work requires the consent of the copyright holder. if the author cannot be found and consent cannot be obtained, then the work cannot be used. as protection is extremely long (author's life + 70 years) and the number of published works is increasing, these cases are becoming more common. aside from the fact that, in general, works are actually used more often without having asked for permission, i believe that, from a legal point of view, there is a problem that needs to be solved.
member of the commission. − madam president, thank you for the opportunity to comment on parliament’s draft report on the 18th report on better legislation. first, allow me to thank the committee on legal affairs for its work in preparing this report. it is a welcome contribution to the smart regulation agenda, which the report acknowledges as a shared responsibility. it also highlights some very important issues concerning relations with national parliaments. the commission will respond more formally to the report in due course but, for now, i would like to make a few general remarks on the smart regulation agenda, which remains a key priority for the commission. first, your report correctly indicates that impact assessment is a core element of smart regulation. the european court of auditors and other independent studies found that the commission’s impact assessment system compares favourably to other systems in the european union. the commission strives to continuously improve its impact assessment system, for instance by providing services with further operational guidance on the assessment of specific impacts such as sector competitiveness, fundamental rights or smes. the president has reinforced the role of the impact assessment board so that, in principle, a positive opinion from the iab is needed before a proposal can be put forward for a commission decision. the commission welcomes parliament’s initiative in setting up an impact assessment directorate and, in particular, the renewed commitment of parliament to carry out impact assessments prior to the adoption of substantive amendments. the commission is willing to exchange views, share methodology and background to its assessments with the parliament, as already agreed in the common approach to impact assessments. we should all bear in mind, of course, that an impact assessment is not an end in itself. it should lead to better policy at the end of the decision-making process and is a joint responsibility. your report rightly places considerable emphasis on the need to minimise regulatory burdens for business. the commission has proposed measures to reduce the administrative burden by 33%. we invite parliament and the council to approve pending proposals rapidly to bridge the small remaining gap and so ensure that we reach the 25% reduction target by the end of the year. we consider that all future legislative proposals should be based on the premise that micro-enterprises, in particular, should be excluded from the scope of the proposed legislation, unless the proportionality of their being covered can be demonstrated. when they need to be covered, we should seek to find adapted solutions and lighter regimes for both micros and smes, and their impact should be analysed as an integral part of the impact assessment process. we are also strengthening the implementation of the commission ex-post evaluation policy. now all significant proposals must, in principle, be based on an evaluation of what is already in place. we are working on further developments to improve the way we do this. we are also focused on further improving implementation and consultation. the commission will produce a scoreboard to show that proposals it has produced are having a significant impact on smaller business, to show what changes parliament and council adopt in the legislative procedure and how member states implement the adopted regulatory measure, identifying best practice and any ‘gold plating’. the scoreboard will be updated on a yearly basis. a central element of the commission’s approach is a strengthening of the involvement and consultation of small businesses in better law-making. conferences are already being held in member states with small businesses and an eu-wide consultation process has been launched to identify the ‘top ten’ burdensome eu regulatory measures for review. we have also strengthened the voice of stakeholders, by extending the minimum period for public consultation from 8 weeks to 12 weeks, as of the beginning of this year. the commission has also initiated a review of its consultation policy. furthermore, a follow up to the 2010 smart regulation communication, taking stock of the progress made and drawing lessons from experience, is planned for adoption around the end of this year. a 12-week public consultation was launched on 27 june. your report emphasises the importance of respect for the principle of subsidiarity when drawing up legislative proposals and stresses the importance of the participation of regional parliaments with legislative powers in this process. subsidiarity issues are key aspects taken into account by the commission when carrying out its impact assessments and on which the impact assessment board focuses when scrutinising the quality of impact assessments. the commission is fully committed to ensuring that in future subsidiarity justifications are better reflected in the explanatory memorandum of its proposals. concerning relations with national parliaments, let me reassure you that the commission pays very close attention to the work of regional parliaments and even receives opinions directly from some of them. after all, we regularly encourage national parliaments to consult regional parliaments with legislative powers, where appropriate, in the process of subsidiarity scrutiny, as set out in the treaty. the commission is committed to making progress on smart regulation and looks forward to working with parliament, the council and the member states to ensure effective delivery as a joint responsibility.
on behalf of the epp group. the concepts of subsidiarity and proportionality are fundamental elements of the policy-making process within the eu institutions. the subsidiarity control mechanism available to national parliaments helps to increase the transparency of the process. most of the commission's proposals were adopted by national parliaments without any significant discussion on subsidiarity. the only real debates on how to interpret subsidiarity have been between the european parliament and the council, thus leading to a proper balance between the responsibilities of the eu and those of the member states. in practice, it can be seen that the implementation of community legislation remains a problem at national level and i believe that better communication between national parliaments and the european parliament could lead to improvements. the report also addresses a number of issues of particular importance to the european parliament, including the need to revise the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making, the adoption of legislation on smes and, not least, further improvements to better law-making. as the shadow rapporteur of the epp, i would point out that there was no disagreement between the main political groups in the committee on legal affairs, and a compromise was reached which will help to clarify the reversal of the burden of proof for certain categories of undertakings, for which i thank the main report.
i would like to begin by stressing the need for european legislation to be clear, simple, easy to understand and accessible to all. i therefore welcome the stronger involvement of national parliaments in the european legislative process, in particular with regard to legislative proposals on control based on the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. however, i regret that only 16% of the opinions received from national parliaments in 2010 raised subsidiarity concerns. welcomes the first use of the 'yellow card' procedure in may 2012 by adopting reasoned opinions against the commission's proposal for a council regulation on the exercise of the right to engage in collective activities in the framework of the freedom of establishment and the freedom to provide services. i welcome the introduction of the ipex website, which can act as a catalyst for further improvements and greater involvement in the functioning of the subsidiarity control mechanism. i believe, however, that national parliaments should organise public debates on european legislative proposals. only in this way will member states, citizens, the administration and, above all, industry be able to prepare for the proper implementation of european legislation.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that social objectives are playing an increasingly important role for investors, alongside financial ones. in this context, the creation of a european social investment sector and the establishment of a legal framework are necessary steps. i believe that the adoption of the regulation will increase investor confidence in those funds. at the same time, it is welcome because it will reduce costs and simplify administrative formalities. confidence will also be enhanced by the existence of uniform criteria and rules applicable to european social entrepreneurship funds. i would point out that there is a need for effective enforcement. this will ensure that the regulation is coherent and can be applied properly. in this connection, i would stress the importance of cooperation between the competent authorities of the member states.
in writing. − social enterprises are companies that have a positive social impact and are more focused on social objectives than profit maximisation. the sector already represents 10% of all european companies and employs over 11 million people in europe. although these companies often receive public support, private investment through funds that invest in social entrepreneurship remains vital to their development. however, these specialised social investment funds are rare or not large enough. i would like to draw attention to the fact that the rules applicable to social investment funds differ from one member state to another and are often burdensome and complex. for this reason, i believe that the new proposals will simplify the rules.
in writing. − investments in the european social entrepreneurship fund will be beneficial for the european union in the current period, especially if the application of methods that are as transparent as possible regarding the policy and objectives of these investments is encouraged. it is essential that their primary objective is not profit but social outcomes, i.e. the provision of services to vulnerable or marginalised people. this will contribute to the fight against poverty in the member states, which is one of the union's objectives.
in writing. − i expressed my support for this initiative and for the text that was agreed between the european parliament and the council. my position is underlined by my belief that we in europe should foster the development of undertakings that are committed to tackling important issues such as, for instance, ensuring inclusion, fighting marginalisation and poverty. the regulation on the european social entrepreneurship funds would make an important contribution to promoting those undertakings that pursue a social impact in their activity rather than just monetary benefits. securing better funding opportunities for them is key to supporting the role they fulfil in our societies. the matter is even of a bigger importance, given the economic and societal problems we are facing nowadays in the eu. however, i give my full support to the rapporteur, ms sophie auconie, who called for the final vote on the legislative resolution to be postponed due to the council’s decision to renegotiate the previously agreed text. i consider that this regulation should not simply be a legislative exercise. the justification for it lies in its potential socio-economic impact, and the european parliament must stay committed to its position in the renegotiation process.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the amendments to the proposal for a regulation on european social entrepreneurship funds (esfs), which is part of the social entrepreneurship initiative presented by the commission in its communication of 25 october 2011. increasingly, investors are interested in pursuing social objectives and a social investment market has therefore emerged in the union, partly composed of investment funds targeting social enterprises. these funds finance social enterprises, which are drivers of social change, provide innovative solutions to social problems and make an important contribution to achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. it is necessary to adopt a regulation laying down uniform rules applicable to the efsi seeking to raise capital in the union and imposing corresponding obligations on its managers in all member states. those requirements should ensure the confidence of investors wishing to invest in those funds. in order to provide capital to social enterprises, the efsi should invest at least 70% of the total capital injections and unpaid committed capital in such enterprises.
in writing. − i support the adoption of the regulation on european venture capital funds, because through them a european venture capital investment sector for small and medium-sized enterprises is being created. by providing financing and advice to smes in the early stages of their formation but with high growth and expansion potential, venture capital funds stimulate economic growth, contribute to job creation and capital mobilisation, while increasing their investment in research and supporting entrepreneurship, innovation and competitiveness. this regulatory framework is intended to encourage venture capital funds to carry out cross-border activities, which will contribute to the development of the internal market.
in writing. − access to finance is essential to increase the competitiveness and growth potential of smes. in the context of the current crisis, marked by a decline in lending to the real economy, it is increasingly difficult for such companies to access loans. risk capital provides early financing for start-ups and is an important source of long-term investment for new and innovative smes. however, the small size of the funds and the fact that they can only provide low levels of capital have prevented them from playing a more important role in financing new businesses. as a result, smes continue to rely on short-term bank loans. i think that an increase in venture capital funds means more capital for individual companies and will give the funds the ability to specialize in certain sectors, such as information technology, biotechnology or health.
in writing. − small and medium-sized enterprises are the backbone of the economies of the eu member states, which is why i believe it is important to involve european venture capital funds in their financing. this will stimulate economic growth, help create new jobs and capital, and allow the emergence of new smes and the expansion of innovative enterprises.
in writing. − the role of the european venture capital sector is to support sme financing and to encourage innovation and technological progress, but in the european union this sector is fragmented and we need to address these shortcomings by harmonising legislation across all member states. i believe that greater attention should be paid to the regulation of venture capital investments in green technologies. they are an important factor in the recovery of the economy, also taking into account the european union's major objective of being the world leader in the efficient use of energy resources. the adoption of legislative rules that provide incentives for investors will therefore undoubtedly attract venture capital in the field of green technologies.
in writing. - i voted for the amendments proposed by the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation on european venture capital funds. i consider it important that the objective of this regulation is to support growth and innovation in small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in the union. at present, venture capital plays a minor role in sme financing. smes rely mainly on bank loans, which account for over 80% of their financing, while only 2% of financing comes from venture capitalists. the corresponding figure in the united states is 14%. i voted to make it possible for managers of a qualifying venture capital fund to attract additional capital commitments over the life of the fund. additional capital commitments should be allowed on the basis of criteria and conditions set out in the fund rules or in its instruments of incorporation. they argue that the core business of venture capital funds is to provide finance to smes through primary investments. venture capital funds must not engage in systemically important banking activities outside the normal prudential regulatory framework (the so-called shadow banking system).
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that through the two agreements the union will be able to open up its market even more and at the same time increase its exports to the two countries. in this context, i would like to stress the importance of the safeguard clause in the liberalisation of trade in agricultural products. it is a safety net in the event that markets are faced with certain disruptions as a result of the signing of bilateral agreements. i also draw attention to the monitoring and reporting arrangements. they are essential for the correct application of this regulation. moreover, they have an even greater impact on sensitive products, such as bananas. another important aspect concerns social and environmental standards, which must be fully respected in the implementation of the agreement.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft legislative resolution because i believe that a safeguard clause should be introduced to protect the european banana sector, which is a source of employment, from imports from third countries. on the other hand, banana production imported into the union from colombia or peru must benefit from adequate and decent wage, social and environmental conditions in order to avoid dumping to the detriment of european producers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the amendments to the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council implementing the bilateral safeguard clause and the stabilisation mechanism for bananas in the trade agreement between the european union and the republic of colombia and the republic of peru. the introduction of appropriate safeguard instruments is necessary to avoid serious damage to european banana crops, a sector with a very important share in the final agricultural production of several outermost regions. the banana sector is a sensitive production sector, given the limited capacity of these regions to diversify their economies due to their natural characteristics. the creation of efficient mechanisms for the management of preferential imports from third countries is therefore essential to ensure that european banana production is maintained under optimal conditions, as this is a sector that is essential for employment, especially in the outermost regions. we voted to respect international labour standards, developed and monitored by the international labour organization. ensuring decent working conditions for all must be a top priority for this sector, bananas imported from colombia or peru must be produced under fair wage, social and environmental conditions so that union producers do not become victims of dumping.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the amendments tabled to the proposal for a regulation on the application of the bilateral safeguard clause and the stabilisation mechanism for bananas provided for in the eu-central america association agreement. the agreements contain a safeguard clause to avoid serious disruption of the parties' markets and the device needs to be transposed into european law. the agreements provide for further reductions in eu customs duties on banana imports, improving the conditions under which signatory latin american countries export to the community market. imports of bananas into the eu are subject to a 'single customs duty' system, which came into force in 2006, ending the quota system applied since the establishment of the common market organisation (cmo) for bananas in 1993. the commission should present an annual report on the implementation of the agreement, safeguard measures and stabilisation mechanism for bananas, including up-to-date and reliable statistics on imports from central america and an assessment of their impact on market prices, employment, working conditions in the union and the evolution of the union production sector, with particular attention to small producers and cooperatives.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the lack of a framework for online and cross-border access to orphan works in libraries and archives has not yet been remedied. the creation of a legal framework for the circulation of these works is one of the key points in the finalisation of the digital single market. we need to have clear indicators that define these works, taking into account the need to respect copyright. it is particularly important to prevent the emergence of new orphan works in the future. clear ways of identifying and locating copyright holders should therefore be established. i also consider situations where an opera has been wrongly classified as an orphan opera. respect for copyright is essential to stimulate innovation and creativity at eu level.
in writing. − i support the directive of the european parliament and of the council on the crossborder use of books, newspapers, publications, films, music, television productions, etc., whose copyright holder cannot be identified. a digital database accessible to all union citizens is created for the use of the vast cultural heritage in member states' archives and libraries, which is not yet used. by publishing them via the internet or other distribution channels, europe's cultural diversity will be strongly promoted and made available to all.
in writing. − in a fast-moving information society, the preservation and dissemination of europe's cultural heritage is essential. as such, the digitisation of collections and archives belonging to museums, libraries, various archiving systems in public institutions, education, cinemas and cinemas, and public broadcasting organisations in all member states will allow for the extension of access to works held by these structures to the general public. however, it should not be forgotten that respect for copyright is essential, as this will stimulate innovation, creativity, investment and production and thus ensure that creative activity is rewarded.
in writing. − the digital age has also considerably affected the sphere of copyrighted works, with a widespread trend towards the creation and public availability of digital libraries and archives. for works where the authors are known to each other, there is harmonised and comprehensive legislation governing copyright remuneration, which is a key factor in stimulating innovation and is the foundation of the creative industries. on the other hand, i consider that works by unknown or no longer identifiable authors, generically called orphan works, must be equally accessible to the public without prejudice to the institutions that hold them. i therefore support this measure as a positive one, as making works available online for cultural and educational purposes is a way of protecting europe's cultural heritage.
in writing. − the adoption of this directive creates the framework for research into and use of orphan works by public institutions, for example libraries or museums, and for accelerating the digitisation of europe's cultural heritage so that it is available to all citizens. the adoption of this directive will allow wider access to culture, in support of all those who wish to enrich their knowledge.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a directive on certain permitted uses of orphan works. the purpose of the directive is to address the specific problem of the legal determination of the status of orphan works and its consequences for the authorised users and uses of works or phonograms considered as orphan works. the directive also covers certain uses of orphan works by publicly accessible libraries, educational establishments and museums, as well as by archives, film or sound heritage institutions and public broadcasting organisations established in the member states, in order to achieve objectives related to their public interest missions. different approaches in the member states to the recognition of orphan works may constitute obstacles to the functioning of the internal market and to the use of and cross-border access to orphan works. these different approaches may also lead to restrictions on the free movement of cultural goods and services. it is therefore appropriate to ensure the mutual recognition of that status, as this will allow access to orphan works in all member states.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution to express my concern at the serious deterioration of the situation in syria. i support the european union's efforts to increase pressure on the syrian regime. the main objective must remain the cessation of repression against the civilian population. un sanctions are the best solution to support a peaceful resolution of this crisis. intensive political dialogue between the opposition forces and syrian society must be promoted. this dialogue will be able to respond to the expectations of the citizens regarding the achievement of a peaceful and democratic transition in syria. my concern about the violence in syria is all the greater, as romania has the second community of foreign nationals residing on syrian territory. i am also concerned about the possible spillover effect of the syrian crisis to the region.
in writing. - the banking union is the most ambitious response to date to the debt crisis and to risks in the banking system. there are, however, a number of risks to be aware of. there are serious warnings about the risk that the banking union will disadvantage locally-owned banks in eastern europe, in the face of unfair competition from the big banks in the euro area. it also appears that the decision-making forum will be composed of representatives of the euro area countries only. for example, in the event of major risk, a decision to withdraw capital from the subsidiaries in eastern europe to stabilise the euro area parent banks is being considered. i am in favour of the project, provided that the position of non-euro area countries is fairly regulated, provided that decisions at the level of the banking union will affect all 27 member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the creation of a banking union, convinced that a single regulatory mechanism is necessary to stabilise financial markets and to move towards a genuine economic and monetary union. i also believe that the decisions of the european union need more democratic legitimacy. the involvement of the european parliament, as the representative of european citizens, in the process of establishing the banking union is therefore a necessity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on proposals for a european banking union (ebu), having regard to the ep resolution of july 2010 on the management of cross-border crises in the banking sector and the ep report on the proposal for a regulation establishing the european banking authority. the parliament thus identified solutions to the problems of managing cross-border financial crises, an integrated supervisory mechanism, reform of the deposit guarantee mechanism and the creation of a european stability fund. parliament's full participation is essential for the democratic legitimacy of the process leading to the establishment of a banking union. i believe that any major change to the oversight system, including transfers to other institutions, must be accompanied by an equivalent increase in the transparency and accountability of these institutions to parliament, which must have full powers of inquiry and full powers of appointment and budgetary procedures. i support the need to pay due attention to the potential spillover effects of the euro area banking union on non-euro area member states.
like other colleagues, i am obviously concerned about the situation in south africa and condemn the violent repression by the police of the miners' protests. it goes without saying that we respect the trade union rights of south african miners. on the other hand, i cannot help but wonder if they are not in danger of falling into a trap set by an unscrupulous leader. julius malema has, i believe, outgrown his role as a negotiator and is now taking advantage of social discontent to test his political power. his call for an illegal general strike in all the mines of south africa is, in my opinion, an incitement to violence. malema's speech to former south african soldiers yesterday has led to a state of high alert in the military and these actions certainly concern us. but i hope that in the end, the common good will prevail and not partisan interest.
the marikana platinum mine massacre is the bloodiest incident of its kind since the end of apartheid in south africa. a critical analysis of the evolution of social relations in this country after liberation from the racist nightmare is required. first of all, i think that the investigation into the deaths of the 34 miners should be directed primarily at the police forces who opened fire with violence. it is outrageous that 270 workers are to be tried on murder charges for the deaths of their own colleagues. we demand an objective investigation, otherwise there is a risk that the anger will flare up again. it's time to remind the african national congress that it promised a better life for all its citizens in the post-apartheid era.
member of the commission. − mr president, high representative/vice- president ashton visited south africa only a few days after the tragedy at the marikana mine. the tragedy has not only touched south africa, but people across the world have followed the dramatic events. we express our condolences for the lives lost. ms ashton discussed the situation in depth with those south african officials that she met, including the foreign minister and dr nkosazana dlamini-zuma, south african minister of home affairs and newly-elected chair of the african union commission. we welcome the appointment by president zuma of a full judicial commission of inquiry into the incident and of an interministerial committee to deal with the aftermath of the marikana killings. ms ashton also told our south african partners that the eu would be following with keen interest and attention its proceedings and findings. the commission established by president zuma will be chaired by a retired judge of the supreme court of appeal, a positive sign of its independence. the ten-member inter-ministerial committee appointed by president zuma is providing assistance and support to the families of the deceased and is trying to find solutions to the instability of the mining industry. it would be wrong to speculate and to try to anticipate the findings of the judicial commission, but clearly it is important, in our view, to examine the root causes as well as the precise circumstances of these events.
in writing. – the clashes between the police and striking miners in south africa resulted in a toll of 34 people killed, plus 10 more killed in the days preceding the event. this massacre shows that south africa has many challenges ahead. as regards this situation, i support the initiative of establishment of a judicial commission of inquiry to investigate the facts leading to these extreme acts of violence and i express my confidence that all those responsible will be held accountable for their actions. lives that were lost represent an irreparable damage. there are important steps that can be made in order to avoid the recurrence of such a situation ever again. the south african authorities should make robust and consistent effort to strengthen the rule of law and human rights, to ensure equality and to eradicate corruption, which i believe can contribute in important ways to the socio-economic development of the country. the police regulations and country’s labour dispute mechanism also should be reviewed. hence i gave my support to this resolution.
