this week we witnessed a new incident, a new victim of inter-ethnic war in the world, the american ambassador killed in benghazi, a case that was evoked at the beginning of the session of our parliament, which has always supported the fight for fundamental freedoms. sadly, though, bloody anarchy tends to do as much harm as repressive dictatorship. that's why i want to draw attention to the cause of the inter-ethnic clashes and the excessive intervention of the burmese law enforcement. three men from the rohingya minority raped and killed a buddhist woman. then more than 80 people died in fighting in rakhine state between buddhists and muslims. we call on the burmese authorities to recognise the rohingya minority and to make efforts to integrate them and address the humanitarian crisis. the equation of democratization and reform in burma is closely tied to the cessation of inter-ethnic hostilities in that country.
the author. - recently, a french minister made defamatory statements about the romani community in romania. i am outraged, but my outrage cannot be the subject of an emergency resolution. because any parliament that respects itself, respects the rules laid down in the regulation. under rule 122 of the rules of procedure, this situation cannot be the subject of an emergency resolution. it's not a matter of rule of law, it's not a matter of democracy, it's not a matter of human rights. applying this issue to the relations between two countries while everyone recognizes that it was an agreement that worked perfectly legally and both sides, both hungary and azerbaijan respected their rights can be the subject of indignation but not of a political resolution, in a circumstance where the security situation in the area can be quite damaged by promoting such actions. and i would like to ask rhetorically, how do you explain that in the yerevan press it is already known that this resolution has been adopted. i would like to see us stop trying to play games in this matter in favour of one side or the other, and destabilise a situation in which the european union should play a decisive role. that's why the liberal group withdrew its signatures from this resolution, that's why the liberal group will not vote for it.
i would first like to congratulate my fellow rapporteurs on the realism with which they have dealt with this important subject. i also raise the question of the danger of the cessation of payments in the rural development sector and other sectors already mentioned by other colleagues. i would also like to stress one point in the opinion of the committee on agriculture concerning payments for rural development measures. in its opinion, the committee on agriculture asked the commission to give the member states the necessary flexibility to transfer unspent funds between the axes. this flexibility is necessary and can contribute to economic growth. i therefore reiterate this request and draw attention to the fact that the time left to make the necessary adjustments is very short.
the union's policies and budget should make a substantial contribution to revitalising sustainable growth in the union and addressing major societal challenges such as resource scarcity, climate change, the relocation of european industry, underinvestment in education, health, research and the lack of job opportunities. the financial year 2013 is very important as it is intended to prepare the launch of the connecting europe facility and i therefore support maintaining the level of commitment and payment appropriations proposed in the draft budget. i consider that the needs for the development of transport infrastructure in the new member states should be duly reflected both in the financial year 2013 and in the future multiannual financial framework. finally, the inability of romania's previous governments must not lead to the reduction of the structural funds that romania needs to use in the current financial period and which it very much needs.
the 2013 'european year of citizens' should aim to raise citizens' awareness of their rights as union citizens when exercising their right to move and reside freely within another member state, for example as students, workers, jobseekers, volunteers, consumers, young entrepreneurs or pensioners. i insist on the removal of the obstacles which continue to prevent the exercise of the rights deriving from european citizenship. in this context, i stress the importance of removing the barriers to the free movement of romanian and bulgarian workers. we cannot really talk about european citizenship as long as there are barriers and differences between citizens of the member states. i therefore call for the lifting by the first quarter of 2013 at the latest of all barriers imposed by some member states on romanian and bulgarian workers. facilitating the free movement of persons and increasing the mobility of workers are important means of addressing the consequences of demographic changes in the labour market.
in writing. european development policy is, alongside trade policy and political relations, one of the cornerstones of the european union's external action. its main objective is to reduce poverty. support to developing countries to improve access to education is key to achieving this goal, given that over 100 million children worldwide are not included in the education system. without education, these children have little chance of gaining a job that will later enable them to enter the labour market, and poverty reduction efforts in these countries are hampered. as such, i consider eu support essential for the participation of as many children as possible, especially those from rural areas, in quality educational programmes - primary education and vocational training. the eu should also support the development of sectoral plans that also take into account the cultural specificities of each region or country, with a focus on involving civil society in those countries as much as possible in their implementation.
recently, a group of six member states asked the european commission to reinstate visa requirements for balkan states, citing false asylum claims. i think it is an unfounded and wrong request in two ways: firstly, abuse of the european asylum system is only possible because of its internal weakness. instead of restricting freedom of movement, we should speed up the adoption and implementation of the new asylum package. secondly, this solution would be identical to the one canada took three years ago when it reimposed visas for czech citizens. at that time, all the eu countries criticized the canadian government, and now they are only following suit. this duplicitous behaviour by the eu is shameful and contrary to european values. citizens from the balkans must be able to move freely within the eu, just as citizens from the czech republic, romania and bulgaria must be able to travel freely to canada or the united states. the commission must not grant this request.
i would like to welcome the agreement on banking supervision reached at the recent european summit. stricter supervision of banking activities is indispensable to avoid a repetition of banking crises, but also to ensure an adequate level of protection for depositors. however, the way in which member states will be able to participate in the single supervisory mechanism needs to be clarified, in particular as regards the status of non-euro countries. we must not ignore the gap between the cross-border dimension of banks' activities and their supervision at national level. in romania, banking capital from the euro area accounts for about 80%. last but not least, we must ask how we can ensure the integrity of the single market if we divide the banking union between participating and non-participating countries. that is why i am advocating equal rights for all member states under the new supervisory structure, including voting rights.
the union and the member states must develop, finance and implement an industrialisation strategy. over the last 30 years, the union has suffered a process of dismantling european industry. in the pursuit of greater profits, large european companies shifted production to third countries, where labor and raw materials were cheaper. today, most of the consumer products used by european citizens are imported from developing third countries. the difference between the selling price on the internal market and the low cost of production in these countries ensures huge profits for a small number of entrepreneurs, at the expense of the loss of millions of jobs in the union. the industrialisation of the union ensures job creation in europe, a decent living for european citizens, investment in schools, hospitals and basic infrastructure, thanks to the revenue from the member states' budgets. investing in the industrialisation of the union, not in austerity, will help the union to overcome the current economic, financial and social crisis.
tuberculosis, especially chemoresistant tuberculosis, and the spread of hiv as a result of injecting drug use, continue to be serious health problems, accentuated by the financial crisis facing our society, among the countries with a significant number of tuberculosis cases being romania. financial assistance to romania from the global fund to fight hiv, tuberculosis and malaria ended in september this year, leaving behind a significant number of patients who will no longer be able to continue their treatment, access adequate medication or receive any support for these conditions in the future. in the context of the increasing number of cases of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis and hiv in the countries of eastern europe and central asia due to a lack of funding, i believe that at eu level we must support the revision of eligibility criteria for funding from the global fund, emphasise the importance of policies to reduce the harm caused by drug use in third countries, and improve social integration activities for vulnerable groups of affected populations.
mr president, i would also like to start by congratulating our colleague, mr paul rübig, for this report. as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on international trade i worked on it myself, and i would like to thank him for his cooperation. it has already been stressed by mr rübig that this report also has within its scope the aim of enhancing trade and business conditions for smes which are already engaged internationally, and of tackling some of the barriers that are deterring many smes from actually getting involved in international trade. rationalising the support for smes supplied by public institutions and the business community is very important, as is giving individual support to those companies whose profile matches business opportunities in third markets. smes from the new member states are at a disadvantage and should benefit from specific information delivered to them in a more accessible way. in conclusion, the internationalisation of smes is also very important for european smes.
micro-enterprises and smes are suffering in this period of economic crisis because of the difficult access to finance necessary for their development. 85% of new jobs in the european union between 2002 and 2010 were created by smes. industry plays a key role in the european economy and generates 25% of direct private sector jobs in the european union and accounts for 80% of private research and development. we support the enhancement and efficiency of assistance to smes at union, national and regional level for their access to the single market and to third country markets, in particular on issues related to promotion and access to information, protection of intellectual property rights, participation in public tenders, information and communication technology, standardisation and regulation. i welcome the new cosme programme on the competitiveness of smes and call for the simplification and rationalisation of the various union instruments dedicated to access to credit.
in writing. in romania, between 2008 and 2010, the number of employees in the sme sector remained at the same level as before the crisis, while in large companies the number of employees decreased by 6%. the jobs generated by smes are therefore much more stable than those in large enterprises. support for smes is therefore part of the solution needed to achieve 'healthy growth'. the opening up of external markets to smes, and in particular the expansion of opportunities to participate in intra-community trade, would bring important benefits to all employees of these enterprises. a special case is small rural enterprises. in the context of the need to diversify rural economies, the new common agricultural policy must provide adequate funds for the establishment and development of these enterprises. rural smes can absorb a significant part of the surplus labour force in agriculture and at the same time provide rural people with the services they need. last but not least, hundreds of successful businesses have been born in rural areas, exploiting the opportunities offered by rural development programmes. this is another argument in favour of an appropriate budget for agriculture in the future multiannual financial framework.
in the transport trade and economic relations between the european union and the united states of america, there is a need to reform the restrictions on foreign participation in airlines in the united states of america. the lack of reciprocity between european and american maritime and air transport rules, and the current imbalance between the ability of european companies to cabotage in the united states market and the ability of american companies to cabotage in the european union, is an obstacle that needs to be overcome in order to unlock the full potential of the transatlantic economic relationship. i also consider the agreement on interoperability between egnos, galileo and gps to be particularly important, as it will allow the development of european and american industries and applications using satellite positioning systems. finally, in the context of trade and economic relations between the european union and the united states of america, cooperation in the field of standards and legislation relating to the protection of personal data is becoming increasingly important.
european airspace must be made as efficient as possible and its use must be made in conditions of maximum safety. this will bring important benefits both in terms of economic growth and job creation and for the environment. the completion of the single european sky will lead to a more sustainable aviation system; i therefore believe that the progress made so far must be sustained and continued as rapidly as possible. we need high-quality air services, especially in the current situation, when air traffic is in a continuous growth. furthermore, i believe that there should be a uniform approach and a homogeneous situation in all member states, and cooperation and coordination in this regard is extremely important.
the achievement of the single european sky requires measures to meet the european union's aviation safety objectives, with a view to strengthening the current rules and ensuring a uniform and high level of aviation safety. i would stress the importance of programmes such as galileo and gnss for the achievement of the single european sky, and the importance of a binding timetable for the implementation of the single european sky, while taking account of commercial considerations. according to the commission, the timely introduction of sesar will bring tangible benefits to passengers by reducing flight time by approximately 10%, a 50% reduction in cancelled flights and delays, and a possible reduction in ticket prices. i call for the development of the single european sky to take full account of all european union airports, including regional airports, given their contribution to reducing network congestion and increasing air traffic capacity.
i welcome the consolidation and improvement of passenger rights. i believe that their implementation is a priority and must be done in a complete and uniform manner to avoid any confusion. furthermore, travellers must be kept informed of their rights and the information provided to them must be clear, simple and accessible. transparency needs to be improved in all services offered to eliminate unfair trading practices. i would stress that all consumers are entitled to a high and equal level of protection and that the role of national supervisory authorities in this respect is particularly important. the implementation of passenger rights legislation in all modes of transport will strengthen free movement in the internal market.
i stress the importance of developing a set of rules on passenger rights for all modes of transport and welcome the commission's decision to continue the information campaign on passenger rights until 2014. we recommend that national authorities and national consumer centres participate in this campaign. in addition, in order to meet the needs of disabled persons or persons with reduced mobility and to provide more comprehensive assistance to passengers in the event of major disruptions to travel, we recommend that information points and assistance desks be available at departure and arrival points at airports, railway stations, bus stations and ports, accessible both physically and by electronic means. i think it is important to address the proliferation of abusive clauses in air carrier contracts, such as the abusive requirement for passengers to use a one-way ticket for a return ticket or for passengers to use all coupons on a successive flight ticket. we call on the commission to take the necessary measures to protect passengers.
the böge-kalfin report reflects and emphasises the priorities set by parliament in the sure report. the european union budget is an indispensable tool in addressing the effects of the financial crisis. we are talking about a budget that is 94% reinvested in the member states and that must be used to create economic prosperity through investment and job creation. austerity measures were necessary, but to be effective they must be complemented by measures to catalyse the economy. therefore, an increase in the budget is indispensable and a freezing of the ceilings at the level of 2013 is excluded. the perception of the union budget and the deadlock created in the negotiations on the new multiannual financial framework can only be changed by a thorough review of the own resources system. a new system of vat collection and a financial transaction tax are two innovative directions that should benefit from our unconditional support. as regards our work in the european parliament, i believe that the strategy authorised by the contact group leads us, in the case of a proposal below the ceiling proposed by parliament, to a negative vote. if this happens, because it is not certain that a sufficient number of members will vote against the council's decision, it will cause a delay to the detriment of the european union. the strength of the european parliament lies in the codecision procedure. we must trust all the members of this parliament and allow the normal negotiations on european policy files, the horizontal files, to proceed. this approach is likely to change the position of many member states.
i have asked to speak at the end of this debate in support of amendment 72, which was initiated and tabled by a number of colleagues. the amendment concerns direct payments in agriculture and aims to replace the idea of reducing the current gap with the idea of convergence of direct payments between member states. the difference between the two expressions is very clear and very significant. this parliament has, in many resolutions, expressed itself in favour of fair treatment of member states in respect of agricultural payments. we can't say at this point that the idea remains valid, but only for the future. by today's resolution, parliament gives the president of the council a genuine mandate in the consultations to come. this mandate is incomplete without the legitimate and well-founded aspirations of the citizens of eastern europe.
in writing. as rapporteur for the imco opinion, i welcome the proposed multiannual financial framework (mff) for the period 2014-2020 and its alignment with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. in the current economic context, we need to focus on measures that can lead to economic growth and overcome the economic and financial crisis we are facing. part of the solution is the proper functioning of the internal market, which can only be achieved through adequate funding. we are in the process of implementing the single market act. i consider that the mff must contain the financial resources necessary to implement the commitments entered into. another important element for growth and job creation is smes, so the cfm must give strong support to an eu policy aimed at improving access to finance for smes. no less important is the policy of consumer protection, with the ultimate aim of increasing consumer power. the successful functioning of the internal market is also not possible without adequate infrastructure, the connecting europe facility being an important step towards the creation of the single energy and digital markets and towards enhancing the free movement of goods, services and people.
in writing . it is to be welcomed that the european council remains committed to boosting growth and jobs in the context of the europe 2020 strategy. the pact for growth and jobs, agreed in june, provides the overall framework for action at national and eu level, using all the necessary instruments and policies. all the commitments set out in the pact must therefore be implemented fully and as rapidly as possible. it is known that smes provide around 90 million jobs in the eu, of which 30% are micro-enterprises, and 85% of all new jobs were created between 2002 and 2012 by smes, especially by newly created enterprises. access to finance is essential to finance business investment, to ensure that businesses realise their growth potential and to facilitate the creation of new businesses, which allows for future growth and jobs. moreover, the commission must support member states in reprogramming the structural funds so that they are strongly focused on growth and job creation, especially for young people, women and vulnerable people.
in writing. the key to the success of the single banking supervisory mechanism will be to ensure equal participation of member states in the decision-making process. the dominant share of euro area capital in eu member states with national currencies requires a balanced configuration of the new regulatory framework. otherwise, the european union will not only become a structure of 17 decision-makers and 10 victims, but the conditions for major systemic risks are created. the agreement on the gradual introduction of banking supervision in the euro area marks the end of the counterproductive disputes over the place of the banking and budgetary union in the european order of priorities. the franco-german compromise, indispensable to community cohesion, may be the right answer to the imperative of reducing the dangerous dependence between banks and governments. but we need not only measures to stop the vicious cycle of rising interest rates, falling ratings and liquidity problems, but also a framework that forces the banking sector to be sustainable and accountable in the face of speculative temptations. the serious effects of the financial sector crisis require us to act in such a way that 'ethical banking' is no longer a contradiction in terms.
in writing. i welcome the conclusions of the european council of 18-19 october, in which it reiterated its commitment to take firm action to address financial market tensions, restore confidence and stimulate growth and job creation. however, we believe that there has not been sufficient progress on the implementation of the pact for growth and jobs adopted in june and therefore call for firm, rapid and results-oriented action. in this context, we ask the commission to support the member states in the process of reprogramming the structural funds so that they are more strongly focused on growth and jobs. the eu's competitiveness and its economic and social development depend on the provision of modern and efficient transport, energy and communications infrastructure and information technology. in this regard, the connecting europe facility will address bottlenecks and missing cross-border links in trans-european transport infrastructure, complete the internal energy market and achieve a fully functional digital single market by 2015, and promote research and innovation, as well as improve the competitiveness of eu industry, as these will help to boost economic growth and create and retain jobs across the union.

in writing. − the commission's proposals for a new multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 include a set of proposals on reforming the union's own resources system. these include a proposal for the seventh own resources decision on abolishing the current vat own resource and replacing it with a new eu vat resource. under the current mff, a uniform rate of 0,30% of the harmonised vat base is levied in each member state in respect of own resources based on value added tax. the taxable base of vat is capped at 50% of gross national income for each country, to allow less wealthy member states to avoid paying disproportionate amounts (in low-income countries, vat generally represents a higher percentage of national income). this proposal represents a major improvement on the current system and can become a stable and viable resource for the eu budget.
in writing. − the procedures for drawing own resources to the eu budget must be carefully regulated, taking account of all the technical details, but also ensuring simplified methods that can be implemented uniformly by all member states. this new proposal on the own resource of value added tax is more transparent and provides greater adaptability and flexibility for member states compared to the previous regulations. however, i regret that the procedure for calculating the monthly contribution required to be carried out by each eu country in four steps is still complex and needs to be further simplified in the future, while also taking into account the vat systems in force in each member state.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation on the methods and procedure for making available the own resources based on value added tax, as the objective of the proposal is to simplify the way in which national contributions are calculated, thus reducing administrative costs and ensuring greater transparency. the new proposed calculation method uses the figures for vat receipts as a starting point. in order to achieve the greatest possible degree of simplicity and transparency, the regulation proposes that the commission establish a single average eu-wide share of vat revenue from supplies of goods and services for final consumption subject to the standard rate in each member state. member states shall apply the single eu average weight to their adjusted revenue. the figure obtained representing 'taxable vat revenue' is converted into a basic value, excluding taxes, using the effective standard vat rate of each member state. after the taxable amount has been established, the rate laid down in the implementing regulation of the own resources decision shall be applied for the calculation of the actual contribution.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the review of the financial system is taking place at a very opportune moment. the new regulation could help the union to implement a more effective neighbourhood policy. at the same time, the new rules in question would bring a number of advantages, including greater flexibility and speed in the disbursement of financial assistance to third countries. in addition, the regulation provides for some special measures for quick payment in times of crisis and a reduction in administrative burdens. they consider that the general objectives pursued by the new regulation correspond to the overall objectives of implementing the union's policies. i would like to stress that they also seek to respect the principle of sound financial management. simplifying procedures and rules is another positive thing that will ensure attractiveness and accessibility.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation on the financial rules applicable to the annual budget of the union. the regulation lays down the rules for the establishment and implementation of the general budget of the eu, the presentation and auditing of the accounts. the establishment and implementation of the budget shall respect the principles of unity, budgetary accuracy, annuality, balance, unit of account, universality, specificity, sound financial management and transparency. this regulation should promote the objective of e-government, in particular the use of electronic data in the exchange of information between institutions and third parties. pursuant to article 317 tfeu, the regulation consolidates the fundamental control and audit obligations of the member states in the implementation of the budget under shared management, to the extent that those obligations are currently provided for only by sectoral rules. the regulation creates a coherent legislative framework to enhance overall legal certainty, the effectiveness of controls and remedies and the protection of the financial interests of the union. it thus contains provisions on common management and control obligations for administrative structures, the annual declaration of assurance on management (by which administrators assume responsibility for the management of the union funds entrusted to them), the verification and acceptance of accounts, and suspension and financial correction mechanisms managed by the commission.

the agreement between the european union and israel on conformity assessment and acceptance of industrial products is beneficial for relations between the two parties, but raises two legal issues. the first concerns the territorial extent of the israeli authority to be established, and in order to comply with european and international law, we must allow israel to distinguish between its own territories and those occupied. the second issue concerns the types of products that can be added to this agreement, unfortunately without the consent of the european parliament. cosmetics will probably succeed pharmaceuticals, with parliament deprived of its right to co-legislate. the union's democratic forum has a duty to draw attention to these legal gaps and to vote responsibly, giving the european commission the chance to clarify these problematic aspects of its proposal. therefore, i consider it necessary both to request the referral of the case to the committee of the whole and to adopt the statement proposing the correct delimitation of the territorial extent of the future israeli authority. i hope that these elements will be fully taken into account by the council and the commission, whatever the outcome of the vote this evening.

madam president, we need to have an organised and unified european air traffic control system for commercial flights. the current high volume traffic and outdated technology has led to increasingly congested skies with more delays for passengers. with an ever-expanding demand for air travel, these problems can only get worse without proper infrastructure and a new approach. the nation-centric approach we see today is no longer fit to handle air traffic on its own. it is estimated that with a more coordinated approach presented by the single european sky, delays and cancellations may be reduced by as much as 50%. the coordination would foster growth and competition by allowing for more efficient use of air space. the single european sky would not impede national sovereignty and each nation would retain unilateral control over its air space for military purposes.
