madam president, in order to dig our way out of the financial crisis, everyone must fully understand the context behind job creation. in fact between 2002 and 2010, 85% of all new jobs within the european union were created by small and medium-sized businesses. the commission must accomplish the aim to increase and help small and medium-sized businesses by ensuring that they have access to structural funds. these funds provide small and medium-sized enterprises with a source of money for the development and expansion of their businesses. the commission must also promote more harmonisation between the member states in order to enhance competition, which will further grow the economy. as part of this step towards more harmonisation, the commission must also conduct a fitness check to review any existing erroneous or overbearing regulations. we need simple, clear and transparent regulations that are also predictable. these steps entail a long, time-consuming process, which is what we have now. that is why i say we need clear and predictable rules to a short deadline. we must work together to improve the job outlook and the european economy.
i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the presence of european smes on the international market should be better supported and encouraged. they represent the vast majority of all companies and are also the main source of jobs and innovation in the union. i therefore believe that the potential of this sector must be better exploited. this will boost the economy back to growth. moreover, smes can make a major contribution to promoting and extending the vocational information system, and in this way youth unemployment could be substantially reduced. i would also like to stress that support for smes must take account of the specific needs of each enterprise. we do need a more coherent and coordinated european policy on smes and the implementation of the new strategies must be done as soon as possible.
i voted in favour of the report because i believe that trade between the european union and the united states should be used to the benefit of both parties. the elimination of duties on bilateral trade could benefit those member states adopting policies to stimulate investment. romania is also a case in point, with its strategic partnership with the united states promoting cooperation in several areas. in addition to defense and cooperation within nato, the us and romania have committed to deepening ties in key areas such as energy security and the it sector. the romanian market has been successfully operated by renowned it and carbonated beverage companies for some time. the highly skilled workforce has led them to transfer some of their business to my country. other investors, like chevron, have also entered the energy sector. i want to continue to encourage the presence of american companies in romania.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the objectives of the draft amending budget. i think it is very important that a percentage of the european regional development fund and the cohesion fund for the next period is being re-allocated to risk-sharing instruments. however, this transfer must be carried out correctly and at the same time be subject to appropriate and effective control. moreover, the budgetisation of own resources forecasts will lead to a useful and welcome change in the way member states allocate their own resources contributions to the union budget among themselves. parliament's information in this procedure must be a priority.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the council position on draft amending budget no 4/2012 (pbr 4/2012 ) of the european union for the financial year 2012, section iii commission. the draft amending budget (dar 4/2012) concerns: a revision of the forecasts for traditional own resources (tor, i.e. customs duties and sugar levies), the bases for calculating vat and gni, the budgeting of the corresponding corrections in favour of the united kingdom and their financing and the revision of the financing of the gni reductions in favour of the netherlands and sweden in 2012; the creation of four budget lines for the implementation of the risk-sharing instruments financed by the european regional development fund (erdf) and the cohesion, convergence, regional competitiveness and labour force fund; the amendment of budget line 16 the preparation of the budget line 05 03 to allow the final payment of the euro (gni) to be made in the form of a symbolic replacement. the use of updated own resources forecasts leads to a more accurate determination of the payments to be made by the member states during the budgetary year and reduces the inevitable errors in the forecasts of the previous year.
in writing. − the main objective of the authority is to provide independent and transparent scientific advice on matters that have a direct or indirect effect on food and feed safety. the authority should improve the openness and transparency of the risk assessment process to take due account of independent and peer-reviewed scientific literature and to provide detailed justifications when rejecting divergent views. the authority should be encouraged to intensify dialogue and cooperation with external experts and national agencies, in particular where there are divergent views on the risk assessment process. certain elements of importance for the discharge have been addressed and retained and the roadmap for further actions under the common approach is expected to take full account of these aspects. i voted in favour of granting discharge to the european food safety authority in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2010.
in writing. − i voted for granting the discharge to the european food safety authority in order to acknowledge the measures implemented by the authority and the commitments it made since the postponement of the discharge last may. i acknowledge in particular the executive director’s commitment to foster the authority’s transparency towards european citizens by proposing that the management board elect its chairperson by open ballot and by working with the european commission in order to define the modalities of full public access to unpublished raw data. i also welcome the authority’s intention to consider the possibility of publishing the outcomes of the breach of trust procedures and to reinforce the mandate of its committee on conflict of interest. however, the authority should further strengthen its independence policy and consider adopting rules, including among others sanctions and publishing the curriculum vitae and declarations of interest of the in-house experts and scientists. it is crucial for the authority to keep the discharge authority regularly informed on the progress achieved, and in this respect i believe that its annual activity report should include a special section describing the actions taken to prevent and manage conflicts of interest from now on.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european food safety authority (efsa) for the financial year 2010. i would stress that the main objective of efsa is to provide independent and transparent scientific advice on matters that directly or indirectly affect food and feed safety. i welcome the fact that efsa has developed a tool for grants and procurement to improve the monitoring of tendering processes, contract management and payment forecasting capacity. i welcome the fact that a new database on subsidies and public procurement was launched on 28 june 2012. i welcome the significant reductions in the costs of meetings of the management board, which amounted to eur 6 175 per member in 2010, and in particular the reduction in expenditure of 66% compared to 2010, achieved through the switch to audio on demand, the use of english as the sole language for council meetings and the organisation of all meetings at the parma location.
in writing. − the work of the european medicines agency is important in providing the best possible scientific advice to eu member states and eu institutions on issues related to the evaluation of the quality, safety and efficacy of medicinal products for human and veterinary use. i have noted that the agency has improved the scope and methodology of systematic ex-ante and ex-post checks related to the verification of declarations of interests and i welcome the agency's decision to carry out an annual evaluation of its revised declaration of interest policy. the agency shall inform the discharge authority periodically, on a six-monthly basis, of the implementation of its revised policy and in particular of its systematic ex-ante and ex-post controls. the agency shall include in each of its annual activity reports a specific section describing the actions taken to prevent and manage conflicts of interest. i voted in favour of discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european medicines agency for the financial year 2010.
in writing. − i voted in favour of granting the discharge to the european medicines agency in order to acknowledge the measures implemented by the agency since the postponement of the discharge last may. the agency has shown a commitment to addressing the concerns raised by the european parliament. i commend in particular the efforts made by the executive director and his team to foster the agency’s transparency towards european citizens through, for example, its commitment to developing public access to clinical trial data. i also welcome the its commitment to improving the prevention and management of conflicts of interest with systematic ex-ante and ex-post controls related to the screening of declarations of interest as well as a yearly evaluation of its revised policy on declarations of interest. it is crucial for the agency to keep the discharge authority regularly informed on the progress achieved, and in this respect i believe that its annual activity report should include a special section describing the actions taken to prevent and manage conflicts of interest from now on.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european medicines agency for the financial year 2010. i would like to recall the importance of the work carried out by the agency in providing the best possible scientific advice to the member states and institutions on the evaluation of the quality, safety and efficacy of medicinal products for human and veterinary use. i welcome the efforts to reform the system of payments for services provided by member states' authorities, which should be clearly based on real costs. i believe that a high level of reliability in terms of declared interests can only be achieved if pharmaceutical companies also make public the list of experts and research centres with which they work and the amounts involved in their financial reports. the appropriateness of introducing a legislative initiative in this area should be examined. the agency should also include in each of its annual activity reports a specific section describing the actions taken to prevent and manage conflicts of interest.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is important to have control over the conditions under which forestry material is imported into the union. third countries exporting forest reproductive material to the european union must comply with the same conditions as union producers. for this reason, i believe that these materials must comply with european rules as regards both the system of authorization and registration of the source material and the rules concerning the subsequent production of reproduction material from that source material. only in this way can we ensure that imported forest reproductive material does not destabilise the ecosystems of the european union. the protection of the environment and forests must remain a constant concern for the union.
in writing. − the rules on the internal marketing of plant reproductive material are laid down in council directive 1999/105/ec. in order to facilitate and to respond promptly to market demand, the directive provides for the council to establish rules for authorising the import of reproductive material from third countries on the basis of a system of equivalence. this update was proposed by member states and parties in order to facilitate trade, in particular the import of forest reproductive material, and to respond promptly to market demand, in particular for fast growing energy/biomass tree plantations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of including forest reproductive material in the category 'qualified' in the scope of that decision and for updating the names of the authorities responsible for authorising and controlling production. national certification rules for forest reproductive material in canada, croatia, norway, serbia, switzerland, turkey and the united states of america provide for an official on-site inspection during the harvesting and processing of seeds and seed production. the systems for the authorisation and registration of basic material and the subsequent production of reproductive material from that basic material should comply with the oecd system for the certification of forest reproductive material for international trade. as regards 'qualified' material, those conditions should include the provision of information on whether the products are genetically modified or not. at the time of entry of the seed and planting stock into the territory of the union, the supplier importing such material shall inform the official body of that member state in advance of the import.
in writing. − the concept of european citizenship introduced by the maastricht treaty aims to strengthen and deepen european identity and at the same time to enable european citizens to participate actively in the process of european integration. a sense of belonging to the european union is a very important factor in shaping and defining civic participation, which only enhances the collective identity on which the future of the union depends. i welcome the commission's decision to make 2013 the european year of citizens and believe that this will give new impetus to the debate on citizenship of the union and put the effective and informed exercise of this right at the heart of the political agenda.
in writing. − the right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states is an essential individual right deriving from citizenship of the union, and citizens must be fully aware of and enjoy the full range of rights granted to them by union law. the european year of citizenship is an important impetus for a better awareness of union citizenship, as well as to stimulate citizens' participation in the democratic life of the union and to address democratic deficits and high absenteeism in european elections. concrete ways are needed to close the gap between the eu institutions and the citizens of the union, to address democratic deficits and the low turnout in european elections. citizens must have access to simple and transparent information on the european parliament elections, the programmes and objectives of political parties and candidates, and their electoral rights. at the same time, the voting procedures should be simplified. i call for the promotion of information, education and awareness campaigns that are easily and freely accessible to all eu citizens and especially to vulnerable groups. i also call on the commission to draw up a comparative handbook explaining the terminology, scope and content of citizenship of the union in order to promote a common understanding of the concept.
in writing. − i support the proposal to establish a european year of citizens in 2013 to give all european citizens the opportunity to become more aware of the association between union citizenship and the right to free movement, given that only 43% of europeans claim to be familiar with the term 'european union citizen', and around two thirds of respondents from the 27 eu member states (67%) are not well informed or not informed at all. as the representative of the citizens, parliament must make an important contribution to their understanding of european policies, with a focus on participatory democracy and the new rights created by the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, in particular the citizens' initiative.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of the report on the european year of citizens because i believe that this is an opportunity to enhance awareness of the rights attached to union citizenship, in order to help citizens make full use of their right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states. it is important to give concrete solutions to achieve better and equal opportunities for all. citizens must be fully aware and take full advantage of the broad array of rights granted to them under union law, both in their country as well as in cross-border situations. moreover, i am convinced that the european year of citizenship will increase citizens’ awareness on union citizenship and will stimulate citizens’ participation in the democratic life of the european union. any restrictions imposed on european citizenship, such as the ones in place for romanians and bulgarians, must be ended as soon as possible in order for the citizens of these countries to benefit fully from their rights.
in writing. − 2013 will mark the 20th anniversary of the introduction of the concept of 'citizenship of the european union' by the maastricht treaty. the institution of european citizenship has affected the lives of millions of people, creating a number of benefits such as cross-border access to healthcare. yet a recent eurobarometer survey shows that 48% of citizens say they are not sufficiently informed about their rights as european citizens and only 30% of citizens believe they can personally influence the european process. a 2011 eurobarometer survey shows that only one third of eu citizens are fully or partially satisfied with the eu's administration's efficiency, availability of services and transparency, with the rest expressing dissatisfaction, particularly with the latter. despite the modest budget allocated (€1 million compared to the 2011 european year, which had a budget of around €11 million), we must make the most of the 'european year of citizens' to remind our citizens of what the european union can do for each of us.
in writing. − the maastricht treaty gives all citizens of the union european citizenship, which is in addition to their national citizenship and gives them the right to travel, study and work in any of the member states, as well as a number of other related rights. unfortunately, almost half of the citizens do not know these rights and cannot exercise them. this is why the establishment of a european year of citizens in 2013 20 years after the introduction of european citizenship is welcome. the actions planned for 2013 can increase awareness of european rights, values and history among the population so that citizens can benefit from the opportunities of eu membership. any initiative that brings citizens closer to the european institutions is certainly useful. i personally believe that the actions of the european year of citizens must be coordinated at community level to ensure that information is transmitted uniformly to every corner of the union. unfortunately, the budget for this programme is insufficient, much less than the funds allocated to other european years. in addition, no co-financing is provided for projects by civil society organisations, so we can anticipate limited success of this initiative.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft decision on the european year of citizens because 2013 will mark the 20th anniversary of the establishment of citizenship of the union. the union is founded on the indivisible and universal values of human dignity, freedom, equality and solidarity and is based on the principles of democracy and the rule of law. every citizen of the union must enjoy the rights set out in the treaties and the eu charter of fundamental rights. in order to enable union citizens to make informed decisions on whether to exercise their right to free movement, it is essential that union citizens are also adequately informed of other rights they have under union law in cross-border situations. i also voted to make the multilingual 'europe to you' web portal, which is a 'one-stop shop' information system on the rights of citizens and businesses in the union, more popular with eu citizens. all initiatives launched for and in the context of the european year of citizens should raise awareness of citizens' rights among staff of public authorities, whether at union, national, regional or local level.
in writing. − the european air traffic management system remains fragmented in terms of airspace organisation, technological equipment and air traffic control procedures. this has led to inefficient flight operations and additional costs of eur 1 billion per year. at the same time, there has been a considerable increase in air traffic levels and the forecasts are that this trend will continue in the near future, especially in south-east europe. the increased level of air traffic can only be managed effectively and safely if neighbouring states and air navigation service providers cooperate more closely in the future. the creation of the single european sky is a key mechanism to overcome future challenges and should generate sufficient capacity to manage the increasing number of flights registered on the continent, in order to reduce delays, increase safety and cost efficiency, and to reduce the environmental impact.
in writing. − at a time when the european union is focusing on creating new jobs, we must also bear in mind that the implementation of the ses will lead to better organisation and management of air traffic in europe, which will result in a high demand for highly skilled jobs, i.e. with high-level skills and very well paid. a more efficient european airspace will, on the other hand, bring additional economic gains at european level, including benefits in terms of growth, job creation and the environment. europe cannot afford to lose 30% of eu gdp, 58% of the jobs that can be created or 110% of co2 savings if the deployment of sesar were delayed by 10 years.
in writing. − the report aims to address the implementation of air transport legislation, given that it plays a major role in the eu economy and society. in this context, air traffic management (atm) is essential for air transport operations, while addressing the challenges of competitiveness, safety and sustainability. it is important to take into account that air traffic is rapidly approaching its maximum capacity and, as time goes on, the problem continues to intensify and the implementation of single european sky (ses) legislation is urgently needed to avoid possible security or operational risks caused by unprecedented traffic flows and outdated technologies. the project is expected to have a cumulative impact on eu gdp of eur 419 billion, create 328 000 jobs and save 50 million tonnes of co2. the ses is also open to neighbouring countries, with the aim of enlargement, and benefits a geographical area larger than the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the implementation of the single european sky legislation because it shows a lot of progress on the implementation of the single european sky and 2012 is a key year for the implementation of the single european sky (ses). european airspace is among the busiest in the world, with over 750 million passengers using eu airports. given that air traffic volume is continuously increasing, leading to insufficient capacity and increasing delays for passengers, we draw attention to the urgency of the successful implementation of the ses legislation, in order to avoid increased congestion and to ensure greater coherence of european aviation safety provisions. in this respect, we ask that regional airports be taken into account in the development of ses, given their contribution to decongestion of the network and to increasing air capacity. we ask the commission to report to the transport and tourism committee by march 2013 on the progress made in implementing the ses legislation, together with an assessment of the consequences of delays in implementing the functional airspace blocks.
in writing. − the mass transport of european citizens is no longer a simple aspect of our lives. with the increasing number of citizens of the member states travelling, the use of transport is an integral part of the european economy, society and culture. it is the duty of the european authorities to ensure that interactions between citizens and operators in this sector are transparent and fair. however, it must be remembered that the proper conduct of travel requires not only respect for the rights of travellers but also for their obligations. the commission's information campaign on the rights of travellers in the eu should be extended, and greater emphasis should be placed on informing people of their obligations. as an increasing number of european citizens use the internet to purchase or validate travel authorisations, this process should be encouraged, precisely because of its benefits in terms of increasing the speed of boarding procedures, as well as its tangible benefits in terms of environmental protection. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i welcome the commission's policy of guaranteeing common and comparable rights and conditions for all road, rail, air, sea and inland waterway passengers, and support all measures aimed at removing the obstacles that prevent european citizens from exercising their rights effectively, within the framework of an intermodal approach. i also believe that particular attention should be paid to improving information for passengers and their compensation in the event of disruption, cancellation of travel or loss of luggage, and to defining the rights of passenger organisations, which are best placed to inform and support citizens.
in writing. − in a europe where citizens have the right to move where and when they want, according to their needs and interests, better connectivity of all means of transport and, by implication, the application of a single regulation on passenger rights for all modes of transport is essential. on the other hand, i believe that member states should cooperate more closely in developing a european, multimodal travel planner that would allow travellers to plan their journey across europe, including the most diverse means of transport.
in writing. − in aligning the rights of all eu citizens to all types of transport, i believe that more attention needs to be paid to people with disabilities and reduced mobility and their travel needs. the report provides some measures to support these people, especially in terms of providing specialist assistance, which significantly improves the current situation. however, i believe that in the future we must concentrate our efforts on finding solutions at the level of each eu country in terms of accessibility of transport infrastructure, in order to harmonise and adapt the standards imposed at the unit level to the architectural specificities of the member states. this will remove architectural barriers to the safety and security of disabled people and persons with reduced mobility and enable them to fulfil their role as active members of society.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's own-initiative report on passenger rights for all modes of transport. i believe that future initiatives by the commission on passenger rights must address the missing elements of the existing regulations, namely a smooth journey for all passengers and all modes of transport. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the right to a minimum standard of quality of service offered by carriers, the right to compensation, reimbursement and information, in a common legislative framework that creates conditions for fair competition between the different modes of transport. it is important that passengers receive clear information on the liability of carriers in the event of damage to luggage during the journey, on differences in the baggage allowance and on compensation for delays. i also stress the importance of the following: in the case of online ticket purchases, no additional costs should be added before purchase; the need for quick complaint handling through simplified procedures; clarification of liability in the event of damage to mobility or assistance equipment, the replacement cost of which often exceeds the maximum reimbursement amount provided for by international law.
in writing. − i voted against the discharge for the implementation of the council's budget for the financial year 2010. i regret the difficulties encountered in the open dialogue between the council and the committee on budgetary control and, in particular, the council's refusal to answer parliament's supplementary questions, which is a legitimate part of the discharge procedure. an effective way of monitoring the budget implementation process depends unconditionally on proper interinstitutional cooperation between parliament and the council; i would therefore like to reiterate that this process requires the utmost responsibility on the part of all parties involved.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2010, section ii council, refusing to grant the secretary-general of the council discharge in respect of the implementation of the council's budget for the financial year 2010. parliament's right to grant discharge is in accordance with articles 316, 317 and 319 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which must be interpreted in the light of their context and purpose, namely to subject to parliamentary control and oversight the implementation of the entire budget of the union without exception and to grant discharge separately not only for the section of the budget implemented by the commission but also for the sections of the budget implemented by the other institutions referred to in article 1 of the financial regulation.
in writing. − following the requests of the european parliament, the european environment agency (eea) became more involved in 2010 in actions to improve its communication with the public and the media, such as the global monitoring for environment and security (gmes), the international year of biodiversity through the green façade project, the eye on earth platform. the european environment agency has thus used the union funds in the thematic manner provided for by the european legislator and the european budgetary authority. the european court of auditors had no comment on the agency's accounts for 2010, which it considers to be reliable and in line with the laws and regulations in force. in addition, the eea has always provided timely, detailed and satisfactory answers to all the rapporteur's questions and the eea board has taken steps to prevent any uncertainties in the future. in view of the above, and the excellent work carried out by the agency, i considered it necessary to vote in favour of the discharge for the implementation of the agency's budget for the financial year 2010.
in writing. - the vote in favour of appointing leonard orban as a member of the court of auditors is based on his extensive professional experience in european and non-european affairs. this statement is supported by the positions held over the years by the minister of european affairs, a position also held during the previous government, former european commissioner, former presidential advisor, and chief negotiator of romania for eu accession. there is no doubt about his professional competence.
in writing. − mr. orban has a wide experience in european affairs; he is a former commissioner and minister of european affairs in the romanian government, having been appointed to these posts due to his expertise and not to political affiliation. he was also chief negotiator on behalf of romania for the country’s accession to the european union. in this position he supervised the establishment of the audit and control system in romania, acquiring a good knowledge of auditing. these are the reasons why i voted for his nomination.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as i believe that the support provided by the european globalisation adjustment fund is welcome in the current situation. the global economic and financial crisis has hit ireland hard in recent years. that's why i think the loss of 592 jobs is very important for the irish economy. the loss of revenue due to redundancies at the irish company will generate significant indirect job losses through a decrease in workers' disposable income and a reduction in the purchase of irish goods and services at local and regional level. i therefore believe that the use of the european globalisation adjustment fund is very important in the current situation for the recovery of the local economy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i think it is a good idea to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund to help workers who have suffered as a result of the economic and financial crisis. in the context of the crisis, several member states decided to strengthen their budgets. in many cases, this consolidation has come at the expense of research and development programmes and many companies in the sector have been forced to reduce their activities. through the funds made available, some 700 workers will be reintegrated into the labour market through various forms of assistance such as job search assistance, vocational training and retraining, self-employment assistance and measures to stimulate older workers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund in relation to the application submitted by sweden in the case of the pharmaceutical company astrazeneca. the request refers to 543 redundancies in the astrazeneca company between june and october 2011. another 444 redundancies (987 in total) took place before and after the reference period and are linked to the same collective redundancy procedure. sweden has had a strong position in medical research and the mass layoffs at astrazeneca were unpredictable, although the situation in the pharmaceutical sector was expected to worsen as a result of the increasing dominance of generics and the outsourcing of r & d outside europe. i believe that egf support should be allocated primarily to training and job search activities. the coordinated package provides for a jobseeker's allowance of eur 7 170 (calculated for an average duration of participation of 6 months) and a mobility allowance of eur 500. i believe it is important to facilitate access to egf funds for the reintegration of redundant workers into the labour market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that workers affected by the economic and financial crisis should be supported in their attempts to reintegrate into the labour market. in the context of the crisis, the metal and construction industries were the main affected by the decline in global orders. many of these have been forced to limit their activity, and some have even had to stop. shipbuilding is no exception. as the outlook for the sector is not very optimistic for the future, it is expected that more and more workers in this sector will lose their jobs. the proposal for a decision should be supported to provide for measures for the reintegration of those made redundant.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund in respect of the application submitted by spain concerning the company metal, in the region of galicia, spain. the application concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 4 325 854 from the egf for spain in respect of 878 redundancies in the period from march to december 2011 in 35 enterprises in the region of galicia active in the manufacture of metal products. the disposals in the shipbuilding industry are aggravating the difficult employment situation in galicia. the main economic sectors in galicia were fishing, along with the automotive industry, the textile industry, the natural stone industry and the shipbuilding industry. given the impact of the crisis, the prospects for future reintegration into the labour market of displaced workers in this area do not look very encouraging. i would stress that assistance from the egf should not replace actions which are the responsibility of undertakings under national law or collective agreements, nor measures to restructure undertakings or sectors of activity. we ask the spanish government to inform the european parliament and the commission annually about the employment rate of persons who have benefited from egf assistance.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i support the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of changes in the structure of world trade. the construction sector in the netherlands, as well as in the european union as a whole, has been severely affected by the crisis. the crisis also affected some of the investments in infrastructure and housing programs. this has led to a substantial increase in the unemployment rate in the gelderland region, with the construction sector being the most affected. in this context, the regional authorities are considering a series of measures to stimulate the integration of the 435 workers concerned into the labour market, such as assistance in finding a job, vocational training and retraining, assistance for the placement of dismissed persons and the promotion of entrepreneurship.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund in respect of the netherlands request. this application relates to the mobilisation of eur 2 898 594 from the egf for the netherlands. the request concerns 516 redundancies in 54 construction companies in the region of gelderland, the netherlands, in the period from february to november 2011. the construction sector is a major employer in the gelderland region and redundancies have had a negative impact on local communities, with 4 100 jobs already lost in the sector in 2010 and youth unemployment rising by 10% in 2011. i recall the importance of improving the employability of workers, especially those in low-skilled occupations, through tailored training measures and by recognising the skills and competences acquired during their professional careers. i welcome the fact that the egf contribution is intended to be used exclusively for active measures in favour of the workforce, through training and counselling.
in writing. - i voted for this report because i support the mobilisation of part of the european globalisation adjustment fund to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of changes in the structure of world trade in the netherlands. in this country, the european aluminium sector has experienced a decrease in consumer demand. moreover, there was also a decrease in the average production of aluminium in the union, which created a negative impact on the dutch company concerned, which was heavily dependent on the construction and transport sectors. that is why i think the measures envisaged to reintegrate workers into the labour market are welcome. and the coordinated package of personalized services will help the laid-off workers in their drive to get back into the market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund on the request submitted by the netherlands in connection with redundancies in zalco. the application concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 1 494 008 from the egf for the netherlands to support the 616 redundancies caused by zalco aluminium zeeland company nv and its two suppliers (ecl services netherlands bv and start) in the netherlands during december 2011. the dutch authorities argue that these redundancies were the result of the global financial and economic crisis, which caused a sharp drop in consumer demand, illustrated by the 25,7% reduction in the average eu-wide use of aluminium between 2008 and 2009, especially in the automotive and construction sectors. i consider that the procedure for adopting decisions to mobilise the egf should be swift and smooth. it provides one-off, time-limited individual support aimed at supporting workers made redundant as a result of globalisation and the financial and economic crisis. we ask the dutch government to inform the ep and the commission annually about the employment rate of persons who have benefited from egf assistance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that workers affected by the consequences of the economic and financial crisis must be supported in their attempts to reintegrate into the labour market. i think the decision to mobilise the fund in favour of france is welcome. the economic crisis has worsened the prospects for economic growth as well as credit conditions in this country. and because of this, the security of workers in terms of a stable job has been greatly diminished. the car market suffered in france, where car sales fell sharply. and this was despite the temporary measures taken by the authorities. therefore, i consider that the measures in question represent a good way to remedy the current situation. they are to provide individual support to workers in need.
in writing. - the financial and economic crisis had serious consequences for the european automotive industry, and by implication for the labour market, and these effects are still being felt. the european car market has experienced a major decline, leading to staff reductions and social tensions. concrete measures are needed to support the 2 089 workers made redundant by psa peugeot citroën. they should focus on providing assistance in job search, guidance, training and retraining. however, special attention should be paid to the retraining of vulnerable people affected by redundancies. in this respect, i support the development of the professional potential of vulnerable groups and the recognition of skills acquired during their professional careers. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european globalisation adjustment fund plays a crucial role in the economic recovery of regions following large-scale redundancies, including in the newly acceded states. i would like to welcome the european commission's proposal to allocate eur 2.9 million from the european globalisation adjustment fund to romania to provide assistance to workers made redundant by nokia.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund in favour of france in the case of peugeot. this application relates to the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 11 949 666 from the egf for france in respect of 2 089 redundancies which occurred within the undertaking psa peugeot citroen between november 2009 and february 2010. the worsening growth prospects and tightening credit conditions seen during this crisis have raised concerns among individuals about their job security and led them to delay the purchase of a vehicle. the companies have reduced their investments and, consequently, the renewal rate of their fleet. peugeot citroën automobiles is obliged by french law to participate in the revitalization of these regions, contributing to the creation of new activities and new jobs in order to mitigate the effects of redundancies. i regret that the evaluation took 27 months, i.e. from the submission of the application in may 2010 to the adoption of the budgetary authority's proposal for a decision in august 2012. we call for the mobilisation of egf funds to be facilitated so that redundant workers can be reintegrated into the labour market as quickly as possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i think it is a good idea to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund to help workers who have suffered as a result of the economic and financial crisis. the commission established the profitability of the sampled union producers by expressing the pre-tax net profit of the sales of the like product to unrelated customers in the union as a percentage of the turnover of those sales. as renewable energy production seems to be migrating from europe, i believe that urgent action is desirable. thus, it would be a good idea to reduce production and transport costs, while also reducing the distance between customers and markets. in addition, measures aimed at reintegrating redundant workers into the market are welcome in this context. they are very useful individual support that will benefit the people affected.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the support provided by the european globalisation adjustment fund is welcome in the current situation. in germany, the market for printing equipment is already operating on a global scale. however, more and more important players in the market are creating fierce competition for german producers. although competing products are often low-priced, they are also of inferior quality. as a result, the german company's sales in this area decreased and its profits decreased considerably. i believe that the measures envisaged can contribute to a positive development of things. the package of services to be financed aims at reintegrating redundant workers into the labour market. i would like to stress their importance in this context.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the amendment to the regulation is welcome in the context of global technological progress. there is a need for close control of exports of products which could be used for purposes other than civilian purposes. however, the impact on the relevant industries must also be considered. in the current economic context, we must not jeopardise the global competitiveness of smes. romania is very interested in the consequences of the amendment. my country is the largest producer of heavy water in the world. heavy water is used to cool candu nuclear reactors. in this respect, i would not want any heavy water exports to be hampered in the future. the commission should adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu. cooperation with member states and other stakeholders will also be required.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the training of crews on board ships is of particular importance for maritime safety. navigators must always be able to operate in conditions of maximum safety. european legislation in this area must therefore be brought into line with international standards. i welcome the commission's proposal, which aims to achieve just that. we need a coherent and comprehensive european shipping policy. it must aim at improving working conditions and training crews. in this context, i would stress that the minimum rest period is essential and must be respected in all situations. thus, fatigue-related hazards and accidents can be avoided. i would point out that the global dimension of shipping requires the adaptation of european rules as soon as possible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on the minimum level of training of seafarers. the union maritime sector is characterised by a high level of maritime expertise, which underpins its competitiveness. the quality of training for seafarers is important for the competitiveness of the sector and for attracting union citizens, especially young people, to maritime professions. in order to maintain quality standards in the training of seafarers, measures to prevent fraudulent practices in certificates of competency and skills should be improved. to that end, member states shall adopt and implement appropriate measures to prevent fraud and other illegal practices in relation to certificates and attestations issued and shall provide for effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties. better training of seafarers should include appropriate theoretical and practical training to ensure that seafarers are qualified to comply with safety and security standards and are able to manage risks and emergencies. quality standards and quality standard systems should also be developed and implemented on the establishment of a european reference framework for quality assurance in education and training in the field.
in writing. − the additional protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement between the eu and the state of israel on conformity assessment and acceptance of industrial products will allow eu exporters to test and certify, if they wish, their industrial products before export, once, according to the same aligned requirements and standards, and to access the israeli market without having to undergo any further conformity assessment-based certification procedures. it will also apply the reverse process, with the same aligned requirements and standards. i voted for this agreement which aims to improve trade between the eu and israel on a reciprocal basis. it is a beneficial agreement for both european citizens and those of the state of israel, who will be able to benefit from trade in goods, especially medicines, under favourable conditions: reduced costs for european patients, faster access to markets, diversification of pharmaceutical products, optimisation of control of pharmaceutical products produced outside the eu. the arguments against this agreement did not convince me because they do not prove consistency, being at the same time of an economic and political nature. moreover, the highly likely assumption in the event of rejection of the acaa, of losses that the eu market may suffer (reciprocity could also work towards sanctions from israel), was completely ignored.
in writing. − the eu's development policy has as its main objective to support developing countries' efforts to eradicate poverty, including the target of achieving the millennium development goals by 2015. the european union must choose the best combination of policies, tools and resources to be effective in fighting poverty, paying particular attention to the quality of the aid it provides by directing its support to the countries where the impact can be greatest. i believe that in the future, eu efforts should focus on supporting sustainable growth, which does not harm the environment, biodiversity and natural resources or increase vulnerability to natural disasters. eu development policy should therefore promote a 'green' economy that is able to create jobs without causing undesirable effects on the environment. they also believe that actions to improve the capacity of developing countries to cope with the consequences of climate change should be encouraged and supported. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the european union and its member states are world leaders in innovative finance for the financial sector, in combating climate change or in development. the european commission regularly feeds into the debate at european level and carries out assessments of potential innovative sources of funding. although the eu is the world's largest donor of development aid, i believe that aid alone is not enough to reduce poverty sustainably. we need policies that overcome trade, geographical and governance barriers and help to make the most of the opportunities offered by globalisation.
in writing. − our efforts, as representatives of the citizens of the european union, are to guarantee their rights and freedoms at the level of the union, but also to offer them solutions for sustainable and equitable development, reducing the disparities between the social classes in each country and inequalities of all kinds. in the field of development in particular, the future of eu policies must be based on a sound, unified application of the principles of administrative and fiscal governance, with a view to eliminating extreme poverty and aid dependency among citizens in developing countries. but i think that in this proposal too little attention has been paid to the situation of people with disabilities in developing countries, who unfortunately live below the poverty line by 82%. in this regard, our efforts must be directed towards finding solutions and generating immediate benefits for these disadvantaged people, in close cooperation with the private sector.
in writing. − small and medium-sized enterprises are one of the most important sectors of the european economy because they provide jobs for a significant number of european citizens and because they make a decisive contribution to economic growth and development in the european union. small and medium-sized enterprises must receive appropriate support and attention because they are one of the main actors involved in the research and innovation process and because they remain a major contributor to the development of the competitiveness of european economies. as the effects of the economic and financial crisis are becoming more widespread, boosting the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises is becoming essential. this cannot be achieved by returning to protectionist formulas, but by encouraging the presence of these economic actors more and more on international markets. the european union, together with the member states, needs to act more consistently to change complex customs rules, to eliminate unclear technical regulations or to encourage freer and less costly access to information that can encourage the international expansion of small and medium-sized enterprises. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the global economic crisis that started in 2008 has affected small and medium-sized enterprises in europe, which continue to struggle to recover. despite the difficult environment in which they operate, smes have retained their role as the backbone of the european economy. the 20.7 million smes represent over 98% of all european enterprises and employ over 87 million people. the majority of smes (92.2%) are microenterprises with fewer than 10 employees. current estimates show that smes account for 67% of total employment and 58% of gross value added. the trends in the various member states are increasingly divergent and i believe that a positive signal must be sent in terms of employment. in this delicate situation, decisive policy action to address the drivers of sme growth could tip the balance.
in writing. − there are some 23 million small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in the eu, representing 99% of all companies. smes provide jobs for 75 million people (70% of total eu jobs). if the eu can improve the competitiveness of smes and adopt measures that can reduce the administrative burden faced by smes, then the potential of european entrepreneurs will be developed and the eu economy will be boosted back to growth. the eu should invest in programmes that aim to identify the entrepreneurial potential of european citizens as a viable alternative to employment, especially among young people, women and migrants. expanding the entrepreneurial culture in the eu and attracting more people to the world of entrepreneurship through ad-hoc programmes, incentives such as sme-friendly tax systems and tax benefits could help people overcome the fear of failure and give them the courage to start or expand their business. the natural consequences will be new jobs, more innovation and more economic growth for all businesses, whether they are industrial, service or social.
in writing. − the international presence of european smes needs to be improved, as only 25% of them are active in the single market area and only 13% were active outside the union. in a globalising world, european smes need to be encouraged to become more involved in activities in other non-eu countries and, in particular, in the new emerging countries, where there is insufficient potential.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on smes: competitiveness and business opportunities. i am convinced that smes play a central role in the eu’s economic development. the eu should invest in programmes whose direction addresses the entrepreneurial potential of european citizens as a real alternative to employment – particularly in the poorest and most vulnerable countries of europe. in order to encourage entrepreneurs to take the risk of starting their business, two key points should be implemented: the entrepreneurial culture should be made more attractive through ad-hoc programmes and the administrative and fiscal barriers that young entrepreneurs face should be reduced. finally, creating a business environment supportive of the sustainable development of smes is fundamental.

in writing. − 'small and medium-sized enterprises are rather an expression of a specific mood and attitude', declared a former german minister of economy in charge of economic design for west germany in 1956. decentralisation at member state level has played a decisive role in the development of smes. it is proven that smes seek the support of regional administrations and regional financial institutions. studies carried out at local level show that small enterprises mainly develop long-term links with local actors. we need integrated european policies for smes that aim to increase access to finance and investment in research and innovation. facilitating their access to international markets can make a decisive contribution to the growth of exports. i am convinced that in the present period, when we are increasingly faced with outsourcing processes, smes can prevent these risks. their added value is their high adaptability at relatively low costs. the european standardised system should allow their participation in decision-making processes at all levels, including in public-private partnership contracts between member states and the commission. the standardisation of information technology and an integrated system of cooperation are priority measures to increase their competitiveness.

in writing. − the european union and the us enjoy the best integrated economic relations, illustrated by an unrivalled level of mutual investment stocks, amounting to over €2.1 trillion. total us investment in the eu is three times that in asia and eu investment in the united states is about eight times the value of eu investment in india and china combined. investment is thus the real driver of the transatlantic relationship, contributing to economic growth and job creation on both sides of the atlantic. for these reasons, and in the current economic context, i believe that trade between the eu and the us must be better used to stimulate smart, strong and sustainable growth.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on trade relations between the european union and the united states of america, considering that closer trade links between the two partners and increased investment would boost job creation and economic growth. it is also important to underline that in certain areas the perspectives of the union and the us remain different, in particular as regards the use of genetically modified organisms or cloned animals.

in writing. − i have voted in favour of the report on trade and economic relations with the united states, as i welcome the ongoing discussion between the eu and the us on how to work collectively to increase growth potential and foster financial stability in order to create high quality jobs. furthermore, i am convinced that working closely with the council, the commission, the us congress, the us administration and the stakeholders will make it possible to achieve the full economic potential of the transatlantic economic relationship, in order to create new opportunities for businesses and workers on both sides of the atlantic and strengthen eu and us leadership in the global economy. nevertheless, there are still some problems that persist in the relations between the eu and us, and which also affect the economic climate, one of the most important being the visa-free restrictions for the citizens of four eu countries. visa-free travel should be granted equally to all eu citizens in order to increase mutual confidence and to boost economic and trade relations.
in writing. − the protection of geographical indications is indeed one of the important bilateral issues, but i am convinced that the current impasse can be overcome. we have the example of the recently concluded agreement, under which from 1 june organic products certified in the eu or the usa will be able to be marketed as organic in either region. this agreement will open up important trade opportunities for both partners. in agriculture as a whole, trade relations are mutually beneficial, with the us being the eu's second largest trading partner for agricultural products. but i have my doubts about the possible effects of a complete abolition of export refunds in eu-us agricultural trade. such a decision should be based on a thorough study.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on trade and economic relations with the united states, as the eu and the us are each other's main trading partners, with the two economies together accounting for about half of global economic output and almost a third of world trade flows. trade and foreign investment between the eu and the us must be better used to drive smart, strong, sustainable, balanced, inclusive and resource-efficient growth, which eventually leads to job creation. we stress the importance of further strengthening transatlantic economic relations while upholding eu interests in areas such as environmental, animal health and welfare, food safety, cultural diversity, workers' rights, consumer rights, financial services, public services and geographical indications. we also welcome the initiatives taken to develop common standards in key areas of technological evolution such as nanotechnology, electric vehicles, smart grids and e-health. given the growing importance of electronic commerce, data protection standards play a key role in protecting consumers in both the eu and the us. we stress that the eu and the us need to address the growing cybersecurity threats in a concerted manner and in an international context.
