madam president, i would like to thank commissioner barnier for his strong commitment to deepening the single market, which is evident in the single market act. despite the benefits the single market has brought to citizens and businesses, and to our economy overall, i think we should be critical in identifying the areas where we can do better, and take the necessary measures. this process was started with the first single market act, which is under implementation, and it is now being completed with the single market act ii. i believe the approach taken by the commission and the priorities identified are correct. nevertheless i would like to stress that these measures must be accompanied by better governance of the single market and a strong commitment from member states to transpose the legislation correctly and in a timely and more transparent way, making maximum use of correlation tables. enforcement is a key priority if we want the single market to deliver. last but not least, it is essential to communicate more with businesses and citizens and to associate them as closely as we can with the deepening of the single market.
in writing. the 20th anniversary of the launch of the single market is an opportunity to reflect on the obstacles that prevent european citizens from fully enjoying their fundamental rights. the right to free movement, which is still restricted by protectionist measures, is a good example. if european citizens and consumers are at the heart of the european project, then measures taken at european level must facilitate their access to the labour market while ensuring their fundamental freedom to move freely within the eu. that is why i believe that the time has come to talk about relaunching the single market, leading to real inclusion and restoring the confidence of european citizens in this market. i welcome the measures taken so far by the european commission in this direction, but i would urge more firmness on the part of the european executive to punish protectionist tendencies in certain member states.
in writing. 500 million consumers, 21 million businesses, €2.8 trillion of intra-eu trade and €1.5 trillion of world trade is a nice balance sheet for the european single market. it has transformed the way we live, shop, work, study, and travel. in addition, the rights of millions of european citizens, who can do these things in the country they want, are protected by european law in all member states. the implementation of the single market has enabled and continues to enable the process to be steadily improved. that is why i believe that european citizens should be increasingly involved in decision-making, and the european year of citizens in 2013 will be a good opportunity for them to have their say on their wishes and dreams.
in writing. in october, 20 years after the single market was established, the commission adopted the single market act ii - 'together for new growth'. the document focuses on developing fully integrated networks within the single market, promoting the cross-border mobility of citizens and businesses, supporting the digital economy across europe and strengthening social entrepreneurship, cohesion and consumer confidence. the single market in transport, energy and communications requires the elimination of disparities between the transport, energy and communications infrastructures of the states that joined the eu on 1 may 2004 and those of the other member states. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the right to vote and stand as a candidate in elections to the european parliament. finally, one of the medium-term objectives of the european union and the member states should be to shift towards a computerised public administration, particularly in terms of its cross-border dimension. the implementation of e-procurement across the eu could generate savings of at least €100 billion per year for public finances. support the completion of the framework for the modernisation of eu public procurement rules by imposing electronic invoicing as the standard invoicing method in public procurement.
erasmus is a flagship programme of the european union. after the free movement of people and goods, erasmus is considered one of the european union's great achievements. parliament therefore supports increasing union support for education and training in the period 2014-2020 in order to raise the level of skills of citizens and to help tackle high levels of youth unemployment in several member states. given the importance of education for the future of the union, we are not only calling for an increase in the budget of the erasmus programme in the next financial period, but also for the following: the inclusion of the increase in the number of people over 35 years of age benefiting from lifelong learning among the general objectives of the programme, the inclusion also of the mobility of people for educational purposes in the field of entrepreneurship, therefore that erasmus programme for young entrepreneurs, and the inclusion among the european union policies relevant to the erasmus for all programme, of the european union industrial policy.
in writing. erasmus is one of the most successful programmes of the european union. it offers significant educational benefits to students, giving them the chance to travel and to come into contact with other cultures. unfortunately, the lack of funding from the union budget risks affecting the programme. more than 1 500 foreign students arrive in romania each year, and another 4 500 young romanians study in eu countries with the help of erasmus grants. the large number of students confirms the success of the programme, further proof that we need sufficient funds for vital union policies. we cannot sacrifice education policies when one of the union's main problems is high youth unemployment. we need to encourage education and vocational training programmes to prepare young people for the labour market. the european people's youth therefore sent a letter to the heads of state and government attending the epp congress in bucharest, asking for their support for the amended budget proposal that the commission will present. the letter calls for the release of funds necessary to enable the beneficiaries to continue projects in various fields. the letter demonstrates the epp's commitment to the proper funding of the most important european policies.
in writing. erasmus is part of the community lifelong learning programme and comprises actions for european cooperation in higher education. erasmus currently provides mobility grants for thousands of students, with a focus on ensuring academic recognition of the studies undertaken. in this context, it is worth noting that in october 2009 the european commission celebrated the reaching of 2 000 000 erasmus students at european level. the erasmus experience remains a unique intercultural, academic and personal experience, not only for those who have participated in the programme, but also for those who are motivated to join. the issue of financing remains a key one, especially in times of economic crisis. the european union should make efforts to secure the necessary funds for the erasmus programme to continue in the period 2014-2020. there is a need to introduce 'social criteria' in the award of erasmus grants, allowing students with low incomes to benefit from mobility periods without fear of lack of sufficient financial resources. europe is young and needs young people with skills. to do this, we need to invest in education so that young people can benefit from jobs that match their skills.
the erasmus programme helps to improve the skills of young people and makes it easier for them to find a job. we must not risk this investment in future generations! i urgently appeal to the commission and the member states who have asked for 5 million euros less and who should be covering these gaps with funds that have not been accessed! this budget cut will only increase inequalities between young people and the erasmus programme will become a privilege for students with better financial situation, instead of a right for everyone! i would also like to propose an extension of this program. an initiative that could function as a mechanism to promote the erasmus brand outside europe. such a move would not only improve cooperation with countries such as the us, japan, australia and new zealand, but funds would no longer be limited to the european area. the erasmus programme is in danger and we should not play with the future of young people!
in writing. i welcome the firm position taken by the european parliament (tuesday) and the european commission (wednesday) in favour of the continuation of the erasmus programme, while also standing up for the values which underpin it. erasmus has enabled 2.5 million european students to travel, study in another country, and experience another european culture in the 25 years since it was launched. these included 35,000 romanian students since 2000. i will allow a comparison with another european programme, which is of the same age and has had a similar evolution: the european food aid programme, also established in 1987. this programme, which currently benefits 18 million citizens, or more than one in thirty europeans, has been in jeopardy for the past few years. i congratulate the european commission on its recent initiative to create a fund for the assistance of disadvantaged people in the european union for the period 2014-2020, which will replace the food aid programme. the two programmes, erasmus and food aid, now a quarter of a century old, are two european programmes par excellence which must continue and develop.
in writing. other we are aware of the current difficult economic situation in the member states of the european union (eu), but i feel it is unworthy that the erasmus programme or cohesion fund support for poorer regions is jeopardised by funding problems. one of the milestones in the eu's success story is the erasmus programme, which requires some €90 million to continue its tradition. it is a great opportunity for the beneficiaries to gain a unique experience. in the community budget, the use of this amount is also justified because it is one of the community projects that makes the benefits of the union tangible and makes the citizens feel the concrete benefits of the eu. erasmus is essentially the implementation of european values, like the euro or the schengen area, the free movement of people across borders. it is interesting that, in addition to the euro-related concerns, some member states are also pushing for reform of the schengen area, i.e. tightening the conditions for free movement of persons, just when erasmus funding is in danger. let's face it, it's a small sum compared to the common budget or the european debt crisis. it is unacceptable to jeopardise the most popular eu-related initiatives by restricting them, thus undermining the professional prospects of the next generation and fuelling euroscepticism among young people.
mr president, i support the agreement between parliament and the commission. the single market was formed to increase the flow of commerce between member states, without barriers. today, unfortunately, that is not the reality. we need to assure our citizens that they benefit from eu membership and that they all belong to the same community. to make that a reality, we must further deepen the single market, thus increasing competition, economic growth and job creation, and making available more money to increase social benefits. we must accomplish this, but how do we do it? we must promote harmonisation; we must create a single rail system, for example; we must introduce standardised rules for small and medium businesses. we need less regulation and clearer regulation. harmonisation is vital for the single market and for our citizens.
i voted in favour of this report because strengthening the single market is a key element in the recovery of growth and employment. to this end, i believe that existing obstacles, such as free movement in the single market, must be removed as soon as possible. this will enable citizens to enjoy all their rights to the full. romanian citizens still face restrictions, but they are not justified and should be removed. in the context of the economic crisis, it is all the more important to address the identified gaps and barriers. this will help us to innovate, grow, be competitive and build confidence in the single market. i would like to stress the importance of better governance, with improved cooperation as the main objective. moreover, i believe that the economic and social well-being of the citizens of the union must be at the heart of the approach.
in the context of the current global financial crisis, it is important to remember that the european union must also play its part in the changing global economic competition. some say the 21st century will be the century of asia, let alone china. among the emerging countries, the asean member states - singapore, malaysia, vietnam, indonesia - will have the capacity to achieve amazing economic performance. in this context, we must do everything we can to ensure that the eu develops its trade relations with the region, especially with those states that are already well-functioning market economies. one of these steps is the proposed free trade agreement with japan, which, based on the experience of a similar agreement with south korea, could have a significant trade-enhancing effect and thus bring benefits to both parties. we know that the elimination of customs duties and charges which stand in the way of free trade is not the most difficult task, nor is the removal of non-tariff barriers the key to achieving genuine free trade. europe needs to pay more attention to east asia, as there is still a lot of potential in trade with the region.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the conclusion of the stabilisation and association agreement between the european union and serbia marked a historic moment in the relationship between the two parties. the granting of candidate status to serbia this year was also another step forward in its approach to the union. i believe that by adopting these additional procedures for the application of the stabilisation and association agreement and the interim agreement, we will be able to stimulate trade with serbia in the agricultural and fisheries sectors. the union will also be able to ensure that serbia respects the conditions of competition when it introduces products to the european market. last but not least, these procedures will stimulate serbia to advance reforms in other key areas with a view to deepening cooperation with the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this regulation which will enable the european commission to ensure the correct application of the interim agreement between serbia and the european union and thus the functioning of the trade provisions, which are so important for consolidating a stable and prosperous society in serbia and for leading this country on the road to accession to the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on certain procedures for implementing the stabilisation and association agreement (saa) between the eu and the republic of serbia and for implementing the interim agreement between the ec and the republic of serbia. the saa and the interim agreement provide that certain agricultural and fishery products originating in serbia may be imported into the union at reduced customs duties within the limits of tariff quotas. it is therefore necessary to lay down rules governing the management and review of these tariff quotas in order to allow for their detailed assessment. it is appropriate to use the consultation procedure for the adoption of measures immediately applicable in exceptional and serious circumstances, given the effects of such measures and their sequential logic in relation to the adoption of definitive measures. where a delay in the imposition of measures would cause damage which would be difficult to remedy, the commission services should be empowered to adopt provisional measures with immediate effect. in order to ensure the correct and harmonious application of the interim agreement, the commission proposes an implementing regulation laying down the rules and procedures for the adoption of detailed rules for the implementation of certain provisions of these agreements.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the standards applied by the european union when it comes to seed control must also be respected by third countries exporting these products to the union. the production of these seeds should also be carried out in compliance with all the safety standards imposed by the union. only in this way can we ensure that there will be no risk to human or animal health. it is important to know whether the seed marketed in the union, including seed which is not definitively certified, has been chemically treated or the variety has been genetically modified. last but not least, detailed rules on the exact particulars to be mentioned on the label of certified seeds imported into the european union will have to be maintained.
in writing. − i agree with the rapporteur that parliament should accept the commission proposal in its current form, given the importance of continuing the seed import regime.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of council decision 2003/17/ec extending its period of application and updating the names of third countries and authorities responsible for authorising and controlling production. council decision 2003/17/ec lays down the list of countries recognised for the purpose of applying the principle of equivalence for the import of seeds, fodder plants, cereal seed, beet seed and seed of oil and fibre plants from third countries. the decision lays down the detailed requirements to be met, in particular for limiting the period of recognition of equivalence to five years, which may be extended if all relevant requirements are met. i consider that in order to ensure the supply of the eu market with the required seed, these rules should be extended by extending the deadline until 31 december 2022, even if the temporary extension currently provided for is only for five years. annex i to decision 2003/17/ec lists the countries to which the equivalence system applies. croatia already benefits from the equivalence regime and serbia should be mentioned as a participating member of the oecd seed certification system for varieties for international trade and as a member of the international seed testing association (ista) for sampling and seed testing.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that more attention should be paid to good management of fisheries areas and resources. i also support the rapporteur's position on the extension of coastal zones. i think it is extremely important that the reform allows member states to take more management decisions. they could thus cooperate on a regional basis. at the same time, i think the reform that's being proposed should be towards a decentralized regime that focuses on doing these things. with the 12 miles of coastline having worked well so far, the expansion is welcome. we need a reform of the common fisheries policy to make it work to its full potential.
in writing. − fishing continues to be essential for many local economies in the european union. despite the modest overall contribution of fisheries to the economies of the member states (less than 1% in most cases), many local communities depend on the income of more than 300 000 full-time or part-time fishermen working in the union. in addition, we must take into account the related industries of the fisheries sector, which employ several hundred thousand people. yet, it must be remembered that this activity can continue only if there are enough fish. for these reasons, i believe that a policy on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources is necessary.
in writing. − i agree with the rapporteur's position to accept the current proposal to extend the regime for two years, while also continuing the proposal to extend national control over coastal fishing areas as part of the wider cfp reform package.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report and support those scientifically based measures which are genuinely necessary for the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources. such measures are needed in the black sea, which has been exposed to continuous deterioration in the quality of coastal waters and exploitation pressure for the past 30 years. as a result, marine living resources have declined dramatically, leading in some cases to depletion of stocks of exploitable organisms. the annual catch was over 15 000 tonnes in the mid-1980s, but in 2008 it was barely 500 tonnes. today, only 5 of the 26 commercial fish species are exploited in the black sea. several species of sturgeon are threatened with extinction, as are dolphins, sharks, and seahorses. the seal, several species of shrimp and clams, dozens of plant and animal species have already disappeared from the black sea. i therefore support the conservation of fisheries resources, such as those included in this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources under the common fisheries policy (cfp). within the framework of existing cfp legislation, article 17 (2) of council regulation (ec) no 2371/2002 provides for a derogation from the principle of equal access for the area less than 12 nautical miles from the coast of each member state. the derogation shall apply from 1 january 2003 until 31 december 2012. the current proposal aims to extend this period until 31 december 2014. the management of the fishing grounds 12 miles offshore has been a success. this demonstrates that member states can manage the fishing areas. the effective and stable management by each member state within the limits of coastal zones is welcomed. in general, the effectiveness of member states' control in areas up to 12 miles from the coast demonstrates that management according to the local situation works best. we welcome the current proposal to extend the regime for two years, while continuing to campaign for the extension of national control over coastal fishing areas as part of the wider cfp reform package.
in writing. − the european union has developed precisely because of the widespread acceptance and adoption of the principles of free trade. at the same time, consumer protection is equally important by maintaining a high level of transparency as to the origin of agricultural and food products. the analysis of this agreement must start from the need to reconcile these two imperatives. i support the approval of the agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova on the protection of geographical indications of agricultural products and foodstuffs, not only because it complies with the formalities required by community law, but also because it represents a major opportunity for the republic of moldova to move closer to the european union by intensifying economic exchanges. i also believe that the conclusion of this agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova will make a decisive contribution both to the successful development of the union's initiatives in this part of europe, such as the eastern partnership, and to the establishment of the necessary climate of cooperation and mutual trust.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that there is a need for improvement in the conditions under which bilateral trade between the european union and the republic of moldova takes place. they should promote the quality of food products and, at the same time, stimulate the value of sustainable rural development. i would like to stress that the interests of the union are well protected under this agreement. at the same time, given that the republic of moldova is one of the most important eastern partners of the union, which is to conclude a deep and comprehensive free trade agreement in the framework of the association agreement with the european union, i believe that this agreement should be supported in order to improve and strengthen trade relations between the two parties.
in writing. − the european union is an important economic partner of the republic of moldova. this refers to various aspects of economic activity: foreign trade, foreign investment and remittances. the share of agri-food products in exports to the eu is much lower than in the total exports of the republic of moldova. this is due to the non-compliance of the product category with the existing technical standards in the eu. in order to address this, the republic of moldova has started the process of aligning with eu regulatory technical standards. i welcome the existence of the agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova on the protection of geographical indications of agricultural products and foodstuffs, as it will contribute to improving the conditions of bilateral trade, promoting quality along the food chain and stimulating sustainable rural development.
in writing. − this agreement is the result of bilateral negotiations concluded on 18 april 2011 aimed at addressing the potential misuse of eu geographical indications at source and at protecting geographical indications of the republic of moldova. i voted in favour of the eu-moldova agreement on the protection of geographical indications as it will benefit producers and traders in the republic of moldova and the eu and improve the conditions of bilateral trade by ensuring quality along the food chain, thus stimulating sustainable rural development.
in writing. − i consider that this report is of the opinion that the eu's interests are well protected under the agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova, which aims at the mutual protection of geographical indications, with the aim of improving the conditions of bilateral trade and promoting quality along the food chain.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the protection of geographical indications of agricultural products and foodstuffs. this agreement was signed to provide a suitable framework for the political dialogue between the eu and the republic of moldova. the main goal of the agreement is to promote trade, investment and harmonious economic relations between the parties and also to encourage their sustainable economic development. moreover, it is very important to underline that this agreement will provide a basis for legislative, economic, social, financial and cultural cooperation, and it will support the efforts that the republic of moldova is making to consolidate its democracy.
in writing. − geographical indications of agricultural products and foodstuffs have started to be protected in the european union to prevent misuse, imitation of the products concerned or false indications of origin, thus ensuring a higher quality of products offered to consumers. the purpose of registering names is also to help producers to obtain higher revenues through the added value that this identification brings. since 1992, a system of registration of these intellectual property rights has been established at european level, and protection of these rights is also provided at international level, albeit less effectively. in its relations with third countries, the union shall apply the same standards for the mutual protection of geographical indications. this is also the case with the agreement with moldova, which will improve the conditions for bilateral trade. it should be noted that for products from third countries there is an additional condition to community products, namely that the names must be protected in the state of origin at the time of application for community protection. this agreement with the eu gives the republic of moldova the possibility to extend and protect its current geographical indications throughout the union, with a view to the deep and comprehensive free trade agreement within the association agreement.
in writing. − i welcome the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova on the protection of geographical indications of agricultural products and foodstuffs, for which i was rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on agriculture and rural development. the mutual protection of geographical indications is essential to improve the conditions of bilateral trade and will bring significant benefits to eu and moldovan producers and traders. the romanian producers have welcomed the conclusion of similar agreements with other countries and are also looking forward to the conclusion of an agreement with the united states of america, the union's most important trading partner.
in writing. − i supported this agreement to increase the protection of geographical indications of foodstuffs. more and more products are having their geographical indication recognised, and this protects the unique characteristics of local, traditional food produce, brings income to traditional food-producing regions and helps to preserve our rich culinary diversity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova on the protection of geographical indications of agricultural products and foodstuffs. the european union and the republic of moldova shall pursue the mutual protection of geographical indications with a view to improving the conditions of bilateral trade, promoting quality along the food chain and stimulating sustainable rural development. the agreement gives the european union the possibility to intervene at the source of potential misuses of eu geographical indications. moldova is the next eu eastern partner to conclude a deep and comprehensive free trade agreement under the association agreement with the european union. i believe that this agreement opens the way to closer trade relations between the eu and moldova. the proposed agreement has no implications for the eu budget.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because hunger and food insecurity are still major international problems. although we are in the year 2012, more than 13 percent of the world's population does not have sufficient access to safe food. despite technological advances and economic growth in many countries, this problem has not been eradicated. moreover, over 60% of those affected by hunger are women, confirming the vulnerability of certain groups to this phenomenon. the conclusion by the european union of the food assistance convention will enable it to continue promoting its humanitarian aid policies internationally. i believe that the eu's efforts will be better targeted and integrated into a global strategy to eradicate hunger.
in writing. − hunger and food insecurity remain major global problems, despite efforts and progress on some fronts. in 2010, about 925 million people, or 13.6% of the world's population, did not have enough to eat, 98% of the undernourished live in developing countries, and 60% of them are women. the food assistance convention 2012 aims at improving food assistance policy, requiring: a shift from a product-based approach to a more diverse, needs-based and locally adapted mix of instruments; long-term solutions through activities facilitating the transition from aid to rehabilitation or recovery programmes; donor coordination and mutual training around food assistance policy and practice. the european union will thus have to ensure that a food aid policy is established that is as effective as possible and that meets the food and nutrition needs of the most vulnerable populations on the basis of objectively identified needs. a mechanism should also be developed at european level to enable the active involvement of representatives of countries affected by emergencies as a means of increasing the legitimacy of the food assistance convention.
in writing. − today, hunger and food insecurity remain global challenges. while there has been considerable progress on some fronts over the past decade, progress on hunger and malnutrition has remained consistently low. i therefore believe that there is still a clear need for a legally binding international framework defining and providing for commitments and instruments for the provision of food assistance to developing countries.
in writing. the rapporteur stated before the vote that 15 000 people worldwide would die of starvation today alone. the eu has a duty to take the world's poor into account in the policies it implements. the eu must also think of its own poor, which is why i welcome the commission's initiative to create a fund to help the most deprived people in the european union for the period 2014-2020. let us never forget that almost 9% of europeans cannot afford a meal containing meat or fish every other day - a basic need according to the world health organisation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the conclusion on behalf of the eu of the food assistance convention (fac 2012). according to recent statistics, in 2010, some 925 million people, or 13.6 percent of the world's population, did not have enough to eat. 89 percent of the undernourished live in developing countries, and 60 percent of these are women. malnutrition is the root cause of more than a third of all child deaths, with an estimated 2.6 million deaths per year. i believe that fac 2012 will enable the eu to ensure the establishment of a food assistance policy of maximum efficiency, which will respond to the food and nutrition needs of the most vulnerable populations, based on objectively identified needs. however, it is important to prepare the ground in advance for long-term solutions through activities that facilitate the transition from aid to rehabilitation or recovery programmes, inter alia, by strengthening local production and livelihoods, thus avoiding long-term aid dependency. the 2012 fac is fully in line with the eu's ongoing efforts to contribute to poverty reduction and the eradication of hunger worldwide, under the millennium development goals.
in writing. − citizenship of the european union confers on citizens whose member state is not represented by an embassy or consulate in a third country the right to obtain protection from the diplomatic or consular authorities of any member state of the union, under the same conditions as nationals of that state, which is undoubtedly one of the clearest expressions of the union's solidarity and identity. in order to ensure that this right is not illusory and that citizens can enjoy the practical benefits of union citizenship, it has been necessary at european union level to clarify the content and manner of the effective exercise of this right and to simplify cooperation and coordination between consular and diplomatic authorities. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal and mrs bauer's report, which remove the existing obstacles when it comes to the diplomatic or consular assistance that citizens are entitled to receive when they need protection, in cases where they are outside their country of origin. i consider that the way in which the accessibility of the embassy or consulate has been defined is appropriate for assessing whether a citizen is represented or not in a third country, as it facilitates the resolution of emergency situations without delay.
in writing. - i voted for this report because i believe that solidarity between member states must be supported. the treaty of lisbon has made it possible for any citizen of the union to enjoy, in the territory of a third country in which his member state is not represented, the protection of the diplomatic or consular authorities of any member state. this is all the more important as there are many member states that do not have a very well developed network of embassies and consulates, which may expose citizens to certain risks. the directive creates a framework for every european citizen to enjoy the fullest possible diplomatic and consular protection in any country. i think that's another reason to strengthen our sense of belonging to the union.
in writing. − the right of a national of an unrepresented member state to request assistance from the consular authorities of other represented member states is one of the rights conferred by citizenship of the union. in order to facilitate access to consular protection for eu citizens in third countries, it is necessary to strengthen the existing legal framework. in this regard, the council directive on the consular protection of union citizens abroad should extend the role of eu delegations in the exercise of consular protection and clarify the coordination and cooperation measures necessary for the day-to-day consular protection of unrepresented eu citizens. in addition, the commission should ensure that information on consular protection is made available to the widest possible public, in order to clarify that citizens should continue to benefit from the full range of consular assistance provided by member states' representations. member states should consider establishing a 'consular protection trust fund' from which the embassy or consulate of the assisting member state can advance the costs of assistance to an unrepresented national and the member state of the unrepresented national who has received assistance is to reimburse the financial advance.
in writing. - we all know that the right of a citizen of an unrepresented member state to request assistance from the consular authorities of other represented member states is one of the rights conferred by citizenship of the union. i therefore consider that one of the major problems is that citizens are not informed that they have the right to obtain assistance from the consulate of another member state if they are in a third country where their state is not represented. this new directive must also address this issue.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on consular protection for citizens of the union abroad because according to the lisbon treaty the solidarity among member states shall be sustained, therefore in everyday cases of consular protection, such as loss of identity documents, arrest, detention or death, an unrepresented citizen has the right to request the help of any diplomatic or consular authority of any member state. it has been noticed that one of the major problems for european citizens is that they have not been aware of their right to obtain help from the consulates of another member state when they are in a third country in which their own member state is not represented. for this reason i believe that we should raise awareness, to reduce citizens’ lack of knowledge of their rights, but we should also clarify that they should continue to benefit from the full range of consular assistance customarily provided by member states’ representations, and make clear that the role played by the authorities of represented member states does not mean that unrepresented member states are excluded from providing assistance.
in writing. − our first priority as representatives of the citizens of the european union is to protect them both within the eu's borders and outside the member states; this is why this measure is more than salutary. critical situations faced by citizens who are not represented by embassies or consulates in third countries can now be solved much more easily through consular cooperation at local level, which increases trust in community policies and, above all, citizens' sense of belonging to the european union project. i believe, however, that in future we must pay special attention to people with disabilities and to the treatment of critical situations in which they may be, through special consular assistance and protection adapted to their specific needs, in accordance with eu policies applicable within the member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report and stress the importance of enhanced consular protection for union citizens abroad, especially in view of a recent event in indonesia. in this country, four european citizens from my constituency were arrested for christian religious propaganda and their rights were not protected, which caused their families great concern.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a directive on consular protection of union citizens abroad. eu citizens travelling to or residing in a third country where the member state of which they are nationals is not represented at consular or embassy level are entitled to consular protection by the consular authorities of any other member state. the proposal for a directive lays down the cooperation and coordination measures necessary to facilitate the protection of union citizens in the territory of a third country where the member state whose nationals they are is not represented by the diplomatic or consular authorities of another member state under the same conditions as those enjoyed by nationals of that member state. the member state concerned is obliged to provide assistance to unrepresented eu citizens under the same conditions as its own nationals. recent crises have affected many eu citizens, for example in libya, egypt and bahrain after the democratic uprisings in spring 2011 or in japan after the earthquake in march 2011. and in everyday situations, such as serious illness or when a citizen is the victim of a crime, consular protection is often indispensable.
in writing. − in the current economic context, the ini report on 20 main concerns of european citizens and businesses with the functioning of the single market supports the process of relaunching the single market and of consolidating and making it work. the internal market is a real solution to overcome the current financial crisis and to economic development. the engine of the internal market is smes, whether we are talking about job creation or economic growth, and this report pays particular attention to them. among the problems highlighted in this report are the recognition of professional qualifications, social security, tax obstacles, access to finance, online shopping, transferability of pension rights, etc. solving these problems is essential to enable europeans to fully enjoy their right to free movement and the benefits of eu membership, and to increase their confidence in the single market.
in writing. - i voted for this report because i believe that we need a relaunch of the single market, through which we can restore the confidence of european citizens and consumers in the european project. we must therefore avoid the fragmentation caused by the protectionist tendencies of certain member states. the right to free movement, one of the fundamental freedoms of the single market, must be guaranteed within the european union. the lifting of restrictions on employment for romanian and bulgarian nationals would only bring benefits in the current context of economic crisis, where the mobility of workers should be encouraged, not inhibited.
in writing. − i believe that citizens' awareness of taxation in the european union urgently needs to be improved and the tax barriers faced by crossborder workers and employers must be reduced, in order to facilitate their mobility and to promote crossborder economic initiatives, while countering any possibility of tax evasion or fraud.
in writing. − in achieving the europe 2020 goals of sustainable and inclusive growth, we must focus all our efforts on ensuring the functioning of the single market as a key element in winning the full trust of citizens and their sense of belonging to the european union project. in the context of current technological developments, however, i believe that the consolidation of the european digital single market, in which the internet plays a key role, is an extremely important aspect. however, the present proposal makes very little mention of the european digital single market, which is why i believe that in the future we must urgently regulate it in a uniform way, which will bring significant benefits to both citizens and businesses, facilitating access to new markets and opportunities for economic growth.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the main concerns of european citizens and businesses with the functioning of the single market as it is a key element for achieving the objectives of sustainable growth, job creation and social inclusion. freedom of movement is a fundamental right which workers must be able to exercise without discrimination on grounds of nationality between workers in the member states as regards employment, remuneration and other conditions of work and employment. i support supporting the eures system and its effective interconnection with national traineeship systems as one of the ways to combat unemployment in the eu. it is also important to strengthen consumer confidence and security by ensuring the protection of consumers' personal data, the security of digital signatures, improving dispute resolution mechanisms and increasing trust in the security of the means of payment used, in order to create a genuine european digital single market. the commission, together with the member states, regional and local authorities and civil society representatives, should launch regular european information campaigns, strengthening the dialogue with citizens on the benefits of the single market, and on citizens' rights and responsibilities.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the anti-dumping duty is a particularly important one. i consider that it is necessary to clarify the decision to limit the investigation to a reasonable number of producers using samples. in addition, there is a need for clarification as regards the anti-dumping duty applied to imports from producers not included in the investigation. i would point out that the amendments sought must be implemented as soon as possible and must cover all categories of investigations, both new and ongoing. furthermore, i believe that the three-month time limit for determination cannot be used in many of the anti-dumping proceedings. that's why i'm advocating for his removal. the amendment of the regulation plays an important role in ensuring legal certainty.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal to amend regulation no 1225/2009 on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community. amendment of regulation no 1225/2009 is necessary in the interests of legal certainty and the principle of sound administration in the light of the judgment of the european court of justice of 2 february 2012 in case c-249/101 p brosmann and others v council. the court of justice has ruled that the sampling technique set out in article 17 of regulation no 1225/2009 cannot be applied for the purpose of establishing met claims made in accordance with article 2 (7) (c). the court found that the cooperating non-sampled producers are entitled to their claim for met, regardless of whether an individual dumping margin was to be calculated for the non-sampled companies. the court also emphasised that the determination referred to in article 2 (7) (c) must be made within three months of the initiation of the investigation.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on eu trade negotiations with japan as the eu and japan together account for over a third of world gdp and over 20% of world trade. japan's ability to remove non-tariff barriers and market access obstacles in public procurement is a precondition for the opening of negotiations on the eu-japan free trade agreement (fta). we stress that the free trade agreement must be comprehensive, ambitious and fully binding in all its trade provisions, as it must lead to a real opening up of the market. for an fta to be truly beneficial for the eu economy, the council should set a clear timetable and include the following in the negotiating directives drawn up by the commission: significant concessions on public procurement, guaranteeing market access for european companies in strategic japanese sectors, including railways and urban transport, as well as the same degree of openness as eu public procurement markets, removing barriers to market access for european smes. in addition, in the context of the march 2011 disaster, attention should be paid to energy cooperation and increased access to markets for environmental goods and services.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that one of the main objectives of the european union in terms of development assistance is the eradication of poverty and hunger in the world. but achieving these goals requires better coordination between eu policies in this area. the synergy between trade, agriculture, migration and security policies must be maximised for development policies to deliver optimum returns. as the world's leading donor of assistance, the european union must ensure that this assistance is directed and used in the most effective way. i believe that this is why we must also create stronger mechanisms to monitor the way in which the aid that the european union is distributing is used.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it presents a comprehensive approach to european development. the report provides the framework for positive, sustainable growth through cooperation and transparency in a variety of fields. the united nations has presented the goal of 0.7% of gni going toward development assistance. this report urges accountability within all structures. development projects and goals must be shared between member countries. eu nations must support each other as we move forward toward better infrastructure and sustainability. fishing and farming must be ecologically sustainable in order to ensure future growth. nations must also observe basic human rights by providing core labour standards and protection for migrants. within the eu, we must strive to meet this goal. by creating accountable and sustainable policies we will be able both to increase funding and to ensure that eu funds are used efficiently in development projects. democratic assessment and oversight are crucial to the success of future development.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the eu's 2011 report on policy coherence for development. the resolution calls for development policies to be based on: recognition of the right of a country or region to define democratically its own policies, priorities and strategies to protect the livelihoods of its people, in accordance with the un international covenant on economic, social and cultural rights. i support the commission's commitment to support small producers and promote fair, green and ethical trade initiatives. i believe that small farms are particularly important in fighting hunger and that adaptation measures are high on the food security agenda. support for women smallholders is also particularly important and should be increased. i voted to develop an integrated approach to food and to establish a dedicated trust fund to address malnutrition in developing countries and to mobilize the resources needed to carry out the basic interventions that could prevent the vast majority of malnutrition. in this respect, it is essential to intervene in particular during the critical period of 1 000 days from conception to the age of 2 years.

measures for the banking sector, so that we have transparency, accountability and security for investors and savers throughout the financial markets, leaving no room for regulatory arbitrage, within start the trilogue discussions very soon. we share the same objectives on the mifid directive on a number of issues, and the report you have prepared, mr markus ferber, reinforces and consolidates our own proposals. firstly, as regards the structure of the market, commission and parliament, we want all forms of negotiation, whether multilateral or bilateral, to take place in a transparent environment. parliament has opted to introduce a definition of the over-the-counter market, coupled with an obligation to trade on transparent execution platforms for small-scale transactions. i'm willing to investigate this lead; however, the possible removal of the otf (organised trading facility) category for the equity market must be analysed very carefully. we must also weigh the consequences of such amendments against our own proposal. if we limit multilateral trading to the regulated markets and the so-called mtfs, we will be abandoning the current situation, which allows high-frequency traders to cross-order with investors on certain platforms, without the latter having a say. we must therefore think carefully before limiting the scope of the tfo in this way. secondly, high-frequency trading. if we want to encourage the migration of transactions to multilateral and transparent trading platforms, then, yes, we need to better regulate high-frequency trading, which is precisely on its preferred terrain when it comes to these platforms. again, i think i can say that we share the same goals. in general, this text is an opportunity to set the rules on high frequency trading straight. i am prepared to acknowledge - i have said this before - that there is some use for high frequency trading to provide liquidity but it is undeniably, at the same time, a source of systematic risk to the markets. in the banking sector, we have made a vigorous effort to monitor and reduce this type of risk. we cannot and must not be less ambitious in the field of markets. that is why the commission has proposed a set of specific rules to guide and hold these actors to account. they will now have to be licensed and supervised by the competent authorities. they will also have to commit to providing liquidity to the markets. i sincerely thank your rapporteur, markus ferber, for proposing to maintain these points and i would also like to remind you that the commission is continuing to vigorously take this debate beyond the european union, in international fora, so that we can achieve a level playing field in regulation, achieve high common standards. thirdly, the commodity derivatives markets. these markets are not financial markets like any other, since their proper functioning involves the daily lives of all consumers and, as we know, in some developing countries, involves the food security of a large part of the population. i think that speculation on raw materials and the consequences that this speculation may have on the food security of a number of countries is absolutely unacceptable. i would like to make it very clear that i support your proposals which are both to strengthen your position limits regime while preserving the possibility for commercial firms to use these markets when it really comes to hedging. fourthly, the introduction of a european system for the provision of services by firms from third countries. i am glad that our proposal has been supported by parliament. i believe that this system is the best way to ensure effective regulation of international markets and to avoid any risk of regulatory arbitrage, as i said at the beginning of my speech. this is very important in the context of regulatory convergence both at the g20 level and also at the financial stability board. ladies and gentlemen, this important debate gives me the opportunity to raise two or three other subjects by telegraph on which we should also maintain our high level of regulatory requirements. firstly, the transparency of the negotiations. we must be firm and not take the risk of giving certain actors the opportunity to continue negotiating in complete opacity by means of specific provisions. the level of transparency should be the same regardless of the technology used, regardless of the type of investor, whether retail or professional. the second area of vigilance is the protection of investors. we want, we must move towards legislation that improves investment conditions by clarifying the role and financial interests of each party. for this reason, i do not think that simply disclosing the fees of intermediaries would ensure an adequate level of investor protection or an adequate level of independence. the proposal we made to prohibit the charging of fees for independent advice and portfolio management seems to me to guarantee greater security and independence. these are the only ways to attract sound investors and sound investment. we must also maintain our demands as regards the range of instruments which can be considered as not being complex. too much of it would increase the risk that inappropriate products would then be sold to investors. the last point is non-discriminatory access. i am convinced that creating the conditions for healthy competition in the postmarket is necessary to create a genuine single market in financial markets and to prevent excessive concentration of risk in monopolistic market infrastructures. that is what i wanted to say very frankly, ladies and gentlemen, in the dialogue that is going on between us. i was moved by what markus ferber said. i confirm to him my own and my teams' readiness to continue working and to succeed as quickly as possible in concluding, on an ambitious, rigorous and demanding basis, this major piece of legislation, the mifid directive. we must find the right balance together to win the confidence of investors and i believe we can work together to achieve this.

in writing. the european union has always taken on the regional dimension of its initiatives. the whole process of european integration can be seen to some extent as an expression of regional awareness problems and benefits which, because of their geographical proximity, cannot be the subject of action by states alone. it is all the more important that the danube region, one of the historical points of development of european civilization and economy, develop its potential and become a main axis of the european union once again. the development by the european union of a multi-field strategy for this region is important not only from the perspective of the complex areas addressed environment, transport, economy or governance. the european strategy for the danube region has a major role to play, because it is a true test of the institutional capacity and direct benefits of the integration project. what most countries in the region want is not necessarily the contribution of material, human or financial resources, but a real transfer of expertise and experience. protecting the environment, developing a more interconnected public transport system or building an integrated and efficient system of environmental protection requires, first of all, institutional strengthening of the cooperation process, together with the extension of good practices in the areas concerned.
the danube and its tributaries form one of the most important water systems in europe. the danube river has played a crucial role in the political, socioeconomic and cultural development of central and south-eastern europe. it is the world's most international watershed, covering 817,000 km2, one third of europe and crossing 18 countries. the danube is of paramount importance for europe's biodiversity. more than 5,200 species of flora and fauna are found in the danube delta. however, the river and its life have suffered considerable losses, especially in the last century. today, the danube basin covers only 20% of the original water surface, of which only half is still naturally occurring. many areas are polluted, and faulty sewage systems and construction have increased the risk of flooding and compounded the problems caused by pollution. in view of the above, i believe that a european union strategy for the danube region is necessary.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, firstly i would like to say that the european commission agrees with many points of the present european parliament’s draft resolution on russia’s accession to the wto. although the wto accession process of russia was long, the results are impressive. our exporters will now find it easier to access russian markets. reductions in customs duties will mean savings of eur 2.5 billion a year. our services industries will also have easier access – particularly in finance, telecommunications and retail. moving goods across the border will be eased with the new rules on customs valuation, fees and transit procedures. russian export duties on many raw materials have been capped and will be reduced for key inputs like wood, and we will have a more predictable regulatory environment for our investment in russia. however, russia has taken a number of protectionist measures that cause great concern – both in terms of russia’s willingness to play by the rules of the wto and of their significant negative impact on the eu economy. for example, russia’s decision on levying so-called ‘recycling fees’ on imported vehicles is problematic, because it discriminates against european producers and infringes the most basic wto rules, and duties on cars are now higher than before russia’s wto accession. russia’s ban on live pig imports is a clear case of a regulatory measure acting as a tool of trade protection, lacking any valid scientific basis, and is disproportionate to the issues it seeks to address. we have identified a list of more than 300 products with discrepancies between the applied import duties and the agreed tariffs in the wto, and in most cases giving least-favourable treatment to eu exporters in sectors like paper, agriculture, automotive products and textiles. lastly, the preferential export duties for our wood imports from russia agreed upon prior to wto accession are still not in place. we will start by trying to find agreed solutions, failing which we will not hesitate to enforce our wto rights if they are violated. the commission takes note of the european parliament’s policy study on russia’s wto accession, which correctly concludes that membership of the wto is only a starting point for the sustained and diversified growth of the russian economy. what is needed is a thorough reform of the domestic economy and business environment. only russia can choose to pursue such a reform, but the eu is willing to help through a new framework agreement. in this context, the european commission is not asking for new market access commitments. however, there is scope to break new ground on a range of regulatory issues, and europe has one of the world’s most advanced regulatory regimes and useful experience to share. this agenda is complicated by the creation of a customs union between russia, belarus and kazakhstan. the european commission’s priority remains to develop our bilateral trade relations with russia first, as it is the only wto member among these three countries, and the political situation in belarus remains a serious matter of concern.
russia's accession to the wto at the end of eleven years of negotiations offers a new perspective on relations with the european union, which have been characterised by an asymmetry in trade. russia has thus committed itself to aligning its trade rules and practices with wto standards, in particular with regard to non-discriminatory treatment for imports of goods and services, ensuring transparency in the implementation of trade measures, reducing agricultural subsidies and improving intellectual property rights. i believe that russia's efforts in this direction are substantial and that the swift implementation of these commitments will facilitate trade with wto member states, encourage new job creation and contribute to the growth of russia's gdp. at the same time, the decision to join an international trade organization involves not only advantages but also compliance with rules agreed upon. arbitrary measures such as the ban on imports of animals from the european union should therefore be avoided in the future. it should also be borne in mind that the negotiations for a new eu-russia agreement will be centred on the wto obligations of both parties, which is a good opportunity to establish common principles and objectives in the field of trade. i support the idea of including in the new agreement a substantial and legally binding chapter on energy, with a view to ensuring a transparent and non-discriminatory energy market, and a chapter on sustainable development, through which we encourage russia to respect both human and workers' rights and international environmental standards. last but not least, member states should establish a list of common interests so that their approach in future negotiations with the russian federation is a concerted one.
i welcome russia's accession to the wto on august 22. it will facilitate investment and trade and accelerate the modernisation of russia's economy, providing business opportunities for both russian and eu companies. i consider the long-term strategic partnership between the european union and russia to be important and stress the importance of strengthening the energy partnership. the intensification of energy cooperation represents an opportunity for both sides to deepen economic and trade cooperation in an open and transparent market, taking full account of the union's need to diversify transport routes and energy suppliers. this cooperation must be based on transparency, equal access to markets, infrastructure and investment, and a legally binding framework guaranteeing the reliable and regular supply of energy to all eu member states, based on equal standards. i believe that the main objective should be an open and transparent energy market between the european union and russia. finally, russia's accession to the world trade organisation will facilitate the development of trade in the black sea region as well.
russia's accession to the world trade organisation is a good opportunity to boost relations with the european union. the wto provides the best framework for the development of trade between both parties. on the other hand, russia must work towards full wto integration and better compliance with wto rules. i am particularly concerned about russia's decision to ban imports of live animals from the european union. the measure was not taken on the basis of a detailed analysis and is in breach of wto rules. i also note that there are still barriers for european companies when it comes to awarding public procurement contracts. russia needs to show greater openness in its trade relations with the union, as strengthening trade within the wto is in the interest of both parties.
russia's accession to the wto is in its own interests, but also in the interests of the european and global economy as a whole. the world bank estimates that productivity will increase, with positive effects on gross domestic product, as russia will be able to attract new foreign investors and acquire quality technological products. the european union is russia's main economic partner, with over eur 138 billion worth of products exported to the eu, and russia's integration into the multilateral trading system and, by implication, its adherence to the rules established by it, is a step towards improving the eu-russia bilateral relationship.
i, for one, welcome russia's accession to the world trade organization after 18 years of negotiations. romanian producers, especially those of animal products, are eager to enter a market with huge consumption potential where, unfortunately, they have so far faced arbitrary and sometimes hostile measures. but there are still problems, some of which have already been raised in the debate. russia must eliminate protectionist measures, such as the ban on pig imports. last but not least, he must stop abusing his health. i would like to remind you of the attitude of russia in march when it banned imports of live animals from the european union in the wake of the schmallenberg virus crisis, even though the restriction was not in line with the standards of the international organisation for animal health. the examples could go on and on. last but not least, i would like to recall the position of this parliament, which has made it clear that we must expect our agricultural trading partners to meet exactly the same standards of quality and food safety as we expect from european farmers. i ask the commission to consider all means of action to ensure that russia's accession to the wto will bring commercial benefits to both russian and european farmers and that the relationship will not be an unbalanced one, as it has been in many other situations.
i would like to draw the attention of my colleagues, and in particular the commission, to a very serious problem which has made it impossible for a number of romanian ngos and foundations to operate in recent months. the operational programme in the human resources development sector in romania has suffered setbacks, which have led the commission to freeze the funding of the projects it has won for the duration of the investigations. of course, i am not disputing the legality of the investigations and the need to expose abuses, but i would simply like to draw attention to the unfair situation that thousands of ngos' operations have been put at risk by the romanian authorities' delay in transferring the aid awarded for months. some organisations are trying to bridge the uncertain period with bank loans, but the implementation of many socially extremely useful projects has now been called into question. we cannot allow the entire human resources development programme to fail in romania because of the bad faith of a few beneficiaries or the incompetence of some public authorities.
we are all aware of the financial difficulties - and not only - faced by european farmers as a result of adverse climatic conditions, such as extreme drought in certain regions of the union. for example, in romania, drought has destroyed almost half of the crops of cereals and technical plants this year, and this situation is seriously damaging the agricultural sector. to help alleviate these difficulties, i believe that a number of measures at european union level are urgently needed. the european union must stand in solidarity with farmers whose work has been wasted by this year's drought. national and local administrations have done all they can in this situation, but the support of the european union is essential. the european union has set up the eu solidarity fund to help people in regions affected by natural disasters such as floods. solutions must also be found for drought, given that this phenomenon has major implications for farmers and food security.
last week, in conjunction with the alde group's visit to bucharest, a debate on sme financing was organised by the alde group, which was attended by more than 100 representatives of small and mediumsized enterprises and the banking sector, together with representatives of the european institutions, including commissioner tajani, and the romanian government. it was a very important opportunity to see what the real concerns of smes are, which is very important. we have often heard that parliament and the european institutions in general are very far removed from the real concerns of small and mediumsized enterprises. i believe that both we, the members of parliament, and the commission need to have as much dialogue as possible with smes so that, at european level, we can develop policies that take their needs into account as much as possible. many smes complain about the unfavourable conditions for participation in european programmes. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, including the creation of a european network of national experts in the field of smes, and the creation of a european network of experts in the field of smes.
i call on the european commission to urgently propose a strategy to counter the disastrous effects that the increase in cereals prices will have on the european market. the drought-induced under-harvest has led to alarming shortages of wheat and corn, which has been reflected in soaring food prices. the situation is affecting consumers severely. also, throughout the european union, farmers are concerned that they will not have enough to feed their animals, which will be reflected in new prices. recently, ukraine expressed its intention to suspend its wheat exports from november 15, which caused the immediate increase in the price of wheat on the chicago stock exchange. the european commission is now talking about unnecessary tensions in international agricultural markets. these tensions are not unnecessary, they reflect a state of affairs, a bad harvest, doubled by the increase in oil prices. let's not forget that prices will remain high. food prices will hit their highest level in history in the first quarter of next year and continue to rise, fueling agribusiness inflation. the european union needs a quick strategy to overcome this situation. the commission is always asked about such a strategy and it replies that we need structural measures. of course, but we also need to find solutions in time for crises like the one we are facing.
the incompetence of romania's right-wing governments over the past two years has led to financial corrections and the recent suspension of most of three programmes co-financed by the european union's structural funds. for the period 2010-2011, the commission identified serious weaknesses in the management and control system of the operational programmes 'transport', 'regional' and 'increasing economic competitiveness'. in order to ensure that this suspension does not lead to a reduction in the amounts that romania can absorb in this financial period, the romanian government has two months to remedy the deficiencies reported. i ask the european commission to be fully available and to cooperate with the romanian government in order to remedy the shortcomings and to be able to resume the co-financing from european funds of projects that can contribute to the economic and social development of romania and that romanians so greatly need.

in writing. − i voted for the legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the signing and conclusion of the agreement between the government of the united states of america and the european union on the coordination of energy-efficiency labelling programmes for office equipment, as new applications and functions emerge. office equipment will be responsible for an increasing share of energy consumption in the future. the us-eu agreement aims to maximise energy savings and environmental benefits by stimulating the supply and demand of energy-efficient products. to this end, a common set of energy efficiency specifications and a common logo will be used to define coherent targets for manufacturers and thus optimise the impact of their individual efforts on the supply and demand of these products. according to the agreement, the common specifications should be formulated so as to cover no more than 25% of the most energy-efficient models for which data are available at the time of specification. efforts will also be made to ensure that energy-efficient products can be identified by consumers by the presence of the label on the market.
