in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the annual report on the activities of the european ombudsman in 2011. the 2011 eurobarometer on citizens' rights and the performance of the eu administration showed that citizens place a high value on their right to complain to the european ombudsman. the right to free movement and residence within the union, as well as the right to good administration, are very important to them. the main types of alleged maladministration investigated by the ombudsman in 2011 related to issues of legality (28% of inquiries), requests for information (16,2%), fairness (13,6%), reasons for decisions and possibilities of appeal (8,1%), reasonable time limits for decisions (7,3%), requests for public access to documents (7,1%), lack of discrimination (6,8%) and the obligation to reply to letters in the language of the citizens and to indicate the competent official (5,8%). the most inquiries opened by the ombudsman in 2011 concerned the commission (231), with epso in second place (42). the ombudsman publishes a brochure entitled problems with the eu? who can help you? which contains comprehensive information on the mechanisms for citizens to solve eu-related problems is an important support for european citizens.
in writing. − in a context where irresponsible behaviour such as food speculation and high frequency trading is causing poverty and increased instability in the financial system, i voted in favour of the report on financial regulation, wanting to see these types of activities eliminated.
in writing. − i voted for the amendments relating to the proposal for a directive on markets in financial instruments and repealing directive 2004/39/ec. the markets in financial instruments directive (mifid), which has been in force since november 2007, is a key pillar of the integration of financial markets in the eu. mifid establishes a regulatory framework for the provision of investment services in financial instruments by banks and investment firms and for the operation of regulated markets by operators. the document also sets out the roles and responsibilities of the national competent authorities in relation to these activities. three and a half years after entry into force, there is more intense competition between trading venues for financial instruments and a wider range of options for investors in terms of service providers and available financial instruments. these advances have been amplified by technological developments in recent years. the proposed directive amends the specific requirements for the provision of investment services, the scope of the exemptions provided for in the current directive, the organisational and professional conduct requirements for investment firms, the organisational requirements for trading venues, the current and authorisation obligations applicable to data service providers, the powers of competent authorities, the sanctions and rules applicable to third country companies operating through branches.
in writing. − i voted for the amendments relating to the proposal for a regulation on markets in financial instruments and amending the [emir] regulation on otc derivatives, central counterparties and trade repositories. the recent financial crisis has brought to the fore a number of deficiencies in the transparency of financial markets, which can cause negative socio-economic effects. i support increased transparency to strengthen the financial system. in order to increase transparency and improve the functioning of the internal market in financial instruments, it is necessary to lay down uniform requirements as regards the transparency of transactions in markets for financial instruments. in order to increase the transparency and efficiency of european markets and to ensure a level playing field for the different venues offering multilateral trading services, it is necessary to introduce a new class of organised trading facility (otf) for bonds, structured finance products, emission allowances and derivatives and to ensure that it is properly regulated and that it applies non-discriminatory rules on access to the facility. the new category includes cross-order systems as well as systems that should be eligible for trading of derivatives that are eligible for clearing and sufficiently liquid but do not have the characteristics of existing trading venues.

in writing. - i voted for this resolution because i believe that russia's accession to the wto opens up new perspectives for its relationship with the european union. adherence to common rules will give greater predictability to trade relations between the two partners. on the other hand, energy is one of the most delicate subjects when it comes to negotiations with russia. however, it is also one of the most important for the european union, due to its dependence on gas imports from russia. we remember the gas crisis in 2006, when supplies to europe were cut off. to avoid a repeat of such episodes, russia must demonstrate that it is a reliable partner. i therefore consider it necessary to include a legally binding chapter on energy in the new eu-russia agreement.
in writing. − in a globalised world, especially economically, russia's accession to the world trade organisation is an advantage because it will enable russia to benefit from a number of international trade instruments developed by the organisation. i believe that russia's accession to the world trade organisation is in its own interests, but also in the interests of the european and global economy as a whole. the world bank estimates that productivity will increase, with positive effects on gross domestic product, as russia will be able to attract new foreign investors and acquire quality technological products. the european union is russia's main economic partner, with over eur 138 billion worth of products exported to the eu, and russia's anchoring in the multilateral trading system and, by implication, adherence to the rules established by it is another step towards improving the eu-russia bilateral relationship.
in writing. − the european union is a strategic trading partner for russia, being its first source of imports, still growing, its main export destination and a key investment partner (foreign direct investment received), accounting for 47.1% of russia's overall trade; as this relationship expands, russia has become the second source of imports (eur 158.6 billion) and the fourth destination for eu exports (eur 86.1 billion) (2010 figures). russia's accession to the wto can facilitate trade flows between the eu and russia, while boosting economic growth and job creation on both sides, and the conclusion of a new agreement is seen as an additional opportunity to contribute to a strengthened partnership between both sides, while promoting sustainable development in their common neighbourhood. i welcome russia's accession to the wto, ratified by the russian state duma on 10 july 2012, and consider russia's anchoring in the multilateral trading system and the rules governing it as another step towards improving the eu-russia bilateral relationship.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution and particularly welcome the references to the well-founded concerns about russia's failure to fulfil its obligations, namely to lift the ban on imports of live animals from the eu or to return to establishing seasonal import rules for sugar. the commission must ensure that the interests of european agricultural producers are protected in the negotiations with the russian federation, in particular as regards the application of sanitary and phytosanitary measures, where only justified temporary prohibitions can intervene, and the protection of geographical indications. last but not least, the commission must ensure that the future agreement requires our agricultural trading partners to meet the same standards of quality and food safety as we require from european farmers.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on eu-russia trade relations after russia's accession to the wto because i believe that russia's accession to the wto will improve the eu-russia bilateral relationship. russia is the eu's third largest trading partner and the eu is russia's largest trading partner. in 2011, eu exports to russia were eur 108,4 billion, eu imports from russia were eur 199,5 billion and total trade in goods was eur 308 billion. i support the further development of the european union's relations with russia, in line with the principles enshrined in the partnership for modernisation, based on common interests and a deep commitment to universal values and democratic principles, respect for fundamental and human rights and the rule of law. i believe that the eu-russia partnership for modernization (pom) is a useful initiative to strengthen the new economic and trade relations between the two sides in the wto and bilaterally. i also believe that by promoting synergies between the trade and investment strategies of the two sides, the full potential of russia's economic modernisation and diversification can be realised more effectively.

the european area of freedom, security and justice facilitates access to justice, in particular through the principle of mutual recognition of judicial and extrajudicial decisions in civil matters. in order to progressively establish this area, the union should adopt measures in the field of judicial cooperation in civil matters with cross-border implications in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market. mutual trust in the administration of justice in the union justifies the principle that judgments given in a member state should be recognised without the need for special procedures and that the duration and costs of cross-border litigation should be reduced. in order to ensure the protection of consumers and employees, to protect the jurisdiction of the courts of the member states in situations where they have exclusive jurisdiction and to respect the autonomy of the parties, certain rules of jurisdiction in this regulation should apply irrespective of the domicile of the defendant. in order to protect the rights of employees, we stress the importance of the provisions of articles 19 and 20, in particular the provision that an employer who is not domiciled in a member state may be sued before a court of a member state. in the case of contracts of employment, consumer contracts and employment contracts, the disadvantaged party should be protected by rules of jurisdiction more favourable to his interests than the general rules applicable. i would like to conclude, mr president, by welcoming the express reference to respect for the charter of fundamental rights of the union.
unfortunately, the wrongful removal or retention of a child is not an isolated or rare event. when parents divorce, differences often arise over custody of the children, and in some cases one parent may prefer to leave the country with the child without the other's consent. such situations exist in many countries of the world. before the convention was adopted, there were problems when it came to securing the return of the child, because of the difference between the judicial systems of each state. forced to live in a foreign environment, children can develop social and linguistic disorders that manifest themselves over the medium to long term. i think the accession of the eight states to the convention must be achieved as soon as possible. i would also like to ask commissioner reding whether there is an estimate of the number of cases affected by the delay and what measures the commission is considering to unlock this situation.
for the security of the union and its citizens, it is very important that we maintain strict control over substances that can be used as cluster bombs. as you know, improvised explosive devices are the terrorists' favorite tool. last year, in the oslo bombing, substances such as ammonium nitrate were used, which is included in the annex to the proposed regulation. to avoid such tragedies in the union, we must be careful. the marketing of dangerous substances to unauthorised firms or persons must be punished much more severely by the member states to discourage such practices, and national authorities are obliged to constantly check the authorisations issued. voluntary reporting of suspicious transactions in such materials will also play a very important role in avoiding dangerous situations.
mr president, colorectal cancer is the most common cancer in europe. bearing in mind the guidelines for colorectal cancer screening from 2010, last week i hosted the conference which launched a white paper setting the standards for the prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care of colorectal cancer across europe. with 450 000 new cases of this cancer being diagnosed every year in the eu, what struck me was the opportunity to reduce the number of new cases. speakers confirmed the possibility of reducing new cases by 30 % by embracing a lifestyle of healthy food, exercise and not smoking. screening can identify a further 30%. such initiatives could prevent about 270 000 new cases per year. i therefore ask the commission to urge the implementation of a local primary health strategy, to embrace a healthy lifestyle, awareness campaigns and the early introduction of screening programmes across europe so that we can meet our goals of healthy ageing by 2020.

in february 2010, i was reporting on the difficulties facing the national research and development institute for microbiology and immunology cantacuzino in my country. at the time, the institute had its license to manufacture and market injectable products, including many serums and vaccines of great public health importance, revoked. after difficult negotiations with the government of the day and the establishment of a plan of action, the cantacuzino institute regained its right to function normally. unfortunately, my repeated appeals and assistance fell on deaf ears of the pdl governments, and the situation of this institute of strategic importance, not only national but also european, continued to deteriorate gradually, reaching the verge of bankruptcy. this is the stage where it was taken over by the usl government, led by victor ponta, who, despite all the adversity, managed to put together, in record time, a strategy to save the cantacuzino institute. of course, this is only the beginning, which is why i stand before you today, reiterating my call for a more active involvement of the european institutions in monitoring and supporting the work of these institutions of strategic european importance, for the benefit of all the citizens of europe.
the european payments market must function as efficiently and accurately as possible. its full potential is still far from being reached and there are still obstacles to be overcome. paying with a card on the internet or on a mobile phone can offer many advantages to consumers. they thus benefit from more flexible, convenient and fast payment systems. there are still large differences in card payments between member states and markets remain fragmented. the single euro payments area aims to close the existing gaps. it contributes to the transformation of the market into a more innovative and competitive one. but the question is, how secure are these systems in countries where there is not yet a tradition of this, and the risk of fraud persists? i think a high level of security should be ensured, as a guarantee against the risk of fraud.
the development and widespread use of card payments on the internet and mobile phones will allow the development of european e-commerce. in order to facilitate cross-border electronic commerce and to ensure a genuine digital economy, it is essential to develop transparent, secure and efficient payment systems in the european digital market. standardisation and interoperability requirements should aim to improve the competitiveness, transparency, innovation, security of payments and efficiency of the european payments market. i consider that there is a need for greater transparency and better consumer information on surcharges and additional charges for various payment methods, given that traders often include transaction costs in the prices of their products and services and therefore consumers are not properly informed in advance of the total cost. according to the judgment of the court of justice of the european union of 24 may 2012, the mif can be considered anti-competitive. how does the commission intend to implement this decision?
mr president, virtual transaction systems are constantly being improved in order to save time and effort for users, but their security is in my opinion a reason to remain vigilant. the vulnerability of virtual transaction systems consists of two main factors: firstly, technical vulnerabilities due to the fact that virtual transactions still represent a new online practice and, secondly, the human ignorance factor. many people are easily tricked into revealing personal information online and into making unsecure transactions with third-party entities. that is why i think the most important measures which should be taken are: raising user awareness regarding internet transaction security; respecting the recommendations of secure pay; and last but not least, achieving total transparency of costs for users and the freedom to choose preferred payment methods.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i absolutely agree with the discussion and with the speeches by members saying that payments are one of the most common expressions of the single market for its 500 million citizens. it is a very rapidly evolving field and it is important that europe supports the developments providing for simplicity and safety and guaranteeing the best value for payment services used by the citizens. now, a lot has been done but we need to go forward, as underlined in the report by mr terho, who supports the objectives of the green paper and who also argues for a more integrated payment market. this integration was taken forward by the regulations establishing a deadline for the migration to a single europe payment area for credit transfers and direct debits. thanks to that, from 2014 on there will be no difference between national and cross-border payments any more. but a true and integrated internal market in payments must also involve payments by credit card, internet and mobile phone, as underlined by the speakers: we need choice for consumers; we need innovation safety to free up the potential of e-commerce. you know that we do have problems with e-commerce at this moment, because only 35% of internet users shop online because of problems related to payments. therefore there are clearly specific problems to be solved. first of all, we must defragment the payment services markets, which are far too often national. we must facilitate the access of new entrants and significantly increase the transparency of the cost of the different payment methods. we need to address issues of standardisation, interoperability, security of payments, data protection and the good governance of the system. we are currently working on all these issues, such as the multilateral interchange fees, surcharges, governance and standardisation, as well as account access and security, and we will need to find the right balance. it will doubtless involve changing the regulatory framework of the directive on payment services. the rapporteur’s report is a milestone in this debate. it constitutes a good basis for the work that we will carry out together to achieve a well-functioning digital single market beneficial to consumers. i thank parliament for its support and i have noted your call to legislate in this field. i can tell you today that your view is fully shared by the commission and will be realised in the coming months.
i welcome this initiative to improve the monitoring and regulation of the shadow banking system. prudential and market conduct aspects can be addressed appropriately through enhanced supervision. we need a global picture to identify developments in this sector, and this requires close international cooperation. we have to consider both the positives and the risks and the things that need to be fixed. in this context, i stress the importance of eliminating misconduct and reducing systemic risk. only in this way will we be able to achieve a high level of transparency and increase the safety and stability of the financial system, and only in this way will the positive effects of the parallel banking system on the real economy and the stimulation of economic growth be felt.
38% of european young people aged 9-12 and 77% of those aged 15-16 are on sites such as facebook. measures to protect children in the digital world address illegal and inappropriate content, harassment, discrimination and limitation of access to services, online surveillance, attacks on privacy and freedom of expression. the fact that personal information and data are often provided by minors and remain online may lead to their unlawful processing and to the exploitation of minors, thus potentially seriously harming their dignity, identity, personality and social inclusion. minors need to understand the potential dangers they face online, and competent authorities, families, schools and civil society need to share responsibility for the proper education and protection of children in the digital world.
we often talk about the need to teach children to use the internet in a safe way, without realizing that teachers sometimes know much less about this virtual world. in the context of the massive increase in the number of social network users, from very young ages, i believe that urgent action is vital. digital education needs to be a priority in schools so that children are aware of the dangers lurking in the virtual environment and that could affect their lives irreversibly: violent content, racism, pornography, online harassment. at the same time, teachers and parents need to acquire minimum digital skills, because otherwise we risk not being able to help children avoid the pitfalls of the internet. eu member states, public institutions and internet providers need to adopt a strategy for the firm protection of young people in the digital space.
mr president, the exposure of children to inappropriate digital content is unfortunately a negative consequence of the evolution and accessibility of technology. however, i would like to stress the importance of monitoring exposure to online and offline digital content, such as video games, which psychologically manipulate children. in this regard, it is absolutely crucial for us to fight against the risks associated with such content and to promote educational campaigns for the protection of minors against harmful activities associated with the negative exposure affecting their development. we need to ensure that all actors concerned with children’s education – parents, teachers and the media – are actively involved in a common effort to shelter minors from the psychological dangers of the digital world.
in writing. european children spend up to 40 hours a week in front of the television. they spend 88 minutes a day online (2 hours for the 15/16 age group), starting on average at age 9, but there are cases where they start much earlier, even before they go to school and can read. unfortunately, children are exposed to huge risks, such as psychological manipulation, child pornography, invasion of privacy, online gambling, commercial fraud, and behaviors that can have a range of consequences, such as cyberbullying and sexting, and other age-inappropriate elements, such as inappropriate advertising, violence, sex and so on, that generate fear and anxiety. it is our duty to defend the innocence of children and to protect them from the dangers to which they may be exposed as a result of accessing the internet or television. in this regard, the continuity of the 'safer internet' programme must be ensured, as well as the encouragement of measures to combat online crimes against minors, successfully adopted by certain member states, which facilitate the exchange of information with internet and e-mail service providers.
in writing. prevention activities, through normative education, play a key role in training children to make decisions about their online activity. for young people, their perception of what is normal and acceptable in society is very important. it is important that they have a good understanding of digital media use so that in the future they can decide for themselves which paths they want to take on the internet and which paths they prefer to avoid. since an attitude is defined as a predisposition that is formed over time and is used in judging a context, a young person's attitude to the internet is formed over time and is very likely to be the result of the attitude of friends, family or educators to this environment. i appreciate the idea of a campaign for parents to help them understand the digital content their children are manipulating and, more importantly, how to protect them. i also find it very useful to call on the member states and the commission to develop information programmes to protect against cybercrime. international cooperation between law enforcement authorities and civil society organisations involved in combating and monitoring online activities harmful to minors should be strengthened.
the report on consumer credit calls for a better level of consumer protection. we demand that financial institutions provide consumers with a personalized, comprehensive and easy-to-understand explanation of the risks involved in lending in foreign currency and the impact that higher interest rates on foreign currency loans have on rates. these explanations must be provided before the signing of any contract. in the case of credit, we stress the importance of the right to information on the costs of ancillary services and the right of consumers to purchase ancillary services, such as insurance, from alternative providers. consumers should be informed in advance of the change in interest rates in order to allow them sufficient time to examine the market and choose another credit provider before the change in interest rate becomes effective.
i welcome this report, which aims to harmonize consumer protection and strengthen competition. i agree that the crossborder consumer credit market needs to be strengthened. this will promote the functioning of the internal market. at the same time, consumers need to be better informed and have a higher level of protection. accurate and comprehensive information is needed to help consumers understand the risks they may face. this will enable them to make the best informed decisions. the supervisory authorities have a very important role to play in this respect. they must monitor and prevent the risks involved in lending in foreign currency. i also believe that more importance should be given to informing consumers about the cost of services.
the unemployment rate at eu-27 level has exceeded 10%, with the union facing extremely serious problems with regard to youth unemployment. other pressing issues are the situation of low-skilled workers, facing a declining demand for labour, and the increasing number of people living in poverty and at risk of social exclusion. recent responses to the crisis lack the social and employment policy dimension. social investment aims to prepare individuals, families and societies to adapt to changing economic conditions and labour market demands. economic governance and macroeconomic surveillance must be complemented by measures on social and employment policies. we call on the commission and the member states to adopt a concrete strategy on social investment, adequately funded, including through the european social fund.
i welcome the initiative of my colleague, which i consider particularly important in the current context. i too believe that there must be a shift from welfare states to states that invest in job creation and generate competitiveness. my main concern is the situation of young people, because they are the most affected by the economic crisis and unemployment among them has reached alarming levels. in this context, vocational training programmes are vital and the re-establishment of vocational schools is important. job creation must also be made as a result of the exploitation of own mineral resources and not only from foreign investments. facilities must also be provided to stimulate the employment of young people by reducing the contributions of employers. however, action is also needed at european level. i ask the commission, in line with the conclusions of the european council in january, to come forward with proposals to support young people.
social economy enterprises employ over 11 million people in the european union, representing 6% of the total workforce in the union and 10% of all european enterprises. the european union's structural funds and programmes play a significant role in facilitating access to finance for enterprises in the social economy sector. access to european funds should therefore be simplified, allowing for an appropriate level of flexibility at member state level. i stress the importance of a strategy and measures to promote entrepreneurship and innovative social enterprises, especially for young people and disadvantaged people. we call for the continuation of the erasmus programme for young entrepreneurs and for its attractiveness and visibility to be increased in the social economy sector.
i would also like to congratulate my colleague on his work on this report. we are currently experiencing an increase in demand for social services, due primarily to demographic change. social enterprises face difficulties in finding the funding they need, depending on their level of development. incentives are therefore needed for those providing services of general interest. i believe that first of all we must ensure access to private finance, but also the mobilisation of european funds to support social enterprises. member states could also adapt the legal framework by improving access to public procurement. last but not least, the visibility and management capacities of social entrepreneurs should be improved. this could be achieved, including through programmes such as erasmus for young entrepreneurs.
social entrepreneurs are characterised by ambition and persistence, using their energies to identify solutions to the shortcomings facing society. they are visionaries but also realists, their efforts aimed at adapting the social system to the needs of the community. global financial institutions recognise the benefits of development investments by supporting social enterprises and prefer to finance them rather than social aid programmes. i believe that social enterprises provide the necessary link between the private environment, which is focused on maximising profit, and the public environment, which must respond to social needs. combining the two approaches generates cost efficiencies and reduces losses, with the direct beneficiary being the citizen. social enterprises should benefit from the support of european prudential funds with access to various financial instruments. they also need the support of national, regional and local authorities both in terms of funding and promotion in order to legitimise social entrepreneurship initiatives.
although they represent some two million enterprises, with 11 million employees, social enterprises in the european union have underdeveloped funding systems. in this connection, i consider it absolutely necessary to promote additional financial means, both at national and european union level. one solution is to simplify access to the relevant structural funds under the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, and a second solution may be to include specific axes for microfinance and social entrepreneurship under the european social fund, the european regional development fund, the horizon 2020 fund and the social change and innovation programme. only then will we be able to guarantee adequate support for social enterprises, which promote high quality jobs, combat poverty and social exclusion and invest in education and training for european citizens.
we know that the social dimension of the economic and financial crisis will be felt more and more in the period ahead. more and more people are saying that in europe's crisis management, in addition to reducing public debt and meeting budget deficit targets, too little attention has been paid to the social consequences of the crisis. in recent years, economic issues have overshadowed all other considerations, and citizens rightly feel that there are no answers to rising unemployment, problems in education systems or the phenomenon of poverty. the governments of the member states are well aware of the consequences of ignoring certain social needs. it is time to give social issues a high priority at european policy level. this requires a joint effort by the council, the commission and parliament. we cannot allow european countries to sacrifice their developed social systems on the altar of crisis management.

union level. in order to ensure simplification of the legal framework and a high level of operational safety, occupational safety and environmental protection, the technical requirements and in writing. the objective of this legislative proposal is to establish harmonised rules for the manufacture of agricultural and forestry vehicles, so that the existing legislation on vehicle type-approval is simplified. i believe that the new regulation should be flexible enough to allow both the continuous development of existing machines and the introduction of new types of machines. the technical requirements for the type-approval of agricultural vehicles with regard to numerous safety and environmental elements have been harmonised at union level in order to ensure a high level of road safety, occupational safety and environmental protection. in conclusion, i would like to stress that the proposal contributes to the competitiveness of the industrial sector and to the proper functioning of the internal market.
the maastricht treaty marked a key milestone in the history of the european union by creating a single currency, backed by both an economic and a monetary pillar. however, as monetary policy took shape with the successive adoption of the european treaties, the macroeconomic dimension was reduced to simple coordination. the lack of a genuine economic policy has deprived the union of a crisis-ready response, leading to severe social costs. to address these shortcomings, the european commission proposes the creation of a banking union. i support her proposal. we need more economic integration and the tools to respond to today's economic and social challenges. but if we focus on the single banking supervisory mechanism without developing common rules for preventing bank failures and a single deposit guarantee system, we will repeat the mistakes that have undermined economic and monetary union. at the same time, it is necessary to avoid excluding non-euro area member states from the decision-making process on the single supervisory mechanism.
i voted in favour of the report because the free movement of judgments is a key objective for the strengthening of the european union. i believe that the present proposal will remove obstacles to the procedure for the recognition and enforcement of a judgment in civil and commercial matters in another member state. it is also very important to extend the provisions to nationals of third countries in the union. the introduction of choice of court agreements will also increase the efficiency of judicial procedures. the court chosen by the parties to settle a dispute will thus always have priority. this will lead to simplified procedures and lower costs. we must give citizens and businesses in the union the opportunity to resolve their disputes as quickly and efficiently as possible.
madam president, the european court of human rights has decided in numerous cases that the right of access to a court would be illusory if a contracting state’s domestic legal system allowed for a final binding judgement to remain on paper and not be enforced to the detriment of one party. the right of execution of a judgement derives from the essential principle of the rule of law. we need to unify the rules on the conflict of jurisdiction in civil and commercial matters in all eu member states. the exequatur for all civil and commercial judgements must be abolished. this will be a significant step forward in access to justice for citizens and businesses. the measure will simplify the procedure which allows a claimant who has obtained a judgement from a member state to enforce that judgement in any other member state. this would be totally to the benefit of our citizens.
madam president, i voted for the report on the marketing and use of explosives precursors. it follows and supports the commission’s approach in restricting access by the general public to 15 high-risk chemicals in concentrations that can be used for the manufacture of home-made explosives. the free movement of goods will not suffer from this measure. for instance, eight substances listed in annex i may continue to be sold in concentrated form but only if the buyer presents a licence granted by a national competent authority. the sale of other substances would remain restriction-free but be better controlled. wholesalers and retailers would be obliged to report any suspicious transactions. i also welcome the decision to support the commission’s approach involving setting up a more harmonised licensing system instead of a dual system as proposed by the council. by limiting access by the general public to these 15 substances, the regulation should reduce the frequency and impact of terrorist attacks.
madam president, i support this agreement between the european parliament and the council. as a fully functioning market economy we need to open up national markets in the economic sector of consumer credit. accomplishing this will promote competition, eliminate market distortions between operators and improve the functioning of the internal market. however, statistics show that cross-border consumer credit has not increased in years. some legal and practical barriers still remain. i am supporting this proposal to further harmonise and improve the consumption of consumer credit. it is very important in terms of strengthening the internal market in the area of consumer credit with regard to cross-border transactions. in addition, it includes a high level of consumer credit protection, which is extremely important in order to promote confidence in purchasing consumer credit. thus, economic growth and investment greatly depend on the adoption of this directive.
madam president, i support this report which sets out an initiative of the commission on combating the currently stagnant eu economy. this report calls on member states to arrange for a system of investment, education and employment targets in coordination with the eu 2020 goals. the social investment pact will contain enforcement mechanisms to ensure that each nation is meeting its goals and to stimulate economic growth. the current unemployment rate in the eu’s 27 member states is now above 10 %, up from 7.1 % in 2008. youth unemployment is far worse: it is currently over 20 %. this report calls for actions that will help alleviate some of the economic problems the union is now facing. we must ensure that the labour market improves, growth is stimulated and that an improvement in employment opportunities is sustainable.
madam president, this proposal finally adds several long expected regulations to the l-category vehicles market. currently these vehicles account for a high level of pollution. they are also dangerous compared to other vehicle types: two-wheeled power vehicles account for 16% of driving-related deaths in the european union while accounting for just 2% of total kilometres driven. i welcome this proposal because it sets out better safety standards such as multi-standard anti-lock brakes along with tougher emission standards to reduce the environmental impact. this will ensure that these vehicles become safer for their operators and friendlier for the environment, and lives will be saved.
madam president, i rise on this occasion to support the proposal of the european parliament and the council, as the manufacturers, suppliers and aftermarket stakeholders, including the trade unions, think the completion of the internal market in this area is a good idea. more specifically, harmonisation regarding the rules and regulations between all vehicles will enhance competition within the european union. the machinery directive will enable better monitoring of third-party products entering the european union. furthermore, harmonisation will foster occupational and vehicle safety as well as environmental protection. thus this proposal will limit market distortion from third-party products while improving our own industries.
i voted in favour of this report because it is essential to ensure a high level of road safety and environmental protection. this will help to improve the functioning of the internal market. simplifying the legislation in force will improve the competitiveness of the sector. harmonised standards are needed for the manufacture of agricultural and forestry vehicles. we also need a common framework for the marketing of products. he will contribute to the implementation and compliance of the new regulation. unrestricted and non-discriminatory access to vehicle repair and maintenance information is very important. i think that there has to be a balance that is right, that guarantees open access to technical information. furthermore, i believe that we should consider all the concerns related to consumer protection and fair competition.
madam president, this report proposes the further integration of the european card, internet and mobile payment market. with the ever-expanding use of non-cash payments through cards, there is an increasing need to develop a system that is both consistent and efficient. with proper eu oversight the card market will be able to reach its full potential. this would be achieved by the further integration of the market to alleviate problems associated with the transfer of payments among member states with different policies. this resolution serves to provide integration without fundamentally changing the market. cross-border standard payments and payment security are both provided for by this resolution. a further goal is to foster competition by decreasing multilateral interchange fees and surcharges. unnecessary or artificially inflated fees are technical obstacles that must be removed. in doing so, we will increase the efficiency of and competition on our market.
madam president, i rise to affirm this proposal. if banks are left unregulated in regard to shadow banking, then this lack of regulation will further destroy the economy. for instance, shadow banking accounted for eur 21 trillion in 2002 and then jumped to eur 51 trillion in 2011. in other words, shadow banking now represents 25% to 30% of all banking activity. placing shadow banking under the common regulatory framework will increase stability across the european union’s banking system. direct regulation such as establishing bank reporting requirements is a valuable tool for tackling shadow banking activity. i support this report because lack of oversight in regard to shadow banking contributed to the current financial crisis and the current banking system needs a lot of patchwork in the area of shadow banking if we are to fight the financial crisis in the eu in an efficient way.
madam president, almost 15% of internet users aged between ten and seventeen receive some form of sexual solicitation. last october a french teenager committed suicide after being the victim of blackmail on a famous social network, facebook. though it proves to be an asset for the education sector we can see that the use of the internet involves substantial risk to the privacy, dignity, safety and even the life of children and teenagers. member states must transpose and implement as soon as possible directive 2011/92/eu on combating the sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children and child pornography. at the eu level, i welcome the creation of the new cyber security agency based at europol and i call for adequate resources for its child protection team. a top-down approach alone is not enough: children and teenagers must receive the information and training to be able to protect themselves online. eu programmes such as the safer internet programme are very positive.
i voted in favour of the report because we need to be more involved in the development and education of minors. i believe that the responsibility for avoiding some dangers lies primarily with parents, but also with internet service providers. everyone must ensure that minors are protected when they use the internet, and internet providers must find ways to block children under 18 from accessing such harmful material. i'm considering developing filters to verify the age of users. child pornography remains a major problem for minors' access to the internet and, in this regard, member states need to transpose the directive on combating sexual abuse of children as a matter of urgency. those who facilitate the production and distribution of such material must be held accountable, without exception.
madam president, we need a favourable climate for social enterprises and innovation. social enterprises employ 6% of the entire eu workforce, or over 18 million people. they provide social services in areas such as health and education that are beneficial to society. social entrepreneurs are innovators and key players in the social economy and must be protected. a stronger social enterprise economy will help accomplish the goals of the single market act as well as the europe 2020 strategy. they need support that is specifically designed for their benefit. this support may come from eu-supported banking, funds and microcredit. we must make sure that the measures suggested by this proposal will ensure just that.
madam president, i support the creation of an economic, monetary and fiscal union. we have created a common market and a single currency, yet we do not have a unique political decision. the european people’s party has consistently advocated closer economic integration as an answer to the current financial crisis. today i would like to refer to two recommendations in the thyssen report that i find particularly relevant: recommendation 2.7 on ensuring the democratic oversight of the european stability mechanism, and recommendation 4.2 on european financial backstops. as the rapporteur on the 2010 discharge of european agencies, i do have an insight into the spending of eu money. we cannot create a help fund for member states without ensuring that this money is spent in a correct, efficient and justifiable way. we are talking about substantial amounts of money with many political interests at stake. we must be clear on who is responsible for control and oversight. the european parliament has proved that it can take this responsibility seriously. we have taken a leading role in the fight against corruption and conflicts of interest. we must continue to support measures to stamp out potentially ambiguous practices.
i voted in favour of this report because economic and monetary union must lead to sustainable growth and high employment. we need more europe, but for that we also need increased parliamentary involvement. most member states are facing a difficult economic situation and that is precisely why an urgent decision is needed on the future and the direction in which the union will continue to go. we need a good climate for entrepreneurs and investment, and creating jobs and ensuring decent conditions is a key element in overcoming the current problems. europe must move towards a democratic federation of nation states, capable of formulating a coherent economic policy and a relevant foreign policy on the international stage.
in writing. − i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on the efforts made during the negotiations, because through this regulation, citizens and businesses in the european union will have access to a coherent legal framework, which allows judgments given by courts competent in civil and commercial matters to be recognised and enforced promptly in a member state other than the one where the judgment was given, and in this way they will be able to fully benefit from the rights they have gained in court. i support the amendment proposed by the rapporteur, to abolish the exequatur procedure for judgments in civil and commercial matters, because in this way any judgment obtained in one member state will be automatically recognised in any other member state, and this leads to a significant improvement in the access to justice guaranteed to citizens and businesses, while also contributing to the acceleration of the judicial process. i believe that this proposal is also important for european consumers, who are among the main beneficiaries of this reform of judicial cooperation. it is essential that they are always guaranteed the right to bring an action against the other party to the contract before the courts where they are domiciled.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the proposal for a regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. i consider it important to achieve the union's objective of maintaining and developing an area of freedom, security and justice, which should, inter alia, facilitate access to justice, in particular through the principle of mutual recognition of judicial and extrajudicial decisions in civil matters. certain differences between national rules governing jurisdiction and the recognition of judgments impede the proper functioning of the internal market. it is essential to adopt provisions to unify the rules on conflicts of jurisdiction in civil and commercial matters and to ensure the rapid and simple recognition and enforcement of judgments given in a member state. this regulation shall apply in civil and commercial matters, irrespective of the nature of the court or tribunal. it does not apply, in particular, to fiscal, customs or administrative matters, nor to the liability of the state for acts or omissions by it in the exercise of public authority.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's first reading position on the adoption of the regulation on the marketing and use of explosives precursors. the illicit manufacture of explosives should be made more difficult by setting concentration limit values for certain explosives precursors. the free movement of those explosives precursors is ensured and subject to a safeguard mechanism below these concentration limit values. beyond those concentration limit values, access to those explosives precursors by the general public should be restricted. the regulation on the classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures provides that substances and mixtures classified as dangerous must be correctly labelled before being placed on the market. economic operators, including retailers, also either classify and label these substances or rely on the classification established by an upstream actor in the supply chain. it is therefore appropriate to provide in this regulation that all economic operators, including retailers, who make available to the general public substances restricted under this regulation ensure that the packaging indicates that the acquisition, possession or use of the substance or mixture by the general public is subject to a restriction.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that, in the context of accession to the european union, croatian citizens will have to benefit from derogations in order to be able to work in the union institutions. this is all the more important as translators, interpreters, editors and proofreaders of croatian origin will have to be employed in order not to affect the ability of the institutions to work in croatian, which will become an official language of the union. since a similar procedure was adopted for the accessions of the last 12 members of the union, i believe that the same can be done for the situation in croatia. it is important that there is a fair distribution of nationality within the european institutions. the employment of croatian nationals must therefore start immediately after the effective date of accession to the european union.
in writing. − the accession of croatia next year is an important stage in a long process, which is a testimony to the strength and unity of the european union. it shows that in an unprecedented period of crisis, the eu did not turn inwards, but was able to continue the work started and not listen to those who felt that the enlargement process was moving too fast. but we must not sit back complacently, because without the integration of the western balkans there will never be any lasting stability in the post-yugoslav states, and without these countries there will never be a whole europe. enlargement must continue, and the western balkans must be given a clear and unambiguous perspective in the accession process. we need to narrow our expectations and alongside them make continuous progress in converging our economies, our legal systems, our societies and our policies. croatia's example shows that work pays off.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation introducing, on the occasion of croatia's accession, special and temporary measures concerning the recruitment of officials and temporary staff of the european union. this regulation provides, in the context of the accession of croatia, for a derogation from the general rules on the recruitment of officials and other servants of the european union, according to which recruitment must be open to all citizens of the european union, irrespective of nationality. the requirements have been temporarily adapted in the event of accession to the union to allow 'positive discrimination' in favour of acceding countries, thus allowing them to be adequately represented among officials and other servants of the european union. i welcome the commission's proposal to follow the same procedure as for the accession of 12 new countries in 2004 and 2007 and for croatian citizens. the proposal for a regulation allows certain recruitment competitions to be reserved for croatian nationals until 2018. i welcome the organisation of competitions for recruitment of croatian language linguists (translators, interpreters, editors, proofreaders and press attachés), as well as for general administrators and assistants.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that a higher level of safety is needed in offshore oil and gas operations. the recent accident in the gulf of mexico further underscores this need. i think that a sustainable governance policy for offshore activities is more than welcome. in this context, i support the commission's proposal and believe that the union should promote international cooperation to improve safety at sea. i also want to stress the importance of maintaining an optimal ecological situation and avoiding tragic consequences in the future. the ratification of the protocol would be an important step forward in this respect and would help to ensure an optimal level of cooperation.
in writing. − i consider that the accession of the european union to the protocol on offshore activities is necessary to protect the marine and coastal environment of the mediterranean and to promote international cooperation towards the sustainable governance of offshore activities. the scale and severity of the deepwater horizon accident in the gulf of mexico in 2010, as well as other dramatic accidents, require a high level of safety for oil and gas exploration and production. the mediterranean sea is increasingly the site of offshore exploration and exploitation activities and is particularly vulnerable because of its semi-enclosed configuration and significant seismic activity. the aim of the 'offshore protocol' is to increase the safety of offshore exploration and exploitation activities and to protect the marine environment in the mediterranean sea. it lays down the conditions to be met before such activities can be permitted, the conditions for the removal of abandoned or decommissioned installations, the use and disposal of harmful substances, and measures relating to safety, emergency planning and monitoring.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the eu's accession to the protocol for the protection of the mediterranean sea against pollution resulting from the exploration and exploitation of the continental shelf, the seabed and the seabed. the convention for the protection of the marine environment and the coastal region of the mediterranean, also known as the 'barcelona convention', was originally signed in barcelona in 1976 and amended in 1995. one of the barcelona convention protocols concerns the protection of the mediterranean sea against pollution resulting from exploration and exploitation of the continental shelf, the seabed and the seabed. the european union has neither signed nor ratified the protocol on offshore activities. it is therefore necessary for the union to conclude this protocol. one of the objectives of the european union's environmental policy is to promote measures to solve regional environmental problems at international level. with regard to the protocol on offshore activities, it is particularly important to take into account the high probability of transboundary environmental effects in the event of an accident in a semi-enclosed sea such as the mediterranean sea. it is therefore necessary for the european union to take all necessary measures to support the safety of offshore exploration and exploitation activities and the protection of the marine environment in the mediterranean sea.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this recommendation because the fisheries partnership agreement with greenland has proved to be a success and i believe that it should be further supported and promoted by a new protocol. it is a key element of eu-greenland cooperation and nordic fisheries cooperation, which has brought a number of benefits to both sides. i consider the financial contribution provided for by the new protocol for the period 2013-2015 to be appropriate and believe that it will ensure a responsible and sustainable sectoral fisheries policy for greenland. i also welcome the addition to the new protocol of a suspension clause in the event of violations of fundamental human rights or democratic principles. i believe that this is an indispensable part of the effective functioning of the agreement in question.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community, of the one part, and the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland, of the other part. the fisheries partnership agreement with greenland was established after greenland's withdrawal from the ec in 1985, on the basis that the community could maintain its traditional fishing rights by paying an annual financial compensation in return. the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and the former home rule government of greenland was adopted on 28 june 2007 together with the current protocol setting out the annual fishing opportunities and financial contributions until 31 december 2012. greenland's economy is highly dependent on fishing and the export of fishery products to the eu. in 2012, exports to eu markets amounted to eur 331 million (92,7% of total exports), while the value of imports from the eu was almost twice as high (eur 641 million). the fisheries sector creates 6 500 jobs, but only 2 000 full-time jobs are directly provided by the fisheries sector. i welcome the renewal of the protocol for a period of three years from 1 january 2013.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it was necessary to simplify the procedures for citizens who are not resident in the state in which they stand for election to the european parliament. it is important that the checks on eligibility are carried out by the member states and become an automatic procedure for each candidate in elections. this will encourage the submission of candidatures and give voters the opportunity to choose from a wide range of candidates. last but not least, simplification of procedures can be a step towards a uniform regulation of the right to vote in elections to the european parliament. in the future, greater harmonisation will be required between the way in which elections to parliament are conducted.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it clarifies and facilitates the procedure for european citizens residing in a member state other than the one of which they are nationals to stand as candidates in european parliament elections. this is paramount in the current eu context, where migration from one member state to another is a highly common practice. thus, those in this situation need a clear and easy process to ensure that they are granted one of the fundamental rights of a democratic entity - that of being able to stand for election. i also welcome the fact that both the council and the european parliament will work to make the directive operational for the 2014 elections.
in writing. - i voted for the amendment of directive 93/109/ec on the right to elect and be elected to the european parliament for citizens of the union residing in a member state of which they are not nationals. the right of every citizen of the union to elect and be elected to the european parliament in his or her member state of residence is recognised under article 20 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and in the charter of fundamental rights of the eu. the member state of residence shall verify that union citizens who have expressed their wish to exercise their right to stand for election have not been deprived of that right in their member state of origin on the basis of an individual judgment or an administrative decision, provided that the latter can be subject to appeal. in order to facilitate communication between national authorities, member states should designate a contact point responsible for the notification of information on applications. the directive requires that, when the application is submitted, the union citizen submit a certificate from the competent administrative authorities of the home member state certifying that he has not been deprived of his right to stand for election in that member state or that the authorities are not aware of such a deprivation of rights.
in writing. − one of the fundamental principles of the single market is precisely the harmonisation of legislative conditions in order to increase the efficiency of economic exchanges. the contouring of this legislative framework on consumer credit removes regulatory differences on the one hand, and in practice offers consumers a much wider range of services and offers. on the other hand, through such initiatives, the common market becomes a concrete reality, with real coverage, which gives substance to the mechanisms and institutions of the european union. it is equally important, however, that the process of extending trade or the coverage of credit services be carried out with consumer protection as a permanent priority. i support the adoption of the report and believe that it is imperative that member states take decisive action to better inform consumers about the products and services to which they have access.
in writing. − the consumer credit directive has undoubtedly brought an extra layer of consumer protection, which is welcome. in general, i think we can be satisfied with the implementation process and i do not think that a revision of the directive is necessary at this point. the priority must be, as this report suggests, to ensure proper implementation in the member states. the sweep control procedure undertaken by the commission has been particularly useful in identifying problems in implementation. some sustained efforts must be made to ensure that the provisions of the directive on information on offers in advertising are not misrepresented. consumers also need to be better informed about the risks of taking out a loan in a foreign currency due to exchange rate fluctuations. last but not least, i believe it is important to provide consumers with more information about the possibility of taking out a loan in another member state. this is likely to increase crossborder lending and foster the creation of an internal credit market, which is currently in deficit, even if there are other reasons for this, such as linguistic ones.
in writing. − i also welcome the commission's initiative to carry out a study on the crossborder impact and effects of crossborder cooperation on the internal market and consumer protection. consumers in cross-border areas need to be better informed about the conditions under which they can obtain consumer credit in another member state for the purchase of durable goods, cars or other purposes, and about their rights when concluding such a contract, in particular where the credit is in a currency other than that of the beneficiary's state of residence.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the implementation of the consumer credit directive 2008/48/ec. the consumer credit directive has two objectives: to improve consumer protection and to strengthen the crossborder consumer credit market. the report on consumer credit calls for a better level of consumer protection. one of the objectives of the directive is to ensure the availability of information, thereby promoting the functioning of the internal market and the granting of loans. we consider it necessary to assess whether the number of cross-border loan agreements is increasing. i stress the importance of communicating to consumers that, where they exercise their right to withdraw from a contract where the supplier or service provider directly receives the corresponding amount of payment from the credit provider by an ancillary contract, consumers do not bear any fees, commissions or other costs relating to the financial service provided. we call on the commission to present to the european parliament and the council an evaluation report on the implementation of the directive, as well as a full impact assessment of its impact on consumer protection, taking into account the consequences of the financial crisis and the new eu legal framework for financial services.

in writing. − in the context of the economic crisis, the negative effects of member states' austerity measures on employment and competitiveness in europe must be considered. it is important to take measures that facilitate growth and employment, such as well-targeted social investment, which prepares citizens to adapt to changing economic conditions and labour market demands. alongside ensuring the sustainability of public finances, member states should focus equally on helping the unemployed, especially those who have been unemployed for a long time, to re-enter the labour market, on creating sustainable and quality jobs for both women and men and on improving labour productivity. at the same time, investment in education and training needs to be supported and the skills of graduates and workers need to be matched to labour market demands. the balance between flexibility and security at work and reconciliation of family and professional life must be improved. member states must take the necessary measures to reform the pension system and to create good working conditions until old age, in order to prevent poverty and social exclusion.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on social investment pact as i believe that is a good response to the crisis. the idea set forth in this agreement shall be an exit strategy from the economic and social crisis. a crisis that is still a real threat to the stability of many european union countries which are facing enormous problems, especially in terms of unemployment. even more worrying are the rate of youth unemployment and the chronic lack of jobs among people with low but also high qualifications. the crisis requires not only to remodel social policies of the member states but also to actively transform the welfare state, in a state that invests in people, in a state that provides citizens with the tools and incentives, in a state gives them a chance to build a real career and a real future.

in writing. − one of our main objectives, as representatives of the citizens of the european union, is to restore sustainable economic growth in europe. it is our duty to help society to adapt to the constant and difficult economic changes and labour market demands, and we need to provide an effective response, as manifested by well-targeted social investment. with the unemployment rate continuing to rise, we must focus on reintegrating the unemployed into the labour market and creating new jobs that are sustainable and, most importantly, accessible to a wide variety of disadvantaged groups. i believe that more attention needs to be paid to the difficult situations which arise in the case of young unemployed people. the european commission should, in my view, support apprenticeship systems and the growth of apprenticeship numbers, taking as a reference the dual system of education and vocational training in countries such as germany or austria, which is an essential component of the transition of young people from studies to the labour market. i am also pleased that most of my proposals are reflected in my colleague danuta jazłowiecka's report, which is a comprehensive report on this sensitive subject.
in writing. - i voted for the social investment pact. in 2011, the poverty rate for 16-24 year olds in europe averaged 21.6%, and young people are more likely to be in precarious, fixed-term or part-time jobs, while also being more likely to be unemployed. social investment should be an important part of the economic and employment policies and crisis responses of the eu and the member states in order to achieve the social, employment and education objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. all social and health and education benefits, and services provided in these areas by private sector providers, can be considered social investments. i would remind you that these are defined in the treaties as part of national competence. facilitating and focusing on social entrepreneurship and access to microfinance for vulnerable groups and those furthest from the labour market are key elements in the context of social investment, as they allow for the creation of new and sustainable jobs, often resulting in permanent changes in the business cycle.
