member of the commission. − mr president, the commission presented the reform proposal for the eu data protection regime in january for two reasons: first, to ensure a high level of data protection for individuals as provided for in the treaties and second, to offer european businesses a future-proof and technologically neutral data protection regime. we must now make rapid progress to reach agreement on the package on the table. in parliament the progress has been particularly noticeable in the different working documents and draft reports prepared by the rapporteurs. for the commission, progress means that the regulation and the directive continue to be negotiated as a package. the freedom and security of our european citizens are two sides of the same coin. these are two policy objectives that should be reached with the adoption of the proposals to reform the european union rules on data protection. as regards the personal data processed in the context of police and judicial cooperation, we currently have a multitude of rules and different legal instruments. the entry into force of the lisbon treaty allows the establishment of a comprehensive data protection framework. we can ensure a high level of protection for individuals’ data whilst respecting the specific nature of the field of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. in particular, the revised eu data protection framework can now cover both cross-border and domestic processing of personal data. this would reduce differences between the legislation in member states. the status quo may not always facilitate the smooth exchange of information between member states. the rules set by the pre-lisbon framework decision that the proposed directive aims to replace are limited to cross-border processing. in practice, police and law enforcement authorities may not have always distinguished between cross-border and domestic processing. it is not always feasible to draw this distinction in the daily work of a policeman or of a court. for instance, a single national database used in the law enforcement field may contain personal data that were both collected nationally and received from another member state. it would be inefficient to create two separate databases in such situations; it would also be inefficient to apply two different sets of data protection rules within a single database. the proposed directive aims to cover both domestic and cross-border processing. this has been a longstanding request from parliament. the proposed directive also contains the same protection principles as those enshrined in the regulation. this also echoes parliament’s request to extend the application of the general data protection rules to the areas of police and judicial cooperation. key elements enshrined in the draft regulation are also introduced in the proposed directive, such as: data protection by design and by default; the appointment of data protection officers; the obligation to notify personal data breaches; and the extension of the powers of the commission to adopt adequacy decisions for international transfers to third countries. these novelties emphasise the importance of robust protection rules in instruments allowing for data exchange. let us never lose sight of the fact that the protection of personal data is a right enshrined in the union’s treaties and in the charter of fundamental rights. this is why the new data protection rules will have to be taken into account in sectoral instruments, in particular in the area of the former third pillar. once a directive has entered into force the commission, within three years, will have to review and possibly amend other acts adopted by the european union which regulate the processing of personal data by law enforcement authorities.

member of the commission. − madam president, let me start by excusing commissioner de gucht, who is at this moment negotiating with his canadian counterparts on the free trade agreement with canada. the commission is very grateful to mr leichtfried, the rapporteur, to chairman moreira, and to the other honourable members who worked on this report, and for the overall support for the commission’s proposal. the european parliament has proposed many amendments, most of which we can accept. in particular, the commission can accept the change to the period of time of the delegation, from unlimited to a five-year period with tacit renewal. however, certain amendments are not acceptable to us. some of them deviate from the common understanding on delegated acts that the three institutions have committed themselves to respecting. this concerns, for example, amendments which impose specific obligations on the commission in the preparation of delegated acts. other amendments prolong the period for objection to a delegated act. we cannot accept this, unless the extension of such a period is justified by the specificities of the regulation concerned. as for those amendments on which we have different positions, the commission is confident that we will be able to have constructive discussions in the trialogue, with a view to finding an acceptable solution. let me conclude by registering the commission’s appreciation of the work done on this issue. we look forward to working with parliament to bring it to a conclusion by reaching an agreement in the trialogue.
i welcome the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending ten regulations on the common commercial policy in accordance with the provisions of the treaty of lisbon. i would like to congratulate my colleague, mr jörg leichtfried, on the work he has done in producing this technical report, which is so important for the smooth functioning of the interinstitutional system. it is well known that, in the european institutional sphere, the european parliament and the council have the responsibility for adopting legislation. however, the treaty of lisbon introduces delegated acts for the first time in european law, through article 290. parliament and the council can thus delegate to the commission the power to adopt non-legislative acts, by delegating part of their respective powers, in order to facilitate the adoption of more effective decisions. the two co-legislators, on the other hand, retain the right to revoke the delegation at any time or to object within a certain time-limit. in this context, i share the rapporteur's view on the possibility of ensuring access for parliament's experts to expert meetings organised by the commission, with a view to preparing and implementing delegated acts in respect of regulations relating to the common commercial policy. at the same time, i agree to limit the delegation of powers to the commission to a period of five years. i think that this way parliament maintains greater control over the decisions of the european executive.
in a relatively short time, the economies of the european union and china have reached an impressive level of interdependence. the trade flow between the two partners currently amounts to around one billion euros a day, and the economic partnership between the european union and china is the second most significant globally. although beijing joined the wto in 2001, its trade relations with the eu continue to be often marked by the imposition of barriers to the movement of goods and services. these include difficult market access for economic operators, restrictions on exports of raw materials, the use of subsidies and dumping. the commission, as the commissioner said, has recently launched, following complaints from european companies, two investigations into the sale of chinese solar panels at artificially low prices. in fact, it is estimated that these products are sold at prices that are up to 80% below their cost of production. the european union benefits considerably from trade relations with china, but the type of behaviour mentioned above affects the ability of european companies to remain competitive in a context where the european union needs to promote its industries and create jobs. i believe that relations between the european union and china need to be strengthened, but they must be based on reciprocity and respect for trade rules. that is why i ask you, commissioner, in addition to the urgent analysis you must make, as other colleagues have asked, to take measures to protect european workers and businesses, in effect by developing an industrial strategy, as my predecessor has said.

mr president, any eu member state can be stricken by a natural or man-made disaster, or even be a victim of aggression such as a terrorist attack. we must be able to react fast to such instances and provide support to a fellow member state. this is why member states and the european union must develop a policy for the prevention of and response to all major security threats identified. better safe than sorry. creating a voluntary pool of pre-committed civil protection assets would, for example, much improve eu readiness. another crucial issue is to find a proper balance that would allow for a quick response, involvement of all eu institutions, and enforcement of the principle of accountability for the decisions taken. accountability is vital.

mr president, in march 2011 the european parliament faced a cyber attack that targeted its computer network. a week before, the european commission was the victim of a similar attack. cyber threats and attacks against government, administration, military and international bodies are a rapidly growing menace. we must address them and protect our communication structures and infrastructures from any kind of intrusion. our first step is to update the european security strategy in order to identify how to pursue and prosecute individual, network-related and state-supported cyber attackers. other conditions, sine qua non, are the development of an eu cyber security strategy with a common definition of cyber security and defence, and the creation of a critical infrastructure warning information network at the european level. i would also like to say that cyber criminality is not limited to cyber attacks: vulnerable populations are also targeted by criminals acting from behind the computer. we must, therefore, also take steps in this direction.

in writing. - i voted for the report on the baltic salmon stocks and the fisheries exploiting them. according to scientific advice, improper stock enrichment practices can have significant implications for the genetic diversity of baltic salmon stocks. there is also a risk that the high number of farmed fish dispersed annually in the baltic sea will affect the genetic integrity of wild salmon populations. i think that stock enrichment should be subject to stricter controls. in addition, the conditions governing the procurement of genetic material for the propagation and growth of salmon breeding stock, as well as the conditions applicable to stock enrichment procedures, should be laid down in the multiannual plan, in order to ensure that stock enrichment does not have adverse effects on genetic diversity. the commission should ensure that member states take the necessary administrative or criminal measures to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. i consider that the member states concerned should provide and publish reports containing data on the return of female salmon to their rivers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the delegation of power to adopt certain measures relating to the common commercial policy. the proposal aims to adapt a number of regulations in the field of commercial policy to the new primary law provisions of the treaty of lisbon. the proposal aims to align the regulations with article 290, which introduces delegated acts into european law for the first time. article 290 allows the legislator to delegate to the commission the power to adopt non-legislative acts of general scope supplementing or amending certain non-essential elements of a legislative act. the legislator still has the right to revoke the delegation at any time and then take a decision himself. in addition, any decision taken in the form of a delegated act may be subject to a veto by the legislator. it is therefore sufficient for either the council or parliament to oppose a draft delegated act proposed by the commission. the parliament's proposal limits the delegation of powers to the commission to a period of five years. the commission shall submit a report on the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the extension of the technical rules for a further transitional period is necessary given that a regionalised framework for technical measures has not yet been adopted in line with the common fisheries policy. i agree with the proposal on transitional technical measures, but i believe that the european parliament and the council must do everything possible to reach a political agreement on this complex cfp issue in good time. it is very important that european fishermen have a clear and explicit legal framework in their field of activity. i welcome the fact that the report proposes not only to extend the validity of the current technical measures but also to update the existing ones. i believe that with the adoption of this report and the subsequent adoption of a regionalised legal framework, a sustainable way of fishing will be ensured.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the conservation of pine fishery resources and technical measures to protect the seaweed nursery. a new framework for technical conservation measures is expected in the context of the ongoing reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp). the unlikely entry into force of this new framework before the end of 2012 justifies the extension of the application of these transitional technical measures. i stress the importance of continuing the conservation and proper management of marine biological resources. council regulation (ec) no 850/98 of 30 march 1998 should be updated by incorporating the transitional technical measures into its text. in order to ensure the continued conservation and proper management of marine biological resources in the black sea, it is necessary to establish the minimum landing size and the minimum mesh size for the cod fishery. an equivalent measure for the minimum landing size for hams should also be introduced in terms of fish per kilogram, in order to simplify the work on board vessels catching this species and to facilitate control measures ashore.
in writing. - i voted against this report because i believe that in some cases the possibility of obtaining derogations from regulation 1185/2003 is acceptable. i would point out that no evidence is presented to prove the practice of 'finning' in european waters and/or by the european fleet. i therefore consider that the adoption of this report is contrary to the commission's principle of basing its policy actions on scientific data. furthermore, i consider that a quantitative assessment of the socioeconomic impact is strictly necessary in this case, and this is currently lacking. i therefore consider that, as long as there are no scientific data on the practice of 'finning' in european waters, derogations from the existing regulation may be allowed.
in writing. − this barbaric practice of cutting the fins off of sharks on board ships and then dumping their bodies into the sea continues to be widely practiced around the globe and has led to dramatic declines in the populations of these hunted species. the 2003 official eu regulation allows member states to issue special fishing permits, which authorise on-board processing, so that the fins of sharks can be detached from carcasses by respecting the proportions of fins allowed to be removed. however, there have been many cases where fishermen have landed their floats and carcases in different ports. i therefore believe it is very important that the competent authorities in the european union extend checks and inspections to ensure that the regulation is strictly enforced and to punish those who violate it. i also recommend that these rules apply not only to fishing vessels flying the flag of the member states but also to all vessels in european union maritime waters.
in writing. − i welcome the fact that the european commission responded positively to parliament’s written declaration on this issue and proposed to close the loophole in the shark finning regulation. the delicate marine eco-system is continually put at risk by overfishing, but the cruel practice of shark finning is particularly damaging because of the additional vulnerability of shark populations. i voted against those attempts by some members to allow the loophole to remain open. the long term sustainability of the fishing sector – and with it our food security – will be ensured by effective, enforceable regulation, not laws with loopholes.
in writing. - i voted against the report on the removal of sharks' fins from ships. examination of shark catches rates generally indicates that many stocks are seriously threatened, although the situation is not the same for all species, or even for the same species in different sea areas. according to the international union for conservation of nature (iucn), more than 25 percent of all pelagic shark species, of which more than 50 percent are large ocean pelagic sharks, are threatened. in recent years, the catching, keeping, transhipping or landing of an increasing number of shark species, including highly commercially valuable swimming sharks, has been prohibited under union law or in the framework of regional fisheries management organisations. blue and mako sharks, classified by the iucn as 'endangered' and 'vulnerable' respectively, are currently the predominant shark species caught by the european fleet, with blue sharks accounting for around 70% of all reported shark landings. however, other species, including hammerhead and tiger sharks, are caught in union waters and outside the union and contribute to the economic viability of the fisheries sector.
in writing. − the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is of great importance, because it establishes a system allowing participating states to cooperate in order to find a solution to international child abductions, by determining which courts are competent and which law is applicable when deciding where the child should reside. we know that the european union has obtained exclusive external competence in the field of international child abduction. the accession of new states (gabon, andorra, the seychelles, the russian federation, albania, singapore, morocco and armenia) should be accepted by those states which are already members in order for the convention to apply between them. given that the convention does not allow international organisations to become members, the european union should empower the member states to act in its interest when accepting the abovementioned accessions. in the interest of european citizens who would benefit from the adoption of those decisions, it should renounce efforts to impede the proper functioning of the european union on false legal grounds.
in writing. − serious situations of trafficking in persons, especially minors, raise an alarm that prevention measures are ineffective or too slow. it is our duty to bring protection against this phenomenon back into the light. every moment lost because of the council's lack of communication has had a negative impact on the many horrible situations that some children find themselves in. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 helps in the fight against the trafficking of minors. it establishes an effective system, allowing participating states to cooperate in finding solutions to international child abductions and in rapid repatriation; therefore, the accession of the 8 third countries is of utmost importance. in my view, the council must take immediate steps to adopt the decisions proposed by the commission and stop delaying the adoption of the decisions by invoking various shoddy legal grounds. i fully agree with my colleagues that the eight countries should rush to join the convention to gain ground in this very unpleasant situation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the acceptance of the accession of eight third countries to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction provides a system for states parties to cooperate in finding a solution to international child abduction by establishing the competent courts and the law applicable when determining the residence of the child. the convention thus provides for the prompt return of abducted children to their countries of residence. the european union has already exercised its internal competence in the field of international child abduction, in particular through regulation (ec) no 2201/2003 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters and the matters of parental responsibility. accession of new states must be accepted by those states which are already members for the purpose of the mutual application of the convention. the convention does not allow international organizations to become members. the european union should empower member states to act in its interest when they accept the accessions mentioned above.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the forthcoming world conference on international telecommunications (wcit-2012) of the international telecommunications organisation (itu) and the possible extension of the scope of international telecommunications regulations. i consider it important that all amendments to international telecommunications regulations are compatible with the eu acquis and facilitate the achievement of the objective of promoting the internet as a truly public space, where human rights and fundamental freedoms, in particular freedom of expression and assembly, are respected and compliance with the principles of the free market, net neutrality and entrepreneurship is guaranteed. i support any proposals to maintain the current scope of international telecommunications regulations (itrs) and the current mandate of the itu and consider that the itu or any other single centralized international institution is not an appropriate body to exercise regulatory authority over the governance of the internet or internet traffic flows. we call on member states to prevent any changes to international telecommunications regulations that could affect the open nature of the internet, network neutrality, end-to-end principle, universal service obligations and multi-actor participatory governance.
in writing. − climate change is undeniably real and represents the greatest environmental threat facing humanity. the european union is making considerable efforts to reduce its member states' greenhouse gas emissions and to encourage other countries around the world to follow suit. there is no silver bullet to stop climate change, and that is why i believe it is absolutely necessary to reach a consensus among all countries in their efforts to limit carbon dioxide emissions. a new international agreement on reducing emissions is imperative. in this respect, the eu must play a more active and influential role in international climate change negotiations. all eu institutions need to further expand their climate diplomacy to make the eu's position on climate change policy clearer and to convince partners around the world, including china and the united states, that it is in everyone's interest to participate in an international agreement.
in writing. − the degradation of the earth's climate is a constant danger. the durban platform recognises that climate change is an irreversible threat to people and the planet. the eu delegation plays a vital role in the climate change negotiations - we are responsible for developing the basis for international agreements on environmental protection. the doha climate change plan must be implemented by 2020: global emissions must be reduced by at least 50%. this is an emergency. recent studies show that climate change is getting worse, severely affecting the arctic region and especially the people living in poor countries. i believe the top priority is to phase out fossil fuel subsidies and redirect funds to climate finance and r&d investment. i recommend using funds extracted from international financial transaction fees and international shipping/air taxes. i agree with my colleagues that in order to combat this phenomenon we must coordinate european decision-making powers. the eu must speak with one voice, alongside the world, and the pretext of economic crisis for inaction and non-cooperation must be removed.
in writing. − if we think back a few years to the copenhagen conference and the importance which was attached to it, it is quite striking how little media attention the subsequent negotiations in cancún and durban have received in comparison. this has obscured the fact that these more recent negotiations have in fact produced constructive – if modest – progress. the developments we have seen on issues such as forestry monitoring and reporting and the clean development mechanism are both encouraging and significant. they might not always be headline news, but they show that international cooperation is working and that meaningful progress can be made. we should continue to build on this progress, especially in the area of forestry and financing. deforestation is one of the single biggest contributory factors to co2 increases. effective international forestry management will not only reduce these emissions, but will also help preserve biodiversity and the invaluable eco-services it provides. we do not have to wait for a finalised international agreement on emissions before we put in place concrete measures which will deliver not only co2 reduction but also wider environmental, economic and societal benefits in the medium and long term.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the doha climate change conference. climate change is an immediate and potentially irreversible threat to human societies and the planet, and therefore requires international action. according to the international energy agency (iea), global energy demand is projected to increase by one third between 2010 and 2035. most of the gradual increase in energy demand and emissions will occur in emerging economies. decarbonising the industry and energy sector through innovation would be an asset for the eu, given its pioneering role in the growing global market for energy goods and services. i believe that ensuring policy coherence and mainstreaming environmental protection in development projects are essential to the effectiveness of the eu's climate change mitigation and adaptation strategy. i stress the urgent need to avoid a funding gap beyond 2012 and to identify a way to secure climate finance for the period 2013-2020.
in writing. − the process of enlargement by accepting new member states has been on the agenda of the european union since its inception, and the last decade has shown that enlargement benefits the union as a whole and makes it better equipped to face global challenges. while enlargement of the union is desirable, it is necessary for states wishing to become eu members to fulfil all the accession criteria set out in union law and to be able to fulfil the obligations they have assumed. this report underlines that the issue of enlargement of the european union must be treated with increased attention in the current context, looking not only at the reforms that a state is able to carry out to align with european standards, but also at the union's capacity to integrate new states into the european construction. i believe that in the process of negotiations with countries wishing to join the european union, the respect for fundamental rights and the proper functioning of the justice system should be a priority criterion.
in writing. − enlargement is a successful process for the eu, contributing to peace, stability and prosperity across europe. the eu also continues to be attractive because of its unique combination of economic dynamism and a social model, and i regret that this social dimension is largely neglected by the enlargement process. the social acquis includes minimum standards in areas such as labour law, equal treatment between men and women, and health and safety at work. failure to comply with basic social standards constitutes a form of social dumping which is to the detriment of european businesses and european workers and would effectively prevent a candidate country from participating in the single market. greater attention should be paid to developing enforcement mechanisms, such as labour inspection, to protect workers and ensure respect for their social rights, health and safety standards, and to combat exploitation, especially of undeclared workers. i also believe that it is important to mainstream gender equality policies. among the countries that deserve to join the european family is the republic of moldova. the negotiations on an association agreement with the eu bear witness to this. a. moldova is a success story because it has made progress with concrete results in a short period of time.
in writing. − in a globalised world, it is beneficial that the european union continues to be attractive to candidate countries through the principles it promotes and its model, and the enlargement process must continue to be based on the copenhagen criteria. these must remain the foundation of the enlargement process, because they will enable the candidate countries, as was the case with the central and eastern states of the continent, to adapt to the requirements of the union and become full eu states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on enlargement: eu policies, criteria and strategic interests. after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, parliament has increased its co-legislative powers, including with regard to the instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa). i voted for the paragraphs which stress that failure to respect the eu's common basic social standards constitutes a form of social dumping which is to the detriment of european businesses and european workers. i also stress the importance of the eu's assistance to the candidate countries. we call on the commission to simplify the administrative procedure and reduce the administrative burden for ipa funding, to increase its accessibility and to strengthen the participation of small and decentralised civil society organisations, trade unions and other beneficiaries. we call for strengthening support for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), which are essential for socioeconomic progress in all countries involved in the accession process. at the same time, we call for attention to be paid to the problems of high unemployment and the integration of the most vulnerable into society. we underline the importance of the use of ipa and neighbourhood policy investments by the candidate countries and for the implementation of the objectives of macro-regional strategies such as the eu strategy for the danube region.
in writing. − as is well known, the common security and defence policy is based on the member states. the european union is currently going through a period of austerity, driven by the global economic crisis, marked by the inclination of european states to keep their defence budgets low. but developments in syria and the congo show that the common security and defence policy remains a strategic need for the eu, and its role cannot exist without the capabilities needed to carry out missions, both territorial defence and those at strategic distance or proximity. we must therefore ensure the convergence and cohesion of initiatives and processes such as 'smart defense' and 'pooling and sharing' in the future, developing eu and nato capabilities in a coordinated and complementary manner.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the implementation of the common security and defence policy. the geostrategic context of the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) and the common european security and defence policy (csdp) is undergoing major changes, in particular as a result of the turmoil in the middle east and north africa and the emergence of new actors with regional or even global ambitions on the international scene. climate change is also a major and multiplying threat to global security, peace and stability. i believe that the european union must respond to these threats and challenges by adopting a united position, thereby ensuring the coherence of its response, acting in a spirit of solidarity between its member states and using all the means and instruments at its disposal to guarantee the peace and security of its citizens. i support the need for a white paper on eu security and defence, which would define the eu's strategic interests in a context of continuously evolving threats, from the perspective of the security capabilities of its member states and the ability of the eu institutions to act in an effective, coherent and united manner.
in writing. - mr paşcu's report is an ambitious and realistic report and i congratulate him on its preparation. i personally believe that we do not need a new instrument at european level, but we need better interaction between the existing instruments. the eu has also established mechanisms for emergency and crisis coordination, european civil protection, the eeas operational and crisis coordination, the eu intelligence analysis centre, the commission's strategic analysis and response capabilities centre, the europol network, the atlas network, argus, the frontex agencies. all these instruments must be adapted and coordinated accordingly. i hope that next month the high representative for foreign affairs will specify the situations that would trigger the solidarity clause, as well as the practical mechanisms for its implementation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on 'eu mutual defence and solidarity clauses: political and operational dimensions', given that the security of eu member states is indivisible and all european citizens must have the same security guarantees and an equal level of protection against traditional and unconventional threats. the defence of peace, security, democracy, human rights, the rule of law and freedom in europe is indispensable for the good of our peoples and must remain a fundamental objective and responsibility of the european countries and the union. i believe that european countries need to have credible military capabilities and i encourage member states to step up their collaborative efforts in military capability development, in particular through the eu-nato 'sharing and sharing' and 'intelligent defence' complementary initiatives, which are a very important solution for times of defence budgetary constraints. where a member state is the victim of a terrorist attack or of a natural or man-made disaster, the union and the member states shall act jointly in a spirit of solidarity to provide assistance at the request of the political authorities of that member state.
in writing. − in recent years, both public and private sector it emergency response teams have been established in the form of small clusters of it experts who can react quickly and effectively to information security incidents and cyber threats. they have proven to be a key component in the strategy to defend against these threats by preventing, detecting and correcting vulnerabilities and security breaches. the teams thus warn their clients of vulnerabilities and threats and can recommend risk mitigation actions.
in writing. − i believe that the protection of critical information infrastructures should be included in the european union's internal security strategy, in the context of increasing the level of security of citizens and businesses in cyberspace.
in writing. - i voted for the report on defence and cybersecurity. in today's globalised environment, the eu and its member states rely crucially on a secure information space, on the secure use of resilient and reliable information and technology and on connected infrastructures. in the context of the increasing use of new technologies, challenges, threats and cyber attacks are also increasing at a dramatic rate. they constitute a major threat to security and defence. we call on the commission and the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy to consider the possibility of a serious cyber attack against a member state in the future proposal on measures to implement the solidarity clause (article 22 tfeu). all eu cybersecurity policies must be based on and designed to ensure maximum protection, preservation of digital freedoms and respect for human rights online.
in writing. − global warming and the concrete problems generated by climate change are the great challenge of the century we are living in. finding solutions to limit the effects of this phenomenon is and has always been in the interest of the whole world. at the same time, it is very important that the solution to this problem is practical and easily understood by citizens and those who have to implement public policies of the european union. the fact that the subject of global warming is being debated is certainly a positive thing, but finding solutions to the problems facing the citizens of the european union is equally important. the european union needs to develop not only its political capacity to act to prevent climate change, but also its institutional capacity to intervene to ensure the immediate safety of european citizens in the event of climate-related crises and natural disasters. i believe that the common security and defence policy can be the institutional framework from which we can start to achieve the objective of protecting the population in such situations.
in writing. − in recent years, due to the problems of the economic and financial crisis, climate change has been relegated to the background. extreme weather events that have hit different countries have put new pressure on the world economy through the direct costs of reconstruction and aid, but also in the form of indirect costs in insurance premiums, product and service prices. i believe it is essential that the impact analysis of potential climate-related natural disasters is integrated into the csdp's operational strategies and plans and that we also need to have contingency plans for mitigating risks in the most exposed regions, taking into account the humanitarian principles set out in the lisbon treaty.
in writing. − i believe that the european union needs to consider the security implications of climate change in its dialogues with third countries such as india, and that a truly effective response will require a multilateral approach and joint investments with third countries.
in writing. − i think this topic is debated at the appropriate time, in view of the recent hurricane sandy and especially at this time when the cypriot presidency launched the non-paper on eu military capability development which will contribute to the preparation for the debates focusing on defence issues at the european council in december 2013. there is a need for close coordination, as security is inter-connected with natural disasters. our challenge in the future is to enhance the early warning mechanism and to bring about further movement on early prevention actions. i am glad the rapporteur shared the vision i expressed in my amendment on the need for a climate security envoy within the external action service.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the role of the common security and defence policy in the event of climate-related crises and natural disasters. energy security is closely linked to climate change. energy security must therefore be improved by reducing the eu's dependence on fossil fuels, such as those imported from russia via pipelines that may become vulnerable to disruption due to melting permafrost. i support the need to address the multiplier risk through a strengthened eu strategy for the arctic. we call for the development of a strengthened policy on eu-generated renewable energy and energy efficiency, which will significantly reduce the union's dependence on external sources and consequently improve its security position. i believe it is important to align the wider developments in the european defence industrial base with the specific requirements of climate-related crises and natural disasters. they advocate that public procurement and capacity-building programmes allocate financial means, as well as other appropriate resources, to specific needs to respond to the effects of climate change and natural disasters.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution containing the european parliament's recommendation to the council, the commission and the european external action service on the negotiations for an eu-kazakhstan expanded partnership and cooperation agreement. i attach particular importance to eu-kazakhstan cooperation in the field of energy, in particular in terms of energy security and the development of the trans-caspian energy supply route, as well as attracting investment for projects of common and regional interest in the field of energy. i support the stepping up of technical assistance to kazakhstan in the field of water conservation and water management in general, under the eu's water initiative for central asia. i believe it is important to support kazakhstan in adopting effective measures and programmes on radioactive waste and reducing radioactive pollution in the semey/semipalatinsk region. i believe that the adoption by kazakhstan of eu rules and regulatory systems (including sanitary and phytosanitary (sps) agreements, technical barriers to trade (tbt) and intellectual property rights (ipr)) would lead to increased trade and investment flows, which would promote the modernisation and diversification of the kazakh economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because its provisions place greater emphasis on the specific features of small-scale fishing. the report also attempts to find an appropriate response to the problems currently facing the sector. small-scale fishing has a high potential and therefore needs to be taken more into account in the process of developing the reform of the common fisheries policy. i believe that the flow of information in this area is crucial for more effective management. concrete measures to support small-scale fisheries are needed to ensure that the reform of the common fisheries policy is responsible and sustainable.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on small-scale coastal fishing, artisanal fishing and the reform of the common fisheries policy. it calls on the member states to take into account the importance of the economic, social and cultural role of women in the fishing industry, so that they can access social benefits. the active participation of women in the various fishing activities contributes to the preservation of cultural traditions and specific practices and to the survival of communities, thus ensuring the protection of the cultural diversity of these regions. i believe that the rules for implementing the future european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) should make it possible to finance actions, in particular in the following areas: improving safety, living and working conditions on board vessels; increasing economic and environmental sustainability; investing in more sustainable fishing gear; building specialised fishing ports with specific facilities for landing, storing and selling fishery products; promoting and marketing artisanal fisheries and extensive aquaculture products by creating a european label; supporting education and marketing campaigns to inform consumers and young people about the importance of small-scale fishing for consumers.
in writing. − in the context of the 2014 european parliamentary elections, european political families must propose candidates for the presidency of the commission and candidates must play an important role in the parliamentary election campaign. it is important to strengthen the political legitimacy of both parliament and the commission by linking their choice more directly to the choices of the electorate. it is well known that women are underrepresented in politics, although they have an indispensable role in resolving crises and conflicts. women have demonstrated internationally that it is imperative that they participate in global politics. the european commission must generate legislative proposals on gender equality in politics, and the rest of the european institutions must extend equality at all levels. the proportion of women in political decision-making has not increased in recent years, and in some decision-making structures this proportion has even declined. although i voted for equal participation of women and men in the elections to the ep, which would have guaranteed balanced representation in the european forum, i regret that the plenary of the parliament did not vote, especially the european right, on the effective achievement of gender equality.
in writing. − in preparing for the next elections to the european parliament, in addition to the technical details of organisation, i believe it is important to focus on how to attract as high a share of the electorate as possible to the polls. considering that the 2009 elections for the european union's legislative forum had the lowest turnout in the institution's 30-year history, with only 43% of eu citizens entitled to vote, i appreciate the need for large-scale campaigns to inform citizens about the importance of expressing their electoral choices. i also believe that people should be aware that the european parliament now has much more power than in the past, after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, and it is inconceivable that the representatives of the citizens, that is, those who will use this power, should be voted by less than half of those whom they will directly influence through their decisions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution of 22 november 2012 on the 2014 elections to the european parliament. citizens are directly represented at union level by members of the european parliament, and the president of the european commission is elected by parliament on a proposal from the european council, acting by a qualified majority on the basis of the results of the elections to the european parliament. the european council should have had appropriate consultations before making the nomination. we call on the next president of the commission to ensure that the european commission is a balanced representation of women and men and we recommend that each member state nominate both a female and a male candidate for the next college of commissioners. parliament calls on the member states to establish in their electoral law, in accordance with article 3 of the act concerning the election of the representatives of the legislative assembly by direct universal suffrage, appropriate and proportionate minimum thresholds for the allocation of seats, so as to reflect adequately the choices of citizens expressed at the elections. however, i am not in favour of holding elections to the european parliament in may.
sattar beheshti is not just another example of the restriction of freedom of expression, he is the representative of a civil society whose aspirations for freedom are systematically brutally crushed. but as long as there is a civil society in iran, the european parliament will not stop defending its fundamental rights. i therefore call on the iranian authorities to investigate impartially the circumstances that led to the death in custody of sattar beheshti and to inform his family of the outcome of the investigation. i would also like to express my concern about the sakharov prize winners, nasrin sotoudeh and jafar panahi, and call on the iranian authorities to stop their crackdown on civil society.
the recent death of iranian blogger sattar beheshti is emblematic of the dramatic human rights situation in that country. here in parliament, we have repeatedly denounced human rights violations in iran. indeed, the defenders of these rights - journalists, bloggers, artists, students, lawyers, trade unionists - are regularly subjected to government pressure and live under the constant threat of ending up in iranian jails. this was the fate of beheshti, whose courage in exposing the abuses of the iranian regime was rewarded with death in prison. and worse, according to multiple sources, his death is the result of torture he was subjected to. when we know iran's history of deaths in prison, this conclusion is perfectly justified. however, we must insist that this case be investigated and the guilty punished. as one of the supporters of the epp group in the nomination of nasrin sotoudeh and jafar panahi for the sakharov prize, i conclude by calling for their immediate release.
the murder of iranian blogger sattar beheshti is all the more shocking as it is the death of a man who did nothing but peacefully express his opinions on a blog. it is one of the many crimes of the regime in tehran, which demonstrates its inhuman absurdity. as has been said here, we must do more than condemn, of course, in the strongest possible terms, this outrageous crime, to the end of the inhuman torture to which this young blogger has been subjected in prison. i also call on the iranian authorities to investigate this crime and to end the brutal repression against freedom of expression. the european union also has an obligation to urge iran to establish a moratorium on executions, the number of which is worryingly increasing, and to take the step towards abolishing the death penalty, which is now applied even to minors. sanctions are needed to compel the iranian authorities to respect the fundamental rights of the human being and the citizens of this country.
freedom of speech is one of the fundamental principles of a democracy. that's why the iranian blogger's case is of particular concern to me. his arrest and death, in at least suspicious circumstances, raises questions about the iranian authorities' defense of democratic principles. such practices should be discouraged by all means. the union, as a promoter of fundamental rights, should find ways to put pressure on the iranian authorities. political prisoners must be released immediately and discrimination against religious minorities must end. i am referring in particular to the sakharov prize winners, who must be able to receive their award in parliament in december. for iran to regain its credibility, it must abide by the international covenant on civil and political rights.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank members for their very pertinent views and for the serious debate today. the european union is seriously concerned about the deteriorating human rights record in iran. the continuous repression of political opponents, human rights defenders, journalists, artists, bloggers, lawyers, women and minority groups is a real problem. the european parliament is playing an important role in denouncing this situation. the award of this year’s sakharov prize to two leading iranians defending freedom of thought – the lawyer nasrin sotoudeh, and the film director jafar penahi – is a very significant example of parliament’s commitment to human rights. the tragic death of blogger sattar beheshti in custody is a poignant example of the precarious situation of human rights activists in iran. the european union responded swiftly by urging the iranian authorities to conduct a thorough investigation into the circumstances of his death. afterwards the iranian judiciary announced that an inquiry had been launched and that the persons responsible would be prosecuted. we shall of course closely follow developments. early october saw a spate of arrests of prominent human rights lawyers. the eu reacted to this on several fronts by summoning the iranian ambassador to the eu in brussels, issuing a statement and carrying out a démarche in tehran. iran’s extensive use of the death penalty is particularly worrisome. so far we have confirmation of 338 executions this year. this reconfirms that iran is one of the world’s most frequent users of capital punishment. in addition, collective and public executions are common in iran. the eu has a strong stance against the death penalty and we have repeatedly condemned executions in iran. the high representative and vice-president, catherine ashton, issued her latest statement on 23 october condemning the collective executions of 10 iranians charged with drug smuggling. the eu also remains deeply concerned about the position of ethnic and religious minorities in iran. despite constitutional guarantees of equality, they are subject to an array of discriminatory laws and practices. we are using all tools available to raise awareness and call on iran to respect the principles of equal treatment and non-discrimination. we recall that 78 on behalf of the alde group. – madam president, the commission’s approach to negotiations with latin america has always been a ‘region-to-region’ approach. nevertheless, so far none of the agreements have been concluded. the association agreement with the andean community has failed and instead tomorrow we will approve, i am convinced, a multi-party agreement with colombia and peru. at the same time, the negotiations with mercosur are rather hectic and unpredictable due to a number of things, including the versatile membership of mercosur, which means that the association agreement we are discussing today with central america is the first concluded by the eu after the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. more importantly, it is the first comprehensive partnership between the regions which marks the result of the parties’ unbending political will. this association agreement contains three main pillars – political dialogue, cooperation and trade – thus marking a decisive step forwards in the integration of central america and going far beyond mere questions of free trade. it is, at the minimum, the starting point for a coherent and holistic approach towards cooperation between the parties. otherwise, can we sincerely believe that the eu, particularly now in these times of economic and social crisis within its own territory, would conclude association or partnership agreements with each and every country in central america? of course i am aware of the asymmetries which exist between the two regions and among the central american countries, and i am conscious of the efforts to be made in order to generate greater synergies between both regions, but i also truly hope that this agreement will bring benefits to all parties and boost integration on a regional, social, economic and cultural level.

antimicrobial resistance has dangerous implications for human and animal health. in the european union, norway and iceland, antimicrobial-resistant bacteria have caused about 400 000 infections and 25 000 deaths annually, with costs in additional healthcare and lost productivity of at least €1.5 billion. we call for support for research into new antimicrobials, alternatives to them, and scientifically based strategies to avoid infectious diseases. we call on the european food safety authority to pay particular attention to the monitoring and analysis of the antimicrobial resistance situation in the union. the commission and the member states, in agreement with the competent union agencies, should develop and promote prudent use guidelines with the aim of reducing non-essential and inappropriate exposure to antimicrobials in human and veterinary medicine.
in writing. the resolution on the threat of antibiotic resistance, for which i was the epp group rapporteur in the committee on agriculture, is a step forward in effectively addressing this challenge. as i have said in the amendments approved by the committee on agriculture, the main aim of a farmer must be to raise animals in a healthy and productive way and to ensure their welfare, and the appropriate use of antimicrobials is a necessary tool. we must be constantly aware that antibiotics could become completely useless in treatment, because of their misuse and overuse. increased resistance to antimicrobials commonly used in veterinary medicine also leads to production losses, increased costs and occupational risks for farmers. however, a complete ban on antibiotics is a misguided and impractical approach, and is necessary in many situations. i therefore consider that the position taken in the report is a balanced one and should be approved in the form proposed by the commission.
in writing. to find the right solutions to the phenomenon of antimicrobial resistance, we need to look at the causes that have led to this situation. these are primarily the inadequate use of antibiotics in human and veterinary medicine, but also a slow pace of innovation in the discovery of new antibiotics. the fact that we have fewer and fewer effective treatments available for certain multidrug-resistant infections such as tuberculosis (tb) or pneumonia indicates the need for urgent action by member states in this field. the most important measures include investments in research and development, namely the discovery of new antibiotics and vaccines, improved cooperation between member states, and intensive information and education of the public on the responsible use of antibiotics in both human and veterinary medicine. given the cross-border nature of these chemoresistant infections, the european commission has a responsibility to help member states financially to meet such challenges. even if there is political will in some countries, such as romania, which has already developed an effective plan to fight multidrug-resistant tb, they often cannot cope with the costs involved.

the digital freedom strategy in the european union's foreign policy recognises that uncensored access to the open internet, mobile phones, communications and information technology has had a real impact on human rights and fundamental freedoms. information and communication technology facilitates transparency and good governance, literacy, education, assistance, effective election monitoring and disaster relief, particularly in remote areas and in developing societies. effective european union development and human rights policies require the integration of information and communication technology and the closing of the digital divide by providing basic technological infrastructures, facilitating access to knowledge and information and promoting digital skills worldwide. union development and human rights programmes should include aid programmes promoting digital freedoms, in particular in non-democratic countries, as well as in countries in a period of political transition or in post-conflict situations.
a fragmented patent market and differences in law enforcement impede innovation and progress within the internal market, complicate the use of the patent system and hinder the effective protection of patents, in particular for smes. the creation of the european union patent is an opportunity to strengthen innovation in europe. a perfectly unitary european patent may be licensed for the whole or part of the territory of the participating member states. the unitary patent should reduce the costs for applicants by about 70%. the level of renewal fees is set taking into account, inter alia, the situation of specific entities such as smes. however, i believe it is essential to ensure both the linguistic register for all member states and the legal value of translations into all the official languages of the union. unfortunately, machine translation does not ensure the legal value of translations. finally, i believe that romania should host a regional division for south-east europe within the community patent jurisdiction system.
the establishment of a single court will establish a coherent system for the settlement of patent disputes. i believe that the existence of such a court is particularly useful in relation to software applications, for which patenting varies considerably from one state to another. my recommendation for future structures dealing with unitary patents is to pay particular attention to the system of protection of new technologies, especially software applications, in order to grant good quality patents and to avoid litigation and lawsuits. i also believe that in the future the quality of translations should be improved by using specialists in technical translation. the current level of machine translation software is too low to achieve the quality required by specialized technical-legal language.
in writing. the adoption of a single european union patent is a historic decision. after nearly 40 years of negotiations, an agreement was reached on the establishment of a community patent. although not all countries will participate in enhanced cooperation, i hope that in the future the patent will apply in all countries of the union. until now, the cost of validating a patent in half the member states was 10 times higher than in the united states or japan. this was a major reduction in the competitiveness of european firms, particularly affecting smes. in the context of the fact that smes are the main engine of growth and innovation in the union, they need to be supported. at the same time, ensuring uniform protection will stimulate innovation among european entrepreneurs. last but not least, i believe that the creation of a single patent court is one of the conditions for the functioning of the community patent system. it will improve the application of patents in the union, provide legal certainty and lead to the strengthening of the single market. the adoption of a community patent will contribute to deepening the single market and increasing the union's global competitiveness. if europe is to be at the forefront of innovation, unitary patent protection at union level is indispensable.
in writing. i am delighted that after 40 years of discussions, we can finally say that we have a european patent to protect european inventions. if we really want to boost innovation and the eu's economic competitiveness, i think this instrument was absolutely necessary. the single european patent will considerably reduce the costs of protecting inventions. it is estimated that the cost reduction could be as high as 80%, which can only be beneficial for eu companies competing on the world market with firms in the united states or japan, where the patent process involves much lower costs than in the eu today. i welcome the result that has been achieved on the subject of languages. the translation costs would have had a negative impact on the total costs of the procedure. therefore, the use of 3 languages and the automatic translation system is welcome. this will undoubtedly be beneficial for businesses, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, but also for universities and researchers. it is regrettable that, at present, two member states are not participating in this project and i hope that in the future all eu countries will be part of this project, which is vital for boosting the competitiveness of european businesses.

mr president, the european patent is 13 times more expensive than in the united states and 11 times more expensive than in japan, thus suffering from lower productivity and development. we must change this. unitary patent protection has been a goal for several decades, but certain obstacles such as legal uncertainty and high costs have not been eliminated, and this has led to a fragmented and insufficiently competitive system. we need a european patent with unitary effect that will help innovation and increase legal protection that now renders it complex and costly. this is why i say we need to put all our efforts into boosting growth through innovation and help european business, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises, to compete globally, especially during the economic crisis. the unitary patent system is paramount for the future competitive edge of the eu.
mr president, at present the holder of a european patent must have the patent validated separately in all those member states where he seeks protection. to do so, the patent must be translated into the respective national languages. this complex procedure involves very high costs. the overall cost of validation of a european patent averages eur 12 500 if validated in only 13 member states, and over eur 32 000 if validated in all the eu member states. the current european patent system is extremely expensive. it also lacks legal certainty due to the very expensive and risky pursuit of multi-forum litigation, which often results in contradictory judgments in several member states. today we have taken a step forward. the present regulation limits translation arrangements to the three working languages of the european patent office. however, we must acknowledge that english is the predominant language in international trade and promote it as much as possible in our patent system. moreover, even if reduced, translation costs will remain high, especially for small and medium enterprises.
mr president, the establishment of an effective unitary patent protection must come at the same time as a unified jurisdictional system. the unified patent court would replace widely differing national court systems and procedural rules with one coherent system. this will ensure legal certainty and international competitiveness, as well as improving the enforcement of patents. the composition of the court should be multinational to ensure that it is unified, with both legally and technically qualified judges, to ensure the highest capacity in the field of patent litigation and anti-trust law. it also must fully respect and apply union law, as the guardian of the union legal order is the court of justice, and to ensure the uniformity of the union legal order and the primacy of european law. i support the creation of the unified patent court as it would maximise the quality and efficiency of proceedings, cut litigation costs, and ensure legal certainty through the uniform interpretation of the applicable rules.
mr president, i would like to welcome this first region-to-region association agreement between the european union and central america. i believe it is important for the union to continue on the path of regional integration, whhile also strengthening its efforts to promote human rights, rule of law and anti-corruption measures. the agreement achieves these objectives. moreover, the report, which received a two-thirds majority of votes in committee, makes clear our support for democratic principles. the relevant trade provisions go hand-in-hand with clearly spelled-out political objectives. i believe this text strikes a good balance between economic incentives to central america and the creation of proper mechanisms for pressuring governments to fulfil their commitments to democracy and justice and rule of law. i would like, therefore, to show my support for the next negotiation by my colleagues and vote in favour of the important recommendation, which i did.
mr president, i voted in favour of this report and parliament’s consent to the trade agreement between the eu and colombia and peru. union investment is expected to lead to a 1.7% increase in the gross national product of colombia and a 0.7% increase in the gnp of peru. these figures prove that trade improves people’s lives and acts as a catalyst for much-needed political reforms. the special procedure which led to the adoption of this report by the inta committee shows that colombia and peru are willing to address their human rights and environmental protection issues. in the process of negotiating such bilateral agreements the union must always make clear its requests, and support, for political reforms for democracy and justice. parliament has played a positive role; the present consensus is also the result of our joint efforts to make the governments of colombia and peru take concrete steps to fulfil political objectives.
mr president, women have a longer life expectancy than men – 82.4 years as opposed to 76.4 years. however, if we focus solely on healthy life expectancy, the difference is less substantial – 62 years for women and 61 years for men. women might live longer, but unfortunately not healthier. we need to improve our policies on the prevention of diseases. for instance, if the mammography coverage rate were above 70 %, breast cancer deaths among women aged over 50 could be reduced by at least 30 %. targeting actions solely on elderly women is not enough and is the wrong policy. women are facing a broad range of inequalities in their professional life, such as the employment rate scheme or even salary. all these have a major impact later on their pension contributions and will make them particularly vulnerable to situations of insecurity, illness or poverty. this is why we need policies to prevent age-related diseases for women from a very early stage.
mr president, every year antimicrobial-resistant bacteria cause some 400 000 infections and 25 000 deaths in the european union, norway and iceland. antimicrobial resistance also costs at least eur 1.5 billion in extra healthcare costs and productivity losses. for eighty years we have used antimicrobials rather automatically, but this has resulted in their loss of effectiveness. member states must review the legal status of all antimicrobials that are available to patients without a prescription. self-treatment with antimicrobials must be discouraged. new anti-bacterial drug development costs tens of millions of euros in research. development has been pretty rare in the last forty years. it is therefore crucial to maintain the effectiveness of existing antimicrobials and to strengthen incentives for public and private sector cooperation. we cannot afford a return to the pre-antibiotic era.

in writing. − the european union was built around the principle of the common market. although we have made a great deal of progress in this direction, it must be said that there are a number of sectors where we still face significant difficulties. the digital single market is one such sector. there are still barriers to online transactions between eu member states. over 40% of europeans buy goods online, but less than 10% buy from traders operating in other eu countries. this is all the more difficult in the face of the massive growth of online commerce worldwide, as evidenced by the success of companies such as amazon and ebay. moreover, there is a worrying disproportion within member states of households with no access to the internet or with access only to very slow connections, and i am not only talking about the case of romania, where the fact that 50% of households do not have access to the internet can explain the weak development of online commerce, but also about the situation in more developed countries such as spain or italy, where 30% of the population has never used the internet, or the case of poland, where 40% of the population has access to low-speed connections. addressing this issue should be one of the priorities of the european parliament in the coming period.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the council's first reading position with a view to adopting the regulation laying down transitional provisions for bilateral investment agreements concluded between member states and third countries. the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) confers on the european union exclusive competence in the field of foreign direct investment, within the framework of trade policy. thus, only the union can legislate and adopt legally binding acts in an area in which it has been granted exclusive competence. in the absence of an explicit transitional regime in the treaty clarifying the status of agreements concluded by member states, this proposal for a council and parliament regulation will authorize the maintenance of all investment agreements currently in force between member states and third countries. this proposal provides an explicit guarantee of legal certainty as regards the conditions to which investors are subject. the proposal maintains the status quo and provides for a transitional solution, authorising the maintenance in force of bilateral investment agreements concluded between member states and third countries.
