in writing. - i voted in favour of amending the regulation establishing a european maritime safety agency (emsa). emsa contributes to measures taken for maritime safety and security and the prevention of marine pollution from ships, including by monitoring and evaluating the application of relevant eu legislation. much of its work consists of advising the commission and/or the member states. the revised emsa regulation will extend the agency's remit to prevent and manage environmental disasters such as oil spills. the agency will use the cleanseanet information system to monitor the impact of oil pollution from offshore installations. the agency will also work to improve coordination between national authorities to strengthen prevention methods, encourage best practice and speed up the response to disasters. at the request of parliament, the agency will also contribute to the fight against maritime piracy. parliament called for emsa to have a stronger role in improving the training of seafarers. increasing the attractiveness of maritime jobs for eu citizens is a long-term objective. the revised regulation allows the agency to facilitate the exchange of good practice in training and education to meet the current and future demand for highly qualified seafarers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because, so far, the absence of a community patent has affected european smes the most. the costs of patent licensing in several countries, as well as the costs of patent translation, were hindering innovation. compared with competitors in the united states and japan, european companies have to pay up to three times more for patent registration procedures in a single member state. i believe that in the current economic context, smes are the main engines of growth and innovation and they must be supported. i therefore believe that the adoption of a community patent will contribute to deepening the single market and increasing the union's global competitiveness. if europe is to be at the forefront of innovation, unitary patent protection at union level is indispensable.
in writing. − after fourteen years of debate, the european union will finally have a unitary patent system, which will allow small businesses in particular to eliminate a host of red tape and extra costs. the unitary patent will bring benefits to these enterprises, whose innovations will be protected more effectively and more easily, but also to consumers. businesses will be able to grow and open up their services to new markets, and consumers will have access to these services regardless of the member state in which they live. i therefore welcome the adoption of the report and believe that further action is needed to remove unnecessary bureaucratic measures from the burden of small and medium-sized firms in the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation implementing enhanced cooperation in the area of the creation of unitary patent protection, as unitary patent protection will encourage scientific and technical progress and the proper functioning of the internal market through easier, less costly and legally secure access to the patent system. the main feature of a european patent with unitary effect is its unitary character, i.e. it provides uniform protection and has the same effect in all participating member states. unitary protection should be available to holders of european patents both in the participating member states and in other states, irrespective of their nationality, residence or place of establishment. as an object of property, a european patent with unitary effect shall be deemed, in its entirety and in all the participating member states in which it has unitary effect, to be a national patent granted by the participating member state determined in accordance with specific criteria such as the residence, principal place of business or place of business of the applicant. a european patent with unitary effect may be licensed for the whole or part of the territory of the participating member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the objective of creating unitary patent protection in the european union has been pursued for a very long time. until now, the cost of validating a patent in half the member states was 10 times higher than in the united states or japan. this was mainly due to translation costs. the commission therefore concluded that the union industry suffered material injury within the meaning of article 3 (5) of the basic regulation. the introduction of machine translation into the languages of the european patent office will considerably reduce registration costs. and ensuring a single protection will boost innovation among european entrepreneurs. at the same time, smes or natural persons who will obtain european patents should benefit from additional reimbursement of translation costs. the presence of european smes on the international market could thus be better supported and encouraged.
in writing. - i voted for amendments nos 22, 23, 25, 28, 29 and 31 because i believe that there should be legal value for automatic translations as well.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation implementing enhanced cooperation in the field of the creation of unitary patent protection as regards the provisions applicable to translation. i voted for amendments 3 and 7 which require that, once the automatic translation of patent applications and patent descriptions is available in all the languages of the union, in accordance with article 6 (3), it be made available online and free of charge, upon publication of the patent application and the granted patent. i also voted in favour of amendments nos 28, 29 and 31, which require that translations of the patent file into an official language of the participating member states be a translation with legal effect. i regret that the text of the translations provided for in article 6 (2) will have no legal value, and that they are for information only. i voted in favour of amendment no 23, which provides that applicants whose language is not one of the official languages of the european patent office should be able to submit their patent applications and any other procedural documents to the european patent office in any of the official languages of the union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because the creation of a single patent court is one of the conditions for the functioning of the community patent system. the court will improve the application of patents in the union, providing legal certainty and leading to the strengthening of the single market. it will also help to reduce the cost of dispute resolution. and the parties will no longer have to go to courts in different countries in parallel. in particular for smes, it is essential that the judicial system established is efficient and delivers quality judgments. the tribunal should also be composed of judges who are legally and technically qualified and who enjoy full independence. it is also important that the parties are represented by lawyers who have the necessary experience in both patent law and procedural law.
in writing. − i believe that the unified patent court must fully respect and apply union law, in cooperation with the court of justice of the european union, just like any other national court.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the court system for patent disputes as effective protection by unitary patent can only be ensured by a functioning system for the settlement of patent disputes. the priority of the unified patent court should be to strengthen legal certainty and improve patent enforcement, while balancing the interests of rightholders and stakeholders. the court of first instance and the court of appeal must be multinational and the local divisions must be multinational as soon as possible. the tribunal must be composed of judges with legal and technical qualifications and the period for the intensive training and preparation of judges must be five years. there should be a certain set of procedural rules applicable to proceedings before all the divisions and courts of the general court. the language of proceedings before local or regional divisions shall be the official language of the contracting member state in whose territory the division is situated or the official language designated by the contracting member states belonging to the same regional division. the decisions of the general court shall be based on union law, the agreement, the european patent convention (epc) and national legislation adopted pursuant to the epc, the provisions of international agreements applicable to patents and binding on all contracting member states.

on behalf of the alde group. the development of mediation in civil and commercial matters, as well as other mechanisms for out-of-court dispute resolution, represents a real opportunity both for the parties involved and for the judicial system, especially in many of the countries where it is overburdened. the mediation directive is a very useful instrument and i think it is absolutely essential that it is implemented as correctly as possible in order to achieve its objective. if the mediation directive has not so far achieved its objective in terms of the proportion of disputes that are mediated compared to the number of cases that reach the courts, i believe that this is largely due to the lack of information on mediation. even if the directive imposes an obligation to inform the general public about the opportunity to use mediation, i do not think that this provision is being exploited optimally. citizens do not take mediation into account because they simply do not know that it exists, do not know what it is, and do not know who to contact to initiate such a procedure. in the area of trade, the new directive on alternative dispute resolution for consumer disputes, which is being debated in parliament, will certainly bring improvements, as traders will be obliged to provide the general public with information on mediation and other alternative mechanisms. however, this directive has a limited purpose, which is why i believe that both the commission and the member states should promote mediation more actively, especially in cross-border and family law disputes. it is not - and never has been - a question of developing a system parallel to the judicial system; mediation must remain an opportunity and we must find a balance between mediation and judicial proceedings. i do not know whether it is indispensable to set percentage targets for cases under mediation. we must do everything we can to develop a culture of mediation and alternative dispute resolution, which is cheaper and faster than judicial procedures, and which is clearly an advantage for citizens.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i welcome the debate in the european parliament on the situation of fundamental rights. you know that when i took up my duties, one of my first commitments was to present an annual report on the application of the eu charter and to have a general debate every year on the way in which this charter is being applied. by this i was responding, de facto, to a request made by the european parliament one year ago: i would just like to recall the 2007 report of johannes voggenhuber. i am glad to see that today, on the basis of the report prepared by ms flašíková-beňová and the commission’s annual reports, we are able to hold a fully informed discussion. let me start by stressing that, since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty and then of the charter, progress has been achieved on three fronts: firstly, the commission has defined a clear policy on how to put the charter into practice. this was laid down, as you know, in the strategy for the effective implementation of the charter, and it has also ensured that the charter has become a compass for all eu policies. the strategies were assessing the consequences of having a legally binding charter and the measures taken by the commission to ensure its respect: for instance, checking the new legislation for compliance with the charter. so not a single initiative comes from the commission without passing this compliance check with the charter. furthermore, when the commission went before the court of justice to take an oath to respect the treaties, we also gave an oath that we will respect the charter. this is a symbolic act, i know, but it is also a political commitment from the whole college to ensure that the charter is respected. this policy has already brought tangible effects for our citizens because not only does the commission go ahead with putting the charter into practice, but the commission has also been followed by the council. for instance, the impact assessment which the commission makes on its basic texts has been followed by an impact assessment which is carried out by the council on its own amendments to commission proposals. let us not forget that the court of justice is applying more and more rules on the basis of the charter. there are, for instance, two pieces of eu legislation which have been invalidated by the court of justice for non-compliance with the charter. this, i believe, shows that the charter has evolved into a powerful tool. of course, not everything is perfect. however, we can no longer say that the eu institutions do not take fundamental rights seriously. the charter and the active work in promoting its application have ensured that today these rights play a fundamental role in the development of new policies – not only in the general application of the charter, but also in specific policy initiatives dedicated to specific fundamental rights. let me just quote some of them: the agenda on the rights of the child, the eu framework for the national roma integration strategies, the strategy for equality between men and women and the european disability strategy. all these strategies have given a new momentum in these specific areas, and the citizenship report, which is going to be presented in 2013, will look at the very specific area of rights for citizens when crossing borders. it will also present further concrete actions during the european year of citizens to enhance those citizens’ rights. the second front relating to the application of the charter is the effective enforcement of the charter in the member states. you all know our famous article 51, which has been quoted again and again in this chamber: the charter is addressed to the institutions, the bodies, the offices and the agencies of the union, and to the member states only when they are implementing eu law. but in this context, the commission takes very seriously its role as guardian of the treaties. some examples: the question of the roma in france in the summer of 2010 and in the summer of this year, and the actions regarding hungary and romania. these examples reveal our determination to intervene, where necessary, when the commission has the power to do so. let me come to the hungarian example, where the commission did not hesitate to refer hungary very quickly to the court of justice regarding the independence of the data protection supervisory authority and the age of retirement of judges, prosecutors and notaries. we were followed by the court of justice in this case, and now the very short transitional period has been declared incompatible with the eu equal treatment law. hungary will, therefore, have to change these rules in order to comply with the eu law. you will recall the events last summer in romania, where the commission set out in detail its concerns in its report under the verification mechanism adopted on 18 july 2012. the romanian government made a number of important commitments, and the commission is analysing what is happening in practical terms and will issue a further report analysing whether these concerns have been addressed and whether democratic checks and balances have been restored. another very important element is gaining ground, and this can be seen in our national courts. as explained in the 2011 commission annual report, national courts, when addressing questions to the court of justice (preliminary rulings), have increasingly referred to the charter. as compared to 2010, in 2011 these references rose by 50%. that is a very strong progress that means something; that really shows the reflection in our judiciary, not only at the european court of justice, but in our national courts. in general, the reflection that there is this charter and that it needs to be applied is gradually gaining ground. the third front where there was key progress is the development of new secondary legislation on fundamental rights. you know all of those, but let me just quote a few to show you want i mean. the data protection rules, which are real routes to better protection of personal data of individuals, or another element, which is the recently adopted proposal for women on corporate boards. what is interesting in this proposal is that we had to balance several fundamental rights included in the charter: gender equality, of course, but also non-discrimination, which has many court cases dedicated to it, and the freedom to conduct a business. so we have, if we present new legislation, always to strike a balance between different rights. i am sure that the parliament, with its relentless commitment, will turn the commission's proposal into a legally binding act. let me also quickly remind you of all the work which has been done on procedural rights for the accused, but also on the rights of victims in criminal proceedings, and all the new directives which have already been adopted or which will be adopted very soon. the recent adoption of the new directive on victims’ rights will improve the rights of an estimated 75 million crime victims annually across the eu. so, when you really look at what has been done since the charter has become our compass, it is remarkable, although it is a direction in which we are going; we have not reached the destination yet, but we are on the path. let me finish, president, with one remark concerning the fundamental rights agency, which we need in order to support our fundamental rights policy, because the agency has the role of gathering comparative data. if we did not have these data, we would be facing a data gap, and we would then have difficulties in obtaining the necessary evidence to underpin our policies on fundamental rights. this agency is, therefore, really necessary. unfortunately, the good work done by the agency is being jeopardised, as it now seems clear that the council will not be in a position to adopt the multiannual framework for the agency by the end of the year. i am seriously worried about this, because we all knew about the deadline. this also explains why the eu institutions made intense efforts in order to enable an agreement to be reached on time among the member states in the council. that also explains the concessions to the council. the concession, for example, that the agency will not be able to initiate work on police and judicial cooperation on criminal matters on its own initiative. it has to be asked by the parliament, by the commission or by the council. that was something i did not like to give in to, but i gave in for the sake of unanimity in council, in order to get this unanimity. now, in spite of this, one member state has failed to take the necessary steps which would have ensured that the multiannual framework is adopted in time, and as a result the agency and its staff will be in caretaker mode from january. now, we have again here an example of how the requirement of unanimity is blocking the work in the union, so i regret this very much and i hope that the problem can be solved, but it is very unfortunate.
on behalf of the alde group. – mr president, i want first of all to thank the rapporteur for her very good work and for the report she drafted in strong cooperation with us. she has taken on board the suggestions and requests of all the shadows, including the epp, which is why the epp decision to vote against it without any prior notice was equally unexpected and unfair. this is most unfortunate as it sends a negative message to our citizens in relation to this parliament’s position on fundamental rights, putting at risk the adoption of this report, while the epp alternative resolution is completely empty. i cannot but hope that the epp, as a group, will not fall into the trap organised by some of its members to cover up what their national parties are doing back home. the alde group fully supports the report, as it consolidates this house’s continuing concerns in relation to the situation of fundamental rights, democracy and the rule of law in the eu and in its member states. we all know that the european union is experiencing not only an economic crisis but also a deeper crisis in terms of our basic principles and values. this is why we have to use to the maximum all the potential instruments that our treaties give us and reflect on strengthening these powers in the future. the eu institutions should make full use of articles 2 and 7 of the treaty on european union and address the copenhagen dilemma by developing a clear set of indicators, monitoring and sanctioning mechanisms, including an early warning and freezing mechanism that the epp has suggested in the past. among other things, this report also addresses the rights of specific groups such as roma minorities, lgbt persons, people with disabilities, migrants and refugees, which is one more reason to hope that, in the same week when the eu received the nobel peace prize and the world celebrates human rights day, the european parliament will vote in favour of a report on fundamental rights at home.
in writing. in a period marked by continuing economic and financial uncertainties, it has become apparent that economic monitoring and coordination at community level requires significant reinforcement. economic and monetary union will enable the union to achieve its medium and long-term objectives, but i believe that it has been set in the wrong direction from the start. in my view, a genuine economic and monetary union must not be limited to a system of rules. europe needs now more than ever a strengthened budgetary capacity, based on own resources, to support economic growth, facilitate increased competitiveness, support cohesion across the union and lead to the correction of existing macroeconomic imbalances.
i voted in favour of this report because i believe that an increase in payment appropriations is useful to meet the outstanding needs until the end of the year. this will allow commitments to be honoured and financial penalties to be avoided, and beneficiaries to receive funds provided for by union policies. in the context of the risk that cohesion policy or other important union programmes such as erasmus would run out of funding in the last months of the year, the budget amendment was absolutely necessary. i believe that the reduction of expenditure at union level must not affect the union's most successful policies and that to solve problems such as high youth unemployment we need sufficient european social fund funding. the reduction in appropriations for commitments and payments is also necessary to meet real needs by the end of the year.
i voted in favour of the report because, in the context of the economic crisis, the adoption of the 2013 budget is an emergency. i welcome the commission's new proposal because it contains important elements to facilitate convergence between parliament and the council, which has proved to be limited in recent negotiations. the new budget also underlines the importance of honouring previous commitments, particularly at council level. these new elements will contribute to the conclusion of an agreement as soon as possible. i believe that the budget should take account of the fiscal policies of the member states. it must also be complemented by actions aimed at increasing investment and economic stability, and adequate funding for the most important european policies is essential. this will give us a budget that will effectively promote growth and cohesion in europe.
i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the commission's proposal will increase the efficiency of ground handling services. i also believe that the improvement of the legislative framework will ensure an even greater opening of the market. at the same time, however, some important issues remain to be resolved in order to ensure better conditions for passengers. greater transparency and optimisation of services for users are needed. i also believe that the opening of the market for ground handling services in the union should be done in a balanced way. this will avoid a high degree of instability which would generate other problems over time and could lead to higher costs for passengers. i would also like to draw attention to the fact that there must be minimum standards to improve the quality of services and the operation of airports.
i voted in favour of the report because i too believe that the commission's proposal is a first step towards improving efficiency at airports. in this respect, ensuring optimal allocation and use of slots is essential. the system has so far proved ineffective and reinforcing the mechanisms and ensuring their effective application is of the utmost importance to remedy this. at the same time, we need to boost the competitiveness of operators and promote fair competition, and this can be done by increasing the transparency of the procedure. the provisions need to be streamlined and clarified. in addition, i believe that more importance should be given to the independence of coordinators and that the secondary market for airport slots should be better regulated.
mr president, according to the international civil aviation organisation, in just a few years more than five million people in europe will be affected by the high level of noise from aircraft. this is the reason why i totally support this proposal aiming at reducing the number of people affected by the harmful effects of noise due to living in the vicinity of airports. we should pay considerable attention to the economic aspects of this issue, since we are in times of crisis and cost-effectiveness is one of our main priorities. health and social aspects are of high importance in this matter as well. they should be equally considered. we cannot afford to miscalculate the cost and the benefits of noise-related operating restrictions. therefore i call on the commission to lay down the procedures for carrying out complete assessments able to determine whether an operating restriction is a cost-effective method to deal with a noise-related problem.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in my view, the commission's current proposal on european statistics on security vis-à-vis criminals does not clearly address the questions of methodology and funding. common statistics at european union level play a very important role in the field of criminal law and must be characterised by coherence and transparency. unfortunately, at the moment, these characteristics are not well defined. in this connection, i believe that a new legislative proposal from the commission is needed, which would also make it compulsory to carry out a cost-benefit analysis of the funds used. furthermore, i believe that the involvement of all member states in the surveys is indispensable to demonstrate their usefulness and benefits.
in writing. − i believe that we need common statistics for the development of european union policies. therefore, the appropriate and necessary eu instruments should only be designed and adopted on the basis of common statistics and sound and coherent background information. however, the need for these data does not amount to a blank cheque for automatic acceptance of the proposed instrument. therefore, any proposed instrument must be methodologically sound and coherent and, at the same time, be based on a cost-benefit analysis of the funds used and the results expected.
in writing. − more than ever, there is a need for an individual-level inquiry into crime security in the european union. such an inquiry would complement crime figures from administrative sources such as police reports, which are notoriously difficult to compare between member states. moreover, an investigation in this respect could collect information based on a common methodology and a common questionnaire. however, i believe that such a survey should be carried out in all eu member states, with the exception that 'france and ireland are not obliged to collect data on violence between members of the same household'.
in writing. − i voted against commission’s proposal for a regulation on european statistics on safety from crime and therefore for the rapporteur’s resolution. i would like to underline the lack of real added value of the surveys and the lack of information on how they will be used for future proposals for legislation. what is the benefit of the surveys to the eu institutions? how will the people that are not victims fit in the survey? we underline the random character of the survey. what if it happens that none of the people interviewed have ever been victims? why would the person interviewed give an answer to a survey rather to the police? how can one guarantee that this information will not be used for other purposes? why does not eurostat use official data regarding crimes that were reported? in conclusion, i decided to follow the rapporteur’s position due to the methodology proposed for the achievement of these statistics. the added value of the survey, the cost-benefit and outcome of the survey remain the main concerns and therefore the commission should come up with an improved proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european security statistics on crime. common statistics at eu level provide an important basis for the development of eu policies. this applies all the more in the area of criminal law as a mixed competence (article 4 tfeu), where the eu is obliged to respect the principle of subsidiarity (article 5 teu) and where criminal law is linked to the understanding of fundamental rights in a free society. therefore, the appropriate and necessary eu instruments should only be designed and adopted on the basis of common statistics and sound and coherent background information. we ask the commission to indicate the number of member states already carrying out such surveys and their costs and to compare and analyse the added value and costs of previous surveys co-financed by the commission, such as the european crime and safety survey. survey questions should be drafted in a clear and precise manner, allowing for clear answers, the analysis of which can be used in future policy design.
in writing. − ground handling services are vital to the smooth running of air operations. according to the european commission, the turnover of ground handling services amounts to eur 50 billion. the number of jobs in this sector is estimated to be at least 60 000 across europe. the evolution of wages in the ground handling sector remained below the level of inflation and below the level of average wage growth. staff costs amount to approximately 75% of the production costs of the services. the commission notes that the airport services agreement concluded between ryanair and ams was signed on 30 june 2014 and entered into force on 1 january 2014. the commission notes that the airport services agreement concluded between ryanair and ams was signed on the same day. the commission's proposed regulation, which would replace directive 96/67/ec, aims to reduce delays and improve the quality of air passenger services. in order to achieve this objective, the commission intends to further liberalise the market for ground handling services by authorising at least one more independent third party ground handling company.
in writing. − ground handling services are vital to the smooth running of air operations. there are eleven categories of ground handling services: ground administrative assistance and surveillance; passenger handling; baggage handling; cargo and mail handling; ramp handling; aircraft services; fuel and lubricant handling; aircraft maintenance; flight operations and crew administration; ground transport and catering services. the number of jobs in the ground handling sector is estimated to be at least 60 000 in europe. the eu trade unions stressed that the evolution of wages in the ground handling sector remained below the level of inflation and below the level of average wage growth. the commission notes that the airport services agreement between the airlines and the airport operator was signed on 20 june 2014 and entered into force on 1 january 2014. it is unacceptable that wages in the ground handling sector are falling further and that more and more permanent jobs are being converted into temporary contracts. employees are responsible for air traffic safety, for maintaining technical flight security, but also for combating terrorist threats. the increasing social pressure on workers in this sector and their precarious situation, together with the liberalisation of the market for handling services, is contrary to the safety interests of the population.
in writing. − the quality of ground handling services within the european union’s airports is of high importance nowadays and it affects us all daily. i took note of the commission’s proposal intending to improve the efficiency of ground handling services, but i regret that important aspects were overlooked. no minimum standards or performance indicators were formulated for the attainment of these services overall quality. in order to increase the performance of the whole eu aviation chain and to achieve the realisation of the single european sky, we need to provide harmonised minimum requirements for airports and their operators. i urge the commission to clearly define obligatory minimum quality standards and to implement key performance indicators, applicable for all suppliers of ground handling services and self handling users, in order to improve the functioning of airports within the eu and to ensure a better service quality for the passengers.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of this report because i am sure that we can reach better conclusions by pursuing the debate. the committee on transport and tourism has two months from now to draw up a final report. it would have been a missed opportunity to reject the commission’s proposal and i am convinced that we will find a compromise that will satisfy the majority and that will benefit the citizens and the aviation industry. in view of major growth for air traffic, i think that liberalisation is necessary, at the same time as the establishment of minimum quality standards to improve the groundhandling services.
in writing. − globally, air transport has recently experienced unprecedented developments. if in the last 10 years 800 airlines have left the profile market, instead over 1 300 companies have appeared. at the same time, airlines operate some 90 000 flights a day, more than a quarter of which are within eu airspace. eurocontrol forecasts a steady growth of 5% in the number of flights in europe over the next decade, and the numbers could increase considerably once the current economic crisis is over. while at eu level we are facing congestion at the main airports, according to eurostat data, regional airports are reporting steady decreases in annual profit rates. in this respect, i am convinced that the allocation of slots at eu airports must take account of these discrepancies. regional airports can balance capacity and demand for passenger and cargo air transport. the efficient allocation of time slots should take into account the improvement of access at regional hub airports, which could significantly contribute to the growth of economic and tourist activity at regional level.
in writing. - i voted for amendment no 1, which proposes that the commission's proposal on the use of hadling services at union airports be rejected. i voted to reject and refer the proposal back to the commission, as voted in the transport and tourism committee (tran) of parliament on 6 november 2012. the main criticism of the tran commission to the commission's proposal concerns the social impact of the liberalisation of ground handling services for employees. there were also doubts about the positive impact of the proposal on quality of service and safety aspects. ground handling services are vital to the smooth running of air operations. however, i believe that further liberalisation of the ground handling market at the expense of workers is not the solution to make european airports and airlines more competitive. i voted to refer the motion back to the tran committee, which is the committee of the parliament responsible for this file. this will allow the existing text to be improved until a new commission proposal is made. however, if the tran committee's demands are not met, namely that the liberalisation of handling services should not be at the expense of workers, we will continue to support the rejection of the proposal for a regulation.
in writing. − airport capacity continues to decrease and their infrastructure develops slowly. it is absolutely necessary to improve the regulations regarding the limited resource of slots available in european union airports. however, the slot allocation process should be transparent, and coordinators and schedule facilitators must be independent and free from conflicts of interests. we also need to guarantee the neutrality and equality in the allocation, management and use of slots, in order to encourage effective competition and avoid fraud or misleading information. therefore, i call on the commission to clearly define strict criteria ensuring transparency of coordination activities and schedules facilitation.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of this report because it made the airport slot allocation process more transparent and more efficient and it allows airports to be more involved in the way their capacity is being used by airlines. this vote approved landing and take-off slot allocation and exchange rules designed to ensure that unused slots are made available to interested operators as soon as possible and without prejudice to connections between regional airports and major hubs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation on the allocation of slots at european union airports. the system of allocating slots does not ensure the optimal allocation and use of slots and, consequently, of airport capacity. the allocation and use of slots can be made more efficient by introducing mechanisms for the exchange of slots, while ensuring that unused time slots are made available to interested operators as soon as possible, in a transparent manner and by reinforcing the basic principles of the system, both in terms of the allocation and management of slots and their use. in addition, it is important that access to hub airports from regional airports is maintained where such routes are essential to the economy of the region concerned. concerns about the efficient allocation of slots must continue to take into account the need to protect the external benefits of air transport services, in particular the value they create for european regions. in order to further improve the system for allocating slots at eu airports and in the light of the evolution of joint projects, the progress made in the implementation of the single european sky and the results of the evaluation report, the commission shall adopt delegated acts to establish the post of european coordinator.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because the number of people affected by airport noise is constantly increasing. and this has negative health effects. in recent years, air traffic has increased, and airports have expanded even more. in this context, i consider that the noise level in the vicinity of airports in the union must be reduced as quickly as possible. to avoid harming the health of those living near airports, stronger noise control measures are needed, including the development of new noise standards for aircraft and new technologies. we need to consider both the economic benefits and the impact on health and quality of life in order to make the right assessment. i also want to draw attention to the fact that we must make every effort not to harm the health and well-being of people.
in writing. − the proposal aims to update existing measures to enable local authorities to improve noise levels in the vicinity of airports in the union. this approach must be done in a coherent manner. the eu is actively supporting the development of new noise standards for aircraft and investing in new technologies through the framework programmes and the clean sky project. however, land-use planning, together with related isolation and compensation programmes, is a national or local competence. operating procedures are the responsibility of the airport or air traffic service providers and are governed by the single european sky legislation. the proposal therefore covers noise-related operating restrictions as well as process-specific requirements and transposes international commitments into european law.
in writing. − i have voted in favour of this report because it aims at updating existing measures in order to enable local authorities to improve the noise climate around airports in the union within the international framework of the icao’s balanced approach on noise management. local authorities should also take into account economic and social aspects as well as health.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the reports on the allocation of slots at european union airports and the introduction of noise operating restrictions at eu airports. i welcome the attention paid to airports and their operation, especially in terms of passenger services. but we should also be concerned about the future of regional airports, and in this context i ask the commission to consider revising the threshold for operational aid by the member states up to one million passengers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation on the introduction of noise operating restrictions at airports in the union. additional noise reduction measures should be developed following a systematic environmental monitoring and control process and should be based on a conservative approach, aiming at the prompt identification of necessary management and/or operational monitoring-based corrective measures. the airport operator must allow the choice of the most cost-effective noise reduction measures, taking into account health, economic and social aspects, in accordance with the 'balanced approach', so as to ensure the sustainable development of the airport and the capacity of the air traffic management network in a 'gate-to-gate' perspective. the use of approved noise abatement operating procedures should ensure that the necessary safety of flights is maintained by taking into account all factors that could affect a particular operation. operational noise abatement measures shall not prevent or prohibit security measures for the purpose of combating terrorism. noise assessments should be carried out or supervised by external and independent control agencies.
in writing. − the european union must continue to develop a statistical programme, as the need for information on the union's dynamics among european citizens and economic actors is growing. at the same time, it is only by carrying out accurate research that the union can act to increase its own institutional transparency. at the same time, it should be borne in mind that, in the context of increasing global interdependence, policy-making and policy implementation or the drafting of legislation must rely on increasingly complex statistics, which the present project has the capacity to achieve. moreover, in the current economic and financial crisis, the ability of states to collect and provide accurate and adequate statistics in short time frames is limited. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the launch of a new statistical programme can provide european citizens and economic operators with data on the basis of which effective public policies or commercial strategies can be adopted.
in writing. − i consider the proposals of the rapporteur on the european statistical programme 2013-2017 to be positive and have therefore voted in favour of this report. in the current crisis, which requires coherent and effective policies, access to reliable and high-quality statistics is indispensable. a rigorous governance structure must therefore be developed to allow for the strict monitoring of statistics at european level. at the same time, government influence must be diminished to maintain and increase confidence in the statistics presented. i welcome the proposal to increase the role of eurostat, which, by publicly expressing its views on member states' practices, would increase transparency in this area. the implementation of public standardised audit systems that would effectively monitor the eu-wide accounting system and prevent fraud is also of particular importance.
in writing. − high-quality, regulated and reliable statistics are important components of the economic policy-making process. this procedure aims at creating a rigorous governance structure to ensure the integrity and quality of statistics at eu level. the main issues addressed in this report are: strengthening governance frameworks, including the independence of statistical offices; standardised public audit systems; easy-to-use statistical information; supporting member states to ensure compliance. in the wake of the crisis and with the start of the process of implementing the eu's new economic governance framework, high-quality statistics are particularly important. the rapporteur believes that the legislative authorities should take this opportunity to create the most reliable and accountable systems possible, either through more efficient funding mechanisms, by giving eurostat a greater role or by strengthening governance structures.
in writing. − for evidence-based decision-making, reliable and high-quality statistics are essential. recent economic events have demonstrated the importance of credible statistics for the public and financial markets to have confidence in such decisions. i am glad that the commission's proposal focuses on the independence of the national statistical institutes and, in particular, of the directors of these authorities. however, i believe that the national statistical authorities should be closely monitored and that irregularities should be discouraged by means of tough sanctions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the regulation on the european statistical programme 2013-2017 because the implementation of eu policies requires comparable and reliable statistical information on the social, economic and environmental situation in the eu, as well as its components at national and regional level. european statistics are also indispensable for europe to be understood by the general public and for citizens to participate in the democratic process and in the debate on the present and future of the eu. the financial envelope for the implementation of this programme is set at eur 299,4 million, including eur 57,3 million for 2007-2013 and eur 242,1 million for 2014-2017. in addition to the financial envelope established by this regulation, the individual statistical actions adopted for the implementation of this programme, in particular by agreement between the national statistical institutes and other national authorities and the commission (eurostat), shall receive adequate funding at national level. in order to implement the programme, the commission shall adopt annual work programmes which meet the requirements laid down in article 17 of regulation (ec) no 223/2009 and set out the objectives pursued and the expected results. the financial contributions from the union may take the form of grants or public procurement contracts or any other intervention necessary to achieve the objectives referred to in article 2.
in writing. − the european union is built around the principle of integration. the possibility of introducing a financial transaction tax is one of the main points of debate on the european union's agenda. the institutional benefits that such a move can bring are equally relevant at a time when the european union states are facing the severe effects of the economic crisis. the decision of some states to go in this direction increases the relevance of the current debate. however, the institutional and budgetary impact of the adoption of a financial transaction tax is difficult to estimate at the moment. it is important that more actors take concrete steps towards deepening the process of cooperation in the fiscal and financial field, but any final decision at this level must take into account the cumulative effects produced at the level of all european economies. however, it is clear that the expected results can only be achieved if similar measures to tax financial transactions are adopted at eu-wide or even global level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation because it is important that the union can strengthen its revenue system. only by harmonising the legislation on the financing of the budget from own resources can we contribute to deepening integration and moving towards a genuine political union. a correctly applied single financial transaction tax could complement regulatory measures aimed at avoiding future economic and financial crises. the common tax could also be a source of revenue to accelerate economic growth. on the other hand, a rigorous impact assessment of the effects on participating states and especially on non-participating states is indispensable. we must ensure that the rights, competences and obligations of non-participating states are not infringed and their competitiveness is not affected.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the recommendation on enhanced cooperation on the financial transaction tax. this tax will reduce volatility in financial markets and will also be a fairer method of taxation. the financial sector must also contribute to the recovery. in this context, i hope that as many eu member states as possible will decide to join the eleven that have decided to adopt a financial transaction tax.
in writing. − the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and the achievement of its objectives depend to a large extent on the decisions we take during this period on the structure of future programmes and their budgets. although the financial sector has been highly profitable over the past two decades, it played the main role in triggering the economic crisis, while the costs were borne by public administrations and european citizens. that is why i believe that financial institutions must contribute equitably and substantially to covering the costs of the recent crisis. in addition, in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market for financial transactions and to avoid distortions of competition, the european union urgently needs to harmonise legislation on indirect taxation of financial transactions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the council decision authorising enhanced cooperation in the field of financial transaction tax. as a result of the recent financial and economic crisis, some member states have started to implement new forms of taxation of the financial sector, while other member states already apply specific tax regimes for financial transactions, which leads to undesirable effects such as: a fragmentation of the tax treatment in the internal market for financial services, the absence of a fair and substantial contribution by financial institutions to the costs of the recent crisis and the lack of a fair tax treatment of the financial sector compared to other sectors. the implementation of a common system of financial transaction tax applied in a sufficient number of member states would bring immediate benefits to financial transactions in the framework of enhanced cooperation. the position of the participating member states would also improve in terms of delocalization risks, tax revenues, financial market efficiency and avoidance of double taxation or double non-taxation. the legislation and policy of other member states in the field concerned will not be affected, as operators in those member states can also benefit from the reduction of fragmentation of the internal market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because in recent years the transport time of animals has increased. and often the conditions under which they are transported cause them undue suffering. the petition signed by over a million union citizens calling for an eight-hour limit to the journey of animals for slaughter should be taken into account. the transport of products of animal origin is a simpler and more economically reasonable solution than the transport of live animals. last but not least, member states should ensure that animal control standards are met. this could be achieved by developing an objective and reliable system for assessing the welfare of animals during transport. and to do this as well as possible, specialised control institutions will have to be set up.
in writing. − since 1977, the european union has had rules on the protection of animals during transport, which aim to remove technical barriers to trade while ensuring a high level of animal welfare. european union legislation on animal welfare during transport was updated by council regulation (ec) no 1/2005 on the protection of animals during transport and related operations, which entered into force on 5 january 2007. i consider that the harmonised enforcement and implementation of animal welfare rules is a key element in maintaining high animal welfare standards and avoiding market disruption in the eu.
in writing. − european legislation must guarantee the welfare of animals and their freedom from unnecessary suffering at all the main stages: rearing, transport and slaughter. in order to put this principle into practice, i believe it is necessary to set a maximum time limit for the transport of animals for slaughter, but with certain derogations to take account of the exceptional situations in some member states due to geographical conditions, road infrastructure, remote locations or the possibility of transporting certain animal species. higher standards for the means of transport, the equipment with which the animals are equipped and the staff who care for and accompany the animals can ensure that animal welfare standards are met during transport even where, due to these exceptional circumstances, the maximum journey time cannot be respected. in order to avoid stress and other negative effects that animals may experience during transport and to reduce economic, social and environmental costs, i consider that animals should be slaughtered as close as possible to the place where they were raised. the council and the european commission must encourage a regional animal production model whereby animals are born, raised and slaughtered in the same region, rather than being transported over extremely long distances.
in writing. − it is well known that animal health implies animal welfare, a certain minimum biological comfort, without which full expression of vitality, including natural behaviour, appropriate to changes in the environment is not possible. i therefore believe that effective and uniform implementation of existing eu legislation on the transport of animals in all member states must be maintained at eu level.
in writing. − the cruel conditions under which some animals are transported are of high concern for us. we need to immediately take action in order to enforce the eu regulation for their protection. therefore, i voted in favour for this report. however, in order to prevent law infringements in all member states, we need to harmonise the sanctions and penalties across the eu. only in this manner we can halt practices that worsen the conditions for the transport of animals. i call on the commission to regulate dissuasive sanctions at a unitary level in the nearest future, in order to ensure animal welfare during transport.
in writing. - i voted in favour of introducing the maximum eight-hour time limit for the transport of animals for slaughter, because we all want humane conditions for the transport of these animals. however, i would like to point out that the discussions should be more concerned with the conditions under which the animals are transported, not just with setting time limits. we should also be concerned about setting up local slaughterhouses that completely eliminate this discussion. last but not least, if we impose this rule in the eu, we should not allow the importation into the union of meat from animals that have been tortured in every possible way.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution on the protection of animals during transport. i voted for paragraph 14, which considers that the welfare of animals during transport depends in some cases on the existence of appropriate facilities at the vehicle level and the proper treatment of animals, as demonstrated in the opinion of the european food safety authority (efsa) of december 2010. however, we call on the european commission and the member states to establish guidelines on best practices to improve the application of regulation (ec) no 1/2005 and to strengthen control mechanisms in order to guarantee animal welfare. we support supporting local slaughterhouses and local food supply chains to avoid unnecessary transport of animals over long distances. we believe that, in principle, animal welfare legislation should be based on science. we ask the commission to update the rules on the transport of animals in view of the gap between the legislation and the latest scientific evidence identified by the european food safety authority (efsa). i also voted for paragraph 30, which calls on the commission to ensure that veterinary checks are carried out on animals to be transported at the end of the journey. finally, we believe that eu animal welfare rules must take into account the disadvantaged geographical situation of the peripheral and outermost regions.
in writing. − the effective defence and promotion of rights must be a general objective of eu policies and a proactive institutional commitment to human rights, developing and consolidating a true culture of fundamental rights in the union institutions and in the member states. despite existing legislation on combating discrimination, women still face discrimination in various areas of everyday life and i regret that after some 40 years of this legislation, the gender pay gap has not been eliminated. violence against women is the most systematic violation of the rights of girls and women worldwide, including in the eu. the commission should designate 2015 as the european year for the elimination of violence against women and develop an eu-wide strategy to combat violence against women, including mandatory instruments, awareness-raising, data collection and funding for women's ngos. the eu and its member states must work to achieve the objectives of the european pact for equality between women and men 2011-2020 and take action to tackle the gender pay gap, occupational segregation and all forms of violence against women.
in writing. − i believe that at eu level, a sufficient level of funding for programmes dedicated to fundamental rights and anti-discrimination for civil society organisations at all levels must be ensured in the future multiannual financial framework.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on fundamental rights in the european union. this report aims to guarantee that the eu is beyond reproach in upholding fundamental rights. today we can envisage living in a european union where respect for fundamental rights is the reality of everyday life. i personally regret that roma citizens are subjected to collective expulsions and deplore the weak reaction of the commission in certain cases. i welcome the fact that the report highlights the many gaps found in most of the roma integration strategies presented by member states to the commission and calls on national governments to allocate sufficient resources to meet the aims of those strategies.
in writing. − i am pleased that the european parliament, through the work of its committee on petitions and its subcommittee on human rights, continues to be an important voice on issues of human rights and democracy. i have only two observations to make on this subject: - increased attention must be paid to the protection of the rights and dignity of migrants at europe's borders. i am referring in particular to cases of children being arrested and held in european prisons for 'waiting for border controls' - the organisation of an annual conference, organised by the european parliament's committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs and the committee on petitions, would add value to the debate on fundamental rights in the eu.
in writing. − i voted against the report on the situation of fundamental rights in the eu (2010 and 2011) because of the view of the rapporteur on certain of these rights. besides, some of these rights go against the maintenance of a balanced european area of freedom, security and justice that europe has being trying to build since the very beginning, and to consolidate since the lisbon treaty. rights regarding: the right to vote of stateless people in local elections, drugs, illegal residents, transgender rights and naming the specific problems in the different member states go beyond the principal of the functioning of the fundamental rights system of the eu. nevertheless, the report points out rightly key issues such as discrimination, rights of minorities (including national, linguistic minorities and roma), equal opportunities, gender equality, detention of immigrants (including minors), access to healthcare for immigrants (including for irregular migrants, especially pregnant women and children) fighting against homophobia, rights of the child and citizenship. all these issues have to be respected in the european union and have to be taken into consideration for the future eu legislation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation of fundamental rights in the european union, because article 2 of the treaty on european union (teu) establishes the union as a community of indivisible and universal values. these values include respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, gender equality, non-discrimination, solidarity, the rule of law and respect for human rights and civil liberties for all people living in the eu. i believe that the under-representation of women in the political decision-making process is a deficit for fundamental rights and democracy, and the positive measures introduced in france, spain, belgium, slovenia, portugal and poland, such as systems of legislative parity and quotas for women's representation, are essential good practices. calls on member states where women's political representation is particularly low to consider the introduction of binding legislative measures. we argue that violence against women is the most systematic violation of the rights of girls and women worldwide, including in the eu, and we call on the commission to establish 2015 as the european year for the elimination of violence against women. we call on the commission to develop an eu-wide strategy to combat violence against women.
unfortunately, the union has not yet had a unified approach to human rights worldwide. the adoption of the strategic framework will provide more coherence in the field. i too believe that human rights must be at the heart of relations with all third countries and that respect for them must be mentioned in all agreements concluded by the european union. the commission should therefore develop clear criteria for the application of the human rights clause, as well as mechanisms leading to a simpler activation of the human rights clause. i therefore support the rapporteur's idea that parliament should be a co-decision factor in this area. finally, speaking of human rights, i would like to remind you of the repeated violations of human rights in the regions of frozen conflict, and i am referring in particular to the transnistrian region.
russia's accession to the world trade organisation can ensure a strengthening of the partnership with the european union. but this partnership, characterised by interdependence, must also be an equitable one. the fact that the russian side has shown its willingness to comply with international trade rules is not enough. russia has to meet all of its wto obligations before we can talk about a new deal. the introduction or prolongation of restrictive trade measures, such as a ban on imports of animals from the european union, favouring russian producers in public procurement or imposing import duties on certain types of sugar, are practices that are contrary to wto rules. it is therefore imperative that the new agreement contains provisions relating to trade and investment. the new framework for negotiations with russia must also include a chapter on energy, one of the most sensitive but also most important issues for the european union. although negotiations on a substantive and legally binding chapter are currently at an impasse, the european commission must make every effort to ensure that the principles of transparency, free competition, reciprocity and non-discrimination in the energy sector are respected by russia.
in writing. – in the last decade of the twentieth century the west failed to push back russia from containing its imperial ambitions. in the first decade of the twenty-first century the west failed to establish a partnership for integrating russia within the european system of security, stability, freedom and prosperity. in the second decade of the twenty-first century the west finds itself in front of an assertive russia which is no longer the old enemy and not quite its ally, but which is in a contest of interests with it. the problem is that the eu is unable to define a common position concerning its geo-strategic interests. therefore it prefers to engage in a deadened way of exporting values by transforming the adoption of its standards beyond the need for interoperability into the conditionality for the progress of political cooperation. russia could not be forced to accept such a deal and the eu has no strength to impose it. the only way to reset the eu-russia relations is by transferring the negotiations to the rational field of interests where the eu can promote a strategy of joint projects aimed at achieving a balanced multipolar global order and a secure common neighbourhood.
president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, we are all following the domestic political situation in egypt with increasing concern. last week saw violent clashes during demonstrations, leading to several deaths and many hundreds injured. the situation between president morsi’s supporters and the main opposition, the national salvation front, is seemingly blocked. further protests are called for by both camps. an agonising question that boggles the mind is: what about egypt’s democratic transition? on monday, we discussed the situation in egypt in the foreign affairs council. ministers agreed that we need to see a de-escalation of the situation and an all-inclusive dialogue to find a solution based on consensus and joint ownership. and evidently, egypt needs a strong constitution that represents all egyptians. honourable members, allow me first to recapitulate some of the events that have led to this deeply divisive political crisis. on 22 november, president morsi issued a constitutional declaration whereby he, among other things, put the presidency beyond judicial control. on 30 november, a draft constitution was adopted by the islamist-dominated constituent assembly and presented to the president. a public referendum on the constitution was called for on 15 december. demonstrations by both camps followed, initially peaceful but – regrettably – turning violent last week. last thursday, president morsi addressed the nation, calling for talks; however, not budging on the constitutional declaration and keeping the set date for the referendum. the national salvation front, which is the main opposition bloc, consisting of liberal and secular parties, including, inter alia, former presidential contenders amr moussa and mohamed el-baradei, refused to take part in the talks, since none of their requests were complied with – namely, to rescind the constitutional declaration, cancel the constitutional referendum and create a new constituent assembly. on saturday, and following the planned dialogue that convened some 60 political figures – but not, however, the national salvation front – president morsi nullified the initial constitutional declaration but then he issued a new one, which included keeping a date for the referendum. as we speak, new demonstrations are being called for by pro-morsi supporters and by the opposition, but the situation is calmer in the streets. the national salvation front has announced today that it will participate in the constitutional referendum and campaign for a ‘no’ vote. this lends a new level of legitimacy to the vote. on the economic front, egypt decided to freeze – for the moment – the imf loan for a month. this is not a final decision and we will need to see how the situation unfolds. all along, high representative/vice-president cathy ashton, as well as the eu special representative bernardino león and the eu delegation in cairo, have been in constant touch with the main political protagonists – not least foreign minister mohamed amr – passing on messages on the need for de-escalation and conciliatory moves. this has been judged the preferred course of action, given the degree of polarisation and controversy between the parties and also the sensitivity on both sides about outside interference. as you will know, last wednesday, high representative/vice-president ashton also conveyed in a public statement the importance of egypt continuing its democratic transition and called for inclusive dialogue. going back to my initial question on egypt’s democratic transition, democracy-building is not a ‘quick fix’. many of you have witnessed this process recently in your own countries. you know that building deep and sustainable democracy is a long process which requires hard work, commitment and stamina as well as patience – domestically and internationally. sometimes, actions and measures will be taken that, in hindsight, are not particularly well-considered. as one of my colleagues in the foreign affairs council stated on monday, transition is always messy and entails divisive decisions at times. it is important, however, to take account of opposition demands. i think this statement summarises the situation in egypt very well, and it is now up to the leadership, together with the opposition, to truly engage in an inclusive dialogue to find a consensual solution that has joint ownership – also to restore confidence regarding egypt’s commitment to democratic transition. again, i repeat that it is of the utmost importance that egypt gets a constitution that represents all egyptians and ensures human rights for all, independently of faith, gender or any other consideration. people lost their lives in tahrir square and elsewhere in their legitimate request for their political and socio-economic rights. let us never forget that. honourable members, egypt is currently facing an extremely delicate situation, but they have to find a solution themselves. egypt belongs to the egyptians, and we should not and cannot impose a solution. what we can do now is to show that the european union supports the people of egypt through the democratic transition and continue our call for inclusive dialogue for a solution based on consensus – and, evidently, banning any violence. the european union also needs to convey firmly and clearly our expectations for a democratic transition, recalling the successful eu-egypt task force of 13-14 november in which some of you actively took part and which established a new momentum in eu-egypt relations based on respect for social justice, socio-economic development, the rule of law, human rights and good governance.
on behalf of the epp group. i would like, first of all, to welcome the debate we have today on the situation in egypt; it is a really urgent discussion, because, as we all know, the egyptian revolution is in danger. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment. i am sad to say that every day that passes takes us further away from this objective; suffice it to mention the recent adoption of decree 107, which authorizes the egyptian army, in the run-up to the constitutional referendum, to arrest civilians and to bring them before military courts. it is known, on the other hand, that president morsi eventually agreed to withdraw the decree that would have made him a hyper-president, but this did not happen until after two weeks of opposition protests, marked by violent attacks by supporters of the muslim brotherhood. moreover, egyptian society never seemed to be so deeply divided. this is not about whether or not to support president morsi, this is about a deeper division over the place of religion in public life, and this division cannot be overcome by imposing a constitutional text. the european parliament has also called for the commission to be given the task of drawing up a report on the situation in the middle east, which will be presented to the european parliament in the near future. we must therefore insist that the authoritarian drift of the egyptian regime be brought to an end and that a genuine and inclusive dialogue be launched. it's the only way out of the current crisis. the events of the last few hours only serve to reinforce that conclusion. the egyptian military announced that it was holding talks with the opposition to cancel them at the last minute, without specifying another date. moreover, egyptian officials are still pressing for the constitutional referendum, although there is considerable confusion: it is not clear whether the vote will be held on december 15 or both december 15 and 22, and according to the latest information, it has already begun for voters from abroad. such a consultation has more the air of a comedy, of a charade, than of an inclusive democracy. i think that's why we have to insist that the fundamental law of a country cannot be adopted in such a petty way.
we all thought that after the election of the new egyptian president the political situation would stabilize. but unfortunately, in the last couple of weeks, things have gotten out of hand. president morsi's decision to increase his constitutional powers may pose a threat to the path to democracy. i strongly supported all the arab spring movements, including the one in egypt, but i believe that one authoritarian regime should not be replaced by another. that's why i think it's necessary for the president of egypt to abandon the decree that extends his prerogatives, and for the egyptian citizens to abandon the violent protests. the best way for them to make their voices heard is to vote in the constitutional referendum on 15 december, and the adoption of a new constitution will be a further step in the transition to democracy.
mr president, the ukrainian dilemma is not about the choice between values and interests. it is about the choice between promoting the euro-atlantic interest and the eurasian interest. ukraine is the most important geo-strategic asset on the as yet unsettled border between the european union and the emerging eurasian union. those who are able to integrate ukraine in their system will be able to master their security at that border. ukraine expressed loud and clear its choice of integration with the european union. to reject ukraine, irrespective of the reasons – or rather pretexts – formulated to this end, means to betray our values and our interests. we betray our values by alienating the ukrainian people, who are disappointed by our hypocrisy, short-sightedness and unfairness, and by pushing it towards a union which does not cherish our standards. we betray our geostrategic goals because we refuse the benefit of the instruments offered by the already negotiated association agreement in order to bring ukraine, slowly but steadily perhaps, into our union through economic integration, political association and institutional convergence, thus forcing it to become a eurasian outpost at our eastern borders. let us not fool ourselves. postponement means refusal. one might say that the ghosts of ribbentrop and molotov, as well as the geostrategic logic of their pact, hide behind this refusal. therefore we must refuse the refusal. we must move forward by signing the association agreement with ukraine right now.
mr president, the eu recognises ukraine’s european credentials. the conclusion of the negotiations on the association agreement and the evaluation of the visa facilitation action plan are facts underlining the seriousness of the eu’s commitment to ukraine. the electoral process reflects the health of democracy in any society. therefore, when discussing the recent parliamentary elections in ukraine, we naturally evaluate the democratic reform process there. in that respect we salute the decision of the ukraine to set up a commission to evaluate the lessons learned from the last elections, hopefully with an eye to the 2015 presidential elections. however, one should not be too schematic. naturally no election process is perfect, and to conclude from that that the entire democratic commitment should be questioned would be an oversimplification. equally ukraine should be aware that the weightiest factor conferring credibility on its declared objective of further political association and economic integration with the eu is ultimately the success of its democratic, economic and social reform process.
