the council conclusions of monday underlined again ukraine's european orientation and the union's willingness to support this country. on the other hand, as we know, the realisation of the european opportunity requires the fulfilment of a number of conditions, and i am referring here to the democratic process, elections, the question of justice and, of course, the reforms provided for in the association agenda. as for the elections, the october 28 elections clearly marked a deterioration from the level reached before ukraine. the main shortcomings have already been pointed out, and i say this, they concern unequal access to mass media, to resources, but also, very importantly, harassment and intimidation of opponents. if this is harassment, we're obviously talking about convicting members of the former government in trials that are far from meeting international standards. i have said it before in this parliament, and i, and my colleagues, have said it before, that the sentencing of yulia tymoshenko has become a symbol of the politicization of justice, not just in ukraine, but more broadly in the world. finally, i would like to emphasise the crucial importance of cooperation with the council of europe and the venice commission in revising the law on the functioning of the office of the prosecutor general, reforming the criminal code and the police, the role of the superior council of justice and the law governing the legal system and the status of judges, the correct implementation of crucial legislation, as well as the fight against corruption. i too express my wish, my hope, that at the vilnius summit we will see an improvement in all these aspects which will obviously help ukraine on its european path.
monitoring the application of fundamental rights is one of the european union's most important tasks, and the fundamental rights agency is its most effective tool. if the eu is to be truly an area of freedom, security and justice, it is essential that fundamental rights are fully guaranteed in all member states to the same standard. it is regrettable that the union does not have the means to ensure these principles in many respects, and that is why member states may approach the issue differently. if we are serious about the rules we have set together, there must be a coercive force - even at union level - to ensure that fundamental rights are respected. reading the rapporteur's position, i was unfortunately not surprised to find that several member states in the council attempted to discriminate against national minorities. some member states would prefer to sweep the problems of national minorities living in their territory under the carpet. the reason is that to this day, equality in all areas of life has not been guaranteed. several member states have done little to protect the rights of national minorities. it is time for the eu to ask about minority protection measures not only for candidate countries, but also for member states to monitor the process. if citizens of the union are guaranteed the same fundamental rights and if the union guarantees their enforcement, then the situation of national minorities cannot be a matter for the member states. national minorities are not immigrants, they are not the result of migration processes over the last hundred years, but communities that have lived in the same area for centuries. the solution to their situation is therefore what is considered to be good practice in the rest of the continent: to provide some form of self-government while respecting the national framework.
i think today's discussion is extremely important. unfortunately, in 2011, poverty and social exclusion in the european union increased dramatically, going from 49% in bulgaria to 17% in luxembourg. i believe that the european union needs a process of reindustrialising europe because only in this way can we create jobs and ensure economic growth. the european union is first and foremost about its 500 million citizens, and it is important that we can provide jobs based on the education that young people have. smes are important. the growth pact must finance and secure job creation. austerity alone cannot ensure economic growth. i welcome the fact that the financial transaction tax will allow the banking system to contribute to the process of economic growth and pay part of the cost of the crisis to which it has contributed substantially.
at a time when financial problems persist, europe needs more than ever urgent measures to support the recovery of economic growth, and that is why i believe that a close link between the commission and parliament is absolutely necessary to find successful solutions. a particularly important issue that the commission must address as a matter of priority is the danger of deindustrialisation in europe. we must be aware that without a strong industrial base, europe has no chance against global competitors. given that industrial investment has fallen by 2.5% of gross domestic product over the last three years, i believe that new sources of finance are urgently needed to stimulate economic recovery and bring innovation and new technologies back into the factories. if the european union does not keep pace with the investments of the other great powers in the adoption and use of these technologies, our future competitiveness will be seriously affected and europe's role as a world leader will be compromised.
in writing. economic recovery and stronger economic growth are necessary to create jobs and prosperity and are essential to make member states' public finances sustainable. european industry is of crucial importance to the eu as a world economic leader. a competitive industry can reduce costs and prices, create new products, improve quality and create jobs, thus contributing to an increase in productivity across the economy. industry is the main source of innovation needed to meet the challenges facing society at eu level. research and innovation lead to increased productivity and competitiveness of industries. the transition to a sustainable economy with efficient use of resources and low carbon emissions is of crucial importance for maintaining the long-term competitiveness of european industries. investment in the small and medium-sized enterprises sector should be promoted, given that smes account for almost 59% of the value added produced in the eu. it is worth noting that 23 million smes currently provide some 90 million jobs in the eu private sector, 30% of which are micro-enterprises.
mr president, in the union we created a common market and then we created a single currency. however, we did not create, and we do not have, a common political will and a common policy. our vote in favour of the financial transaction tax is an important step towards introducing a unique policy. even if it is adopted for only 11 member states, the creation of the financial transaction tax system will make a substantial contribution to covering the costs of the recent crisis. it is important now to concentrate on expanding this system to a unitary level. it is only through harmonised legislation on financing the eu budget by own resources that we can achieve a democratic, fiscal and monetary union.
i voted against the report because i believe that some of its aspects violate the principle of subsidiarity. where the union lacks competence in certain areas, the responsibility lies with the member states. i also think that the report should have put more emphasis on the issue of roma inclusion at european level. romania has a specific problem, having the largest roma community in europe. the national roma inclusion strategy therefore aims to create the conditions for their integration. the main problem remains inadequate funding, as the union has not made additional funds available to the states to implement the strategy. a downside of this strategy is that the states have to allocate money from national budgets, although the issue of roma integration is a european one, not a national one. i think in the future budget, we should find funding sources for national roma inclusion strategies.
mr president, when it was created in 2007 the european agency for fundamental rights was given a five-year multiannual framework. today, we – myself included – consented to the new multiannual framework of the agency for the period 2013-2017. this new multiannual framework broadens the agency’s scope of action to include roma integration – although not to the end of the period – and judicial cooperation with the exception of judicial cooperation in criminal matters. however, although i voted in favour of the council decision, i believe that we should assess in depth the performance of the european fundamental rights agency as well as its added value as against civil society organisations performing similar tasks in order to avoid duplication of work and loss of taxpayers’ money.
i voted in favour of the recommendation because the work of the agency has contributed to a better implementation of the principles of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. in its published reports, the agency has highlighted problems of discrimination, racism, xenophobia or access to justice. it should therefore continue its work in the same thematic areas in the period 2013-2017. we need to ensure that those vulnerable categories are protected in an effective and similar way in absolutely all member states. discrimination on grounds of sex, race or ethnicity cannot be tolerated in a union moving towards greater integration, and the agency can offer the best solutions to such problems. greater involvement of the commission in the development of european policies in this area will strengthen respect for fundamental rights in the union.
mr president, i voted in favour of the report on human rights and democracy in the world. the union needs clear guidelines, principles and benchmarks for its human rights policy and spending. external financial instruments, such as the european instrument for democracy and human rights, for which i am a shadow rapporteur, can help protect the lives of human rights defenders and support civil society organisations in their fight for democracy, the rule of law and justice. we must make use of all these tools together with the principle of ‘more for more’. this means we should both help people in need and pressure local governments to fulfil their political commitments. a gradual process of political reforms monitored by the eu can lead to very good results. the republic of moldova is an excellent example of the effectiveness of our eastern neighbourhood policy. we should draw the right conclusions from this success story and continue to make the union’s human rights policy coherent with our external action.
i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the union must promote human rights everywhere in the world. the first step is the adoption of the human rights action plan. the inclusion of freedom of expression online in the plan is very important, especially in the context of the impact of internet censorship on fundamental rights in many third countries. one example is iran's plan to build a "clean internet", which will block citizens' access to the global web. but there are human rights violations at the borders of the european union too. it is a matter of concern that in countries such as ukraine and russia, the judiciary is being used as a means of putting pressure on political opponents. if the union's human rights action is to be effective, a monitoring mechanism must be set up with very clear criteria.
mr president, we reviewed the eu strategic framework on human rights and democracy, and this is good. i want stronger conditionality and benchmarks that are transparent, measurable, concrete and consistent. in 2012, the union took decisive steps towards enforcing its human rights policy in all eu external action strategies, including by nominating the eu special representative for human rights and by creating the european endowment fund for democracy. the european parliament has actively participated in this process and called repeatedly for more concrete implementing measures. we need to make clear our commitment to measurable criteria for progress on issues such as democracy, justice and the rule of law. we should also continue to reward high achievers and apply the ‘more for more’ principle. the report supports this approach and a tougher stance against those who fail to deliver. i agree with this.
i voted in favour of the report because a genuine partnership between the european union and russia must be based not only on common interests but also on shared principles and values. the respect for the rule of law and the guarantee of fundamental rights and freedoms should be a mandatory part of these. with its influence in the region, russia should become a model for its neighbors. cases such as that of khodorkovsky, or more recently, sergei magnitsky, are known to all members of parliament. therefore, any agreement with russia should contain clauses on human rights and democratic reform issues, and failure to comply with them should automatically lead to the application of sanctions or restrictive measures.
i voted in favor of this resolution. i believe that unilateral decisions do not encourage the peace process in the middle east. although i support the two-state solution, the palestinian authority's move at the un has complicated efforts to resume bilateral negotiations, which is why romania abstained from the vote. hamas attacks on israeli territories have only made the situation worse. at the same time, however, the decision to build new housing in east jerusalem and the west bank also jeopardizes the two-state solution. i believe that a major effort is needed to restore confidence in the area. the resumption of dialogue is essential for ensuring stability in the region. the role of the international community will be to bring the two sides back to the negotiating table. it is likely that without political will, no significant progress will be made.
mr president, ukraine takes over this year the chairmanship of the oecd, and it can play an important role in the ‘5 + 2’ negotiations regarding the settlement of the transdnistrian conflict. the signing in 2013 of the association agreement between the union and ukraine, which includes a dcfda, could be a great achievement for both sides. however, ukraine must also act like a credible international actor and honour its commitments. double-talk is not acceptable. this month, the foreign affairs council highlighted three areas where the union wants more progress from ukraine. one of them is selective justice. we do not want selective justice; we cannot blindly go forward and sign agreements without any evidence that the principles of the rule of law and justice – and i mean justice – are respected. i hope that the ukrainian authorities, as well as the ukrainian people, understand this and take it seriously.
i voted in favour of the resolution because i want to reaffirm my support for albania's european path. i believe that the political agreement of november 2011 between the ruling party and the opposition will accelerate the pace of reforms in the priority areas. however, i must point out that, like many countries in the western balkans, albania also has persistent problems with corruption and the functioning of the judiciary. the commission will have to closely monitor the implementation of reforms in these sectors. another aspect that concerns me is the protection of minorities. the fact that many of them, like the romanian minority, do not yet enjoy official status prevents them from studying in their mother tongue and preserving their culture. last but not least, i hope that the albanian authorities will be more active in combating discrimination against the roma population.
mr president, the steel industry in the union is facing a considerable drop in demand. employment is also decreasing. we cannot afford to become dependent on massive imports from third countries. therefore i urge the commission to urgently adopt measures to foster competition in the steel market in compliance with the eu competition laws. romania, the country i come from, is an important actor in this sector, with more than nine steel plants in various locations. unfortunately, the romanian steel industry is one of the slowest-growing in the european union. employment and exports have been seriously affected. therefore i call on the commission to supervise developments in all member states that can ensure fair competition in the steel market, thereby leading to cost savings.
given that the steel industry is vital to the competitiveness of the european industry as a whole, it is in everyone's interest that it maintains a high level of its activities and ensures security of supply through domestic production. if the european union is to achieve its industrial objective of increasing the share of industry in gross domestic product from 16% to 20% by 2020, the commission must urgently take measures to support the development of the european steel industry. in this respect, i recommend: implementing a new action plan on the sustainable competitiveness of the construction sector and, by implication, the steel sector; developing measures to attract new foreign direct investment; ensuring a level playing field; and, last but not least, avoiding potential abuses of a dominant market position.
i voted in favour of the resolution because the steel sector is facing serious difficulties at the moment. the main challenges are related to the obligation to reduce emissions and costs, and the need to maintain a skilled workforce. furthermore, climate change and new environmental legislation are other issues to consider. the steel industry has so far managed to cope relatively well with the rapid changes in the global steel market. in my country, too, the situation is difficult and the sector has suffered significant losses, especially since the crisis. the galata ironworks lost several thousand employees in the last year. we need coordinated actions and measures to enhance the long-term competitiveness of the industry and to overcome the challenges facing the sector. ♪ i'm not a girl ♪
in writing. − the human rights platform, the agency's management board and the european group of national human rights institutions believe that the agency's remit should explicitly include social rights and a special role in the independent monitoring of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the thematic area on roma integration should also be reformulated. it is regrettable that there is no agreement in the council on the inclusion in the new multiannual framework of proposed new thematic areas, police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, they are an integral part of union law and therefore fall within the scope of the agency's tasks. the agency needs new thematic areas to address in order to have continuity in its activities. if, by the beginning of 2013, there is no multiannual framework, the agency may only work if there is an express request from an institution, and not on its own initiative. the commission should assess and propose the revision of the tasks, areas of activity and working methods of the agency in 2013 in order to ensure the effective monitoring and application of the charter of fundamental rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the proposal for a council decision establishing a multiannual framework for the european union agency for fundamental rights for the period 2013-2017. in accordance with article 5 of regulation (ec) no 168/2007 establishing the european union agency for fundamental rights, the thematic areas of activity of the agency are established by a multiannual framework with a duration of five years. this decision establishes the multiannual framework referred to in article 5 of regulation (ec) no 168/2007 for the period 2013 to 2017 with the following thematic areas: access to justice; victims of crime; information society and, in particular, respect for privacy and protection of personal data; roma integration; police cooperation, taking into account the specific nature of this area; judicial cooperation, taking into account the specific nature of this cooperation when it concerns criminal matters; the rights of the child; discrimination based on race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic characteristics, language, religion or belief, political or other opinion, membership of a national minority, homophobia, disability, age, racial or sexual orientation; immigration integration; xenophobia and related intolerance; and migration and asylum.
in writing. − in recent years, the european parliament has managed to gain more and more powers, giving it the power to take legislative initiative in many areas of major interest to european citizens. i therefore support the rapporteur's proposals which encourage each member to use his or her prerogatives to table proposals for union acts which can have a real impact on policies developed at european level. at the same time, i believe that improvements in the use of written statements, which the european parliament has at its disposal to draw attention to matters of public interest, have the potential to enhance the usefulness of this instrument.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because it called for a simplification of the rules of procedure for written declarations and legislative initiatives. first, i consider that written statements must be based on issues falling within the competence of the union and in which the union may intervene to remedy deficiencies. the signing of a written declaration by a larger number of initiators is also welcome, giving it more legitimacy and increasing the chances of its subsequent adoption. last but not least, the possibility of electronic recording and distribution, as well as the option of withdrawing the signature, will simplify the procedures for written statements. in addition, informing the competent institution of the status of the declaration within a maximum of 3 months will increase the effectiveness of the declarations.
in writing. - i voted to amend rules 123 and 42 of the rules of procedure of the european parliament: written declarations and legislative initiatives. following the extension of parliament's powers and the introduction of the european citizens' initiative, written statements can continue to be a useful tool for members to draw attention to issues of public interest. at least 10 meps from at least three political groups may submit a 200-word written statement on a subject falling within the exclusive competence of the eu. the declaration may not call for legislative action and may not concern the subject of proceedings pending in parliament. written statements shall be published in the official languages on parliament's website and entered in an electronic register with the names of the signatories, accessible on parliament's website. any member may sign a statement entered in the electronic register and his signature may be withdrawn within three months of the entry of the statement in the register. in the event of withdrawal, the member concerned may not re-sign the declaration. if the institutions to which a statement is addressed do not inform parliament within three months of receiving the statement of their intention to act on the statement, one of the authors of the statement may put the matter on the agenda of a subsequent meeting of the committee responsible.
in writing. − in its external action, the european union has developed a number of policy instruments and guidelines to implement its commitment to human rights and democracy. i believe that the institutions of the european union must cooperate as closely as possible both in the development of european human rights policy and in its implementation, because only concerted action has the potential to produce the desired effects. the european union must use all the instruments at its disposal to help improve the situation of fundamental rights in countries where the population does not enjoy them. i therefore stress that the development of a methodology aimed at improving the analysis of the human rights situation in countries outside the european union when trade and/or investment agreements are launched or concluded is essential. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − democracy and the rule of law are the best ways to protect human rights and fundamental freedoms, non-discrimination in all its forms and tolerance towards individuals and communities, and to ensure equality for all. the eu must step up action to stop female genital mutilation, early and forced marriages, honour killings and sex-selective abortions. access to adequate healthcare and information and education on sexual and reproductive health and rights and the well-being of women and girls in all countries is important. the role and participation of women in political, economic and social life are essential, in particular in post-war peace-building processes, in negotiations for a democratic transition, as well as in conflict resolution and reconciliation and stabilisation processes. the eu must work with un women to ensure that women's rights are respected. not only should health education and appropriate programmes for sexual and reproductive health and rights be promoted, but women should also have equitable access to public health systems and adequate gynaecological and obstetrical services.
in writing. − we must be aware that fundamental human rights and freedoms cannot be ignored or disregarded, and that it is essential that they be protected by a system of law. in the interest of respecting human rights worldwide, i would like to highlight the contribution of non-governmental organisations in implementing the 'early warning' function and in supplementing the information provided by the authorities to international bodies. speaking specifically about cases of human rights violations, i would like to express my concern at the decision of the belarusian authorities to expel the ambassador of the kingdom of sweden to the republic of belarus, together with the swedish diplomatic staff accredited to minsk, which has led to a deterioration in relations between the two countries. the european union must maintain pressure on the political regime in belarus.
in writing. - i voted in favour of all the amendments relating to access to family planning and abortion. coming from a country where abortions have been banned for nearly 40 years, i know the trauma such a ban can cause. the right to choose in safe medical conditions must be guaranteed to every woman.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the 2011 annual report on human rights and democracy in the world and the european union's policy on the matter. i support the increased role and full participation of women in political and economic decision-making processes, especially in post-war peace-building processes, in negotiations for a democratic transition, and in conflict resolution. they also support the increased role of women in reconciliation and stabilisation processes, with a view to raising awareness and paying greater attention to eliminating discrimination against women in the process of democratisation in third countries. while the increasing reliance on information and communications technology infrastructures is likely to create new vulnerabilities and security concerns internationally, many of the decentralised features of the internet that have made it a cyber security concern are precisely the reasons that have made it a powerful tool for human rights advocates living in countries with repressive regimes. i believe that a digital freedom strategy is needed, as well as the development of policies and programmes on cyber security and the fight against cybercrime.
in writing. − as the eu is founded on the principle of respect for human rights, i believe that the legal obligation, as laid down in the treaties, is to put human rights at the heart of all eu and member state policies, without any exception.
in writing. − the fundamental principle on which the european union is founded, namely respect for human rights, must also be reflected in our external actions. experience has shown that it is not enough to create financial instruments for these actions, but that better coordination is also needed to avoid the fragmentation of the present and the inefficiency of spending resources. as regards the neighbourhood policy, i think it would be useful to put more emphasis on dialogue with civil society actors such as ngos, the media, trade unions and educational institutions. they are the authority that can give us a more accurate picture of the political, economic and social situation in their respective countries. as for official relations with these countries, i welcome the new approach in this area: 'more for more', because only by holding the governments of the partner countries to account will we be able to help them implement democratic reforms. i personally express my confidence in the ability of the new eu special representative for human rights to implement the strategy in this regard. i welcome good cooperation with the european parliament, which has repeatedly demonstrated its commitment to fundamental rights, whether in the union or in third countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the review of the eu's human rights strategy. the eu is founded on the principle of respect for human rights and has a legal obligation, as laid down in the treaties, to put human rights at the heart of all eu and member state policies, without exception, and at the heart of all international agreements. this renewed policy should lead to a stronger commitment by partner countries to deeper democratic reforms and to respect for fundamental rights and in particular for fundamental rights of the foundation such as freedom of expression, freedom of conscience, religion or thought, freedom of assembly and association. i would remind you that development, democracy and the rule of law are prerequisites for respect for human rights, but they are not equivalent to it, they interact and support each other. i call on the eu to support the establishment of ideals based on the principle of democracy and human rights throughout society, in particular with a view to promoting gender equality and the rights of the child. i also call for impact assessments to cover the full range of human rights, including online rights, which must be understood as an indivisible whole.

in writing. − mr president, the alarming situation in taranto is not unique within the eu. a lack of modernisation in steel plants from different european locations leads to harmful emissions and dangerous effects on the local population’s health. therefore i call on the commission to identify suitable possibilities for encouraging investments in this industry. the member states should also support modernisation of plants that comply with eu environmental law, in order to re-establish an ecological balance. only when we start encouraging competitiveness and sustainability will the steel industry grow again. thank you!
in writing. − i voted for the parliament's resolution on a new sustainable and competitive steel industry (based on a petition received), as the petitioners expressed deep concern about the extremely high levels of dioxin emissions from the ilva steelworks in taranto, which have had and continue to have a significant, negative and lasting impact on the health of the local population. parts of the ilva steelworks have recently been closed by the italian authorities and the authorities and the current owners of the plant have an obligation to ensure that harmful emissions are drastically reduced. the steel industry, which employs some 360 000 people, is a crucial economic sector in the union. parliament has a duty and a responsibility to show solidarity with the employees of the steelworks ilva and their families. in the context of eu industrial policy, it is strategically essential to prevent the relocation of steel mills and production outside the european union and to ensure the safety of the european workforce. we call on the commission and the council to develop a new policy for the steel industry that will stimulate growth and employment in the face of the economic crisis and that is compatible with the health and safety of all eu citizens and residents.
author. − the takeover of the city of goma by m23 rebels has clearly demonstrated rwandan control over the congolese province of north kivu. this foreign involvement is one of the facets of the endless war that is traumatizing the democratic republic of congo. this is not just a civil conflict, but an inter-african war for control of the resources of the great lakes region. and because this is the bloodiest conflict since world war ii, the international community is obliged to push the warring parties to continue the talks that started in kampala. in the surrounding area of goma, there are over 130,000 refugees, many of them housed in schools that have ceased to function, and children have been forcibly recruited as soldiers. the population is deprived of basic means of subsistence and there have been numerous rapes and mass executions. the 11-day occupation of goma must prompt an urgent re-evaluation of the world's largest peacekeeping mission. i don't think the expected 2,000 additional blue-helmet troops and the possible use of drones are sufficient solutions to the complicated conflict equation in the region. after the un mission has proven, in so many situations, incapable of protecting civilians, i believe that a new strategy is needed to combat the insurgency, its effects on the civilian population, but also to control the use of revenues from the exploitation of huge natural reserves in the financing of rebel militias.
if i count correctly, this is the sixth time since the beginning of this mandate that we have discussed the grave and very grave situation in the democratic republic of congo. we have discussed this issue, and the resolution we have today is very close to the one that was adopted there and at the acp-eu joint parliamentary assembly in paramaribo a few days ago. one of the conclusions of these discussions is the need for coordination with regional partners, with the united nations. in particular, i believe that support for the implementation of the measures decided at the high level meeting of the international conference of the great lakes region on 24 november 2012 is very important.
the author. - the text of our joint resolution is based on several recent incidents in the town of dharmapuri in tamil nadu and in the village of dabra in hisar, incidents which show us that discrimination against the dalit caste is still a tragic reality in india. mrs lochbihler, our colleague, explained what dalit means, a term that has replaced the old term intubabili, which is much more present in the ordinary discourse. moreover, the mobilization around the imposition of this new name shows that, in the end, the cause we are defending here has won international support. but while we recognize the efforts that the indian government has made to eliminate caste discrimination, we obviously want better implementation of the legislation, and also knowing, of course, that eliminating discrimination is a long process, because it requires a change of mindset, we think that there are some concrete steps that need to be taken, and it's very simple to explain. for example, we need an independent police force that is not corrupt to record all cases, all complaints of those who feel discriminated against. we are far from that, unfortunately, in india. i also believe that the indian parliament needs to pass the bill to ban humiliating sanitation work, which directly affects this caste and keeps them in the plight of marginalization in which they find themselves.
the european parliament has also called for the commission to take action to combat the illegal trade in human beings. unfortunately, women are doubly discriminated against, for non-caste and for being women, as is the case with the dalits. they are often victims of marginalization, ill-treatment and rape, without the possibility of real and effective access to justice. it's a situation that the indian authorities have a duty to remedy, especially since it's a major segment of the population: one in six indians is a dalit, that is, excluded from the caste system. in fact, india needs to enforce its own constitution, which prohibits caste discrimination, and enforce the representation quotas that have improved the situation of dalits, such as in employment. i also believe it is important that the european union, especially through the high representative for foreign affairs and the special representative for human rights, develop a new strategy against such discrimination and that the member states include this issue in their dialogue with the indian authorities in order to encourage them to adopt concrete programmes.
in writing. – i deplore the alarming discrimination against dalits still occurring in india. although abolished through the provisions of the constitution of this country, the discriminatory and untouchability practices still affect millions of people. india is the largest democracy in the world. however it is unacceptable that justice in this country is not able to address properly violence against human rights. today, i urge the government of india to reinforce the legislation protecting dalits and any other vulnerable groups. indian authorities must ensure the intervention of police in gross acts of violence against people and their assets. in parallel, serious efforts must be made in order to ensure that the judicial system of the country will guarantee protection and justice whenever these atrocities are reported.
